# AGENTS-recipes.md — matching recipes & session history (on-demand reference)

 companion to `AGENTS.md`. AGENTS.md is the minimal handoff every agent loads.
**This file is the detail archive: read it ON DEMAND (grep for what you need — never bulk-read all 16k lines into context).**

Contents below is the verbatim bulk moved out of AGENTS.md (everything after §4),
plus an index. New matching recipes go here, not in AGENTS.md.

## Index

- Compiler deep-dive + QB constants + struct passes: original §4b
- Micro-fix catalogs: §§4p, 4s, 4t, 5p, 5q, 4q, 4r
- Workflow details: §§4c–4o (FPR quirk, auto-matchers, WIP loop, m2c pipeline, FAIL attacks, NEAR playbook)
- Full tools table: §5 · progress: §5b · reference artifacts: §5c · env quirks: §6 · boot: §7 · next steps: §8
- All `6*`/`7*` batch-session learnings (chronological, newest at end)
- Tip: `grep -n "^## " AGENTS-recipes.md` for the section list; `grep -n -i "<keyword>" AGENTS-recipes.md` to find a recipe.
- §7q: reload copy (`fmr`/`ps_mr`) needs a NON-ESCAPING standalone local; ngccc's 4-byte local sorts before an 8-byte one.
- PS frame templates: under `-mps-float` BOTH `f32` members of `union { f32 lo, hi; __ps_t ps; }` land at offset 0 — use `f32[N]` arrays (docs/parkings/06-paired-single-ops.md, addendum 2026-10-02).

## 4b. The compiler discovery (read before touching cflags_game)

> **SDK library version (distinct from the compiler):** `docs/dolphin-sdk.md`.
> thug2 links Dolphin SDK `0x2301` (OS build Mar 17 2003, GX Feb 7 2003), but
> `libs/dolphin/` is zeldaret/tp's **2004** build of the same SDK — a superset.
> Read it before wiring up or adapting `libs/dolphin`.

**4b-SDK. Wiring a DolphinLib module — the hybrid extern-route recipe (M8.112–8.114).**
When wiring a `libs/dolphin` module, prefer **tww's Sep-2002 sources** (`../tww`,
byte-identical banners); tp's Apr-2004 copies are a superset and must be adapted
down. Verify the candidate source FIRST by compiling it standalone with the
DolphinLib cflags and comparing **per-function sizes** against the retail
boundaries in `symbols.txt` — if every live function size matches, the source is
right. Two traps that produced false "clean" and false "different revision"
conclusions on SI:
- **Stale-orphan trap**: a missing compile rule (e.g. split key case mismatch
  `pad/Padclamp.c` vs `pad/padclamp.c`, or a lib listed in configure.py but not
  emitted) makes the link silently consume old `.o` files → DOL looks clean.
  Always force-recompile the new objects (`rm obj; ninja`) before trusting cmp.
- **Truncated-disasm trap**: judging "revision gap" from a partial disassembly
  of one function — read the FULL function range before concluding.

The **extern route is NOT safe for big data.** Externing `.data`/`.bss` statics
that the compiler allocates registers around (`Si`, `Packet`, `Alarm`, `Type`,
`TypeCallback`, `InputBuffer*`, …) changes register allocation: frame sizes,
`stmw` spans and load order all drift and the `.text` stops matching. Only the
**4-not-8-aligned `.sbss`/`.sdata` scalars** are safe to extern (they're only
address-taken / `@sda21`-referenced → identical codegen). mwld bumps any
4-aligned `.sbss` claim to 8-align (docs §8.12/8.14), so those symbols stay in
auto-asm (`scope:global` in symbols.txt) and the C declares them `extern`.

Final hybrid recipe (SI, M8.114 — DOL byte-clean, 24 fns):
1. `.data` + `.bss` stay **static**, claimed in splits.txt at 8-aligned starts
   (`.data` @ 0x8030F780, `.bss` @ 0x803C85C0 — no mwld bump).
2. `.sbss`/`.sdata` externs: `cmdTypeAndStatus`×2, `__PADFixBits`,
   `SamplingRate` (set `scope:global` so dtk auto-covers it), `__SIVersion` ptr.
3. Version string: the **pointer** is `.sdata` (extern), the **string** must stay
   in `.data` AND be linkable as the auto unit's relocation target — emit it as
   a `#pragma force_active` **global** `char lbl_8030F780[] = "..."`. Do NOT use
   `static const char[]` — const arrays go to `.rodata` (wrong section).
4. Keep dead functions in the source when their **string literals survive in
   retail `.data`** (SI: SIDecodeType/SIProbe/SIGetTypeString own the type-name
   strings) — the linker dead-strips the `.text` but the `.data` stays.
5. Match struct strides to retail: `SISamplingRate` indexes `XY` with stride 4
   (`slwi rN, msec, 2`) → struct must be `{u16 line; u8 count; u8 pad;}`.

Trying to match the first function with mwcc failed **for every version and flag
combo** (1.0→4.x, `-O0`→`-O4,p`, `-schedule`, `-opt level=...`). The tell:
THUG2 loads 32-bit constants as `lis r0, 0x12b9; ori r0, r0, 0xb0a1` (unsigned,
18,212 occurrences in `.text`), while **every** mwcc emits `lis/addi` (signed).
The DOL also contains the string "Please See the ProDG manual" — the game used
SN Systems **ProDG**. dtk's compiler archive ships ProDG 3.5–3.9.3 (`ngccc.exe`,
`cc1.exe`, `cpp.exe`, all GCC 2.95.2-based).

Matching recipe (verified byte-identical on `fn_800034A0`):

```
ngccc -O2 -G0 -mcpu=750 -fno-common -I include ... -c fn.c
```

- **`-G0`** is the critical flag: it disables small-data, so globals use plain
  `@ha/@l` relocations instead of `sda21` — exactly what the original does.
- **Store order matters**: the original was compiled from statements written in
  **ascending address order** of the globals; any other order shifts the register
  allocation and breaks the match (objdiff reloc-diffs catch this).
- `-mcpu=750` / `-fno-common` are codegen-neutral for matched functions but era-
typical; keep them until proven otherwise per-file.
- ProDG version (3.5–3.9.3) did **not** change the instruction stream for
  matched functions; the project is configured on **`ProDG/3.9.3`** (M5.0).
  Detection caveat for cross-clone comparisons: the ngccc build rule in
  `tools/project.py` and the `"ProDG": "ngccc.exe"` map are STOCK
  dtk-template code present in every dtk fork — their presence proves
  nothing. Only a `"mw_version": "ProDG/x.y"` on a GAME-code lib counts
  (e.g. bfbb/ratatouille use ProDG/3.5 solely for the licensed Bink
  library while their game code is mwcc).
  `tools/gen_leaves.py` derives `C_DIR` from configure.py's `mw_version`, so
  the draft sweep always uses the same compiler as the build.

**M5.0 — ProDG/3.9.3 unlocks paired-single (PS), but `-mps-float` is NOT
safe globally.** 3.9.3's `cc1.exe` is "2.95.3 SN BUILD v1.76 for Nintendo
Gamecube" — the only in-tree compiler with the full PS template set
(`ps_muls0`, `ps_merge00/01/10/11`, `ps_sum0/1`, `ps_sel`, `ps_res`,
`ps_rsqrte`, `ps_cmpo0`). PS is emitted from the builtin type `__ps_t` +
`-mps-float` (no intrinsic functions; pointer-cast reinterpretation
`*(__ps_t *)&local` reproduces the game's stfs→psq_l→ps_mr idiom). The
game uses PS pervasively — ~50K instructions in ~895 functions — so it was
built with a PS-capable SN compiler. 3.9.3 is byte-identical to 3.7 for
non-PS code (verified on 110+ functions AND a full rebuild: DOL stays
byte-identical). **BUT `-mps-float` forces 16-byte stack frames whenever an
FPR is saved** (the issue-01 +8 quirk, §4c) — adding it globally broke 14
matched FPR functions, so it stays OUT of `cflags_game`. For a PS function:
`Object(Matching, "fn_X.c", extra_cflags=["-mps-float"])` (appends to
inherited lib cflags; `promote_wip.py` stamps a `// extra_cflags: -mps-float`
marker in the promoted header and `add_gen_leaves.py` turns it into that
Object line — keep the marker when editing promoted PS sources).
**M6.85 — QB script-hash constants (the Ollie question).** The game passes
trick/script names around as opaque u32 QB hashes (`0x9B65D7B8` in 5 drafts
is the hash of `"Ollie"`). `tools/gen_qb_constants.py` builds the hash→name
dict from .prg plaintext, scans src+wip for non-address 8-digit hex
literals, and emits `include/qb_constants.h` — 206 `#define
QB_<NAME> 0xXXXXXXXX` (e.g. `QB_OLLIE`, `QB_TEXTURE`).
`tools/apply_qb_constants.py` sweeps src+wip rewriting the literals and
inserting the include; `fill_wip_drafts.py` postprocess applies the same
substitution so regenerated drafts keep the names. Byte-safe (#defines
expand to identical literals): DOL byte-clean after rebuild (49 promoted
files use constants), 12/12 touched wip drafts compile standalone, sweep
idempotent, `gen --check` stable post-sweep (macro usages keep constants
alive). Masks (`0xFFFFFFFC`), MMIO (`0xCC008000`) and DOL addresses
(0x80000000..0x803FFFFF) are never named `QB_<NAME>` — DOL addresses stay
out of the map entirely; floats/masks/MMIO only appear as `QB_UNKNOWN_0x…`
placeholders (M6.87c), never misnamed. Names are uppercase `QB_`-prefixed;
collisions get `_N` suffixes deterministically. See §5 tools table.
**M6.86 — .qb script names unlock 164 more (206 → 370 defines).** The
compiled QB scripts on the disc (`levels/**/*.qb`, 19 files — mainmenu/level
menus, editor, default) embed plaintext symbol names the .prg binaries
never carried: `LoadTerrain`, `rot_angle` (the `0xED344E1B` in promoted
`fn_8004549C`!), `SkaterInit`, `NodeArray`, `ui_string`, `Obj_MoveToPos`…
`resolve_qb_hashes.build_dict` gained `extra_globs` (defaults add
`levels/*/*.qb`); dict 118,520 → 122,163 hashes. Sweep rewrote 428 literals
across 213 files (12 promoted). Byte-safe: DOL byte-clean after rebuild,
10/10 new-constant drafts compile, sweep idempotent, `gen --check` stable.
Note the 16-bit truncation dead end (NOT extended): with 122k names over
65,536 buckets, unique trunc-matches are pure chance (354 observed vs 343
expected) — 4-digit literals are never hash-named.
**M6.86b — .ngc/.ps2 level data surveyed: 0 new names.** The 89
`.ngc`/`.ps2` files under `levels/**` are geometry/collision/texture
binaries, not name tables: 3,228 printable runs pass the name filter but
1,164 are already-known strings and the rest are binary junk (`A9dVT`,
`AAAAYba`) — hashing the FULL raw set resolves **0** magic constants that
prg+qb didn't already cover. Not wired into the dict (would only add noise).
Remaining ~4,700 unnamed magics are float bit-patterns, masks, or hashes of
strings that don't exist as plaintext anywhere on the disc.
**M6.87 — QB constants expansion (M6.86 continuation): 372 → 3,863
defines, 8,756 literals named across 1,995 files (1,013 promoted).** Three
new dict sources unlocked the magic `0x89E8C244`/`0xCF74F6B7` class
(plan `docs/plans/2026-09-03-qb-constants-expansion.md`): (1) the DOL
`.data 0x80303464` script-command registry (`docs/rodata2-script-

PAL the run filter drops; `resolve_qb_hashes.build_dict` gained `.tsv`

Dict 122,163 → ~245k hashes; DOL `.text` lis+ori resolution 528/3177
(16.6%) → 2,577/3177 (81.1%, `docs/dol-qb-hash-resolved.tsv` regen'd).
Byte-safe: DOL byte-identical after full rebuild (`cmp` + sha1
`ff6faeb0…`), sweep idempotent, `gen --check` stable, 8/8 touched wip
samples compile standalone. `gen_qb_constants.py --check` + an
`apply_qb_constants.py --dry-run` zero-literals check now run WARNING-ONLY

**M6.87a followup — `.rodata2` standalone-word harvest (1 literal).** The
config-flag table at vaddr `0x8029007C` (`CD/NotCD/NoExtraMem/Pal/NTSC/
FrameRate/50/60`) holds the `ScriptSetConfig` param names as NUL-delimited
words; the run-scan filters (min_len 5, all-caps case-shape) dropped
`NTSC`, so `0x86137A88` in `fn_80119094.c` stayed raw. New
`resolve_qb_hashes.merge_dol_tokens` harvests `\0`-delimited letters-only
words (len 2-40; generalized to all DOL data sections in M6.87b) as a
LOWEST-priority gap-fill run AFTER the decoded
archives (so a case-variant duplicate like rodata2 `FAM` vs a script's `fam`
keeps the script spelling — the hash is case-insensitive) → `QB_NTSC
0x86137A88` (+1 define, +1 literal, header/TSV otherwise unchanged).
`0xAF11B50F` stays raw: the string that hashes to it (`NoExtraMemory`) is
absent from the entire disc — the table only has `NoExtraMem`, which hashes
to a different value (`0xECB06BC6`). Proven exhaustively: a sweep hashing
every printable run (2-64) + NUL word in all 18 DOL sections, all 163 pre
archives (raw + fully LZSS-decoded payloads), and every other disc file
finds ZERO strings hashing to `0xAF11B50F` — the name existed only as a
compile-time C++ string constant, never emitted to disc as data. (Later
identified from THPG's debugger table — see M6.87d.)

defines, 30 literals swept).** A disc-wide "does any string hash to each
unnamed literal?" sweep found 45 candidates; occurrence forensics (inside
a decoded `.qb` / DOL section = genuine; `[raw]`-only hits in compressed
streams/media = byte coincidences) confirmed ~21, and four new gap-fill

`ngc_60hz/50hz`, `showmessage`. All four are lowest-priority gap-fills
(never override), which is why the header diff is pure additions. Doc:
`docs/dol-qb-hash-resolved.tsv` 2,577 → 2,587 rows (81.4%). Byte-safe:full rebuild `cmp`-identical, sha1 `ff6faeb0…` unchanged.
**M6.87c — `QB_UNKNOWN_0x<value>` placeholders for every unnamed literal
(3,887 → 5,084 defines, 2,246 literals swept across 923 files).** The 1,197

rebuild `cmp`-identical, sha1 `ff6faeb0…` unchanged; `gen --check` + sweep

**M6.89 — bulk struct detection & application (58,334 sites rewritten
across 6,080 files).** New `tools/detect_structs.py` extracts every
`*(T *)((char *)BASE + 0xNN)` deref site in src + src/wip (~68.8k sites, incl.
bare-decimal offsets and one nesting level), groups them per (file, base) into
14.6k layouts, and merges layouts into **898 shared struct types** by
(offset, width) signature — identical signatures fold into superset classes
(no transitive glue), conflicting-width offsets and alignment-shifting fields
are dropped, unknown file-local typedef casts (`MgrC_t *`) canonicalize to
`void *`/`s32`. Emits `include/structs.h` (~7.3k fields, `unk0xNN`
absolute offsets, `pad0xNN` gaps, ~98% site coverage). `tools/apply_structs.py`
rewrites sites to `((Unk_XXXX *)base)->unkNN` ONLY on exact cast-type match
and byte-verifies every matched src file via `compile_fn` (revert on any
masked mismatch or size drift — caught 5 real `-mps-float` store-order/regalloc
shifts, e.g. fn_801B27F8/fn_801B175C); wip drafts get a compile-sanity check.
Result: 3,058 src files + 3,010 wip drafts rewritten, 12 reverted; full
rebuild sha1-identical `ff6faeb0…`. Re-run order: `detect_structs.py` (header)
then `apply_structs.py --apply`; both deterministic and idempotent (already-
rewritten sites no longer match the raw pattern). WIP regenerations revert to
raw offsets until re-applied.
**M6.89b — address-form (stack) struct pass (3,608 sites rewritten across
475 files).** Extended both tools with the `&BASE` deref family
`*(T *)((char *)&base + 0xNN)` — the stack/static/global-object sites the
pointer pass never matched (locals like `&sp8`, `lbl_*` globals). Layouts are
keyed `('a', base)` so they never vote on pointer-family classes; amp classes
fold into an existing class only on an identical final field map, else append
(31 new `Unk_*` for 4,202 sites, e.g. `Unk_59AB5482` = the dense 16×s32
frame-region layout shared by 414 files, `Unk_E01B0030` = packed RGBA byte
slot). `detect_structs.py --extend` runs the amp family alone against the
frozen cache and appends its typedefs to `structs.h` without rewriting
the pointer section (incremental path for an already-applied corpus). Result:
24 src files byte-verified + 451 wip rewritten, 12 reverted (5 `-mps-float` /
asm-pinned pointer leftovers, 7 wip breaks-compile — no amp-specific reverts);
full rebuild byte-identical.
**M6.89c — direct-form (`BASE + LIT`) & stride-array struct pass (~3,500
sites across ~450 files).** Extended both tools with the direct deref family
`*(T *)(BASE + 0xNN)` (no `(char *)` cast — e.g. `self + 0x18` on `void *`
params and int bases), which was the largest remaining literal family. Its
addend is in units of the base's DECLARED type, so byte offsets are
LIT × element size (1 for int/char/void bases; pointee size for typed
pointers; sites on unknowable pointees are excluded) — `decl_type`/
`base_add_mult` resolve the declaration per (file, base), shared by detection
and apply. `collect_i_layouts` keys them ('i', base); classes fold into an
existing class only on an identical final field map, else append. Also added
the stride form `*(T *)((char *)BASE + ID*W)` with W == sizeof(T) →
`((T *)BASE)[ID]` (array element access, no struct class; e.g.
`((s32 *)lbl_8038E254)[r1]`). Extend/apply now iterate to a fixed point
(`--extend` until `new: 0`, then `--apply`); applied to a committed
already-applied corpus end-to-end: ~150 src files byte-verified + ~300 wip
rewritten across 5 converge waves, all reverts are the known fragile
`-mps-float`/asm-pinned cases; full rebuild byte-identical (`main.dol: OK`).
Deterministic: repeated `--extend` is sha-stable (`31332824…` cache /
`a62daa0b…` header).
**M6.89d — cast-form fallback + majority-width recovery sweep (7,293 extra
sites across ~1,550 files).** Root cause of the remaining raw sites:
7,177 same-offset type-mismatch sites (f32-vs-s32 views of one layout) and
2,588 offset-missing sites (width conflicts dropped class-wide, overlaps,
odd-align). Two changes: (1) width-conflict offsets are no longer dropped —
`collect` keeps the majority (offset,width) vote per layout and
`class_field_types` prefers a naturally-emittable width/type per field, so
conflicted offsets become real members; (2) a new apply-side address-cast
rewrite form `*(T *)&((Unk_XXXX *)BASE)->unkNN` fires on ANY same-offset
site whose field exists, regardless of the site's cast type (byte-safe —
reads/writes a member through a `&`-cast of arbitrary width, incl. the
`(s32)0x0`-style sites). Result: 656 src files byte-verified + 897 wip
rewritten, zero new reverts; odd-align-wide sites that cannot be C members
stay raw. Final leftover pointer-family re-detection added to `--extend`
(55 new classes from sites orphaned by the old width-drop rules);
extend/apply converged to fixed point (`new: 0`) across all families. Full
rebuild byte-identical (`main.dol: OK`); header `7040063a…` / cache
`ffd574b3…` sha-stable across re-extends.
**M6.89d-note (2026-09-23) — a merged class's member type can be WRONG for
the function you are matching; check it before suspecting scheduling.**
`fn_8005B5FC` scored 2.2% because the draft typed its receiver as `CStruct`,
whose `unk0x4`/`unk0x8` are `s32` (majority vote of every site in the
corpus) — so `arg0->unk0x4 = farg0;` became a float→int conversion
(`fctiwz`+`stw`) instead of want's plain `stfs`. Declaring the real
2-field f32 layout (a local typedef mirroring the promoted sibling
`src/fn_8005B65C.c`'s `S5B65C`) took it straight to 100%. Tell: the
compiled code has `fctiwz`/`stw` where want has `stfs`, or `lwz` where want
has `lfs` — `tools/score_body.py` masks nothing about opcode class, so scan
for a float/int class mismatch at the same offset before chasing
register colouring. Shared `Unk_*` classes are merged across the whole
corpus, so a single-site f32 access commonly loses the vote to a majority
s32 view; the function's OWN file is the right place for the true layout.

   **Second instance: `CScreenElement_SetScale` (2026-09-28, 6.02% → 100%)** —
   the mega-merged `Unk_C7387A53` types an `xy` pair as `s32`, so every read
   compiled to the int→float dance instead of `lfs`. A file-local `typedef`
   with real `f32` members fixed it wholesale. Sub-detail: the sub-struct needs
   explicit `char _00[0x2C]` padding, or GCC folds the base pointer away and
   emits `lfs f0,0xd0(r31)` instead of want's `addi r9,r31,0xd0` + `lfs 0x2c(r9)`.
**M6.89e — struct-pointer param retyping (4,258 files, ~21k casts
dropped).** New `tools/type_params.py` turns object params that are only
used through struct casts into typed struct pointers:
`void fn_X(void *arg1) { ((Unk_E80761A5 *)arg1)->unk0x19C |= 0x400; }` →
`void fn_X(Unk_E80761A5 *arg1) { arg1->unk0x19C |= 0x400; }`. Per-param
qualification requires every use to be safe under the new pointer type:
`((Unk_X *)NAME)` cast sites (majority type T), other explicit casts
(`(char *)NAME` / `(s32)NAME`), and benign bare uses (compares, booleans,
call args, assignments/returns); dangerous uses (bare pointer arithmetic or
scaling `NAME+k`/`NAME[k]`/`NAME++` that would re-scale against the new
pointee, `&NAME`, bitwise/shift/divide on the bare value, param
reassignment, and `#define NAME` macro-redirects like the fn_800BB9BC PS
draft) disqualify the param. Retypes are mirrored positionally into
in-file self-prototypes (draft-promotion artifacts — a retyped definition
would otherwise conflict with the stale `s32 fn_X(void *);` decl). Pointer
retyping is codegen-neutral by construction, but every rewritten src file
was still byte-verified per-file via `compile_fn`: 2,485 src verified +
1,773 wip rewritten (incl. `-mps-float` PS files), 0 reverts after the
macro guard. Full rebuild byte-identical (`main.dol: OK`); apply fully
idempotent (re-run finds 0 remaining, decls already `Unk_ *`).
**M6.89f — same retype for function-top LOCALS (5,533 locals / 27.9k casts
dropped / 2,379 files).** `tools/type_params.py` now also retypes locals
that only ever hold struct pointers (`void *temp_r9;` ->
`Unk_F5317C5D *temp_r9;`, `var_r3 = var_r3->unk0x5C;` linked-list walks
included). Locals differ from params: the declaration is discovered by
scanning function-top declaration statements (single declarators only; no
volatile/const/arrays/fn-pointers/`__asm__`), WRITES are allowed (`p =
expr;` — the write target never rescales, only the variable's OWN
arithmetic disqualifies: `p + k`, `p[k]`, `p++`, `&p`, plus `#define p`
macro redirects), and there are no self-prototypes to mirror. Two classifier
subtleties caught in review: (a) `(s32)p_a[2]` — a cast-preceded name is
only safe when no POSTFIX operator directly follows it (`[`/`->`/`.`/`++`
bind tighter than the cast, so `(s32)p_a[2]` subscripts the ORIGINAL `u8*`
byte-wise — fn_8023DE60's p_a/p_b stay raw); (b) GOOD-cast evidence
requires the cast to wrap the name completely (`((T *)NAME)` — `((T
*)NAME->member` casts the MEMBER; counting it flip-flopped fn_80184CD0's
temp_r3 type on re-scan). 701 src files byte-verified + 1,678 wip,
0 reverts; full rebuild byte-identical (`main.dol: OK`); apply idempotent
(re-run finds 0).
**M6.89g — stack-VALUE local retype attempt (1 verified, mostly false
positives — documented so the family isn't re-attempted blindly).**
`tools/type_params.py` also tries retyping address-form bases declared as
narrow scalars (`u16 sp8;` with `((Unk_XXXX *)&sp8)->unk0xNN`) into actual
struct locals (`Unk_XXXX sp8;`), converting `((C *)&s)->unkN` → `s.unkN`,
redundant `((C *)&s)` → `&s`, and whole-value accesses of the original
scalar width → `*((T *)&s)` so they stay exact same-slot accesses. 628
candidates in 422 files (16 src / 406 wip) but the per-file byte gate
destroyed the src set: only **1 of 16 src files verified** (fn_801359DC,
2-align 6-byte struct). The 15 reverts are pure FRAME-LAYOUT drift — the
prologue `stwu` constant grows because the merged amp-region struct
(accesses like `&sp8 + 0x3C` on a 4-byte local) is bigger than the region
retail actually allocated: retail used narrower locals, so the amp-region
"struct" is mostly a false overlay. The 401 wip rewrites are compile-
checked only (drafts aren't byte-checked); 20 files (15 src + 5 wip)
re-verify-fail on every run and stay raw. DOL rebuild: `main.dol: OK`.
**M6.89h — promoted/renamed functions (Script* handlers etc.) now covered;
new void*-retype rule for pointer-evidenced integer params.** The param/
local/stack-value planners locate the function definition by its generated
`fn_ADDR` name only, so the 1,261 promoted files whose definition was
renamed off that prefix (every QB `Script*` command: ScriptSetConfig,
ScriptGetPlatform, ...) were INVISIBLE — their pending `((Unk_X *)arg)`
casts, locals and stack-value sites never planned. `find_definition` now
falls back to a generic `name(params) {` scan (control keywords and fn_
names excluded), and `self_proto_segments` matches by any definition name.
Second gap: m2c drafts type forwarded-but-never-dereferenced args as
integers (`s32 ScriptSetConfig(s32 arg0)` where arg0 only flows into the
still-asm QB getter helpers). New VOID rule in `plan_params`: when a param
has NO struct-cast evidence but IS provably a pointer — explicit
`(void *)arg0`/`(char *)arg0` casts, or a bare pass into a callee position
whose file-local prototype declares it pointer-typed (`fn_801286D0(void *,
...)`) — and every occurrence is safe (integer scalars only: s32/u32/s8/
... never f32), the decl becomes `void *arg0` and redundant pointer casts
drop. Two classifier bugs caught by the byte-gate loop: (1) occurrence
scan now body-only — a param's name inside OTHER functions' prototypes
(`extern s32 fn_X(void *arg0);`) once minted self-referential pointer
evidence and mangled the extern line; (2) `x[NAME]` subscript-INDEX uses
are rejected (an index is an integer role a pointer can't fill — fn_
800F164C's row[arg1]). 581 src files byte-verified + 350 wip rewritten
(struct rule: e.g. ScriptGetPlatform/ScriptGetGoalManager arg1 →
`Unk_B6E8234C *`; void rule: ScriptSetConfig/ScriptSetLoadingBarPos/etc.
arg0 → `void *`); 36 reverts are the known sv frame-drift/PS-fragile set;
no systematic reverter remains. Params with NO in-file pointer evidence
stay s32 (e.g. ScriptObjectExists' name-hash arg0) until the QB getter
helpers propagate their real struct types. DOL rebuild: `main.dol: OK`.
**M6.89i — definition-driven struct propagation: forwarding params become
`Unk_2EF06E12 *` and forward declarations sync to the real signatures.**
The void* stopgap for forwarded args was wrong-headed: ScriptSetConfig's
arg0 IS the QB data block — its deref sites live in the getter family
(fn_801286D0/801289E4/80127F60/801294BC, all promoted as
`Unk_2EF06E12 *arg0`), and every decompiled CALLER only forwards it, so
file-local prototypes (`s32`/`void *` guesses) never named the class. Two
new mechanisms in `tools/type_params.py`: (1) a lazily-built corpus map of
every fn_-named DECOMPILED DEFINITION's per-index param types
(`def_sigs()`) — bare-pass occurrences now vote the callee definition's
class, so `fn_801286D0(arg0,...)` evidence retypes `ScriptSetConfig(arg0`
to `Unk_2EF06E12 *` directly (no deref in the caller needed); iteration to
fixed point walks the forwarding chain (fn_80128228 → fn_80127F60 → ...);
(2) `sync_callee_decls` fixes each caller's extern prototypes of
decompiled callees to the definition's signature (`fn_801286D0(void *,
...)` → `fn_801286D0(Unk_2EF06E12 *, ...)`), restricted to shared-header
Unk_/builtin pointer types, same arity, non-`(void)` decls — the byte gate
caught and the guards now prevent three breakage classes: call-statement
mangles (line-anchored prototype scan), arity-mismatched `(void)` wrappers,
and hand-named struct types (S_80013F94/Big56) not in structs.h;
`ensure_include` inserts the header at the end of the TOP include block
(a stray mid-file #include used to strand it after the first Unk_ use).
Two more integer-role classifier gaps closed: `switch (NAME)` operands and
`x[NAME]` subscript indices disqualify retype (fn_800B48D4/fn_800F164C).
Result: `ScriptSetConfig(Unk_2EF06E12 *arg0)` (its fn_801286D0/289E4/
28228 decls synced), fn_80128228/282E0/284EC/285A4 defs retyped,
ScriptTimeGreaterThan/GetElapsedTime/WaitForEvent/etc. — the whole QB
block-forwarding network. **4,155 files rewritten** (src byte-verified per
file, wip compile-checked), iterated to a fixed point of 57 reverts (33
wip breaks-compile + 24 src mismatch — all sv-frame-drift or noisy-draft
files that were already reverting, incl. fn_800704B4/fn_801626D0);no
new systematic reverter. DOL rebuild: `main.dol: OK`.

**M6.89j — member-type retarget: fields whose EVERY textual use is a
same-width pun get retyped to the pun type (`tools/apply_structs.py
--retarget-types`).** The pun forms `*((T *)&((Unk_X *)B)->unkNN)` that
earlier applies left behind (site cast type ≠ class field type) are only
retargetable when the member is NOT genuinely shared: eligibility requires
a single pun type T, no plain uses (cast form, bare `p->unkNN` on typed
locals/params, `&member` address-of) and same width (T/decl both in the
4/2/1-byte map; volatile/width-changing puns stay raw). Measured corpus:
1,827 pun sites on 417 members, but only **4 members / 16 sites** qualify
(Unk_F6393DBC.unk0x4 s32→f32 + unk0x14 void*→f32, Unk_82779A3F.unk0x5C
void*→f32, Unk_838B6CE3.unk0x4C void*→s32) — the rest of the puns sit on
mega-merged shared classes whose declared type IS the real 4-byte view
(e.g. C7387A53's s32 slots are read as PS pairs by one fn but as scalars /
pointer at 0x154 by byte-verified others, so they must stay). The pass
flips the field in header + frozen cache, rewrites the puns to plain
member access (same-width access at the same offset — codegen-identical
by construction) and byte-verifies each affected src file; un-rewritten
puns still compile (redundant `*((T*)&T-member)`). **8 files / 16 sites, 0
reverts, idempotent.** DOL rebuild: `main.dol: OK`. **Typed-base
extension:** the inline-cast pun form only ever matched `&((Unk_X *)B)`;
members accessed via a *typed* base — `*((T *)&name->unkNN)` with `name`
declared `Unk_X *` — were invisible to the pun scan and their `name->unkNN`
text counted as a plain read, wrongly disqualifying the slot. The pass now
recognizes typed-base puns as pun evidence (class resolved per file through
the decl map; sites blanked from the plain/address-of scans; rewritten to
plain `name->unkNN` only when the base's class is unambiguous in that file
and that exact (class, offset) flipped). Corpus scan: 876 typed-base pun
slots, but the same mega-merged-shared reality holds — e.g.
`Unk_B6E8234C.unk0x18` is pun-cast as f32 (fn_80070570's `stfs` weather
setter) yet stays s32 because byte-verified siblings store pointers
(fn_80077840 `= (s32)lbl_80295768`) and pass it as s32 (fn_8009FE04) — only
**1 member / 1 site** qualified (`Unk_42076946.unk0x14 s32→f32` in the
asm-heavy fn_802415C4). **1 file / 1 site, 0 reverts, idempotent.** DOL
rebuild: `main.dol: OK`.
**M6.89k — arithmetic-tolerant param retyping: `void *`/`char *` params whose
only disqualifier is bare byte-arithmetic get retyped to the struct, with
those sites rewritten to explicit `(char *)NAME`.** The M6.89e/h param rule
rejected `((Unk_X *)arg0)`-only params that also do `arg0 + temp->unk0x20`
(byte-address arithmetic into a struct at runtime — e.g. fn_8005E660's
vtable callback region, Vtable0x803084AC_m4's `arg0 + 4` record walk).
Since `void *`/`char *` arithmetic is byte-based, retyping is safe when each
bare `NAME ± expr`/`NAME`-in-`(char *)`-cast context is re-spelled
`(char *)NAME ± ...` (`char *` params need no fix — `char *` arithmetic is
already byte-based). Guarded against `NAME++`/`NAME--` postfix (would
increment the RETYPED pointer — wrong) and `(cast)NAME` prefixes that are
themselves the only use (cast already wins). Fixes only emit under the
struct-good rule, never for the void/defcls rules. Byte-gated per-file like
M6.89i; isolated pass rate on src: **168/168 verify, 0 failures** (the ~24
combined failures are the pre-existing SV frame-drift set reverting anyway).
Full apply: **168 src verified + 670 wip written**, iterate to fixed point
(0 writes/wave; 58 reverts = the pre-existing fragile set), DOL rebuild:
`main.dol: OK`.
**M6.89l — call-only struct slots retyped to function-pointer members
(`apply_structs.py --fnptr-fields`).** A 4-byte field whose EVERY corpus use
is a cast-call target `((RET (*)(ARGS))SLOT)(...)` (vtbl/handler slots; the
call-only bar mirrors M6.89j) is retyped in header + cache to its
STRICT-majority signature `RET (*)(ARGS)`. Majority sites drop the cast
(`s->fn(args)`); deviant-signature sites keep an explicit fn->fn cast
(legal, codegen-neutral); sites that load the slot into a local first retype
the local (`s32 L;` → `s32 (*L)(void *);`), cast `(s32)` at the load when the
local is a genuinely dual-use s32 (m2c register reuse), or inline single-use
m2c temps. **42 members flipped / 77 files / 132 sites, 0 reverts**; DOL
rebuild `main.dol: OK`; idempotent (re-run finds 0 — flipped decls contain
`(` and majority sites are cast-free). Two correctness details the byte gate
caught: pun-wrapped callees (`*((void **)&M)`) are NEVER rewritten (dropping
the pun changes codegen), and the effective callee of a window is the LAST
member access in its callee zone — chained bases like
`((Unk_X *)a->unkN)->unkM` read `a->unkN` as data, not a call, and only the
outer slot is the call target.
**M6.89m — non-member cast-call cleanup (`apply_structs.py --local-fnptrs`):
fn-ptr locals, int locals holding fn-ptrs, and `(s32)` bridge callees.**
Three families that survive M6.89l because the callee is not a struct slot:

* **A — fn-ptr-declared locals called through a cast.**
  `s32 (*var_r9)(s32, s32, s32);` … `((s32 (*)(void *, void *, void *))var_r9)((char *)arg0 + r, a, b);`
  — the decl's arg list is retyped to the call's actual argument shapes
  (pointer-typed call args become their pointer type via the declared type of
  a bare ident / the inline cast; ints keep their spelling; f32 stays f32 —
  only the GPR/FPR split changes caller codegen, so p/i retypes are
  byte-neutral), every fn-ptr cast feeding the local (decl + load lines) is
  retyped to match, and each call drops its cast: `var_r9((char *)arg0 + r, a, b);`.
  Skip rules: call-arg count ≠ decl-arg count (m2c register-reuse temps,
  `()` old-style decls), or any load-cast whose arity differs.
* **B — int-typed locals that hold a fn pointer.**
  `s32 fp; fp = vt->unk0xC;` … `((void (*)(void *, void *))fp)(a, b);` — when
  every occurrence of the local (masked text, so comments don't disqualify)
  is a call-callee or an assignment LHS `NAME = …;` (RHS content is free — the
  load gets wrapped in an explicit `(RET (*)(ARGS))` cast), the decl is
  retyped to the call signature and the call drops its cast. All call windows
  must agree on the signature. Register-asm dual-use integer registers are
  excluded (they compute addresses AND call — retyping would add casts).
* **C — redundant `(s32)` bridge over a raw scalar member callee.**
  `((s32 (*)(void *))(s32)(p->unk0x3C))(x)` — the bridge is a no-op when the
  member's header field type is already the 4-byte scalar the fn-ptr cast
  loads (s32), so it's dropped to the member-direct spelling
  `((s32 (*)(void *))p->unk0x3C)(x)` used by every other raw member site;
  wider/narrower members keep their bridge (it may be a real widen).

**89 files / 220 sites written, 0 reverts** (4 byte-verified src + 85 inert
wip drafts; DOL rebuild `main.dol` cmp-identical; idempotent — re-run finds
0). The m2c spurious-extra-arg calls (register noise: real call is 1-arg,
draft passes 2) stay untouched — family A's arity check skips them, and
self-arg passes (`f(f, …)`) compile-gate to a revert, so they remain as-is.
**M6.89n — scalar struct slots whose reads are exclusively `Unk_X *`
pointer uses retyped to typed nested-struct pointers
(`apply_structs.py --nested-ptrs`).** A field typed `s32`/`u32`/`int`/`long`
or `void *` whose every corpus occurrence is a wrapping `((Unk_X *)SLOT)`
cast or a load into an `Unk_X *`-typed local (stores must be pointer/null
against a pointer-typed RHS; scalar reads, bare pointer-arg passes, puns,
and address-of uses disqualify) is really a pointer to that nested struct:
the header + cache field is retyped to `Unk_X *`. Because the typedefs are
positional, a member that references a class defined LATER in the header (or
its own class) uses the struct-tag form `struct Unk_X *` (legal C89 — the
reference declares an incomplete tag that the later typedef completes).
Reads were already typed loads/casts from the earlier passes, so the wave is
header/cache-only — no corpus site text needed changing; when future
detection waves reintroduce direct `((Unk_X *)SLOT)` wraps, the apply step
drops them (same 4-byte load, codegen-neutral). **91 members retyped** (incl.
`Unk_838B6CE3.unk0x4C -> Unk_89391A04 *`, the `Unk_C8FEE62D`/`Unk_C7387A53`
big-object slots, vtable-ish `Unk_AA90F24E`/`Unk_2EF06E12` pointer fields,
self-referential list-node slots); DOL rebuild `main.dol` cmp-identical;
idempotent — re-run finds 0.
**M6.89o — absolute-address `lbl_XXXX` externs retyped to their real
scalar type and the `*(T *)&lbl` deref casts dropped
(`apply_structs.py --lbl-types`).** m2c emits `extern char lbl_802FFE54[];`
plus `*(s32 *)&lbl_802FFE54 = 0;` for DOL data globals. A lbl whose EVERY
corpus use is a cast-deref `*(T *)&lbl` of one scalar type (load or store;
no `lbl[i]` indexing, no `&lbl + off` address arithmetic, no array-decay
bare uses in char[]-decl files) gets its decl retyped to `extern T lbl_X;`
and each site becomes a plain `lbl_X` — same address, same load/store
width, codegen-neutral, verified per-file like all applies. Bare value uses
are allowed only in files whose decl is ALREADY the scalar (they keep their
decl; only cast-deref files are retyped). Multi-declarator extern lines,
struct-y casts (`S4`, `sn_ps`, `const u8` tables) and SDA-relative sites
whose sandbox compile can't resolve the symbol are left untouched. **970
lbls retyped / 2,067 sites rewritten across 732 files** (incl. the
`lbl_802FFE54` state globals); DOL rebuild `main.dol` cmp-identical;
idempotent — re-run finds only the 1 unverifiable SDA site. **Value-cast
pass (M6.89o part 2):** the same run also drops redundant identity value
casts `(T)lbl_X` on lbls the file already declares as that exact scalar
(no brackets) — `if ((s32) lbl_80311290 != 0)` → `if (lbl_80311290 != 0)`.
Per-site rule keyed on the file's own decl, so `(s32)lbl_802A83F8` over a
`char[]` decl stays (a real conversion) and bracketed-decl files are
skipped. **417 sites / 246 files** (74 in byte-verified src); byte-gates
hold, DOL still cmp-identical, re-run finds 0.
**M6.89p — definitions extended to the arity callers actually pass
(`tools/fix_fn_args.py`).** A def like `void fn_8001473C(void)` while
retail callers load an argument into r3 before the call means the original
prototype had the parameter and the callee just never reads it (m2c drops
unused leading params, keeping slot-derived names on the rest). When the
corpus's MOST COMMON real call-site arity E exceeds the def arity D (with
E's count strictly dominating every other arity, ≥2 calls at E), the def
is extended to E params — existing params kept verbatim (fn-pointer /
array declarators untouched), appended ones typed per the majority caller
declaration and always named (mwcc rejects anonymous params in
definitions). Unused params emit no code, so src defs stay byte-verified;
caller files are left alone (each already declares exactly what its own
calls pass — Metrowerks rejects arg-count mismatches against an in-scope
prototype). Redundant call-site casts are dropped (identity `(T)x` over a
`T`-typed param, int-casts over address-y operands passed to pointer
params). Variadic-like ties (no dominant arity) and single-stray
high-arity callers are left alone; comments/strings are masked so
`// fn_X(a,b,c)` prose never inflates arity; when a fn exists in both
`src/` and `src/wip/` the byte-verified src copy is the def target and the
wip draft follows via its own-file spans (selfdecl/prototype extensions
stay in the file they were measured in). **463 defs extended across the
corpus** in the first sweep, plus 5 follow-up fixes; every touched src
file byte-verified, DOL rebuild `main.dol` cmp-identical, idempotent —
re-run finds 0.
**M6.87d — THPG debugger name table identifies 574 unknowns, incl.
`0xAF11B50F` (5,084 defines unchanged; 1,394 placeholder renames).** The
PS2/Wii debugger name dump (`debugger_names.dbg`, 8,510 `0x<hash> <name>`
pairs from tcrf.net) uses the SAME Neversoft QB hash — verified 3,401/3,401
agreement with THUG2's disc-derived names and 0/200 sample mismatch. The
list is committed as `docs/thpg-qb-names.tsv` and consumed by new
`resolve_qb_hashes.merge_dbg_names` (LOWEST-priority gap-fill, each pair
re-hash-validated on load — 0 skipped). 574 of the 1,197 `QB_UNKNOWN_0x…`
placeholders get real names: `0xAF11B50F → QB_NOEXTRAMEMORY` (finally — the
name existed only as a compile-time constant; the disc's `NoExtraMem` was a
different value), `0x2B248E4A → QB_LANGUAGE`, `0xAF11B50F`'s siblings
`warn`/`led`, `in3`/`wgt`… `apply_qb_constants.py` gained a placeholder-
rename pass (`qb_hash.subst_qb_placeholders` — same comment/string
discipline, idempotent): `QB_UNKNOWN_0x<val>` refs in src are rewritten to
the new `QB_<NAME>`, so identifying constants later is now a one-shot
gen+apply round-trip with zero churn elsewhere. Docs TSV 2,587 → 2,777
rows (87.4% DOL lis+ori resolution, +190). Byte-safe: full rebuild
`cmp`-identical, sha1 `ff6faeb0…` unchanged.
**M5.0c: 7 PS pair-copy leaves promoted** via `__ps_t` array assignment
(`arg1[0] = arg2[0];` → `psq_l`/`psq_st` — sweep with
`--extra-cflags "-mps-float"`). **M5.0d: +3 larger static-offset copies
(80024668, 800804E4, 801B7A48)** — 8-pair copies and derived
base-pointer copies (`__ps_t *dst = *(__ps_t **)((char *)arg1 + OFF);`
materialized as a local ONCE — inlining the deref per store emits a fresh
`lwz` per store and breaks the match). The frameless static-copy family is
now exhausted (the 8 remaining `mr r9, r3` copies were UNPARKED in **M5.0e**:
an empty `__asm__("" ::: "r3")` clobber after the first copy statement
reproduces the game's dst-pointer copy exactly — the game compiler
modeled PS ops as clobbering r3). **M5.0f: +2 guarded (branch) PS copies
(800BA64C, 8022C778)** — `if (flag) { pairs; }` bodies with mixed
int/`__ps_t` copies match exactly (`beqlr`/`or.` guards included);
800FDD50 parked on an `addi r11,r9,0x10` scheduling artifact. The 11
framed straight-line copies are NOT matchable in plain C: the game built
a stack temp via `stfs`+`psq_l/psq_st` (its `-mps-float` struct-copy
idiom) while 3.9.3 uses direct `stfs`/`lwz,stw`/rodata pair constants.
**M5.0g: +3 framed copies WITH helper calls (800FD4C4, 800FD560,
80024610)** — trailing/leading `bl` + pair copies; the mr-r9 clobber
applies, and the helper call must be OLD-STYLE no-arg (`void f();` +
`f();`) or 3.9.3 adds `crclr cr1eq` + an arg-restore `mr` (game never
does). 800D5AA8 parked on an r6/r7 ABI placement quirk.
All PS arithmetic is unrolled loops (m2c territory). See
`docs/parkings/06-paired-single-ops.md`
§M5.0c–§M5.0g. Remaining PS gap: `ps_muls0`/`ps_merge00`/`ps_sum0` idiom
shapes.

**C vs C++: stay in C — the language policy (verified).** `ngccc.exe` is the
SN ProDG **C++ driver** — it carries BOTH front-ends (`cc1.exe` = C,
`cc1plus.exe` = C++, both GCC 2.95.2-based), and the source extension picks
the language: `.c` → C codegen with unmangled symbols, `.cpp` → C++ codegen
with mangled symbols (verified: `int add(int,int)` compiles to `add` from
`.c`, to `add__Fii` from `.cpp`). The game's engine is C++, yet **every
matched function is a `.c` file, byte-identical** — C reproduces the codegen.
- **Virtual calls are `mtlr`+`blrl`, NOT `mtctr`+`bctrl`.** The game
  dispatches via `lwz rX, off(rY); mtlr rX; blrl` — express it exactly with a
  fn-pointer cast `((s32 (*)(void *, void *))*(s32 *)((char *)obj + OFF))(args)`.
  Scans for `mtctr/bctrl` find nothing; always match on the `mtlr`/`blrl`
  pair. 1070 functions contain memory-fed `blrl` dispatches; 45 are already
  matched in C (e.g. 80009B80, 8000B680). Constructors that install vtables
  (`lis/addi` + `stw` of a static address into the object, e.g. fn_8009E0B0
  at +8) are plain stores — they match in C too.
- **When C++ is actually required** (the small tail, typically <5% in
  SN/GCC-era projects): global ctor/dtor glue (`__sinit_*`, `__ct__`/`__dt__`
  thunks), `operator new`/`delete`, and the genuine stragglers where the
  C++ frontend's implicit `this` handling flips register allocation. Treat
  those **per-function**: the per-object `extra_cflags` mechanism
  (`Object(..., extra_cflags=[...])` / `// extra_cflags:` marker /
  `--extra-cflags`) is the escape hatch — a C++ case would compile THAT one
  object as `.cpp` or with `-x c++` (ngccc accepts both; verified). Never
  switch `cflags_game` globally for it.
- m2c only emits C, so drafts are C by construction — fine, since C is the
  default target language.

`patch_dol.py` is **game-specific** by design: it encodes `R13_BASE`, `BUILT_R2`,
`ORIG_R2`, `SDATA2_START/END`. It fails fast with asserts if the assumptions break.

## 4p. Scheduling/regalloc micro-fixes that flip NEAR→EXACT (M4.66–4.70)

> **M4.93 addition — check the callee signature FIRST.** Issue 10
> ("pure regalloc swap", fn_80201C80) turned out to be a **missing call
> argument**: the draft called `fn_802010FC()` with no args, but the callee
> reads r3 as an object pointer (`mr r30, r3; lwz r0, 0xa9c(r30)`). Passing
> `arg0` extends its live range across the call and flips GCC's
> saved-register allocation to the game's exact mapping — 100% byte-exact,
> promoted. Before parking anything on a "regalloc coin flip", disassemble
> each callee's first ~8 insns and check for `mr rX, r3` + load via `(rX)`.
> See `docs/parkings/solved/10-pure-regalloc-coin-flip.md`. A harvest sweep
> found 107 structurally-matching drafts, but 0 verifiable improvements
> until the compile-FAIL backlog is cleared.
>
> **M4.94 — compile-FAIL backlog cleared (60 → 0).** Added postprocess rules
> to `tools/fill_wip_drafts.py`: (1) dedupe duplicate `static s32 M2C_CARRY
> = 0;` decls, (2) strip m2c's guessed fn-ptr param lists `((s32
> (*)(void *, ...))` → `((s32 (*)())` (they disagree with actual call args),
> (3) fix `(s32 *)((s32)(expr))` and `(char *)A + (s32 *)B` arithmetic,
> (4) two per-address masked-address stragglers. Verified: 0 regressions on
> the ~8665 compiling drafts. **Sweep methodology**: when extracting a draft
> body for compilation, strip `//` comment lines AND `#include` lines — do
> NOT `split('#include')` (leaves a stray string that fails every compile).
> The fixed sweep tests 112 candidates, 4 improved, all with callees that
> provably `mr rX, r3` + load — only inject the arg when that check passes.
> **M4.94b — postprocess rule-ordering fix (code review).** The M4.94
> fn-ptr param-list strip `((s32 (*)(...))` -> `((s32 (*)())` must run
> BEFORE `fix_fptr_proto`, not after: running after undid its
> re-prototyping and reintroduced the spurious `crclr cr1eq` before
> indirect calls (~110 drafts). Also made `fix_fptr_proto` argtype
> inference f32-aware (float args -> `f32`, not `void *`), and fixed two
> latent bugs it had: `.replace(..., 1)` replaced the FIRST occurrence
> instead of the matched one (wrong proto when a function has calls of
> different arity -> "too few arguments"), and the greedy `([^;]*)\);`
> args capture swallowed the rest of the statement (m2c chains calls with
> comma operators on one line) -> now a balanced-paren scan from the
> call's `(`. Verified: all 110 deref-form drafts re-prototyped, 0
> compile failures, DOL byte-identical. **Known gap (not a regression):**
> `fix_fptr_proto` only matches the `(char *)X + (s32)0xN` deref form.
> Var-form calls `((s32 (*)())temp_r9)(args)` (146 drafts) and
> address-base forms `((s32 (*)())*(s32 *)0xADDR)(args)` (23 drafts)
> keep unprototyped calls and still emit `crclr` — they compile fine,
> matching the committed tool's behavior.


All six of these were one-line source restructures that flipped 71–98% NEARs
to 100% EXACT. Check for the diff signature, then apply the fix.

1. **Ternary null-check** — diff `cmpwi rX,0 | li rY,0` (adjacent swap, loop
   head): rewrite `var = NULL; if (x != NULL) { var = x - K; }` as
   `var = (x != NULL) ? x - K : NULL;`. The ternary emits cmpwi-then-li;
   init-then-if emits li-then-cmpwi. (800689D4, 80068A98)

2. **Copy-before-load** — diff `lwz r0, 0xFC(r11) | lwz r0, 0xFC(r30)` (base
   reg differs, same family): move the loop-update copy statement (`var_r30 =
   var_r31;`) to BEFORE the load in source. GCC reorders to load-then-copy
   but keeps r11 as base instead of coalescing onto r30. (800689D4/68A98)

3. **Base-pointer indexed load** — diff `lwzx r11, r9, r0 | add r9,r9,r3;
   lwz r11, 4(r9)`: compute `base = (void **)((char*)arg0 + 4);` as a named
   variable then `x = base[arg3];`. A named base var forces the lwzx indexed
   form; inline `arg0[1 + arg3]` strength-reduces to lwz+add. (80243840)

4. **u8 byte loads** — diff `lbz | lwz` (same offset): change the deref to
   `*(u8 *)`. Preserve the exact statement structure when doing so — a
   rewritten structure (e.g. dropping the temp pointer var) reorders the
   whole function. (8023EEF4)

5. **Extern-symbol base var** — diff `addi r9,r9,-0x57e0; addi r31,r9,0x10 |
   addi r31,r9,0; addi r31,r31,0x10`: materialize the symbol into a SEPARATE
   `char *base = lbl_XXXX;` variable, then `p = base + 0x10;`. The want keeps
   base in r9 and ptr in r31; a single var folds into r31. Always check
   symbols.txt for an existing `lbl_` at the address. (8011BD0C)

6. **Address constant via extern symbol** — diff `addi | ori` on the low half
   of a 0x8xxxxxxx constant: the want is an ADDRESS (lis+addi), the got an
   integer constant (lis+ori). Reference `extern char lbl_XXXX[];` (symbol
   exists in symbols.txt) instead of a bare literal. (800534DC)

**Marker size rule**: always verify the range marker's size against
`config/G2TE52/symbols.txt` (`fn_X = .text:0xX; // size:0xN`) BEFORE promoting.
A wrong size misaligns the split → linked DOL differs → auto-revert. Run
`tools/venv/bin/python tools/check_markers.py` to scan all WIP drafts.
(8023EEF4 & 8011BD0C failed promote once each from bad markers.)

**M5.15/5.16 — prototype & pointer-arith micro-fixes (the 25% push):**

7. **Missing callee prototype** — diff a spurious `crclr cr1eq` immediately
   before a `bl`: the callee is being called via implicit declaration
   (GCC clears CR1EQ before the call). Add a forward declaration with the
   REAL arity — read the callee's arg registers from its first ~8 insns.
   (800A5A20/800A5A60 wrappers → `void fn_800A4C28(s32,s32,s32,s32,s32,
   s32,s32);` — note 800A5A60's 7th arg is `2`, not `1`; 8012D0D8 → the
   callee takes the pointer as an argument, `void *fn_8012B2A0(void *)`,
   NOT `(void)`.) When a standalone compile is 100% but the real build
   reverts, check (a) the range marker size vs symbols.txt and (b) that
   the callee prototype matches what other promoted files declare.
8. **char*-offset vs element-index scaling** — diff `addi rX,rX,0x94` |
   `addi rX,rX,0x250` (stride ×4): the draft indexes with `(s32 *)ptr + n`
   (element arithmetic scales by 4); WANT uses byte offsets. Rewrite with
   `(char *)ptr + n` casts. (8009D208, 8009D2EC/D320, 800F3090 — the
   0x94-byte-stride family.)
9. **Tail store order** — WANT `stw r4,0x2c(r4); stw r4,0x30(r4)`, got
   the reverse: ngccc emits stores in reverse source order, so write the
   LAST-stored field FIRST in source. (800F3090, 800D4D30 — the M4.33
   store-permutation recipe, re-proven.)

**M5.17–5.19 — more micro-fix families (the 25% push, +20 fns):**

10. **Inverted early-return order** — diff `beq|bne` at the branch + where
    the `li r3,0` lands: `if (x == K) return A; return B;` vs
    `if (x != K) return B; return A;` flip which block is fall-through.
    Match the WANT's branch direction (which block is at the bne target).
    (801291FC `== 1 → ptr first`, 8000FA54 `!= 0 → load first`,
    80235CB4 bit-test-true → u16 load.)
11. **u16/u8 typed stores & loads** — diff `sth|stb|lhz|lbz` vs
    `stw|lwz` at the same offset: change the C type (`u16`/`u8`) AND fix
    sibling ops (e.g. `srawi`→`srwi` on the u16 shift comes free).
    (801CD180/1CD1DC u16 pairs, 80240B44 u8 stores, 80235CB4 u16 load.)
12. **Extern symbol MUST exist in symbols.txt** — before referencing
    `extern char lbl_XXXX[]`, grep symbols.txt for the exact symbol.
    A fabricated base (e.g. `lbl_80300000` when only `lbl_80301610`
    exists) compiles standalone (reloc-masked) but the real link fails
    with undefined symbol → the whole promote batch rolls back. Use the
    actual symbol at the target address: `lbl_80301610` directly, not
    `lbl_80300000 + 0x1610`. (80072688/800725B8)
13. **mftb timebase read** — WANT `mftb r3, 0x10c` (TBR 268): inline
    `__asm__("mftb %0" : "=r"(r));` emits it exactly. (80267848)
14. **Ternary returns beat if/return for the cmp+branch+li idiom** —
    `x > 0 ? 1 : 0`, `x == t ? 0 : 1`, `x & mask ? 1 : 0` reproduce the
    game's `li rX,1; bgtlr; li rX,0` shape that a plain `if` inverts.
    (8009138C/8004C840, 80009C84, 8007D454)
15. **char*-offset vs element-index (reprise)** — `(s32 *)ptr + N` scales
    N×4 (0x200 vs WANT 0x80); `(char *)ptr + N` keeps byte offsets. For
    base-plus-index loads use a named `char *p` var first, then
    `*(s32 *)(p + 0x80)` — the temp forces the exact `add`/`lwz` shape.
    (800360B0/C4/D8 family: `arg0 + arg1*0x78` then +0x80.)

**M5.22–5.26 — the missing-arg harvest (crclr sweep + passthrough, +32 fns to 26.47%):**

16. **Callee-proto sweep via WANT crclr check (M5.22, +92 fns).** The
    single highest-yield automation: for every draft, find calls without
    a prototype; if WANT has NO `crclr cr1eq` before the corresponding
    `bl`, inject an arity-matched prototype; keep only fixes that
    compile AND raise match%. Correctness gate: raw hex callee
    addresses must map to `fn_XXXX` names, and prototypes must match
    (never `void` for value-returning callees). 92 drafts hit EXACT in
    one pass. Re-run after every batch that adds callee knowledge.
17. **The missing-leading-arg family (M5.23/5.25, +31 fns).** The most
    common "regalloc coin flip" is actually a dropped argument: the
    draft's call `callee(1)` compiles to `li r3,1` but WANT has
    `li r5,1` / `li r4,1` with no r3/r4 setup — the leading args pass
    through from the wrapper's own params (or from a previous call's
    return value still in r3). Fix: (a) read the CALLEE's prologue to
    count its real params; (b) widen the wrapper signature to receive
    the passthrough params; (c) widen the call + prototype.
    Sub-patterns: `fn_801839F0(arg0, arg1, 1)` 40B wrappers (WANT
    `li r5,1`); `fn_800F0F84(arg0, 1)` (`li r4,1`); const-in-r4 =
    `fn(arg0, const)`; `mr r3,r4` at @0C = unused first param + arg in
    r4; call arg = previous call's return (`fn(ret_of_800F0F84, ...)`).
    VERIFY the caller's setup before assuming param passthrough
    (disasm a caller: `mr r3,r29; lwz r4,8(r1); bl` confirms 2 params).
18. **The field-pass missing-arg (M5.24).** `lwz r3, off(rX); cmpwi
    r3,0; beq; mr r4,rY; bl callee` — the loaded field is callee's
    arg1 (r3 stays set after the compare, GCC only copies rY to r4).
    Widen to `callee(field, rY)` with 2-arg proto. If GOT instead
    loads into r0, that's the smoking gun: GCC used r0 because the
    field is NOT needed by the (too-narrow) call. (8012F2D8 →
    `fn_80128ACC(field, arg1)` ×2 sites.)
19. **Bit-array set fns (M5.25).** `*(s32 *)((char *)base + idx) |= 1
    << n` with byte index: the s32* element form emits `slwi r11,r11,2`
    + `lwzx` with base/index swapped; the char* form emits the WANT's
    `lwzx r9, r8, r11` directly. Near-twin check: compare base offsets
    (801A6CF8 arg0+4 vs 801A700C arg0+0x2A4 — not identical!).
20. **Missing-proto pitfall on rewrite (M5.26).** When regenerating a
    verified EXACT body by hand, keep ALL callee prototypes — dropping
    one makes the call implicit (crclr cr1eq) → promote REFUSEs
    "NOT byte-exact" and rolls back silently (the first run printed
    "promoted" then vanished from src/). If src/fn_ is missing after a
    promote, re-check the draft body, not the build.

**M5.90–5.96 — the fn-ptr/lbl/order micro-fixes (the 30% push, +13 fns to
30.015%):**

21. **Unprototyped fn-ptr calls keep the crclr+mtlr/blrl form.** WANT has
    `crclr cr1eq` (or `crclr cr1eq` before an indirect call) — write the
    call UNPROTOTYPED: `(*(s32 (**)())lbl_XXXX)(args)` (or
    `(*(s32 (**)())*(s32 *)0xADDR)(args)` for a hard address). A
    prototyped cast `((s32 (*)(s32, s32, ...))...)` makes ngccc omit the
    crclr and the bytes diverge. This is the flip side of item 16
    (prototype ONLY when WANT has NO crclr before the call).
    (8001B658, 8001B838 — `crclr cr1eq; mtlr rX; blrl` wrappers.)
22. **Extern lbl symbols force the lis+addi address form.** Diff `addi |
    ori` on the low half of a constant: an ADDRESS (0x8xxxxxxx, e.g. a
    vtable) is materialized as `lis+addi` (signed @ha/@l) while a bare
    integer literal becomes `lis+ori`. Reference
    `extern char lbl_XXXX[];` (symbol MUST exist in symbols.txt, item 12)
    and pass/assign `(s32)lbl_XXXX` — never the raw literal.
    (8001B658/8001B838 → fn-ptr table `lbl_80300178`; 8001B658 →
    string arg `lbl_80290E68`; 80098DF8 → `lbl_8037B7E8`; 801EFC18 →
    vtable store `lbl_802ADE98`; 80014B40 → `lbl_80290A70`.)
23. **Chained calls: the second call's r3 is the first call's return.**
    WANT `bl fnA` then `bl fnB` with NO `li/mr` r3 setup between them:
    write `fnB(fnA(...), ...)` as ONE expression — separate
    statements make GCC discard the intermediate value and load a fresh
    constant into r3. (800F0610 → `fn_800F05C0(fn_800F0F84(arg0, 1),
    arg1)`; 8007D584 → `fn_8007D474(fn_80009A44(0x28), arg0, arg1)`.)
    Callee's return type must be non-void for the chain to keep r3 live.
24. **ngccc emits stores in REVERSE source order.** Write stores in the
    OPPOSITE order of WANT's output sequence (same rule as items 9 and the
    §4b "store order" note): 801EFC18 source (0x24, 0x4, 0x1E8) → output
    (0x1E8, 0x4, 0x24) — a true reversal; 80014B40's ascending source
    (0x80, 0x84, 0x88) matched exactly. When a tail of const/zero/lbl
    stores is in the wrong order, reverse the source statements.
25. **arg0 pass-through to a wider callee.** WANT shows the callee called
    with MORE args than the draft's call, and the extra leading arg is
    the wrapper's own first param (r3 untouched — no `li/mr r3` setup
    before `bl`): read the CALLEE's prologue (`mr rX, r3` + loads), widen
    the wrapper signature to receive the passthrough param, and pass it
    through. Distinct from item 17 (passthrough of CONSTANTS): here the
    arg is the wrapper's own arg0, so r3 survives the call naturally.
    (8010F130 → `fn_801280E0((void *)arg0, 0, &sp8, 0)` — 4-arg callee,
    arg0 pass-through + a stack temp.)
26. **Save-order flip in the CALLER's prologue = a "no-arg" call is
    actually taking arg0.** WANT and GOT agree on everything except the
    saved-register order at the top (`mr r31, r3; mr r30, r4` in WANT vs
    `mr r30, r4; mr r31, r3` in GOT): the FIRST call in the body that
    LOOKS like a no-arg call (`bl fnX` with no li/mr setup) really takes
    the wrapper's arg0 — the callee's prologue does `mr rX, r3` + loads,
    so passing arg0 extends its live range and flips ngccc's allocator.
    Verify via the CALLEE's first 8 instructions, then add `(arg0)` to
    that call. (801F83E8/801F9594 → fn_801F8B94/fn_801F8BD4/fn_801FC11C;
    80243F88/802448E4 → fn_80243FC8/fn_80245570; also 801B0240,    whose 4-arg signature leaves arg1 genuinely UNUSED — prologue saves only
    r3/r5/r6 — so keep the full signature; do NOT "simplify" it to 3
    args, it would break the build.)
27. **Declaring a float-RETURNING callee kills the crclr/crset before `bl`.**
    GOT emits `crclr cr1eq` (or `crset cr1eq`) before a call but WANT has
    nothing — per SN convention a float-returning callee manages cr1eq
    itself, so declaring the callee `f32 fn_X(f32);` (float return) makes
    ngccc drop the cr-setup while an `s32`/`void` return keeps it. The
    float ARG form (`f32 fn_X(f32)`) is what suppresses it — even when the
    callee's own asm ends with `li r3, 1` (int-looking). Also: a missing
    prototype for ANY callee emits crclr (item 16), so try (a) adding the
    proto, then (b) switching its return type to f32. (8011D4F8,
    8011D440, 8011C0B0 — audio-sys call family.)
28. **`volatile double _dummy;` forces the +8-byte stack frame.** When WANT
    has a 0x18 frame and GOT a 0x10, declare a `volatile double _dummy;`
    local — GCC 2.95 keeps a spare 8-byte slot (same quirk family as the
    FPR-frame issue-01, §4c). Combine with item 27 for call-only functions
    that need both the f32-ret proto AND the bigger frame. (8011D4F8 —
    both fixes together hit 100%.)
29. **Split a large displacement to force an independent `li` between
    `addis`/`addi`.** WANT `addis r9,r3,1; li r11,X; addi r9,r9,LO` but
    GOT groups the address pair (`addis; addi; li`): write the base as
    two statements (`p = base+0x10000; li-equivalent here; p += 0x3C94`)
    so the constant materializes between the two halves with zero size
    change (same 2 address insns). (8023590C — 92.86%→100%; file-local
    0x18-byte copy struct also replaced the `Unk_DB0E2BAB` casts.)

## 4s — return-boolean polarity (M6.23)
For `return callee() != 0;` style wrappers, ngccc 3.7 materializes `li r3,1; bne; li r3,0`
(1 first). When WANT shows `li r3,0; beq; li r3,1` (0 first), the original source used the
explicit if/else form:
```c
if (callee() == 0) { return 0; } else { return 1; }
```
All ternary/boolean/negation variants emit 1-first; only the explicit if/else flips it.
Verified on 800D5304, 800D5334, 800D5838, 801CDD84 (identical 0x30 bodies).

### 4s2 — the bool typedef conversion (M8.x) and the return-type-token trap
`Script*` handlers in the retail C++ source returned `bool`; the decomp's C mirror of a
bool return is `typedef int bool` in `include/types.h` (NOT an enum: ngccc types
`enum { false, true } bool` as *unsigned* (no negative enumerators → GCC convention),
so `b >> 1`/`b / 3`/`b > -1` flip codegen; and NOT `char`: PPC plain char is unsigned,
and 1-byte arithmetic inserts `extsb`/byte-store codegen the original doesn't have).
With `bool == int == s32` under types.h, retyping matched `s32 Script*` functions to
`bool` + `return 1/0;` → `return true/false;` is generally byte-invisible — a mass
retyping of ~950 Script* defs verified byte-identical end to end, EXCEPT one shape:

`return var != 0 ? callee((void *)var) : 1;` — a call in a ternary arm, with the
condition on a call-chained local. Under `s32` (typedef `signed int`) the schedule
is `mr. r0,r3; li r3,1; beq; mr r3,r0; bl` (1 hoisted before the branch); under the
`bool` token the same source emits `mr. r3,r3; beq; bl; b; li r3,1` (call first, 1 in
the far tail) — different bytes, same 100B function length. Generic matrix probes
(`return x != 0 ? c() : 1;` on a plain param) show s32/bool/B2 typedefs identical and
only *native* `int` returning a different schedule, so this is shape-triggered, not
consistent; the only safe rule is: **retyping a matched function's return type is a
real codegen event — rebuild the DOL (not just the unit) after any bulk retyping and
protect byte-identity with the `ok` hash check**; `fn_80220B44` keeps its `s32` token
for exactly this reason.
Semantics note for struct layouts: the original C++ `bool` was 1 byte in *fields*, so
a matched struct that mirrors a C++ `bool` member must declare it as an explicit
byte-width type (`s8`/`Unk_*`), never via this 4-byte typedef. Register/arg/return
positions are size-agnostic (word in r3), so bool-typed call signatures match fine.

Game *globals* that are C++ `bool` (ProDG C++ `bool` = 4 bytes in the original — the
promoted "global bool" leaf idiom is `lwz`+`cmpwi`, never `lbz`) are typed
`extern bool lbl_*;` for the ~253 declarations whose scalar uses are provably 0/1
(option-flag cluster `lbl_802FFE40`–`lbl_802FFE68` etc.). Two rules when doing this:
  - only retype between 4-byte forms (`s32`/`u32` ↔ `bool`) — `char`/`u8` declarations
    lbz/sb codegen and are NOT retypeable; array decls must keep the `[]` suffix
    (`*(s32 *)lbl_X` cast-decay sites break if the decl is scalared);
  - only touch ngccc-compiled TUs: the Dolphin-SDK ISR files (fn_8025EFD4 family,
    `mwcc_sjis` rule) are mwcc `-lang=c`, where the `bool` token is rejected
    ("';' expected"). Restrict any mass type sweep by the build.ninja rule name.

### 4s3 — m2c pointer/label noise: retype declarations, never cast call sites

The m2c bulk-fill left ~12k "passing arg N of `F` makes pointer from integer" /
"assignment makes pointer/integer" / "incompatible pointer" warnings in promoted
sources (present at HEAD since the m2c era; the DOL matches through them — they
are warnings, not the blocker). Root cause: m2c degrades C++ types to
`s32`/`char[]` stand-ins, so struct-pointer values flow through int-typed
declarations. Fire-hose casting at call sites (~7k `(Type)` inserts) was tried
and reverted — proper fix is to retype the DECLARATIONS so sites type-check
naturally, verified per-file by .o byte-equality (recompile with the exact
ninja ngccc flags incl. objcopy/fix_fp_pool, revert on any byte diff):

  - Proto pass (caller params/locals): the wave arg is often a plain
    `arg1`/`temp_r30` whose enclosing fn declares it `s32` while the callee's
    param is `CStruct *`/`Unk_xxx *`/`void *`. Retype the def's param token
    AND the file-local typeless sub-prototype `void fn_X(s32, s32);` to match
    (conflicting types otherwise). Verified ~31 TUs; big waves needed the
    label pass below — deeper param/locas staged for later.
  - Label canonicalization pass: wave labels (args of the CStruct-family
    helpers AddInteger/AddString/GetChecksum_*/GetInteger/... and friends)
    are pointer-object globals in the original — audit says bare value-loads
    dominate (++struct-decay patterns ~0), so declar them
    `extern TYPE *lbl_X;` ( choosing TYPE from the most specific existing
    typed decl `Unk_yyyy *`/`CStruct *`, else the callee param type).
    Replaces fuzzy per-TU `extern s32 lbl_X;`/`extern char lbl_X[];` decls;
    `*(s32 *)&lbl_X` value-read stand-ins equal a bare label load (`lwz`),
    so stripping them at arg sites is codegen-identical. 181 TUs / 258 decls
    verified byte-exact in the first sweep.
  - Deferred long tail: TUs where a label's use class is MIXED (array indexing
    `lbl[i]`, `&lbl` address-of, arithmetic, or both value and struct-object
    shapes) — those need a per-label manual audit; 295 TUs + 45 reverted TUs
    fell out of the first sweep. Labels used both as pointer-object and as
    struct-object across files need their use sites split per TU
    (separate externs per TU are fine — each TU's .o only sees its own decl).
  - Tools entry points live in /tmp scratch only (one-off nature); the
    reusable pattern is per-TU: edit DECL, recompile, byte-cmp .o, revert.



### 4t. Chained-return fills r3 across calls (no save slot)

Pattern: two back-to-back calls where the SECOND call's r3 is never set in the
function body — e.g. `bl fn_a; bl fn_b` with only r4..r6 set before `bl fn_b`.
The C is `fn_b(fn_a(), x)` — r3 flows straight from fn_a's return into fn_b's
arg0, so GCC needs no callee-saved register and no `mr` at all. m2c drafts
collapse this to `fn_b(x)` (dropping the chained arg) AND declare the second
callee's proto 1 arg short, which shifts ALL call args down one register and
breaks the whole function. When the game's asm shows the second call setting
r4/r5 but not r3, try `fn_b(fn_a(), r4val)`. Corollary: if a call sets r4..r6
but r3 is the function's own incoming arg that's live only across that one
call, it's a plain arg0 pass-through (`fn(arg0, ...)`) — same as 4p, but with
no save slot because arg0 dies right after the call.

Verified M6.30: 80234D60, 801890DC (chained); 80176EE0 (arg0 through 2 calls).

## 5. tools/ inventory

**Tools hygiene (the default that makes the rest of this unnecessary):**
`tools/` must stay a curated set of documented, reusable tools. **One-off
debug scripts and temporary files go in `/tmp/` — never in `tools/`, and
never in the repo root either** (`tmp_*.py` at the project root is the same
violation; M8.14 swept 51 strays that had been committed via `git add -A`
before batch-end cleanup). Write them as `/tmp/<name>.py` from the start;
if a probe MUST live inside the repo for a tool to reach it (e.g. write_file
paths resolve against the project root), create it under a throwaway dir,
delete it in the SAME command that commits, and never `git add -A` while a
probe exists. Examples of things that belong in `/tmp/`:
ad-hoc disasm/compile probes, single-address experiments, throwaway
`verify_*.sh`/`commit*.sh`, bucket/list scripts that were superseded by a
better tool, and any output files (logs, dumps, generated C) you only need
for the current round. **Caveat:** this sandbox's `/tmp` is wiped on
restart, so nothing you want to keep may live there — anything that proved
genuinely reusable must be promoted into `tools/` **and** added to the table
below (with a purpose description) before the round ends. Two rules of
thumb: (1) if you're not sure you'll need it next round, it's `/tmp`;
(2) if it earns its place twice, it's `tools/`.

**Backstop cleanup (only if something slipped into `tools/`):** one-offs
have recognizable naming: `dbg_*`, `dump_*`, `check_*`, `inspect*`,
`body*`, `leaf*`, `raw*`, `re_*`, `iso*`, `log_*`/`perstep`/`trace`-style
tracers, `test_<family>.py` pattern validations, one-off
`commit*.sh`/`verify_*.sh`, `park_*`, `scan_*`/`survey_*` discovery scripts
that were superseded. Reuse `tools/cleanup_oneoffs.sh` (it encodes the
current keep-list and re-verifies every doc-referenced tool still exists) or
delete by hand with this policy. Keep: everything in the table below, the
re-sweep pipeline (`sweep3.sh`, `promote3.sh`), the FAIL-round tooling
(`verify5.py`, `verify36.py`, `bucket_fail5.py`, `bucket_fail6.py`,
`trace_rules.py`, `bisect_rules.py`, `iso_chunk31.py`), the tail-repair
tools (`errlines.py`, `repair_tail.py`, `fix_tail2.py`), and generic
utilities (`vtest.py`, `disasm.py`, `cmp_dols.py`).

Always validate a sweep with a positive control (strip a known pin, confirm it is rediscovered) — a `"rr26"`-style template bug once made every variant a silent compile FAIL and the tool reported 0 wins |

drops any redundant wraps; see M6.89n** **M6.89o `--lbl-types`: retypes `extern lbl_XXXX` globals whose every use is a single-scalar `*(T *)&lbl` cast-deref to `extern T lbl_X;` and drops the casts (same address, same width — codegen-neutral); excludes indexed / `&lbl + off` address-arithmetic / array-decay-in-char[]-file uses and multi-declarator lines; bare value uses allowed only with an already-scalar decl; also drops redundant identity value-casts `(T)lbl_X` on lbls the file already declares as that exact scalar (real conversions over char[]-decls stay); For each param/local whose every use is safe under a struct pointer — `((Unk_X *)NAME)` cast sites (majority type T; evidence requires the cast to wrap NAME completely), other explicit casts incl. `(void *)NAME`/`(char *)NAME` (safe, pointer evidence), benign bare uses (compares, booleans, call args, assignments/returns), and for locals plain writes (`p = expr;`) — retypes the decl to `T *NAME` and drops the redundant `((T *)NAME)` casts; dangerous uses disqualify (bare pointer arithmetic/scaling `NAME+k`/`NAME[k]`/`NAME++`, `&NAME`, bitwise/shift ops, param reassignment, subscript-INDEX use `x[NAME]`, `switch (NAME)` operand, postfix ops directly on a cast-preceded name — `(s32)NAME[k]` subscripts the ORIGINAL byte pointer — macro-redefined names). **Arithmetic-tolerant rule (M6.89k):** when the ONLY disqualifier is bare `NAME ± expr` byte-arithmetic on a `void *`/`char *` param, retype anyway and re-spell those sites `(char *)NAME ± ...` (byte-based either way; `NAME++`/`NAME--` still disqualify — they'd advance the retyped pointer). Occurrences are scanned BODY-only (names inside other functions' prototypes never count). **Evidence hierarchy for bare passes**: (1) the callee's DECOMPILED DEFINITION signature (corpus `def_sigs()` map) — an `Unk_X *` position retypes the param to that class directly (`ScriptSetConfig` arg0 → `Unk_2EF06E12 *`, the QB data block; iteration walks forwarding chains); (2) `void rule`: file-local pointer-typed prototype positions / explicit pointer casts with no class → `void *`. **Callee-decl sync** fixes each caller's extern prototypes of decompiled callees to the definition's real signature (`fn_801286D0(void *, ...)` → `fn_801286D0(Unk_2EF06E12 *, ...)`) — restricted to shared-header Unk_/builtin pointer types, matching arity, non-`(void)` decls, found via a line-anchored scan (calls are never prototypes). Locals are discovered from function-top single-declarator statements (no volatile/const/arrays/fn-ptrs/asm). Param retypes are mirrored positionally into in-file self-prototypes. Byte-safe by construction (pure type-level change); matched `src/fn_*.c` files byte-verified per-file via `compile_fn` (revert on any mismatch), wip drafts compile-checked. Stack-value locals (M6.89g): narrow scalar decls whose ADDRESS is cast to a struct (`u16 sp8` + `((Unk_XXXX *)&sp8)->unkN`) retype to `Unk_XXXX sp8;` with `((C *)&s)->unkN` → `s.unkN`, `((C *)&s)` → `&s`, and whole-value accesses → `*((T *)&s)`; NOTE the per-file byte gate reverts most of these (frame-layout drift — the merged amp regions are usually overlays of narrower retail locals; 1/16 src verified, see M6.89g). `--dry-run` / `--apply` / `--jobs N` / `--limit N` / `--plan-file <path>`.
