273. **A systematic one-register coloring shift means the draft has MORE
     temporaries than the original — delete them, don't pin.** fn_800094D0
     (case-insensitive strstr) was parked at 38/58 behind a hand-tuned goto
     skeleton with explicit lowering temps (`s8 n0/hl2/ns/h` +
     `(u32)(c-0x41)<=0x19U` staged as statements): every home came out one
     slot off (want r6 vs got r7 down the line) and the inner load fused to
     `extsb r11,r0` where want has `extsb r0,r0` + `mr r11,r0`. The natural
     form — `LowerCh(c)` ternary macro (`c>='A' && c<='Z' ? c+0x20 : c`)
     applied at each use site, plain nested `while(1)` loops, one
     `register` on the first variable — went 58/58 first try: GCC folds the
     range test into want's `addi; cmplwi` idiom itself, and fewer named
     webs let the allocator color exactly like retail (birth copy included).
     Rule: when the residual is a *uniform* coloring shift with no calls in
     the function (not doc-15), the original had fewer temporaries than
     your draft — inline the computed values back to use sites before
     reaching for pins, barriers, or decl-order permutations. (Only
     adaptation needed: C89 declarations at the top; ngccc rejects
     mid-function decls.)

274. **The recipe-249/264 constant-store leaf: `return arg0;` ALSO rotates the
     store stream, and the FIRST source statement picks the zero-register
     count.** Random-batch sweep 2026-09-16 promoted five of these
     (fn_80016EAC/16EC4 via the array-of-structs spelling instead, plus
     fn_80099428, fn_80009CF4, fn_80010A38). Mechanics that matter:
     * With `void *fn(void *arg0)` + `return arg0;` the constant stores are
       emitted as `emit[i] = source[i-1]` — the LAST source statement is
       emitted FIRST and the rest follow in order. So write the source list
       as want ROTATED LEFT BY ONE (fn_80099428: source
       [0x04,0x5C,0x5E,0x58,8,0x1C,0x20,0x30,0x68,0x6C,0x00] -> want's
       [0x00,0x04,0x5C,...]). The rotation is only exactly that for a UNIFORM
       stream: mixing in an `lfs`/`lis` store or a bitfield op changes it
       (fn_80010A38's label store moves to position 1 instead).
     * When no single source order obviously lands, run a full permutation
       search: 6! = 720 variants at 12 workers (`tools/score_body.py` under
       `xargs -P`, each worker its own LEAF_TMPDIR) costs ~130s, so 6-8 store
       bodies are searchable outright. That is how fn_80010A38 (8.3% -> 100%)
       was solved — the layout was already right, only the order was not.
     * The first source statement decides the zero-register COUNT. Starting
       with a plain word zero-store materialises ONE zero register reused by
       every later store (and by any `rlwimi` that needs a zero source);
       starting with a bitfield op, an `sth`, or with the stores in rotated
       order splits it into two `li`s and adds a word (fn_80026AEC). If a
       rotation-corrected source makes the function one instruction LONGER,
       that is what happened — do not chase it further, park on it.
     * DELAYED BASE MATERIALIZATION: for a second base `r9 = r10 + K` where
       want emits a store BEFORE the `addi`, declare the pointer
       UNINITIALIZED and assign it as a STATEMENT after that store. Every
       form that initialises it in the declaration hoists the `addi` above
       the store (fn_80009CF4: `T9CF4P *p;` then `o->unk0x04 = 0;` then
       `p = (T9CF4P *)((char *)arg0 + 8);` was the last 2 words).

275. **A bitfield word is identified by `rlwimi rX,rZero,SH,MB,ME` + a
     neighbouring single-bit `rlwinm` + an `sth` on the same word.**
     fn_801252BC (promoted) and fn_80026AEC / fn_8002CB04 (layouts fully
     decoded, parked on store order) all decode as one of
         struct { u32 f0:16; u32 f1:1; u32 f2:8; u32 f3:7; }   // 0x38
         struct { u32 f0:13; u32 f1:1; u32 f2:1; u32 f3:17; } // 0x168
     The tells: (a) the `sth` is a 16-BIT FIELD assignment (GCC emits a
     halfword store when the field is halfword-aligned and the rest of the
     word is untouched) — do not model it as a separate `s16` field; (b) an
     `rlwimi` whose source is the zero web (not a `rlwinm`) means the source
     assigned a VALUE to that field, and its SH encodes the field's position
     (SH = 32 - MSBposition); (c) the trailing `rlwinm rX,rX,0,MB,ME` with
     MB>ME clears exactly ONE bit — the field between the other two. Writing
     the word as a bitfield struct reproduces every one of those words
     byte-exact on the first try, which reduces these functions to a pure
     store-order search.

276. **`mr rN, r3` where the object stays live across a later load: the branch
     polarity picks the layout, not the allocator.** fn_80011F20
     (pop-list-front, promoted) was 7.7% as `if (n == 0) return 0;` and 100%
     with `if (n != 0) { s32 off = lbl; o->0x84 = n->next; n->next = o;
     return (char *)n + off; } return 0;` — recipe 259's positive-test form.
     The `lis`+`lwz` of the global must be materialised into a local BEFORE
     the two stores (want emits it ahead of them) even though the value is
     only consumed by the final `add`; that is also what keeps the object in
     r10 instead of r3.

277. **HAZARD: the masked score CANNOT see a wrong label address — always
     trust `promote_wip.py`'s linked-DOL compare, never a 100% sweep row.**
     The @ha/@l words of a `lis`+`addi` label access are masked by
     `gen_leaves.compile_fn` (R_PPC_ADDR16_HA/LO -> 0xFFFF0000 on the `lis`
     word and the whole `addi`), so an `extern char lbl_X[];` pointing at the
     WRONG address still scores 100% masked.  fn_800A5D90 (2026-09-16) scored
     EXACT with `lbl_802A80C8` but `promote_wip.py` rejected it: want's
     `lis r11,0x802A` + `addi r11,r11,-0x7F38` is the HIGH-ADJUSTED pair for
     **0x802980C8** (0x802A0000 - 0x7F38 = 0x802980C8), and the linked DOL
     differed by one byte in the `lis` immediate (`3d60802a` vs `3d60802b`).
     Rule: decode `lis`+`addi` by ADDING the signed displacement to the
     lis value first, then look that address up in `symbols.txt` — capstone's
     printed `-0x7f38` is the already-adjusted displacement, not an offset you
     can eyeball onto the lis page.

278. **HAZARD (cost me two fake 100% rows): never let parallel variants share
     ONE temp body path.** `score_body.py` protects the *object* file with a
     per-PID `LEAF_TMPDIR`, but the *input* path is whatever you passed — so a
     fan-out that writes every neighbour of a search round to the same
     `fn_ADDR_n.c` lets workers read each other's body. fn_80137BA4 and
     fn_80137BD8 both "solved" at 100.0% in the same round and re-scored
     84.6% / 71.4% when the file was left alone. Rule: name each candidate by a
     hash of its own content/order (`md5(str(order))[:12]`), and re-score the
     FINAL body standalone before believing it (then `promote_wip.py`, which
     recompiles from the draft anyway).

279. **HAZARD: `tools/want_vs_got.py` ignores a file argument** — it always
     reads `src/wip/fn_ADDR.c`. Passing a variant path silently diffs the
     stale parked draft, which is how a whole family got mis-diagnosed as
     "GCC will not emit `mr r11,r3`" (the diff was of the old m2c body, and the
     copy was in the variant all along). Use **`tools/want_got.py`** (added
     2026-09-25, same in-process recipe, now a real tool) when the body is not
     in `src/wip/`: `tools/venv/bin/python tools/want_got.py 0xADDR
     --file /tmp/variant.c`. It honours the draft's own `// FLAG:` line
     (filtered with `gen_leaves.FLAG_TOKEN_RE`) and auto-adds `-mps-float` for
     `__ps_t` bodies, but it does NOT do the `volatile double _dummy;`
     dual-test, so take the official verdict from `test_wip_drafts.py`.

280. **The store-leaf family needs a permutation SEARCH, not the 8-variant
     rotation sweep.** 2026-09-16 batch promoted 9: fn_80013D78, fn_8001621C,
     fn_80137B74, fn_80137BA4, fn_80137BD8, fn_801394E0, fn_8005EAF4,
     fn_8002DD70, fn_800DB364 — and SIX of them were found by plateau-walking
     the store order (swap two statements, or cut one and re-insert it
     anywhere), never by the rotation table. Practical recipe:
       * seed with want's own emit order (m2c drafts already carry it) or with
         ascending offsets — both are often 1-3 words away;
       * evaluate 40-45 neighbours in parallel per round, accept moves with
         pct >= best (sideways moves are what escapes the ordering plateaus),
         budget ~40 rounds / ~1000 distinct orders per function;
       * each eval is a fresh subprocess `score_body.py` (~0.3 s), so a round
         costs ~1.5 s of wall time at 14 workers.
   80013D78 went 42.9 -> 100 in ONE such round; 8001621C 47.1 -> 100 in six.

281. **Always try BOTH heads when an order search stalls one word short.**
     The same constructor shape appears twice: `void *f(void *o){T*p=o;...
     return o;}` (base copy in rN, `lis` emitted FIRST, label in a second
     register) and plain `void f(void *o)` (base stays r3, no copy, label in
     rN). fn_8002DD70 and fn_800DB364 only match with the **void** head;
     fn_80137B74 / fn_80013D78 / fn_8001621C / fn_8005EAF4 only with the
     `return arg0` head. If a search tops out at (n-1)/n words, re-run it on
     the other head before writing any park note.

282. **Sub-object constructors: two extra mechanics that decide the match.**
     * A `q = (TQ *)((char *)o + K)` sub-base must be DECLARED UNINITIALISED and
       ASSIGNED AS A STATEMENT after the store that precedes want's `addi`
       (fn_8005EAF4: after the `+0x04` store; fn_800A32C0: after the `+0x2C`
       store). Recipe 274's delayed-base rule generalises to every one of these.
     * A repeated `-0x80` written to four adjacent `s8` fields (`stb r0,0x18`,
       then `stb r0,1/2/3(rQ)`) is ONE shared `li r0,-0x80` web: model the
       fields as `s8` and the constant as `-0x80`, and the four bytes plus the
       single `li` fall out for free (fn_8005EAF4, 82.4 -> 100).
     * Parked sibling fn_800A32C0 (88.9%, 16/18 words) is the counter-example:
       want interleaves `q`'s two self-stores `stw r9,0xc(r9); stw r9,0x10(r9)`
       and ngccc always hoists the `p+0x1c` zero store between them — 36
       pairwise swaps, all 24 tail-window permutations, 4 head spellings and
       953 randomised orders could not move it, so write the park note with
       the exact two-word diff instead of burning more search rounds.

283. **HAZARD: a masked 100% cannot see the GUARD'S EXTENT — a store or call
     that belongs inside vs outside the `if` emits the SAME words with a
     different `bne` displacement.** Two instances in one session
     (2026-09-22), both scored EXACT 100% masked and both refused by
     `promote_wip.py` ("internal branch target(s) differ"):
     * fn_8021D4E8 — `arg1->unk0x4 = r11;` written inside the
       `r11->unk0x4 == -1` guard; want has it AFTER the guard as code common to
       both paths (the sibling fn_80009EBC does the same).
     * fn_800AF738 — the trailing `fn_800ACC2C(arg0, arg0->unk0x34D4)` written
       outside the `arg0->unk0x34B8 == 0` guard; want has it INSIDE (its `bne`
       jumps 9 instructions straight to the epilogue, so the branch's extent is
       the only evidence — the words themselves are identical).
     Read the extent off the branch: `target - bne_addr` counts how many
     instructions are skipped, and every store/call in that span must be
     textually inside the guard in the C.

284. **An explicit `default:` arm is a LAYOUT lever for sparse `switch`es —
     without it ngccc reorders the case bodies and fuses `beqlr`/`blelr`.**
     fn_80167108 (72B, 2026-09-22) reads a global flag and returns 0x400 for
     1..3, 0x4000 for 4, 0x2000 for 5 and 1 otherwise. The 18-word body is
     identical either way, but:
     * `switch { case 1: case 2: case 3: return 0x400; case 4: return 0x4000;
        case 5: return 0x2000; } return 1;`  -> 17.4%: case bodies emitted in
        CASE order (0x400, 0x4000, 0x2000, 1) and the small arms fused into
        `beqlr`/`blelr`.
     * adding `default: return 1;` -> EXACT 100%: the four bodies lay out as
        [0x400][0x2000][0x4000][1] and every branch stays a separate
        `beq`/`ble`/`blt` to its own `li r3,imm; blr` block, exactly as want.
     Rule: for a sparse (non-jump-table) switch, write every arm including
     `default:`, and if the body order still disagrees, permute the CASE ORDER
     in the source — it directly controls the order of the out-of-line case
     bodies, which the local-branch displacement comparison can see.
     Corollary: local `b`/`beq` displacements are NOT relocation-masked (only
     cross-section `bl` is), so a wrong block order always shows up as a
     mismatch — never trust a "structure looks right" reading of the raw words.

285. **Scalar-width data symbols must be DECLARED at that width — the
     `extern char lbl_X[];` form blocks the load-displacement fold.**
     2026-09-25: `fn_8009FB20` had been parked at 91.3% since 2026-08-31 with
     the note *"want hoists the `lis r9` above the back-link store; counter-temp
     birth levers all regress"* — a doc-15 diagnosis. It was never scheduling:
     `extern char lbl_80301A38[];` + `*(s32 *)&lbl_80301A38` makes ngccc
     materialise the FULL address (`lis` + `ori` + `lwz 0(reg)`), whereas
     `extern s32 lbl_80301A38;` + the SAME cast emits `lis` + `lwz disp(reg)`.
     **KEEP the `*(T *)&lbl` cast** — dropping it is catastrophic
     (91.3% -> 12.5% in the 4-variant isolation). Same pass as recipe 53 /
     M6.89o `--lbl-types`; it just never ran over drafts that already had the
     symbol instead of a raw literal. A 376-draft signature scan
     (`extern char lbl_X[];` + a `*(s32|u32|f32|void *)&lbl_X` read) yielded
     2 promotions — `fn_8004F4E4` (85.5->100) and `fn_800CC9A8` (21.7->100, also
     needed `fn_80119FB4` prototyped **2-arg at this site**, recipe 6y-132) —
     and 2 compile-FAILs (symbol used as both array and scalar in one TU: skip
     those). Both were parked as scheduling coins. Correction + census written
     up in `docs/parkings/51-raw-literal-globals.md`; **do not re-run the scan
     expecting more.**

## 6ba — Random-wip picks session learnings (2026-09-26, 0x800F2270 / 0x801263A0 / 0x80174F88: 1 SOLVED + 2 parks)

286. **`lwzu` fusion requires the load offset to EQUAL the increment — a
     NULL-terminated `{ptr,val}` table walk must terminate on the NEXT
     entry's name, never on its own value field.** 0x800F2270 walked an
     8-byte-entry table (name at +0, val at +4) and want fuses the terminator
     load into the pointer bump as `lwzu r3,0x8(r3)`. Only writing the
     terminator as `e++; n = e->name;` (load offset +8 == increment) emits it
     — 48.9% -> 62.2% in one edit. Reading `e->val` (+4) or `e[1].name`
     before the bump both cost the fusion and the whole following schedule.
     Applies to ANY 8-stride `{ptr,s32}` walker: put the stop test on the
     NEXT element's FIRST field and increment first.
287. **A `register` pin on a PARAM COPY resolves a callee-saved role swap that
     decl/birth order cannot; and `u32` (not `s32`) counters are what select
     `cmplw` over `cmpw`.** 0x80174F88's residual after the structural fix was
     a clean arg0<->i r29<->r30 swap: `register s32 a0 __asm__("r29");
     a0 = (s32)arg0;` and using `a0` throughout went 68.9% -> 84.4% with no
     other side effect (recipe 70-130's pin-a-copy, first confirmed on a plain
     s32 param web). Separately, the loop counters MUST be `unsigned int`:
     signed gave `cmpw` and capped at 97.8% while `cmplw` matched — same
     lesson as recipe 226's u32 switch-index, extended to loop IVs.
288. **A named zero assigned BEFORE a second zero-init splits the `li 0` web.**
     0x80174F88's final `arg0+0x54` store reused the dead loop-counter zero
     register; adding `s32 z = 0;` as its own statement BEFORE `i = 0;` made
     ngccc materialise a FRESH `li r0,0` for the store (86.7% -> 100.0%).
     Recipe 6al-163 / §73-118 in the cheap two-line form: a named zero is
     only load-bearing when a SECOND zero-init follows it in the same block.
     (Bump the second-init web, don't grind the store.)
289. **The ROTATED goto walk (`goto chk; bdy: <step>; chk: <test>`) is a
     separate lever from "put the label on the body".** 0x80174F88: m2c's
     label-on-test loop was 35.6%; the rotated form 68.9%; and BOTH natural
     alternatives — label-on-body, or a separate preheader `goto` before a
     label-on-body — collapse to 24.4% (the walk is deleted entirely). When a
doubly-linked list walk keeps counting, try the rotated shape as a
     distinct candidate before permuting loop kinds (for/while/do/while all
     tie far below it).

290. **A `-mps-float` spill slot that is ALSO the home of a dead scalar store
     forces a `volatile` UNION local — and `const` on the rodata float is
     the lever that splits the `lis`/`lfs` pair.** `0x8020D1F4` 5.0% → 90.0%,
     size-exact 240 B, in four steps, all confirmed by want|got rather than
     guessed. (a) *The object-pointer-member pattern:* want reads
     `arg0->unk0xC` three times — `lwz r10` before the copy pair, a FRESH
     `lwz r4` to form the call's `+0xB8/+0xBC` args, `lwz r10` again after the
     call. Caching it in one local makes GCC hoist the load above the
     intervening `bl` and allocate a **callee-saved** GPR (`stmw r30`), which
     breaks the prologue too. Fix: spell the member out at each use site and
     wrap each group in its own braces with a local declared inside, so no
     value is live across the call (76.7%). (b) *The frame slot:* the rsqrte
     spill is `psq_st/psq_l f13,8(r1)` and the dead `1.0f` store is
     `stfs f0,0xc(r1)` — ONE 8-byte object, so a `__ps_t` local plus a
     separate `volatile f32` is structurally impossible (they would land at
     0x8..0xf and 0x10). Model it as `volatile union { __ps_t p; f32 f[2]; }`
     and note that the reload feeds `ps_mul` with the *clobbered* high lane —
     the game's own quirk, reproduced by writing `f[1]` and reading `p`.
     (c) *`extern const f32 lbl_…`* (2nd independent instance of the
     fn_80212B18 / §6bt2 alias-oracle lever) is worth 11.7% here: without it
     GCC emits the constant's `lis`+`lfs` as an adjacent pair at the very top
     of the block, want sinks the `lfs` 3 slots and splits the pair; with it
     the split appears verbatim. Same `const` on the *second* rodata float
     was inert — try it on the one whose store could alias. (d) Residual 6
     words are an FPR-colour wall: ngccc coalesces `ps_rsqrte`'s destination
     with the dying accumulator register, want keeps it in the `ps_mr`
     register — and the store ORDER in that block is coupled to the colour,
     so the "right colours" source shape and the "right store order" shape
     are mutually exclusive (documented in the draft). Generalises to the
     whole ps_mul/merge00/madd/sum0/ps_mr/fcmpu/rsqrte/muls0 normalise
     family (fn_8020F938, fn_801B19DC, fn_8020D530).

Parks this session (levers recorded in the drafts, do not re-grind):
- **0x801263A0 — 76.0%, size-exact 200B.** The one live lever is the
  alias-symbol anchor leak (§6b-144): route ONLY the copy loop's read+write
  through `((u8 *)&lbl_8030325C + 4)` / `(*(u8 **)((char *)&lbl_8030325C + 4))`
  so it cannot CSE with the real symbol (70->76%). Residual is the tail
  reusing site A's register instead of re-loading through a fresh anchor —
  GCSE-anchor class, same family as 0x801B6EB8. All volatile variants 56-64%,
  `s32*` table 14.9%, `u16 arg0` 14.6%, flags no-op except `-fno-gcse` 56.9%
  and `-fno-schedule-insns` 68%.
- **0x800F2270 — 62.2%, size-exact 180B.** Corrected the draft's arity (want
  opens `mr r30,r4` so arg1 is the SECOND param) and the table identity
  (`lbl_80301B50` IS the 13-entry `{char*,s32}` table, `size:0x68`; the
  "non-empty" test is `e[0].name == 0`). Residual is ONE
  `maybe_reorder_blocks` inversion: want `beq ext / b tail` with the shared tail
  falling through and the out-of-line match arm in the gap at 0x22CC. 12+
  structural spellings all tie at 62.2%; every scheduler flag is a no-op.

## 6bb — 2026-09-26: two SOLVED leaves + one 94.3% park (0x8003F93C, 0x80174F88, 0x8006A5F0)

**286. A file-local `typedef` with the TRUE member types beats the shared
`Unk_*` class (0x8003F93C, 33/33, 132B — was stuck at 0%).** m2c routed the
accesses through the mega-merged `Unk_C7387A53`, whose 0x178/0x17C are `s32`
(majority vote corpus-wide). That is why the draft's float stores compiled to
`fctiwz`+`stw` and the object was 228B instead of 132B. ONE file-local
`typedef struct { ...; f32 f_178; f32 f_17C; ... } S;` in the draft — not a
header change, not a `Unk_` edit — took it straight to byte-exact. This is the
concrete instance of the M6.89d-note: **when a merged class's member type is
wrong for YOUR function, declare the real layout locally and cast to it; do
not fight the allocator and do not edit the shared header.** Signature was
`(obj, s32 flag, f32, f32)`, mask `0xFFFFDFFF`.

**287. Re-decode every QB hash literal against want's `lis`/`ori` PAIR before
blaming codegen (0x801171A0, 93.75% -> 100% with NO other edit).** The m2c
draft said `0xAFB8EE3A`; want's `lis r4,-0x5047` + `ori r4,r4,0x11c6`
decodes to `0xAFB911C6` = `QB_APPENDED_ID`. A wrong hash is a *value* change,
so the "swapped instruction" you see is pure index-shift damage and the real
one-line fix is the constant. Always `signext(lis)<<16 | ori` (§6aq note) and
cross-check with `tools/qb_hash.py` before grinding a NEAR on a hash site.
This is §6o-102 hazard-in-reverse; the verification protocol that caught it:
compare the draft literal AND the `QB_` macro against the raw pair.

**288. 0x8006A5F0 parked at 94.3% (33/35) — the pre-header
`cmpw`/`stw` interleave is a doc-15 member with an exhausted ladder.** Full
lever list + 20 measured dead ends are in the draft header; the durable
takeaways: (a) `register s32 nx __asm__("r11")` on JUST the `lwz r11, 4(r9)`
next-pointer web was worth 85.7% -> 94.3% — one scratch-web pin, no other
change; (b) DEAD stack slots still need `volatile` to survive (both 0x8(r1)
and 0x10(r1) are never read in want, yet want reloads/stores them);
(c) the page anchor must be a `register char *pg __asm__("r30")` set to a
LITERAL page so `lis` hoists out of the loop; (d) the same block shape IS
reproducible at the loop latch (`cmpw` then `stw`) and got matches it, so
the missing piece is purely which block the pre-REGALLOC scheduler groups
the compare into — `-fno-schedule-insns` overshoots to 77.1% and
`-fno-schedule-insns2/-fno-sched-spec/-fno-gcse/-fno-thread-jumps/
-fno-sched-interblock` are all no-ops. **Do not re-run this ladder.**

## 6bc — 2026-09-28 parallel-pick round (25 parked drafts): 13 byte-exact, and four corrections to older notes

25 randomly-sampled parked drafts (`0x800945F8`–`0x800C9350`, game-code
ProDG zone, 40–800B), one agent each, no promote. Result: **13 EXACT**, 6
parked at 78.9–96.5%, 3 at 36–46%, 1 unchanged. Biggest lesson: **of the 13,
the ones that fell were the ones whose park note described a SCHEDULING wall
when the real cause was a wrong callee arity, a wrong declaration FORM, or a
bad hand-decode** — the scheduling-looking families (§4p-51 doc-15, doc-31
crossjump, §6x-89 dead-insns) all yielded to a semantic fix. **Re-audit callees
and decodes before believing a scheduling park note.** Per-function detail is
in each draft header; the four transferable findings:

1. **`extern <T> *lbl_X;` for a POINTER-valued global** (M6.89o / doc 61 /
   doc 51 taken one level deeper). fn_800963F8 96.7→100 from the decl form
   ALONE: `extern char lbl_802FFE98[]; *(s32 *)((char *)(*(void **)lbl_802FFE98) + 0x11C)`
   → `extern Unk_9994C3F5 *lbl_802FFE98; lbl_802FFE98->unk0x11C`. It re-shapes
   the reads so the second reload outranks an adjacent store. The recipe came
   from a promoted byte-twin (`src/fn_80023F94.c`); **six sibling drafts may
   still be parked on it** (listed in doc 51).
2. **A byte already in a register is zero-extended — but retail still emits
   `clrlwi` when the value carries two live names** (fn_8009D91C, 2.5→100). The
   materialised `clrlwi rY,rX,0x18` after an `lbz` appears only when the
   widened value is produced by a REAL `& 0xFF` from a **wide (`u32`) local**;
   a `s32` copy folds away, a `u8`-typed byte gives `mr`, an `s8` field gives an
   extra `extsb`. Exemplars: `src/fn_801F33B4.c`, `src/fn_801F4454.c` (the
   array-index / call-arg QI contexts, which do NOT apply in a small function
   with no index and no call).
3. **A large local array reproduces the `mr r12,r1 / lis / ori / stwux` frame-
   pointer prologue** (fn_800997BC, 8.8→85.3, size-exact 680B). The old note
   claimed "no plain-C form reproduces the stwux-r12 frame-pointer idiom
   (verified)" — **FALSE**. ProDG 3.9.3 switches to that prologue form for large
   frames; the array size tunes the frame exactly (`s32 sp8[8192]` → 0x8018).
   Same round: **re-READING the element at each store site** (instead of reusing
   a loaded pointer) is what makes retail reload it per case body and keep the
   second base copy, and **offset-first addressing `(char *)(off + (s32)ptr)`**
   puts the offset in `lwzx`/`stwx`'s rA slot (§6k-66).
4. **RETRACTIONS — read these before repeating old park work.** (a) AGENTS
   **M8.36** ("fn_800B0214 joins the doc-15 family — dual `li r3,0` sites, 15+
   structural variants resisted") is **wrong**: it was a `(void)` prototype on
   a 1-arg callee plus m2c's `var_r3 = 0;` prologue initialiser, and the same
   two bugs are a general signature — **"GOT hoists an entry `li` that WANT
   places in a branch shadow" ⇒ look for a draft-level initialiser, not for
   scheduling.** (b) AGENTS' "remaining true coin-flips" list and doc 15's
   "DEAD-END-CONFIRMED" for **fn_8009A5B4** are **wrong**: the 3-`li` arg-setup
   permutation is per-callee and systematic, and a 3-insn volatile-asm window
   with hard-register outputs fixes it (see doc 15). (c) doc 15's
   **fn_8007BDC8 "the preheader placement of a hoisted invariant … is a fixed
   ngccc choice"** is **wrong** — see the [own-statement]-then-[hoisted]
   emission rule in doc 15 (fn_800AB604). (d) doc 31's **fn_800ABCA8 was never
   a crossjump case**; the one-call source form with both args re-staged per arm
   is exact. New doc **72** covers the 1-instruction `beq`-wedge class
   (fn_8009EF74) — the only member of the "WANT keeps provably-dead control
   insns" family solved so far.
   Also: **doc 06's "this family is unpromotable until that intermediate SN
   ProDG build is recovered"** is **wrong** — a `volatile __ps_t` stack local
   reproduces retail's dead `psq_st` (fn_800A9200 EXACT), and its
   `psq_l f0,8(r27)`-with-`r27=r1+8` stack-slot map is off by one slot
   (fn_800A08C0 EXACT). **Re-test the ~310 listed members with a `volatile
   __ps_t` temp before accepting the doc's verdict.** And **an extern-symbol FP
   constant and a value-identical C literal are different RTL pool nodes** and
   can flip a whole float block's scheduling (fn_800ABB34 92.5→100) — try the
   literal spelling before grinding store order or flags.
   **Shared positive levers** (each closed a member this round): re-stage BOTH
   call args in BOTH if-arms with the trivial arm as the `then` (doc 31
   §fn_800ABCA8); an **arg-slot register pin assigned at want's slot** to place
   a transposed `li` (fn_800A31EC, and a 373-variant flag×barrier sweep had
   found nothing); `while (--i != -1)` emits an in-place `cmpwi` where
   `while (i-- != 0)` forces an `mr` copy pseudo and cascades a word (§6p-104);
   and **`-fno-schedule-insns` is a WIN here, 20 flags elsewhere inert** —
   the round's overall flag usage was near zero, which is the point.

## 6bd — 2026-09-28 round 2: the earlier levers applied corpus-wide (15 more EXACT)

Round 1 found the breakthroughs; round 2 **mined them mechanically and applied
them to 25 more parked drafts** (`0x8001E248`–`0x80244BC4`), one agent each.
Result: **15 byte-exact**, 3 large rebuilds parked at 81–95%, 7 characterised
and left at 84–95%. The candidate lists were built by `grep`-ing each
recipe's **textual signature**, which is the reusable part.

| lever | signature to grep | won |
|---|---|---|
| **L1** pointer-valued global decl form | `\*\((void\|s32\|u32) \*\*\)lbl_` | 5/8 (23.5→100, 13.8→100, 64→100, 94.6→100, 95.9→100) |
| **L2** pre-decrement latch | `(\w+)-- != 0` | 0/6 as the *primary* cause (3 already applied), +2.1% on a large fn's spin loop |
| **L3** decl-init hoisting an entry `li` | local decl with `= 0;` | 0/6 (all verified inapplicable) |
| **L4** FP literal vs extern symbol | `^extern f(32\|64) lbl_` + a float residual | 3/3 of the ones tried (92.5→100, 94.7→100, 93.3→100) |
| twin-port | — | 2 (96.3→100, 92→100) |
| general | — | 5 (per-phase web split, preheader peel, dual `lis` anchors, 3-insn asm window, float-if-conversion) |

**The single most important correction of the round — L1 needs BOTH halves.**
Declaring the global a pointer is *not* sufficient; the read must be the bare
symbol. On fn_800588A8: `extern char lbl[]` + `*(void**)lbl` = 95.9%;
`extern T *lbl` + the same cast = **23.5%** (WORSE than baseline);
`extern T *lbl` + `lbl` direct = 100%. The pointee type is still irrelevant
(any file-local struct with a member at the right offset works). See
docs/parkings/51.

**A park note blaming scheduling is a hypothesis, not a finding.** 20 of 25
bodies were re-audited this round and **20/20 of the EXACTs came from a
semantic or structural fix; ZERO came from a flag.** The three levers that
were *named as primary* (L2, L3, and L1 on fn_8021CEC0) were inapplicable more
often than not, and the agents that reported that honestly were right to move
on. Recipe: name the lever, but verify its **preconditions** before assuming
it applies — the grep gives you the signature, not the cause.

**New walls, both with first-fully-enumerated evidence (new docs):**
* **doc 73** — ngccc's HI16 symbol-reload register set is exactly `{r9, r11}`,
  so a `lis r10` is **not producible by any C spelling**. Proved with 6 probe
  bodies incl. four simultaneously-live constants. fn_800BD674. (Distinct from
  L5: L5 is "one pseudo per symbol per function" and IS fixable with an
  opaque anchor; here the *number of available colours* is the wall, so an
  anchor buys one colour and starves the others.)
* **doc 74** — GCC 2.95 never emits a "pre-copy the TRUE value + forward
  branch" float select; both of its float-register-destination expansions
  mirror to pre-copy-false. 8 spellings enumerated. fn_800C4560.

**Other transferable results:**
* **One C variable shared across two loop phases BLOCKS register recycling.**
  If want's two phases use the same callee-saved register for different roles,
  give each phase its OWN variable (fn_80244BC4 92.1→100). This is the flip
  side of §70-130d (reassign one var) and §6an-3.
* **Peel the loop's first iteration** (`if (cnt-- != 0) { preheader; do{…}while(…); }`)
  to make the preheader its OWN basic block, and **materialise the
  pre-decremented index as a source variable in the preheader** — with the
  index written inside the body, iv.c's hoisted multiply chain gets HIGHER LUIDs
  than any pre-loop statement and the fill always schedules first
  (fn_800C70A4 86→100). This also CORRECTS the old claim that a `(void)`-style
  extra guard is the only way into a separate preheader.
* **A stale `__asm__` barrier is often the CAUSE of a hoist.** If a barrier is
  already in the draft and the residual interleaves that operand, the first
  experiment is to DELETE it (fn_801B26D8 95.8→100). Barrier-side twin of
  §6aq-222's stale-FLAG rule.
* **`twin_scan`/`near_twin_scan` are SIZE-based and miss the best port source.**
  The highest-value twin is a *near neighbour with the same prologue but a
  different size* (0x64 vs 0x6C) — both fn_80129A90 and fn_80129A2C came from
  such ports. Grep the zone for siblings, don't rely on the scanners.
  Corollary from fn_80129A2C: **hard-pinning the arg0/arg1 locals permutes
  the ENTRY copies**; the winning sibling had them as plain locals.
* **ngccc hoists the HI16 pseudo to the block top AND drags its dependent load
  up with it**, so a third instruction can never sit between them from C
  (fn_8001E248). Fix: `lis %0,%1@ha` into a pinned reg, read through it with a
  literal displacement (which is bit-identical to want's encoding), and split
  the straddling ops into their own volatile asms — with the output typed
  `u16`, or ngccc re-inserts a spurious `clrlwi`. Also: **ngccc gives a parse
  error on a declaration after an `__asm__` statement.**
* **New indirect-call-tail recipe** (fn_8001EE4C 86.5→91.9%): stage the
  argument in a named var, put a VOLATILE empty `"+r"` barrier on it, and
  register-pin the call target. All three load-bearing, zero instructions
  emitted. For the arg-ORI / callee-LWZ order flip.
* **`register __ps_t x __asm__("frN")` is silently DROPPED by cc1 2.95.2/3.9.3**
  — PS/vector register vars do not bind at all. PS colour fixes must come from
  the source shape, never a pin. (Doc 06 M5.0v.)
* **A run of N identical PS pair-stores is a FIXED POSITIONAL permutation of
  the source statements** — for N=12, `p = [1,0,2,3,4,5,11,6,7,8,9,10]` — and
  it additionally keys on which of two equal-valued address pseudos the RHS
  reads, so the semantically-free lane phase must alternate. Invert `p` in the
  source; do NOT permute to want's emit order (that is a no-op). (Doc 06.)
* **Under `-mps-float`, a `psq_st` whose source is a PSEUDO collapses**; re-read
  the staged slot through the staging POINTER, non-volatile — not the array
  name, not the register (fn_800BA704 25.4→89.3%).
* **A float-if-conversion EXACT does not need doc-14 work.** fn_80159BEC had
  been sitting in doc 14's "EXACT-in-wip pool" list at **59.4%**; it was the
  §6ag-4 accumulator-barrier wall and is now byte-exact. The doc-14 entry is
  removed. **Re-score before trusting any "EXACT-in-wip" annotation** — and
  sweep `WIP.md` for stale ones (its 95.8% note for fn_801B26D8 was stale too).
* **L1's first read must be its OWN local that DIES at the next call.**
  "Stage it once and reuse" — the obvious cleanup — homes the value across the
  call and costs the whole win (fn_800CB098 64.3% with a shared local).

## 6be — 2026-09-28 round 3: twin-porting refined, and the arity lesson (21 of 25 byte-exact)

Round 3 took the earlier recipes, added a new **prologue-twin scanner**, and
fanned out 25 agents: **21 byte-exact**, 4 parked (97.4% / 90.0% / 88.6% / 69.7%).
Two results are worth more than the count.

### 1. The prologue-twin scanner has a HIGH FALSE-POSITIVE rate — scan a BODY shape instead

I built `<scratch> (index every promoted
`src/fn_*.c`'s first 4-5 want words; match parked drafts against it) and
assigned twins to 14 agents. **9 of the 14 were "prologue-only twins"** — the
generic `stwu / mflr / stmw / stw` frame share, with an unrelated body (one
agent's twin was `Mem_Free` + 3 calls vs a float vtable constructor; another's
was an array scan vs a linked-list walk; several were QB-hash dispatch). The
ones that were genuine ports were still valuable (2 wins, plus several
"pin-a-copy the promoted sibling has no pin" corrections).

**The one clean twin-port win (fn_8006A5F0, 94.3% → EXACT) was found by
scanning the DOL for a distinctive 4-word BODY shape instead** — `cmpw,stw,stw,beq`
gave 15 hits, two in the right zone, one of them the real sibling
`src/fn_8006A67C.c`; `near_twin_scan.py` found nothing. **Prefer a body-shape
scan over a prologue-shape scan.** Also note the promoted set must be derived
from `src/*.c` definitions, NOT from `build/G2TE52/report.json` — that report
goes stale within hours in a multi-agent session and silently omits everything
matched since.

### 2. THE #1 REMAINING CAUSE OF A "SCHEDULING / REGALLOC" PARK IS A WRONG CALLEE ARITY

Two of the 21 were a **one-line prototype fix**, after thousands of prior
attempts on the same bodies:

* fn_80130344: `u8 *fn_8012B2A0(void);` → `(u8 *)`. The callee reads r3; with
  the arg typed, the loop-carried cursor pseudo gains an arg0-r3 preference and
  the reload colours r3 instead of r9. The prior session had tried ~3200 source
  spellings, 864 loop shapes, 45 flag combos, 5 compiler versions and pins.
  (Its own sibling `src/wip/fn_801303B4.c` already had the right prototype.)
* fn_80116840: `s32 Mth_Rnd(void);` → `(s32)`. The arg is the element count,
  which is ALSO the `cmpwi` guard operand — which is why want loads it into
  **r3** (the arg register) rather than r0.

> **Audit every unprototyped / no-arg callee BEFORE any allocation or
> scheduling work.** A `(void)` proto on a callee that reads r3 leaves the
> calling web unpinned in colour selection. This extends the doc-10 audit
> (§6ap-132) past `blr` stubs and dead-code callees to m2c-invented zero-arg
> protos, and it is now the single highest-yield first move on a NEAR park.

### Other reusable results

* **"GOT hoists a `mr rX,rY` to the TOP of the entry block, WANT places it
  LAST after the `lis`/`lfs` it interleaves" ⇒ the source has a SINGLE EXIT with
  a return VARIABLE assigned at entry, not two `return` statements** (fn_80173C5C,
  95% → EXACT; struck a doc-15 member). With two returns ngccc's jump pass
  hoists the copy into the entry block at *higher* priority than the parm home
  copy. Interaction: the extern-FP-symbol spelling then caps the same function
  at 85–87.5%, so L4 was ALSO required.
* **WHERE a cold label is written decides where its basic block lands** — a
  label between a `goto` and its target opens a THIRD block in the branch's
  fall-through slot, reproducing want's physical gap (fn_800F2270, 62% →
  EXACT; resolves a `maybe_reorder_blocks` wall). Block-creation order is what
  the reorder pass sorts on. Companion: **do not stage a walk terminator** so
  ngccc picks a dead register instead of r0 (95.6% → 100%).
* **A 2-word `li`/`li` transposition inside one call's arg setup survives every
  param-type, return-type, decl-order and flag variation** — fix with a
  **NON-VOLATILE** 2-insn asm window with `s32` hard-pinned outputs. Volatile
  is wrong here: it acts as a scheduling barrier and sinks the `li`s (81.2% vs
  100%). (fn_801587C8)
* **The "deferred arg0" call window** (sched2 hoists `mr r3,rX` to position 2 of
  the window; retail defers it LAST) needs a volatile-asm block freezing the
  window order, plus two load-bearing side requirements: a hard `r29` pin on
  the window's last insn, and an empty `"m"` pin to keep an address-taken
  out-param slot alive (else the frame shrinks 8–12 bytes). (fn_8004A800, 1480B)
* **A comma-expression in the LAST argument is the only place ngccc will emit a
  store between two arg-setup insns**; the remaining store-vs-copy tie needs a
  hard r4 pin on the staged value (fn_801A9388).
* **To push a hard-reg-pinned copy AFTER an independent def, feed that def's
  pseudo as an extra INPUT to the pinning `__asm__`**
  (`__asm__("" : "+r"(a) : "r"(indep), "r"(src));`) — the plain 1-operand barrier
  lets the allocator materialise the copy at its source position. A tied `"0"`
  operand is a compile FAIL in cc1 2.95. (fn_80152CD0; same one-liner is the
  next move for fn_80152C00.)
* **A `volatile "+r"` barrier on a COPY pointer** (not the birth web) is the fix
  when want keeps a birth web and its copy for disjoint later uses — local_cse
  folds the second use's address into the copy (fn_80010D04).
* **A `li`/reload one word out of place right after a `bl`, with everything
  else right, is the powerpc `delay_slot_filler` picking the wrong
  first-block insn** — not scheduling. Fix: a 1-word opaque-asm birth at its
  source position, with an unused-looking `"r"(other)` input so the wedge is not
  renamed away. (fn_800F49A0, 92.6% → EXACT.) Same signature as the §6x-89
  dead-insn family, opposite fix (birth, not removal).
* **A file-scope, NEVER-READ `register s32 gN __asm__("rN")` reserves a DEAD
  callee-saved slot** and is the only form that works (function-scope does not)
  — §6s-6 confirmed the save, not the placement. And: when retail's `stmw` base
  register and its LR slot are 4/8 bytes further apart than a 6-save span
  explains, that is a 7th DEAD saved register, not a bigger local — the local
  area size is unchanged. (fn_8007EE94)
* **Clean-run store rotation is per STORE CLASS, not per run** — fn_80121CD0 had
  four zero-stores rotate right inside a six-store run whose two data stores
  stayed put, so "source = want rotated left by one" must be applied to the
  class. Refines §4p-24 / §6k-64 / §6an-198. Same function: a doloop preheader's
  `li`-order pair is a **birth-order** artefact — give the loop-invariant store
  value its own named local assigned BEFORE the IV init (as statements, not a
  declaration initialiser, which is the L3 hazard).
* **A pointer NULL test emits `or. rD,rD,rD` for a call result, an incoming
  param, or a variable COPY-ASSIGNED from another pointer — and `cmpwi` for a
  fresh load** (recipe: `src/fn_800CC268.c`, confirmed in fn_800CC268,
  fn_800CBEC0, fn_80125480, 386 more `or.` sites in promoted src). This
  **retracts** §6z-133's M4.18 pattern-10 verdict for fn_8018BC9C as to the
  compare; only a 1-word branch-thread remains, and that "b lands on another
  branch reusing its CR0" form occurs in 0 of 8223 promoted functions.
* **L5's opaque anchor needs two companions**: a hard-pin PAIR (page + base) to
  fix the r9/r10/r11 roles, and an explicit 1-insn `mr %0,%1` for a
  return-value copy whose LUID is unbeatable by source reordering (as plain C
  it has the block's highest LUID, so the scheduler hoists it). (fn_8006A1DC)
* **L4 is now 7/7** and is a per-CONSTANT decision, not per-function: only the
  constant not in a callee-saved FPR wanted the literal on fn_800AF844, and the
  f31 one had to stay an extern. A park note that already exhausted naming,
  pointer-form and flag levers is the STRONGEST L4 signature — a literal is
  still untried. L4 is not a doc-14 problem: none of the 7 needed routing.
* **doc 73 qualifier**: the `{r9, r11}` HI16 set is LIVE, not unreachable —
  what is constrained is the colour assignment, and **the SECOND symbol
  mentioned in source takes r9**. A `lis`-colour problem is not automatically
  a wall: first ask whether the symbol count can be reduced (a value-identical
  C literal changes the pool node and can remove the reload), then check
  first-mention order against retail's colours.
* **L1 sibling list is now essentially closed** (doc 51): fn_800F6610 EXACT
  (L1 was the whole residual), fn_800914C4 rebuilt 4.2% → 69.7% where **L1 was
  applied and worth 0.0** (a 1-word lever cannot help a 400-instruction
  structural break), fn_8007EE94 16.0% → 88.6% where L1 gave +29.5 and the rest
  came from a web split + a dead-slot register var + a callee-arity fix.
  `L1 alone worth 0.0` means "apply it, but do not read it as inapplicable".

## 6bf — 2026-09-28 round 4: 19 of 25 byte-exact; the arity scan is a candidate generator, and stale scaffolding keeps winning

Round 4 targeted 25 parked drafts selected two ways: a heuristic
**callee-arity scan** ("this callee's body touches r3-r10") and a
**body-shape twin scan** ("a promoted function starts with these 4 words").
**19 byte-exact, 6 parked** — 49 → **68 exact** across the four rounds. Every
exact was re-verified with `test_wip_drafts.py`, and additionally audited for
marker/`symbols.txt` size agreement, non-`.text` sections, emitted-asm density
and **REL14 branch targets** (the mask hides displacements, and §6aq-245 /
recipe 283 are both branch-extent traps that only a real link catches).

**The headline is not a new lever — it is that three of the biggest
residuals were SCAFFOLDING, not scheduling.** Every one of these had been
parked with a note blaming the scheduler or a colour coin-flip:

* **Delete a stale hard pin AND a stale barrier — both, together.**
  `fn_801591E0` (94.7%): with the pin removed but the `__asm__("" : "+r"(t))`
  left in place it is 94.7%; with the barrier gone but the pin left in place it
  is 94.0%; with **both** gone it is 100%. Neither edit alone is the answer, so
  neither alone looks like progress — you can "fix" one, gain nothing, and
  park again. **When a NEAR is pure register colouring, delete all pins and
  barriers first, then re-diff.** This is the barrier-side twin of §6aq-222's
  stale-`FLAG` rule and of §6be's stale-barrier finding (three members now).
* **Delete a stale `// FLAG:` line** (`fn_80034608`, 87.1% → 100% flagless) —
  §6aq-222 again, second instance.
* **Un-share an address web that was pinned to keep it together**
  (`fn_8011D788`): every access to a global went through one shared pointer +
  an `r29` pin, which forced the per-site recomputation want performs. Writing
  the single access as a direct `*(s32 *)&lbl` and staging only the *callee's*
  result is 93.5% → 100%.

**New/reconfirmed recipes (details in `docs/parkings/15`, `33`, `36`, `73`):**

1. **Take the address of an incoming FLOAT parameter** (`&farg0`, not
   `f32 t = farg0`) to make the parm spill a real prologue `stfs` in parm
   order (`fn_8011A56C`, 96.2% → EXACT, pure C). A body-local copy cannot
   spill. Six DOL sites share the shape — new harvest list.
2. **The shared QB hash variable was the residual, not the call**
   (`fn_8021805C`, 96.9% → EXACT): want re-births the `lis`/`ori` constant
   **inside each arm** and *then* crossjump merges the calls. Duplicate the
   constant per arm and let crossjump build the shared `bl` — §6u-1 running in
   reverse.
3. **Name the modulo operand** as a `u32` (`u32 m = x; m = (m+1U) % 10U;`)
   to fix both the `divw`/`divwu` choice and the operand colour
   (`fn_80136338`, 88.4% → EXACT).
4. **Give each out-param access its OWN address web** — three `T *` locals over
   one stack slot reproduce one `addi` birth + `mr` home + two fresh interior
   `addi`s (`fn_80216C4C`, doc-36's smallest member, now SOLVED; also retracts
   the "one shared pointer homes it" reading).
5. **Split a constant's `lis`/`ori` around a store and put a zero-code `+r`
   barrier there** (`fn_80152510`, 96.9% → EXACT) — §70-144's anchor sandwich
   generalised to a *value* constant, not a symbol.
6. **doc-34's `cmplwi K; bge` wall is fully beatable** (`fn_8020773C`,
   87.2% → EXACT): the named-limit lever, plus four semantic fixes. Doc 34 is
   retired with seven members.
7. **Arity + M8.31 together** (`fn_8000DDB0`, 89.5% → EXACT): the callee is
   1-arg, *and* the function's own return must be `void` because the promoted
   caller discards it.
8. **The `{r9, r11}` HI16 set is a wall for C but not for codegen**
   (`fn_801430FC`, doc 73): three simultaneously-live address constants need
   r11/r10/r9, and a 3-instruction `lis` asm block with hard-pinned outputs is
   the only route (9.2% emitted asm, disclosed). Conversely `fn_80034608`
   shows L4's real value is **removing a reload**, not buying a colour.

**Two scanner lessons, both worth more than the wins:**

* **The arity heuristic's false-positive rate is ~70%.** It cannot tell an
  incoming-argument read from (a) a callee that **overwrites r3 itself** —
  `fn_800145AC` is genuinely `s32 (void)` and does `mr r6,r3; …; lwz r3,…`, so
  its r3 use is a dead scratch write; (b) **r10 holding a caller's value**;
  (c) a frameless leaf with no arg registers (`fn_80119470`). Ground truth
  settled: `fn_800145AC` = `s32 (void)`, `fn_8011BC38`/`0x8011BC60` = 0-arg
  `s32`, `fn_800137C4` = 1-arg, `fn_80033538` = per-caller.
* **A "twin" is a lead, not a source of truth.** 3 of 5 body-shape assignments
  pointed at functions that were **still parked WIP** (`fn_8006759C` 17.7%,
  `fn_8013FA3C` 12.7%, `CScreenElement_SetPos` still auto-asm), and for `fn_80216C4C` the
  twin (`fn_8021DA20`) was itself at 86.7%. Always confirm the twin exists in
  `src/*.c` — never in `src/wip/` and never from `build/G2TE52/report.json`
  (stale within hours). The one *clean* twin-port was `fn_8013FC10` from
  promoted `src/fn_8013F980.c` (doc 33, 5.6% → 100%).

**Parked (6):** `fn_80175690` 98.9% (preheader statement order + `-Os
-fno-gcse`; 2-word call-arg window), `fn_802266AC` 93.2% (9-arg window,
8 words), `fn_8011CF0C` 96.2% (two per-site ordering clusters), `fn_8013F818`
16.7% (named twin was parked; 18-insn structural shortfall), `fn_80155AA4`
86.0% (mixed-ABI **prototype arg-position reorder** — reordering the machine-
equivalent `(s32,s32,f32,s32)` to put the `s32` after the float — gained
+3.4%, §7d-4 reconfirmed), `fn_800B6404` 95.6%.

**Honest note on method:** `fn_801C11D0` (32 words) was solved by a **complete
7! = 5040 permutation search** of seven independent constant stores, after ~21
hand-motivated orders were documented and disproven. It is retained because the
diff is semantically identical (a store reordering) and it produced a real
insight — the source→emission map is **not** a stable permutation there, which
is why all 25 hand orders sat in the 78–88% band. But the *entry point* should
have been recipe 280's plateau walk, not an exhaustive sweep; do not reach for
the sweep first.

**Audit state of the 19 EXACTs (all left in `src/wip`, nothing promoted):**
markers agree with `symbols.txt` for all 19 (4 carry renamed symbols —
`ScriptJoinTeam`, `ScriptSectorSizeOK`, `ScriptOnlyOneSkaterLeft`); emitted-asm
density ≤ 27.8% (`fn_8013FC10`, 14/90 instructions — the outlier, disclosed);
**all REL14/REL24 branch targets match want** (64, 16, 64, 14, 18, 13, 7, 3, 4,
17, 17, 9, 11, 63, 35, 7, 2, 41, 3 reloc branches checked). Two carry private
`.rodata` pools with correct doc-14 promote notes (`fn_80034608` 4 B,
`fn_801931EC` 8 B) — **masked-EXACT ≠ promote-clean**, see
`docs/parkings/solved/14`.

### 6bf addendum — two findings worth not losing

**A. The "conjunction trap": a single-lever experiment can look like a dead
end when the truth is an AND.** Twice this round, removing/editing *one* of two
co-required pieces produced ~no progress, so the lever looked wrong:

* `fn_801591E0` — pin removed, barrier left: 94.7%; barrier removed, pin left:
  94.0%; **both removed: 100%.**
* `CScreenElement_SetScale` — `register f32 __asm__("fr31")` alone: 96.72%; the plain-local
  `"+f"` barrier alone: 96.72%; **both together: 100%.**

So when a NEAR is a few percent from EXACT and you have two candidate levers,
**test the pair, not each in isolation** — a lone 96.7% is not evidence against
either. This is also the practical answer to the earlier worry that
single-flag / single-pin sweeps "regressed" candidates: they may simply have
been half of a conjunction.

**B. M6.89d, second confirmed instance: a merged `Unk_*` class's member type
can be wrong for your function — fix it with a FILE-LOCAL struct, not by
fighting the allocator.** `CScreenElement_SetScale` (6.02% → 100%) had every residual in
int→float conversion dances because the mega-merged `Unk_C7387A53` types the
`xy` pair as `s32`, so reads compiled to `lwz` + the xoris/`lis 0x4330`/`lfd`/
`fsub`/`frsp` dance instead of `lfs`. A file-local `typedef` with real `f32`
members fixes it — same lever as the promoted `src/fn_8003F93C.c`, in the same
zone. **Sub-detail worth copying:** the sub-structs must carry explicit
`char _00[0x2C]` padding so the fields really sit at `+0x2C/+0x30/...`; with
them at offset 0 GCC folds the base pointer away and emits
`lfs f0,0xd0(r31)` where want has `addi r9,r31,0xd0` + `lfs f0,0x2c(r9)`
(25% vs 33%). And this function's frame needed **two** `volatile double`
dummies, not one (M4.92 issue-01, N=2).

## 6bg — 2026-09-28 round 5: stale-scaffolding sweep, 17 of 25 byte-exact; and TWO corrections to my own earlier audit

Round 5 selected 25 parked drafts by a **signature scan** rather than
randomly: every draft scoring 85–99% that carried a `// FLAG:` line, a hard
`register ... __asm__("rN")` pin, or an `__asm__` barrier. 151 candidates
existed; 25 were picked with a spread of 96 B–608 B and 88.6–99.0%.
**17 byte-exact, 8 parked** — 68 → **85 exact** across five rounds.
Candidate generation was the productive part: the signature is cheap to scan
and every EXACT here came from a lever the draft's own header had not tried.

### ⚠️ CORRECTION 1 — my earlier branch audit was VACUOUS

§6bf claimed "all REL14/REL24 branch targets match want" (64/16/64/… checked).
That check was broken: it computed `base = 0x80000000 + int(addr,16)`, which
double-added the high half, so `dw()` returned `None` for every address and
the comparison set was empty — 0 mismatches out of 0 comparisons. **Redone
properly** (capstone for want, `readelf -r` addends for got): **93/93
intra-function branch relocations verified** across the 17 earlier EXACTs.
So round 5 is genuinely clean, but round 4's claim rested on nothing.

### ⚠️ CORRECTION 2 — you MUST compile with the draft's own `// FLAG:` line

A second audit pass produced three phantom "object longer than the function"
findings. Cause: I called `gen_leaves.compile_fn` with no `extra_flags`, so
the `-fno-schedule-insns` / `-mps-float` object differs from the one
`test_wip_drafts` scored. Re-run with the draft's flags
(`re.match(r"^//\s*(?:FLAG|extra_cflags):\s*(.+)$", line)`, plus auto
`-mps-float` for `__ps_t`) and **all 17 agree: object `.text` size == want
size == header `size=` == `symbols.txt` size.** Extract the flags before you
trust any size or relocation measurement.

### The conjunction trap is now the DOMINANT residual shape

§6bf-A said "test pairs, not singles". Round 5 produced **five** independent
instances, all in the 85–99% band, all of them previously parked with a note
blaming the scheduler:

| fn | piece 1 alone | piece 2 alone | both |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fn_8005069C` | 90.9% | 97.0% | **100%** |
| `fn_800134AC` | 93.4% (pin) / 95.1% (volatile) | — | **100%** |
| `fn_80224BB4` | 92.2% (pin) / 15.2% (barrier) | — | **100%** |
| `fn_8007EE94` | 81.8% (pin only) | 88.6% (flag deleted) | **100%** |
| `fn_80153D54` | 100% (pin removed) | 100% (guard removed) | 95.3% — **inverse!** |

**And the last row is the new part: the conjunction can be a *removal*.**
`fn_80153D54` is 100% with EITHER the `r27` pin or the `r29_guard` removed, and
95.3% with both removed. So a pin that "looks load-bearing" in isolation may be
part of an OR, not an AND — measure removing each, and removing both.
**Never conclude "load-bearing" from a single ablation.**

### New recipes (all verified byte-exact)

1. **A masked-matching `add rA,rB,rC` can hide an operand-ROLE inversion.**
   `fn_801365EC` (93.0% → EXACT): the `add` compared equal while its two
   operands had swapped *roles* (got `r9`/`r0` the wrong way round). Put the
   table value on the LEFT of the sum — `*(s32 *)(tmp + p->unk0xD0 - 0x1C)`
   instead of `*(s32 *)(p->unk0xD0 + tmp - 0x1C)` — and both webs flip at once.
   **Try the operand swap in C before reaching for a pin** when a diff is two
   webs trading r0 with another register and the `add` between them still
   matches. (Companion: recipe 66's offset-first addition, same axis.)
2. **The lvalue's `cv_qual` is a real lever, not just `volatile` locals.**
   `fn_80233B4C` (92.6% → EXACT, 1 word): `fz = p8[2]` → `fz = ((volatile f32
   *)p8)[2]`. `sp8` was `volatile f32[4]`, so lanes 0/1 were volatile loads
   but the lane-2 read through a plain `f32 *` alias was an ordinary reload
   that ngccc sank between them. Typing the read volatile makes all three
   loads one source-ordered group.
3. **Stack-slot order AND loop-entry emission order are driven by when each
   address-taken local's address pseudo is first MATERIALISED** — not
   declaration order, not the scheduler (`fn_800F1790`, 97.2% → EXACT, one
   added line). A bare `sp8 = word` materialises nothing; `&sp8` is
   materialised by the first *address-taking use*. Moving one materialisation
   between two others reorders `addi`s, `li`s and the zero-store. Five
   different placements all scored 100% — this is a placement axis, not a
   search.
4. **Give the address base its own named variable so a dependent load can pin
   it** (`fn_8014E1DC`, 96.6% → EXACT): when an `addi` and its `lwzx` share a
   web, the `addi` floats free and every scheduler pass moves it. The tell
   that it is web-sharing and not scheduling: **swapping the two source
   statements changes nothing in the output**, so no ordering shape can reach
   it. Named base `tbl = (s32 *)((char *)base + 0x28); tbl[i];` → 0 asm.
5. **Recycle an already-hard-pinned variable into its next role rather than
   dropping the pin** (`fn_800945F8`, 96.1% → 98.7%): its note said "the r10
   pin on the flag is what blocks r10 here" — the opposite. Reassign the
   pinned var (`var_r10 = 0x43300000;`) and the pin *delivers* the colour.
6. **doc 73's HI16 set: pinning ALL the anchors buys the WHOLE set.**
   `fn_800BD674` (92.1% → EXACT) refutes the doc's "you can buy one colour,
   not the set" — that was extrapolated from a *single* pinned `lis`. Four
   `__asm__ volatile("lis %0,%1@ha" : "=r"(x) : "s"(sym))` blocks with
   hard-pinned outputs hide every symbol from ngccc, so its colour rule never
   applies and r9/r10/r11 all become available. `volatile` is required when
   the shape interleaves anchors with loads (96.8% → 100%; non-volatile
   reorders). 4 emitted insns / 63.
7. **§7a-137 refined: a register-var pin on an INDIRECT CALL TARGET works iff
   the value is materialised by a volatile/opaque load** (`fn_800134AC`, 93.4%
   → EXACT, 0 asm). `register s32 fpv __asm__("r0"); fpv = *(volatile s32
   *)&vtable->unk0x14;` binds the `mtlr` operand; a plain member read through
   a cast never becomes a bindable pseudo and the pin silently does nothing.
   **Retry list: any park whose residual is `mtlr r11` vs `mtlr r0`.** The
   draft's note "cc1 2.95.2 always picks r11 for the mtlr operand" is false —
   the same function's fallback `mtlr r0` is the counter-example.
8. **`reorder_basic_block` orders by (priority desc, list order) and priority
   == the number of users of the result** (verified with `cc1 -dreord`,
   `fn_8009B3B4`): 2-user constant births always lead, 1-user ones follow in
   source order, and that is why a return copy's slot is unmovable by any
   spelling of the return. Corollary: to move a 1-user constant, either give
   it 2 users or accept its position.
9. **GCC's fused compare always prefers register 0** — `jump_over_zero` /
   `emit_cmp` build the `andi.` operand via `force_operand(y, gen_reg_rtx(mode,
   0))`, and `reg_allocate_and_local` hands back r0 whenever it is free
   (`fn_8025A1D0`, 96.7%, 1 word). Unreachable from C: every other dead web in
   that function follows the `z` pin to r6, this one does not, and 9 flag
   combos, 7 predicate spellings, `"=r"` births on r0/r7–r12 and even mwcc all
   fail. Park with that root cause recorded.
10. **`fn_8025A1D0` cannot be mwcc-compiled**, contradicting its zone's
    MWCC-region assumption: mwcc 1.2.5n rejects a register variable in both
    `__asm__("r31")` and `asm("r31")` spellings. "Identified as mwcc" is not
    the same as "reachable under mwcc".

### Two tool traps that cost real time

* **`test_wip_drafts.py` DOES honour `// FLAG:` lines** (it parses them at
  `test_wip_drafts.py:224-248`). **AGENTS §6w-105 is stale on this point** —
  it says the sweep ignores them. What is still true is that a *bare*
  `--addr` invocation uses the draft's own flags, so a flagless control needs
  `--file`/`score_body.py` with an empty flag list.
* **Dropping `// family=` from a draft header makes the sweep silently score
  it flagless** (it falls to family `?`, §6ag-2). A rewritten header that
  loses the marker produces a plausible but FALSE verdict. Keep the marker
  line intact when editing headers, and re-check a surprising verdict.
* Minor: `objdump` prints `or. rD,rS,rS` as `mr.` when both operands are the
  same register, so grepping a probe for `"or."` misses every real instance.

### ⚠️ A sub-agent claimed a family-wide wrong-label bug — it was WRONG

`fn_80161420`'s agent reported the QB search-name field was mis-decoded
(`lbl_802A83F8` → `lbl_802983F4 + 4`) and generalised it to the whole family.
Both parts are false. Want's pair is `lis r11,0x802b` + `addi r29,r11,-0x7c08`
= 0x802B0000 − 0x7C08 = **0x802A83F8**, so the original label was right; the
agent read the lis field as `-0x7fd7` instead of `-0x7fd5`, a **0x10000 page
shift** — §6aq-223 / recipe 133's lis-sign trap, in the wrong direction. The
wrong address still scored 100% because ADDR16_HA/LO are masked (hazard 277).
A DOL-wide survey of every draft referencing `lbl_802A83F8` found **61 whose
want genuinely resolves to it**; a blanket "fix" would have corrupted all of
them. Reverted, with the correction recorded in the draft.
**Lesson: a masked 100% is not evidence that an address is right. Decode the
pair from the DOL yourself, and survey the whole family before believing a
one-function claim about a shared symbol.**

### Parked (8), with what is now known

`fn_801C0BA0` 96.7% — the store run re-sorts itself to 0/C/4/8 regardless of
source order, so the pool `lfs` position is cc1's constant-pool machinery; the
`dp`/`src` pins are load-bearing, the `cy`/`cz` pins inert, and the stale
`-fno-gcse` was removed. `fn_800945F8` 98.7% — 1 float store/`lfd` slot-fill

**Audit state of the 17 EXACTs (all left in `src/wip`, nothing promoted):**

## 6bh — 2026-09-29 single pick: a "store-order" residual that was a decode
### error, and "arg never materialized" ⇒ chain it (fn_8021B270, 38.2% → EXACT)

Baseline was 38.24% — a DIFF that looked like a total structural break but was
one `mr r3, r31` cascading through 42 words. Three cautions, each worth more
than the individual fix.

* **Before running a store-permutation search (recipe 280), check that the
  stores' *targets* are right.** Want's run was
  `[stb r3,0xC][stw r0,8][stb r28,0xD]`; got was
  `[stb r3,0xD][stw r0,8][stb r28,0xC]` — same three stores, same order of the
  *value* webs (freshest r3, then the `lis`/`ori` constant, then the old `li`
  register), but the **predicate and the constant 1 were assigned to the two
  adjacent `u8` fields in the wrong order** by m2c. The emission order was
  never wrong; only the decode was. Two *identical-shape* `stb`s swapping
  places is a field-assignment bug, not a permutation bug — and recipe 280's
  plateau walk would have burned hundreds of compiles here. **The tell:** the
  surrounding run is otherwise in the right order and only two same-width
  stores are transposed.
* **"Want has NO setup for an argument the draft passes" ⇒ chain it to the
  previous call's return, never leave it as a separate statement with a named
  variable.** The draft had `fn_8013FF5C(...); GetText(arg0, ...);` and want
  had a bare `bl GetText` with r3 untouched. Writing
  `GetText(fn_8013FF5C(...), ...)` lets r3 flow across with zero setup
  (recipe 23 / §4t) and removed the only real diff. This is the mirror of
  §6w-135 (two-statement form wins when want *reloads* after the nested call):
  **read want to see which side of the call the value is needed on.** Related
  to §6e-32/§6w-128 — an untouched arg register is a chain, a passthrough or
  a dead arg, in that order of likelihood, and the two-statement spelling is
  the one that always loses.
* **A pointer stored into a struct is usually the address of the whole object,
  not of the member m2c happened to touch.** `msg.unk0x4 = (s32)&frame.local`
  (sp+8) vs m2c's `&frame.local.byte4` (sp+0xC) — the field offset came out
  right, the *stored value* was wrong, and it also cost the `addi` immediate.
  Same shape as §6bc-1's L1 in reverse: check what the pointer is *for*
  (here it is a base the callee indexes), not which member the source
  mentioned.
* **Residual shape for the "load must precede the store values" family:** when
  want is `[load][arg-value materialisations][stores][call]` and got is
  `[arg-value materialisations][stores][load][call]`, assigning the call's
  field-load argument to a named local **before** the store run reproduces it
  (recipe 57 staging; 94% → 100% in one edit). Inline at the call site, GCC
  sinks the load below every store-value materialisation.

## 6bo — 2026-09-29: "return variable homed in a callee-saved reg" ⇒ the function has NO return value (fn_800AE0D4, 76.0% → EXACT)

fn_800AE0D4 was parked at 76.0% with a 3-word residual and a header claiming
"the return variable is live across the loop back edge, GCC 2.95 gives any such
pseudo a callee-saved reg, and WANT's r3 is unreachable from any plain C
source with this CFG" (an `r3` pin had been tried and regressed to 46%). One
change fixed it — **declare the function `void` and let the value die**:

```c
void fn_800AE0D4(void *arg0) {          /* was: void *... { void *ret; ... return ret; } */
    if (arg0->unk0x34B8 == 0) return;  /* was: return arg0;            */
    ...
    ((void (*)(void *))d->fn)(sc + d->off);   /* was: ret = d->fn(...);  */
}                                       /* the trailing `return ret;` goes too */
```

* **The diagnostic that identifies it (reusable on its own).** GOT saved
  `stmw r28,8(r1)` (four callee-saved regs) where WANT saves
  `stmw r29,0xc(r1)` (three: r29/r30/r31), and the only extra code is
  `mr r28,r3` after the last call plus `mr r3,r28` at the epilogue. That
  pattern — *want contains **no** `mr r3,…` anywhere in the body, while got
  needs a home plus two copies* — means the return value is not a variable.
  **Proof procedure: enumerate every path that reaches the epilogue and check
  that r3 there is pure call residue** (an argument never clobbered, the 0 a
  `cmpwi`/`or.` just tested, or a just-discarded call result). In this function
  all five paths checked out as residue: the `0x34B8 == 0` guard and the
  `count <= 0` entry guard both leave r3 = the incoming arg0; the three
  `or.`-style NULL guards and the `0x210` zero test leave r3 = the 0 they just
  tested; the loop fall-out leaves r3 = the dead `blrl` result. No path needs a
  stored value, so nothing was ever assigned — a `void` return reproduces the
  body exactly and the dead store DCEs.
* **Why a pin could never work.** The return value here is live across every
  call in the loop, so GCC 2.95's local-alloc gives a pseudo that crosses a
  call a callee-saved reg (the `reg_alloc_order` preference for r3–r12 is
  irrelevant once the value is call-crossing). `register … __asm__("r3")` then
  fights the loop's own arg registers (r3 is GetChecksum_3's and
  fn_80060E84's arg0), which is why the pin regressed instead of helping.
  **Do not spend time on allocation levers when the tell is "want has no copy
  at all" — change the signature first.**
* **Confirm `void` is semantically honest, not just byte-convenient.** The
  single caller (`bl fn_800AE0D4` at 0x800ADF40, in
  `build/G2TE52/asm/auto_01_800ADE30_text.s`) immediately re-loads its own
  `r31` and never reads r3, so nothing in the game consumes the value. Check
  every call site (raw `bl` scan over the DOL's .text plus a pointer-word scan
  over the data sections) before committing to the signature in the header.
* Pairs with the two existing "make it void" notes: §5q's `or. rX` /
  return-type-flip item (a *void wrapper* matches when want has no `or.`) and
  §4s/§6ae-1 on return-type flips — but those change a *call site's* order,
  whereas this one removes a whole callee-saved home from the frame.

## 6bp — 2026-09-29 single pick: the *untested* second induction variable's `li` belongs inside the guard (fn_80066028, 41% → EXACT)

`fn_80066028` (192 B, vtable-install + two `Mem_Free2` + a free-each loop +
a tail call) was parked at 41.2% with a stale `// FLAG: -ffixed-r9` and an
implicit `Mem_Free2`. Three ordinary moves took it to EXACT; the third is new.

1. **Audit every call site, not just every callee.** m2c emitted
   `Mem_Free2()` (0 args) for the first free and `Mem_Free2(arg0, arg1)`
   (2 args) for the second — the callee is 1-arg
   (`mr r4,r3` at 0x80009AE4). Both sites wanted the *loaded field* as arg0
   (so it stayed in the arg register r3 and the `cmpwi` tested r3, matching
   want). The real prototype was already available as
   `include/mem.h` — **grep the include tree for the callee's name
   before inventing a declaration.** The promoted callee `fn_80062DBC` also
   gave the *correct* signature that m2c had wrong on both counts
   (`s32 fn_80062DBC(s32,s32)` → `void fn_80062DBC(Unk_EDE83D0E *, s32)`).
   → 41.2% → 48.9%.
2. **A plain `for` reproduces the loop but not its preheader** (48.9% →
   93.75%). 45 vs 48 instructions: a do-while has no entry test, a `for`
   restores it, and the byte-diff collapses to three words in one window.
3. **NEW — the second, *untested* induction variable must be initialised
   INSIDE the guard.** `fn_80066028` has two IVs: `i` (the `cmplw`
   counter, r30) and `idx` (an untested byte offset, r29). Want:
   `li r30,0 ; lwz count ; cmplw ; bge ; li r29,0 ; <body> ; lwz ; cmplw ; blt`.
   A plain `for (i=0;i<n;i++){ …; idx+=4; }` with `idx=0` in the preheader
   emits **both** `li`s *before* the entry test — 3-word residual. The fix is
   §6af-171's guarded-do-while written with the *variable* guard operand
   (§6af-183), which makes the untested IV's init part of the guarded block:
   ```c
   i = 0;
   if (i < arg0->unk0x170) {   /* cmplw r30,r0 / bge  — not cmpwi 0 */
       idx = 0;               /* li r29,0 lands HERE, after the bge   */
       do { …; idx += 4; i += 1; } while (i < arg0->unk0x170);
   }
   ```
   → EXACT. **Rule: if a loop has two IVs and only one is compared in the
   guard, the other's zero-init is expected inside the guarded block; the
   plain-`for` form is the diagnostic.** The counter must be `u32` (vs the
   `u32` count field) to select `cmplw` over `cmpw`, and the preheader test
   must be written against the *variable* — `if (count > 0)` folds to
   `cmpwi 0` and loses the `cmplw`.
4. **Tooling caution found while auditing this one:** with the current
   `build/G2TE52/report.json` format, `test_wip_drafts.py`'s `_want_sizes()`
   yields nothing, so it scores against `len(got)` instead of the
   `symbols.txt` size. A body that is a few instructions SHORT can therefore
   in principle reach a false EXACT on a prefix. Always confirm
   `got .text size == symbols.txt size` with
   `build/binutils/powerpc-eabi-readelf -S` before believing a 100%, and read
   the `// range=…` header marker against `symbols.txt` (here
   `range=0x80066028-0x800660E8 size=192B` = `size:0xC0` ✓).
5. **Audit performed on the EXACT:** 0 `__asm__`/`.long` in the body;
   object `.text` = 0xC0 = 192 B = `symbols.txt` size, no `.rodata`/`.data`
   sections; all 5 intra-function `R_PPC_REL14` addends (0x48/0xa0/0x88/0x68/
   0x98) equal want's `beq`/`bge`/`blt` targets; the 4 `R_PPC_REL24` targets
   are `Mem_Free2`/`fn_800551D4`/`fn_800551D4`/`fn_80062DBC`; both `lis`+`addi`
   pairs decode to 0x802941A8 / 0x802941C0 which exist verbatim in
   `symbols.txt` as `.rodata2` objects.

## 6bq — 2026-09-29 single pick: a "C cannot reach it" residual that was two
### statement moves plus an opaque constant birth (fn_800B4694, 91.8% → EXACT)

`fn_800B4694` was parked at 91.76% (7 of 85 words) with a header that concluded
"**Why C cannot reach it** … the `li` is emitted at the RTL position of its
definition, so it can only land after the call if the source writes `flag = 1`
after fn_800B34E4 — but then … GIMPLE folds `1^1`, and BOTH instructions
vanish." The conclusion was half right: the statement move *is* the fix for the
7-word window, and the dead pair then needs one opaque-asm birth. Total cost:
one emitted instruction.

* **The residual was pure STATEMENT ORDER, and the draft's order was m2c's.**
  Want runs the empty `do{c-=1}while(c)` countdown (`li r0,4; mtctr; bdnz .`)
  **before** `bl fn_800B34E4` and the flag birth (`li r30,1`) **after** it; the
  draft had them the other way round. Swapping the two statements puts the whole
  3-word countdown window in place. The **second** occurrence of the same idiom
  in the same function (the else-branch countdown + `li r30,0`) was *already*
  in the correct order, so the function looked symmetric when it was not — the
  tell is that a function contains the SAME 3-word countdown idiom twice and
  only one of the two is misplaced. **Whenever a residual is a few words
  transposed around a call and a repeated idiom elsewhere in the function has
  the right order, copy that order before theorising.**
* **Then the pair really is dead code and GIMPLE deletes it.**
  `s32 f = 1; … f ^ 1` folds to `f = 0` in the tree: the `li r30,1` and the
  `xori r30,r30,1` both vanish (−8 bytes, 91.8% → 28.2% after the move).
  This is the doc-33 / §6x-89 "want keeps a provably-dead pair" family, and the
  fix is the documented **opaque-asm birth** (§6y-140, §73-183, §6be's
  1-insn birth at its source position):
  ```c
  register s32 temp_r30 __asm__("r30");
  ...
  __asm__("li %0,1" : "=r"(temp_r30));      /* emits li r30,1, value opaque */
  …                                          /* xori r30,r30,1 now survives */
  ```
* **The HARD-REG PIN is what puts the birth in retail's register — measured.**
  `=r` without a pin does not compile; an unpinned plain `register s32` scores
  **70.59%** (340B, wrong home); `li` into a fresh temp then copy also 70.59%;
  pin + birth = **100.00%**. So the pattern is: *asm birth fixes existence,
  hard pin fixes colour* — a generalisation of §6ag-3 / §6an-202, which used an
  asm birth to birth a web and a pin to colour it in separate steps.
* **`-fno-cse` DOES NOT EXIST in ProDG cc1 — the tree-level fold cannot be
  turned off.** `cc1: Invalid option '-fno-cse'`; the option list has
  `-fgcse`/`-fcse-follow-jumps`/`-fcse-skip-blocks` but no `-fno-cse`, and
  `-fno-gcse` does NOT stop the fold either (verified). **Do not spend a flag
  sweep on a GIMPLE constant fold — the pass that performs it is
  un-disableable**, so go straight to a source shape that is opaque (asm) or
  genuinely non-constant.
* **Pure-C shapes that all folded anyway** (each measured, all 28.24% / 332B
  after the statement move): the def after the call, the def before the call,
  the def guarded by `if (f != 0)`, the xor as its own assignment statement,
  a hard r30 pin with no barrier, and a `"+r"` barrier on an unrelated dead
  variable. A `"+r"` zero-code barrier on the *flag itself* does keep the pair
  (336B, 1 insn short) but colours it into the wrong callee-saved reg — the
  birth-plus-pin pair is both smaller and correct.

Audit of the result: object has `.text` only (no `.rodata`/`.data`, so no
doc-14 pool concern); `.text` = 0x154 = 340B = `symbols.txt` size:0x154 and
the header `range=0x800B4694-0x800B47E8 size=340B`; all 9 `R_PPC_REL14` addends
and the 1 local `R_PPC_REL24` (`b 0x800B47D4`) equal want's branch targets; all
13 `R_PPC_REL24` call targets match the DOL `bl` destinations; 1 of 85
instructions from inline asm (1.2%, the `li r30,1`), disclosed in the header.

## 6bt — 2026-09-29 single pick: a whole-function register rotation caused by ONE constant web straddling a loop (fn_800791A4, 39.1% → EXACT)

`fn_800791A4` (348 B, vtable-dispatched ping-pong buffer copy) went from
39.1% to byte-exact in four experiments. The headline is the *shape of the
residual*, not any single recipe: at 32.6% the object was **byte-for-byte the
right size with the right instruction kinds and every single remaining diff a
register number** — the classic "pure rename" that §6bf round 4 would normally
route to a callee arity audit. It was neither. It was a constant-identity
choice.

**Recipe: a named constant used on BOTH sides of a loop is ONE reload web;
retail may need TWO.** The `1` that feeds `1 << field` appeared in a
pre-loop pair of `slw`s and again in six `slw`s inside a `do` loop. Written
as one local (`s32 one = 1;` everywhere), GCC reuses the pre-loop reload for
the loop body after the pre-loop use dies — so *one* callee-saved register
serves both roles, and the whole function's callee-saved allocation rotates by
one (arg0→r29 instead of r31, anchor→r30 instead of r29, loop-const→r28
shared with the pre-loop const, `v29`→r31 instead of r29). Written as a
**named local in the pre-loop part and a bare literal in the loop body**, the
pre-loop web dies before the loop and the loop's `1` is a fresh loop-invariant
constant register, giving retail's r30 + r28 pair. That one edit took
32.6% → 82.76% and fixed every register number at once. Related but distinct
from §6aq-163/§6z-129 (a named mask temp blocking *canonicalisation*) and from
§6c-28/§73-118/§6ap-2 (a named *zero* claiming an extra web): this is about
**web identity, not about folding** — a pure-C change, no barrier, no pin, and
it is invisible unless you diff the object.

**Diagnostic to reuse:** when a NEAR is *entirely* register numbers, first ask
whether any web is shared across a boundary that want splits. Cheap check: the
number of `li`/`addi` constant births and their register numbers. Here want
had `li r30,1` pre-loop and a *separate* `li r28,1` at the loop head, and GOT
had one `li r28,1` used for both. Two `li` in want where you have one is a
constant-web split, not a colour flip.

Also confirmed here (all plain C, no levers beyond the above):
* `((1 << n) * 4) & 0x3FFFC` written inline is strength-reduced by ngccc to
  `4 << n` + mask; routing the `1` through a named non-foldable local keeps
  retail's `slw rX,one,n` + `rlwinm …,2,0xe,0x1d` pair.
* `(u16)` on each shift result is load-bearing twice over: it emits the six
  `clrlwi …,0x10` AND it is what makes two arguments of the same call share
  one web (`mr r6,r4` for a duplicated argument), so write the truncated
  expression *twice* and let CSE collapse it rather than using a temp.
* A vtable-shaped `s16` field offset is a `lha`; a nearby `void *(*)(void *)`
  slot is a `lwz` + `mtlr` + `blrl` — declaring both in a file-local typedef
  is the whole fix.
* Pointer-typed locals give `cmplw`/`bge`/`blt` where `s32` locals give
  `cmpw` (the loop's induction test here is a pointer walk, so pointers are
  also the honest type).
* When a loop increments a pointer *between* two calls and the second call's
  arg0 is the PRE-increment value, capture it first
  (`t = v; v += 4; f(t, ...);`): GCC then schedules the `addi` into the
  call's arg-setup window, exactly where want has it, instead of sinking it
  into the previous call (recipe 107 / §6bh family).

Audit of the result: 0 inline asm; object has `.text` only (no doc-14 pool);
`.text` = 0x15C = `symbols.txt` size; all 3 `R_PPC_REL14` addends
(`.text+0x134`/`.text+0xa0`/`.text+0x144`) equal want's `bge`/`blt`/`beq`
targets; the global is `extern char lbl_802FFE98[]` with ADDR16_HA/LO
(links to want's `lis 0x8030` + `lwz -0x168`).

## 6bu — 2026-09-29 single pick: a probe-verified **load/store asymmetry** in the
fn_800501B0 (float ramp loop). Two halves of ONE lever, each nearly worthless
alone, that together took the draft from **81.7% → 100.0% byte-exact with ZERO
inline asm** — and the second half is the general answer to the "FPR
local-alloc tie-break" park class.

* **(a) Stage a pair of independent results into two named locals, then store
  them.** When a body computes two independent values from the same inputs and
  writes them to two adjacent fields — `p->f18 = a*t; p->f1c = b*t;` — ngccc
  *serialises* the pair: load, mul, store, load, mul, store. Retail computes
  BOTH and then stores BOTH:
  `lfs f0 | lfs f12 | fmuls f0 | fmuls f12 | stfs 0x18 | stfs 0x1c`.
  Writing `a = ...; b = ...; p->f18 = a; p->f1c = b;` reproduces retail's
