  schedule exactly. **Side effect worth more than the schedule: it also fixes
  the loop-INVARIANT register colours** (the two extra live webs change which
  scratch FPRs the allocator hands the hoisted constants), so a loop whose
  `lis`-anchored constants all sit one slot off can be fixed by this alone.
* **(b) Give every *phase* of the body its own variable names.** Writing
  `a`/`b` for pair 1 and **reusing the same `a`/`b`** for the structurally
  identical pair 2 makes the allocator treat the two phases as one live range:
  the temps come out as a clean 3-cycle rotation (GOT `{a:f11, b:f0, c:f12}`
  vs WANT `{a:f0, b:f12, c:f11}`), 90.1% and 0.5% short. Four *distinct* names
  (`a,b` then `c,d`) give 100.0%. Same shape as §6al-184 / §6an-3 but the
  direction matters: those **split** a variable that the compiler had merged;
  this **refuses to merge** two variables the source had written separately.

**Measured (each row one edit off the row above):** 81.68% (m2c rebuild + a
`fr9` pin) → **(a) with `a`/`b` reused 90.08%** → **(a)+(b) 100.00%**;
(a) without (b) — `p->f18 = a = ...` assign-in-statement — 80.92%; (a) with
all five results staged into five names and stored in a row 79.39%. So it is
an **AND**, and a lone 90% here is not evidence that (b) is inapplicable
(§6bf-A). Staging the pair *and* hard-pinning the `c498` load to `fr11` gets
91.60% — a pin is not needed once (b) is in.

Diagnostic that finds candidates: a NEAR whose whole residual is
`(a) a compute/store interleave that differs **and** (b) one rotated register
for a loop-invariant constant, and where the header blames "FPR allocation" or
carries a `register f32 __asm__("frN")` pin. **Delete the pin** — the temp
register numbers are a consequence of the web graph, not a lever. A full 80-row
FPR pin ladder (fr0/fr8/fr10/fr11/fr12/fr13/callee-saved × with/without
constant pins) was run and *no* pin was worth more than the source-shape fix.

## 6bv — 2026-09-29 single pick: `volatile` on a local's DECLARATION is a stack-slot-ORDER lever, and a volatile STORE is a scheduling trap (fn_80070F28, 78.4% → EXACT)

`fn_80070F28` (500 B, QB skater/skin setter) was parked on a 16-word residual
that the draft header declared "a GCC 2.95 `init_local_quantity` artifact, not a
source shape" — after 8 declaration positions of the offending local, a fully
reversed declaration order, 6 declaration types, and a frame-template struct had
all been tried with no effect. Two levers closed it, and both are new.

* **`volatile` on the DECLARATION re-sorts the frame.** Retail's slots are
  `sp8=0x8, on=0xc, bloom1=0x10, bloom2=0x14, strength=0x18, bytes=0x1c,
  color=0x20, bytes=0x24`; plain ngccc 3.9.3 gave `0x8` to `on` and pushed
  `sp8` down to `0x1c`, shifting six other slots by 4. Writing
  `volatile s32 sp8;` reproduced the EXACT retail layout on the first try.
  Notes for reuse: the trigger is the *qualifier on the DECL* — writing the
  same local through a `volatile` lvalue cast while leaving the declaration
  plain is 82.4% vs 85.6%, so it really is the declaration; the declaration
  *position* is still irrelevant (moved to 1st/2nd/last: 78.4% every time);
  and the semantics are unharmed when the variable is an out-param written by
  C and read by an unknown callee. So: **before calling a stack-slot
  displacement a compiler artifact, try `volatile` on that one local** — it is
  a one-word, always-compiles perturbation of the sort.
* **A `volatile` STORE is low-priority to ngccc's block reorderer and sinks to
  just before the call.** With the slot fixed, the residual was the 2-insn
  word round-trip (`lwz buf / stw sp8`) landing AFTER the vtable reads instead
  of before them, plus the fn pointer then taking r9 instead of r0 (a
  *consequence* of the placement — one register serves both in want). Pinning
  the position by casting back to a plain lvalue —
  `*(s32 *)(void *)&sp8 = *(s32 *)buf1;` — makes the store schedulable again
  and both symptoms vanish. **So the two halves are an AND, not a choice:**
  `volatile` decl alone = 85.6%, plain decl + plain store = 79.2%,
  `volatile` decl + non-volatile lvalue store = 100.0%. Rejected at the 90.4%
  stage (all no-ops): staging the round trip through a named temp, hoisting the
  vtable load above the byte stores, and the comma-expression out-param init
  (§6z-128) — the volatile store's priority, not the source order, was
  pinning it.
* Two smaller confirmations in the same function: a **guarded vcall can take
  the tested value as an extra live argument** (§72-143 again — want keeps
  `bloom1` in r4 across the `cmpwi` into the bl as arg1 and reloads `bloom2`
  into r5 as arg2, so the cast is `(s32 (*)(void*,void*,void*))`); and a
  three-constant same-block store run needs the source rotated LEFT by one
  (recipe 24/64).

## 6bs — 2026-09-29 single pick: a `default:` body that is really a **case
### RANGE**, and MB/ME are MSB-relative (fn_801266EC, 32.4% → EXACT, 284B)

Two decode rules, both cheap, both of which silently cost a whole function.

**1. `cmpwi LO; blt <default>; cmpwi HI; ble <body>` in a compare tree means the
source used `case LO ... HI:` — a GCC *case range*. It does NOT mean two adjacent
`case` labels sharing a body.** The two forms lower differently and build
different trees:

| source | lowering |
|---|---|
| `case 3 ... 4:` (range) | `cmpwi 3; blt default; cmpwi 4; ble body` |
| `case 3: case 4: body;` | `cmpwi 3; beq body; bgt body; b default` |

**m2c reports a case RANGE's body as `default:`** (it can't tell the `blt/ble`
pair from a default arm), so a draft whose `default:` holds a real call is the
tell. Restoring the range also re-roots the tree: a range counts as **one** node
in `balance_case_nodes`, so the median shifts (this function's root moved from 7
to 6, and its whole tree from 13 compares to want's exact shape). Corpus
cross-check that confirmed the difference: sibling `fn_8012DE30` has the same
callee set and DOES use `case 3: case 4:` — its want shows the `beq`/`bgt` form.
**Before believing an m2c `default:`, check whether the tree has a
`blt`+`ble` pair over a 2-value span; if so, the source had a range.**
(case-tree steering levers: §70-124, §6ab-125, §6t-6, §6aq-193, §6an-204.)

**2. `rlwinm`/`rlwimi` MB and ME are MSB-relative (MB=0 is the top bit), and on
big-endian GCC allocates bitfields from the MSB down — so a `rlwimi rX,rZ,SH,MB,ME`
field at LSB bits `[lo..hi]` must be declared with exactly `32-1-hi` bits BEFORE
it.** The 1-word fix loop: take the wanted `rlwimi r0, r9, 0x10, 9, 0xf` → mask
= LSB bits 16..22, SH=16 → declare `struct { u32 pre:9; u32 k:7; }` (9 bits before
`k`). Getting this wrong costs exactly one word and is easy to misread as a
"cannot match" (my first attempt put `k` after `u32 lo:16` and got
`rlwimi r0,r9,9,0x10,0x16` — 98.6%).

**3. Two writes of the SAME word at different widths = two VIEWS, so use a
union.** Here the tail cleared LSB bits 16..22 with a 7-bit `rlwimi` while
`case 7` cleared the whole top half with `sth r0,2(r31)` (LSB 16..31) — those
fields overlap, so they cannot both be bitfields of one struct:
```c
union { struct { u16 a; u16 b; } ab;                            /* +0, +2 */
        struct { u32 h9:9; u32 k:7; u32 m9:9; u32 t7:7; } bits; } w;
```
`ab.a` also supplies the `lhz` (a u16 read of the word) that a plain `s32` field
could not. Extends recipe 110 (§6k-110) with the overlapping-view case.

Also confirmed here (no new lever): a `switch` on a `s32` local holding
`(u16)field & 0x7F` emits `lhz` + `rlwinm …,25,31` (not `andi.`), and the
`cmpwi` (signed) tree follows from the `s32` type of the switch expression, so
keep the mask in a `s32` temp.

## 6bw — 2026-09-30: the CORRECT branch-relocation audit (the one in §6bg
### CORRECTION 1 was vacuous, and the *method* was never written down).
`test_wip_drafts` / `gen_leaves.compile_fn` mask REL14 with `0xFFFF0003`, so it
compares the branch's **opcode + BO + BI + AA + LK but never its target**
(recipe 283 / §6aq-245 both warn that a masked 100% can hide a wrong target or
a wrong guard extent; the linked `cmp` is the real proof). §6bf's
"93/93 verified" style audits have been posted without the method — and at
least one was provably vacuous. Here is a procedure that actually works;
it verified 14/14 sites (9 intra-function + 5 call targets) on fn_8005841C.

**1. PPC branch decoding — the BD field is at word bits 15..2, and AA/LK are
the two LOWEST bits.** I wasted several passes assuming the textbook
`BD = x >> 6`, `AA = x>>30`, `LK = x>>31`. The real I-form numbering is
MSB-first after the opcode, so for a branch at address `a` with word `x`:
```python
opc = x >> 26                     # 16 = bc, 18 = b/bl
LK  = x & 1;  AA = (x >> 1) & 1
#  bc:  BD = sign_extend((x >> 2) & 0x3FFF, 14);  BO = (x>>21)&0x1f; BI = (x>>16)&0x1f
#  b/bl:BD = sign_extend((x >> 2) & 0xFFFFFF, 24)
tgt = a + BD*4 if AA == 0 else BD
```
Sanity check on a `beq 0x80058538` at `0x8005845C`: word `0x418200dc` →
BD = `0x37` = 55 words = 0xDC ✓. For `bc` **skip `BO < 3`** (those are the
CTR-decoded forms); `BO=12` is an ordinary `beq` and reading `BO&4` as the
CTR test wrongly drops every conditional branch.

**2. ProDG's assembler emits R_PPC_REL14 (type 11) with a SECTION-RELATIVE
addend — the target's byte offset inside `.text`, NOT a displacement from the
branch instruction.** So `target = fn_addr + addend`. Reading it as a relative
displacement gives targets far past the end of the function, which is the tell
that you have it wrong. **Type 10 is R_PPC_REL24** (the `bl` calls) and its
symbol is the target; resolve the name through `config/G2TE52/symbols.txt`.
(`gen_leaves` imports both `R_PPC_REL14`/`R_PPC_REL24` from elftools, whose
PPC numbering is 10/11 — the *opposite* of what the name suggests here, so
branch on the integer, not the constant name.)

**3. Do the audit on the whole function, not the last diff.** A masked-EXACT
draft can still have every target right or wrong; check the full set at once
so a single mis-set target is visible against a clean table. On fn_8005841C
the block-layout inversion (§4p-10 / §6a-4) moved the cold blocks into place
*and* the 8 REL14 targets came out byte-correct without any further work.

## 6bt2 — 2026-09-29 single pick: a residual "one independent slot between the
`lis` and the `lfs`" is an **alias** problem, and `const` on the constant is the
fix (fn_801AAE94, 94.6% → EXACT, one declaration change, 0 asm)

`fn_801AAE94` (148 B, frameless per-component min/max of two f32 triples) was
parked at 94.6% with a 2-word residual that read like a scheduler tie-break —
`lis`+`lfs` emitted glued together, want has one independent `stfs` between them:

At 0x801AAEFC through 0x801AAF04 retail loads the label page anchor into r9, stores f9 to offset 0 of r5, then loads f0 from the anchor low half, while the build loads the page anchor into r9, loads f0 with zero displacement, then stores f9, swapping the independent store past the load.

Every scheduling flag was a no-op (`-fno-schedule-insns{,2}`, `-fno-sched-spec`,
`-fno-sched-interblock`, `-fno-gcse`, `-Os`/`-O3`, …) and moving the `K = lbl;`
statement anywhere in the source only moved the glued pair. The fix was
**one word in the declaration**:

```c
-    extern f32      lbl_802ABBB4;      /* 94.6%  — anchor pinned before its load */
+    extern const f32 lbl_802ABBB4;      /* 100.0% — anchor hoisted to block top */
     /* lbl_802ABBB4 is a .rodata2 float, so const is the CORRECT declaration */
```

**The mechanism, which is the generalizable part.** The `lis` is the HI16 reload
anchor `reload` creates for `lfs f0,@l(sym)(page)`. Reload freely hoists an
address computation above instructions it can prove independent — including
independent *loads* (there is exactly one other `lis`/`store`/`lfs`-with-a-store
in-gap instance DOL-wide, at 0x80003BAC, and its anchor sits above two
independent `lfs`es) — but it will **not** hoist it above a store that may alias
the address. A store through a `f32 *` parameter may alias anything, so the
anchor got pinned immediately in front of its own load. Qualifying a read-only
(`.rodata`/`.rodata2`) object `const` tells the alias oracle that nothing writes
it, the store stops being a barrier, and the anchor flies to the top of the
shared block while the load stays at its source position — which is exactly
want's order. `extern const volatile f32` also gives 100% (const alone is
enough); `extern volatile f32` **loses** the fix (94.6%) because volatile pins
the load itself in place.

*Diagnostic that identifies it in one step:* the residual is a `lis` (or `addi`)
address anchor separated from its own `lfs`/`lwz`/`addi` consumer by exactly one
**store**. If the insn in the gap is a load, reload already handles it and the
cause is elsewhere; if it is a store, it is the alias barrier. Read the gap
insn's mnemonic before grinding flags — 18 flags and 5 statement positions all
scored 94.6% here, and the answer was the type of the global. This is the
declaration-side sibling of M6.89d/L1 (a pointer-valued global must be declared
`extern T *lbl`) and of the "scalar global at its own width" rule (§285): *the
`const`/`volatile` qualifiers on a global's declaration are codegen levers, not
just semantics.*

## 6bx — 2026-09-29 single pick: **re-measure a `// FLAG:` after the semantic
fixes — a flag load-bearing on a broken body is masking the structure, and its
real reason can be a completely different one** (fn_8002F298, 34.8% → EXACT)

`fn_8002F298` (584B, 3 list walks + a weight accumulation + a dlist splice)
arrived with `// FLAG: -fno-gcse` and a header claiming the flag was worth
+10 points (34.78% vs 24.69% flagless). Every documented note in AGENTS.md
about stale flags says *remove* it, so the obvious first move was to delete it.
Deleting it was right (24.69% at the original score) — **but after the body was
fixed semantically the flag became load-bearing again, for a reason nobody had
recorded, and was worth +30 points** (58.90% → 88.36%).

**Recipe: measure each flag TWICE — once at the inherited baseline, once after
the type/prototype/structure fixes — and if a flag that was "load-bearing" turns
out to be load-bearing *again* for a different reason, find the new reason
before assuming either direction.**

* **The inherited "stale flag" here was load-bearing because the whole body was
  wrong**, not because scheduling needed it: a wrong `f32`→`s32` arg type made
  ngccc emit an int→float dance with a private `.rodata` pool, which inflated
  the FPR frame (0x40 vs 0x30) and added a `f30` save. The flag's +10 was
  coincidental.
* **The same flag's real job is GCSE stopping the merge of two NAMES for one
  value.** Retail has `arg0+0x18` in r11 for its first use and then a
  `mr r29,r11` home copy, both live until the tail. With GCSE on, GCC collapses
  the two names, the `mr` disappears, r11 is freed for the two list-link webs, and
  the **whole callee-saved allocation rotates** (`stmw r27` span, every FPR/GPR
  home). With `-fno-gcse` the home copy survives and everything lands. This is
  §6ay-177 / §6be's "GCSE merges the webs" mechanism landing on a *pointer*
  web rather than a loop-constant one — and it is a **register-allocation**
  symptom, so it looks like doc-15 to triage tools.
* Corollary: a flag's *value* is not a property of the function, it's a property
  of (body, flag) — always re-run the flag sweep after the semantic round.

**Second new item — a mega-merged `Unk_*`/`CStruct` class can be wrong by a
whole-member OFFSET, not just by member type.** M6.89d/§6bf-B only cover a
wrong member *type* (`f32` typed `s32` ⇒ `fctiwz`). Here the shared class
`CStruct` had its link fields at +0x8/+0xC while this function's node really
has them at +0xC/+0x10 — so **every** list access compiled 4 bytes low and the
whole function read as a total structural break. A file-local
`typedef struct { ... } Lst;` with the offsets AND the member types (`f32` at
+0x60/+0x64 ⇒ `lfs`+`fmadds` instead of `mullw`/`xoris`/`stw`/`lfd`/`fsub`) took
43.8% → 91.8% in one edit. Tell: if a pointer-chase draft is at a *low*
percentage but every individual access looks structurally right, check the
offsets of the *first* member you touch, not just the opcodes.

**Third (small, reusable): two structurally-identical walk temps merged into ONE
variable need only ONE hard pin.** §6bg's dual-pin advice (§6ao-166) is for
*disjoint-branch* pins; here the two link webs (`x = node->unk10` outside and
inside the loop) have disjoint live ranges, so collapsing them into a single
`register s32 v __asm__("r9")` variable coloured BOTH sites at once, where two
pins would have fought. Conversely, pinning the *pointer* type is silently
dropped (§76-178), so the pinned variable must be an `s32` with explicit casts
at the `-4`/sentinel arithmetic. Merging first also un-broke the colouring
consistency: separate temps got r11/r3, one temp got r11/r11, one pinned temp
got r9/r9.

## 6by — 2026-09-30: the "one callee-saved register too many" cascade is a
### **CSE'd value live across a call** — cut the CSE with a `"+r"` barrier on
### its INPUT, not on the value (fn_800BD770, 35.4% → 60.6%)

1. **The diagnostic: a uniform "+1 colour" shift over the WHOLE function.**
   If GOT's `stmw` span is one register wider than want's AND the CR slot, the
   GPR save area and every `mr`/callee-saved colour are shifted by exactly one
   (`r28`↔`r27`, `r27`↔`r26`, ...), do **not** start with pins or flags. Read
   GOT's callee-saved map out of the body and find the web that is live
   **across a `bl`** in GOT but recomputed in retail. On fn_800BD770 (127
   insns, 82 diffs) that web was `(u32)ctr ^ 0x80000000` — ngccc CSE'd the two
   identical int→double conversion words (the `cos` half and the `sin` half of
   one loop body), so the xor had to survive both `bl cosf`/`bl sinf` and took a
   9th callee-saved GPR; retail emits the `xoris` twice in scratch `r0` instead.
   Adding `__asm__("" : "+r"(ctr));` **between the two expressions** (a
   zero-code barrier on the *input*, not on the xor) removed the CSE, dropped
   GOT to 8 saved GPRs, and the whole prologue (`stmw r24,0x58` / `stw r12,0x54`
   / both `mr` param homes) went byte-exact in one edit. Caveat: the barrier
   must be placed *between* the two identical expressions — putting it before
   the first one changes nothing.
2. **NEGATIVE (measured, do not re-grind): `fmuls f1, fA, f1` operand order is
   NOT source-reachable.** GCC 2.95 canonicalizes `MULT_EXPR` operand order:
   `a*b` and `b*a` compile to the identical word, so a retail
   `fmuls f1,f26,f1` next to your `fmuls f1,f1,f26` is a wall. The same holds
   for the two `fmuls` sites of an if/else pair — fixing the destination (by
   making the whole expression chain one temp) is reachable and worth ~4 words,
   the operand order is not.
3. **When the SAME pointer is stored at two offsets, retail usually computes
   each address as `base+idx` then a separate `addi +N`, i.e. the offset is
   part of the POINTER, not the store displacement.** Source
   `pf = (char *)(idx + base); *(f32 *)pf = x;` then
   `pf = (char *)(idx + base) + 8; *(f32 *)pf = y;` reproduces
   `add r9,r30,r9; addi r29,r9,8; stfs f1,0(r29)`; the `pf[idx]` /
   `*(f32 *)(pf+8)` forms fold the offset into the store and land one
   instruction short. Also note the index must be the `add`'s **rA** operand
   (§6k-66 offset-first) — `(char *)(idx + (s32)p)`, not `(char *)p + idx`.
   And an `s32`-typed, `register`-pinned address variable is the only form that
   survives: a pointer-typed pin is silently dropped (§76-178) and an unpinned
   `f32 *pf` lets the indexed `stfsx` form win.
4. **Measured negative, worth recording: NEVER hard-pin an argument register
   (r3-r10), even when the source live range does not cross a call.** Pinning
   the loop-carried `tog` web to r7 (its range provably never spans a `bl`,
   because the `cmpwi` consuming it sits in the preheader and the `or.` writing
   it sits in the latch) produced a **structurally broken** object: 8 bytes
   short, the epilogue collapsed, 7.2% from 60.6%. cc1 still reserves r7 as an
   argument register. The same pin class also showed up here as a *legitimate*
   win for r29 (a data register), so the rule is specifically about the
   argument half of the ABI.
5. **Methodology trap that cost a pass: with `R_PPC_ADDR16_HA/LO` and
   `R_PPC_HI/LO` both masked to `0xFFFF0000`, an `extern f32 x;` vs
   `extern f32 x[];` difference is INVISIBLE to the masked score** — the only
   thing that shows up as a diff is the *anchor register*. Do not read a `lis`
   / `lfs` pair mismatch as "wrong address form". (The array form does change
   the reloc type, which a real link cares about, so keep whichever spelling
   the byte-identical sibling in the same zone uses.)

## 6bz — 2026-09-29 single pick: `sched2` reorders BELOW source order, and the
### frozen-vs-TARGET_INSN split is the lever (fn_800626E8, 82.9% → EXACT)

A 140 B paired-single draft parked at 82.9% with **two** "reordering" residuals
and a header blaming the scheduler for both (a `stw` sunk to the end of its
else-block, and the return copy `mr r3,r30` hoisted to the front of the join
block). ~1700 source permutations, a 25-combo flag sweep and all five ProDG
versions had been exhausted without moving them — because the reordering is
done by passes that run **below any source-level influence**.

**1. The diagnostic that settles "is it my C or the scheduler?": run `cc1`
directly and read the RTL across the passes.** `ngccc` is a driver, but
`build/tools/wibo build/compilers/ProDG/<ver>/cc1.exe -O2 -G0 -mcpu=750
-fno-common -mps-float -dr -dj body.c -o body.s` works if you inline
`typedef signed int s32;` etc. (cc1 does **not** preprocess, so drop
`#include`). It writes `body.c.rtl` (post-`reload`) and `body.c.sched2`
(post-`sched2`), each with the per-insn `INSN_COST` and the REG_DEP chain.
Here the **post-reload RTL was already in the retail order**; `sched2` moved
both insns. That immediately ruled out "wrong source shape" and pointed at
passes no source can reach — which is also why every flag and every
permutation had failed.

**2. The mechanism (the generalizable part): `sched2` only reschedules
TARGET_INSNs, and reload pseudos are FROZEN.** In `body.c.sched2`:

| insn | code | TI? | cost | pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `psq_l f0,8(r1)` | `insn:TI 103` | yes | 349 | `*movps_internal1` |
| `stw r0,0x48(r31)` | `insn 54` | **no** | 512 | `movsi+1` |
| `oris r0,r0,0x8000` | `insn 52` | **no** | 127 | `*iorsi3_internal1` |
| `mr r3,r30` (ret) | `insn 78` | **no** | 52 | `*movsi3_internal1` |

Non-TARGET_INSN insns keep their relative order; the TI `movps` pairs float
around them (cheapest-ready-first, verified by simulating the ready sets).
So an int store/copy always *slips past* a PS pair regardless of source
order, and no flag fixes it. **When a NEAR is "an int insn is on the wrong
side of a `psq_l`/`psq_st` pair", the fix is to change that insn's
frozen/schedulable status, not its position.**

* **A `volatile` WRITE with a NON-VOLATILE READ freezes only the store** —
  the load stays schedulable and still hoists to its retail slot:
  `*(volatile u32 *)p = *(u32 *)p | 0x80000000;`
  The obvious `*(volatile u32 *)p |= 0x80000000;` freezes the *read* too,
  which drags the whole `lwz/oris/stw` group past the preceding pair store and
  costs ~6 words. Measured here: plain store 82.9% → volatile read+write
  77.1% → **non-volatile read + volatile write 91.4%**. This "freeze only the
  store" form is new; AGENTS previously only ever used `volatile` on the whole
  statement.
* **A frozen volatile READ fixes a *split* load/store pair**: when want splits
  `psq_l f0,hi` … integer work … `psq_st f0,hi` around an int group, read the
  volatile source into a **named local** *above* that group and store it below
  (`h = sp.hi; flag; *(__ps_t*)p = h;`). The read is frozen in source order
  so it lands above the group and the store below it; reading it inline in the
  store statement lets the whole pair sink (91.4% vs 82.9%).
* **A zero-code memory fence holds a hoisted register copy to the end of a
  basic block.** `__asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory")` between the last
  memory op and the `return` keeps `mr r3,r30` after the final
  `psq_st f0,8(r30)`. Only the `"memory"` clobber works: a `"+r"` identity
  barrier on the returned value (the usual barrier lever) changes nothing, and
  a non-volatile `__asm__("" ::: "memory")` also works. 0 emitted
  instructions, so this is not a transcription (cf. §6ap-11/§6y-129, which use
  the same fence for store→load ordering and for `maybe_reorder_blocks`).

**3. Corollary for triage tools: "an int insn on the wrong side of a PS pair"
looks exactly like a store-order / scheduling park and will burn a whole
session.** Before writing that park note, dump `cc1 -dr` / `cc1 -dj` and check
whether the post-reload RTL already has want's order. If it does, the
remaining levers are frozen-ness and fences, not permutations or flags.

## 6bu2 — 2026-09-30 single pick: in a sum of products, the SOURCE's **second**
### product is the one `fmuls` multiplies (fn_800A7B40, 53.7% → 59.8%)

A `-mps-float` 4×4 f32 matrix×vector (`fn_800A7B40`, 328 B) was parked with a
header that blamed "sched1 hoisting product 2's operand loads above product 1's
— not reachable from any source form tried". Half of that was wrong: it was a
**contraction-assignment** problem, and reading the two streams side by side
settles it in one comparison.

**The rule (measured twice, opposite results).** For a left-associated sum of
N products `p0 + p1 + p2 + p3`, ngccc's FMA contraction puts **p0's multiply
into the `fmadds`** and leaves **p1 as the bare `fmuls` seed**; `p2`, `p3`
always become `fmadds` addends. So the product that retail multiplies with a
lone `fmuls` is the one that must be written **second** in the source:

```c
/* want:  fmuls f13,f13,f0        <- t1 * m10
          fmadds f11,f11,f10,f13 <- t0 * m00 + acc            */
loc.res[0] = vec->unk0x0 * a0 + vec->unk0x4 * b0          /* a0 = m00, b0 = m10 */
           + vec->unk0x8 * c0 + vec->unk0xC * d0;         /* WRONG: fmuls(t0*m00) */
loc.res[0] = vec->unk0x4 * b0 + vec->unk0x0 * a0          /* RIGHT: fmuls(t1*m10)  */
           + vec->unk0x8 * c0 + vec->unk0xC * d0;
```

Swapping the first two terms of all four rows took 53.7% → 57.3% and made
**row 0 byte-exact** (all 12 words, `addi r9` through the second `fmadds`).
Diagnostic that identifies it in one step: a diff where `fmuls` and `fmadds`
occupy the **same slots** but the two 4-byte words are *transposed as pairs of
operands* — i.e. the multiply/add multiply are attached to each other instead
of to the accumulator — is a contraction-assignment bug, not a schedule
problem. A one-instruction `or.`-test-like difference is the same signature.
(`-ffp-contract=` does not exist in ProDG cc1, so this cannot be tuned by
flag; it is a pure source-order lever.)

**Two small follow-ons from the same function:**

* **`volatile` on a `__ps_t` member of a frame struct pins which slot a later
  reload reads** (+1.2%). With
  `struct { __ps_t sp8; volatile __ps_t sp10; f32 res[4]; } loc;` the final
  `psq_l f0,16(r1)` reloads the *copy* slot; plain, GCC CSEs the pair load and
  re-reads `0x20(r1)` (the original `res[2..3]`) instead — same value, wrong
  encoding. `volatile` on `sp8` as well is worse (47.0%): the volatile load
  then re-orders the whole pack.
* **Once the arithmetic matches, the remaining 33 words were a pure sched2
  look-ahead wall** and resisted *everything*: 30+ `-f`/`-m` flags (all
  no-ops or worse), 4 orders of per-row load staging, a next-row "prefetch",
  `volatile f32 *` aliases, 2D vs pointer matrix access, right-association,
  accumulator temps, an unrolled loop, `const`-qualified matrix, and swapped
  declaration order (−25% when wrong, so decl order is a live axis here).
  **Every staging order produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL object** — the front end
  folds single-use temps straight back into the same RTL — which is the cheap
  proof that the residual is post-front-end (sched2) and not reachable by
  source shape. Diagnose it as: *"which two of a row's independent loads does
  ngccc hoist above the previous row's `stfs`?"* (want: the m0 and m2 columns;
  ngccc: the m1 and m0 columns).

## 6ca — 2026-09-29 single pick: three "allocator wall" clusters that were one
### source variable each, and a masked-100 % whose `bne` still targeted the wrong
### block (fn_8004BB2C, 50.5 % → EXACT, 404 B, 1 hard-reg pin, 0 asm insns)

`fn_8004BB2C` (link-list release/re-attach + sentinel-terminated chain walk) had
a header claiming 148 variants exhausted and "4 clusters, all pure GPR
allocator / reload-shape artifacts, no source form found". All four were one
plain-C statement each. The generalisable parts:

* **A single named zero local for N zero-stores keeps the store ahead of an
  independent load in the same block.** With a bare `0` literal per store, cc1
  creates a *fresh* `li` pseudo for the last one; a new constant birth in the
  middle of a block out-prioritises the neighbouring load, so got emitted
  `[li 0][load][stw]` where want has `[stw][load][0x10]`. With
  `s32 z1 = 0;` used by all four stores there is one web, no mid-block `li`, and
  the store keeps its position. 50.5 → 66.3 %. (Related: §6c-28, §73-118,
  §6al-163, §6ap-2 — all about *which* zero register; this is about the mid-block
  `li` birth itself acting as a reorder anchor.)
* **A second source variable does NOT split a web — only a hard-reg pin does.**
  Want loads the chain head into a scratch and then copies it into the loop
  variable's callee-saved home, so the copy doubles as the NULL test
  (`lwz r9,…; …; or. r31,r9,r9; beq`). Writing it as two C variables
  (`h = arg0->f; if (h->f4 == -1) h = 0; walker = h;`) is byte-identical to the
  one-variable form: local_cse unifies the two pseudos and folds the load into
  the home. A `register s32 h __asm__("r9")` on **either** end keeps them apart,
  and the two pins are an **OR** (removing either, or both, still scores EXACT)
  — measure each pin's ablation, because two pins that each fixed a *different*
  cluster can turn out to be alternative routes to the same allocation. (Here a
  third pin, r30 on an unrelated value, was load-bearing at 94.1 % and became
  completely redundant once the r24 pin landed.) Extends §6y-124 / §70-130:
  scratch-web pins work, but the *tell* that you need one is "I added a variable
  and nothing changed".
* **Staging the COMPARED value into its own local before an assignment makes the
  assignment's copy unconditional — a plain-C way to place a `mr` before a
  `cmpwi`.** The loop step `p = p->next; if (p->+4 == -1) p = 0;` lets cc1 sink
  the copy into the sentinel-taken arm (`cmpwi; bne; li r9,0; mr r31,r9`).
  Written `q = p->next; t = q->+4; p = q; if (t == -1) p = 0;` the copy is
  emitted *before* the compare, matching retail. No barrier, no pin. This is the
  plain-C sibling of §6x-127's `v = off; __asm__("" : "+r"(v))` live-range-split
  barrier — reach for the staged local first. 94.1 → 98.0 %.
* **The last two words (`mr r4,r9` vs want's `mr r3,r25; mr r4,r24`) are a
  *call-argument* register choice: the `&stack_obj` must be read from its
  callee-saved home (r24), not from the scratch its address was born in (r9).**
  `register s32 p __asm__("r24"); p = (s32)&sp8;` where only the two call sites
  use `p` (the member stores keep the r9 birth) fixes it. 98.0 → 100.0 %.
  Related: §6bg-4 (name the base so a load can pin it) and §6bq ("asm birth
  fixes existence, hard pin fixes colour") — here the birth already existed and
  only the *colour* of the call-argument read was wrong. A `"+r"(pA)` barrier
  also fixes those two words but costs 8 elsewhere, so **when a barrier and a
  pin both address a web, score the pin** (pins perturb allocation less).
* **HAZARD re-confirmed (§6bw's method, and it caught a real semantic bug here):
  a masked 100 % said nothing about a branch's target.** The word stream was
  byte-identical with the second `held = 0` and the whole chain walk placed
  *after* the equality test instead of *inside* it — retail's `bne` at
  0x8004BB88 leaves the block (target 0x8004BC84) while the draft's branched to
  the fall-through store. Decoding all 26 `.rela.text` entries
  (`R_PPC_REL14` type 11 with a *section-relative* addend, so
  `target = fn_addr + addend`; `R_PPC_REL24` type 10 via the symbol name) found
  it immediately: 1 mismatch of 26, 0/26 after the fix. **Run the REL14 audit on
  any 96-100 % draft before calling it done** — a masked branch mask
  (`0xFFFF0003`) keeps BO/BI/AA and hides the extent entirely.

## 6cb — 2026-09-29 single pick: a *symbol address* want straddles a `bl` ⇒ make it a named local, and a value want re-cycles across two callee-saved colours ⇒ split it in two and pin each half (fn_8016CD30, 34.9% → 91.1%, 2 levers)

A QB-`viewer_controller` constructor (4 script nodes + 2 float globals + a global
self-pointer). Two findings, both structural rather than scheduling, each worth far
more than any flag or ordering sweep:

* **When want emits a `lis`/`addi` symbol pair with a `bl` in BETWEEN it and the
  store that consumes it, the source materialised the address into a variable that
  is live across that call.** Writing `n->f = (s32)fn_X;` inline lets ngccc
  sink the pair to just before the store, in a *caller-saved* scratch register — the
  value never becomes a callee-saved pseudo, and the whole `stmw`/`lmw` span,
  saved-register count and every register colour in the function then diverge.
  Writing
  ```c
  tmpf = (s32)fn_X;        /* the address becomes a value that lives across the call */
  fn_80009B04(n, 0);
  n->unk0x1C = tmpf;
  ```
  reproduces want's `lis/addi … bl … stw` shape and makes the callee-save span
  appear. **48.5% → 68.3% here, and it fixed the frame, the save/restore and the
  register map in one edit** — far bigger than any diff it explains individually.
  Generalisable tell: *count the calls between a constant's `lis` and its
  consumer; if it is non-zero, the constant is a variable in the original, not an
  expression.* Related but distinct from §6e-32/§6w-128 (that is about a *call's
  argument* surviving; this is about a *stored address* surviving).

* **When one C variable appears in two halves of a function that want gives
  DIFFERENT callee-saved registers, split the variable and pin each half.** Here
  the four function-pointer constants all went through one `s32 tmpf`, and ngccc
  gave it one register for all four; want's constants live in r30 for nodes 1&2
  and in r29 for nodes 3&4 — *swapped* relative to the node-pointer webs (r29 /
  r30). One variable, one colour, period. Two variables — `tmpa` for the first
  pair, `tmpb` for the second — each pinned to the register its half wants,
  reproduce it: **70.3% → 83.2%**. This is the *inverse* of §70-130d / §74-162
  ("reassign one pinned var to its next role") and of §6z-130 ("collapse to one
  var so it recycles"): here the two roles must stay apart because want's register
  *recycling* runs in the opposite direction to the obvious one.

* **Ablation discipline paid again:** with `tmpa`/`tmpb` pinned, three other pins
  (the long-lived getter result → r26, and the two rodata2 name constants → r28 /
  r27) became **completely inert** — removing any one produced byte-identical
  output. The earlier 5- and 7-pin sets scored *worse* (88.1% / 83.2%). Measure
  each pin's ablation before adding a neighbour; a pin that looks load-bearing in
  isolation can be made redundant by a different one.

* **Cost of the final 9 words:** one 11-instruction window where ngccc hoists a
  live-across-call symbol pair to just *before* the call while want emits it just
  *after*, with two `lfs` page anchors sandwiched between the `lis` and the `addi`.
  Every statement position, node-store permutation, anchor staging form, 6
  scheduling flags, `+r`/`+f`/memory-fence wedges and node/const pin sets were
  measured and are listed in `src/wip/fn_8016CD30.c`. A zero-instruction
  `__asm__("" : "+r"(x))` on the *other* pinned const is load-bearing (+1 word) and
  was required in combination with the statement position (an AND). The remaining
  lever is a 2-insn `lis`/`addi` asm anchor for the hoisted symbol with hard-pinned
  outputs, so its LUID can be pinned independently of the call.

* **Also confirmed here:** file-local `typedef struct { char *name; void (*fn)(void);
  void *parent; }` replacing the corpus-merged `CScript` `s32 unk0xNN` fields was
  **byte-for-byte neutral** (90.10% either way) — the merged class was *not*
  wrong here, so don't spend a M6.89d iteration when the access widths already
  match. And every `lis`+`addi` was re-decoded by hand and checked against
  `symbols.txt` (all 15 real), because the masked score cannot see a wrong label
  (AGENTS hazard 277).

## 6cc — 2026-09-29 single pick: **`volatile` on a scalar CONSTANT LOAD is a
### scheduling lever that BUYS REGISTER REUSE**, and it also pins the load WIDTH
### (fn_800B6694, 82.4% → 88.55%)

Two independent wins on one 131-word function, both from the same `volatile`
spelling on a *load through a pointer to a global constant*. Every documented
use of `volatile` in this project so far has been about DEAD-STORE survival,
memory-clobber ordering, frame-slot sorting or a self-init store — this is the
first one where `volatile` acts purely as a **sched-pinning** and **mode-pinning**
device on a *live, non-trapping* load, with no semantic change at all.

**1. `volatile` on a float constant load stops ngccc hoisting it, which is what
lets the allocator reuse a dead FPR.** When a single basic block loads N
`extern f32` constants, the `sched` pass hoists *all* of them to the top of the
block, so all N are simultaneously live at the allocation point and the
allocator needs N distinct FPRs with **no reuse** — even though retail's code
re-uses a register because one constant's range dies early. A `volatile` load is
not schedulable, so it stays at its statement; the earlier constant's range is
already dead by then and the allocator hands it the same FPR.

```c
/* 82.4% -> 83.2% on its own; 88.55% combined with the run order below */
vp[3] = *(volatile f32 *)&lbl_802988F0;   /* the 1.0f */
```
GOT before: all five constants loaded at the top, colours f12/f13/f0/f10/f11,
no reuse, and retail's `lfs f0,-0x7710(r11)` (a *re-used* f0, emitted after the
`fmuls`) unreachable. GOT after: the 1.0f load is emitted right after the
`addi`/`mr r30` pair and lands in **the same f0** the 0.1f used — a byte-exact
match for that pair. **Diagnostic that identifies a candidate in one step:** a
NEAR whose residual is a *rotation of FPR colours* plus "retail re-uses a
register I have to give to a 5th value" is this, not a pins problem. Note
`volatile` on the OTHER constants is a no-op or a 2-word regression, and — see
§6bf-A/§6bg — the `frN` hard-reg pins that used to squeeze the colours out are
now *harmful*, because they forbid exactly the reuse the volatile buys.

**2. `volatile` on an integer load keeps the DECLARED WIDTH — and stops a real
cc1 narrowing bug that moves the wrong byte.** `st.a0C = (s8)*(s32 *)(p + 0x18);`
compiled to `lbz r0, 0x1b(r9)` — byte **3** of the word (offset 0x18 + 3), not
byte 0 — followed by `stb`. Retail has `lwz r0, 0x18(r9)` + `stb`: the
truncation belongs on the *store*, not the *reload*. A volatile load must be
emitted at its declared width, so:

```c
st.a0C = (s8)*(volatile s32 *)((char *)self->mgr + 0x18);   /* 87.8% -> 88.55% */
```
The `s8`/`u8` cast, a `& 0xFF` mask, a file-local struct member, and a staged
`s32` temp all reproduce the bad narrowing; only the volatile does not. Related
to §6ay item 2 (a `clrlwi` that only appears when the widened value carries two
live names): the general rule is that **`volatile` on the LOAD is the only lever
that controls the load's WIDTH** — a cast at the consumer is a scheduler-level
hint, not a mode constraint.

**3. The store run that the reuse enables also has an order to get right, and
it is a hand-picked permutation, not a rotation.** With the F0 load pinned, the
four `stfs` come out in retail's order only for the source sequence
`vp[3]; vp[2]; vp[1];` (0x3C, 0x38, 0x34) — all six permutations of the run
score 84.7–88.55%, and in every one the LAST store of the run is hoisted to
second position by `sched`, so retail's order is not simply source order.

**4. Two register-copy stores in one block: the order of the two ASSIGNMENTS
decides the emission order, and retail's is the one that looks "wrong".**
`st.a0C = <volatile load>` must be written *before* `st.a10 = arg2;`; the other
order hoists the plain `stw` above the dependent `sth` (84.0% → 87.8%). This is
§6ca's "stage the value the scheduler must not hoist" in a two-store form, and it
is the *conjunction* shape §6bf-A warns about: the volatile (lever 2) is worth
nothing without it.

**What is still parked (15 words, one block, 0x800B66B0–0x800B6700):** the two
leading constant loads come out in the opposite ORDER, which swaps the `lis`
page colours. `cc1 -drtl`/`-dcombine` proves the RTL order is the source order,
so the swap is `sched`, and the constant whose result has the most USERS
(here the one feeding two `stfs`) is always pulled to the top regardless of
statement order, declaration order, or which loads are `volatile`. Every
sched/optimisation flag is a no-op or a regression. Recorded so the family is
not re-grinded blindly: the next idea is a real dependency on the multi-use
constant's load (bitfield or struct-copy view), or a small volatile-asm window
around the `fmuls` + first two `lfs`.

## 6br — 2026-09-29 single pick: the HI16 anchor colour set is `{r9, r11, r10, …}`
### (only the first TWO are usable for a two-anchor block), and `reorder_basic_block`
### sorts a 1-user constant `lis` ABOVE a 0-user volatile store (fn_801B6EB8, 80.6% → EXACT)

`ShouldExecuteAction` (0x801B6EB8) is a 36-instruction QB wrapper whose *only*
residual was a 7-word window around the manual int→double store pair. Three
findings, each independently reusable:

**1. `lis r10` is reachable from plain C, but only as the THIRD simultaneously-live
HI16 anchor — so a two-anchor block can never get `{r11, r10}`.** A minimal probe
(`double h(double d, float f){return d + *(double*)sa + (double)(f * *(float*)sb)
+ *(double*)sc;}`) compiles to `lis r9` / `lis r11` / `lis r10` for three live
anchors. But any block with only TWO live anchors always gets **`{r9, r11}`** —
`lbl_802AC1D0 → r9`, `lbl_802AC1D8 → r11` — while retail wants `r11` / `r10`. This
is *not* a spelling gap and *not* a compiler-version gap: `extern f64` vs
`extern f32 x[]` + `x[0]` vs `extern char x[]` + `*(f32 *)&x`, `(sym-4)`/`(sym+8)`
alias symbols, both mention orders, staging locals, and **all five in-tree ProDG
builds (3.5 / 3.5b140 / 3.7 / 3.8.1 / 3.9.3) produce byte-identical output**. Nor
can a `register` local pin it: a `register char *pg __asm__("r11")` holding a
symbol address is ignored by the *reload* pass (the anchor still lands in r9) —
reconfirms §6bg-7 that pins bind pseudoes, not reloads. So doc 73's rule stands,
with the refinement that the set is `{r9, r11, r10, r8, …}` in preference order
and the count of *simultaneously live* anchors decides how deep you reach. The
only route to `{r11, r10}` for a two-anchor block is the §6bg-recipe-6 asm anchor
(3 `lis` here, 8.3% of the function):
```c
extern char lbl_802AC1D0[];                       /* "s" constraint needs an array */
register s32 pg_d0 __asm__("r11");
__asm__ volatile("lis %0,%1@ha" : "=r"(pg_d0) : "s"(lbl_802AC1D0));
...
*(f64 *)(pg_d0 + PG_D0)          /* PG_D0 = signed page-relative delta, -0x3E30 */
```
The register holds the symbol's **PAGE**, so the C side adds the page-relative
delta and the low half folds back into the load displacement — the `@ha` reloc is
still against the real symbol, so the link is unaffected.

**2. A 1-user `lis <const>` is sorted ABOVE a 0-user volatile store, and no flag
fixes it.** `reorder_basic_block` sorts by (priority desc, list order) with
priority = number of users of the result (§6bg recipe 8), so retail's
`[stw r3,0x14][lis r0,0x4330][anchor][anchor][stw r0,0x10]` becomes
`[lis r0,0x4330][stw r3,0x14]…` in plain C. Tried and inert: reversing the two
union stores (72.2%, and the pair then floats above the `bl`), a named `u32 t`
temp, `"m"`/memory-clobber/`"=r"` barriers between the stores, and 15
sched/optimisation flags (only `-fno-schedule-insns` moves anything, and it is
much worse). Fix: emit the constant `lis` as a third `volatile` asm — the
`volatile` order then pins it. **Corollary that proves the source shape:** a
*plain `f64` local* assigned by `(f64)(s32)x` reproduces the window byte-exactly
(same slot, same r11/r10 anchors) but ProDG's DFmode lowering **duplicates the
subtraction** (`fsub f0,f0,f13` then `fsub f0,f0,f12`) and drags in a `.rodata`
pool anchor retail does not have — so retail's source is the manual two-word
union, and the union is the only plain-C form that is even close.

**3. `volatile` asm changes the *following* load order, so the constant-placement
wedge and the anchor wedges are an AND.** With the two anchors as `volatile` asm
but the constant in plain C, the object is 1 word off (the `lis r0,0x4330` lands
after the anchors); add a zero-code `"+r"` barrier and it is 2 words off (the
`lfs f12`/`lfd f0` pair then swaps). Only all three `lis` in asm + the
`// FLAG: -fno-schedule-insns2` that stops the post-reload scheduler from moving
the `lfs`/`lfd` pair across them gives 0 diffs. Measure the trio, not the pair
(§6bf-A), and remember `-fno-schedule-insns2` is only load-bearing *because* the
asm is there — remove the asm and the flag is a no-op.

## 6cs — 2026-09-29 single pick: a NESTED-SCOPE hard register pin buys the
### "born in a scratch, copied UP into the loop home" shape that a
### function-scope pin forbids — and a ONE-WORD prologue gap misaligns
### ~140 words (fn_80093820, 51.0% → EXACT, 12 levers, 0 emitted asm)

`fn_80093820` (1176 B, 294 insns) was a *size-exact* m2c draft at 51.0% — the whole
task was register allocation. Two findings generalise well past it.

**1. A single missing word in the prologue misaligns the entire function, so
count words before reading diffs.** Want's prologue ends with 12 loads + 12 stores
+ an extra `mr r21, r30`; m2c had ONE web for that pointer, so GOT was one word
short and everything after the first `bl` was compared against the wrong index —
144 "diffs" that were really 2 structural facts. **Diagnostic: dump the per-index
WANT|GOT, and find the first index where `got[i] == want[i+1]` (or `+k`); the shift
is `k` words and every diff downstream of it is noise.** Fixing the missing web
(and pinning the *other* copy of it) also fixed the whole 12-FPR prologue
rotation and a call's arg-move order for free — so never start at the first
visible diff.

**2. A `register s32 x __asm__("rN")` pin at FUNCTION scope makes the compiler
emit the defining instruction DIRECTLY into rN; the same pin in a NESTED scope
(an inner block wrapping the use) lets the value be born in a scratch and copied
up into rN — which is what §6s-1's "init → copy" pattern wants.** Measured on one
3-word residual that resisted ~10 source shapes (a second pointer variable, a
comma-assignment call arg, `"+r"` barriers, `volatile`, the whole
M8.31 return-type/param-type matrix):

```c
/* WRONG:  addi r22, r1, 0x68 ; li r3,4 ; mr r4, r22        (99.0%) */
register s32 sp68_s __asm__("r22");
...
sp68_s = (s32)&locals.sp68;
fn_8001EF84(4, (s32 *)sp68_s);

/* RIGHT:  addi r4, r1, 0x68 ; mr r22, r4 ; li r3,4         (EXACT) */
fn_8001EF84(4, &locals.sp68);
{   register s32 sp68_s __asm__("r22");   /* nested scope wraps the loop */
    sp68_s = (s32)&locals.sp68;
    do { ... sp68_s ... } while (...);
}
```
This is the **inverse** of §6as-3/§7c-3 (where a nested pin is used to reserve a
*dead* slot without a save): there the nesting is the point, here the nesting is
what un-poisons the birth. It also composes with the caveat in §73-151 — do **not**
put the same variable in a hard pin at two scopes. Disclosed cost: zero emitted
instructions, so asm density stays 0.

**3. Pin ONE member of a colour-permuted group, not all of them.** The last block
was three webs whose callee-saved colours were cyclically rotated
(want `sp68=r22, one=r23, acc=r25`; GOT `one=r22, acc=r23, sp68=r25`). Pinning
**only** `&locals.sp68` to r22 made the other two fall into place on their own —
pinning all three measured *identically*. Generalises §6ca-2 / §6ca's
"measure each pin's ablation": when N webs are permuted, the pin that removes one
web from the free pool re-orders the rest for free.

**4. A pointer that only a LATER call needs must be passed as the array, not the
saved pointer — that lets its web die and become a scratch, dropping GOT from 12
to 11 callee-saved registers and re-aligning the whole allocation** (83.7% here).
Same family as §6al-180's `volatile` per-site remat, but the fix is in the *call
argument*, not the variable: `fn(sp8p, 0)` early and `fn(locals.sp8, 0)` late.

**5. Preheader BIRTH order assigns callee-saved colours, and only the first
statement's position matters for the two loop-carried pointers.** Five `= 0/1/
ptr/3` inits, 8 hand-tried permutations: `sp70base` first → 94.2%, every other
order → 87-89%. §6o-184/§76-184 said "declaration order assigns roles"; this is
the sharper form — for a *set* of loop-carried webs it is the position of the
FIRST init that flips a colour, and no later statement can compensate.

**6. Value reuse across a guard: name the value a condition tests.** Want
`lwz r31,0x6c(r9); cmpwi r31,0; bne` then `stw r31` reuses r31; the `A && f(p) == 0
{ … *q = f(p); }` spelling made GCC re-load (it cannot prove `f(p)` survives the
call between), costing 2 words and ~100 words of alignment. `(v = f(p)) == 0` in
the condition fixes it (+3.4%). Recipe 57 staging with the assignment *in* the
condition.

**Negative results worth recording:** re-splitting three float reads as
`register f32 __asm__("frN")` pins works only for the **middle** one of a rotated
triple (98.0%); pinning the first or the third scored 96.6% each. And a
function-scope `r31` pin for a stack/global base **pushes arg0 out of r28**
(stmw base and frame both shift, 69.0%) — reserve high registers with a
*nested* pin or not at all.

## 6cv — 2026-09-30 single pick: the OPERAND ORDER of a post-decrement loop
### condition decides whether the latch copy exists at all (fn_802351F4,
### 31.1% → EXACT 476B; 12 levers, 0 emitted asm)

`fn_802351F4` (a manager constructor: byte-writer fill + a 0x3A×0xE8 dword clear
+ 8 `sprintf`/CRC rounds) went from a size-exact 31% m2c draft to byte-exact on
**plain C plus two EMPTY identity barriers**. The headline finding is one line of
C that is *invisible to every diff-based tool*:

**`while (n-- != 0)` and `while (0 != n--)` compile differently, and only the
second matches retail.** GIMPLE always materialises the post-decrement's
*pre*-value, so the left form emits a 4-instruction latch
`mr r0,n; cmpwi r0,0; addi n,-1; bne`, while the right form lets the front end
fold the copy away and emits retail's 3-instruction
`cmpwi n,0; addi n,-1; bne` (the `addi` is parked in the compare→branch gap,
which is legal because `addi` does not set LT/GT/EQ — the same "unrelated
increment between cmpwi and the branch" that loop 2 of the same function has
naturally). Measured across 20 C spellings of that latch and every ProDG build
(3.5 / 3.7 / 3.8.1 / 3.9.3) and 13 scheduling flags: **only the operand order
distinguishes them**; nothing else does. `for(;;){...if(n){n--;continue;}break;}`
and the goto form both give `cmpwi; beq; addi; b` (4 insns, `beq`), and
`while(n){...n--;}` / `for(;n;n--)` fuse to `addic. rX,rX,-1; bne` (2 insns).
*When a countdown latch is 3 instructions with the decrement in the
compare→branch gap, try flipping the comparison's operand order before anything
else* — it is free, and the 1-word difference shifts the whole rest of the
function (that one word was worth ~45 points here on its own).

Three supporting levers, all verified byte-exact on the same function:

* **Two same-valued zero-init webs in one basic block are front-end-CSE'd onto
  ONE `li`; an EMPTY `__asm__("" : "+r"(x))` identity barrier on one of them,
  placed immediately after its assignment, splits them and costs zero emitted
  instructions.** Retail had `li r0,0` … `li r0,0` in the same block (the
  intervening loop clobbers r0, so the value is re-materialised); with one C
  variable GCC merged the two `li`s with the loop counter's `li` and the
  whole tail shifted by one word (55 → 95 points). This is the "second
  zero-init gets a fresh `li`" family of §6c-28 / §73-118 / §6ap-2, extended:
  those levers *provoke* the split by source ordering, this one *forces* it when
  ordering alone cannot (both zeros are 0 in the same block, so any order
  merges).
* **A `Hi`-style second struct reached through ONE page base is what forces the
  12th saved register.** All four accesses ≥ `self+0x10000` go through a single
  `addis rX,31,1` (r26) that must live across the three `sprintf` calls, and
  that value is what makes the save span `stmw r20,0x188` / `lmw r20` (12 GPRs,
  frame 0x1b8) instead of `stmw r21` (11). Writing them as `self->unk0x1772C`
  on a merged `Unk_*` class gives `stw off(r31)` displacements instead and the
  span drops to 11 — a −8 point regression that looks like an unrelated
  register-allocation problem. The base must be born **after** the previous
  loop that also needs `self+0x10000`, or it gets CSE'd with it (that cost
  40 → 18 points when tried the other way round).
* **M8.31 again, in its purest form: a `void` callee whose result is discarded
  still changes its call's RTL, and the return type flipped the FIRST of three
  identical-shaped calls' arg-setup order** so `addi r3,31,0x3524` moved from
  before the six `li r4..r9,0` to after them (94.96 → 100.0). The other two
  calls (which share 5 of the 6 `li`s) are unaffected. Read the want's arg
  order before assuming a scheduling flag is needed — `void`↔`s32` was free
  and exact.

Also re-confirmed while closing this one: three `0x80`-byte `sprintf` buffers
(not `s32` slots) give the exact 0x1b8 frame and the `sp8`/`sp88`/`sp108`
spacing r1+8/0x88/0x108; and the two store runs in the same block rotate in
OPPOSITE directions (recipe 24/64 per-store-class), so they must be fixed
independently — source `[0x80,0x84,0x88,0x8c]` emits `[0x8c,0x80,0x84,0x88]`
while the neighbouring 5-run needs its last two swapped the other way.

## 6cw — 2026-09-29 single pick: a per-LOOP register/FPR rotation is fixed by giving each loop its OWN set of local variables — pointer set first, then the PS staging set (fn_800BA704, 89.3% → 98.3%)

`fn_800BA704` (708 B, `-mps-float`, three near-identical vertex-transform loops)
was parked at 89.3% with a 3-word GPR rotation in loop 3's preheader **plus** a
12-word cascade after it, which the previous session had attributed to the
rotation ("the psq_l is hoisted early, which pushes the accumulator onto
f12/f11/f8, which forces the psq_st/psq_l base"). **The cascade is a second,
independent rotation — and both fall to the same plain-C lever.**

**The tell.** Retail assigns *different* hard registers to the *same role* in a
later loop than in the earlier ones:

Loops 1 and 2 compute the pairs pointer into r6 from frame offset 8 and the output pointer into r7 as r0 plus r9, while loop 3 computes its end into r6 as r9 minus 0x10, computes the pairs pointer into r7 instead of r6 from frame offset 8, and computes the output pointer into r8 instead of r7.

and the same in the FPR class: retail loads the acc[0..1] pair into the register
the acc[2] accumulator *just died in* — f13 in loops 1/2, **f0 in loop 3**.

**The fix is semantic, not an allocation lever, and it comes in two steps:**

1. **Give the divergent loop its own POINTER set** (`tp3`/`pp3`/`end3`/`stride3`
   instead of sharing `tp`/`pp`/`end`/`stride` with the other loops):
   89.3% → **92.1%** — the preheader rotation AND the whole 12-word tail cascade,
   including the base register of the second output store's reload.
2. **Then give it its own PS/FPR staging set** (`pq3`/`P3`/`Q3`/`e33` instead of
   sharing `pq`/`P`/`Q`/`e3`): 92.1% → **98.3%** — the FPR rotation, and it also
   stops `sched1` from hoisting `psq_l f?,24(r1)` two instructions early into the
   accumulator's slot. Killing sched1 with `-fno-schedule-insns` DOES put the
   `psq_l` in the right slot, but collapses the function to 18.1% — so the hoist
   is a *consequence* of the merged staging webs, not an independent wall.

**Why it works, and the boundary.** The allocator sees one pseudo per *variable*,
not per *use site*: a `tp` written in three disjoint loop regions is three pseudos
that get recycled from the same hardregs, which is exactly why cc1 handed loop 3
the same `r6`/`r7` and the same FPR the other two loops use. Retail's source
evidently had separate locals per loop, so its loop 3 had to win fresh registers.
This is §6an-3 / §6bu / §6al-184 ("one variable per web / per phase") applied at
the **loop** level rather than the statement level, and it is the PS-mode twin of
§6cx's GPR result.

**Boundary — do NOT over-apply it.** Splitting *every* loop (loops 1 and 2 each
given their own `stride`/`data`/`pf` too) drops the function to **78.5%**: loop 2's
`stride` then leaves `r10` for `r8`, so retail really does share `stride`, `data`
and `pf` between loops 1 and 2 and only the *third* loop is a separate source
block. Measure each split separately; the rule is "give the loop whose register
assignment DIFFERS its own variables", not "give every loop its own variables".

**Also measured and dead on this body** (all on the 92.1% base, so re-measure if
you are below 98.3%): memory fence `__asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory")` before
the pair load (92.1%, and it swaps the acc[1] `lfs`/`fmadds` pair); `"+f"` barriers
on `pq`/`P`/`e3` in 4 placements (83.6/83.6/91.0/92.1); moving the pair load
before/after the acc[2] chain, the acc[3] store, or the `pairs[0]` store (all
89.8–92.1); `if (x)` vs `if (x != 0)`, a file-local flag typedef, and
`*(s32 *)((char *)pf + 0x20)` (all 92.1% no-ops); an inverted guard plus
`goto skip3` (92.1%); `volatile __ps_t` pair read, `volatile f32` acc, volatile
pair store (all 92.1%); every scheduling/GCSE flag (98.3% no-ops,
`-fno-schedule-insns` 18.1%, `-fno-schedule-insns2` 58.2%, `-Os` 47.5%, `-O1` 7.9%).

**Bonus finding for the remaining 3 words (documented in the draft header).** A
`ps_mr` (the Gekko PS copy, primary opcode 4 with xo5=8 and frC=2) has **no
plain-C spelling in this cc1**: every V4SF copy it can construct is coalesced into
the source register, and the one form that forces a surviving reload (store the
pair through an *array name*, read it back through a *pointer* — the array-name
read is forwarded and collapses the object by 3 words) always yields a real
`psq_l`. There is no `__builtin_ps_mr` in cc1.exe (full builtin list checked).
`__asm__("ps_mr %0,%1" : "=f"(o) : "f"(P))` — 1 insn per loop, 1.7% of the
function — is a **net loss** (71.8% plain / 44.1% volatile / 71.8% `"=&f"` /
74.0% per-loop outputs) because the extra instruction re-rolls the FPR
allocation of the whole loop (cc1 picks f10/f11 for the asm output and swaps
f12/f13). A `register f32`/`register __ps_t` pin tied to the asm output either
ICEs or is silently dropped. **When a PS residual is exactly "a reload where
retail has a `ps_mr`", stop — the length is already right and the instruction is
retail's allocator making a suboptimal choice.**

## 6cx — 2026-09-29: **`register __ps_t x __asm__("frN")` pins DO bind** (the
### §6bd claim is wrong), and a single-use PS *reload* is steerable by them
### (fn_800A0F2C, 78.8% → 80.8%)

§6bd records "`register __ps_t x __asm__("frN")` is silently DROPPED by cc1
2.95.2/3.9.3 — PS/vector register vars do not bind at all; PS colour fixes must
come from the source shape, never a pin." **That is false for `-mps-float`
`__ps_t` locals in ProDG 3.9.3.** Positive control on fn_800A0F2C, same body,
only the pin register changed:

| pin on the `__ps_t` holding `obj->unk0x58` | emitted `psq_l` | score |
|---|---|---|
| none | `psq_l f10,88(r3)` | 41/52 (78.8%) |
| `__asm__("fr11")` | `psq_l f10,88(r3)` | 41/52 (78.8%) |
| `__asm__("fr12")` | **`psq_l f12,88(r3)`** | **42/52 (80.8%)** |
| `__asm__("fr0")` | `psq_l f0,88(r3)` (clashes) | 32/52 (61.5%) |

The register really is being chosen by the pin (fr12 reproduces retail's `f12`,
fr0 puts it in f0 and breaks the whole block). Two caveats that match the
existing guidance: a pin to a register the allocator wanted for a *different*
web makes things much worse, and pinning an **`f32`** operand (here the 12.0f
divisor) broke the `fmr`+`fdivs` tail (48%) — so pin the PS-typed value, not the
scalar.

What makes it worth doing: retail's FPR choice for these normalized-distance
functions is a *rotation* of the whole block (its preferred order here is
`f13, f0, f12, f11, f10` — the multiply web takes f13 and the madd web f0, exactly
as in the PROMOTED siblings `src/fn_800A07F0.c` / `fn_800A1230.c`), and one
rotation of the load registers shifts every later `ps_*` word. When the residual
is "every PS word differs by a register number, same shape", **pin one of the
loads and re-diff before re-running any source-shape permutation** — the pin is
zero emitted instructions and one edit moved two words. Related: §6y-124/§70-130
(scratch-web pins), §6bw (`frN` prefix required), and the per-constant L4-style
"decide per web, not per function" rule.

## 6cy — 2026-09-30 single pick: a loop whose arg0 setup want puts in BOTH test
### blocks is a SOURCE-SHAPE property (birth the arg web in the loop CONDITION),
### and a "2-word residual" can hide a missing call + a wrong pointer type
### (fn_800B2CB8, 52.8% → EXACT, 1440 B, 0 emitted asm)

`fn_800B2CB8` (a QB skater-model constructor, `-mps-float`, 360 words) had been
hand-rebuilt and parked at 52.8% with a header claiming one 2-word residual —
`mr r3, r9` (the GEOMS loop's arg0 setup) in the loop's pre-test and latch
blocks instead of at the top of the body — was a "loop-invariant hoist /
arg-setup placement artifact, not a semantic difference" and that the three
"tried and rejected" shapes were exhaustive. **All three claims were wrong**;
the loop was matchable and the residual was also hiding two unrelated defects.

### 1. The loop recipe: birth the argument web INSIDE the loop condition

*Diagnostic that identifies it in one step.* Want's loop has `mr r3, r9` in
BOTH test blocks (pre-test and latch) and **none** in the body:

At 0x2F54 the pre-test loads the slot into r9, zeroes r31, loads offset 4 into r0, moves r9 into r3 and compares unsigned branching to end on greater-or-equal, at 0x2F6C the body moves r31 into r4 and calls the checksum routine, and at 0x2FC0 the latch reloads the slot, increments r31, reloads offset 4, moves into r3, compares and branches back to the body on less-than.

so the body (which has two predecessors) needs no copy — the arg-setup is
*duplicated by retail into both predecessors*. **GCC 2.95.2/3.9.3 never does
that from a plain loop**: verified against ~20 loop shapes (for / while /
guarded do-while / goto state machine / comma conditions / `volatile` / every
pin) and every `-f` flag cc1 accepts, plus all five in-tree ProDG builds —
the copy is always born at the top of the body, which is one word short and
shifts ~90 words of the rest of the function. **A 1-word length difference in a
loop is worth ~40 points of masked score, so always check the length before
reading any residual as a scheduling problem (§6cs-1, §6cv).**

The route — put the argument variable's *birth* in the condition with a **GNU
statement expression**:

```c
arrp_s = (s32)sp244;                 /* seeds the pre-test block */
for (j = 0; j < (u32)({ arrp_s = (s32)sp244;   /* reload each test */
                         nc    = ((CStruct *)arrp_s)->unk0x4;
                         a3    = arrp_s;         /* <-- arg0 BORN HERE */
                         nc; }); j++) {
    sp240 = GetChecksum((CStruct *)a3, j);
    ...
}
```

* `a3 = arrp_s` inside the condition makes the arg0 web born in the test block;
  `local-alloc` then gives it the **arg register r3** directly, so the call needs
  no copy and the test block supplies it for both the entry and the back edge.
* **The `nc` temp is LOAD-BEARING** (91.94% → 99.44% when added). Without it GCC
  coalesces `a3` with `arrp_s` and reads the bound as `lwz r0, 4(r3)` — the right
  instructions in the wrong order with the wrong base register. Reading the
  bound through `nc` (a dying temp) keeps it off the argument register.
* The redundant-looking `arrp_s = (s32)sp244;` on the line before the loop is
  load-bearing too: it is what seeds the pre-test block's reload. Removing it
  drops 360 → 359 words.
* Statement expressions compile in ngccc 3.9.3 (`({ ... })`), but a *bare*
  `__asm__` used as an expression does not — put the asm INSIDE `({ })`.
* Related: this is the loop-shaped member of the "birth order / web-identity"
  family (§6bt, §6cw per-loop variables, §6an-3) and of the "arg-setup
  placement" family (§6ae-2, §7d-1, §6bh's chain rule). It is also the *only*
  route I found to make GCC put a call's arg0 setup in a loop's test blocks.

### 2. A "2-word residual" header is a hypothesis, not a finding

Re-auditing the parked body per the brief's method order found three defects
the old note had mis-attributed to the loop:

* **A missing call (m2c decompilation bug).** The CLONEFROM default loop's
  first call is `fn_80061DE8(mgr, i)` and its result is CHAINED into
  `fn_8005EFF4`'s arg0; m2c had dropped the call and passed `mgr` directly.
  Restoring it is 3 words. *A 1-word length difference can hide a 3-word
  missing statement* — the index-aligned diff showed a 1-word shift, not a hole.
* **A wrong pointer type.** `ObjB.unk0xC` was declared `s32 *`, so
  `*(arg0->unk0xC + 0x114)` scaled by 4 (`lwz r0, 0x450(r9)` instead of want's
  `0x114(r9)`). `char *unk0xC;` + `*(s32 *)(arg0->unk0xC + 0x114)` fixed it
  (M6.89d, brief rule 4). **Check the FIRST member you touch in a
  mega-merged class, not just the opcodes** (§6bx).
* **A stale zero-arg prototype.** `s32 fn_80057CA0();` on a callee whose
  prologue is `stwu -8; mflr; stw; lwz r3, 0x10(r3)` — it reads r3, so it is
  1-arg, and the unprototyped call emitted a spurious `crclr cr1eq`
  (§6bf's arity audit; the old note never ran it).

### 3. Staged arg0 loads: `"+r"` barrier to hoist above a branch, and a hard
### pin to keep the colour the barrier wins

Two call sites in this function want their arg0 (`lwz r3, 0x210(r27)` =
`arg0->mgr`) materialised **before** the `if (flag == 0)` test; ngccc sank it
into the merge block after the `li r6,0`. Staging the load into a local plus a
zero-code `__asm__("" : "+r"(local))` after the staging assignments puts it back
(3 words each). Two extra details:

* The barrier also beats a **competing stack load** for the same slot, because
  `reorder_basic_block` prefers the stack-sourced `lwz` (§6bg-8). Both call
  sites needed `var_r3 = arg0->mgr;` staged *before* the neighbour's
  `var_r4 = sp234;` so the object's load wins — i.e. the barrier sets the
  barrier'd insn's position, the *source order* picks which of two sibling
  loads goes first.
* The **same barrier on a staged CALL RESULT** (`mr r8, r3` for
  `ContainsFlag` → arg5) flipped the ORDER correctly but moved the copy to r9
  and cost an extra `mr r8,r9` (361 words). Adding
  `register s32 var_r8 __asm__("r8");` on that variable fixed the colour and
  the length in the same edit → **zero-code barrier + hard pin on the ARG
  REGISTER is the pair here** (cf. §6p-111/§6an-3 for arg-slot pins; this is
  the first instance I know of where the *order* needs the barrier and the
  *colour* needs the pin).
* Both `register` vars must be `s32` — cc1 silently drops pointer-typed and
  u8-typed pins (§6az-245, §76-178).

### 4. Audit of the result (all clean, so this is a promote candidate, not a park)

* object `.text` = 0x5A0 = 1440 B = `symbols.txt` `size:0x5A0` = header
  `size=1440B`; only `.text` + `.rela.text` (no private `.rodata` pool, so no
  doc-14 caveat);
* **0 emitted inline instructions** — all six `__asm__` sites are zero-code
  `"+r"` barriers (recipe 180 satisfied with room to spare);
* 26 intra-function `R_PPC_REL14` addends + 68 `R_PPC_REL24` entries audited
  against want's decoded branch targets: **0 mismatches** (§6bw method);
* all 12 extern symbols and SDK names re-checked against
  `config/G2TE52/symbols.txt`; the QB hash literals are plain `lis`/`ori`
  immediates (not relocation-masked), so the 100% verdict already byte-verifies
  them against the disc hash table.

## 6da — 2026-09-30 single pick: in a PS function with SEVERAL pair loads, a
### non-volatile pair read is always floated INTO the consuming `ps_sub`/`ps_madd`
### and so can never be emitted before a volatile one — cast the earlier read
### `volatile` to pin the emission order, and hard-pin the locals to pin the
### colours (fn_801CBBD0, 61.9% → 73.8%)

`fn_801CBBD0` (168 B, `-mps-float`, 5 `psq_l` + 8 opcode-4 ops) was parked as
"a paired-single FPR allocation and scheduler-coloring difference" with no
lever listed. Two plain-C levers (no inline asm, **0 emitted instructions**)
took it from 26/42 to 31/42 words; the residual is one allocator decision plus
the tail.

* **The mechanism of the load order — a non-volatile pair load is emitted at its
  USE, not at its statement.** GIMPLE leaves `other->zw` as a plain MEM inside
  `d1 = pzw - ozw`; `coalesce` deletes the `ozw = other->zw;` statement and the
  load is expanded *inside* the `ps_sub`, i.e. AFTER the `fr.pzw` read — which is
  a **volatile** statement, so volatile reads are hoisted as their own gimple
  statements in program order and always precede it. Result: the RHS pair load
  is emitted after the LHS one, always. Retail wants the reverse.
  **Fix: cast the earlier read's target volatile.**
  `ozw = *(volatile __ps_t *)&other->zw;` — the two reads are then both
  volatile, volatile ops keep program order, and `ozw` is emitted first. Staging
  the value into a named local alone (with or without a `"+r"` barrier, with or
  without `register` pins) does **not** help: `"+r"` spills the PS value to a
  new stack slot (37→21%), and plain staging is coalesced away. Alone this
  lever is worth +1 word; the pins below are worth +6 more.
  (C89 `volatile` cast on a struct field is also a legitimate reading here: the
  object was written by an unknown callee, so the read must be volatile.)
* **`register __ps_t x __asm__("frN")` pins on these reads DO bind** (extends
  §6cx — they bind for a `-mps-float` `__ps_t` local that is *fed by a load*,
  which is the case §6cx already reports; what is new here is using it as the
  colour control for a whole PS value chain). With the FPRs hard-pinned
  `ozw→fr0`, `pzw→fr13`, `oy→fr12`, the four long-lived pair values land in
  exactly want's `f0/f13/f12/f11` and the `lbl_802AD128` pair read falls into
  `f11` and the threshold `f32` into `f10` — 5 previously-wrong words.
  A 4x4 pin sweep (ozw x pzw x oy x d1) x 2 read orders x 2 `fr.pxy` spellings
  (64 bodies) showed the pins are **conjunctive**: dropping the `pzw` pin swaps
  the `oy`/K registers to f11/f12 (−1 word), dropping the `oy` pin costs 2, and
  the `d1` pin is worth 0 (advisory — cc1 writes the result wherever it likes).
* **Statement order is a NO-OP in a PS block with no branches.** 30+ hand-chosen
  permutations of the 8 statements, the `fr.d1`/`fr.d2` store position relative
  to the merge/madd, the `threshold` local inlined at the return, a nested
  `__builtin_ps_merge00` inside the `madd` argument, `d2*d2+merged` instead of
  `madd`, the whole tail as one nested expression, and the `pxy` read at 12
  different statement positions: **every one produced a byte-identical object**
  at 61.9% (before the pins) or 73.8% (after). The sched2 order of an
  acyclic PS chain is a pure function of the data-flow graph, so do not grind
  statement order here — change the *graph* (a pin, a volatile) or stop.
  Likewise every scheduling/GCSE flag is a no-op except `-fno-schedule-insns`
  (42.9%) and `-O1` (9.3%), which are strictly worse.
* **NEGATIVE: ngccc writes a 3-source PS op in-place on the ADDEND (3rd builtin
  arg), and that is not source-reachable.** For `__builtin_ps_madd(d2, d2, m)`
  it emits `ps_madd D=A=C_or_... ` — precisely, `D = m's reg` whenever `m` dies
  at the insn; want wants `D = d2's reg` (in-place on the first arg). None of
  `d2 = madd(d2,d2,m)`, a nested merge argument, `d2*d2+m`, moving the volatile
  `fr.d2` store before/after the merge, a `"+f"` barrier on either operand, or
  pins on `m`/`square`/`d2`/`total` changes it. Pinning `d2` *does* block the
  coalesce, but the result then takes a **fresh** reg (`f12`) and pinning the
  result variable is silently ignored. Worth knowing before you park: five
  standalone probes of `madd` (params, locals, `madd(a,a,c)`, store-then-madd)
  all put `D` in the FIRST operand's reg, so want's form is the *natural* one and
  something in the surrounding context flips it — so treat a 3-source dest reg
  as a possible un-parked residual and try the *graph* levers first.
* **Tail: a scalar lane extract from a spilled PS pair wants `lfs` + a copy,
  and neither spelling produces both.** want ends
  `psq_st f0,40(r1); lfs f0,0x28(r1); fmr f13,f0; fcmpu cr7,f13,f10` — the pair
  is spilled, lane 0 is reloaded with a SCALAR `lfs`, then copied. A
  non-volatile union read gets GCC's pair `psq_l`+`ps_mr` (the `psq_l` is dead);
  a `*(volatile f32 *)&fr.inv` read gets the scalar `lfs` but GCC coalesces the
  reload with the value pseudo and **drops the copy, shrinking the object to 41
  words** (52.4%); pinning that value to `fr13` puts the `lfs` in f13 (still no
  copy) and a pinned `fr0` version costs 8 bytes. A length change is worse than
  the 2 wrong words, so keep the non-volatile union unless you can get both
  instructions. Unparked lead: a second live name for the loaded lane.
  **UNPARKED 2026-10-02 (w75, `fn_800C494C`): the lead is the fix — but the
  container must be NON-volatile.** A *plain* `PV` local (no `volatile`, no
  `register` pin) whose lane is extracted emits **all three** instructions:
  `psq_st <pair>,slot(r1)` (the pair spills to the local's stack home so the
  conversion has a source), `lfs <scratch>,slot(r1)` (lane 0 as a scalar), then
  `fmr <value>,<scratch>` — the copy survives because the reload pseudo and the
  value pseudo are distinct and regmove will not merge them. Reading the lane
  from a *volatile* container gives only `psq_st`+`lfs` (no copy), and a
  non-volatile **struct member** read gives `psq_l`+`ps_mr` instead. So the
  three spellings are three different lowerings; pick by which one want has.
  Measured on `fn_800C494C` 5.4% → 48.6% (6 of 8 slots). Full write-up in
  §6ez; 673 `psq_st`+`lfs`+`fmr` sites in the DOL.
* **Audit state of the 73.8% result** (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):
  object `.text` = 0xA8 = `symbols.txt` `size:0xA8` = header `size=168B`; only
  `.text` + `.rela.text` (no private `.rodata`, so no doc-14 pool caveat);
  **0 emitted inline instructions** (3 register-var pins only); 2/2 intra-function
  `R_PPC_REL14` addends match want (§6bw method) and both `R_PPC_REL24` targets
  are `fn_802203E4`/`fn_801CCF64`; all four externs (`lbl_802AD128`,
  `lbl_802ABADC`, `lbl_80305F9C`, and the `+0x58`/`+0x60` struct offsets)
  re-checked against `config/G2TE52/symbols.txt` and against the promoted
  `src/fn_801CCF64.c` (which confirms the out-param is `dst[0]=src[11]` /
  `dst[1]=src[12]`, i.e. offsets 0x58/0x60). All eight opcode-4 words were
  hand-decoded with `tools/ps_diff.py`'s probe-verified field layout: no
  doc-06/doc-29 wall anywhere in this function.

## 6db — 2026-09-30 single pick: BACK OUT THE MISSING STACK BUFFER'S SIZE ARITHMETICALLY from the prologue, and do not trust a promoted sibling's declaration (fn_8005D60C, 30.0% → EXACT, 4 semantic fixes, 0 asm, 0 flags)

`fn_8005D60C` (188 B) arrived with an m2c body whose only structural error was
`s32 sp8` where retail has an **0x80-byte string buffer**, plus three
unprototyped callees and a raw address literal. All four fixes are semantic;
no pin, barrier, `_dummy` or schedule flag was involved, and the stale
`// FLAG: -fno-expensive-optimizations` was simply deleted.

* **The frame size is a closed-form tell for a missing local's size.** For
  these ProDG/GCC-2.95 frames:
  `stwu_N = 8 + locals_bytes + 8 + 4*nSavedGPRs`, and the save area starts at
  `8 + locals_bytes` (the `stmw`/`stw` offset, or the LR slot minus
  `4*nSavedGPRs` if you only have `stw r0,frame+4`). So **subtract 8 and
  `4*nSavedGPRs` from want's `stwu` immediate and you have the EXACT total
  byte size of the function's locals** — no guessing a buffer size, no
  "add a dmmy and re-check" loop. Here: `0xa8 - 8 - 4*5 = 140 = 0x8C`; the
  4-byte hash slot at `r1+0x88` is already visible in want, so the buffer is
  `0x8C - 4 = 0x88`… **but `char sp8[0x80]` reproduced want's slot layout**
  (buffer `0x8..0x88`, hash at `0x88`, `stmw r27` at `0x94`) — see the
  CORRECTION below, the `-16` form is off by 8.
  **When a NEAR's whole prologue is offset-shifted, do this
  arithmetic before touching anything else — a mis-sized local shifts every
  stack displacement, the `stmw` span AND the frame, which is why the score
  collapses into the 30 % band with a structurally perfect body.**
  (Diagnosis shortcut: if got's `stwu` immediate differs from want's by a round
  0x10/0x20/0x40/0x80, you are one un-sized local away from EXACT.)
* **CORRECTION 2026-10-30 — the ORIGINAL `-16` FORM IS WRONG; the law is
  `frame = Gsave + 4*nSavedGPRs` (equivalently `L = frame - 4*nSavedGPRs - 8`),
  and `L` is NOT rounded up to a multiple of 8.** Verified DOL-wide by scanning
  every GPR-only prologue (m2c-shaped `stwu r1,-N(r1)` + `mflr r0` + `stmw rX,K`):
  **3807 of 4013 match `frame == Gsave + 4*nSavedGPRs` with the LR slot at
  `frame + 4`** (the other 206 are mid-function `stwu` false positives, all with
  `frame == 8`). The `-16` / `8+L+8+4n` form scores **0/4013**, and a
  `8 + round_up(L,8) + 4 + 4*n` form also scores **0/4013**; 1635 of 4413
  GPR-only prologues have a `stmw` displacement that is `4 (mod 8)`, and
  `0x80007a4c` (L=12), `0x800093ac`/`0x80009b04` (L=4) etc. all have L not
  8-aligned — so there is **no 8-byte alignment step**. Worked example:
  want `stwu -0x20 / stmw r27,0xc / stw r0,0x24` ⇒ `Gsave = 0xc`,
  `nSavedGPRs = 5`, `32 = 12 + 20` ✓, so **L = 4**, not 0 and not 8. Use this
  form; the `-16` variant silently over-counts the locals by 8 and will size a
  buffer 8 bytes too large. (FPR-saving functions extend it to
  `frame = max(Gsave + 4*nSavedGPRs, FPR_save_end)`; the GPR-only form above is
  the one that matters for the §4c target pool.)
* **Why the wrong `-16` form nevertheless "worked" on `0x8005D60C` — the
  distinction to keep.** That function's `stwu -0xa8 / stmw r27,0x94` gives
  region `L = 0x94-8 = 0x8C`, but the source declares only
  `char sp8[0x80] + s32 sp88 = 0x84` bytes, so **8 bytes of the region are
  trailing alignment padding, not a local**. The `-16` form happens to return
  `0x84` = the *declared-object* size, which is the number you actually want
  when you are sizing a buffer. So: use the `-8` form to reason about the
  frame and the save-area offset, but note that `region - 8` is a common
