  padding case, and a declared size that is 8 short of the region is normal
  and does not need a dummy. Do not "fix" such a draft by adding 8 bytes.
* **A promoted sibling's declaration of the SAME local name is not evidence
  for yours.** `src/fn_8005D4F4.c` is the same body shape and declares `s32
  sp8` — correctly, because that function has no `sprintf` into it. Here
  `fn_8005D4A8` (the promoted `sprintf` wrapper, `src/fn_8005D4A8.c`) is called
  with `&sp8`, which is what makes it a buffer. Read the *call*, not the
  sibling. (Sister of §6v-120 / recipe 120 "m2c scalar decl can hide a big
  stack buffer"; the frame arithmetic above is how to get the size without
  disassembling every callee to find its highest store offset.)
* **The three remaining fixes were the standard arity + address-form pair**, both
  already documented, and both worth re-checking on every low-score m2c body:
  `fn_8005D7A0` (1-arg, returns a node), `fn_8007B38C` (5-arg even though it
  reads only r3/r7 — dead middle args still need their arg registers set,
  §6t-3), `fn_8005D844` (3-arg void) and `fn_80010760` (void) — the three
  unprototyped calls were emitting `crclr cr1eq`; and `0x8036645C` is
  `lbl_8036645C` (.bss), so a bare `extern char lbl_8036645C[]` reference flips
  the materialise from `lis/ori` to want's `lis/addi` (recipe 22/45).
  The node type is `Unk_897A0ACF *` with `u16 unk0x4` — confirmed from the
  promoted twin — which is what produces want's `lhz/addi/sth` run.
* **Audit state of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object `.text`
  = `0xbc` = 188 = `symbols.txt` `size:0xBC` = header `size=188B`; only `.text`
  + `.rela.text` (no private `.rodata`, so no doc-14 pool caveat); **0 emitted
  inline instructions**; all 7 `R_PPC_REL24` call targets match want's `bl`

## 6de — 2026-09-30 single pick: a field-typedef's **padding array is measured in
### ELEMENTS, so `s32 _pad[N]` is `4N` bytes and silently misplaces every member
### after it** (fn_802357B0, 25.7% → EXACT, 268 B, 0 asm, 0 flags)

`fn_802357B0` (memory-card Script* zone, §6ab) arrived as an m2c draft at
**25.68%** with a 296 B object for a 268 B want. Every one of the 55 "diffs" was
**semantic**; not a single codegen lever was needed. What made it expensive was
that the *real* fix spanned six independent defects that all happen to move
many words, and one of them is invisible.

* **The invisible one: a padding array in a field-layout typedef is in
  ELEMENTS.** The vtable member pair must sit at `+0x10` / `+0x14`, so the
  natural spelling is
  ```c
  typedef struct { char _pad[0x10]; s16 unk0x10; s32 unk0x14; } VT;   /* right */
  typedef struct { s32 _pad[0x10]; s16 unk0x10; s32 unk0x14; } VT;   /* WRONG: 0x40/0x44 */
  ```
  `s32 _pad[0x10]` is 16 × 4 = **64** bytes, so the members land at `+0x40` and
  `+0x44` — the body still compiles, the object is still the right *length*,
  and the only symptom is two `lha`/`lwz` displacements. AGENTS uses the
  `char _pad[N]` idiom in a dozen places (§4f `ai`, §6q-86 frame templates,
  §6dc vtable slots) but never warns that the *element type* is load-bearing.
  **Rule: in a hand-written field-layout typedef, every padding member is
  `char`; reach for an element type other than `char` only for the real
  fields.** This cost one full iteration on an otherwise-100% body.

* **The 25.7 → 97.0 % jump was the arity/field-pass audit alone (brief rule 3),
  and it removed nine `crclr cr1eq` plus a `li r3,0` and a `li r3,3` — i.e. the
  object got SHORTER and the loop test moved.** Four of the five call sites were
  wrong, in three distinct known ways:
  | want | m2c draft | recipe |
  |---|---|---|
  | `bl fn_8023B364` with r3 = the caller's own **entry arg0**, never re-materialised (callee prologue `mr r30,r3`) | `fn_8023B364(temp_r9)` — passed a *6th* arg register | §70-128: old-style `void f();` + bare call leaves r3 alone and emits no crclr |
  | `lwz r3,0x77c8(r29); cmpwi; beq; li r4,3; bl fn_802435EC` — the loaded field is **arg0** | `fn_802435EC(3)` | §6m-43 / §6e-32 field-pass |
  | `lwz r3,0xc(r30); cmpwi; beq; bl fn_802432A8` — callee does `or. r30,r3,r3` | `fn_802432A8()` (also a crclr) | field-pass again |
  | `lwz r3,0(r30); mr r4,r28; bl fn_8022D3C0` — callee reads only r3, but r4 must be materialised | 1-arg (⇒ crclr, no r4) | §6t-3 **dead-arg** proto: declare the arity the CALL SITE shows |
  | `bl fn_8023FAC4` — genuinely 0-arg (its own prologue never touches r3) | 0-arg | correct already; needed the *prototype* (`void f(void)`) to drop the crclr |

* **The loop's argument web is born in the CONDITION** (§6cy again, the cheapest
  possible instance of it): `while ((head = self->unk0x84) != 0) { t =
  fn_802432A0(head); … }`. Retail's loop is rotated — entry `b`s to the latch,
  the body block sits *before* the test — and the test block's `lwz r3,0x84(r30)`
  is consumed as the body's arg0 with **no `mr r3`** in either test block. The
  assignment inside the condition gives `head` r3 as its home, so the
  call-arg copy disappears and the rotation falls out. A plain
  `while (self->unk0x84 != 0)` hoists the body above the test and emits a copy
  (and costs ~30 words of layout).

* **ONE named `zero` for the five zero-stores, and it inherits the loop's
  register.** Retail does `li r31,0` once and reuses r31 for
  `stw` 0x8C / 0x04 / 0x08 / 0x177C8 / 0x0C, and r31 is the register the loop's
  node pointer died in. A single `s32 zero; zero = 0;` gives both (§6ca-1 for the
  single-`li`, §70-130d / §6an-3 for the recycling). With five bare `0` literals
  cc1 births a fresh `li` for the last store, which re-prioritises the
  neighbouring `lwz`/`rlwinm` group.

* **Audit of the result:** `.text` = 0x10C = 268 B = `symbols.txt` `size:0x10C` =
  header `size=268B`; only `.text` + `.rela.text` (no private `.rodata`, so no
  doc-14 pool caveat); **zero inline instructions**; all 7 `R_PPC_REL14`
  addends (`+f8`,`+3c`,`+84`,`+84`,`+48`,`+dc`,`+f0`) and all 9 `R_PPC_REL24`
  call targets verified against want's branches/calls (§6bw method); **no
  extern data symbols**, so the masked-100%-wrong-label hazard does not apply.

**The transferable headline is the brief's own rule, re-confirmed: at 25 % the
problem was 100 % semantics. A 296 B object for a 268 B want, i.e. GOT LONGER,
is itself the tell — a codegen/residual park leaves the object roughly the
right size, while a wrong arity *grows* it (crclrs, `li`s for the constants
that should have been loads). Check `got_size` vs `symbols.txt` before reading
any low-score diff.**

## 6df — 2026-09-30 single pick: a residual that is a pure r29/r30 SWAP of two
### call-crossing locals is one pin on EITHER of them (an OR, and the pin can be
### POINTER-typed) (fn_800F48DC, 29.6% → EXACT, 196 B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags)

`fn_800F48DC` (196 B, a `Skel`-shaped QB/virtual dispatcher) arrived as an m2c
draft at **29.6%** whose header only recorded two successive "missing-prototype
call → `crclr cr1eq`" fixes. It was 4-instructions too long and the whole
residual was semantic.

**A got object LONGER than `symbols.txt` and made of 2 × `crclr cr1eq` + 2 ×
`mr r3,r31` is the doc-56 unprototyped-callee signature, full stop.** Two
prototypes (`fn_80056660` 3-arg, `fn_80056AD0` 2-arg, both verified by
disassembling the callee's first 8 insns) plus the file-local typedefs took it to
**83.7%**, and the 4 extra words were exactly: 2 `crclr` (no prototype) and 2
`mr r3,r31` (arg0 re-materialised where want leaves r3 alone). The two
`mr r3,r31` had two different causes worth separating:
* **the previous `blrl` vcall's result is passed onward** as the next call's
  arg0 — a named local, since an expression chain cannot span an indirect call
  (§6ah-132 / recipe 56); and
* **the tested guard value IS the callee's arg0** — `fn_80013788(arg0)` →
  `fn_80013788(arg0->unk20)` is what turns want's `lwz r3,0x20` + `cmpwi r3,0`
  into a `cmpwi` on the ARG register instead of a `cmpwi r0` (§72-143 again).
  A `blr`-stub/dead-code callee audit (§6ap-132) would also have caught the
  sibling: `fn_800F3A6C(arg0, arg0->p54)` → 1-arg.

**1. `addi base,K` followed by `lwz off(base)` in want = the source REASSIGNED a
base pointer to `p+K`.** A single struct field at `K+off` compiles to one
`lwz K+off(base)` — so retail is not using a struct member here:
```c
e = (char *)arg0->vt50;          /* lwz  0x50(r31)          -> r29   */
o = *(s16 *)(e + 0x58);          /* lha  0x58(r29)                   */
e = e + 0x58;                    /* addi r29, r29, 0x58      -> r29   */
call(*(s32 *)(e + 4), ...)       /* lwz  4(r29)            [want]   */
                               /*  lwz 0x5c(r29)         [if a member] */
```
Same constant in the `lha` and the `addi`, and the `+4` lands in the load
displacement. Use it whenever a vtable chase's fn-pointer load is at `K+4` and
want splits it — and note the s16 offset field must come from a **file-local
struct** (the corpus-merged class types +0x10/+0x58 as `s32` → `lwz` not `lha`).

**2. A residual that is EXACTLY a two-register rotation needs ONE pin, and
which one you pick is an OR.** At 83.7% every word differed only by `r29` ↔
`r30`: `t` (the vcall result) and `e` (the vtable base) had swapped
callee-saved homes. Measured, all at 196 B and byte-for-byte identical apart
from the two colours: 6 declaration orders → 83.7%; the s16-vs-s32 offset
spelling → 83.7%; `void *` vs `s32` vcall return type → 83.7%; a `VtA *`
(typed) vs `char *` vtable base → 83.7%; hoisting the `arg0->vt50` load to the
top of the body → 38.8% (it duplicates the load), without the duplicate → 83.7%;
**`register char *e __asm__("r29");` → 100.0%** and, independently,
**`register void *t __asm__("r30");` → 100.0%**. Either pin alone is enough and
removing both returns 83.7%, so this is an **OR** — never conclude a pin is
load-bearing from a single ablation (§6bf-A, §6ca-2, §6bg's `fn_80153D54`
inverse case). A `register`-var pin is a declaration, not a statement, so it
emits **zero** instructions and stays inside the §4g/§6af-180 30%-asm budget.

**3. CORRECTION / nuance to §76-178 and §6az-245: "pointer-typed register pins
are silently dropped" is CONDITIONAL — try the direct pointer pin first.** On
this function `register char *e __asm__("r29")`, `register void *e
__asm__("r29")` and the `register s32` alias all bind and all reach 100 %; the
`void *` spelling needs no casts at every dereference site, so the *cleanest*
body is the pointer-typed pin. The documented dropped case is a pointer local
whose value comes from a **call result** or a **compound expression** (where
the pin has no single def pseudo to bind). Given a pointer local, spend the
cast noise on the `s32` alias only after the direct pointer pin measures inert.

**4. `li r26,0` placement came free.** The single zero web (used by both
`arg0->p54 = 0` and `arg0->unk20 = 0`) lands **after** the first `bl` in want
and **before** it in the inherited draft. Adding the `fn_800F38B8` prototype
(the inherited draft called it with no declaration in scope at all) moved it to
want's slot on its own — no zero-hoist lever (§6c-28 / §73-118 / §6ap-2) needed.
If a `li` is on the wrong side of a call, audit the *first* callee's prototype
before staging a zero.

0xC4 = 196 B = `symbols.txt` `size:0xC4` = header `range=0x800F48DC-0x800F49A0
size=196B`; only `.text` + `.rela.text`, so no private `.rodata` and no doc-14
pool caveat; **0 emitted inline instructions** (the one `__asm__` in the file
is the `register` declaration on `e`); all 6 `R_PPC_REL24` targets
(`fn_800F38B8`/`fn_80056660`/`fn_80056AD0`/`fn_800F3A6C`/`fn_80013788`/
`fn_800F3794`) equal want's `bl` destinations, and the single intra-function

## 6dg — 2026-09-30 single pick: a per-block-materialised accumulator ⇒ its home IS the
### return register, and the r3 pin is the only route (fn_8003E328, 46.2% → EXACT, 556 B,
### 0 emitted asm). Also: **`too few arguments` is an ERROR in this cc1, printed as a
### "warning"** — a mis-arity call FAILs the draft with no obvious message.

`fn_8003E328` (`GetFacePointsStruct`, script-command zone) was parked at 46.2% with a
header blaming a "phantom-arg drop". Its object was **24 bytes LONGER** than
`symbols.txt` — the §6de tell that the fault is semantic, not codegen.

* **"Object longer than want" is usually a missing prototype, one per call site.**
  `fn_801293FC` (2-arg, `s32`) and `GetInteger` (4-arg) had no declaration in the
  draft, so **10 `crclr cr1eq`** were emitted (8 + 2). Declaring them removed
  40 bytes: 580 B → 544 B. Then the second `GetInteger` call, which m2c gave
  3 args where retail passes 4 (`li r6, 0`), fixed the rest.
  **Portability trap, worth remembering:** ProDG cc1 reports
  `too few arguments to function 'f'` on stderr and exits **1** while
  formatting it as `warning:`. A `grep`-for-`warning` on the compile log will
  miss the only fatal message, and every arity guess in a draft must therefore
  be counted against want's arg registers even when the file "compiles".
* **A boolean accumulator reused for a second conjunct is a different
  statement from a fresh `x ? 1 : 0`.** m2c wrote the third conjunct as
  `out->f = (cond ? 1 : 0)` where retail writes the *same* `var = 0; if (cond)
  var = 1;` shape as the second one and then `out->f = var` (want's single
  `stw r29, 0x20(r31)`). The tell is want storing the accumulator register
  twice with the *same* store instruction rather than a fresh bool. Worth −4
  insns / −16 B.
* **The main lever: an accumulator that want re-materialises in EVERY guard
  block must be homed in the RETURN register, and GCC 2.95's `local_alloc`
  will never choose it.** Want has four blocks, each ending
  `li r3, 0; cmpwi; beq <shared epilogue>`, and the final path `li r3, 1` —
  i.e. **four separate `li r3, 0` and no `mr r3, …` in the epilogue**. Because
  the pseudo's live range crosses ~12 calls, `local_alloc` refuses caller-saved
  hard regs for it, so plain C puts the accumulator in a **callee-saved reg
  (r29)**, where it (a) **merges with the second 0/1 accumulator**, (b) gets
  **CSE'd with the sibling `x = 0` statements** into a single `li`, and (c)
  leaves r3 free so the slot reloads go *straight into r3* with no copy. That
  is a 7-instruction / 28-byte signature:
That is a 7-instruction and 28-byte signature where retail loads frame offset 8 into r0, zeroes r3, compares r0 against zero, branches to end on equal, moves r0 into r3 and zeroes r4, while the build zeroes r29, loads frame offset 8 directly into r3, compares r3 and branches, then zeroes r4.
  `register s32 var_r3 __asm__("r3");` — a register-variable *attribute*,
  **zero emitted instructions** — makes `local_alloc` split the pseudo per
  block, which *is* retail's shape: 528 B → 556 B and the residual collapses
  to store order only (97.1% → 100% with the two store runs re-sourced).
  This is a legitimate exception to §6by's "never pin an argument register":
  the pinned value is **not an incoming argument**, it is the outgoing return
  value, and the pin works precisely *because* r3 is the ABI return reg.
  Five plain-C alternatives all failed (13.6 % / 528 B, measured): pin removal
  with the decl moved first/last, dropping the unused local, dropping the
  redundant `x = 0` statements, and splitting the second accumulator into two
  names. So when a residual is "N `li <retreg>,0` + N `mr <retreg>,r0` missing
  and the object is exactly N*4 bytes short", go straight to the r3 pin.
* **Store-run rotation then lands normally (recipe 274/24/64).** Two runs: the
  four frame-slot zero-inits must be written in **ascending slot** order
  (`sp8, spC, sp10, sp14` → want's `14, 8, c, 10`), and the tail's two zero
  stores in **descending** order (`0x30, 0x34` → want's `34, 30`). Both follow
  "last source statement emits first, the rest in source order".
* Audit: object `.text` = 0x22C = `symbols.txt` size = header `size=`, only
  `.text` + `.rela.text` (no doc-14 pool), 0 emitted asm, 8/8 `R_PPC_REL14`
  targets and 17/17 `R_PPC_REL24` targets verified (§6bw method), all 9 QB
  hashes hand-decoded from want's `lis`/`ori` (unmasked, so byte-verified) and
  no extern data symbols in the body.

## 6dh — 2026-09-30 single pick: a stale `volatile double _dummy` SILENTLY
### DISABLES the sweep's own dual-test (so a FPR draft is scored one way only),
### and the LAST of N repeated loads is INLINE in retail, not through the temp
### (fn_8007904C, 34.1% → EXACT, 7 semantic fixes, 0 asm, 0 flags)

`fn_8007904C` (344 B) arrived as a 34.09% m2c draft whose header blamed a
`store_order_search` sweep and a missing prototype. Both were noise: the draft
was wrong in seven independent semantic ways and **every one of them is a
`lbz` vs `lhz`/`lwz` in the want**, i.e. a data-type error, not codegen.

**1. A stale `volatile double _dummy;` turns OFF the sweep's ambig8 dual-test.**
`test_wip_drafts.py` classifies a 8-aligned FPR-saving want as `ambig8` and
compiles the body TWICE — as-is and with an injected dummy — precisely because
"DOL alone cannot tell you which is right" (`want_fpr_frame`'s own docstring).
But the injection is guarded by `if fpr is not None and "volatile double" not
in body:`. A draft that already carries a dummy is therefore tested **once**,
and a *wrong* dummy is a silent, self-reinforcing verdict. Here want's frame is
0x38 (8-aligned) and ngccc's native frame for this body is also 0x38 — the
inherited `_dummy` pushed it to 0x40 and shifted every FPR/GPR/LR displacement
by +8 across the whole function. Deleting one line fixed all five. **So: on any
FPR-saving NEAR, delete the `_dummy` and let the tool dual-test it — the dummy
you wrote may be the thing that is wrong, and its presence hides the very
mechanism meant to tell you so.** (Siblings of the brief's rule 6 "remove stale
scaffolding": that rule lists pins / barriers / `// FLAG:` — `_dummy` belongs on
the list.)

**2. The LAST of N identical repeated loads is INLINE in retail; the other
N−1 go through a named temp — and that alone is the register colour.**
After the seven semantic fixes the object was 88 words and **3 words** from
byte-exact: the fourth `lwz 0xc(r29)` (reloading the same `arg0->dim` pointer
three earlier loads had already used) had to land in **r11**, and its two
`lbz` off it followed, while got reused **r9** — the register the third load
had used. Writing only that final size expression *inline* off `arg0->dim`
instead of via the `d` temp gives the address pseudo a distinct, later
birth → a fresh scratch colour → **96.51% → 100.00%, one edit, 0 emitted
instructions.** This is §6cw / §6bu / §6an-3 ("one variable per web / per
phase") running in the *other* direction: the point is not that a variable was
split, it is that retail's last use is a bare MEM in an expression, so its
allocation priority is that of a fresh expression rather than of the shared
temp. **Diagnostic: a residual of only a few words, all of them the base
register of a load that repeats identically elsewhere in the function, where
every other word matches — inline ONE of the copies (typically the last) and
re-score before reaching for a pin or a barrier.** Sharing a temp across
copies is not free; a load repeated N times is not necessarily one web.

**3. Six more semantic fixes worth re-using as a checklist for the m2c draft
class at <50 %** (all confirmed against this want):
* a repeated "size" subexpression (`(u16)(1<<b6) * (u16)(1<<b7) * 4`) written
  out at **all four** use sites is what produces four *independent* `lbz` pairs;
  hoisting it into a helper macro/temp collapses them (and, per item 2, the
  inline/temp choice per site is itself a codegen lever);
* a struct field the game reads with `lbz` must be declared `u8` — m2c's
  "bitfield at +6" and "u16 at +7" both came out as `lhz`, and the `clrlwi
  …,0x10` pair that survives on the *shift result* is easy to misread as the
  field being 16-bit;
* a vtable member pair is `s16 off; char pad[2]; void *(*fn)(void *)` — the
  offset is an `lha` and the slot is a real function-pointer member; declaring
  it as `s32` + a cast gives `lwz` and loses the `mtlr`;
* an object-pointer global must be read **bare**: `extern char lbl_X[]` +
  `*(T **)lbl_X` (the form the promoted siblings use) or `extern T *lbl_X` +
  bare `lbl_X` — never `*(T **)&lbl_X`, which materialises the full address
  and turns want's `lis @ha ; lwz -0x168(r28)` into `lis ; lwz 0(r28)`. Same
  masked score, different link-time encoding (hazard 277), so verify the pair
  by hand;
* **prototypes are per-call-site, not per-callee.** This function calls
  `memset` and `memcpy`; want has `crclr cr1eq` before the `memcpy` and none
  before `memset`. So `memset` needs `extern void *memset(void*,int,unsigned)`
  and `memcpy` must stay IMPLICIT (§6an / §6ac-5 in the reverse direction).
* a vcall's return value that is the next call's arg0 needs no copy at all —
  `base = m->getbase(...); fn(base, ...)` lets r3 flow across (recipe 23 /
  §6bh). Here it was true **twice**: vcall#1's return → `fn_80078C5C`'s base
  arg, vcall#2's return → `memcpy`'s dst.
* a call whose arity m2c got wrong in the *header* of the callee: `fn_80078C5C`'s
  own WIP draft reconstructs 6 args, but this call site sets r7 — it is 7
  (`base,w,h,dst,0x20,f32,f32`). Trust the call site, and re-check it when a
  callee draft disagrees.

**Audit:** object `.text` 0x158 == `symbols.txt size:0x158` == header marker;
only `.text` + `.rela.text` (no doc-14 pool); **0 `__asm__` / `.long`**; the
single `R_PPC_REL14` addend `0x138` (= readelf prints addends in HEX) gives
0x80079184, matching want's `beq` decoded from 0x4182000c; all 7 `R_PPC_REL24`
targets match want's `bl`s; want's `lis 0x8030` + `lwz -0x168` hand-decodes to
0x802FFE98 = `lbl_802FFE98`, so hazard 277 is cleared.

## 6di — a PROMOTED stub's own prototype is NOT evidence of the caller-side signature: derive arity from every `bl` site's register set

`fn_80016B50` (288 B, 36.2%) was solved to **100.0% with zero codegen levers** —
all of the gain was *semantic*, and the decisive item is a trap the existing
arity-audit recipes do not cover.

* **A promoted auto-asm leaf whose body ignores its arguments will have an
  m2c-INVENTED prototype, and its being byte-exact does not validate it.**
  The 32-byte GX thunks `fn_8001FC74` (GXSetScissorBoxOffset) /
  `fn_8001FC94` (GXSetScissor) / `fn_8001FF78` (GXSetViewport) in `src/` are
  promoted and byte-identical — but `src/fn_8001FF78.c` declares **10 `s32`
  args**, m2c's guess from one call site. The real signature is
  **`void (f32, f32, f32, f32, f32, f32)` — six floats and NO integer args**.
  A thunk's body is `stwu/mflr/stw/bl <sdk>/lwz/mtlr/addi/blr`, so it assembles
  identically under *any* signature; matching bytes and a right arity are
  independent facts. §6bf's arity audit (and the doc-10 prologue check) both
  start from "the callee is under-prototyped" — this is the inverse: the callee
  is confidently, wrongly over-prototyped, so the audit never fires.
* **How to settle it: scan `.text` for every `bl` to the thunk and read each
  call site's register set.** int-arg count = highest `rN` written since the
  previous def (remember: a leftover `mr` is NOT an arg — count only regs the
  call needs); float count = highest `fN`. The two 0x80075xxx/0x80076xxx sites
  for 0x8001FF78 set `f1..f6` and touch **no GPR at all**, which settles it.
  Beware: the `mr r5,r11` / `mr r6,r11` / `mr r8,r11` in this function look
  like dead arg materialisations but are ngccc's own float-arg-setup copies —
  they appear verbatim in the correct 0-int-arg build.
* **Arity is the cheapest sweep in the project when the object is LONGER than
  want by ~1 instruction per surplus arg.** Measured sweep on fn_80016B50
  (structure otherwise correct): 0 int args → 288 B / **100.0%**; 3 → 300 B /
  53.3%; 4 → 300 B / 52.6%; 5 → 308 B / 48.7%; 6 (m2c's guess) → 308 B /
  48.1%; 9 → 328 B / 43.9%. Each surplus int arg costs one `li`/`mr`, so run
  this BEFORE the pin/barrier/flag ladders. Note how it also *moves the
  register map*: 6 int args force a 4th callee-saved reg, 0 int args give
  want's exact 3 (`stmw r29,0x1c`).
* **Corollary — the `volatile` on a shared int→float cvt union is NOT always
  load-bearing (§6ag-5 / §6aa-3).** Here the four signed conversions share one
  stack double, and `volatile union { s32 w[2]; f64 d; } u;` pushed the slot
  from `r1+0x10` to `r1+0x18` (frame 0x30, 75.0%), while the **plain** union
  gave `r1+0x10`, frame 0x28, 100.0%; adding one `volatile double _dummy` gave
  frame 0x38. Plain `(f32)(f64)(s32)` casts already share one slot on their
  own, so measure plain-vs-`volatile` before adding a qualifier (§6bv's frame
  sort lever, with the opposite sign).
* A hand-built §6j-1 conversion dance that references the real
  `lbl_80290BF8` (so no private `.rodata`, doc 14) scored 23.2% / 29.4% here —
  retail plainly wrote the plain cast. Keep the plain cast; rely on
  `tools/fix_fp_pool.py` for pool routing at promote time.

## 6dj — 2026-09-30 single pick: a countdown whose test is on the PRE-decrement
### value must still be spelled DECREMENT-FIRST, and a zero-code `"+r"` barrier can
### split ngccc's prologue param copies (fn_800312D4, 28.6% → EXACT, 47 words,
### 1 emitted asm)

`fn_800312D4` (188 B: a counted linked-list walk, one f32 getter, a NaN-safe
`fcmpu` clamp and two calls) came in at 28.6% and is now byte-exact. Four of the
seven wins are existing recipes (the **doc-56 arity audit** on two callees, the
**extern-symbol FP constant**, the **M4.92 `_dummy`**, and the
**`if (<=) {small} else {big}` NaN-compare spelling** — the last one worth
pointing out because it is the *fourth* spelling I measured; `!(a <= b)` gives
`bso`, plain `>` gives `bgt`, and only "small arm inline, tested with `<=`" gives
`bns` to the big arm). Two were new enough to write down:

* **When want has `cmpwi n,0 / addi n,n,-1 / beq` the test is on the
  pre-decrement value, but the addi must still be BORN FIRST.**
  Want's loop body is `[cmpwi r4,0][addi r4,r4,-1][beq EXIT][lwz walk]` — the
  decrement is parked in the compare→branch gap and the walk fills the delay
  slot. The natural spelling `if (n == 0) goto out; n -= 1;` emits
  `[cmpwi][beq][lwz][addi]`: sched2 picks the `addi` as the delay-slot fill and
  everything rotates (2 words off, 89.4% → the whole body shifted).
  Writing the exit as **`n -= 1; if (n == -1) goto out;`** fixes it: GCC folds
  the `== -1` back to `cmpwi n,0` (so the opcode is right) but the `addi` is now
  created *before* the test, so the only place sched2 can put it is the gap.
  89.4% → 95.7%. **This is the countdown sibling of §6cv's post-decrement
  operand-order rule**: there the *spelling of the test* selected the latch, here
  the *birth order of the increment* selects which block it lands in. `n--` in
  the test (`if (n-- == 0)`) is catastrophic — 16.7%, because GIMPLE materialises
  the pre-value into a `mr r0,n` copy.
* **A zero-code `__asm__("" : "+r"(v))` after a function's first load splits the
  prologue param copies around it.** Retail's entry block is
  `mr r30,r3; mr r28,r5; lwz r9,0x24(r30); mr r29,r6; b TEST` — one load
  *between* two of ngccc's three `expand_prologue` copies, which it never emits
  (all copies go in adjacent, in param order). Nothing I tried moved it: 12
  permutations of the first two statements and the decrement, a named
  `out = arg3` / `self = arg0` local, a hard `register s32 a3 __asm__("r29")` pin,
  a `volatile` read, a `(char *)`-cast read, an explicit `lwz` asm birth, and all
  seven scheduling flags (all 95.7% or worse). A single zero-code `"+r"` barrier
  on the loaded value did it, 95.7% → **100.0%**. This is the `"+r"`-as-a-
  colouring/positioning lever (§6ar / §6cb / §6ak-178) applied to a *prologue*
  artefact: the barrier makes the loaded web opaque, which changes the LUID the
  last param copy is scheduled against. **Before parking a 2-word
  `load`-vs-`mr home,param` residual, try one `"+r"` on the loaded value** — it
  costs zero instructions.
* Also confirmed, cheap and reusable: **a value-return `?: ` and the
  `x = NULL; if (p) x = e;` idiom compile differently** (89.4% vs 80.9% here).
  The ternary is what gives want's `cmpwi p,0 / li r31,0 / beq / addi` (both
  arms materialised, the branch only skips the second), and — because the `li`
  clobbers the tested register — it also *re-does* the `cmpwi` that m2c's
  redundant store let GCC CSE with the loop's own test. So one source choice
  recovered 2 words at once. And: a `li` that retail keeps but GCC deletes (the
  post-loop `li r9,0`, doc-33/§6x-89) is worth the §6y-140 opaque birth
  (`__asm__("li %0,0" : "=r"(v));`, 1 insn) when it also un-CSEs a later compare.

## 6dk — 2026-09-30 single pick: a local-array slot is re-read after a store through a pointer — the fix is a named local, and its initialisation must come AFTER the last preceding call (fn_8006A4B0, 31.2% → EXACT, 320B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

A doubly-linked-list "remove by script-object id" walk: `A4B0_NODE *sp8[9]`
scratch slots at `r1+0x8..0x28` (the promoted zone siblings `src/fn_8006A5F0.c`
/ `src/fn_8006A67C.c` use exactly this `sp8[0]`/`sp8[2]` idiom), a
`node->next->prev = node->prev` unlink, `Mem_Free`, and a counter decrement.

**The three fixes, in the order they were worth (61.2% → 95.0% → 100.0%):**

1. **m2c's five "stack slots" were file-scope `static`**, so they reserved no
   frame and every store to them was DCE'd — the object was 40B short. Retail's
   locals are a single **pointer array** (`sp8[9]`), and `sp8[4]`/`sp8[6]`/
   `sp8[8]`/the second `sp8[4]` store are *provably dead* in retail yet survive
   because they are array slots (an array local gets a whole frame slot even
   with no read). Two more semantics fixes came first: the callee took
   `walker->unk0x0`, not `arg0` (and had **no prototype**, so a `crclr cr1eq`
   appeared), and the vtable method offset is **`s16` (`lha`)** not `s32`.
2. **A local array slot is re-read after any store through a pointer, because
   GCC 2.95 cannot prove the store does not alias the array.** Retail keeps the
   walker in a register across the unlink; with the slot read inline
   (`sp8[0]->unk0x8->unk0x4 = sp8[0]->unk0x4; …`) GCC reloads `sp8[0]` **twice**
   (once for the unlink base, once for the `Mem_Free` arg) — 2 extra words that
   shift everything after. A named local removes both reloads.
   **But the local's initialisation statement position is load-bearing:**
   - `n = sp8[0];` placed at the **top of the block** (before the two calls)
     makes `n` live *across a `bl`*, so GCC homes it in a **callee-saved reg**:
     frame 0x40 instead of 0x38, one extra `stmw` slot, and the whole param
     homing rotates (`arg0`→r30, `arg1`→r29) — 46% (29.5% with a pin).
   - `n = sp8[0];` placed **immediately before the store run**, i.e. *after* the
     last call, keeps its range inside one basic block, so a volatile reg
     suffices and `mr r3, rN` lands mid-block exactly like retail: 95.0%.
   So the lever is a **pair** (aliasing-reload removal + a post-call birth
   point), and both halves must be measured together — the same shape as
   §6bf-A's conjunction trap, but the second half is *where the statement sits*.
3. **The last two words were a store-vs-load interleave**: retail emits
   `cmpw; lwz r0,4(r10); stw r10,0x20(r1); stw r0,0x18(r1)`, GCC emitted
   `cmpw; stw; lwz; stw`. Writing the *next-pointer* store **before** the third
   walker store (`sp8[4]=n->unk0x4;` then `sp8[6]=n;`) — the two are
   independent and the store RUN of `n`-valued stores still emits
   `0x18, 0x28, 0x20` — puts the load in retail's slot: **100.0%**. This is
   recipe 24/64 (per-store-class ordering) applied to a *load* interleaved into
   a store run: the load is pinned to the statement that consumes it, so
   hoisting it above the earlier store is exactly the fix.

**Two more confirmations, both ORs not ANDs (measure the ablation):**

* Getting the *head* pointer into `r9` instead of `r0` was the last colour
  problem. A `register s32 h9 __asm__("r9")` pin assigned **right before the
  compare** reached 97.5% (it also freed `r0` for the `lwz r0,4(r10)`, fixing
  the interleave for free — the two residuals were ONE cause). **Fix 3 alone
  reaches 100.0% with the pin deleted**, so the pin was never load-bearing:
  measure removing each. Moving the pinned assignment to the **top of the
  block** instead (v13/v21) lets the load float above the store run and costs
  the order back (62%) — same positional rule as fix 2, one level down.
* **A stale `// FLAG: -fno-rerun-cse-after-loop` was worth −70 points** once
  the body was semantically right (97.5% → 26.25%). Re-measure inherited flags
  after the semantic round (§6bx, §6aq-222); here the correct answer was
  *delete it entirely*, no replacement flag: a 20-flag sweep on the final body
  had **zero** improvements and five regressions.

**Generalisable form.** When a NEAR is "one or two words too long, and the
extra words are `lwz <slot>(r1)` re-reads of a local", the cause is almost never
scheduling — it is that the value is an *lvalue* rather than a name. Introduce
the name, then move its assignment to the latest point that still precedes its
first use. Conversely, if introducing that name makes the frame grow by 8 and
the `stmw` span widen, the birth is too early (it crosses a call) — move it
down, do not look for a pin or a flag. Audit (§6bw method): object `.text` =
0x140 = 320B = `symbols.txt size:0x140`; only `.text` + `.rela.text`; 0 emitted
asm; all 7 intra-function `R_PPC_REL14` addends and the local `b`'s `R_PPC_REL24`
resolve to retail's branch targets, and all 6 `R_PPC_REL24` call sites land on
`fn_80069838`×3 / `fn_8013183C` / `fn_800698E0` / `Mem_Free`.

## 6dl — 2026-09-30 single pick: the "arg-setup order" wall is a **per-position permutation of the C arg list**, and the FPR +8 must go at the TOP of the locals region (fn_80034850, 28.7% → EXACT, 324B, 1 hard-reg pin, 0 emitted asm)

A 324 B QB script-command wrapper sat at 28.7% with a park-header blaming
"missing prototype". It was seven semantic errors deep; once those were gone the
last 7 words were a `doc-15` arg-setup residual that a **declaration reorder**
cracked. Three things generalise.

**1. §7d-4 generalised: the value→register mapping does NOT constrain the C
arg-list order, so you can permute the list freely to steer `expand_call`.**
An indirect call's C list order is what decides the *emission* order of the
arg-setup insns, while the value→hard-register mapping is decided only by each
position's C *type* (separate int/float ABI counters). So a cast whose
parameter list is deliberately permuted still lands every value in want's
register, but emits the setup in a different order. On this function want's
vcall window was `[f3][f1][r4][r3][f2][r5][f4]` while every "normal" cast gave
`[r4][r5][f1][f2]`; the winner was
```c
/*  value→reg:  r3=obj  f1=spC  r4=sp8  f2=sp10  r5=sp14  f3=temp_f31  f4=sp18
    (identical to the machine mapping of the naive cast)                   */
((s32 (*)(void *, f32, s32, f32, f32, void *, f32))vt->fn)
    (obj, spC, sp8, sp10, temp_f31, sp14, sp18);
```
i.e. the *floats written before the ints they follow*, not one float-after-one-
int. Recipe: take want's arg-setup insn sequence, and choose each C position's
type so the same value still routes to the same register; then let the LIST
order encode want's emission order. 92.6% → 95.1% (one reorder) → 97.5% (second
reorder of the trailing pair). Sibling lever in the same function: the plain
direct call's `void`→`s32` flip (M8.31) fixed a 2-word `addi r4`/`addi r3`
transposition in the *other* call of the same body.

**2. A post-call float RELOAD feeding a compare wants f1, ngccc always picks
f0 — a hard FPR pin is the only route, and the register is specific.** Want
`lfs f1,0x1c(r1); fcmpu cr0,f1,f31` vs got `lfs f0,…`: 97.5% for a named local,
for the swapped operands, for a `volatile` read, and for the inverted
if/else. `register f32 cur __asm__("fr1");` at *function* scope (declared with
the other locals, so the assignment can sit where the reload belongs) = 100%,
**0 emitted instructions**. `fr0` and `fr2` pins both regress (97.5% / 93.8% —
`fr2` collides with a call arg) and the nested-block form *without* the pin is
97.5%, so the pin is load-bearing and register-specific, not a block artefact.
C89 note: a `register` declaration after statements is a hard parse error in
this cc1, so keep it in the declaration block.

**3. When want's frame is `ngccc-native + 8` (FPR quirk, §4c/M4.92) the extra
8 bytes must sit ABOVE the locals, and `volatile double _dummy;` puts them at
the BOTTOM.** The dummy takes slot 8 and pushes every out-param up by 8
(here: 90.1% → 74.1%, 17 diffs that were all pure slot shifts). Use a
frame-template struct with an explicit `char pad[8]` tail instead (§6q-86) —
6 out-params + an 8-byte tail = the exact `0x20`-byte locals region and the
`stmw` at `+0x28`. 90.1% → 88.9% with 5 of 6 slots correct and the frame right.

Also confirmed: a `s32` local that is *never* read can still be deleted freely
(removing the dead `temp_r5` kept 100%), but the merged-class `s16` fix at a
vtable offset (`lha` vs `lwz`) is only reachable with a **file-local** typedef
(M6.89d) — `Unk_C7387A53.unk0x20` is `s32` corpus-wide. The `crclr cr1eq`
count is a good early signal: an object 2 words LONG with two crclrs is two
missing prototypes, and fixing them can leave the pct *unchanged* while the
object becomes size-exact — score the object length, not just the pct
(§6cs-1), because a length mismatch makes every downstream diff noise.

## 6dm — 2026-09-30 single pick: **two independent side-effect blocks in a guard
### decide a whole-function callee-saved ROLE SWAP** (source order, no pin), and a
### loop-carried update written **after** a call forces a callee-saved home that also
### relocates the hoisted invariant to the END of the preheader
### (fn_8001A9D4 `dvd_file_read_anywhere`, 43.8% → EXACT 420B, 0 asm, 0 pins, 0 _dummy)

A 420 B DVD bounce-buffer reader: 3 guard tests, a head-align `memcpy` +
`DCFlushRange`, and a 341-iteration 24-byte copy loop. The inherited header blamed
`-fno-schedule-insns2` and a "doc-15 arg-setup" residual. **All 4 wins were
semantic; zero flags, pins, barriers, `volatile` or `_dummy`.**

### 1. The missing 8 KiB bounce buffer (43.8% → 50.5%)

m2c modelled the stack DVD target as a 4-byte slot (`s32 sp27`), so the frame was
`0x38` against retail's `0x2050`. Fixed with the *frame-arithmetic* shortcut of
§6db (`locals = stwu_N − 16 − 4·nSavedGPRs`; here `0xa8−16−20 = 0x84` for
`s32 buffer[0x808]` = 0x2020 B) plus the alignment the retail code actually does:

```c
baddr = (s32)&buffer[0];
buf = (s32 *)((baddr + 0x1F) & ~0x1F);   /* addi r0,r1,0x27 ; rlwinm r25,r0,0,0,0x1a */
```

`&buffer[0]` must be an **`s32` temp**, not a pointer expression — `(char*)p + 0x1F`
in a `(char *)` cast chain is rejected by this cc1 ("invalid operands to binary &"),
whereas a `s32` address temp reproduces the exact two-instruction form. **The
alignment statement must sit INSIDE the guard block**: at function top ngccc hoists
it into the entry block, above all three guard tests (2 diffs + a re-flow). The
layout identity to aim for: array at `r1+8`, `+0x1F` then `&~0x1F` ⇒ aligned
buffer at `r1+0x20`, save area at `r1+0x202c`, `stwu -0x2050`, `stmw r23,0x202c`,
LR at `r1+0x2054`.

### 2. m2c's `label:` loop gets JUMP-THREADED — write the anti-rotation form (50.5% → 73.3%, +23)

m2c emits `loop_8: if (n > 0x2000) { body; goto loop_8; }`. ngcc's `thread_jumps`
deletes the goto (the label follows immediately) and then rotates the test to the
top of the body, so the entry edge is threaded *into the copy loop* instead of
into the test. Retail keeps the test BELOW the body with the goto as the entry
edge. The shape that matches — an explicit rotated state machine:

```c
goto loop_8;
body_8:  { …body… }
loop_8:  if (var_r28 > 0x2000) goto body_8;
         if (var_r28 > 0) { …tail… }
```

**Tell:** want has the back-edge branch inside its own test block
(`cmpwi r28,0x2000; bgt <body-top>`) AND a separate entry `b <test>` from the
pre-body path — two edges into one test, body physically above it. That is only
reachable with the rotated goto form, never with `while`/`for`/`do-while` (and
`-fno-thread-jumps` is a no-op, 78.1% either way). Sibling of §6ca/§6af-170/§6an-1,
but the new part is that the m2c form is specifically vulnerable to *threading*,
not just to rotation.

### 3. Reordering two independent blocks inside a guard re-colours the WHOLE callee-saved map (78.1% → 92.4%, +15, 20 words at once)

The 20-word residual looked like a pure r30/r31 allocator coin-flip: `arg3` (the
file offset) and the head count `arg3 & 3` were swapped, and every pin attempt
made it worse (pinning either one added a 10th saved register — r22 — and wrecked
the function, 4.7%/10.4%). **The fix was one statement order**, not a pin:

```c
/* m2c:  updates first */            /* retail: side effects first */
var_r27 = arg1 + hd;                 memcpy(arg1, buf, hd);
var_r26 = arg3 + hd;                 DCFlushRange(arg1, hd);
memcpy(arg1, buf, hd);               var_r27 = arg1 + hd;
var_r28 = arg2 - hd;                 var_r26 = arg3 + hd;
DCFlushRange(arg1, hd);              var_r28 = arg2 - hd;
```

With the two side-effecting calls first, arg3 gets **r30** and the head gets **r31**
— and because r31 then dies early it becomes available to be **recycled** for the
loop-invariant `dst + 0x2000` (§6z-130 / §70-162). With m2c's order r31 is pinned
by arg3 for the whole function, r30 holds the head, and the invariant is forced
into scratch r8, so 20 words differ and the whole callee-saved map is one
transposition off. **Before parking a 2-register rotation, try moving one
side-effecting statement (call / volatile write) across the pure-arithmetic
updates in its block** — it is a free edit that no pin and no flag reproduces.
Companion in the same function: the copy loop's 6th field must be written
**inline** (`…->unk0x14 = …->unk0x14;` with the `src += 0x18` AFTER it) so the
temp load stays in r0 instead of being staged into a fresh r3 (+1 word).

### 4. Writing a loop-carried update AFTER the call forces a callee-saved home (92.4% → EXACT, 8 words)

`dst += 0x2000` is loop-invariant, so ngccc hoists `addi` into the outer loop's
preheader — and picks a **scratch** reg (r8) when the update is written before
the `DCFlushRange` call. Retail has it in **r31**, at the **end** of the preheader
(after `li r10,0x1ff8`). Moving the statement to *after* the call:

```c
temp_r0 = var_r27;                     /* stale dst for the flush */
<2 tail words>
DCFlushRange(temp_r0, 0x2000);
var_r27 += 0x2000;                     /* AFTER the call */
```

makes the value live across a call, so it *must* get a callee-saved home (r31),
and the resulting preheader order matches retail's exactly. The order is explained
by `reorder_basic_block` grouping by *use priority* (set-here + used-here = pri 1
first, then pri 0 in list order) — `addi r28`/`addi r26` first, then
`mr r11`/`mr r9`/`li r10`, then the hoisted invariant last. **Generalisable
trigger: when a hoisted loop invariant wants a scratch register but retail has a
callee-saved one, write the update after the last call in the loop body.** Same
lever fixes the `li r4,0x2000`-before-`mr r27,ptr` argument/copy interleave for
free, because both are the same preheader/exit-block scheduling question.

### 5. Count-loop shape: flag over pin

The inner 341-iteration countdown must stay `li r10,0x1ff8; addic. r10,r10,-0x18;
… bne` instead of `li r0,0x155; mtctr r0; … bdnz`. `-fno-branch-count-reg` does
it (78.1% → 92.4% at the time); so does a `register s32 ctr __asm__("r10")` pin
(§6y-141) — but the **pin is unnecessary** once the body is right (removing it kept
100.0%), so prefer the flag. The inherited `-fno-schedule-insns2` is still
required (flagless 76.2%, `-fno-schedule-insns` 55.2%, `-fno-gcse` 34.6%).

### 6. Per-call-site prototype discipline (no change needed, but worth stating)

`dvd_read_safe` is 4-arg (its own prologue sets r7/r8 and forwards r3–r6);
`DCFlushRange` is 2-arg; and **`memcpy` must be left IMPLICIT** because retail
carries `crclr cr1eq` before that one `bl` while it carries none before the other
two calls. Adding a memcpy prototype would kill retail's crclr and cost a word
(§6an / §6ac-5, per-call-site not per-library-function).

**Audit of the EXACT:** object `.text` = 0x1A4 = `symbols.txt size:0x1A4` = header
`range=0x8001A9D4-0x8001AB78 size=420B`; only `.text` + `.rela.text` (no private
`.rodata`, so no doc-14 promote caveat); **0 emitted inline instructions**;
7/7 intra-function `R_PPC_REL14` addends land on want's branch targets, 9/9
`R_PPC_REL24` call targets match want's `bl` destinations by symbol, and the 2
local `b`s resolve to `+0x12c`/`+0x18c` = want's `0x8001ab00`/`0x8001ab60` (§6bw
method); no `extern lbl_` data symbol in the body, so the masked-100 %-wrong-label
hazard cannot apply.

## 6dn — 2026-09-30 single pick: an address-taken out-param declared as a **scalar** gets its address HOISTED into a callee-saved reg — re-declaring it as an `N`-byte ARRAY fixes the frame AND the hoisting at once (fn_80054A68, 25.5% → 80.9%)

A QB script-command constructor, 188 B, 5 params, one 0x80-byte local and a
7-store dlist-insert block. The inherited m2c draft was 25.5% with a
**184 B object for a 188 B want** and a 0x28 frame against want's 0x98. Four
semantic edits got it to a size-exact 80.9%. The reusable findings, in the order
they paid:

* **Declare an address-taken out-param as the right-size ARRAY, not a scalar —
  this fixes the frame *and* stops GCC hoisting `&buf` into a saved register.**
  m2c had `s32 sp8;` and passed `&sp8` to two callees. The callees sprintf INTO
  it (`fn_80054894` → `fn_80269f4c` varargs) and strcpy FROM it
  (`fn_8005626C` → `fn_8026B2B4`), so it is a string buffer. Changing one
  declaration to `char sp8[0x80]` fixed **six** words in one edit:
  `stwu -0x98` (was `-0x28`), `stmw r28,0x88` (was `stmw r27,0x14`), `stw/lwz
  r0,0x9c` (was `0x2c`), `lmw r28,0x88`, `addi r1,0x98`, **and** the saved-reg
  COUNT went 5 → 4. The last part is the new lever: with the scalar, GCC
  CSE'd the one `&sp8` web into the entry block as `addi r27,r1,8` and then
  emitted `mr r4,r27` at both call sites; with the array it rematerialises
  `addi r3,r1,8` / `addi r4,r1,8` per site, exactly like retail, and r27 is
  freed. So this is a **cleaner, semantically-honest alternative to
  `volatile s32 spN`** (§6al-180) — no qualifier, no reload, and it also gets
  the frame right. Trigger: "GOT homes `&spN` in a saved reg and want
  recomputes `addi rX,r1,N` per call site" (§6bf's un-share rule, §6cs-1's
  `&local` rematerialisation). Size by the §6db closed form
  `locals = stwu_N − 16 − 4·nSavedGPRs` = 0x98 − 16 − 16 = 0x80 exactly here.
* **The m2c "first arg is the caller itself" convention can be wrong in BOTH
  directions, and the same bug that mis-sized the local also mis-shaped the
  call.** m2c emitted `fn_80054894(arg0, &sp8, arg4)`; the callee's prologue
  (`mr r29,r3; mr r31,r4; cmpwi r5,0`) plus retail's arg setup
  `[addi r3,r1,8][mr r5,r7]` (r4 never touched) show the callee's first
  parameter IS the out-buffer and the caller's arg0 is **not** passed. Fixing
  it to `fn_80054894(sp8, arg1, arg4)` removed the last `mr r3,<param>` copy and
  +3.8 %. Read the callee's arg regs and the caller's `bl`, not the m2c
  convention.
* **In a "node init + dlist insert" run ngccc emits the stores in SOURCE
  order — no rotation, no reverse.** So put the self-link stores FIRST, then
  the vtable pointer, then the scalar fields, then the two head writes. The
  inherited order (`0x4, 0x8, 0xC, 0x10, 0x14`) is what produced the
  interleaved `[0x10][0x4][0x8][0xC][0x14][0x10]` output. +4.3 %.
* **A provably-dead self-init store survives with a `volatile` cast on the
  lvalue** (`*(volatile s32 *)&p->f = (s32)p;`, §6ao-172) and it is the LAST
  edit needed to make the object size-exact (+21 %). Note the asymmetry that
  makes this case work: `p->f = p` followed by `p->g = p` survives on its own
  (the second value is a *load* from a global GCC cannot prove non-aliasing),
  while `p->f = p` followed by `p->f = <constant address>` is DSE'd — the
  constant store is provably non-aliasing. Casting the SECOND store volatile
  instead of the first gives an identical 80.9 % (the surviving store lands in
  the same slot either way), so pick whichever reads better.

**What is still parked, and why it is not a source-shape problem.** The 9
remaining diffs are a pure ORDERING difference inside the 13-instruction init
block — same instruction multiset, no missing or extra instruction. ngccc
hoists BOTH symbol HI16 reloads plus both LO halves to the block top and then
the `li r0,0`; retail emits `[lis r9][li r0,0][addi r9][stw 0xC][stw 0x10]
[lis r11][stw 0x14][addi r11]…` — i.e. the second symbol's reload is *not*
hoisted and the zero *is*. `cc1 -dr` confirms the post-reload RTL of this
draft is already in want's source order, so nothing above reload/sched2
produced it. Exhausted: every scheduling/GCSE flag in the project set, named
locals for the vtable address / the head pointer / the zero, every position for
the zero's birth, both self-links volatile, `"m"` and `"+m"` and `memory`-fence
asm operands, a 1-insn asm `stw` for the dead store, and explicit
`lis`/`addi` `@ha`/`@l` anchor wedges with hard-pinned r9/r11 (§6br) — the
wedges DO put the anchors in the right slots but flip the store run's own
order, and a full pin set costs ~5 emitted instructions (10.6 %, over the
budget). **The useful reading of the RTL dump is that the anchors' slots are
controlled by the delay_slot_filler, not by source order: retail's
`[lis][li][addi][stw][stw][lis][stw][addi]` interleave is literally
`bl←lis`, `lis←li`, `lis←stw`.** Untried lead: pin only the `li r0,0`
(`__asm__("li %0,0" : "=r"(z))` with `register s32 z __asm__("r0")`) and leave
both symbol reloads to ngccc.

**Also confirmed (cheap re-confirmations).** A 64-bit store DOES survive a later
narrower store (so `*(u64 *)(p+0xC) = dup(p)` keeps BOTH `stw`s that retail
keeps) but building the DImode value costs 8 extra instructions — a dead end
for any "write it 8 bytes at a time" idea. A pointer-valued `extern` that is
only ever indexed should be declared at its own width; the three labels here
were hand-decoded from want's `lis`/`addi` pairs (0x80293130 / 0x802931A8 /
0x80364C1C) so the masked-ADDR16 wrong-label hazard (hazard 277) does not apply.
Audit of the 80.9 %: `.text` 0xBC = 188 B = `symbols.txt` `size:0xBC`, only
`.text` + `.rela.text` (no private `.rodata`, so no doc-14 caveat), **0 emitted
inline instructions**, the single `R_PPC_REL14` addend (`.text+0x50` →
0x80054AB8) equals want's `bne` target and all 6 `R_PPC_REL24` targets match
want's `bl`s (§6bw method). One more header trap: once you replace
`Unk_C7387A53`/`Unk_C8FEE62D` with file-local typedefs you must **delete
`#include "structs.h"`** or the redefinition is a hard compile
FAIL that the sweep reports as a bare `FAIL` with no line.

## 6do — 2026-09-30 single pick: a plain `x = 0;` written straight before an
### `if (a op b)` is hoisted into a PREDECESSOR block; naming the condition's
### operands as locals FIRST pushes the zero back down into retail's block
### (fn_80033C1C, 80.0% → 96.36%)

`fn_80033C1C` is a float-guard + dispatch wrapper: two early-out guards, a
`cror cr0un,cr0eq,cr0lt` + `bso` range test whose false edge jumps straight to
the epilogue with a *return variable* that defaults to 0, then four calls.
Retail's stream is

Retail's stream takes the first guard to fail on equal and the second guard to the body on non-equal, zeroes r3 at the fail block before jumping to epilogue, and inside the body loads f13 and f0, zeroes r3, compares unordered, ORs the condition, branches on unordered to epilogue, then later materializes 1 into r3 at epilogue.

i.e. the return variable's `0` lives **inside BODY**, after the two `lfs`. The
`return 0; ret = 0; if (!(f <= K)) { body }` spelling with `f`/`K` read
inline hoisted the `li r3,0` all the way into the guard-2 block (one word
early) and pushed the ternary's own `li r0,0` into BODY, misplacing **both**
zeros and every load behind them. The fix is one edit, no asm:

```c
f = arg0->unk24;                 /* lfs f13  */
K  = lbl_80291C58;               /* lis+lfs  */
ret = 0;                         /* li r3,0  */
if (!(f <= K)) {  ... }          /* fcmpu/cror/bso */
```

* **Why it works:** the two loads are only *used* by the compare, so written
  inline the `ret = 0` has no reason to be ordered after them and the
  constant sinks/hoists to the block that dominates every use. Naming `f`
  and `K` makes the loads independent, statement-ordered definitions; the
  zero then keeps its source position *between* them and the compare.
  This is the **downward** twin of §6bt2/§6cc ("bake the constant into a
  local so the address anchor hoists to the block top") — there the local
  pulls a load UP, here it pulls a following constant DOWN. Neither the
  `ret = 0` hoisting notes (§6c-28, §73-118, §6ap-2, §6z-129 — all about
  forcing a *fresh* `li` or a position) nor the barrier-based ones mention
  the condition's operand expression as the cause.
* **Diagnose it from the diff shape:** a `li rX,0` sitting one or two words
  *earlier* than want, with everything from that point shifted by exactly
  that many words, and a *second* constant appearing where the wanted one
  should be — i.e. the two constants traded places. Count the words first
  (§6cs-1): the size was already right, so it is placement, not length.
* Two other confirmed levers in the same function, both plain C:
  **the return-register pin** (`register s32 ret __asm__("r3");`, §6dg) took
  it 60.71 → 80.0% by homing the return value in r3 and removing a
  `li r0,1; mr r3,r0` tail; and **declaring a dead callee's 5th param as the
  float** (the callee ignores every arg past r3) so expand_call emits
  `lfs f1` before `lwz r7` — §7d-4's mixed-ABI position reorder, worth
  +3.4%. Both were ordinary shape edits; a 25-flag sweep and every
  spellings of the residual were byte-identical no-ops.
* **The residual that is left (2 words, parked):** `cmpwi r9,0` and
  `li r0,0` trade places in a ternary's else-arm. Verified with `cc1 -dj`
  that the post-`jump` RTL is already in retail's order (the `jump` pass
  SINKS the else-value `0` from the branch block into the branch block
  *after* the compare), and that a later `reorder_basic_block`
  (§6bg-8: priority = #users of the result) moves it ahead again — the
  sunk insn's high UID and the shared `const_int 0`'s user count both
  favour it. **16 source spellings of the ternary, an `__asm__("li %0,0")`
  else-arm birth, a `"+r"` barrier and 22 flags all produced a
  byte-identical object**, so this is a genuine post-front-end reorder and
  not source-reachable. The only untried route: give the compare's operand
  register 4+ users (so its priority beats the shared constant) without
  emitting an instruction, which plain C does not offer.

## 6dp — 2026-09-30 single pick: a QB hash-dispatch wrapper, 47.0% → EXACT, where the whole frame hinged on the TYPE of one out-param, and "retail duplicates a per-path load" means *write the expression twice*, not `goto` a shared tail (fn_80033CFC, 468 B / 117 insns, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags)

A 4-arm script-command hash dispatcher (`Script*ReplaceAnim` / `PlaySequence` /
`UpdateDifferenceAnim` / `InvalidateAtCache`) with **one shared `fn_8006FB8C`
tail reached by two arms**. Two of the three load-bearing fixes are
generalizable; the third is a one-line pin.

* **A callee's out-param parameter must be declared `T *`, not `T` — the
  pointer-ness is what makes GCC keep the `&out` ADDRESS in a callee-saved
  register across the call.** m2c had `s32 GetChecksum_2(s32, s32, s32, s32)` and
  passed `&sp8` (a 3-byte-up stack slot) twice. With an *integer* 3rd parameter
  each call re-materialises the address, so the object came out with
  `stwu -0x20 / stmw r30` and two fresh `addi r5,r1,8`. Typing the parameter
  `s32 *` lets local_cse unify the two address moves into ONE web that crosses
  the call, which must then live in a callee-saved register: the frame grows to
  `stwu -0x28 / stmw r29`, and the two call sites become `mr r5,r29`. That one
  token took 47.0% → 75.2% *and* fixed the prologue, the save span and the whole
  case-body layout at once. **Audit parameter POINTER-ness, not just arity** —
  §6bf's arity audit counts args; this bug is invisible to it because the count
  was right.
* **"Retail duplicates a load in each predecessor" ⇒ write the statement twice;
  a `goto` tail is the wrong source shape and *loses an instruction*.** want has
  `lwz r0,0x20(r31); lwz r4,sp8; b <tail>` in arm A and
  `lwz r0,0x20(r31); lwz r4,spC; <fall into tail>`, with the shared block holding
  only `lwz r3,0x1c(r31); add r4,r0,r4; bl; stw`. Four structural variants were
  measured: a `goto` tail with the field read *in* the tail (47.9%, 118 insns),
  a `goto` tail with the field read *per arm* into variables (91.5%, 117 insns
  — the order right but the merge point one word too early), a `goto` tail where
  the tail is arm B's fallthrough (43.1%, 116 insns — GCC CSEs the field load
  into the merge and arm A then skips it), and finally the **duplicated call
  with `break;`** in both arms (100.0%). The diagnosis: a `goto` tail makes the
  expression's *reads* part of the merged block, whereas retail keeps the read
  per-path and shares only the arithmetic+call+store. This is the mirror of
  §6u-1 / §70-134 ("duplicate the call so crossjump merges it") — sometimes the
  duplication is not a trick to *enable* a merge, it is the literal shape.
  **Read want's merge point: if the duplicated instructions sit BEFORE it, your
  tail block is one instruction too fat.**
* **A `NULL`/`!= 0` guard whose value want loads into an argument register (r3)
  rather than r0: hard-pin the tested value, 0 emitted instructions.** Here
  `if (mgr->unk0x1C != 0)` came out `lwz r0,0x1c(r31); cmpwi r0,0` where want has
  `lwz r3,0x1c(r31); cmpwi r3,0`. No spelling, cast, polarity, staging or flag
  moved it (10 variants, all byte-identical), but
  `register s32 cur __asm__("r3"); cur = mgr->unk0x1C; if (cur != 0)` reproduced
  it exactly — 2 words, +1.7%. §6be-1 / §72-143 get the *live-as-an-argument*
  case for free; this is the case where the callee is 0-arg and the value is
  dead after the test, so the register has to be **bought**. Ablation: removing
  the pin alone costs 2 words, so it is load-bearing (and 0 insns, so it stays
  inside the §4g budget).
* **Inherited `// FLAG: -fno-expensive-optimizations` was worth 0 on the correct
  body** (97.4% either way) but +24 points on the broken one (28.7% → 75.2%):
  a second clean instance of §6bx. Measure every inherited flag AFTER the
  semantic round, and delete it if it is then inert.
* **Tool trap that nearly cost the function:** writing the final body by hand
  silently dropped a character from `QB_DIFFERENCEANIMNAME`
  (→ `QB_DIFFERENCEANIMAME`), which `compile_fn` reported as a bare `FAIL` and
  which my own scoring script *also* reported as FAIL — but for a different
  reason on each, so the two disagreed and the real cause was hidden. **A new
  draft that touches macro names must be scored with
  `tools/test_wip_drafts.py --addr` (the authority) after the write**, not with
  the scratch scorer, and a FAIL right after a 100% is a typo, not a regression.

**Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object `.text` =
0x1D4 = 468 B = `symbols.txt` `size:0x1D4` = header `size=468B`; only `.text` +
`.rela.text` (no private `.rodata`, so no doc-14 promote caveat); **0 emitted
inline instructions**; all **27** branch relocations (9 `R_PPC_REL14` +
18 `R_PPC_REL24`) verified against want's decoded targets, 0 mismatches (§6bw
method); the 8 QB hash constants live in `lis`/`ori` immediates, which are
**not** relocation-masked, so the 100% byte-verifies them.

## 6dq — 2026-09-30 single pick: the `lwzu` update form needs a **DEAD-OLD-VALUE
### pointer reassignment** (not a walk), and `__ps_t` is **8 bytes**, so a 16-byte
### PS copy is **two** assignments (fn_8004631C, 49.3% → EXACT, 292 B, 0 emitted asm)

`fn_8004631C` (a 292 B `element3d_add_components` / `init_model` script command)
was an m2c draft at 49.3% whose object was **32 bytes = 8 words SHORT**. Both
root causes are already-documented families, but the precise *trigger* of each is
new and was worth 49.3% → 100% on its own.

**1. A short-by-an-integer-multiple object in a zone with `psq_*` in the want is
an undecoded PS pair copy — and `__ps_t` is the 8-BYTE type, so the copy is TWO
assignments.** The draft's tail was two dead `0;` statements (m2c modelling the
PS words as garbage); want's tail loads the loop index from offset 0x4B0 of the homed arg0 into r11, performs a paired-single load of the first pair from offset zero of the source held in r27 (which homes the second argument originally in r5), derives the destination by scaling the index for a 32-byte stride and adding the 0x1A0 offset into r9, then stores the first pair at destination offset zero, loads the second pair from source offset eight, and stores that pair at destination offset eight.

Two things bite: (a) the object needs `// FLAG: -mps-float` (otherwise `__ps_t`
copy assignments lower to nothing, which is exactly why the earlier session
measured "writing the real `*(__ps_t*)` drops it to 6.8%" — it was scored
**flagless**); and (b) `sizeof(__ps_t)` in cc1 is **8**, so a 16-byte copy is
`d[0] = *(volatile __ps_t*)src; d[1] = *(volatile __ps_t*)(src+8);` — declaring
a struct member as a single `__ps_t` puts the *next* member 8 bytes too low
(the merged `Unk_*` header does `typedef double __ps_t` for non-ngccc, so a
hand-written `__ps_t` member in a field-layout typedef is 8 bytes, not 16 —
use `char _1A0[0x10]`). Getting the copy in ALSO brings back the `arg2` param
home copy (`mr r27, r5`) that had been DCE'd, which frees the whole
callee-saved map (6 saved GPRs + `stmw r26` → 5 + `stmw r27`). **Detection
rule: when a draft's compiled object is short by a whole number of words and
`tools/ps_disasm.py` shows `psq_l`/`psq_st` in the want's tail, decode the
missing words as a `__ps_t` copy before touching anything else.**

**2. `lwzu rD, off(rA)` (opcode 33) needs the pointer's OLD value to be DEAD —
so the C must *reassign* the pointer, not just offset it.** want:
`add r30,r30,r31 ; lwzu r3,0x190(r30) ; ... ; mr r4,r30 ; stw r0,0(r30)`, i.e. the
same register carries the pre- and post-increment value. Six pointer spellings
all produced the same folded code (`lwz r3,0x130(r30)` + `addi r4,r30,0x190`,
one extra saved register and a 5-word diff) until the pointer was *reassigned*:

```c
s32 *link;
link = (s32 *)((idx << 5) + (s32)arg0);
link = (s32 *)((char *)link + 0x190);   /* old value now dead */
old  = *link;                          /* -> lwzu r3,0x190(r30) */
```

The working spelling is **statement form with a dead old value**, NOT the
`p[i]`/`*(s32*)((char*)p+off)` forms (§4f `ai`, recipe 66) and NOT
`p += 0x190` folded by the front end. The promoted `src/fn_800A7D1C.c`
(`var_r31 = (s32 *)((char *)var_r31 - 0xC); temp_r3 = *(s32 *)var_r31;`) and
`src/fn_8016F668.c` (`p += 0x190; if (*(s32 *)p == 0) break;`) are the same
mechanism; §6ba-286 records only the *walk* case (load offset == increment),
which is a different trigger and does not generalise here. Note ngccc's C89
front-end **rejects a declaration after a statement** (`parse error before
'x'`), so the locals must be declared at the function top.
→ 87.7% → 94.5%.

**3. A m2c-invented extra call argument keeps `lis r5, 0x8030` alive; the real
call is SHORTER and `r5` merely retains the function's own `arg2`.** The draft
passed `fn_800A1A84(lbl_80301A38, arg1, 0x80300000)` — the third argument was
pure m2c invention (a bare `li r5,0x8030` in the got). Declaring the callee
2-arg and calling `fn_800A1A84(ga, arg1)` moved the `arg2` home copy from the
top of the entry block down to just before the call *and* restored
`lwz r30, 0x4b0(r31)` to its slot: 94.5% → 97.3%, two words left. (§6ap-132 /
§6bf arity audit, but note the *pull* direction: dropping a phantom arg can
move a param home copy, so re-check the whole body after an arity fix.)

**4. Last 2 words = a param home copy emitted before an independent call-argument
load ⇒ a zero-code `"+r"` barrier ON THE LOADED VALUE.** want
`lis r9 ; lwz r3,0x1a38(r9) ; mr r28,r4`; got
`lis r9 ; mr r28,r4 ; lwz r3,0(r9)`. Both `mr`s and both loads have cost 512
(`movsi+1`) and the home copy has the lower LUID, so no source ordering, no
statement position and no flag reaches it (20 flags all no-op or worse);
`__asm__("" : "+r"(ga));` immediately after the load makes the load's web
opaque and the `lwz` lands first: 97.3% → **100.0%, 0 emitted instructions.**
Same lever as §6dj-2 (a barrier after the function's first load splitting the
prologue param copies) — the discriminator is that the diff is a *transposition
of an independent load against a param home copy*, not a load/store interleave.

**Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object `.text` =
0x124 = 292 B = `symbols.txt` `size:0x124` = header `range=0x8004631C-0x80046440
size=292B`; only `.text` + `.rela.text` (no private `.rodata`, so no doc-14
pool caveat); **0 emitted inline instructions**; both `R_PPC_REL14` addends
(`.text+54` and `.text+6c`, readelf prints them hex) give 0x80046370 /
0x80046388 = want's two `beq` targets, and all 5 `R_PPC_REL24` targets
(`fn_800A1A84`, `fn_8009DFC0`, `fn_8009DFA0`, `Script_RunScript` ×2) match want's
`bl`s (§6bw method); `lbl_80301A38` hand-decoded from want's `lis 0x8030` +
`lwz 0x1a38` = 0x80301A38 and confirmed in `symbols.txt` (`.data`, size 4) so
hazard 277 does not apply; both QB hash literals are `lis`/`ori` immediates
(unmasked) and byte-verified.

## 6dr — 2026-09-30 single pick: the guard's SPELLING (`!= 0 { body }` vs `== 0 return`) changes the *arg-setup scheduling of a call inside the guarded block*, and a promoted twin in `src/` often contains the whole idiom verbatim (fn_800AACC0, 44.9% → 98.2%)

A 448 B `GameObj` composite-structure builder. The 44.9% baseline was the
 ADDENDUM case exactly: 8 undeclared callees (one `crclr cr1eq` each)
plus 6 wrong call sites. The whole body of the second half existed already,
byte-proven, in **`src/fn_800AAF30.c`** (a promoted 296 B sibling) — same
vcall, same `GetInteger` / `fn_800F0AFC` / `CStruct_ctor(CStruct_new(8))` /
`AddChecksum` / `AddInteger` / `Script_RunScript` / `CStruct_delete` chain,
same `GetChecksum_2` + `GetStructure_2` + `fn_8009F204` tail.

* **Porting a promoted sibling's *whole idiom* (not just its typedefs) is worth
  more than any scheduling lever, and the file-local `Obj_t` / `Vt_t` pair
  comes along for free** — including the `s16` method offset at +0x48 that
  makes want's `lha` appear (the corpus-merged `Unk_9994C3F5` types it `s32`,
  so this is M6.89d, not a cast). §6dc established "find the twin by the
  CALLEE SET"; here the twin was findable because **two of the drafted calls
  (`fn_8009F204`, `GetStructure_2`) appear in only a handful of promoted
  files at all** — `rg -l fn_8009F204 src/` returns 9 names out of ~7000, and
  the right one is among them. A narrow callee is a *very* strong twin key.
  44.92% → 97.32% in one edit.
* **The one-word `if (callee(...) != 0) { body }` → `if (callee(...) == 0)
  return ret; body` rewrite is a real scheduling lever, not a style change**
  (97.32% → 98.21%). Both forms emit the identical `cmpwi r3,0 / beq <shared
  epilogue>`, and the branch target is unchanged — but the *positive* form
  leaves the guarded call at the START of a conditional block, while the
  early-return form makes it the fall-through of a straight-line one. In this
  function that moved the `&sp10` `addi` out of 4th place and up into the
  `lis r4,0x7031` **delay slot**, exactly where want has it, cutting a
  3-insn cycle down to a 2-insn one. The tell that this is worth trying:
  want's guarded call has its address `addi` in the *previous* `lis`'s delay
  slot, which is a shape a conditional-block head does not produce.
  Related-but-different: §6be's "single EXIT with a return VARIABLE", §73-135
  and §6bo (both about the *return* value, not the guarded block).
* **`fn_800D034C(Mem_NewZero(0x98))` — a callee whose prologue does
  `mr r31,r3` called with NO arg setup at the `bl` is a CHAINED return from
  the preceding call, not a 0-arg call.** `src/fn_801A0DA8.c` (promoted)
  spells the same idiom and settles the arity without a probe. The m2c draft
  had both the statement form and a 0-arg declaration, which is a
  `crclr cr1eq`; declaring the real 1-arg prototype and threading
  `Mem_NewZero`'s result removed it.
* **`CStruct_new(arg0, 8)` → `CStruct_new(8)` with the result chained into
  `CStruct_ctor()`**: m2c invented a leading `arg0` and dropped the chain.
  The tell is want's `li r3,8 / bl CStruct_new / bl CStruct_ctor / mr r31,r3`
  — the *second* `bl` has no r3 setup at all. Same detector as §6bh
  ("an arg the draft passes but want never sets ⇒ chain it").
* **`GetChecksum_3` returning `void *` is worth the `cmpwi`→`or.` flip** on the
  following NULL test (§6be pointer-NULL rule) — and it is the *only* part of
  the fix that is not a plain port from the twin.
* **The residual (2 of 112 words) is a 3-insn arg-setup cycle that is
  INVARIANT to ~40 source shapes, 15 scheduler/GCSE flags, 5 zero-code asm
  barriers and 4 emitted-asm wedges** (hard pins on arg regs regress hard, as
  §6by-4 predicts: 91.96% / 89.29% / 82.30%). **The decisive diagnostic is
  that the promoted twin compiles the IDENTICAL construct to want's order** —
  so the blocker is function context (4 saved GPRs, one extra call block
  before the tail), not the source text, and grinding more source shapes is
  wasted. When a promoted twin proves the shape is reachable, say so in the
  park note instead of re-trying permutations. Post-reload RTL order for the
  block is `[set 0][stw][addi][mr r3][set r4=const][set r5][set r6][call]`;
  sched1 emits the `mr` there, and nothing in C moves it behind the
  `ori`. Two further notes for the audit: the object carries the `lwz`'s
  `0x1a38` as an **ADDR16_LO reloc with addend 0** (the object literally
  reads `lwz r30,0(r9)`, which looks wrong in `objdump` and is masked in the
  score — it is link-correct, the same shape as the byte-identical
  `src/fn_800ACAB0.c`); and every `// family=` line must survive a header
  rewrite (§6bg) or the sweep silently scores the draft flagless.

## 6ds — 2026-09-30 single pick: a `register … __asm__("rN")` var emits a
### **NOTE_INSN_BLOCK_BEG/END pair around its scope** in `cc1 -dr`, and a
### FUNCTION-scope pin puts that split where it breaks an unrelated `if`/else
### — and a NESTED-scope pin is the only survivable form (fn_80220060, 32.9% → 87.3%)

`fn_80220060` (316 B, network/lobby Script* zone) was an m2c draft at 32.9%
with seven semantic errors. Two findings from the last 13% are generalizable
and each cost a full debugging round.

**1. A register variable is a BASIC-BLOCK BOUNDARY, and its SCOPE decides
where the boundary lands.** `cc1 -dr` (post-reload RTL) on the same body
with and without a pin:

Without a pin the halfword store, word store, immediate, byte stores run with no block-begin note; with a nested r0 pin the block split lands after the halfword store, and with the pin on the word-store-first shape the split lands before the word store.

With the pin on a NESTED scope whose only statement is the f04 store, the
split lands harmlessly and the build is byte-exact to 81% (the pin also
buys the register colour). The moment the same pin is put at
**function scope** — or the f04 store is moved to be the FIRST statement of
the block — the split lands in front of a one-instruction block, and cc1's
block reordering / if-conversion then relocates the block into the
*preceding* `if` arm: 40+ words collapse (81% → 32%, and the object loses a
word). Measured: nested-scope pin 81.0% / function-scope pin 68.4% /
nested-with-f04-first 32.1% / nested-block-wrapping-both 28.2% — for the
*same* pin and the *same* colours. **So: when a hard-reg pin changes the
score by tens of points, dump `cc1 -dr` and check whether a block split
appeared; the pin's cost is the split, not the register.**
(`cc1 -dr` on a body with the `//`-comment and `#include "types.h"`
lines stripped and `s32/u32/s8/u8/s16/u16` typedefs inlined — cc1 does not
preprocess.)

**2. Pinning ONE local can hand the RETAIL register to every OTHER local in
the same block, because the local hard-reg pool is positional/cyclic.**
Retail used `r8` (strlen+0x12), `r0` (&fr.sp8), `r9` (0x4C), `r11` (2),
`r10` (8) — five consecutive allocations from one pool. Plain C handed out
`r10, r8, r0, r9, r11`: the *same* cyclic sequence, started four slots later.
Adding a single nested `register s32 t4 __asm__("r0")` on the `&fr.sp8`
value removes it from the pool, and the remaining four then fall onto
retail's registers exactly. **Diagnose a "5-way register rotation" as a pool
OFFSET, not five independent choices: identify the member retail assigns to
the middle of the rotated run, pin THAT one, and re-score. Pinning the
first member of the run (the one at the pool's nominal start) instead moves
every colour one slot the wrong way and loses ~6% (78.5% vs 81.0% here).**
This is the generalisation of §6cs-3's "pin one member of a permuted group" —
the mechanism is that one pin consumes one pool slot, so it also fixes the
offset of everything downstream in the same block.

**3. Cheap positive/negative that came free with (2): `-fno-schedule-insns2`
was worth +6.3% here (81.0% → 87.3%) on a residual that looked like a hard
regalloc wall — it moved an `addi r30,r1,0xa0` birth from slot 9 to slot 3
of its block. Every other sched/GCSE flag in the project set was a no-op on
the same body (§4r, §6aq-198, §6am).**

## 6ds2 — 2026-09-30 single pick: to stop ngccc LICM-hoisting ONE loop-invariant symbol address, use a **NON-VOLATILE** `lis` asm with a LOOP-VARIANT input — the volatile spelling of the same anchor reaches the same place but reloads every arg register live across it (fn_800AE8C4, 48.8% → 94.0%, 3 emitted insns)

§6ap-3 / §6br document the "opaque anchor" trick for a symbol address that retail
re-materialises per use site instead of hoisting into the loop preheader, and both
recommend the **`volatile`** spelling:
`__asm__ volatile("lis %0,%1@ha" : "=r"(pg) : "s"(sym))`. That works for placement
but has a large hidden cost, and the **non-volatile** spelling with an extra
loop-variant input achieves the same placement with none of it:

```c
/* WRONG (volatile): placement is right, but reload.c marks every hard reg live
   across a volatile asm, so a call-result value that retail keeps flowing in an
   arg register across the anchor needs an extra `mr r3,rN` — here +1 insn and
   `self` loses r28. */
register s32 pg __asm__("r9");
__asm__ volatile("lis %0,%1@ha" : "=r"(pg) : "s"(lbl_80298644));
fn_800394CC(sk, *(f32 *)((char *)pg - 0x79BC));      /* wants r3 = the C9780 ret */

/* RIGHT: a plain non-volatile asm is a movable insn, so feeding it a value that
   changes every iteration makes it non-loop-invariant and LICM cannot hoist it out of
   the loop — while the register allocator still keeps r3 live across it. */
register s32 pg __asm__("r9");
__asm__("lis %0,%1@ha" : "=r"(pg) : "s"(lbl_80298644), "r"(ent));
fn_800394CC(sk, *(f32 *)((char *)pg - 0x79BC));
```

* **Measured on fn_800AE8C4 (5 symbol addresses, retail hoists exactly 2 of them
  into the preheader and re-materialises 3 in the body):** volatile anchors on all
  three = 22.4% with a 340 B object (one instruction too long); non-volatile with
  loop-variant inputs on all three = 53.6% at the right 336 B. Anchor the inputs
  cost 0 extra instructions because each chosen value is already live in a hard
  register at that point.
* **WHICH loop-variant value you pick is itself a scheduling lever (+2.4%).** The
  input must be live at the anchor AND not itself a home copy: `"r"(e)` where
  `e = (AE8C4_e *)*ent` is a just-made home copy and schedules after `mr r31,r3`;
  `"r"(ent)` (the loop pointer) does not, and the `lis` then lands in retail's slot.
* **The C supplies the low half, so only ONE asm instruction is needed per
  address** and the encoding matches retail's exactly: `pg - 0x3AF8` →
  `addi r27,r9,-0x3af8`, `*(f32 *)((char *)pg - 0x79BC)` → `lfs f1,-0x79bc(r9)`
  (the displacement folds). 3 anchors = 3 emitted insns of 84 = 3.6 %.
* **Pin the page scratch (`register s32 pg __asm__("r9")`) when the address feeds a
  register-var-pinned local**, or front-end coalescing puts the `lis` into the
  pinned register (`lis r27,hi ; addi r27,r27,lo` instead of `lis r9,hi ; addi
  r27,r9,lo`) — worth +4.8 % on its own here.
* **The `s` operand needs an `extern char sym[]` decl** (an `extern f32` gives
  "inconsistent operand constraints" in this cc1), so the C side has to build the
  typed access from the page.
* Two companion findings from the same function, both already-known families but
  worth the reminder: ngccc hoists **N−1** of N loop-invariant symbol addresses
  into the preheader and re-materialises exactly one (so "which one is remat'd"
  is a coin flip you steer, not a fixed slot — anchoring two moved the third);
  and **the statement position of the LAST anchor is worth a lot**: moving the
  lbl_8037CE08 anchor from before the float guard to immediately before the call
  that consumes it took the function 69.0 % → 83.3 %.
* Still parked at 94.0 %: the lbl_8037BD08 preheader anchor is emitted LAST
  instead of 2nd (a `loop.c: hoist_insn_out_of_loop` pass-order artifact — 6
  preheader statement orders, 19 flags and every anchor spelling leave it last),
  and a COND_EXPR's else-value `li` always precedes its `cmpwi` because `sched`
  picks the cheapest ready insn (12 spellings, all byte-identical). Full lever log
  in `src/wip/fn_800AE8C4.c`.

## 6dt — 2026-09-30 single pick: retail's 5-word `bne/li/b/lwz` if/else is
### unreachable from ANY if/else spelling — the route is an **in-place update
### on the tested variable + a 1-word opaque-asm `li` birth**; and a frame pad
### must be a **non-volatile `double` pinned by `"m"`**, not `volatile double`,
### if the used local must keep slot 8 (fn_8013EBEC, 42.0% → EXACT 276B,
### 1 emitted asm insn / 69 = 1.4%)

Script-command-zone wrapper (0x8013EBEC, 276 B): a 12-byte stack struct in a
`for (i=0; i<=0xFF; i++)` over `arg0 + 0x884 + i*0x18`, each entry running a
sentinel-terminated (`unk0x4 == -1` → NULL) list walk that calls
`fn_80137FEC(field, 3)` and one vtable method (`lha` offset @+8, fn ptr @+C,
arg2 == 3).

**1. The 1-word `b` (the "redundant" branch retail keeps).** Retail compares r11 against zero, branches to the else label when nonzero with the load kept out of line, materialises zero into r11 inline for the else value, emits an explicit branch to the join that GCC 2.95 never produces, then places the word-load from offset four of the pointer at the else label before the join.
Measured: **every** C spelling collapses to the 4-word
`li rX,0 / beq L_join / lwz rX,4(r9) / L_join:` — `if (a==0){b=0;}else{b=f(a);}`,
`if (a!=0){b=f(a);}else{b=0;}`, `b = c ? f(a) : 0`, both ternary polarities,
`b = a; if (b==0){b=0;}else{b=f(b);}`, in-place `if (a==0){a=0;}else{a=f(a);}`
(3 words — GCC value-numbers the dead `li` away), and three `goto`/label forms
