with and without a cold empty label. Identical on **all five in-tree ProDG
builds** (3.5 / 3.5b140 / 3.7 / 3.8.1 / 3.9.3), and `-fno-thread-jumps`,
`-fno-schedule-insns{,2}`, `-fno-sched-interblock`, `-fno-gcse` are all no-ops.
The `b` is `simplify_jump` inverting the test away; you cannot stop it from C.
**The route is the in-place update plus an opaque birth of the `li`:**
```c
register void *n __asm__("r11");                 /* colour */
...
if (n == NULL) { __asm__("li %0,0" : "=r"(n)); }  /* the value retail has  */
else            { n = *(s32 *)((char *)n + 4); }  /* in-place: base == dest  */
```
268 B → 276 B and EXACT, with the `li` counted as the very instruction retail
emits. It is §6x-89 ("want keeps a provably-dead `li`") + §6bq's opaque birth
(§6y-140 / §73-183), but the *conjunction* is the new part: **the asm birth
alone is not enough** (a 2-variable `b` with the same `li` birth scored 68.1%),
and the in-place update alone is not enough (it folds the `li`, 268 B). It is
also a third instance of §6bf-A: neither half alone looked like progress.
**Generalises: when retail has a provably-dead constant `li` sitting in a
branch's fall-through, first try making the update IN-PLACE on the tested
variable, then the `li` birth — and measure the pair, not the parts.**

**2. A frame pad that preserves the *other* local's slot: `double` + `"m"`
pin, NOT `volatile double`.** Want's `stwu -0x30` / `stmw r27,0x1c` / 5 saved
GPRs implies exactly 20 bytes of locals, with the 12-byte used struct at
`r1+8`. §4c's `volatile double _dummy;` adds the 8 bytes and keeps the base
register — but the `volatile` local is 8-ALIGNED, so it takes the lowest
8-aligned slot `r1+8` and pushes the used local to `r1+0x10`, costing the
`addi r11,r1,8` word. What works: a **plain `double` kept alive by a single
zero-code pin**, which lands *above* the used local and leaves the frame and
`addi` alone:
```c
s32 sp8;  double _dummy;
... body ...
__asm__("" : : "m"(_dummy));     /* zero instructions, reserves the 8 bytes */
```
Measured, all of them: `volatile double` → 95.65% (1 diff, the `addi`);
`char _pad[16]` / `s32 _p0,_p1` / `char _pad[8]` → dropped entirely (frame
stays 0x28, 89.9%); `double _pad` + `"m"` pin → **100%**. Two extra facts:
* **the pin's POSITION matters** — before the first store it also re-sorts the
  prologue (94.2%), at the very END of the function it is inert and correct
  (the cold-path form of §6ap-5).
* **every 20-byte SINGLE local destroys the base register**: `s32 sp8[5]`,
  `struct { s32 a,b,c,d,e; }`, `char sp8[20]`, and a nested-scope
  `register char *bp __asm__("r29")` all drop the `&sp8` web into `r1`
  displacements and save only 4 GPRs (7.5%). So the pad must be a SEPARATE
  object, not a bigger one — the opposite of the §6db "size the buffer to
  fill the frame" instinct, which fails here because the pad is never read.

**3. Pointer-typed register pins DO bind (soft form of §76-178/§6az-245).**
`register void *var_r11 __asm__("r11");` on the outer list-node temp (33.8% vs
20.6%) and the same pin on the inner, non-overlapping live range (35.3%) put
both node temps in r11 exactly as retail does. This is §6df's conditional
form: cc1 binds a pointer pin whose value has a single def pseudo. Pinning the
*loop index* to r10 (where retail's `li r10,0` lives) was a REGRESSION
(35.3% → 26.9%) — pin the pointer webs, leave the induction variable to
`local_alloc`, and remember §6by-4 (r10 is an argument register).

## 6du — 2026-09-30 single pick: **a zero-code `__asm__ volatile("")` as the FIRST
### statement of an `else` arm flips ngccc to want's branchy `bne/li/b/<then>/<join>`
### select, and a `"+r"` barrier in that arm's `v == NULL → v = NULL` keeps the
### otherwise-dead `li` alive** (fn_8000A3DC, 45.5% → 92.2%, 308B, 0 emitted asm)

`fn_8000A3DC` (node-family list-advance, sibling of the promoted
`fn_8000A1FC` / `fn_8000A288`) went 45.5% → **92.2%, size-exact 308B, and
everything from word 11 to word 77 byte-identical** with two changes, both of
which emit **zero** instructions. The other 5 fixes were ordinary (prototype
audit, statement order, frame padding, two store-run rotations).

**1. The `else`-arm `__asm__ volatile("")` chooses the block layout, and the
wrong choice is also the wrong LENGTH.** Want compares r9 against zero, branches to the then-label when nonzero, materialises zero into r9, branches explicitly to the join, places the word-load from offset four of the pointer at the then-label, and joins on the store to offset 0x40 of the homed arg0,

i.e. the NULL arm inline with an explicit `b`, the load out of line, the join
on the store. Every plain spelling produces one of the *test-then-materialize*
shapes instead, which are 4–5 words where want has 6 — so the object is the
wrong length and everything downstream compares shifted. Measured, all
308 B or not: ternary both polarities, `if/else` both polarities, separate
result variable, pre-init + conditional assign, `if (v)`, goto state machine
(§6az), `+r` barrier before/after the test, `volatile` on the local — 14
spellings, **none** gave `bne`. The winner, and the only difference between
the best and second-best variant (76.6% → 88.3% when the shape flipped):

```c
if (var_r9 == NULL) {
    __asm__ volatile("");          /* <-- the whole lever */
    var_r9_2 = NULL;
} else {
    var_r9_2 = *(s32 *)((char *)var_r9 + (s32)0x4);
}
```

**Sibling worth knowing:** the same barrier placed at the *top of the `then`
arm* instead pushes toward the same layout (it is what makes the else block
distinct at all); placed at the *end of the whole if* or after the test it is
a no-op. This is §6ad-173 / §6y-129's "empty `asm volatile("")` is a real block
boundary" used for **layout** rather than for a delay-slot fill.

**2. When retail keeps a `li rX,0` in a branch SHADOW, a `"+r"` identity
barrier is enough — no opaque `li` birth needed.** Here the source arm is
`if (v == NULL) { v = NULL; } else { v = v->0x4; }`, which is *provably* a
no-op, so cc1 deletes both the assignment and the `li` and the select collapses
to 5 words (4 bytes short). One zero-code barrier on the tested variable,
placed **before** the redundant assignment, makes the pre-test value opaque
to the redundancy check and the `li` survives — and because the value is
opaque the compiler also keeps the *branchy* block layout rather than
if-converting. Recipe:

```c
if (v == NULL) {
    __asm__("" : "+r"(v));
    v = NULL;                       /* want's `li r9,0` in the branch shadow */
} else { v = v->0x4; }
```

This is the cheap (0 emitted instructions) cousin of §6y-140 / §70-145 /
§6aq-145's `__asm__("li %0,0" : "=r"(v))` opaque-**birth**: the birth is
needed when the dead `li` feeds a *store*, but when it is only a branch-shadow
materialisation a `"+r"` barrier already defeats the fold, and it additionally
re-rolls the surrounding `maybe_reorder_blocks` decision. **Prefer it — 0
insn, and it never needs a hard-reg pin.**

**Other reusable facts from this function, all measured:**

* **§6av's "unprototyped callee ⇒ spurious `crclr cr1eq`" applied to a
  PROMOTED callee.** `fn_8000A19C` is byte-identical in `src/` with
  `(Unk_C7387A53 *, s32)`, but the m2c draft had no declaration in scope and
  called it as `fn_8000A19C(3)`. Adding `extern void fn_8000A19C(void *, s32);`
  and passing the real field load `fn_8000A19C(*(void **)((char *)arg0 + 0x3C), 3)`
  removed the `crclr` and moved 45.5% → the whole function's worth of
  alignment. **A callee that is already promoted is still a missing
  prototype in the caller.**
* **An OOB-addressed scalar local is the ONLY thing that makes ngccc
  materialise a scratch base register + `mr` home copy** (§6ap-6 extended and
  bounded). `s32 sp8;` with `&sp8+4` / `&sp8+8` gives
  `addi r9,r1,8 … stw 4(r9) … mr r30,r9`; the *same* accesses on a
  `s32 sp8[3]`, `s32 sp8[4]` or a 16-byte struct fold to `r1+displacement`
  and the `mr` disappears (measured 296 B vs 308 B), and a named-pointer
  version homes the address straight in r30 with no birth copy. Corollary and
  the parking reason for what is left here: **the OOB scalar is allocated
  LAST in the locals area, so it can never sit at the bottom** — with 4/8/12
  bytes of `volatile` padding the base lands at 0x0c/0x10/0x14/0x18 for every
  padding size, type (`volatile s32/double/char[]`, `p[3]`) and declaration
  order tried. So "grow the frame by 8 bytes" and "get a base register at
  `r1+8`" are mutually exclusive here. **When a draft's base register is at
  the wrong frame offset, check first whether its stores land inside its own
  declared local** — if they land in the callee-save area the body is not
  promotable at any masked score, and a negative-offset OOB form
  (`&sp8 - 0xC + 4`) is the semantically-correct fallback (88.3% here:
  right addresses, wrong base/displacement signs).
* **Entry-block statement order is a 3-way lever, not a 2-way one** (recipe
  57 / §6o-81, sharpened): with the `var_r11` load *last* you get want's
  `lis`-first + `+8`-store-first entry order but the object shrinks to 292 B
  and `mr r31,r3` falls to 4th; with the load *first* you get the right
  length and `mr r31,r3` first but the `lis` lands 2 words late. All four
  remaining permutations of the other three statements score identically, so
  the choice is binary.
* **`-fno-schedule-insns2` fixes the entry window and wrecks the else branch**:
  70.1% with the wanted store order and `lis` position but a whole-function
  re-allocation of the `else` arm and the tail. No flag beat the default.

## 6dv — 2026-09-30 single pick: a want-side **5-insn `bne/li/b/lwz` select** is
### present in the POST-RELOAD RTL but is destroyed by `fold_cond_expr` (branch
### polarity) and by the `jump` pass (arm hoist) — only a **MEMORY** destination
### survives (fn_8022BBD0, 24.0% → 42.0% size-exact 200B, parked)

`fn_8022BBD0` (200 B, ProDG zone, no calls) is an inlined `search_t` iterator walk.
The inherited m2c draft was 24.0% and structurally wrong; the semantic rebuild
(16-byte `search_t` + a `Node_t` typedef, `arg0 += 0xAC` param reassignment, a
do-while whose latch back-edge targets the `cmpwi r4,0` HEAD, two `&sp8` address
webs) reached **size-exact 200 B at 42.0%**. The last item is a genuine compiler
wall, and it is worth recording because the DIAGNOSTIC generalises.

**The residual: want emits, twice, a five-instruction select** that compares the pointer against zero, branches to the load label when nonzero, materialises zero inline as the fall-through, branches to the join, and places the word-load from offset four at the load label before the join.
i.e. the standard `expand_expr` COND_EXPR layout, but the branch **jumps to the
`else` arm** (polarity `bne` = jump-if-true to the load) and the `li` block is the
*fall-through* and ends in a real `b` to the join. Everything else in the function
now matches.

**Root cause, measured with `cc1 -dr` on a 6-line probe** (`cc1` does not
preprocess, so inline the `s32` typedef and drop `#include`; AGENTS §6bz already
documents the invocation). For
```c
T *q1(T *m) { T *r; r = (m == 0) ? (T *)0 : m->b; if (r == 0) { gv = 1; return 0; } return 1; }
```
the **post-reload RTL is already the 5-word shape**:
```
(compare 84 = (reg 82 0))  (jump 10: if (84 == 0) → label 15 else fallthrough)
(set 83 = mem[82+4])      (jump 13: → label 18)  (barrier 14)
(label 15) (set 83 = 0)   (label 18) (compare 85 = (reg 83 0)) ...
```
So the shape is *reachable*; two things then destroy it:
1. **`fold_cond_expr` (front end)** rewrites the test from `m == 0` to `m != 0`
   with the arms swapped. That is semantically identical but it **flips the
   branch polarity** — probe3's RTL branches `beq → the lwz block`, want branches
   `bne → the lwz block`.
2. **the `jump` pass** then hoists the arm's pure `SET 83,0` above the branch and
   deletes the now-dead `b`, collapsing 5 words to 3 (`if (m) r = m->b;`) or 4.
   A store is *not* hoistable, which is the whole escape hatch (below).

**Every C spelling I could find collapses it identically** (probe of 18 forms ×
a 13×13 joint sweep of the two diamonds in the real function): ternary both
polarities, if/else both polarities, `m ? .. : ..`, statement-first `r = 0;
if (m) r = m->b;`, the goto form with an explicit join label, a nested
`({ ... })` condition, a distinct destination variable (which does produce want's
`or. rD,rS,rS` copy — §6ca-2 — but still 4 words), zero-code `"+r"` barriers
before and after the select, and every flag cc1 accepts
(`-fno-thread-jumps`, `-fno-gcse`, `-fno-schedule-insns{,2}`, `-fno-sched-spec`,
`-fno-sched-interblock`, `-fno-expensive-optimizations`, `-O1/-Os/-O3`): all
192–196 B, none 200 B. **Measure the length first (§6cs-1) — a 1-word-per-select
shortfall is worth ~2 points of masked score all by itself here.**

**The one construct that DOES survive: a MEMORY destination.** A minimal probe
`if (m == 0) *pp = 0; else *pp = m->b;` emits
```
cmpwi|bne|stw|b|lwz|stw
```
in **all five in-tree ProDG versions** (3.5 / 3.5b140 / 3.7 / 3.8.1 / 3.9.3) —
same 5-word skeleton as want, with a store in each arm instead of a `li`.
Using that shape for the ENTRY select (a scratch struct field + a read-back into a
register) is what brought the object to the exact 200 B; the read-back is *not*
forwarded (2 extra insns), so it trades want's `b`+`or.` for `stw`+`lwz` and still
misses. Using it for the LOOP select makes the loop a word short (184 B). Store
form for one and register form for the other is the 42.0% body.

**Two other things this round measured:**
* **The `goto`-target block's physical slot is decided by the LABEL ORDER in the
  source** (AGENTS §6be, now with a second confirmation and a +6-point swing):
  `fail:` before `ret:` leaves the return block last (36.0%); `ret:` before
  `fail:` lands the FAIL block at want's exact address and gains 6 points.
  Cheap lever, try it on any `goto`-heavy function before touching codegen.
* **A want-side 5-word select is strong evidence of a SPLIT-FUNCTION origin.**
  The sibling `fn_8022BB14` (0x8022BB14, 188 B) shares the first 16 instructions
  of this function EXACTLY and its own entry diamond has the 5-word shape while
  its loop diamond 12 instructions later has the collapsed 4-word shape — retail
  emitting both forms of the same idiom two instructions apart is only explicable
  by an inline/split boundary. That is the park theory; do not re-grind the
  spelling ladder.

Other levers re-confirmed on this function: `arg0 += 0xAC` param reassignment
gives want's `addi r3,r3,0xac; stw r3,4(r9); lwz r,0xc(r3)` (one `addi`, load
off the SAME register — §6av-215/§6cv); a do-while whose latch tests the
loop-carried value gives a back edge to the loop HEAD (§6af-180's "want's
`[entry-test][preheader][body][latch→body]`"); and the promoted `search_t`
typedefs of `src/fn_8021D358.c` / `fn_8021D7F0.c` / `fn_8021D888.c` /
`fn_8021D758.c` are the byte-proven type oracle for this idiom family (§6dc).

## 6dw — 2026-10-01 single pick: a table access at a >16-bit offset is `addis base`
### + `addi base,-off` + `lwzx/stwx base,index` — and **two different levers are
### needed to reach it**, while `-fno-gcse` is what keeps arg0 homed
### (fn_800A5F38, 29.4% → 70.6% NEAR, 272B, 0 emitted asm)

`fn_800A5F38` (40-entry, 12-byte-stride record array at `arg0+0xB038`) went from
a 29.4 % m2c draft to a 70.6 %-NEAR body whose *entire* prologue, both search
loops and the epilogue are byte-identical. Three findings are reusable.

**1. A named `char *` base is the ONLY way to get the indexed `lwzx/stwx` form,
and assigning that base *inside* the loop is what stops it being hoisted.**
Offsets like `0xB03C` do not fit a 16-bit displacement, so the address is split
(`addis rX,base,1` / `addi rX,rX,-0x4FC4`) and retail stores the constant part
in a REGISTER and the loop index in the load's index field: retail multiplies the loop index by 0xC, builds the 0xB03C-based address with a high-part add and a low-part add of negative 0x4FC4 into r9, and performs an indexed word load. An inline address expression instead folds the base into the sum and yields a multiply plus add plus high-part-add plus displacement load; a named base that is loop-invariant gets hoisted into a callee-saved register and yields only a multiply plus indexed load in two words; and a named base re-assigned inside the loop stays per-iteration and reproduces retail exactly.

So: inline ⇒ GCC folds the base into the sum and you get a displacement load;
a named base ⇒ indexed, but loop-invariant hoisting pulls it into a
callee-saved reg (and the object comes out 2–4 words *short*); a named base
re-assigned at each iteration ⇒ indexed **and** per-iteration, which is what
retail emits. This is §6k-66 / §6bg-4 ("name the base so a dependent load can
pin it") plus the hoist lever, and it is worth trying whenever want shows
`lwzx/stwx` with a split 32-bit offset. Same trick fixed all three store sites
in the tail block simultaneously.

**2. `-fno-gcse` stops CSE from propagating a *partial sum* of a big offset into
the callee-saved home, which rotates the WHOLE function's register map.**
With the named bases in place, plain CSE realised that the `+0x10000` half of
every `0xB0xx` access is loop-invariant AND must survive the loop's `bl`, so it
*rewrote the parameter pseudo itself* to `arg0+0x10000`: the `mr r28,r3` home
copy disappeared, every `addis` came out of `r3` instead of `r28`, and the
result/index/pointer colours all shifted by one — 72.7 % → **25.4 %** with
everything else identical. `-fno-gcse` restores the plain home. Note this is
the *opposite* diagnosis from §6ar-223 (there `-fno-gcse` broke CSE that was
merging two NAMES for one value; here CSE's `convert` step merged a value
*into* the param pseudo). **Diagnostic: a drop of tens of points where only
`mr <reg>,r3` at the top of the function and the base register of every
`addis` change is a CSE-propagation signature — try deleting CSE.**

**3. Two stores to the SAME address in the two arms of an if/else get merged
into one conditional store (the else arm disappears); give each arm its own
POINTER VARIABLE to keep them apart.** Source

```c
if (p) { bA = base + 8; *(s32 *)(bA + idx) = p->f18; }
else   { bB = base + 8; *(s32 *)(bB + idx) = p; }     /* 17.5-63.6 %, else arm gone */
if (p) { bA2 = base + 8; *(s32 *)(bA2 + idx) = p->f18; }
else   { bB2 = base + 8; *(s32 *)(bB2 + idx) = p; }    /* 72.7 %, both arms kept */
```

is *semantically identical* text, but CSE's `record_jump_equiv` only rewrites
`if (c) x=a; else x=b;` into `x = c?a:b` when the two MEMs are
`operand_equal_p`; two distinct pointer pseudos stop that. This is the mirror
image of §6bf-recipe-4 / §6bf "un-share an address web" (there you must SHARE
to match retail; here you must NOT). `-fno-gcse` does NOT help — CSE (not GCSE)
is the pass that merges, and `-fno-cse` does not exist in ProDG cc1 (§6bq).

**Also confirmed:** a 12-byte-stride `mulli + lwzx` needs no §4f `ai` struct
trick — a plain `char *` base plus `+ i*0xC` gives it; and the rotated
`for (; i<=N; p += 0xC, i++) { … break; }` shape puts the latch (both `addi`s)
BEFORE the test with the entry `b` straight to the test, exactly as retail, with
the pointer and the counter ending up in the *other* registers than the m2c
draft gives them (`register char *pp __asm__("r30")` on the walker fixed the
swap: 46.2 % → 64.6 %).

## 6dx — 2026-09-30 single pick: a want dispatch that is a **right-linear `cmpw`/`bne`-over-the-body chain with a BODILESS first `beq` to the epilogue** is an if/`goto done` chain whose first arm assigns the DEFAULT value — not a switch (fn_802198F4, 21.3% → EXACT, 240B, 0 asm, 0 flags)

`fn_802198F4` (a QB script-command getter, `fn_8013FF5C(arg0+0x110,H)` →
`fn_80128E34(...,QB_CHECKSUM,&sp8,1)` → hash→small-int map) came in at 21.31 %
with an **already size-exact** object (244B vs 240B want) and 48 diffs. One
edit made it byte-exact. The recognisable part is the *diagnostic*, so it is
worth writing down before the fix.

**1. The tree shape names the source construct.** Want compares the hash in r9 against the first hash value and branches straight to the epilogue with no value materialisation and no body, then tests the second hash and skips its body when unequal before materialising the value three into r31 and branching to the epilogue, then continues the same right-linear pattern for the third hash leading to the value four, so the whole dispatch is a right-linear chain.

`balance_case_nodes` ALWAYS splits a `switch` near the median of its sorted
case values and emits a `bgt`/`blt` (or `cmplwi` for dense ranges) second
branch — got was exactly that (root = the median of 6, `beq`/`bgt` pairs, every
body out of line at the end). A **right-linear chain whose bodies sit INLINE
between the tests** is what a plain `if (x==A) … else if (x==B) …` with tiny
bodies compiles to, so retail's source is an if/goto chain. §6ak-161 said this
for hash dispatches; this is the *byte-level* tell to confirm it in one
comparison, and it generalises to any multi-value map.

**2. The BODILESS first test is the fingerprint of a case whose body equals the
default — and that case is the one m2c dropped.** A `switch` with 7 values gave
got 6; the 7th (`QB_NUM_2` = 0xF6C5D908, hand-decoded `signext(lis)<<16|ori`)
is the arm `var_r31 = 2`, identical to the pre-initialised default, so GCC
deletes the store and all that survives is `cmpw` + `beq <epilogue>`. So: when
you decode a want dispatch, **count the `cmpw`s and compare with the number of
cases in the draft**; a bodiless head is a real case with a redundant body, and
its value is the default. §6an-9 / §6ab-137 steer the tree with a *dummy* case;
this is the mirror — a *real* case whose body vanishes.

**3. `r3` set once and never re-materialised before the second `bl` is a
CHAINED return, and the missing prototype is what hides it.** Want:
`addi r3,r3,0x110 … bl fn_8013FF5C … bl fn_80128E34`. m2c passed the hash
literal as the second call's arg0, which shifted the whole arg-setup window one
slot (r3/r4 vs r4/r5, `li r6,1` vs `li r5,1`). Writing
`fn_80128E34(fn_8013FF5C(arg0 + 0x110, H), H2, &sp8, 1)` (recipe 23 / §4t /
§6bh) is the whole fix, and the `s32` return types (§6a-1 / M8.31) kill the
`crclr cr1eq` that m2c's undeclared callees produced.

**4. The template to copy was already promoted three functions away.** All three
of `src/fn_80219724.c`, `src/fn_80219840.c` and `src/fn_80219A80.c` are
byte-identical promoted files in the same zone using the *same*
`var_r3`/`var_r31`-accumulator + `goto done` + per-hash-`if` shape, and
`fn_80219A80.c` is a near-twin (default set before the call, three arms). §6dc
says "search by CALLEE SET, not body shape or size" — here even body shape
matched, so `rg fn_8013FF5C src/` was enough to hand over the entire template
including the exact `if`/`goto` spelling. Check `src/` for zone siblings before
grinding a `switch`-shaped dispatch: three of the four files I opened were
already solved this way.

## 6dy — 2026-10-01 single pick: a hand-written field-layout typedef whose
### leading pad is OMITTED shifts every member low by the gap — and the
### signature is "correct length, correct instruction kinds, every displacement
### uniformly N low" (fn_801B0A04, 19.3% → EXACT, 200 B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags)

`fn_801B0A04` (CAT destructor: seven `if (arg0->unkN) callee(arg0->unkN, 3);`
blocks + a flag-conditional `Mem_Free`) was an m2c draft at **19.3 %**. Three
*semantic* edits took it to byte-exact; **no pin, barrier, flag, `_dummy` or asm
was involved, and the twin scanners found nothing** (`twin_scan` 0 hits —
`near_twin_scan`'s best candidate shares only the prologue). Worth recording
because the score was low enough to look like a codegen wall and because one of
the three fixes has a *reusable failure signature*.

* **Every call is a FIELD-PASS, and the loaded field is arg0.** m2c emitted
  `fn_801B01C0(3)` (the constant as the ONLY arg) and `fn_801B05B8(arg0, 3)`
  (the object as arg0) for what is really `callee(arg0->unkN, 3)` at all seven
  sites — verified against want's `lwz r3,off(r31) / cmpwi r3,0 / beq / li r4,3
  / bl`, i.e. the value the guard tests IS the first argument. §6m-43 /
  §6e-32 / recipe 43, third confirmation; the tell here is that *half* the calls
  had the object and *half* had the constant, so a per-call-site read of want's
  arg registers was needed rather than one assumption for the family.
* **Both callees needed real 2-arg `void` prototypes** (audited from the retail
  prologues: `mr r31,r3 / mr r30,r4` and `mr r30,r3 / mr r29,r4`, no value in
  r3 at either `blr`). m2c declared neither, so 4 spurious `crclr cr1eq` were
  emitted **and** the `li r4,3` had nowhere to go — the object's *length* was
  right by luck. §6bf arity audit + §6df's "object longer than want by ~1
  instruction per surplus arg" inverse.
* **NEW — the reusable one. A file-local layout typedef must declare the
  LEADING gap explicitly; omitting it puts the first field at offset 0, and the
  score lands in the 85–90 % band that reads as a scheduling residual.**
  I wrote
  ```c
  typedef struct CAT_t { void *unk0x4; void *unk0x8; ... void *unk0x1C; } CAT_t;
  ```
  — a correct-looking member list, wrong layout. Every one of the seven
  displacements came out exactly **4 low** (`lwz r3,0x10` where want has
  `0x14`, `lwz r3,0x0` where want has `0x4`, …). Adding `char pad0x0[0x4];` as
  the first member: **86.0 % → 100.0 %, one line.**
  *Why it is worth the note:* the object is the **exact right length** and every
  instruction kind is right, all seven loads sit at the right positions in the
  right order, and the only diffs are seven `lwz` displacements — i.e. precisely
  the shape that §6do/§6dm/§6by would file as an allocator or arg-setup
  residual and that a scheduling lever ladder cannot move. **Diagnostic that
  settles it in one look: if EVERY differing word is the same instruction with
  its displacement off by the same constant, it is the struct layout, not
  codegen — subtract the constant from want's offsets and check whether the
  first one is 0.** This is the mirror of §6de ("a padding array is measured in
  ELEMENTS"): there the pad was the wrong *type* and the members landed 4× too
  high, here the pad was *absent* and they land too low. Same rule, one line:
  **in a hand-written field-layout typedef, every gap — leading and interior —
  is an explicit `char pad0xNN[]`, and every padding member is `char`.**
* Bonus confirmation, §6de-adjacent: typing the seven sub-pointers `void *`
  (the corpus-merged `Unk_C8FEE62D` votes them `s32`) is safe and costs nothing
  — the guard stays a `cmpwi` (a *fresh load* NULL test is `cmpwi`, not `or.`;
  brief rule) and the call arg stays in r3, so the field-pass form lands
  `lwz r3,off / cmpwi r3,0` with **no** `mr r3,r0` and with no r3 pin needed.
  M6.89d / §6dc applied without a header edit.

**Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object `.text` =
0xC8 = 200 B = `symbols.txt` `size:0xC8` = header `range=0x801B0A04-0x801B0ACC
size=200B`; only `.text` + `.rela.text` in the object, so **no private
`.rodata`** and no doc-14 promote caveat; **0 emitted inline instructions**
(the only `__asm__` string in the file is the word "asm" inside a comment);
**8/8 intra-function `R_PPC_REL14` addends** (0x2c/0x40/0x54/0x68/0x7c/0x90/
0xa4/0xb4) land on want's seven `beq` targets plus the `arg1 & 1` `beq`, and
**8/8 `R_PPC_REL24` targets** are `fn_801B01C0`×4 / `fn_801B05B8`×3 /
`Mem_Free`, matching want's `bl` destinations (§6bw method); no `extern lbl_`
data symbol in the body, so the masked-100 %-wrong-label hazard cannot apply.

## 6dz — 2026-10-01 single pick: a 2-word residual that is only the REGISTER of a
### load feeding a NULL test means m2c passed the WRONG OBJECT to the callee in the
### guarded block — identify the callee's real argument from its FIELD OFFSETS, not
### its arg registers (fn_80055B9C, 21.9% -> EXACT, 276B, 4 semantic fixes, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

A list-manager destructor went 21.9% -> **100.0%** with **four plain-C semantic

a sub-30 % m2c draft is a semantics problem, and the wins are spread across four

  where want has `lwz r3,off(base)` + `cmpwi r3,0`.** Both words, and the only
  two, after everything else is byte-exact. §6dp-3's answer (hard-pin the tested
  value to `r3`) is a **fallback**, and here it would have been wrong: the value
  *is* the callee's arg0, live across the guarding `beq`, so ngccc legitimately
  leaves it in an argument register instead of a scratch. m2c's source had
  `fn_800577A0(arg0)`; retail has `fn_800577A0(arg0->d0)`. **So before pinning,
  ask what the callee is handed.** Here the answer was decisive: `0x800577A0` is
  `li r0,-1; li r9,0; stw r0,0xc(r3); stw r9,0x10(r3); blr` — a two-field reset —
  and the walker called with `arg0->d0` in the very next block
  (`fn_800577B4`) reads `0x10(r3)` and `0xc(r3)` of **its** r3. Same offsets, same
  object, so the two callees must be handed the same pointer and the caller only
  holds one candidate pointer to it. **Generalised detector, and the one this
  brief is really about: match a callee's memory DISPLACEMENTS against the
  caller's fields, not just its argument registers.** §6bf's arity audit and
  §6di's call-site scan both look at *which registers* a callee consumes; this
  is the complementary question — *which of the caller's objects has fields where
  the callee touches* — and it is what identifies a nested `arg0->field` argument
  that m2c silently replaced with `arg0`. It costs one `disasm.py` of the callee
  and settles a whole class of "1-2 word" residuals that read like register
  colouring.
* **The other three fixes, all the standard field-pass / arity families, all
  confirmed here again:** `fn_8005790C(3)` -> `fn_8005790C(arg0->d0, 3)` and
  `fn_8005D734(arg0)` -> `fn_8005D734(arg0->f1e4)` (loaded field is arg0; the
  tell is a `bl` with **no `mr r3,outer`** before it — recipe 43 / §6e-32 / §72-143);
  three undeclared callees (3 spurious `crclr cr1eq`); and a file-local
  `s16 off; char pad[2]; s32 (*fn)(void*,s32)` vtable pair for the `lha r3,8(r9)`
  + `lwz r0,0xc(r9)` dispatch (§6dc / §6dh — the corpus-merged `CStruct` types
  +8 as `s32`).
* **Loop shape: m2c's test-first `loop_N:` while loop vs retail's bottom-test
  rotated loop** (entry `b <test>`, body physically ABOVE the test, back edge
  `bne <body>`) is fixed by the raw-goto form `goto test; body: ...; test:
  node = f(); if (node) goto body;` — the `f()` call then lives in the condition,
  which is why there is no separate init call and why `node` is never read
  unassigned. This is §6ag-1 / §6dm-2 / §6an-1 (raw gotos carry no loop notes, so
  rotation cannot touch them), reconfirmed.
* **A file-local `Obj_t` for the caller's own type** made `d0`/`n27c`/`n280` real
  pointers, so no `*(void **)` casts were needed and every offset is proven by the
  loads it feeds. When you replace the merged `Unk_*` class, remember to drop the
  now-unused `#include "structs.h"` (§6dn).

## 6dz2 — 2026-10-01 single pick: a **repeated FUNCTION-SYMBOL argument must be
### written out at every call site** — hoisting it into a local folds the whole
### address into ONE web, costs an instruction and collapses the match; and the
### HI16 CSE of that repetition is what buys the extra callee-saved register and
### the +8 frame (fn_80138E24, 19.6% → EXACT, 204B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags)

`fn_80138E24` (204 B) called `fn_80139510(self, id, handler, a, b, flags)` four
times, passing the same handler `fn_8013A9D0` at ids 5 and 6. The whole fix was
semantic; the two transferable points are the *negative* and the *frame*.

* **Measured negative — do NOT "tidy" a repeated symbol argument into a local.**
  `s32 h = (s32)fn_8013A9D0;` then two calls passing `h` instead of writing
  `(s32)fn_8013A9D0` twice: **100.0 % → 15.4 %, 204 B → 208 B** (one word too
  long). With one C name, local_cse unifies the two `lis`/`addi` pairs into a
  single address web that spans the call; with the symbol written twice, each
  call site keeps its own `lis r5,+hi` / `addi r5,r5,lo`. **This is the mirror of
  §6bt's "a named constant used on both sides of a loop is ONE reload web,
  retail may need TWO"** — there the fix is to *name* the value, here the fix is
  to *un-name* it. Rule: for a **symbol address** (function pointer or data
  label) used at more than one call site, write the reference at each site.
  For a **value** constant, name it. Same shape, opposite lever; check the want:
  two `lis`/`addi` pairs vs one.

* **The HI16 CSE of a genuinely repeated symbol is what grows the frame.** Want's
  prologue is `stwu -0x18; mflr; stmw r29,0xc(r1); stw r0,0x1c(r1)` — 2 saved
  GPRs and 8 bytes more frame than the 1-saved-register version — while a *sibling*
  with three DIFFERENT handler symbols in the same page is
  `stwu -0x10 / stmw r30` (promoted `src/fn_80138748.c`). Mechanism: the two
  identical `HI16(fn_8013A9D0)` relocs are the *same* RTL, so `cse_basic_block`
  merges them and the shared page value (live across a `bl`) gets a callee-saved
  home (r29); the three *different* symbols of the sibling are distinct relocs,
  so `reload` rematerialises each in a scratch r5. From §6db's closed form,
  `8 + 0 + (4·2+4) = 20`, rounded up to the ABI's 8-byte alignment = 0x18. So
  **a "+8 frame, +1 saved register" residual with no stack accesses is often
  just a duplicated symbol argument, not a missing local or a dead
  `volatile double _dummy`.** Re-read want for two `lis` of the *same* page
  before adding padding.

* **The brief's hidden-arg0-passthrough rule is per-callee, and here passing the
  arg is a no-op.** `fn_8013AB54` provably reads r3 (`mr r31,r3`), and the
  script-zone rule says the `fn_80128xxx`/`fn_8013xxxx` callees are 4-arg with a
  hidden arg0 m2c drops — but the promoted twin calls it as `fn_8013AB54(void)`
  and so does this body: r3 already holds `arg0` at the `bl` (it was only
  `mr r30,r3`'d, not clobbered), so `fn_8013AB54(arg0)` with a typed prototype
  scores **100.0 % too**. Both spellings are safe here; the point is to
  *measure* the passthrough rather than assume it, since the promoted twin's
  declaration is the byte-proven choice.

* Method note: the whole body came from **two promoted siblings found with one
  `rg` each**, no scanner. `rg -l "fn_80139510" src/` returned 8 files, and
  `src/fn_80138748.c` (180 B, not a callee, *not* size-matched) is the same
  idiom with the same `(s32)fn_...` handler spelling, the same
  `fn_8013AB54(void)`, the same rotate-LEFT store order and the same
  early-return tail. `twin_scan`/`near_twin_scan` would have missed it — the
  bodies differ by an entire call. §6dc/§6dr's "search by callee set" rule, with
  a new corollary: **do not filter the search to callees, and do not filter it by
  size.**

**Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object `.text` =
0xCC = 204 B = `symbols.txt` `size:0xCC` = header
`range=0x80138E24-0x80138EF0 size=204B`; only `.text` + `.rela.text` in the
object, so **no private `.rodata`** and no doc-14 promote caveat; **0 emitted
inline instructions**; all **7** intra-function branch relocations verified with
the §6bw method — 1 `R_PPC_REL14` (`beq` → 0x80138ed8), 1 local `R_PPC_REL24`
(`b` → `.text+0xb8` = 0x80138edc) and 5 `R_PPC_REL24` calls to
`fn_8013AB54` / `fn_80139510`×4; the three handler addresses were hand-decoded
from want's `lis -0x7fec` + `addi` pairs (0x8013A9C0, 0x8013A9D0, 0x8013A7D4)
and all three are real `fn_*` symbols in `config/G2TE52/symbols.txt`, so the

## 6cd — 2026-10-01 single pick: `abs()` must be spelled as the **builtin**, never
### hand-expanded — the expansion colours the result into the SUBTRAHEND's register
### and costs 47 %; and a merged `Unk_*` class that is **missing** an offset forces
### m2c's `*(s32 *)` fallback, so a byte field becomes a WORD read/write
### (fn_8009D6FC, 15.2% → EXACT, 316B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

A frameless 79-insn leaf: six copies of the same clamp idiom
(`if (abs(x - 0x80) <= 0x32) x = 0x80;` on bytes at +0x1..+0x4 and +0x13..+0x16).
Zero calls, zero FPRs, zero opcode-4 words, and the compiled object was already
**size-exact 316 B** at the inherited 15.2 % — so every diff was semantic.

* **The manual `t>>31; (m^t)-m` expansion and the `abs()` builtin are NOT
  interchangeable, even though they emit the same `srawi/xor/subf` opcodes.**
  Want materialises the abs result in a register of its OWN (`r9`, constant across
  all six sites) with the sign in `r6`/`r11` *alternating* per site; the three
  hand-written spellings (2 temps `t`/`m`, 3 temps `t`/`m`/`a`, and the "reassign the
  sign temp" variant) all fold the result back into the *subtrahend's* register
  (`xor r0,m,r0; subf r0,m,r0`) and use a single `r7` for every sign. Only the
  builtin picks r9 + the r6/r11 alternation. 48.10 % → 94.94 %.
  This is the integer counterpart of §6bh's `fabs()` note (there the spelling
  changed double-promotion, here it changes register COLOUR), and it is
  *counter-intuitive enough to be worth its own rule*: **when want shows the abs /
  negation result in a different register than its operand, write the library
  function — do not help the compiler with temporaries.** Measured: 3 spellings,
  all 48.10 %.
* **A merged `Unk_*` class with no member at the offset is as wrong as one with the
  wrong type — it makes m2c fall back to `*(s32 *)((char *)base + off)`, so a byte
  field becomes a WORD read and a WORD write.** Here `Unk_549E1971` was voted over
  the whole corpus with fields at 0x2/0x3/0x4/0x14/0x15/0x16 only; the two byte
  accesses at **0x01 and 0x13** had no member, so m2c used raw `s32` derefs, and
  the cost was a phantom `lbz 4(r3)` + `clrlwi` for the 4-byte read of byte 1 plus
  two `stw` where want has `stb`. 15.2 % → 48.1 % from ONE file-local typedef with
  `u8` members at 0x01..0x04 and 0x13..0x16. M6.89d / brief rule 5, with the
  "member absent" case called out because the symptom (a word load in a byte table)
  does not look like a struct-type problem at all.
* **Confirm the 2-store rotation *per run*, not per function** (recipe 24/64/159
  refinement): the top 4-store run (`0x14/0x15/0x16/0x13`) is emitted in plain
  SOURCE order and is already correct, while the two 2-store tail runs rotate
  (source `f_13; f_14` → `stb 0x14; stb 0x13`). Both are byte stores of the same
  constant in the same block-class, so the "per store class" rule alone does not
  predict the 2-runs. 94.94 % → 100.00 % on that one edit.

**Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object `.text` = 0x13C =
316 B = `symbols.txt` `size:0x13C` = header `range=0x8009D6FC-0x8009D838 size=316B`;
only `.text` + `.rela.text` in the object, so **no private `.rodata`** and no
doc-14 promote caveat; **0 emitted inline instructions** (the body contains no
`__asm__` and no `.long`); the 6 `R_PPC_REL14` addends (0x44/0x68/0x8c/0xb0/0xf4/
0xf4 → 0x8009D740/0x8009D764/0x8009D788/0x8009D7AC/0x8009D7F0/0x8009D7F0) match
want's six `bgt` targets exactly under the §6bw method, and want's two `bgtlr`s
