  independent confirmation, and here it did the whole data half). Two *promoted,
  byte-identical* siblings sit either side of the address: `src/fn_80032610.c`
  (the immediately preceding function — same node array, same
  `vt->unk0xC(node + vt->unk0x8, 3)` vcall) and `src/fn_80032588.c` (same
  `off + base` offset-first `add` shift idiom). One `rg` handed over the exact vcall
  spelling, the `(s16 off; char pad[2]; fnptr)` vtable pair (**the merged
  `Unk_C8FEE62D` types +0x8 as `s32`, so the m2c form gives `addi` where retail has
  `lha`** — the §6dc/§6dy "promoted neighbours are the type oracle" rule), and the
  `char pad[0x40]; void *unk0x40[6]; s32 unk0x58;` object layout that the
  `Unk_C7387A53` mega-merge happens to get right here. `78.57%` was reached with
  that alone; the ladder was 78.57 → 87.50 (vtable offsets / `arg1 == *w` operand
  order / latch store-run order, recipe 24/64) → **91.07%** (the `zero` moved out
  of its declaration initialiser into a statement *inside* the `if (i < count)`
  guard, so `li r26,0` lands in the loop preheader instead of the entry block).

* **NEW DIAGNOSTIC — "a loop-invariant hoisted COMPARE is in the wrong slot of the
  preheader" is a compile-origin question, not a scheduling one.**
  `loop.c:hoist_insn_out_of_loop` appends a hoisted invariant to the preheader
  *in loop order*, so its LUID comes from the **loop body**, and
  `reorder_basic_block` (§6bg-8: priority = number of users, then LUID) therefore
  **always sorts a hoisted compare LAST** among the preheader's own statements.
  Here retail has `cmpwi cr7, r11, 0` in **slot 2** (right after the 2-user
  `addi` base address) while every C spelling produced slot 5, and the residual
  was exactly that 5-word window. Retail's slot 2 means the compare was **born in
  the preheader region** — i.e. a source-level test lived there and its branch was
  later *jump-threaded / split* into the loop head, leaving the shared compare
  behind. **Positive control that proves the mechanism** (worth re-using): give
  the source a duplicated loop arm (a test above the loop) and the compare
  **does** move to slot 2 — but the loop is then emitted twice and the function
  collapses (18.84%). So the shape still to be hunted is one that duplicates the
  **branch** and not the loop (`goto` into a shared loop, a `switch`/`&&`
  short-circuit that splits the loop-head block). Corollary that also falls out:
  a hoisted invariant with **one** user can never sort before the preheader's own
  statements — only raising its user count to 2 lifts it into the `addi`'s
  priority bucket, and every 2-branch spelling measured either folded the second
  arm away (91.07%) or emitted extra code (83.93%).

* **Two webs holding the same value at the preheader: retail's
  `addi X` + `mr Y,X` vs got's `addi Y` + `mr X,Y` is a coalesce-DIRECTION
  tie-break, and the register assignment is often already identical.** Here
  `base` and the walking cursor are the same value, and *every* value got the
  right register (zero=r26, base=r27, off=r28, i=r29, arg0=r30, cursor=r31 —
  exactly retail); only which name the `addi` fed differed. 20+ spellings (both
  assignment orders, `char *`/`s32 *` base, the `arr[i]` index form, 4
  declaration orders, a `__asm__("" : "+r"(bs))` split-web barrier per §6s-1)
  all choose the cursor. A hard `register … __asm__("r27")` pin on the base **does**
  move the `addi` onto it — and then the shift loop coalesces its walker onto that
  register and `j` onto r11, costing 8 words (82.14%); the split-web barrier
  moves the `addi` but swaps `base`/`off` in the callee-saved pool (89.29%). Note
  that pins on `j`/`src` were **silently dropped** by cc1 here, consistent with
  §6cw/§7a-137 (a pin needs a single def pseudo). **The sibling
  `fn_80032588` (promoted, byte-identical) uses the OPPOSITE convention**
  (`addi r11` = cursor, `mr r7,r11` = base) and its promoted source needed a hard
  `register s32 wp __asm__("r11")` pin to get it — so read the neighbour before
  assuming your function wants the other direction.

* **A 19-flag sweep on the residual was ALL no-ops** (`-fno-gcse`,
  `-fno-schedule-insns2`, `-fno-sched-spec`, `-fno-sched-interblock`,
  `-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop`, `-fno-strength-reduce`, `-fno-thread-jumps`, `-O3`
  all 91.07%; `-fno-schedule-insns` 14.55%, `-Os` 61.82%), which is itself the
  confirmation that the blocker is a compare's LUID, not scheduling.

**Audit of the 91.07% body (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object has only
`.text` (0xE0 = 224 B = `symbols.txt size:0xE0` = the header marker) and
`.rela.text` — no `.rodata`, so no doc-14 promote caveat; **0 emitted inline
instructions**; all **7** branch relocations verified with the §6bw method (6 ×
`R_PPC_REL14` +0xCC/+0xB4/+0x68/+0xA4/+0x84/+0x3C and the local `b`'s
`R_PPC_REL24` +0xCC — every one equals retail's decoded branch target, so the
residual is a pure 5-word permutation with **no** hidden control-flow difference);
no `ADDR16_HA/LO` entries at all (no extern data symbols), so hazard 277 cannot
apply.

## 6eo — 2026-10-01 single pick: **a narrow-typed loop counter (`s16`/`u16`) is a TRAP even when its stores need the truncation** — it forces a 4-word `addi`/`extsh`/`cmpwi`/`bne` latch instead of retail's fused `addic. r,r,-1; bne` AND makes the object the wrong LENGTH; plus `cc1 -dr` proves `reload` preserves source order for a store run (fn_80018098, 19.4% → 78.6% NEAR, size-exact 224 B, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

`fn_80018098` is a 3-iteration `{ fn_8001CA24(); fn_8001FCF4(); VIWaitForRetrace(); }`
countdown followed by ten stores to ten distinct `.bss`/`.data` globals. m2c
declared the counter `s16` **because retail stores it narrow** (`sth`, three
`stb`, one `stw`). That single wrong type cost 24 points and 8 bytes of object.

* **THE NEW FINDING — "the stores need the truncation, so type the counter
  narrow" is exactly backwards.** With `s16 var_r31;` (or `unsigned short`),
  `var_r31 -= 1; } while (var_r31 != 0);` compiles to
  `addi r0,r31,-1; extsh r31,r0; cmpwi r31,0; bne` — **4 words** — because the
  SImode subtract needs a temp and the SImode→HI truncation is a separate
  `extsh`. With `s32 var_r31;` the same statement gives retail's
  `addic. r31,r31,-1; bne` (**2 words**): the wide type lets cc1 use the 16-bit
  `addic.` form (whose CR0 comes from the 16-bit result) and fuse the test into
  the branch, while the store sites truncate for free because `sth`/`stb` just
  read the low half. 29.3% → **53.6% and the object goes 232 B → 224 B = exactly
  `symbols.txt size:0xE0`.** All of `s16`, `u16`, `while (--v != 0)`,
  `while (v-- != 0)` and `while (0 != v--)` on an s16 counter score an identical
  29.3%, so this is the TYPE, not the latch spelling. This is distinct from
  §6cv / §6p-104 (post-decrement operand order on a *wide* counter) and from
  §6dy (a struct layout shifting members): **the tell is that the object is a
  whole number of words too long AND the diff is 4 words of `addi`/`extsh`/
  `cmpwi`/`bne` where want has `addic.`/`bne`.** Rule: derive a local's width
  from the arithmetic, not from its stores; put the narrowing in the cast at
  each store (`*(s16 *)&g = v;`) and leave the variable wide.

* **The masked store compare keeps the BASE register, so a store-order residual
  and a page-register residual are the SAME diff.** `gen_leaves.compile_fn`
  masks `R_PPC_ADDR16_HA/LO` with `0xFFFF0000`; on a D-form that masks the
  **displacement** (bits 16-31) and keeps opcode + `rS` + **`rA`**. So
  `stw r4,-0x1838(r7)` vs `stw r4,0(r27)` is a *diff*, even though both are
  "the same store to the same address". Consequence when hunting a store-run
  order: fixing the order fixes the base registers for free (a store's base IS
  its `lis` register), and a diff list full of `stX rN, off(rM)` with the same
  `rN` but different `rM` is an ordering symptom, not an allocation one. Read
  `objdump -dr` and map `ADDR16_HA/LO` to symbols to get the true store order —
  the printed disassembly cannot show it (every displacement masks to 0).

* **`cc1 -dr` confirms `reload` PRESERVES source order for a store run, so a
  store-order residual is scheduler-side — and it is genuinely chaotic, not a
  permutation you can invert.** Post-reload RTL had the ten stores in exact
  source order while the final object had them rotated. Two source orders
  produced the *same* position permutation `[1,4,5,9,3,6,7,8,0,2]`; a third
  produced `[4,5,8,9,3,6,7,0,1,2]`, so inverting the measured permutation is
  only locally valid (it took this function 60.7% → 78.6%, but the next
  derivation off the same assumption lost ground). **Flag sweep on that
  residual is pure negative**: `-fno-sched-spec`, `-fno-sched-interblock`,
  `-fno-gcse`, `-fno-thread-jumps`, `-fno-expensive-optimizations` all neutral;
  `-fno-schedule-insns2` 62.5%, `-fno-schedule-insns` 42.9%,
  `-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop` 21.4%. Do NOT burn a round on flags here — go
  straight to recipe 280's plateau walk on the store order (accept sideways
  moves). Also neutral, i.e. the emitted order is insensitive to them: the
  `&`-cast vs typed-direct store spelling, a chained byte trio
  (`a=b=c=(s8)n`), dedicated `s16`/`s8` staging temps, and declaration order.
  And a struct view of a run of adjacent same-width globals is **ruled out by
  the want itself**: retail has 11 separate `lis` page reloads, so it wrote
  every global by name, not through one base pointer.

* **A 3rd instance of the combination trap, in a place it is easy to fall into:
  a lever measured on an intermediate body can be a large LOSS on the final
  one.** Swapping the two out-param loads (`13D0` before `13CC`) was worth
  +1.8 points on the 58.9% body and **−7.1** on the 78.6% body (it moves the
  second value from `r5` to `r7`/`r4`, 4 words). I transcribed the "winning"
  order into the final file and lost 7 points before noticing. **Re-measure
  every lever on the body you are actually keeping** — the fix order itself
  changes which edits are compatible.

* **Small but repeatable wins in the same body, all confirmed:** m2c rendered
  a direct call to a `scope:global` SDK function as an **indirect call through a
  hard-coded literal** `((void (*)(void))0x80260B70)()` → call the SDK name
  directly (§6eg, 2nd instance); a 12-byte callee whose body reads only `r3`
  (`li r0,5; sth r0,0x3c(r3); blr`) is **1-arg**, so m2c's 8-arg call *and* its
  0-arg twin were both wrong and both needed fixing (§6bf arity audit); and
  when want's window is `[call][load a][save][load b]`, the source must put the
  call **before** both loads — with the first load first, ngccc hoists it above
  the call (§6eb's three-way statement-position rule, new instance).

## 6ep — 2026-10-01 single pick: **want has ONE `blrl` reached by two
### `mtlr`-terminated arms ⇒ write TWO `return` statements** (duplication
### *limits* crossjumping to the right granularity), and `cc1 -dr` can prove a
### block-ORDER residual is flow.c's, not the scheduler's
### (fn_801A2E88, 16.7% → 80.5% NEAR size-exact 164 B, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

* **One indirect call in the source, but two `mtlr`s in want, means two call
  SITES in C — and that is the *only* way to keep the tails separate.** The
  signature is `mtlr <A>; b <shared> ... mtlr <B>; <shared>: blrl`, i.e. two
  `mtlr`s with **different registers** feeding **one** `blrl`. That combination
  is unreachable from a single shared `fp`/`base` call site: the `mtlr` would be
  emitted once in the merge block. Conversely, with the natural single call site
  (`if (a) {...fp1 = ..; base1 = ..} else {...fp2 = ..; base2 = ..}
  return fp(base)`) GCC's crossjumping **over-merges**: the two arms' whole
  field-load tails become identical RTL (both objects land in r3), so the tails
  collapse to ONE copy and the object comes out 24 B short. Writing the two
  arms as two separate `return vt->fn(obj + vt->off);` statements leaves the
  per-arm tails differing (arm 1's object is in r11 — the dead loop counter's
  register, recycled — vs r3 in arm 2), so crossjumping merges **only** the
  `blrl` + epilogue, which is exactly want. 35 B → 164 B (exact), 42.9% → 80.5%.
  **This is the mirror of §6u-1 / §70-134:** those duplicate a call *to enable* a
  merge; here duplication *limits* the merge to `blrl`. Read the want's `mtlr`
  operands first — two different registers ⇒ two call sites, one `blrl` ⇒ they
  merged.
* **A merged `return 0` block's POSITION is a flow.c `reorder_blocks` decision,
  and `cc1 -dr` proves it.** The post-reload RTL here was *already* in want's
  order — the count-test block's conditional `jump_insn` had
  `(if_then_else (ne …) (label_ref <arg1-test>) (pc))` with the `li r3,0` block
  as its **fall-through** — yet the final code emitted `beq` forward to that
  block instead. So the inversion happens in `reorder_blocks` /
  `can_fall_through`, driven by the block's successor **edge-list order**, and
  nothing in C or in cc1 reaches it: 22 flags (`-fno-schedule-insns{,2}`,
  `-fno-sched-spec`, `-fno-sched-interblock`, `-fno-gcse`, `-fno-thread-jumps`,
  `-fno-expensive-optimizations`, `-fno-cse`, `-foptimize-register-move`,
  `-fconserve-space`, `-fbranch-probabilities`, …) all produced a
  **byte-identical** object, and ProDG cc1 has no `-fcrossjumping` /
  `-freorder-blocks` / block-layout option at all (check with `cc1 --help`).
  The same shape resisted every source form: `goto ret0` + a bottom label
  (which also breaks the `blrl` crossjump), `if (c != 0) {rest} return 0;`,
  a single exit with a return **variable**, a named `zero`, flipped operand
  order, `!c`, `return (s32)0`, and `__asm__ volatile("")` /
  `"" ::: "memory"` / `"+r"` barriers at all four positions around the two
  guards (no-ops at best, +2 words at worst). **Diagnostic to reuse: when a NEAR
  is "one shared block is in the wrong place", run `cc1 -dr` and check whether
  the post-reload RTL already has want's block LAYOUT. If it does, the blocker is
  flow.c, and the honest park note is a block-order wall, not "scheduling".**
  (§6bz/§6ek use `-dr` to clear the front end and point at `sched2`; this is the
  next step up — the RTL is right and `sched2` is right too.)
* **The two 2-arg signatures came free from the promoted sibling callee.**
  m2c emitted `fn_801A275C()` and `fn_801A26E0(0)`; both read r3 **and** r4
  (`mr r29,r3 / mr r28,r4` and `mr r31,r3 / mr r30,r4`). Promoted
  `src/fn_801A275C.c` declares both, so one `rg` settled the arity of *both*
  call sites without a probe. §6dc's "promoted neighbours are the type oracle"
  extends to **arity** — read the callee's promoted source before writing a
  prototype.
* **Third instance of the m2c "declares the function 0/1-arg when the retagged
  body already exists" trap:** the draft's `((Unk_C8FEE62D *)o)->unk0x14 ->
  ->unk0x38 / ->unk0x3C` came from the corpus-merged class, which types the
  vtable slot `s32` and the method-offset slot `s32`. Retail reads the offset
  with `lha`. The fix is a file-local `typedef struct { char pad[0x38]; s16 off;
  s32 (*fn)(void *); }` — no header edit, no casts (§6dc/§6dh/§6dy).
* **A rotated goto state machine reproduced retail's list walk in one edit**
  (`goto chk; body: walker = walker->next; count++; chk: if (f4 == -1) walker =
  0; if (walker) goto body;`), giving want's `b <test>` / body-below-test /
  backward-back-edge layout. Every `while`/`for`/`do-while` spelling rotates the
  test to the top instead (§6ag-1 / §6am-1 / §6dm-2).

## 6ep2 — 2026-10-01 single pick: **a byte-field's `u8` vs `s8` LVALUE decides the
### SIGN of the `li`/`addi` immediate**, and **a comma expression is the only lever
### that kills a 2-store transposition** — every statement order, flag, barrier,
### `volatile` cast and pin is a byte-identical no-op (fn_80043A34, 17.8% → EXACT,
### 156 B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

A small QB-`CStruct`-style constructor (13 field stores, 2 rodata f32 constants, a
`base`-pointer byte group, 2 calls). The m2c body was wrong in seven independent
ways and every one was semantic; the whole ladder is in the draft header. Four
findings generalise beyond it.

1. **The lvalue's signedness — not its width — picks the immediate's SIGN.** Retail
   materialises the constant as `addi r11,0,0xFF80` (`li r11,-0x80`) and stores it with
   `stb`, i.e. the source's `-0x80` survived as a **signed 16-bit** constant. Writing
   the field as `u8` makes GCC truncate to 128 first and emit `addi r11,0,0x80`; a
   **one-word** diff, and it looks exactly like a scheduling/encoding artifact. 71.8%
   → 94.9% for the whole family once fixed. This is the immediate-sign facet of the
   "declare the real type" knob (recipe 34, §6cc, §6ef's `char`-vs-`u8` `extsb`):
   **ask what register value retail's `stb`/`stw` source must hold, then declare the
   lvalue so that value is what survives the truncation.**

2. **Which FPR a rodata float gets is decided by WHICH STORE EMITS FIRST**, so the
   store order and the FPR assignment are one decision, not two. The value written by
   the first-emitted `stfs` of the run lands in `f0`; the next gets `f13` — and it
   held identically across every declaration-order, load-statement-order and
   `fr0`/`fr13`-pin variation tried (all 13 diffs, pins made it *worse* at 61.5%).
   So on a `lfs`/`stfs` residual: **read the FPR off the store order first, then fix
   the order** — do not start by permuting the constants. Corollary: the per-store
   **CLASS** rotation is a *right*-rotate by one on emit (§6an-198 / §6cd), so the
   source order is the emitted order rotated LEFT per class — 3 f32 stores and 6 s32
   stores rotate independently, and getting both class orders right took 71.8% →
   94.9%.

3. **When one store of a run is one slot off and NOTHING moves it, nest the other
   store in its RHS as a comma expression.** The residual was
   `[stw r0,0x1e0][stw r0,0x190][stfs f0,0x1b4]` vs got
   `[stw r0,0x1e0][stfs f0,0x1b4][stw r0,0x190]` — 2 of 39 words. Byte-identical
   no-ops: 4 source interleavings of the two statements (and of the whole run), 15
   sched/GCSE/`-O` flags, `volatile s32` / `volatile f32` casts on either lvalue,
   `"+r"` and `"+f"` barriers, a named `f32 *` for the lvalue, the inline
   `(f32 *)((char *)arg0 + 0x1B4)` form, and swapping the constants' load order. The
   one that worked, emitting **no extra instruction**:
   ```c
   arg0->unk1b4 = (arg0->unk190 = z, f0);      /* the 0x190 store moved INTO the RHS */
   ```
   This is §6as-2 / §7c-166 (a run's rotation *survives* comma sequence points) run
   in the **opposite** direction: here the sequence point is what *removes* the
   rotation, because the nested store is no longer an independent insn in the same
   run. Practical rule: **before parking a 1–2 word store transposition, try both
   nest directions** (`a = (b = v, w);` and `b = (a = w, v);`) — they are free, they
   emit nothing, and the "which one moved" answer is itself diagnostic (one direction
   gave 84.6%, the other 100%).

4. **The trailing call's POSITION is a frame-size lever, not just a scheduling one.**
   Two rodata `f32` locals that are dead before a call need no FPR save; live across
   it, ngccc homed them in **callee-saved f30/f31**, adding two `stfd`/`lfd` and
   growing the frame from `stwu -0x10` to `stwu -0x28` — 4.55% → 17.5% on the rest of
   the body, with the float *values* already correct. Diagnose it the §6cs-1 way: if
   GOT's frame is a round `0x10`+ bigger and carries `stfd` pairs that want does not
   have, check whether the floats are live across a call before touching a `_dummy`
   (§4c / M4.92) — the fix is to move the call, and no number of `volatile double`s
   will help.

## 6eq — 2026-10-01 single pick: a loop's preheader address-birth ORDER is fixed by pseudo number, so a bare `&local` in a call argument can NEVER sort before an explicit preheader statement — and every way of forcing it costs an extra instruction (fn_801F3A1C, 21.8% → **96.1% NEAR**, 304B size-exact, 0 asm, 0 pins, 0 flags)

A 304B QB array-reader went 21.8% → 96.1% (74/77 words byte-identical) on **semantics
alone** — five m2c bugs and nothing else (§6bf's arity audit, recipe 23/§4t's chain,
plus a *new* rendering artefact below). The parked 3 words are a well-characterised
preheader-order wall worth not re-grinding:

* **A bare `&spC` written as a call argument creates its `addressof` pseudo INSIDE the
  loop body, so it can only ever be hoisted to the preheader *after* the preheader's own
  statements** (`cc1 -dr` shows the preheader containing only the statements the source
  puts there; the addressof and any loop-invariant constant are appended by the loop
  optimizer). So the emit order is "source preheader statements, then the hoisted ones",
  regardless of where in the *body* the address is first used. Measured on fn_801F3A1C:
  moving the `var_r31` init to the body's first statement, to just before its first use,
  and to the body's last statement all produced the SAME order
  (`[const-lis][zero][addi var_r31][addi &spC][ori]`); only the last one (80.3%) broke the
  loop because the increment was then dead.
* **Making the out-param address a preheader statement DOES flip the order, but a NAMED
  pointer always costs one extra instruction.** `s32 *spCp = &spC;` in the preheader
  emits the right `addi` first, yet adds `mr r24,r29`: the VAR needs a callee-saved home
  (its live range spans the calls) and cc1 will not coalesce a VAR with its `addressof`,
  so the address is born in a scratch and copied. **Byte-identical, +1 insn, 27%** — for
  `s32`/pointer/register-var forms, with the pin (`register s32 spCp __asm__("r29")` —
  the pin does NOT bind) and with the assignment before or after the other preheader
  statement. The same +1 `mr` appears with a zero-code `__asm__("" : : "r"(&spC))` input
  barrier in the preheader.
* **The one-insn volatile-asm anchor puts `&spC` in the right slot but destroys the
  loop-invariant CONSTANT beside it.** `__asm__ volatile("addi %0,1,0xc" : "=r"(p))` with
  a pinned output emits exactly the wanted `addi` (so the pin binds) — and the division
  magic's hoisting then changes shape and the whole body diverges. To use this route the
  constant would have to be produced by asm too (2 of 77 insns = 2.6%, within budget) —
  untried because the natural `x / 180` already matches byte-exact and hand-building
  `mulhw/add/srawi7/subf` in C risks the 74 matching words.
* **16 flags are inert on this residual** (`-fno-sched-spec`, `-fno-sched-interblock`,
  `-fno-gcse`, `-fno-expensive-optimizations`, `-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop`,
  `-fno-thread-jumps`, `-O3`, `-fno-caller-saves` all 96.05%; `-fno-schedule-insns2`
  82.9%, `-fno-schedule-insns` 71.1%, `-Os` 38.2%, `-O1` 47.4%), and **all 3 R_PPC_REL14
  addends already resolve to want's exact branch targets**, so it is a pure permutation
  with no hidden control-flow difference. Declaration-order permutations
  (§76-184/§6ec), preheader decl-initialisers, `volatile` on the zero local, and a local
  `count` in the guard are all inert or negative.
  **Diagnostic: "3 differing words, all in the loop PREHEADER, all `addi`/constant births,
  frame + save span + register assignment already correct" ⇒ do NOT run a flag ladder or
  a statement-order ladder; check whether the two addresses can be born in the order want
  has at all, i.e. whether a named-pointer form costs an extra insn.**
* **New m2c rendering artefact worth grepping for: a QB hash constant passed as a
  POINTER.** m2c renders `GetInteger(entry, QB_SPIN, &sp, 0)` as
  `GetInteger(entry, (s32 *)QB_SPIN, &sp, 0)` — a cast to `s32 *` on a value that want
  materialises in `r4` with `lis`+`ori`. The tell is a `(s32 *)QB_…` or `(void *)QB_…`
  in a call's argument list; §6ae-174 says hash *values* stay bare literals, and this is
  the same rule seen from the m2c side. Together with the hidden-arg0 chain and 4
  undeclared callees it was 4 of the 5 semantic wins here.
* Also confirmed, cheap: typing a pointer out-param honestly (`CStruct *sp8` +
  `(s32 *)&sp8` at the `GetArray` call, instead of `s32 sp8` + a cast) is
  **byte-identical** and removes 4 "makes pointer from integer" warnings — the promoted
  siblings in this zone (`src/fn_801F3910.c`, `src/fn_801F366C.c`) use the honest form.

## 6er — 2026-10-01 single pick (PS zone, 0x801CE918): **two proven address-CSE walls
### (budget them, do not grind them)**, plus a pointer hard-pin that beats a second
### derived-pointer pin (12.7% → 77.2% size-exact, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags)

     assigned to a named pointer var* binds fine (second confirmation of §6df's

  **Diagnostic in one look: two `addi rX,r1,K` with the same `rX` base and the
  same `K` for ONE C object ⇒ wall, not structure.**

* **WALL 2 — `local_alloc`'s address split folds `p` and `p+const` into one
  web.** Want's 64-byte block copy stores through TWO bases: six

  `__ps_t *`; indices `[0],[1]` vs `[4],[5]` off `dst+4`; delayed birth after
  the first four stores; birth before the whole group; nested block scope;
  comma-expression; `s32` alias; hard `register __ps_t *__asm__("r11")`; hard
  `register s32 __asm__("r11")`; `__ps_t * volatile`; `volatile`-qualified

  opaque `__asm__("addi %0,%1,0x20" : "=r"(d) : "r"(arg0))` birth **does** force

  the web is folded away *before* allocation, so there is no pseudo to bind —
  the same reason §6cw/§7a-137 pins are ignored on derived webs.

* **The two walls are ±1 word each and must be solved TOGETHER.** Fixing only
  one leaves the object at the wrong length (320 B or 312 B), and the
  one-word index shift turns 4 more otherwise-correct words into DIFFs. That
  is why the masked score looks like "18 unrelated register diffs" when it is
  really **two facts**. **When a NEAR's residual is one extra/one missing word
  in two unrelated places, look for a single cause: want has one more ADDRESS
  WEB than you do.** (Diagnosis order: dump got's per-word stream, find the
  first index where `got[i] == want[i+1]` — the shift is k words and every
  diff downstream of it is noise, §6cs-1.)

  `-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop` / `-fno-expensive-optimizations` /
  `-fno-thread-jumps` / `-fno-strength-reduce` / `-fno-branch-count-reg` /
  `-O3` / `-Os` all 77.2%; `-fno-schedule-insns2` 74.7%; `-fno-schedule-insns`

  `extern const f32` / `extern char[]`+`*(f32 *)` for the `.rodata2` float
  (§6bt2/§6ek) and a §7d-4 permuted-parameter cast for the 3-arg call are all
  77.2% no-ops. Per §6bx the flag sweep was re-run **on the fixed body**, not

* **PROBE TEMPLATE worth keeping (30 s, no full-body compile):** a standalone
  `<T> h(T x)` one-function probe compiled with
  `build/tools/wibo build/compilers/ProDG/3.9.3/ngccc.exe -O2 -G0 -mcpu=750
  -fno-common -mps-float -c p.c` and read with
  `build/binutils/powerpc-eabi-objdump` settles any "can this C shape produce
  two address registers / a duplicated address?" question in one shot, and is
  how both walls above were proven rather than assumed. (Do NOT put a `g =`

## 6es — 2026-10-01 single pick: **a 4-word length shortfall drives the official
### masked score to ~2% even when 80+ instructions are byte-identical — measure
### progress with an ALIGNED diff, not the sweep %**; and the doc-28 **CR-field loop
### condition** is a local-alloc COIN-FLIP, provable with `cc1 -dr` (fn_80138BA0,
### 29.8% → 85%-aligned body, 2.0% official, 0 emitted asm)

`fn_80138BA0` (416 B, 9 calls, 2 indirect vcalls) rebuilds to **81 consecutive
byte-identical instructions** (two runs, 0x80138BD4..C74 and C80..D1C) with only
**8 differing words** — and the official `test_wip_drafts.py` verdict is **2.0%**,
because the object is **4 instructions SHORT** and the masked compare is therefore
mis-aligned by 3-4 words. §6cs-1 already says "1 word of length is worth ~40
points"; this is the extreme case, and it has a hard operational rule:

* **Never judge a NEAR/DIFF draft by the sweep % when `len(object) !=
  symbols.txt size`.** Report BOTH numbers, and get the real one by either
  (a) `difflib.SequenceMatcher` over the **masked** mnemonic+operand streams
  (mask a `b*` branch's displacement, since REL14/REL24 are relocation-masked in
  the score but NOT in a raw `cs.disasm` dump), or (b) a ±k word shift search
  over the *relocation-masked* compare. Both turn a 2.0% into an honest
  "8 words differ, 2 contiguous correct runs". A draft whose header says
  "N %" with a length mismatch is not a measurement.

**The CR-field loop condition (doc 28 / §6t-2 / §7a-133 family) — when retail
keeps a loop condition in a callee-saved CR field instead of a GPR.** WANT shape:
`mfcr r12 / stw r12,0x10(r1) / cmpwi r3,0 / bne EXIT / mcrf cr4,cr0 / <body> /
bgt cr4, HEAD / … / lwz r12,0x10(r1) / mtcrf 8,r12`. Facts, all measured:

1. **A plain `do { … } while (c > 0)` with `c` a loop-invariant CALL RESULT
   produces it**, and the *operator* selects the branch. A standalone probe
   (compile a 10-line function, read the .s) gives the full map:
   `c == 0`/`!c` → `beq cr4`, `c != 0` → `bne cr4`, `c > 0`/`c >= 1`/`c > -1` →
   **`bgt cr4`**, `c < 0` → `blt cr4`, `c <= 0` → `ble cr4`, `c >= 0` → `bge cr4`.
   So when WANT shows `bgt cr4`, write `c > 0`; don't assume `== 0` and then
   fight the polarity. Probing the operator this way is 30 s and removes a
   whole class of dead ends.
2. **Whether the CR field is used at all is a local-alloc coin-flip, and
   `cc1 -dr` proves it** (§6bz/§6ek-3, one step further up): the
   post-reload RTL is **byte-identical** between a stripped-down variant that
   emits `mfcr/mcrf cr4/bgt cr4` and the full body that does not — same
   `(set (reg:CC 93) (compare:CC (reg:SI 92) (const_int 0)))` at insn 35,
   same `(jump_insn … (if_then_else (eq (reg:CC 93) 0) …))` latch, ONE use of
   each. Only the hard-reg assignment differs. **So: if the post-reload RTL
   already matches and the only diff is which hard reg a pseudo gets, the
   blocker is `local-alloc` — park it, do not run a source/flag ladder.**
3. **There is no C-side lever, and the trigger is CUMULATIVE.** Exhausted on
   this body: every loop shape (while/for/do-while/goto-label/early-return
   guard/`for(;;)`+break), 14 latch conditions, ~43 `-f` flags + every `-O`
   level, `volatile` on the frame local, a named `fp` for the callback,
   `void *` vs struct-typed `node`, reusing one variable for `node`/`node2`,
   dropping/re-adding the `var_r27` and `&sp8` hard pins, re-typing the
   condition (`s32`/`void *`/`u32`) and the callee (8 proto variants).
   Single-line ablations never restore it, but three *individual* sub-blocks
   each lose it on their own (`if (callee(...)==0){}else{}`,
   `obj->f = obj->g + v; helper(obj);`, and a 3-argument vcall) while an
   *empty* `else` arm does not — i.e. it is total CR pressure, not any one
   construct. **Next lever to try, if anyone revisits it: dump `cc1 --help`'s
   CR-related options and check whether the ProDG target's CR `reg_alloc_order`
   is short; if it offers fewer fields than the body needs concurrently, cut
   simultaneous CR demand (e.g. share the two `andi. r0,mask` results).**

**Bonus (both re-confirmations worth the trip).** (a) §6bf's arity audit is not
optional: `fn_8013B5C4` is **4-arg**, and at one call site WANT sets r3/r4/r6
only — the source passes the value already sitting in r5 from an earlier load,
so passing a literal `0` there emits a spurious `li r5,0`; the honest argument
is `node->unk0x60` and CSE makes it free. (b) §6de/§6dy's "every interior gap in
a hand-written field-layout typedef is an explicit `char pad[]`" bit me again
in the other direction: `char _q[0x8]` where `char _q[0x4]` was meant put
`unk0x70`/`unk0x74` four bytes high, and the only symptom was two `stw`
displacements — the object stayed the right length and the score looked like a
scheduling residual.

## 6et — 2026-10-01 single pick (skater-state zone 0x801F5898): **a doloop
### preheader's SOURCE-written init statements emit in plain source order**, and
### the tell that a 2-word NEAR is *that* is "every register colour already
### matches" (fn_801F5898, 40.3% -> EXACT, 308B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

A QB script-command wrapper that looks up a node by `goal_id` / `goal_name` /
`goal_index` and otherwise scans 0x32 nodes at 0x370 stride. The m2c draft
scored 40.3% with an object that was **already the exact 308B**, and the whole
40.3 -> 100.0% ladder was **semantic** — no pin, barrier, `volatile`, `// FLAG:`
or store permutation, and no opcode-4/PS words in the want (`ps_disasm.py`
decoded all 77 instructions).

**The recipe proper (the last 2.6 points, 97.4% -> 100.0%).** In a
`mtctr`/`bdnz` doloop, the loop-invariant setup statements that the *source*
writes in the loop-setup region land in the preheader **in source order** — they
are not re-sorted by `reorder_basic_block`'s use-priority rule. So a 2-word
residual that is purely two preheader births swapped is fixed by swapping the two
source statements, with nothing else changing:

```c
/* got  :  li r3,0 ; addi r9,r30,0x20   */
/* want :  addi r9,r30,0x20 ; li r3,0    */
var_r9 = (Node *)((char *)arg0 + 0x20);   /* walker birth FIRST */
var_r3 = 0;                               /* then the byte-offset IV  */
do { ... } while (var_ctr != 0);
```

**Why it is worth writing down:** §6eq established that *hoisted* preheader
statements (a `&local` addressof, a loop-invariant constant) are appended by the
loop optimiser and therefore always sort **LAST**; the complementary case — the
statements the source itself puts in the loop-setup region — keep **source**
order. Both produce the same-looking 2-3 word preheader residual, and they need
opposite fixes (there is nothing to hoist here; just reorder). **Discriminator
that names this case in one step:** the object is already the right LENGTH, every
saved-register *colour* already matches, and the entire diff is two adjacent
`addi`/`li` in the preheader. Then the fix is the statement swap, and it is
worth confirming that the swap changed *nothing* else in the function (it did
not, here) — that is what proves it is birth order and not a scheduler tie.

**The three semantic defects behind the 40.3% (each a known family, each worth
a double-figure jump on its own):**

1. **m2c invented FOUR arguments for a TWO-argument call** —
   `fn_801F5808(arg0, arg1, arg0, sp8)` where retail has
   `lwz r4,8(r1); mr r3,r30; bl` = `fn_801F5808(arg0, sp8)`. m2c's habit is to
   pass the *caller itself* as arg0 and then the callee's own args. Two extra
   `crclr cr1eq` plus two `mr` shifted the whole tail. §6bf arity audit +
   §6dc-1 / §6dn's "the m2c first-arg-is-the-caller convention can be wrong in
   both directions" — read the retail `bl`'s arg registers, not the draft.
2. **A merged `Unk_*` class with NO member at the offset makes m2c emit a WORD
   read.** `Unk_5FCDF30E` had `unk0x0` and `unk0x2C0` but nothing at `+0x2BE`,
   so m2c wrote `*(s32 *)((char *)var_r9 + 0x2BE)` and got `lwz 0x2be(r11)`
   where want has `lbz 0x2be(r9)`. A **file-local** `typedef` with a real
   `u8 unk0x2BE;` between explicit `char pad[]`s is the whole fix (§6cd's
   "member absent" case; M6.89d; §6dy/§6de for the pad discipline). **Tell:**
   want shows `lbz`/`lhz` at an offset the draft reads with `lwz` — the merged
   class is not merely mis-typed there, it has no member there.
3. **m2c's flattened `!(A==0)==0 || B || C` collapses retail's branchy bool.**
   Want is `v=1; if (byte==0) v=0; if (v != 0) { … }`, i.e.
   `li rN,1; cmpwi; bne; li rN,0; cmpwi rN,0; beq CONT`. Restoring
   `v = 1; if (b == 0) v = 0;` + the **positive** `&&` tests reproduced the pair
   verbatim (§4m-10 polarity, §6b-1, §4s). It also freed the walker to take
   r9 and the loop-invariant sp10 to be hoisted into the preheader as r10 — so
   one structural restore fixed five register-colour diffs at once. **Sibling
   proof in the same zone:** the promoted twins `fn_801F5808`/`fn_801F576C`
   (visible in the disasm) use the identical bool idiom and 0x370 stride, so a
   `continue`-shaped loop body is a family trait, not a per-function guess.

**Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object has only `.text`
(0x134 = 308B = `symbols.txt size:0x134` = header marker) and `.rela.text` — no
private `.rodata`, so no doc-14 caveat; **0 emitted inline instructions**; all
**18** relocations verified with the §6bw method (8 `R_PPC_REL14` + 4 local
`R_PPC_REL24` `b`s + 6 call `R_PPC_REL24`); the three QB hashes are plain
`lis`/`ori` immediates (unmasked, so byte-verified against
`qb_constants.h`: `QB_GOAL_ID`/`QB_GOAL_NAME`/`QB_GOAL_INDEX` =
0x9982E501/0xBFECC45B/0x474A6A7F) and there are **no ADDR16_HA/LO relocations**
at all, so hazard 277 cannot apply. Promoteable.

## 6eu — 2026-10-01 single pick (script/list zone 0x8023D8E4): **§6dg's
### `register s32 res __asm__("r3")` return-web pin MISCOMPILES when the same
### variable is assigned a call result — split into TWO variables instead**;
### plus `volatile` on a STRUCT local does block `&spN` address hoisting
### (a counter-example to §6aq-221's negative) (37.2% → EXACT, 172B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

A 5-call wrapper (`fn_80240B0C` byte-fill → `fn_8023DA64` → copy into a second
stack struct → `fn_80237454` → 2 tail calls) with a `res = 0;` default
materialised **before** the guard. All 4 wins were semantic; the whole
`// FLAG:`/pin/barrier surface was never needed.

**1. The `Unk_59AB5482` frame-region class is 64 bytes (16×s32) — check the
frame arithmetic BEFORE anything else (37.2% → the right frame, score dips to
25.0% en route).** m2c used it for a single 8-byte out-param, so ngccc sized the
frame from a 64-byte object (`stwu -0x58` / `stmw r30,0x50` / `stw r0,0x5c`) and
*every* stack displacement was 0x48 too high. §6db's closed form
`locals = stwu_N − 16 − 4·nSavedGPRs` gives 0x20−16−4 = 0x10 = two 8-byte slots
at r1+8 and r1+0x10, which is exactly what the want touches. **The mega-merged
*frame-region* classes are the worst offenders for this** because they are always
huge; a file-local 8-byte `typedef struct { s32 unk0; u16 unk4; }` fixed it.
**Byte-proven type oracle for this family:** the promoted *callee* tells you the
local's true layout. `fn_80237454`'s own prologue reads its arg1 as
`lwz 0(r29)` + `lhz 4(r29)` — i.e. it is the SAME `{s32; u16;}` struct this
function reads out of its own first slot. `src/fn_8023DA64.c` /
`src/fn_80240B0C.c` (both promoted) told me the writers see it as 6 bytes.
Corollary for the *shape* of a score: a large-frame m2c draft can get *worse*
when fixed, because fixing the frame re-aligns the index-aligned compare — the
37.2% → 25.0% dip is not a regression, it is the length finally matching.

**2. `volatile` on a STRUCT local DOES block the `&spN` address hoist
(25.0% → 95.35%).** With the frame right, `&sp8` was hoisted into a callee-saved
home because the address is live across the two callees
(`addi r30,r1,8` / `mr r3,r30` / `mr r4,r30` = 3 words), while want
re-materialises it per call site (`addi r3,r1,8` + `addi r4,r1,8` = 2 words).
`volatile Rect_t sp8;` on the **declaration** blocked it in one edit and also
gave want's r1-relative `lwz r0,8(r1)` / `lhz r11,0xc(r1)` reads instead of the
r30-based one. This is a **counter-example to §6aq-221** ("volatile-scalar
per-site remat does not extend to struct addresses — needs dual pins instead"):
it does not extend when the hoisted web is a *load* the address feeds and the
struct is otherwise read through the frame — measure it before concluding the
negative.

**3. §6dg's return-web pin is a TRAP when the pinned variable is also assigned
a call result — use two variables (95.35% → 100.0%).** The last single diff was
want's `li r3,0` (the default, in the RETURN register, before the branch) vs
got's `li r30,0`. §6dg's diagnosis is right — the return pseudo is live across
3 calls in the taken path, so `local_alloc` gives it one callee-saved home and
the default `0` inherits it — but its *prescription* measured **73.17%** here:
with `register s32 res __asm__("r3")` and `res = fn_...(...)` written directly,
**cc1 2.95 drops the result's live copy entirely** (the object loses both
`mr r30,r3` and `mr r3,r30`, spills the value to the stack, and comes out 1 word
short). Same root as §6be/§7a-137 (pins on call-result webs are unreliable).
The fix is free and pin-free:
```c
s32 tmp, res;
res = 0;                       /* li r3,0  — default in the return reg */
if (cond) {
    tmp = fn_80237454(...);    /* mr r30,r3 — callee-saved home for the result */
    fn_802403A0(...);          /* r3 clobbered twice */
    fn_8023D8D0(arg0);
    res = tmp;                 /* mr r3,r30 */
}
return res;
```
**Generalisable: when want shows the default value materialised in the return
register AND a `mr`/`mr` round-trip of the call result in and out of one
callee-saved register, retail had two webs — split the C variable rather than
pinning it.** (Same "one variable per web" family as §6cw/§6bu/§6an-3, but the
split is what frees the *default* onto r3, not the value onto r30.)

**4. Cheap confirmations in the same body.** A 4-byte `blr` stub called with a
materialised `.rodata2 data:string` address is 1-arg — m2c's 0-arg call dropped
the whole `lis`+`addi` pair, which is the "phantom call argument" family
(§6eg) but the *inverse* direction (the literal is the arg, not an extra one);
a callee whose first arg is a POINTER must be declared `T *` even when m2c's
arity was already right, or the address web is unusable; `void *fn_80237454(...)`
vs `s32` is irrelevant when want only does `mr r30,r3`.

**Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object carries only
`.text` (0xAC = 172 B = `symbols.txt size:0xAC` = the `range=` marker) and
`.rela.text` — no `.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss`, so no doc-14 caveat; **0 emitted
inline instructions**; the single `R_PPC_REL14` (addend `98`, printed in hex) is
0x8023D97C = want's `beq` target and all 5 `R_PPC_REL24` targets are
`fn_80240B0C`/`fn_8023DA64`/`fn_80237454`/`fn_802403A0`/`fn_8023D8D0` (§6bw
method); `lbl_802B0EC0` hand-decoded from want's `lis -0x7fd5` + `addi 0xec0`
and confirmed a real `.rodata2` `data:string` in `symbols.txt`, so hazard 277
cannot apply. Promoteable.

## 6ex — 2026-10-01 single pick (0x801BB804): the store-class model has a **second
### stage** — "class heads in source-LUID order, then class tails in LUID order" —
### which makes the required source order UNIQUELY INVERTIBLE by hand (40.4% → EXACT,
### 192B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

A `Script*` field-fill constructor (12 stores, 5 rodata2 float constants, 2 calls)
sat at 40.4% with a 208B object for a 192B want. Two findings; the first is a
re-confirmation, the second is new and it removed the need for any search.

* **1. Re-confirmed, and the "got is N insns LONG" tell had a second signature:
  a `s32` member that retail stores with `stfs` produces `fctiwz` + `stfd` + `lwz`
  = 3 surplus instructions AND an 8-byte anonymous DFmode temp that inflates the
  frame.** The corpus-merged `Unk_FD1A491C` types 0x34/0xF8/0xFC/0x114 as `s32`;
  retail `stfs`es all four. A file-local typedef with `f32` there removed the
  dance, shrank `stwu -0x18 → -0x10`, and fixed `stmw`/LR offsets in one edit:
  40.4% → 83.3%, object 208B → 192B (size-exact). Same family as §6eh2 TELL 1
  ("count the surplus words against the number of STORES, not the number of
  calls") — here there were **zero** calls in the surplus, which is what
  distinguishes the conversion tell from §6de/§6dg's "one surplus word per
  missing prototype / per surplus arg".

* **2. NEW: the documented per-class store rotation (recipes 24/64/159/198/206,
  §6cd, §6ep2-2 — "ngccc emits the LAST source statement of a store class
  first, the rest in source order") is only stage 1. There is a stage 2 that
  orders the CLASSES: the emitted order is (a) every class's *head* — the member
  the rotation promoted to the front — in source-LUID order, then (b) every
  class's *tail* in source-LUID order.** Both stages were confirmed identical
  across two source orders that differed only inside the classes (emission
  permutation [1,5,7,0,2,3,4,6] over the 8-store run in both), so it is
  deterministic, not a tie-break.

  **Why this is worth more than a search:** the two stages are both invertible,
  so want's store order *determines* the source order — no permutation needed.
  Procedure for a run of N stores split into classes C1..Ck:
  1. group want's emitted stores by source register (f0 / r30 / f10 here);
  2. per class, `src = emitted[1:] + [emitted[0]]` (un-rotate);
  3. order the class heads among themselves by want position, and the class tails
     likewise, then take the single LUID order consistent with both plus the
     per-class orders. On this function that pinned all 8 stores uniquely:
     `114, 34, F8, FC, 100, 17C, 180, 184`.
  Measured ladder: want-order source 83.3% → per-class un-rotated (heads/tails
  still interleaved by want) 89.6%, class-relative orders now correct and only
  the class interleave wrong → 100.0% on the derived order. **Diagnostic that
  names stage 2 on sight: the class-RELATIVE orders of every class already match
  want, and the only diffs are which class comes next — that is stage 2, and no
  intra-class permutation can touch it.**

  Corollary on which stores group at all: only stores that share a source
  register form a class. Here the first four stores of the run (r3, f13, f12,
  f11 — one per register) kept plain source order, and the `mr r3,r31` from
  `return arg0;` (recipe 249) landed mid-run on its own, exactly as in want.
  So do not lump a run into one class; re-check which pairs share a value web
  after every type fix, because fixing a member's type can move a store into or
  out of a class (here the two `s32`→`f32` members joined the f0 class).

  Cheaper companion from the same function, both confirmed once: five `data:float`
  `.rodata2` symbols **in the same 64 KB page** get **five separate page anchors**
  in want's colour order r9/r11/r10/r8/r7 with the loads in f0/f13/f12/f11/f10 —
  plain `extern f32` refs for all five produce that for free (6an-5 / 6br), and
  the FPR colour follows the *load* order, so fix the load order before pinning
  (§6ep2-2). And an empty `for (vc = 4; vc != 0; vc--) {}` compiles to retail's
  `li r0,4; mtctr r0; bdnz .` (a *self-targeting* doloop, doc 30) with no
  `-fno-branch-count-reg` and no pin — don't preemptively add one.

* **Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object has only
  `.text` (0xC0 = 192B = `symbols.txt size:0xC0` = the header marker) and
  `.rela.text` — no private `.rodata`, so no doc-14 promote caveat; **0 emitted
  inline instructions**; all 16 relocations verified with the §6bw method — the
  3 `R_PPC_REL24` targets are `fn_8009F53C`/`Mem_Alloc2`/`fn_80007B94` (want's
  three `bl`s) and the single intra-function `R_PPC_REL14` addend `0x2c` resolves
  to 0x801BB830, i.e. retail's self-targeting `bdnz`; all 6 `ADDR16_HA/LO` pairs
  hand-decoded from want's `lis`/`addi` as `lis_value + signext(addi)`
  (0x802AC518 and 0x802AC394/398/39C/3A0/3A4, the last five `data:float`), so
  hazard 277 cannot apply; the QB hash 0x5E43A604 is a bare `lis`/`ori` pair
  (unmasked) and matches `QB_SKATERCAMERA` in `qb_constants.h`. Promoteable.

## 6ew - 2026-10-01 single pick (0x800F1B5C): **the "named zero local" lever is a
### TRAP when want's constant birth is in the loop PREHEADER - write the plain
### literal and let LICM hoist it** (37.0% -> EXACT, 216B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

`fn_800F1B5C` went from a 37 % m2c draft to byte-exact with **no codegen lever at
all** - and the last two steps were a *regression and a deletion*, which is the
useful part. It is the sharpest correction yet to the most-used recipe family in
this project (§6c-28 / §73-118 / §6al-163 / §6ap-2: "give the zero its own named
local so it gets a fresh `li` / lands in a callee-saved reg").

**The discriminator is WHERE want's `li <const>` sits relative to the loop's entry
branch.** Retail materialises zero into r31, loads offset four of the r29 object into r27, unsigned-compares the two with a greater-or-equal exit branch, and only then materialises zero into r26 in the preheader before the loop.

* **Plain literal `sp8 = 0;` inside the loop body -> 100.0 % EXACT.** `loop.c`
  hoists the invariant def into the preheader, exactly where want has it.
* **A named local assigned *before* the `if` -> 94.4 %** (the only residual was
  this one `li`: it lands in the ENTRY block, before the `cmplw`, because
  `reorder_basic_block` sorts the 1-user `li` behind nothing while the 2-user
  compare is a *loop-generated* insn it cannot reorder).
* **The same named local assigned as the FIRST statement INSIDE the `if`
  (i.e. "put the untested IV's init in the guarded block", §6bp-3) -> 9.1 %**,
  a *massive* regression: the extra def in the preheader pushes the frame
  0x28->0x30, costs a 7th saved GPR, and - worst of all - the now-2-user
  `&sp8` address web acquires a callee-saved home (`addi r26,r1,8` + `mr r5,r26`
  at the call) where want re-materialises `addi r5,r1,8` per site.

**Rule: only introduce a named zero/local when want's `li` is INSIDE the loop
body. If want's `li` is in the preheader (after the entry `bge`/`beq`), the
retail source wrote the bare literal and the loop optimizer did the hoisting -
any explicit local you add is a NEW def with its own block, its own
use-priority and its own address web, and it will lose to the optimizer's
hoisted copy.** This is the third leg of the preheader-ordering family
(§6eq: *hoisted* preheader statements are appended by the loop optimizer and
therefore sort LAST; §6et: statements the *source* writes in the loop-setup
region keep source order; here: don't write one at all and let the optimizer own
the slot). Measured spread on one 3-word residual: 9.1 % / 94.4 % / 100.0 %.

**Second-order, same function, worth the audit notes:** the m2c draft was wrong
in SIX independent semantic ways and *not one* of them was a codegen issue -
(1) `mr r29,r4` in the prologue => **two** parameters, the first unused
(recipe 54 / §6y-127) while m2c had one, so every `arg1->unk0x4` read came out
of the wrong entry register; (2) **two whole calls missing** (`fn_800F0AFC` and
`fn_80129260`, the latter 3-arg with its value from the former) - detected
because want's arg-setup window is `mr r5,r3 / mr r4,r31 / lwz r3,8(r1) /
addi r31,r31,1 / bl` with 3 arg values and only 2 `mr`s; (3) a **3-level chain**
`fn_800F0AFC(fn_80129528(arg1, fn_801293FC(sp8, j)))` (recipe 23 / §4t / §6bh);
(4) **no prototypes at all** for the six callees (the old 37 %'s `crclr cr1eq`s);
(5) a **doubled counter increment** (`j += 1;` AND `j++;` -> `addi r31,r31,2`,
the m2c duplicate-`i` artifact); (6) the outer count needed hoisting into a
local so it lives in a callee-saved reg instead of being re-read in the latch
(this one edit was **37.0 % -> 94.4 %**). At 37 % with the object ALREADY the
exact 216 B and every instruction kind correct, the residual was entirely
"m2c didn't decompile the function", not "the compiler can't emit it".

## 6fa — 2026-10-01 single pick (QB `Script*` zone 0x8017DC0C, 296 B, 35.14% → EXACT, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins): **want stores to N consecutive stack slots that GOT omits entirely ⇒ the N slots are FIELDS OF ONE OBJECT, and the frame is a STEP FUNCTION of that object's `sizeof`, not a linear one**

A 4-scalar m2c draft at 35.14 % whose compiled object was *already the exact 296 B*
— every diff was a mis-decode, and 93 % of them came from ONE root cause. Two
rules worth pulling out, plus one M8.31 confirmation with a new signature.

* **Rule A — "want has stores GOT doesn't" ⇒ merge the siblings into one struct.**
  m2c declared `s8 sp8; s32 sp10; s32 sp14; s8 sp18;` and passed only `&sp8`
  (to `fn_80137CB4` / `fn_8013CC84` / `fn_8013DE78`). Because the other three
  locals are **not** address-taken, GCC 2.95's alias analysis concluded the
  callee cannot reach them and DCE'd their stores across the escaping call:
  GOT emitted only `stb r0,8(r1)` where want has
  `li r9,0xff / stb r0,8(r1) / stw r9,0x10(r1)` and, in the else arm,
  `li r9,2 / li r11,8 / stb r0,8(r1) / stw r9,0x14(r1) / stb r11,0x18(r1)`.
  One file-local `struct { s8 b00; s8 b01; u16 h02; s32 w04; s32 w08; s32 w0C;
  s8 b10; s32 w14; s32 w18; s32 w1C; s8 b20; char pad[..]; }` fixed all of it
  at once (35.14 % → 85.14 %) because the stores become stores to an
  **address-taken object** and therefore observable. This is the *scalar-split*
  form of recipe 117 / §6v-117 (escaping array siblings keep dead stores
  alive) and §6ad-138 (escaped struct ctx out-param): there the draft already
  had one array/struct, here the DRAFT has N separate scalars and the fix is to
  **re-unite** them. Recognition one-liner: a run of `li`/`stb`/`stw` to
  consecutive r1-relative offsets that GOT omits, at the *right length and the
  right instruction kinds* — that is never a scheduling residual, it is missing
  object identity. Read the field widths off the **retail init function**
  (`fn_80137CB4` here writes 0x0/0x1 stb, 0x2 sth, 0x4/0x8/0xC/0x14/0x18/0x1C
  stw, 0x10/0x20 stb), which also proves the minimum struct size.

* **Rule B — the frame is a STEP FUNCTION of `sizeof` for an address-taken
  aggregate, so §6db's closed form gives you the REGION, not the size.** §6db
  correctly gives `locals_region = stwu_N − 16 − 4·nSavedGPRs` (here
  0x40 − 16 − 12 = 0x2C), but you then need a `sizeof` that lands the object
  *in* that region, and the mapping is not linear — measured on this function
  by sweeping the pad array (7 compiles, 10 s):

  | `sizeof` | 0x24 | 0x28 | 0x2C | 0x30 | 0x34 | 0x38 | 0x3C |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | region (save−8) | 0x2C | 0x2C | 0x3C | 0x3C | 0x44 | 0x4C | 0x4C |
  | `stwu` | −0x40 | −0x40 | −0x50 | −0x50 | −0x58 | −0x60 | −0x60 |

  A 0x2C struct — the *arithmetically obvious* answer from the region size — is
  already in the next bucket and costs 16 bytes of frame and 12 of save area.
  **Probe it, don't derive it**; the useful trick is to make the LAST member a
  `char pad[0x7]`-style array and vary only that one number. (With four
  separate scalars ngccc gave region 0xC, so Rule A's merge is also what makes
  the region reachable at all — do A before B.) §6ov's "oversized array
  reproduces an unexplained frame gap" and §6dt's "frame-template tail pad" are
  the same lever from the other direction.

* **M8.31 confirmation with a new signature — the return-type flip can move a
  32-bit CONSTANT arg0's `ori` COMPLETION ahead of args 1..N's `li` setups,
  not just rotate `mr`s.** want: `lis r3,-0xa4 / lwz r31,0x5f9c(r9) /
  ori r3,r3,0x39b6 / li r4,0 / li r5,0 / li r6,0 / li r7,0 / bl`; GOT emitted
  the four `li`s first and the `ori` immediately before the `bl`. Declaring the
  callee `void` instead of `s32` (its result is discarded here) is worth the
  entire 93.24 % → 100.00 % step — one token, 0 emitted instructions. Do NOT
  reach for the old-style `void f();` instead: it drops all four `li`s and
  makes the object 4 bytes long (18.67 %). The tell is a *constant-completion*
  `ori`/`addi` transposed against `li` setups rather than an `mr` rotation.

**Also confirmed, cheaply:** (a) a **0-arg callee needs NO prototype** — the
draft's `fn_8012E970();` (implicit int, reads no arg reg) emitted no `crclr`
either way, so the doc-56 sweep gain here was exactly 5 crclrs from 4 real
missing/incorrect signatures (`fn_8021B554` 1-arg, `fn_8021B55C` 2-arg,
`fn_8021B508` 1-arg, and `fn_8013E184` **3→2 args** — m2c had invented a
leading arg0, and the wrong arity also shifted the arg-setup window, not just
added a word); (b) a hash literal is byte-verified by the masked score because
`lis`+`ori` are plain immediates — but decode them anyway: here
`lis r3,-0xa4` is field `0xFF5C` ⇒ **0xFF5C39B6 = `QB_PATCHCLEANUP`**, the
header value, confirmed correct (the `-0xa4` looks like a 0x10000-shifted page
until you remember `-(0xA4) & 0xFFFF == 0xFF5C`); (c) `extern char lbl[]` +
`*(s32 *)&lbl` for a `.data size:0x4` global produced the correct
`lis`+`lwz disp(r9)` pair **and** a real `R_PPC_ADDR16_HA/LO` against
`lbl_80305F9C`, so the masked 100 % is link-correct (no hazard 277) — the
§285 "declare it at its width" rule was not needed here and was not applied.

Audit of the EXACT: object `.text` = 0x128 = 296 B = `symbols.txt size:0x128` =
header marker; only `.text` + `.rela.text` (no private `.rodata`, so no doc-14
pool caveat); **0 emitted inline instructions**; 4/4 intra-function branch
relocations verified with the §6bw method (3 × `R_PPC_REL14` type 11 with
section-relative addends `0xc0`/`0x78`/`0x10c` → 0x8017DCCC / 0x8017DC84 /
0x8017DD18, plus the local `b`'s `R_PPC_REL24` type 10 at `.text+0x10c`) and
17/17 `R_PPC_REL24` call targets matched want's `bl` destinations. Left in
`src/wip`, not promoted.

## 6fb — 2026-10-01 single pick (0x800F078C, QB `Script*`): a struct can be **`f32`
### for initialisation and `__ps_t` for the copy-out** in the SAME variable, and the
### "split base" (§6at-3) needs the pointer born **between the two constant loads**
### (37.2% → EXACT, 172 B, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers)

A 43-instruction `Script*`-style wrapper: two `GetVector` probes, a `fneg` arm, and a
`else` that builds a 4-float default on the stack and then writes it into the caller's
vector. All four wins were semantic, and the *one* novel construct is a variable that
must have **two different element types at once**:

* **`f32` members to build it, `__ps_t` to copy it out.** Retail's tail stores four scalar floats (from f0 to the stack slot at r1 plus eight, from f13 to offset 0xC of the r9 object, and from f0 to offsets eight and four of that object), then moves the second eight-byte pair from offset eight of the r9 object into offset eight of the arg1 home with a paired-single load and store, and moves the first pair from offset eight of the stack temp into offset zero of the arg1 home the same way.
  i.e. four **scalar** `stfs` fills followed by two **8-byte** paired-single moves. That
  is not expressible with a `__ps_t`-typed struct (the fills would become `psq_st`) nor
  with an `f32`-typed destination (the copies would become `lfs`+`stfs`). It needs
  `typedef struct { f32 x, y, z, w; } V4;` for the fills **plus** explicit
  `((__ps_t *)arg1)[1] = ((__ps_t *)p)[1];` / `((__ps_t *)arg1)[0] = ((__ps_t *)&sp8)[0];`.
  **Diagnostic in one look: a want block with scalar `stfs` fills into a stack temp
  immediately followed by `psq_l`/`psq_st` copies OUT of that temp — the temp is
  `f32`-typed and the copies are `__ps_t`-cast, and both choices are load-bearing
  (a `__ps_t` struct gives `psq_st` fills, a `f32` destination gives `lfs`/`stfs` copies).**
  This is the paired-single twin of §6bq/§6dw's "one 16-byte PS copy" and of
  `src/fn_8001A9D4.c`-style struct assignments; the object needs `-mps-float`, which
  `test_wip_drafts.py` auto-adds because the body mentions `__ps_t`.
* **The split base needs the pointer's BIRTH between the two independent constant
  loads, and it must be used by exactly the right subset of the sites.** Want:
  `lis r11 | lis r10 | lfs f0 | addi r9,r1,8 | lfs f13 | stfs f0,8(r1) | stfs f13,0xc(r9) |
  stfs f0,8(r9) | stfs f0,4(r9) | psq_l 8(r9) | … | psq_l 8(r1)`. So the frame slot
  serves the **first** fill and the **second** pair copy, and the named pointer
  `p = &sp8` serves the other three fills and the **first** pair copy — and the
  `addi` sits *between* the two `lfs`. Writing the first fill through the local and the
  rest through `p` (with `a = lbl_…; p = &sp8; b = lbl_…;` as statements) reproduces
  all of it. This is §6at-3 (split base) + §6an-205 (anchor sandwich) + §6bh-3
  (statement position) composed, and the failure mode is silent: routing **all** four
  fills through `p` gives `stfs f0,0(r9)` instead of `8(r1)` and drops the `addi` out of
  the middle entirely.
* **Store-run reordering is not a rotation of the whole run — the last TWO of four
  were swapped while the first two stayed put.** Source `[x, w, y, z]` emitted
  `[x, w, z, y]` (the fix); source `[x, w, z, y]` emitted `[x, w, y, z]`. Two words,
  95.3% → 100.0%, one hand swap. Sibling of §6ev's two-stage class model and
  §6ep2-2's per-class rotation: read the *emitted* order and swap the minimal adjacent
  pair rather than looking for a rule. (Corollary per §6ep: re-measure on the final body —
  here the swap was neutral-then-correct rather than a monotone gain.)
* **Free confirmation of the §6dc arity/type-oracle rule via a `scope:global` name
  rather than an `fn_` address:** `fn_80128398` is `GetVector` (`symbols.txt:5629`),
  already promoted as `src/fn_80128398.c` with the real
  `s32 GetVector(CStruct*, s32, CStruct*, s32)`. m2c had called it 3-arg with the hash
  in arg0, so both sites were unprototyped (2 × `crclr cr1eq`) and the whole arg-setup
  window shifted. **`grep -n "^<Name> " config/G2TE52/symbols.txt` before guessing a
  callee's signature — renamed/SDK-named functions are the most reliable arity oracle
  in the tree** and m2c cannot know them.
* **The QB hashes were already right in the header** (`QB_POS` = 0x7F261953,
  `QB_POSITION` = 0xB9D31B0A; `lis 0x7f26/ori 0x1953` and `lis -0x462d/ori 0x1b0a`
  hand-decode to exactly those), and both constants are `.rodata2 data:float`
  (0.0f / 1.0f) reachable as plain `extern f32` + bare use — §6ek's `extern f32` vs
  `extern char[]`+`*(f32 *)` axis was NOT the lever here (both forms score the same;
  only the anchor register differs, and it was already right).

Audit: object has only `.text` (0xAC = 172 B = `symbols.txt size:0xAC` = the `range=`
marker) and `.rela.text` — **no `.rodata`**, so masked-EXACT is also promote-clean
(no doc-14 pool); **0 emitted inline instructions**; all 3 intra-function branch
relocations verified with the §6bw method (2 × `R_PPC_REL14` type 11 with
section-relative addends `0x98`/`0x64` → 0x800F0824 / 0x800F07F0, and the local `b`'s
`R_PPC_REL24` type 10 at `.text+0x98`), 2 `R_PPC_REL24` calls both to `GetVector`, and
4 `ADDR16_HA`/`LO` pairs hand-decoded from want's `lis 0x802A` + `addi -0x4CFC/-0x4CF8`
as 0x8029B304 / 0x8029B308 (both real `data:float` symbols), so the hazard-277
masked-wrong-label case cannot apply. Left in `src/wip`, not promoted.

## 6ey — 2026-10-01 single pick (0x80014D54, 284B): the CONVERSE of §6dx — a
### **median-rooted** dispatch tree proves the source is a `switch`, and m2c
### CANNOT represent a `case` FALLTHROUGH, so it invents a `goto` into a
### different arm (40.85% → EXACT, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins)

§6dx reads a *right-linear* want tree as "the source was an if/else chain, not a
switch". This is the other direction, and it is the one that fires on m2c drafts.

**1. The tell, in one comparison.** A `switch` lowering is a median-rooted
binary search (`balance_case_nodes`, §6an-204/§6t-6/§70-124); an if/else-if
chain is always right-linear. So: retail roots the dispatch at the median case value three with a greater-than branch to the right subtree, splits the left subtree again at value two with a greater-or-equal branch, tests values zero and one for early return and the next body with equality branches, falls through to the end, and handles values four and five in the right subtree with equality branches to their bodies before converging on the end.
is a `switch (arg1) { case 0..5 }`, full stop. If the draft is if/else + `goto`,
**rewriting it back to a `switch` can be the entire fix** — here it took
40.85% → **57.75%** and simultaneously fixed three things at once: the compare
tree, an early-return case, and a fallthrough chain (below). Do not try to fix an
if/else draft's tree with polarity flips (§4s), `lim` variables, or case-tree
steering; measure the root against the median of the case set first. (My one
hand-written if/else + `goto tail;` attempt scored **15.94%** — worse than the
inherited draft — so this is not a free "try the other form" change: identify the
tree first.)

**2. NEW m2c pathology — `case A: case B: <body> /*fall through*/ case C:` has
no if/else representation, so m2c emits a `goto` to a label placed inside a
DIFFERENT arm.** Its signature in the want: two case arms reach **one** body
block, and the *later* case's entry `beq` lands at the **start of the earlier
case's body** (i.e. the later case skips the earlier case's work) while the
earlier case *falls through* into it. In this function the two arms also
*contributed different amounts of work* to that one block (case 2/3 ran a
3-condition `memcpy` guard, case 4 ran none), which is the tell. Restoring
`case 2: case 3: <guard> /* fall through */ case 4: <tail>` is what makes one
shared basic block appear at want's address.

**3. A `case N: return;` is NOT the same as `case N: break;` when the switch is
followed by a call** — m2c rendered `case 0: return;` as `case 0: break;` and
the body then fell into the trailing `fn_80013410(...)`. Cost: the `beq` went to
the wrong block. Cheap check: does any case arm in the want branch to the
EPILOGUE rather than to the block after the dispatch? If so that arm is an early
`return` and m2c dropped it.

**4. For a balanced switch tree the physical order of the case BODIES follows the
case-LABEL source order, not the tree order** (§6dx/§70-125) — and here that
single reorder was the biggest single jump in the function. Want: case1, case5,
case2/3, case4. Source order `1, 5, 2, 3, 4` scored **97.18%**; the same code
with `1, 2, 3, 4, 5` scored 57.75%. Cheap and worth doing before any flag or

## 6ev — 2026-10-01 single pick (0x800F1E1C, 212B): a ZERO-valued RETURN variable used as the loop entry guard's comparison operand, and `-fno-gcse` as the fix for a "ONE word short + a missing address `mr`" signature (36.4% → EXACT, 5 semantic fixes, 1 flag, 0 emitted asm, 0 pins)

A table-remove wrapper: `i=0; fn_800F0374(arg1);` then a guarded do-while over a
0xC-stride array at `self+0x1000C` (count at `self+0x10008`), and on a hit
`fn_800F1790(self,i)`, `n = --count`, `if (i != n) copy last(n) into p;
fn_800F18B0(self,count,i)`. All 36 words of the inherited 36.4 % m2c diff were
**semantic**; only ONE codegen lever was needed.

* **DECODE AID — "want has `li r3,0` in the ENTRY block, a `cmplw` against the
  count, NO `li r3,0` before the epilogue, and `li r3,1` in the found arm" ⇒ the
  RETURN VARIABLE is also the guard's zero operand.** This is §6c-27 (a *variable*
  holding 0 keeps the immediate form) plus §6ap-183 (guard operand need not be the
  counter), but the identification is new: r3 falls through the whole loop
  untouched, so it is not a per-block `li` — it is one pseudo living from the entry
  `li` to `return res`, and the tail `li r3,0` that a naive `return 0` would emit
  is exactly what's missing from want. Writing
  ```c
  res = 0;
  if ((u32)res < (u32)*(s32 *)((char *)arg0 + 0x10008)) { ... res = 1; break; }
  return res;
  ```
  reproduces `li r3,0 / lwz / cmplw r3,r0 / bge` byte-exactly and is the only
  spelling that does (a `0 < count` literal gives `cmpwi`). **Corollary for triage:
  a size-EXACT-object draft that is missing a single `li r3,0`/`li rX,0` at the
  epilogue is looking for a return variable, not for a deleted instruction.**

* **`-fno-gcse` is the fix for "object is exactly ONE word short AND an address
  `mr` copy is missing" — a signature distinct from every `-fno-gcse` case in
  §6ar-223 / §6am-179 / §6bx / §6dw-2.** Here want sequences the entry block as the callee call followed by the page-anchor high-part add, a zero materialisation into r3, a word load from offset eight of the anchor, and an unsigned compare against zero branching to the end, with the guard block then copying the anchor into r30 and deriving the next pointer by adding 0xC,
  i.e. the page anchor is materialised **at its point of use in the entry block,
  after the call**, and the `hp` variable assigned *inside* the guard is a real
  copy of it. With GCSE on, `loop.c:hoist_insn_out_of_loop` recognises the address
  as loop-invariant (the loop reads `hp[2]`), hoists it into the preheader, and
  `cse_basic_block` then **fuses the guard's inline `*(s32*)((char*)arg0+0x10008)`
  web with the `hp` variable** — so (a) the `mr` disappears (object 1 word short)
  and (b) the `addis` jumps above the `bl`. `-fno-gcse` keeps the anchor at its
  point of use and the two webs stay split. Same pass, same flag as §6ar-223, but
  the tell there was a rotated callee-saved map and here it is a **length
  delta of exactly 4 bytes with one `mr` unaccounted for** — worth checking this
  flag FIRST on any "one word short" NEAR in a loop that reads a constant-offset
  global through a pointer assigned inside a guard.

* **Caller-side prototype must be WIDER than the promoted callee's own definition
  when the callee narrows on store (§6di, second instance).** `src/fn_800F18B0.c`
  (promoted, byte-identical) declares `void fn_800F18B0(s32,s32,u16)` and its body
  does `sth r5,0(r3)`. The caller here must declare it `(void*, s32, s32)`, else
  ngccc emits `clrlwi r5,r28,0x10` (1 surplus word) in front of the call. Same
  rule as §6ey's promoted-stub case but with the direction reversed: here the
  *definition* is right and the *call site* is wrong.

* **The 3-swap store run needed its loads and stores in ASCENDING offset order
  (not the documented rotate-left).** With the two-pointer shape
  (`q9 = base + n*0xC`, `q11 = q9 + 3`, values staged as `v0/v4/v8`, then
  `p->f0/p->f4/p->f8`) the run emits want's `lwz 0xc(r9) / addi r11,r9,0xc /
  lwz 8(r11) / lwz 4(r11) / stw 8 / stw 0 / stw 4` verbatim. 3 of 36
  load/store permutations of that block reach 100 %, the rest 84-96 % — it is a
  two-way local tie-break, **not** a permutation problem, and the offsets staying
  ASCENDING is the informative part (§6ev's stage-then-store, §6bu). Related:
  writing the swap source offset-first `(char *)(n*0xC + (s32)arg0) + 0x10000`

* Audit: object `.text` = 0xD4 = 212 B = `symbols.txt size:0xD4` = header `range=`
  marker; only `.text` + `.rela.text` (no `.rodata`, so no doc-14 caveat);

  2 × `R_PPC_REL24` type 10 calls to `fn_800F0374` / `fn_800F1790` /
  `fn_800F18B0`, 1 local `b` to `.text+0xc0`); **no `ADDR16_HA/LO` entries at all**
