## 6fc — 2026-10-01 single pick (script-command zone 0x80130898, 340B): **move the `if`
LATER in the source to move its BRANCH later (the compare stays put)**, and when a
hard pin fixes N diffs but breaks 2 more, **pin the OTHER member of the register
permutation** (38.4% → EXACT, 1 hard-reg pin, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags)

A plain m2c draft with 6 semantic errors. Three findings, in the order they paid.

**1. A guard whose `cmpwi` is early and whose branch is N instructions late = the
`if` belongs AFTER the load/store run in the source (worth +28 points here, and it
is a *statement position*, not a scheduling problem).** Retail loads offset 0xBC of the homed arg0 into r3 and compares it against zero, then runs nine instructions in the same block before the equal-branch to the join: an indexed load combining the r11 and r9 bases, an address add into r30, a store to offset 0xC8, a word load from offset four of the derived pointer into r9 with a store to offset 0x18, a word load from offset eight with a store to offset 0x10, and a final word load from offset 0xC into r29.
m2c's order (guard immediately after the test) puts `beq` right after `cmpwi` and
out-lines the whole body before the four load/store pairs: same instruction
multiset, same length, 28 points of diff. The fix is to read the branch's
**extent** (§6bq / §4aq tell) and make those nine instructions part of the
guard's block by moving the `if` *below* them, with the tested value in a saved
local:
```c
old = arg0->fBC;                     /* load stays early  */
arg0->fC8 = ...; rec = ...;           /* the run         */
arg0->f18 = rec->f04; arg0->f10 = rec->f08; link = rec->f0C;
if (old != 0) { CObject_RemoveRefLink(old, p28); arg0->fBC = 0; }   /* branch lands here */
```
The `cmpwi` is a separate RTL insn that `sched1` hoists next to its load no
matter where the `if` is; only the *branch* is pinned to the end of the block, so
**block membership is the lever, and the compare's position is not yours to
control.** Reordering the run's own statements, every scheduling flag and every
pin were no-ops on this residual. Sibling of §6be (label placement) and §6dm-3
(two blocks in a guard decide a callee-saved swap), but the *fix* here — move
the `if` down — is new; the classic member of this family only ever tried moving
the guarded work up.

**2. A hard pin on a web that want also *coalesces* elsewhere DESTROYS that
coalesce — so when a pin fixes the permutation but breaks 2 other words, pin the
OTHER web in the swap.** Residual after (1) and the bitfield fix: a two-register
rotation, `count` in r11 vs want's r9 and `base` in r9 vs want's r11 (9 diffs,
89.4%). `register s32 off __asm__("r9")` on the count gave 97.65% — and broke
`addi r0, r9, -1` / `stw r0, 0x38(r31)` into an in-place `addi r9, r9, -1`, because
hard-pinning the source makes the decrement's destination pseudo coalesce *into*
it. Neither a second local for the stored value nor a `"+r"` identity barrier
recovered the separate dest (the barrier made it worse, 96.5%). **Pinning the
co-existing `base` web to r11 instead — via an `s32` alias, since cc1 drops
pointer-typed pins (§76-178) — left the count free to land in r9 with its natural
separate dest: 100.0%, 0 emitted instructions.** Rule: measure a pin's
*collateral* (a store that went in-place is the usual signal), and when a pin is
in the middle of a permutation and also a coalesce source, aim it at the
**neighbour**, not the member you first noticed.

**3. A union lets the "read the whole word" and "write one bit" views coexist in
one variable** (`ret = obj->fB4.w >> 31` at the top, `obj->fB4.bf.b31 = x >> 26`
at the bottom) and is what produced the wanted `rlwinm r0,r0,6,0x1f,0x1f` +
`rlwimi r9,r0,0x1f,0,0` + `stw r9,0xb4(r31)`. The plain mask/or form
`(w & ~0x80000000u) | (((x>>26)&1) << 31)` is semantically identical and folds
to `rlwinm 5,0,0` + `clrlwi` + `or` instead (68.6% vs 89.4% here) — §6o-110 /
§6bs, with the union being the instance where the same variable is read at two
widths *inside one function*.

**Also confirmed (all zero-cost):** the record array's element is addressed as
`(char *)base + (idx * 0x2C)` for the `lwzx`/`add` pair — a struct-typed element
gives `lwz 0(rec)` and never the `lwzx`; and the promoted siblings
`src/fn_8009DFA0.c` / `fn_8009DFC0.c` / `fn_8012701C.c` / `fn_80126FF4.c` /
`fn_801347CC.c` supplied every callee signature *and* proved `fn_80126FF4` is
`void` (m2c had `s32`) and `CStruct_delete` is 2-arg (m2c called it with one
literal) — §6dc/§6di, and the call site had to pass the *guarded field* as
`CObject_RemoveRefLink`'s arg0 (§6dz), not the function's own arg1.

Audit: object `.text` = 0x154 = 340B = `symbols.txt size:0x154` = header marker;
only `.text` + `.rela.text` (no private `.rodata`, so no doc-14 caveat); **0
emitted inline instructions** (the one `__asm__` string is the `register`
attribute); 7/7 intra-function branch relocations verified against want's
independently decoded `bc`/`b` words (§6bw method) and all 7 call/ADDR16
relocations resolve to real `symbols.txt` entries, with `lbl_8030342C`
(`.data:0x8030342C`) hand-decoded from want's `lis 0x8030` + `lwz 0x342c` so
hazard 277 cannot apply. Promoteable.

## 6fd — 2026-10-01 single pick (0x8007F15C, 184B, 34.78% → EXACT, 0 emitted asm,
### 0 flags, 0 pins): the m2c `0;` STUB COUNT is a byte count for the missing PS words
### — and the PS *destination declaration form* decides whether cc1 spends 2 or 3
### address words on it

A "fill 8 f32 fields with one rodata constant, then copy the block into a 32-byte
global as four paired-single pairs" tail. m2c rendered the four `psq_l`/`psq_st`
pairs as four `0;` statements and the whole body then compiled 28 bytes short.

* **`N` consecutive `0;` lines ⇒ `8*N` bytes of missing `.text` ⇒ `2*N`
  undecodable words, all of them pair copies.** That is a *length* prediction you
  can check before writing any C: `want_size − got_size == 8 * (number of 0; lines)`.
  Here 184 − 156 = 28, not a multiple of 8 — the extra 20 is the 5 prologue/
  epilogue words m2c's wrong local offset had already cost, so measure
  `got_size` against `symbols.txt` FIRST (§6cs-1), then attribute the
  whole-word remainder to the stubs. **This is the concrete size rule behind
  §6dq-1 / §6ec-1's "three-way ambiguous `0;`" note.**
* **`tools/disasm.py` stops dead at the first PS word, so the stubs are at the
  very place you are not shown.** Capstone prints `?` from 0x8007F1DC on, and the
  draft header's `range=` marker then makes the missing tail look like a
  statics-DCE husk. Decode the raw words yourself past the stall
  (`struct.unpack('>I', d[fileoff+4*i:…])`):
  **primary opcode 56 = `psq_l`, 60 = `psq_st`**, D-form fields are
  `OPCD|D|rA|W|I|d` with D at bits 6-10 and rA at 11-15 (so `E00A0008` =
  `psq_l f0, 8(r10)` and `F0090008` = `psq_st f0, 8(r9)`). Companion of §6ag-9 /
  §6ai-152, but the *workflow* step those notes lack is "the stall hides the tail,
  so read past it".
* **A `union { __ps_t p; f32 f[2]; }` local makes cc1 silently LEAVE PS mode** —
  no ICE, no warning, just integer `mr`/`lwz` register shuffling, 4 extra saved
  GPRs, a wrong frame, and 26% instead of 100%. §6am-190/§6ai-154 record the ICE
  and the const-fold traps; this is the third failure mode, and it is the one
  that costs a whole round because it *compiles*. **Keep PS-carrying locals
  `f32`-typed and cast only on the READ side**
  (`dst[k] = *(__ps_t *)((char *)p + 8);`) — that reads as a pair and writes as
  scalars, which is exactly what the game's `stfs`-then-`psq_l` stream is.
* **The PS *destination* declaration form decides the base register, and costs a
  whole instruction.** `extern __ps_t lbl_X[4];` + `lbl_X[k] = …` makes cc1
  materialise `lbl_X` itself (`lis r9,@ha; addi r9,r9,lo`, **2** words) and put
  every `psq_st` displacement off it. Writing the first destination as
  `*(__ps_t *)((char *)lbl_X + 8)` makes `lbl_X+8` the base instead
  (`lis r11,@ha(lbl_X+8); addi r11,@l; addi r9,r11,-8`, **3** words) — which is
  one word long and shifts every stack offset after it. A named
  `__ps_t *d = (__ps_t *)lbl_X;` is NOT enough on its own: with `*(d+1)` first,
  cc1 re-roots the web on `d+1`. **The `extern __ps_t sym[N]` form is the one that
  wins.** This is the PS/array axis of §6ek's `extern f32` vs `extern char[]`
  declaration-form lever and of §6bt2's `const`-on-a-rodata-global lever.
* **Two named local pointers can be load-bearing purely to create the base
  registers that SPLIT one stack object's accesses** — want has
  `addi r10,r1,8` / `addi r11,r1,0x18` and then uses `stfs f0,8(r1)` for the first
  lane of each 16-byte group but `8(r10)/0xc(r10)/4(r10)` for the other three, plus
  one `psq_l` off each register. With plain `a.a = f; a.b = f; …` every access
  folds into r1 displacements and the object is 8 bytes short (41%). Declaring
  `S4 *pa = &a;` and `S4 *pb = &b;` — and placing the two births either side of
  the constant load (`pa = &a; f = lbl; pb = &b;`) so the `addi`s sandwich the
  `lfs` exactly like want — reproduces it. §6bg-4 / §6ap-6 / §6cs-5 each cover a
  piece; the new part is that the pointers are *never dereferenced differently*,
  they exist only to own a base register.
* **Pointer arithmetic inside the pair read must be `(char *)p + 8`, not `p + 1`**:
  `S4 *` is 16 bytes so `p + 1` skips a whole group. 100% → 78.3% on one token
  (recipe 66's char*-cast rule, with the PS-pair stride as a new instance).
* **THIRD measured instance of the §6bx stale-`FLAG` sign flip** (after fn_8002F298
  and fn_8005896C): the inherited `// FLAG: -fno-schedule-insns` was worth
  **+2.17 points on the broken m2c body** (32.61 → 34.78) and cost **−47.83 on the
  correct one** (100 → 52.17). Re-measure every inherited flag after the
  semantic round, and treat a small inherited gain as a *symptom of the broken
  body*, never as evidence the flag is wanted.

## 6fe — 2026-10-01 single pick (0x8001BFA8, 2616B, 34.4 % → EXACT, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins): **M8.31 SCALES over a call table — a non-void return on the callee puts arg0's `li` in the LAST slot of EVERY arg-setup window (4 of 6 words differ per call)**; and **a float constant repeated in more than one arg slot folds into a CHAINED copy only when it is a C literal, not an `extern` symbol — but a one-call standalone probe picks the WRONG page-anchor colours, so model the following call too**

`fn_8001BFA8` (video/GX mode init + a 96-entry `fn_8001FFF8(group,idx,a,b,c)`
table) went 34.4 % → **EXACT** in five steps, no inline asm, no flags, no pins.

1. **Head repair (34.4 → 26.3 % with the length becoming exact).** Six missing
   callee prototypes; `fn_8001FF78` re-typed as **six `f32`** (m2c had invented
   two int args `0x80290000` and let default promotion make the rest `double`);
   a file-local typedef with `u16` at +4/+6/+8 and `u8` at +0x19 (the merged
   `Unk_5AA7B5D7` types them `s32` and has nothing at +0x19, so m2c emitted
   `lwz 0x64` for the guard); two **swapped** two-arg call sites; the ratio as
   `(f32)(f64)(u32)h8 / (f32)(f64)(u32)h6` (the game's pool constant
   `lbl_802910B8` is 0x4330000000000000, the **unsigned** 2^52 magic, so the
   operands need a `(u32)` cast or cc1 picks the signed one). Frame
   0x10 → 0x18 falls out of the conversion's 8-byte stack temp.
2. **THE LEVER (26.3 → 99.5 %): `s32 fn_8001FFF8(...)` → `void`.** m2c had
   declared the callee value-returning. With a non-void return, GCC emits
   `li r3,0` **last** in the 5-arg window (`[li r4][li r5][li r6][li r7][li r3]`)
   where want has it **first** — and because the function is a *table* of
   identical calls, this is 4 diffs × 96 calls and it was 475 of the 482
   remaining diffs. **Diagnostic signature:** the object is the exact right
   length, every `bl` lines up, and the diff is the same 4-word transposition
   inside every call's arg window. Do NOT grind store order, statement order or
   flags — run the M8.31 return-type flip first. (All 10 project flags tested
   were neutral or worse here, which is itself the tell.)
3. **Extern FP symbol → literal, for a REPEATED constant (99.5 → 100 %).** The
   first call is `fn_8001FF78(0, 0, 512.0f, 384.0f, 0, 1.0f)` with the same
   rodata value in arg slots 1, 2 and 5. With `extern f32 lbl_802910A8;` cc1
   creates **three** separate address+load webs and folds them as
   `fmr f2,f1` + `fmr f5,f1`; want has the **chained** `fmr f2,f1` +
   `fmr f5,f2`. Writing the same values as **plain C literals** gives the chain
   verbatim — an extern-symbol MEM (`(mem (hi sym) (lo_sum …))`) and a
   compiler-pool MEM (`(mem (symbol_ref))`, no address computation) fold
   differently. This is §6bg-4 / §6be-L4 ("literal vs extern is a per-CONSTANT
   decision") extended to the **FPR copy graph**, not just the anchor register.
   *Independent confirmation the source really used literals:* the game's
   `.rodata2` block `0x802910A8..0x802910BF` is **byte-identical** to the
   24-byte pool `ngccc` emits for the literal spellings — `0.0f, 512.0f,
   384.0f, 1.0f` then the 2^52 `f64` synthesised by the `(f64)u32` conversions.
   Pool order and retail order coincide, so `tools/fix_fp_pool.py` retargets the
   five HA/LO pairs to `lbl_802910A8/AC/B0/B4/B8` with no reordering.
4. **A one-call standalone probe is MISLEADING here — model the NEXT call too.**
   The isolated call gave the right FPR chain but swapped the `lis` page-anchor
   registers (`AC→r10, B0→r11`); adding the *following* int call
   `fn_8001FC94(0,0,0x200,0x180)` to the probe gave the retail colours
   (`AC→r11, B0→r10`), because the subsequent call's arg registers change
   `reload`'s preference. Same class as §6ds-2 (a pin fixes downstream colours
   by consuming a pool slot): **an NEAR whose residual is "the FPR/GPR copy or
   anchor colours in one call" must be re-measured in situ, not in a probe.**
   Corollary for `extern` forms: a named-local temp (`f32 t = K; f(t,t,…,t,…)`)
   is a no-op here — the front end copy-props it back into the symbol, and all
   5 such spellings gave a byte-identical object.

**Method note for large functions:** at 34 % with an already size-exact object,
the whole score was misaligned by the 78-instruction head, not distributed. A
single `tools/want_got.py` pass that groups the `>>>` lines into runs identified
"4 diffs per call window, 96 times" in one look and turned a 2616-byte problem
into two token edits.

## 6ff — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x800F0074, 432B, 32.7% → EXACT, 1 register-var pin, 0 emitted asm): **an object exactly ONE WORD short on an otherwise byte-perfect body = a COALESCED copy, and the fix is TWO variables, not a flag** (§6ev's 1-word-short had a different cause)

A `material-name -> "TRG"/digit` parser (two nested loops, ten calls, an 0x3E4-byte
stack string buffer). The m2c draft scored 32.7%. After the semantic rebuild the body
was **instruction-for-instruction identical to want except that the compiled object was
428B for a 432B want** — and the masked score read **28%** purely because of the index
shift. Two things came out of it.

* **The missing word was a `mr` the COALESCER deleted, and the source had spelled the
  copy as a SECOND variable.** Retail calls the 0x8012DF28 getter, tests the raw result in r3 with a record-form or, branches on zero, copies r3 into r29, materialises zero into r27, and loads the first byte through the copy, while the build tests the result directly in r29, loads the byte before materialising zero, and additionally materialises the frame address into r30.

  With one variable (`src = f(); if (src != NULL) { use src; }`) ngccc coalesces `src`
  with the call-result pseudo, drops the `mr`, emits the NULL test as `or. r29,r3,r3`
  instead of `or. r3,r3,r3` — and the object is exactly **4 bytes short**. Writing it
  as `p = f(); if (p != NULL) { src = p; … use src … }` restores both the `or.` polarity

## 6fg — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x800AEA14, 440B PS, 36.4 % → EXACT, 1 register-var pin, **1 emitted asm insn**, 0 flags): **a missing FIFTH callee-saved register (and its 8-byte frame) is diagnosed by the §6db frame arithmetic, not by the residual instruction** — and it is fixed by a nested-scope pin whose RHS is the already-materialised POINTER, not the address expression

A QB `Script*` "Model" updater: 8-pair `psq_l/psq_st` 64-byte copy, a chained
`fn_800C9780(skel)` argument, a self-targeting empty `bdnz`, and a dead
`li r30,1; xori r30,r30,1` flag pair. The inherited draft scored **36.4 %**
with a 436 B object and a header that concluded "the residual is retail's
fifth callee-saved home (`mr r27,r9`) and it is not reachable" after a large
lever sweep. It took one pin and one asm wedge.

* **A 4-byte LENGTH shortfall plus a frame 8 bytes smaller than want is a
  CALLEE-SAVED-COUNT symptom — compute it.** GOT `stwu -0x58` / `stmw r28,0x48`
  / `stw r0,0x5c` vs want `-0x60` / `stmw r27,0x4c` / `stw r0,0x64`: §6db's
  closed form `frame = round8(8 + locals + 4·nSavedGPRs)` gives 0x40 bytes of
  locals in BOTH (the `volatile __ps_t spbuf[8]` is exactly 0x40), so the
  whole 8 bytes is one missing save slot, not a mis-sized local. Retail's
  `mr r27,r9` is a stack-buffer address live ACROSS a call (`mr r4,r27` at the
  `fn_8005FD68` call), which GCC 2.95 rematerialises as `addi r4,r1,8`
  because nothing forces a callee-saved home. **Try the pin FIRST whenever the
  frame delta is exactly `4·k` for small `k` and `stmw`'s base register is the
  first one you did not expect** — no source-shape or flag work moves it.
* **Refines §6cs-2: the pin's RHS decides whether retail's `mr` copy is
  reproduced or cc1 RE-BIRTHS the value into the pinned register.** All three
  of these pin the same address to r27 and only one gives want's `mr r27,r9`:
  ```c
  register s32 spb __asm__("r27");  /* nested scope */
  spb = (s32)spbuf;   /* 80.9 % — cc1 emits `addi r27,r1,8`, a RE-BIRTH      */
  spb = (s32)sp;      /* 94.5 % — `sp` is a separate pointer var, so this is   */
                      /*          a genuine REGISTER COPY out of the store base */
  ```
  A function-scope pin instead of the nested one *also* gives the re-birth
  (that is exactly §6cs-2's "function scope emits the defining instruction
  directly into rN"). **So: a nested-scope pin is not enough — the RHS must be
  a second NAME for the already-materialised pointer, otherwise the two are
  the same pseudo and the pin binds the birth instead of the copy.** This is
  the mirror of §6ff's "an object one word short = a coalesced copy, split it
  into two variables" and of §6bt's web-identity rule: *two names, so the copy
  survives; one name, so it is folded away.*
* **The pinned STATEMENT's position inside its block is a separate lever
  (94.5 % → 98.2 %).** The block must be a nested scope that opens *after* the
  loop's setup and contains the call, with the pin assignment as its first
  statement. Placing the assignment after the `ctr` doloop leaves `mr r27,r9`
  inside the loop body (one word late, and the 2-word transposition it causes
  downstream is a pure index shift); opening the block *before* the doloop
  collapses the pin back to 4 saved registers (39.1 %). Family: §6cs-5 /
  §6an-3 (birth order), with the new part that a *hard pin* has a placement
  window of its own.
* **THE LAST 2 WORDS: an int insn on the wrong side of a `psq_l/psq_st` pair
  is a FROZEN-ness problem, and a 1-instruction `asm` (not `__volatile__`!) is
  the fix — `__volatile__` CHANGES the scheduling and loses the match.** Want
  `psq_l` → `li r30,1` → `xori r30,r30,1` → `psq_st`; every C spelling emits
  `li` → `psq_st` → `xori`. That is §6bz exactly (`movps` are TARGET_INSNs and
  float around frozen integer insns), and the dead pair cannot be moved by
  source position (3 positions, comma-expression in the copy / in the call
  arg, all 98.2 %). Exhausted at 98.2 %: `volatile` store / read / both on the
  pair, a `volatile` pointer (84.5 %), `"memory"` fences before and after,
  zero-code `+r` barriers on four different variables, opaque `"=r"`
  re-births (matched and unmatched operand), and
  `-fno-sched-interblock`/`-fno-sched-spec`/`-fno-thread-jumps` (all no-ops),
  `-fno-schedule-insns2` (87.3 %), `-fno-schedule-insns` (84.5 %). The winner:
  ```c
  flag = 1;
  __asm__("xori %0,%0,1" : "+r"(flag));        /* 100.0 % */
  __asm__ __volatile__("xori %0,%0,1" : "+r"(flag));  /* 97.3 % — DO NOT add */
  ```
  **Recorded toolchain fact worth not rediscovering: in ProDG cc1 2.95.2 /
  3.9.3, adding the explicit `__volatile__` qualifier to an otherwise
  identical `asm` with an output operand is NOT a no-op — it changed this
  function from 100.0 % to 97.3 %.** If an asm-based fix ever regresses after
  a cosmetic edit, check the `__volatile__` first. (1 emitted insn of 110 =
  0.9 %, disclosed in the draft header; the object has `.text` only, so no
  doc-14 pool caveat.)
* **Reconfirmed from the same body** (all zero-cost): `twin`-free fix chain
  for a "missing 5th saved reg" is *entirely* the pin, no flag; `while
  (--ctr != 0)` with `ctr` initialised to a literal is the self-targeting
  `li/mtctr/bdnz .` empty loop with the first `psq_l` in the delay slot
  (doc 30, no `-fno-branch-count-reg` needed); a 64-byte N-pair run is emitted
  "last statement first, then the rest in source order" from an ASCENDING
  source run (recipes 24/64/159), and the two `psq_st`s that *overwrite* slots
  of the same buffer must go through the ARRAY name (`spbuf[6]`, r1-relative)
  while the copy run goes through the pointer var (register-relative) — GCC
  keeps those two bases apart, and routing the overwrites through the pointer
  changes the offsets by 8.

## 6fg — 2026-10-01 single pick (0x801ECD84, 248B, 38.7% → EXACT, 0 emitted asm): **a
### 2-register `local_alloc` role swap is UNREACHABLE by any source shape — but a
### payload POINTER held as a single `register s32` (never a duplicate pointer
### variable) binds the colour, and a SECOND `register s32` for the pre-offset value
### splits `lwz scratch; addi pinned,scratch,K` (§6az-245 + §6an-3 composed)**

`fn_801ECD84` (`0x801ECD84`, 248 B, 5 calls, no FPRs, no opcode-4 words) went
38.7% → **100.0%** with five *semantic* fixes and **two zero-emitted hard-reg pins**.
The two recipe-worthy items:

1. **A 2-register `local_alloc` role swap between two long-lived pointer locals is
   not source-reachable; a `register s32` carrier IS.** After the semantic round the
   function was size-exact with a *single* transposition left: want homes the
   **payload** pointer in r30 and the **object** pointer in r31, ngccc gives them
   r30/r31 the other way round, and *every* source shape gave the same 17-diff
   object. Measured and all inert at 72.58%: **all 24 declaration orders** (the
   `local_alloc` order is by live-range size, not `DECL_UID`), birth order p-first
   and obj-first, `p` split into two variables, `obj` retyped as `s32`, `p` retyped
   as `char *`, plain `obj->f = 0` vs the register-recycling form, a
   function-scope `register Unk_X *obj __asm__("r31")` and a nested-scope variant
   (both *worse*, 53-58%: cc1 2.95 then double-assigns r31 to `arg0` **and** `obj`),
   and `register s32 *p __asm__("r30")` on the *pointer-typed* variable (70.97%,
   pool shifted by one: `arg0`→r31, `h`→r29, `one`→r28).
   **The winner: make the payload pointer a single `s32` register-var carrier and
   delete the pointer variable entirely** — `register s32 ps __asm__("r30");` with
   `*(s32 *)ps` / `(void *)ps` / `(char *)ps + 4` at the use sites. The crucial
   detail is that there must be **no second name for the value**: the obvious
   round-trip `p_s = (s32)p; p = (s32 *)p_s;` (which is what you write if you keep
   the typed variable) scores **7.9%** and grows the object by 4 bytes, because the
   extra pseudo defeats the pin. So this is the *dual* of §6eu-3's finding — a pin
   needs a single def pseudo — and the same reason §6az-245's "pointer pins are
   dropped" fired: the pointer-typed spelling does bind, but binds so badly here
   that it corrupts the pool. 72.58% → **96.77%**.

2. **A pinned destination absorbs the address LOAD; pin the pre-offset value too.**
   The last two words were `lwz r9,0x15bc(r29); addi r30,r9,0xc0` (want) vs
   `lwz r30,…; addi r30,r30,0xc0` (got) — the load is coalesced into the pinned
   register and the `addi` degenerates to in-place. A plain named temporary does
   **not** help (it is coalesced too, and so does the same arithmetic written as
   `ps = arg0->f + 0xC0`), and a zero-code `__asm__("" : "+r"(ps))` before the
   statement is also inert. What works is a **second, short-lived register-var for
   the raw field value**: `register s32 bs __asm__("r9"); bs = arg0->unk0x15BC;
   ps = bs + 0xC0;` → the load takes r9 and only the `addi`'s *destination* is the
   pinned r30, which is exactly want's two-insn shape. 96.77% → **100.0%**, still
   **0 emitted instructions** (two declarations, no `.long`, no `__asm__`
   statements — far inside the §4g 30% budget). This is the "name the base so a
   dependent load can pin it" lever (§6bg-4 / §6dw) crossed with §6an-3, and it is
   the cheapest way I have found to keep a *load* out of a register you already
   own. **Do it as a pair: pinning only the destination leaves the load inside it.**

3. **Semantic round that preceded both (worth re-reading the audit, not the diff):**
   the *guard's own loaded value* was arg0 of the guarded 3-arg callee
   `fn_8009F010` (`lwz r3,0x3cc(r29); cmpwi r3,0; beq; lis r4; li r5,0; ori r4; bl`
   — §72-143 again: that is also *why* the fresh load lands in r3 and not r0);
   `Mem_Alloc2(0xB8)`'s return was **not dead** and chains into
   `fn_80108F94`'s arg0 (recipe 23 / §4t) — m2c had called the allocator for
   effect and lost 2 words; and a **single named `one` written as a statement
   before that chained call** both collapsed want's two `li rA,1` into one
   `li r27,1` and created the 5th callee-saved register, which is what produced
   the exact frame (`stwu -0x20` / `stmw r27,0xc` / `stw r0,0x24`).
   Audit: `.text` 0xF8 only (no `.rodata`, no doc-14 caveat), 5/5 REL14 targets
   verified by the §6bw method, 8 REL24 call targets in want's order, 2
   ADDR16_HA/LO against a real `.data size:0x4` symbol, QB hash an unmasked
   `lis`/`ori`. Compiles warning-free.

## 6fh — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x80033904, 496B, 36.3% → 98.4% NEAR, 2 zero-emitted-asm pins, 0 flags): **WHERE the shared block STARTS decides whether you need ONE post-switch tail or the duplicated-call tail (6dp's rule inverts)**, and **a store that must land BEFORE a call whose result is discarded must not be written as a chain through it**

A 4-way QB-hash `Script*` wrapper: `ScriptInvalidateAtCache` /
`ScriptPrecache` / `ScriptPlaySequence` / `ScriptReplaceAnim`, with the last two
arms converging on one `fn_8006FB8C` tail.  Everything below is semantic; the
whole 36.3 % → 98.4 % ladder needed no flag, no barrier, no `_dummy` and **zero
emitted instructions**. The two load-bearing levers are new and both invert or
refine an existing recipe.

**1. The shared-tail form depends on the shared block's FIRST instruction, not
on the crossjumping (refines §6dp / fn_80033CFC, which is the OPPOSITE case).**
§6dp says: duplicate the call in both arms with `break;`, because a `goto` tail
moves a per-arm load into the merged block.  That holds when retail's shared
block *begins at the `bl`* (fn_80033CFC: `bl FB8C / mr r0,r3 / stw / bl / stw /
li r3,1`).  Here retail's block begins **two cheap scalar ops earlier**: the first arm loads offset 0x24 of the arg0 home and the outgoing stack slot at r1 plus eight before branching to shared address 0x80033AC0, the second arm loads the same field and the stack slot at r1 plus 0x20 and falls in, and the shared block loads offset 0x20, adds the two per-arm values, calls the FB8C helper, copies and stores its result to offset 0x1C, then calls the 0x26BF8 helper, stores that result to offset 0x28, and materialises one into r3.

so both the per-arm field/local loads and the `lwz`+`add` pair must be split
1-per-arm / 1-in-the-block.  The single source form that produces it is
**ONE block after the `switch`, reached by `break` from both arms, with the
per-arm values in two temps** (`t24 = arg0->unk0x24; t8 = sp8;` /
`t8 = sp20;`).  The `goto` tail and the duplicated-call tail both start the
merged block at the `bl`, i.e. **1–2 instructions too late**, because they
duplicate the `add`'s operands.  Measured: `goto`/duplicate = 69.6 %,
one-post-switch-block = 82.1 % once the param homes are fixed (§3 below).
**So: read want's shared block and look at its first instruction.  Cheap scalar
ops on per-arm values ⇒ one post-switch block + temps.  A call ⇒ the §6dp
duplicated form.**

**2. `x = f(g(), k);` hides a store that retail emits BEFORE `f` — split the
chain (the mirror of §6bh's "chain it" rule).** Retail calls the inner getter, copies its result from r3 to r0, materialises zero into r4, stores r0 to offset 0x20 of the object, and then calls the outer function whose result is discarded.

Writing it as `arg0->unk0x20 = f(g(), 0);` makes the store be of **`f`'s**
result, which GCC is then free to sink *past* `f` — got emitted
`bl g ; li r4,0 ; bl f ; stw r3,0x20(rN)` (one word short, everything after
shifted).  The matching source is the two-statement form
`arg0->unk0x20 = g(); f(arg0->unk0x20, 0);` (which also gets the
`mr r0,r3` for free, because `r3` is `f`'s arg register).  **Rule: chain when
r3 must flow INTO the next call (recipe 23 / §4t / §6bh); SPLIT when a store
has to land between the two calls, and the outer call's result is dead.**
Worth 1 word of length, i.e. ~15 points of masked score here.

**3. A callee that TRANSPARENTLY FORWARDS r3 must be declared 0-arg when the
call site's r3 is dead (refines §6ap-132 / recipe 119's arity audit).**
`fn_8005525C` is `stwu; mflr; stw; bl 0x800776F0; lwz r0,12(r1); mtlr; addi;
blr` — no `mr rX,r3` anywhere, and it does not *write* r3 either, so whatever
the caller had in r3 is passed straight to its inner callee.  Want calls it
with a **dead** r3 (whatever the preceding `fn_8005527C` left), and a 1-arg
prototype makes GCC materialise a spurious `lwz r3,0x20(r30)` reload that want
does not have.  The doc-10 audit says "check whether the callee reads r3";
the extra question is **"does it clobber r3 without reading it"** — if not, the
incoming r3 is forwarded and a 0-arg prototype is the correct call-site
spelling.  (Contrast `fn_8002D2A0`, which reads r3 and then overwrites it —
also 0-arg here, same net effect but a different reason.)

**4. Pin the SECOND parameter, not the first, when the two parameter homes
swap.**  The two temps above flipped the entry homes to `r31=arg0, r30=arg2`.
`register CStruct *a2 __asm__("r31"); a2 = arg2;` — a **function-scope** pin on
a copy of the *second* parameter — puts `mr r30,r3` / `mr r31,r5` back
(§6cs-2: function scope emits the defining insn straight into rN; the pointer
type binds fine because `a2 = arg2` is a single-def pseudo, §6df/§6dt).
79.8 % without it.  Pinning `arg0` instead made the frame `-0x38`/`stmw r29`
and was strictly worse.

**5. The two temps' registers are an OR, and the *consumed* operand is the one
worth pinning.**  want's `add r4, r0, r4` has `rA` = the `unk0x24` load and
`rB` = the out-param local.  Pinning the local to `r4` (so `r0` is freed for
`t24`) reaches 98.4 %; pinning `t24` to `r0` *instead* caps at 96.0 %; pinning
both is byte-identical to pinning `t8` alone.  Measure each ablation.

**Residual (2 of 124 words) and the thing to try next:** the 6th and last
`GetFloat` in the PLAYSEQUENCE arm has `li r6,1` BEFORE the `ori` that
completes `QB_SPEED`, where the five preceding windows have `ori` first.  The
6th window is structurally identical to the 5th (same callee, same flag, same
insn patterns) and all six windows live in ONE basic block, so a single sched2
pass orders all 42 arg-setup insns.  `cc1 -dr` shows the 5th and 6th windows
have the same post-reload RTL shape, so the decision is made after reload, in
the ready-list cost tie: the `ori` depends on its `lis` and the `li` does not,
so `incr_insn_cost` penalises the `ori` only when it is re-added after its

switches, `-O1/-O3/-Os`, `-mcpu=603/750`) are neutral or worse, and ~20 source
shapes are byte-identical objects (hash through a local, flag through a local,
out-param through a local, `f32[1]` out-param, declaration order both ways,
nested block, comma-chained pair, all 7 `fn_8002DEAC` args staged, base pointer

The object was already size-exact (244 B) at 37.70%, which is the §6cs-1 /
§6cs-2 tell that this is a mis-decode, not a wall.

**1. The new recipe — a nested `|` group with a constant is re-associated into
the outer chain; a named local stops it.** In the `arg5 > 1` branch retail rotates arg5 from r8 left by 0x12 and masks to 0x40000 in r0, ORs 0x30000 into that same r0, and ORs the combined term into the r3 accumulator,

i.e. the pair is ONE pseudo. Written inline as
`… | (((arg5 << 0x12) & 0x40000) | 0x30000) | …`, ngccc's constant handling
hoists the `0x30000` out of the nested or and emits **`oris r3,r3,3` into the
accumulator** plus a separate `or r3,r3,r11` for the mask — 9 accumulator steps
where want has 8, and because the branch is 22 instructions the whole block
slides. Measured equivalences, all scoring the same wrong 75.41%:
`((…) & 0x40000) + 0x30000` (folded back to `|` by `fold`), and
`0x30000 | ((…) & 0x40000)` (already the canonicalised form). **The fix is a
named local computed as a statement before the call:**
```c
s32 g;
g = ((arg5 << 0x12) & 0x40000) | 0x30000;
fp(… | g | …);                    /* 75.41% -> 100.00% */
```
**Diagnostic in one look: want has an `oris r0,rS,K` whose destination is the
SAME register a `rlwinm`/`andi.`/`andc.` just wrote — i.e. the mask and the
constant are one value — while GOT has `oris r3,r3,K` writing the ACCUMULATOR.**
That means GOT's source nested the constant into the chain; give the pair a name.
Generalises §6ey's bitfield-union and §6o-110: it is the register-identity that
tells you, and the lever is *naming the subexpression*, never reordering the
chain's terms. (Counterpart to §6ew's "named zero" trap: a named local here is
what you WANT, because want's value really is a single live value.)

**2. An m2c fn-pointer call with TWO identical-looking arguments is a phantom
second argument, and the old-style cast adds a second bug.** m2c wrote
`(*(s32 (**)())lbl_80300280)(acc, tmp)` for a call where want sets **only r3**
at `mtlr/blrl` (no `r4` write anywhere in either branch — read the whole
function, not just one site). That is the §6dx/doc-58 phantom-argument family,
but the *signature* m2c invented came from the unprototyped cast itself, and
the cast additionally emits the doc-56 **`crclr cr1eq`** (§4n: never leave an
fn-pointer call as `((s32 (*)())sym)`). `((s32 (*)(s32))lbl_80300280)(acc)`
removes both at once: no `crclr`, no `mr r4,r3`, no re-`or` to split the
accumulator. Worth checking on every m2c indirect call, and note the tell is
cheap: **count how many arg registers want writes before the `blrl`.**

**3. Hoisting the last `|` term into a named temp is an m2c tell, and inlining
it is load-bearing twice.** m2c's `temp_r9 = (arg0 << 0x19) + QB_UNKNOWN_0xC0000000`
as a pre-statement both moved the `addis r9,r9,-0x4000` to the TOP of the block
and made the value the call's second argument. Inline as the final `|` operand
and the `slwi`/`addis` land at the tail of the chain, with the `lis`/`lwz` page
anchor for the fn-pointer landing *between* them exactly as want has it.

**4. Operand ORDER in a `|` chain is readable straight off want's first `or`.**
m2c had `arg4 | (arg3 << 4) | …` and that was RIGHT: want's first or is
`or r3,r7,r3` (rA = r7 = `arg4`), not `or r3,r3,r7`. A "fix" that moves a
`|` term is a 1-word diff and it is unambiguous — check the operand slots of the
*first* or in the chain before touching the order of anything else.

**5. The stale-flag confirmation (fifth independent instance of §6bx / §6dh).**
The inherited `// FLAG: -fno-schedule-insns2` was worth 6.45% → 37.70% on the
broken m2c body and cost **72.13% → 50.82%** on the correct one; `-fno-schedule-insns`
27.87% and `-fno-gcse` 1.61% (248 B, off-by-one-word). Deleted.

Audit of the EXACT: object has only `.text` (0xF4 = 244 B = `symbols.txt
size:0xF4` = the `range=` marker) and `.rela.text` — no `.rodata`/`.data`, so no
doc-14 caveat; **0 emitted inline instructions** (the file contains no
`__asm__` and no `.long`); 3/3 branch relocations verified with the §6bw method
(2 × `R_PPC_REL14` type 11 with section-relative addends `0x88` and `0xe0`, plus
the local `b`'s `R_PPC_REL24` type 10) land on want's `bgt 0x8001E570` and
`b 0x8001E5C8`; the 4 `ADDR16_HA/LO` entries are both pairs against the real
`lbl_80300280` and are link-identical to want's `lis r11,-0x7fd0` +
`lwz r0,0x280(r11)` (0x80300000 + 0x280), so the hazard-277 masked-wrong-label
case cannot apply; no opcode-4 words, so the PS/VMX mislabel trap never applied.
Left in `src/wip`, not promoted.

## 6fj — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x8001D668, ARQ chunked-DMA helper, 256 B, 34.4 % m2c husk → **51.6 % NEAR, size-exact, 0 emitted asm, 0 pins, 1 flag**): **the masked % can FALL while the body becomes matchable; a `volatile` re-read of an already-hoisted global is how you drop a callee-saved register and un-rotate the whole map; and GCC coalesces `a = b; b = f(b);` so retail's `mr` has to be re-expressed as a recomputation**

A 34.4 % m2c draft that scored *worse* after a correct hand-rebuild, three
reusable findings, and one measurement caveat that outranks all of them.

* **CAVEAT (read this before keeping any high-scoring husk).** The inherited
  body was a **statics-DCE-style husk**: m2c declared `s32 sp8;` where retail
  has a 16 KB stack buffer, so the frame compiled `stwu -0x48` against retail's
  `-0x40a0`. That body can never match — every stack displacement and both LR
  slots are ~16 KB off. The rebuild with the correct frame scored **20.6 %, i.e.
  LOWER**, because the husk's short prologue accidentally aligned the arg-setup
  block so a few dozen `mr`/`li` words lined up. **A masked % is only evidence
  about a body whose *structure* is right; when a semantic fix lowers the score,
  keep the fix** (§6de's "object LONGER than want is itself the tell" applied to
  the frame instead of the object length). Verify with the closed form of §6db
  (`locals = stwu_N - 16 - 4·nSavedGPRs`) before believing any low score.

* **A `volatile` re-read of an already-hoisted global is a REGISTER-COUNT
  lever.** The body spins on a completion flag: `lbl = 0; ARQPostRequest(...);
  if (lbl == 0) do {} while (lbl == 0);`. Two `lis` of the same symbol is what
  retail emits — one in the outer loop preheader (r21), one in the *spin* loop's
  preheader (r9, **caller-saved**). Plain C hoists the second one all the way
  out of both loops and gives it a callee-saved register, so 14 registers are
  saved instead of 13 — and because the local hard-reg pool is positional
  (§6ds-2), that one extra saved register **rotated the entire callee-saved map
  by one** and every colour in the function was wrong. Writing the *inner* read
  as `*(volatile s32 *)&lbl == 0` blocks the address CSE for that read alone:
  the anchor stays in the spin preheader, lands in r9, and the save count drops
  to 13 → `stmw r19, 0x406c` matches and the whole allocation un-rotates
  (50 → 52 diffs, but the prologue goes 0/4 → 4/4 and the masked % recovers
  later). **Diagnostic: "everything is one register off, and `stmw` starts one
  lower than want" ⇒ count the saved registers before touching anything else;
  a `volatile` re-read is the cheapest way to give a hoisted anchor back to a
  caller-saved register.** Side effect to know: the volatile read also makes
  ngccc reserve 8 extra bytes of frame, so the array's `sizeof` has to be
  declared 8 smaller to keep the closed-form frame (§6fa's step function).

* **`a = b; b = f(b);` — GCC coalesces and DROPS the copy.** Retail keeps
  `add r30, r28, r29 ; mr r26, r30 ; addi r30, r30, 0x1f ; rlwinm r30, r30`:
  the sum is born in a register, copied, and then rounded *in place*. Every
  C spelling of that (two variables, the copy inside a branch per §6ff) still
  emitted only 3 instructions and the object came out 4 B short, which by
  §6cs-1 makes the rest of the function's score meaningless. **Fix: express the
  second value as a RECOMPUTATION from the same cheap operands**
  (`raw = chunk + off;` twice) — semantically identical, and it restores the
  64th instruction so the length is exact again (43 → and then the flag took it
  to 31/64). Length-first beats shape-first when a copy is the only thing
  missing.

* **CONFIRMED INERT here (so the next agent does not grind them):** local
  declaration order (6 permutations, byte-identical — unlike §6ec), hard-reg
  pins on values with 2-3 defs (silently dropped, §6cw/§7a-137) *and* on the
  single-def ones (they bind but cascade nothing, 32-46 diffs), the raw/rounding
  statement position (7 positions, 31-52), `-fno-gcse` /
  `-fno-sched-interblock` / `-fno-schedule-insns2` /
  `-fno-expensive-optimizations` / `-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop` (all no-ops).
  **Load-bearing:** `-fno-schedule-insns` (43 → 31) and the `volatile` spin read.
  A `>`-spelled chunk test (`if (count > 0x3FFF) chunk = 0x4000 - off;`) and
  both ternary forms flip retail's `bgt` to `ble` and cost ~6 diffs, so the
  `if (count <= 0x3FFF) chunk = count;` pre-init form is *required*, not
  stylistic. A 1-insn `asm("mr %0,%1")` copy wedge does not even compile:
  cc1 rejects a `register` declaration after a statement inside a loop body
  (§6cq). Residual is a pure 13-way `local_alloc` colour permutation with all
  5 REL14 and all 4 REL24 targets already matching — the §6bw audit passes, so
  nothing hidden is left behind a masked-EXACT-looking window.

## 77 — 2026-10-02 single pick: **a byte field at offset 2 of a callee-written
### word is only reachable as `(s8)*(volatile u16 *)&word`** (cc1 2.95 narrows a
### 16-bit read to the WRONG byte), and **M8.31 fires on a callee whose result is
### discarded at every call site** — but only when the two call sites share a zero
### web (fn_8016F69C, 40.2% → 92.78% NEAR, 388B, 1 hard-reg pin, 0 emitted asm)

A QB `Script*` wrapper: two `GetChecksum_2` out-param inits, `ContainsFlag`, a
`GetInteger` + byte/word/halfword field split, an optional `SKY` re-read, two
more `GetInteger` calls, then a 3-store copy into a 16-byte out-param block and an
8-arg call. **All seven residual words are two sched1 transpositions (parked);
everything else is byte-identical.** Four findings, in the order they paid.

* **THE BYTE-FIELD TRAP (biggest single fix, 67.0% → 69.1% on its own, and it is
  the only reason the `lbz`/`lhz`/`lwz` triple matches at all).** Retail splits
  a callee-written `u32` at `0x20(r1)` into three byte stores: the top byte is reloaded from offset 0x23, the whole word is reloaded from offset 0x20 and shifted right by eight before storing one byte to offset 0x19, then a halfword is reloaded from offset 0x20 and stored to offset 0x1A, and finally the whole word is reloaded from offset 0x20 and stored to offset 0x18,
  i.e. byte 0 of the word is copied with a **halfword** load. cc1 2.95.2 has a
  narrowing bug on exactly this shape: for `x.unk0x2 = (s8)(u16)w;` where
  `unk0x2` is an `s8` **member**, it folds `(u16)w` to a **byte** load and reads
  byte **3** (`lbz 0x23`) instead of byte 0. Measured in isolation:
  `(s8)(u16)w` → `lbz 0x23`; a staged `u16 t = *(u16*)&w; x.unk0x2 = (s8)t;` →
  `lhz 0x22` (the promoted sibling's spelling, still wrong base); a
  `volatile`-qualified **u16 lvalue** → `lhz 0x20` ✓. General rule:
  **`volatile` on the LOAD is the only lever that pins a load's WIDTH in cc1**
  (extends §6cc-2 from "byte vs word" to "halfword vs byte", and the cast at
  the consumer is a scheduler hint, not a mode constraint). C89-legal reading:
  the word was written by an unknown callee through a pointer, so the re-read is
  volatile. The other two lanes need nothing — `*((u8 *)&x) = *((u8 *)&w + 3);`
  and `x.unk0x1 = (s8)(w >> 8U);` are already exact (and the `>> 8U` vs `>> 8`
  unsignedness matters: the signed shift folds the mask).
* **M8.31 ON A CALLEE WHOSE RESULT IS DISCARDED — and the precondition that makes
  it work is a SHARED ZERO WEB, not the return type alone (67.0% → 92.8%).**
  Both `GetChecksum_2` calls discard their result (`void` in m2c's draft), yet
  declaring it `s32` moved `mr r3,r31` from the LAST slot of the arg window to
  the FIRST — worth 5 of the 7 residual words and the whole prologue ordering.
  The reason it is *not* the usual "the return is live" story: both call sites
  read the SAME callee-saved register as the value they just stored
  (`li r30,0` once at function top, `stw r30,0x18` then `stw r30,0x1c`), so with
  `void` GCC folds both zeroes onto the neighbouring zero and hands the shared web
  a different register. **Try the return-type flip on a discarded-return callee
  whose call sites share a constant web — the flip is worth far more than the
  one `mr` it moves, because it un-folds the shared web too.** (Same flip on
  `GetInteger`, whose result IS tested, is inert: 92.78% either way.)
* **m2c's three separate out-param scalars are ONE array, and the array is what
  sizes the frame AND keeps a provably-dead store alive (59.8% → 67.0%).**
  Retail's block at `r1+0x8..0x17` is `[0]=sp34 (dead), [1]=unused,
  [2]=colour word, [3]=colour word`; m2c had `s32 sp8; s32 sp10; s32 sp14;` and
  passed only `&sp8`/`&sp14`, so (a) ngccc sized the frame from three 4-byte
  objects (0x48 vs want's 0x50, every stack displacement off by 8) and (b) with
  the other two not address-taken the callee could not reach them, so
  `stw r34,0x8(r1)` was DCE'd. One `s32 sp8[4];` fixes both. This is §6fa's
  scalar→struct merge in its array form, and it is the cheapest instance of
  §6db's frame arithmetic: the closed form gave the 16-byte region, the array
  is the only spelling that lands it at `r1+0x8`.
* **PARK (documented so it is not re-grounded): 7 of 97 words, both clusters are
  one swapped pair and the post-reload RTL already agrees with GOT, so it is
  post-front-end.** (A) `addi r5,r1,0x18` vs `stw r30,0x18(r1)` in the FIRST
  `GetChecksum_2` window — the *identical* construct at the second call is
  correct in both, so it is a one-instruction tie-break, and every C spelling
  that puts the address first also moves `li r6,0` out of its slot. (B) the
  `sp8[3]` store is the head of a 3-store run in want and the tail of it in got
  (6 words of index shift). Exhausted: 13 flags, 6 statement/comma shapes for
  (A), 6 orderings + 4 comma/nested-block/hoist shapes for (B), 4 zero-code
  memory fences (all 74–85%), 4 declaration permutations, a 6-way
  prototype/param-type matrix — **all byte-identical 92.78% or worse.** Full
  lever log with every score is in the draft header, together with the two
  1-instruction `asm` births that are the only untried route.

## 6fj — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x80066834, 340B, 34.4% → **95.3% NEAR, size-exact, 1 emitted asm insn, 1 flag, 0 pins**): **the shared `/tmp/leaf` scoring path makes an EXPERIMENT LADDER silently non-reproducible — set `LEAF_TMPDIR` per agent**; and **`x*12` must be spelled shift-add or it folds to one `mulli`**

* **HAZARD, and the most expensive one in the project: `gen_leaves.compile_fn`
  writes the body to a FIXED path `$LEAF_TMPDIR/fn_<ADDR>.c` and reads
  `$LEAF_TMPDIR/fn_<ADDR>.o` back. The default is `/tmp/leaf`, which EVERY
  agent in a multi-agent session shares.** A concurrent whole-`src/wip` sweep
  (or another single-address sweep) compiles *its* draft into that same path;
  your next `test_wip_drafts.py` / `want_got.py` run then reads the other
  function's object while believing it is yours, and returns a
  deterministic-looking verdict for your source. Measured here: **the identical
  source scored 91.76% on one run and 69.41% on the next**, and two different
  ladder rows "measured" the same score because the race was swamping them.
  **Always `export LEAF_TMPDIR=/tmp/opencode/<yourdir>` before any scoring
  tool**, and **re-measure the whole ladder** once you notice it: `test_wip_drafts`
  and `want_got.py` are only meaningful relative to a private path. §6bc-278
  covers parallel *variants inside one search* (protect the input file too — name
  each candidate by a hash of its own order); this is the parallel-*agents* form
  and it is strictly worse, because it corrupts the baseline every experiment is
  measured against and nothing in the output looks wrong.
* **`arg2 * 0xC` folds to ONE `mulli`; only `((arg2 << 1) + arg2) << 2` gives
  retail's `slwi r3,r29,1 / add r3,r3,r29 / slwi r3,r3,2`** (100% of this
  function's residual improvement: 26.5% → 63.5% at the point it landed, and it
  restores the object to size-exact after the latch edit takes 8 bytes out).
  `x*3*4`, `x*12`, `x*2+x` and `(x+x)*2` all strength-reduce to the same
  `mulli` — the front end canonicalises the whole product before `loop.c`/iv.c
  ever sees it, so *every* C spelling that lets it see the product at once is a
  dead end. This is the **arithmetic-side twin of §6db/§6dv's "don't let the
  compiler fold the address math"**: put the shifts in the source so there is
  no multiply left to fold. Corollary for the 2-insn `slwi/add` that wants
  `add rD,rS,rS`: the first half also needs the explicit `<< 1` (`x+x` folds to
  `add rD,rS,rS` only after the shift form survives).
* **A `volatile` asm freezes an insn against a `call` (a call is a full
  barrier), so it DOES reach "GOT hoists a cheap `addi` above a `bl`" — but it
  pays for it in the ENTRY BLOCK.** `__asm__ __volatile__("addi %0,%1,-1" :
  "=r"(var_r27) : "r"(arg2))` in place of `var_r27 = arg2 - 1;` fixed that
  2-word transposition outright (non-volatile: no help; `volatile`: fixed),
  and simultaneously rotated the prologue from want's
  `mr r31,arg0 / mr r29,arg2 / mr r30,arg1` to
  `mr r31,arg0 / mr r30,arg1 / mr r29,arg2` — `expand_prologue` emits parm home
  copies in **first-reference order**, and the asm changes the entry insn list.
  A straight 2-for-2 trade, and **no hard-reg pin reaches it**: pins on a copy
  of arg1 (r30) and of arg2 (r29) are both inert, and pinning both gives 5
  saved registers and 10.5% (§6bh-1's "pin a copy of the parm" does not apply
  to a parm-home *copy*; cc1 drops the pin). Worth knowing as a price tag: a
  volatile asm is the right tool for a body transposition whose cause is a
  `call`-relative hoist, but budget for one entry-block swap.
* **The wall this function parks on, for the do-not-re-grind list:** both
  residual pairs are want emitting the **more expensive** insn first where
  `sched2`'s cheapest-ready-first tie-break puts the cheap one first
  (`bl`+`addi`, `lfs`+`lwz`). `cc1 -dj` shows the POST-RELOAD RTL is already in
  want's order in both windows, and every lever is inert or worse: 20+ flags
  (`-fno-schedule-insns` is required for the other 81 words, `-fno-schedule-
  insns2` on top is 81.2%), source order at 6+ positions, `volatile` on both
  sides of each pair, `memory` fences, zero-code `"+r"`/`"+f"` barriers,
  1-insn asm for the `addi` and for the `lfs` (volatile and not), a dedicated
  reload variable for the store after the `lfs` (CSE'd straight back), and a
  non-coalescable address form for the `stfs` (does not remove the dead
  `mr r3,r31`). Same class as §6do's COND_EXPR `li`-before-`cmpwi` and §6ec's
  1-user `lis` above a 0-user volatile store: **a `sched2` cost tie, not an
  ordering choice** — if the post-reload RTL already matches and every diff in
  a window is an adjacent *permutation* of instructions with different costs,
  stop permuting source.

Audit of the 95.3% body: object has only `.text` (0x154 = 340B =
`symbols.txt size:0x154` = the `range=` marker) and `.rela.text` — no
`.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss`, so masked-EXACT would also be promote-clean (no
doc-14 pool caveat); **1 emitted instruction of 85** (the hard-pinned
`lis %0,%1@ha` anchor, §6ds2/§6br) plus 1 `register`-attribute declaration and
2 `volatile` lvalue casts (0 insns); 2/2 `R_PPC_REL14` addends (readelf prints
them HEX: `.text+0x84` → 0x800668B8, `.text+0x6c` → 0x800668A0) and 7/7

## 6fk — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x8000EE70, 668B, 37.8% → **84.4% NEAR, size-exact, 0 emitted insns, 0 flags, 0 pins**): **the frame-closed form extends to FPR frames and couples the locals size to the callee-saved REGISTER COUNT — so "tune the buffer until the frame matches" is the wrong axis; get the count right and the buffer follows.** Plus a zero-code barrier variant on a *memory lvalue*.

* **The full closed form (extends §6db, which is GPR-only).** For these
  ProDG frames
  `frame = 8 (sp) + locals + 4*nSavedGPRs + 4 (LR) + 8*nSavedFPRs`, and the
  save area starts at `8 + locals` (the `stmw`/`stw` offset; LR at
  `+4*nSavedGPRs` from there). Worked example: want `stwu r1,-0xe0(r1)`,
  `stmw r23,0xac(r1)`, `stfd f30,0xd0(r1)` ⇒ `0xe0 - 8 - 4*9 - 4 - 8*2 = 0xA0`
  bytes of locals, with the buffer at `r1+8` and the `lbl_802FFE54`-era
  conversion slot at `0xA0/0xA4`. **The 4 unused bytes at `0xA8..0xAB` are not a
  dead local** — they are the 8-alignment padding ngccc inserts before the
  FPR save area once the GPR count is odd, so the `stmw` offset (0xac) and the
  frame (0xe0) are *both* consequences of `nSavedGPRs = 9`.
  **Diagnostic that makes the whole thing legible in one comparison:** when a
  `char buf[N]` sweep produces a *correct* frame with the *wrong* number of
  callee-saved registers — and the compiler-synthesised DFmode temp lands at
  `0xA8` instead of `0xA0` — then the buffer is 4 bytes too BIG, not too
  small. `sp8[0x9C]` gave frame `0xE0` with 8 saved GPRs; `sp8[0x98]` gave the
  right locals region with frame `0xD8`; **`sp8[0x98]` + the 9th register gives
  want exactly.** Do NOT chase the frame with `_dummy`/pad/array-size levers
  while a register-count deficit is visible in the `stmw` span — they fight
  each other (a 4-byte `s32` pad is DCE'd, a `double` pad lands at slot 8, and
  §6dt's `"m"`-pinned `double` is the only pad that survives without stealing
  a slot).
* **A zero-code `__asm__("" : "+r"(LVALUE))` is the length-preserving way to
  keep a call-result copy that GCC would coalesce away.** §6ff fixes a deleted
  copy with *two variables*; that works when the value is later tested. When
  the result feeds a single store and nothing else, every two-variable and
  temp spelling still coalesces (measured: 664 B object = 1 word SHORT, 48.2%),
  and a `"+r"` barrier on a *temp* is worse (660 B). Putting the barrier on the
  **memory lvalue** —
  ```c
  arg0->unk0x114 = f(...);
  __asm__("" : "+r"(arg0->unk0x114));   /* 0 instructions */
  ```
  — makes GCC re-emit the store instead of forwarding r3 straight into it,
  which restores the exact length (668 B) and buys the `mr`/web-split that want
  has. Semantically a no-op (the same value is written twice); the residual
  cosmetic cost is that the copy appears as a duplicate `stw` rather than
  want's `mr r0,r3` + one `stw`. **Do NOT reach for it before the arity is
  right**: with the old-style prototype the barrier is worth nothing (81.4%
  either way) — the 3-arg prototype has to kill the `crclr cr1eq` first
  (§6di per-call-site arity), and only then does the barrier pay (+3.0).
* **The new wall this exposes, recorded so it is not re-grounded: a
  rematerialisable HI16 reload that want hoists into a callee-saved register
  and ngccc rematerialises at its use.** Here want saves NINE callee-saved

  promoted ctor's source.** `src/fn_801252BC.c` (52 B, promoted, byte-identical)
  already contains the exact layout as a *file-local* struct:
  ```c
  typedef struct { u32 a:8; u32 b:1; u32 c:7; u32 d:16;
                   s32 unk0x04; s32 unk0x08; s32 unk0x0C; } T252BC;
  ```

  once, and it is the cheapest oracle in the project — one `rg` away, and it
  carries the game's *field names* (not just offsets). §6dc says the promoted

  the right neighbour** — it is the one promoted file guaranteed to encode every
  field view, because it initialises all of them.

## 6fm — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x801CDA44, 292B, 31.5 % → **EXACT in ONE experiment**, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins): **when a promoted sibling contains a `static __inline__` helper, port the helper VERBATIM — its LOCAL DECLARATIONS are load-bearing twice (they size the frame and they create the FPR web split) — and let it be inlined 3×, because the merged-pair + separate-`bso`-copy layout in the want is exactly what that produces**

`fn_801CDA44` (a QB `Script*` wait-time getter) went from a 31.5 % m2c draft to
byte-exact in one build, with **zero** codegen levers, because
`src/fn_801147F8.c` (`ScriptWait`, promoted, byte-identical, 0x80 KB away) already
contains the game's whole idiom.

* **Cheapest twin key for the "unsigned clamp" conversion family: the `xoris`
  marker.** `grep -rln "0x80000000" src/*.c` listed 20 promoted files in one
  command and immediately surfaced the right one. The want's tail is
  `fsub / fctiwz / stfd / lwz / xoris r3,r3,0x8000`, and ScriptWait's promoted
  source spells it as a `static __inline__ s32 wait_unsigned(f32 value)`
  helper. Callee-set and size keys (§6dc) both work too, but this one is a
  single `grep` with no address arithmetic and it never returns a
  *false* twin, because the helper's body is a distinctive instruction
  sequence rather than a shape.

* **Port the helper's LOCALS, not just its logic.** ScriptWait's helper is
  `f32 temp_f13; f64 threshold; s32 result;` before the compare, and all three
  declarations are load-bearing:
  `temp_f13 = value;` is what produces want's `fmr f13, f0` after the `fmuls`
  (a *second name* for the product — §6cw / §6an-3 / §6bt web identity: without
  the copy GCC coalesces the multiply result straight into the compared pseudo);
  `f64 threshold;` gives the `lfd` a home and makes the compare
  `fcmpu cr0, f13, f12`; and together with the caller's `f32 sp8` plus
  cc1's own DF convert temp they fill the 28-byte locals region
  (`stw r31,0x24(r1)` ⇒ locals = 0x24−8 = 0x1C, frame −0x28) with **no
  `volatile double _dummy`, no pad array and no frame arithmetic at all**.
  Writing the same logic as a macro, or hand-inlining it, loses the frame and the
  FPR colour simultaneously — so **when you port a helper, copy its declaration
  block verbatim, even if a given local looks unused.**

* **Inlining it 3× is the POINT, and it is what produces the want's two
  different branch forms.** The three call sites are
  `return wait_unsigned(sp8 * C_sec);` / `return wait_unsigned(sp8 * C_frm);`
  / `return wait_unsigned(sp8);`. GCC 2.95 then crossjump-merges the two
  *multiply* paths into one shared block that the frames arm reaches with an
  explicit `b` back into it, while the third (no-multiply) arm keeps its OWN
  copy of the compare in the `cror cr0un,cr0eq,cr0gt; bso` form
  (§6av-207's `if (f >= K) {slow}` shape) and the merged copy uses
  `bns` + a second `b` (§6ai-156's `!(a >= b)` shape). All three appear in
  retail's stream. **Do not try to unify the three returns into one** — that is
  the single most tempting wrong move here, and it is what an earlier
  hand-rebuild would have done. The same construct in one function gives you
  BOTH branch polarities, which is otherwise hard to coax.

* **Do not "fix" `fcmpu` against an `lfd`-loaded double.** Want compares an
  **f32 in an FPR** with the **high half** of an `lfd`-loaded `f64` and
  `fsub`s the same pair: `fcmpu cr0, f13, f12` / `fsub f0, f13, f12`. That is
  GCC 2.95 lowering `(f64)f32 >= f64` with no SF→DF conversion — a real game bug,
  faithfully reproduced. Casting the left side to `f32` (or making `threshold`
  an `f32`) changes the load and breaks the match. The source must keep
  `(f64)temp_f13 >= threshold` with `threshold` an `f64`.

* **m2c renders the CR condition as a constant, so BOTH return blocks DCE and
  the object comes out ~25 % short** (216 B for a 292 B want) with a
  `0;` stub and `if (0 != 0) { goto block_10; } goto block_9;`. This is §6eh's
  pathology in a different costume: there the whole block vanished behind
  `if (0)`, here it vanishes behind the two return labels. **An object short by
  a round ~76 B with the right instruction kinds elsewhere is a lost control
  block, not a codegen problem** — look for m2c's `if (0)` / bare `goto` /
  `0;` triple before touching a pin.

* Arity/scaffolding, all standard and all needed: `mr r31, r4` in the prologue
  is the hidden unused leading `arg0` with the real object in `arg1` (recipe 54
  / §6y-127), and m2c had swapped the two parameter types; `GetFloat` is
  **4-arg** `s32 GetFloat(CStruct *, s32, f32 *, s32)` and m2c invented a 5th
  `0x802B0000` argument that cost a whole `lis`/`ori` pair. The 4 QB hashes
  (`QB_SECONDS`/`QB_SECOND`/`QB_FRAMES`/`QB_FRAME`) were already correct in
  the draft header and are plain `lis`/`ori` immediates, so the 100 % byte-
  verifies them (no mask involved).

**Audit of the EXACT** (left in `src/wip`, not promoted): object has only `.text`
(0x124 = 292 B = `symbols.txt size:0x124` = the `range=` marker) and
`.rela.text` — no `.rodata`, so masked-EXACT is also promote-clean (no doc-14
pool caveat); **0 emitted inline instructions** (the file contains no `__asm__`
and no `.long`); **9/9 intra-function branch relocations** verified with the
§6bw method (6 × `R_PPC_REL14` type 11 with section-relative hex addends

0x801CDB14/0x801CDB40, plus 3 local `b`'s `R_PPC_REL24` type 10 at
`.text+0xFC/0x70/0x110`) — all equal want's decoded targets; the 5 call

all 5 `ADDR16_HA/LO` pairs hand-decoded from want's `lis -0x7fd5` +
`lfs/lfd -0x2d3C/-0x2d38/-0x2d30/-0x2d28` as 0x802AD2C4 / 0x802AD2C8 /
0x802AD2D0 / 0x802AD2D8, every one a real `symbols.txt` `data:float`/`data:double`
entry, so the hazard-277 masked-wrong-label case cannot apply. **No opcode-4
words** (all-scalar float: `fcmpu`/`cror`/`fmuls`/`fsub`/`fctiwz`/`stfd`/`lfs`/

mislabel trap applied. `// family=m2c` retained so the sweep keeps scoring it.

`fn_80016B50` (0x80016B50–0x80016C70, 288 B) and `fn_80016C70` (0x80016C70–
0x80016D58, 232 B) are the *same* 3-call GX wrapper on the *same* data, the first

  that applies to an **adjacent, already-solved** draft. The detection is one
  arithmetic step, no scanner: subtract your own size from your address (the
  `range=0xS-0xE size=NB` marker is in your header) and
  `ls src/wip/fn_<that>.c src/fn_<that>.c` — also worth trying `+size` for the
  following function. If the file's header contains a `STATUS …: **EXACT` line,
  **port its recipe immediately**; that is a much higher prior than any scanner
  hit. The exception is safe precisely because it is *gated on the STATUS line*,
  not on the file merely existing — which is the exact failure mode §6be-1 warns

## 6fo — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x801232EC, 188B, 25.5 % → EXACT, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins): **WANT'S register reuse tells you which SYMBOL SPELLING the source used for a field that is ALSO its own `lbl_` — and a second `base+OFFSET` address web steals a callee-saved register and grows the frame by 8**

`fn_801232EC` (an `AUDSimple*Exit`-shaped audio-decode shutdown: a `"NONE"`
state guard, `OSDisableInterrupts`, 2× `AXSetVoiceState`/`AXFreeVoice` on a
2-entry voice-pointer array, two indirect callbacks) was 100 % semantics. The
m2c draft had five **implicit** SDK callees (5 spurious `crclr cr1eq`, doc-56 /
§4n) and the guard spelled as `*(s32 *)((char *)lbl_8039BA58 + 0xA0)`. Adding
the prototypes took 25.5 → 18.75 % (the crclrs went but the body was still
wrong), and the real fix is below.

* **The tell: want folds the guard's offset into the load AND reuses that base
  register later, so the source reached the field through the OBJECT, not
  through its own symbol.** Want is
  `lis r9,page / addi r31,r9,-0x45a8 / lwz r9,0xa0(r31) / cmpw` — r31 =
  0x8039BA58 and the +0xA0 stays a plain displacement. `lbl_8039BAF8` (the
  field's own symbol) exists in `symbols.txt` and the *promoted address-adjacent
  sibling* `src/fn_801233A8.c` legitimately uses it, so both spellings exist in
  the game. Writing the guard as a bare offset expression made cc1 build a
  SECOND address web for `base+0xA0` (`addi r28,r9,0xa0`) that then had to be
  materialised in a **callee-saved register** — 2 saved GPRs instead of 1 and
  frame 0x20 instead of 0x18. A named base fixed both at once:
  ```c
  typedef struct { char pad0[4]; void *unk4; char pad8[0x98]; s32 unkA0; } CB_t;
  CB_t *cb = (CB_t *)lbl_8039BA58;     /* declared at FUNCTION top, before the guard */
  if (cb->unkA0 != 0x4E4F4E45) { ... ((void (*)(s32))cb->unk4)(*(s32 *)&lbl_8039BE6C); ... }
  ```
  One `addi r31,<base>` + `lwz 0xa0(r31)` for the guard and `lwz r11,4(r31)` for
  the tail callback pointer — 1 saved GPR, frame 0x18, want's `r28` = the
  `OSDisableInterrupts` result and nothing else. 18.75 → **100.0 %**.
  **Diagnose it in one comparison: `addi baseReg,page` + `lwz rX,OFF(baseReg)`
  (one HI16, offset in the load) ⇒ write the field as a member of the base
  object; a SECOND `addi baseReg,OFF` or a `lwz` off a fresh anchor ⇒ the
  source used the standalone symbol.** Same family as §6bg-4 / §6dw ("name the
  base so a dependent load can pin it") and §6dx/§6dc ("promoted neighbours are
  the type oracle"), with a new *symptom*: the giveaway is a **+1 callee-saved
  register and an +8 frame** from a base-relative field access, not a colour
  diff. Per §6db/§6fk, compute the saved-GPR count before touching any frame
  lever. Note the field sits at +0xA0, i.e. **past the end** of
  `lbl_8039BA58`'s own `size:0x88` — that is fine and link-correct (the `lwz`
  needs no relocation, it is a plain displacement off a resolved base), so do
  not "fix" it by switching to the out-of-object symbol.

* **Twin-porting was the whole data half, and TWO twins were already promoted:**
  `src/fn_801358F0.c` (`AUDSimpleExitAudioDecoder`, byte-identical, 0x801358F0)
  is the *same* body without the guard and supplied the whole idiom — the `void
  **vp` array local, the `void **cb` callback struct, `AXSetVoiceState(vp[0],0)`,
  the **`vp[1] = NULL; vp[0] = NULL;`** store order (rotate-right, recipes
  24/64/159), and `((void (*)(s32))cb[1])(...)` for the indirect calls (the
  1-arg cast is what removes the `crclr`, §4n/recipe 21). `src/fn_801233A8.c`
  (the address-adjacent one) supplied the guard's `0x4E4F4E45` literal, which
  hand-decodes from want's `lis r0,0x4e4f` / `ori r0,r0,0x4e45` = `"NONE"`.
  §6fn's adjacency rule and §6dc/§6dx's "search by callee set" both apply; the
  cheap key here was `rg "AXSetVoiceState" src/` (5 promoted hits, all this
  family). Copy the sibling's **declaration block** verbatim — the arity split
  `AXSetVoiceState(void *, u16)` vs `AXSetVoiceState(s32, s32)` in the two
  promoted siblings is load-bearing only for warnings, both compile identically,
  so take whichever file you port from.

Audit: object has only `.text` (0xBC = 188 B = `symbols.txt size:0xBC` =
header `range=` span) and `.rela.text` — no `.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss`, so
masked-EXACT is also promote-clean (no doc-14 pool caveat); **0 emitted inline
instructions**; compiles warning-free; all 7 `R_PPC_REL24` targets
(`OSDisableInterrupts`, `AXRegisterCallback`, `AXSetVoiceState`×2,
`AXFreeVoice`×2, `OSRestoreInterrupts`) match want's `bl`s; the single
