## 6fp — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x8012B1C0, 224B, 25.0 % m2c → **EXACT**, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **fall-through case LABELS collapse cc1's switch b-tree — write each `case N:` with its OWN `body; break;`**; plus a **bitfield `rlwimi` store co-existing with a whole-word masked compare needs `union { FLAGS f; u32 w; }`**

A QB-object field-copy helper (`fn_80125480` lookup → byte tag at +2 → 9-way
dispatch, one arm storing `f32` and eight storing `s32` at the same offset).
25.0 % → 100.0 % with **four semantic edits and no codegen lever at all**.

**1. THE NEW RECIPE — `case A: case B: case C: <one body>` is NOT the same
switch as nine `case N: <same body>; break;` lines, and retail used the latter.**
`emit_case_nodes` (stmt.c) has a same-label collapse: when several case nodes
point at ONE label and the values are consecutive, it emits a **range check**
instead of per-value tests *and re-roots the balanced tree*. Measured on the
same 9 values `{1,2,3,4,5,6,10,12,13}`:

| source | emitted `cmpwi` sequence (in address order) |
|---|---|
| 8 fall-through labels + 1 (m2c) | `6 3 1 10 13 12` (root 6, `bge 3` for {3,4,5,6}, `cmpwi 13/bgt` + `cmpwi 12/blt` for {12,13}) |
| 9 separate `case N: body; break;` | `5 2 1 3 4 10 6 12 13` = **want exactly** |

The nine separate bodies are *textually identical* for eight of them, so
crossjumping tail-merges them afterwards into the single shared block retail
has. Two consequences to keep:
* **The b-tree root is `sorted[floor((n+1)/2) - 1]`** where `n` = number of
  **distinct labels** (verified by a probe ladder: n=8→idx 3, n=9→idx 4,
  n=10→idx 4, n=11→idx 5, n=12→idx 5). This is the flip side of the
  phantom/duplicate-case tree steering in §70-124 / §6t-6 / §6aq-193 /
  §6an-204: those ADD a node to move the pivot, this one stops a collapse that
  was re-rooting it. **Before shaping a switch tree with a phantom case,
  check whether the real cases share a label** — the fix may be to un-share
  them, not to add one.
* **Diagnostic in one comparison: want tests N values individually and routes
  them all to ONE block, but got emits a `bge`/`blt` range check.** Want's
  compiler did not collapse; our cc1 does. Separate the labels.

**2. `rlwimi` and a whole-word masked compare on the same field ⇒ a union.**
`lwz r0,0(r31); rlwinm r0,r0,0,9,0xf; cmpw r0,r9(=0xD0000)` is a **masked
compare** (SH=0 keeps the 7-bit field at bits 16..22 *in place*), while the two
stores are `rlwimi r0,r9,0x10,9,0xf` **bitfield inserts**. A bitfield READ
alone gives the wrong extract (`rlwinm r0,r0,0x10,0x19,0x1f` + `cmpwi` — a
shift to the low end); a mask/or/ori store alone gives `rlwinm`+`oris`+`or`
or a separate extract. `typedef union { struct { u32 hi:9; u32 ty:7; u32
lo:16; } f; u32 w; } H;` serves both with zero extra code: reading `.w` masks
and comparing against the literal `0xD0000` reloads it into a register
(`lis r9,0xd` with **no `ori`** — the low half is 0 so the peephole drops the
addi, §6bz's frozen-insn family), and writing `.f.ty` expands to `rlwimi`.
Sister of §6fl's "copy the promoted constructor's bitfield struct" and §6bs's
MSB-relative MB/ME arithmetic (`ty:7` after 9 bits ⇒ MB=9, ME=15).

**3. A 4-byte slot written as `f32` in one arm and `s32` in eight is a UNION
member, and typing it wrong costs a `fctiwz/stfd/lwz/stw` quadruple *and* an
8-byte frame** (`(s32)arg0->v = (f32)x` made cc1 synthesize the whole
`xoris`/`lis 0x4330`/`lfd`/`fsub`/`frsp` conversion, §6di/doc-14). m2c wrote
`*(s32 *)((char *)arg0 + 8) = (f32) ...`; the honest spelling is
`union { f32 f; s32 i; } v;` in the object struct and `o->v.f = t->v.f;` /
`o->v.i = t->v.i;` at the two arms. Same 8-byte-pool reasoning as §6fb's
"f32 to build, `__ps_t` to copy out", at union level.

**4. `*(s32*)((char*)p + 2)` for what want reads with `lbz` is a whole-function
disaster, not a one-instruction fix.** m2c's `temp_r9` was `u8` and the store
type was `s32`; cc1 then constant-propagated the per-case value, rewrote the
bitfield arithmetic as `rlwinm`+`oris` per case, and moved the byte load to
offset 5. The field is a real `u8`; a file-local `struct { char p0[2]; u8 ty;
char p3[9]; union{...} v; }` puts `lbz` at +2 and the `lfs`/`lwz` at +0xC.

**5. The object needed an explicit UNUSED 4-byte word at +4.** The flag word is
at +0 and the callee argument / stored value at +0x8; a naive
`struct { HEAD h; F32I v; }` puts `v` at +4 and every `lwz r3,8(r31)` /
`stfs f0,8(r31)` lands 4 low. Add the `s32 pad4;` (read the offsets off the
want's displacements, §6dy/§6de).

Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted): object has only `.text`
(0xE0 = 224 B = `symbols.txt size:0xE0` = the `range=` marker) and `.rela.text`
— no `.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss`, so masked-EXACT is also promote-clean (no
doc-14 pool caveat); **0 emitted inline instructions** (no `__asm__`, no
`.long`); **18/18** intra-function `R_PPC_REL14` (type 11, section-relative
addends `0xcc`×4, `0xb8`×9, `0x74`, `0xa0`, `0x60`, `0x8c`) plus the one
`R_PPC_REL24` to `fn_80125480` all resolve to want's decoded branch targets
(§6bw method); **no `ADDR16_HA/LO` relocations at all** (the only extern is a
`bl` target), so the hazard-277 masked-wrong-label case cannot apply; no
opcode-4 words (`tools/ps_disasm.py 0x8012B1C0 56` → 0 undecodable), so the
PS/VMX mislabel trap never applied. Promoteable.

## 6fq — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x80081920, 868B mesh-type hash dispatcher, m2c DIFF → **EXACT + promoted**, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins): **a `cmplw`+`ble` guard inside a compare tree is unemittable from `switch` under gcc-2.95.3 stmt.c (proven from release source) — write the dispatch as explicit if/goto, and read `beq`-target arms vs fall-through arms before "fixing" pairings**

`fn_80081920` (11 hash cases + default, one `Mem_Alloc2` + 8-arg chained call
per arm) fell in layers, each a known family: hidden dead `r6` param widening
(the §6bf slot-shift — `r6` has no home-copy, but the slot must be declared or
every later arg slides a register), chained alloc-result `r3` into each callee
(recipe 23 — m2c dropped it AND invented 4-arg `Mem_Alloc2` calls; the real
callee is 1-arg `fn_80009A44`), and the §7d-4 mixed-ABI proto reorder
(`(void*,s32×6,f32,s32)` puts the float 8th so `fmr` lands before the final
`mr r10`, byte-exact). Two findings generalise:

**1. The ble-guard wall is real and proven, not a scheduling artifact.**
Want keeps `cmplw r4,r0; ble→default` after one `beq`, while the structurally
identical singleton node two tests earlier uses bare `beq; b→default`.
gcc-2.95.3 `stmt.c` (fetched release source) shows why no switch spelling can
reach it: `emit_case_nodes` takes the guarded path only when the node's right
child is non-trivial (`right->right || right->left || low≠high`), and the
0xF4D8D486 node is a clean max-value leaf in every balancing — verified by
simulating `balance_case_nodes`, and empirically across all five in-tree ProDG
versions (all 860B, guard absent), both case orders, a degenerate range (folds
to single), and temp-form variants. The fix is §6ag-1 goto-dispatch mirroring
want's block order, with the guard as an explicit `if ((u32)x <= V) goto DEF;`
— first-try EXACT once the arms were right. When a NEAR is "one redundant
bound check away from EXACT" and every switch form ties, stop permuting cases
and port the tree to gotos.

**2. A `bne`-fallthrough test means the arm is shared layout, not a swapped
pairing — decode it before "correcting" m2c.** Want tests the last value with
`cmpw; bne→default` and falls into its arm, so the fall-through block IS that
value's arm (here SHADED→`fn_80087E18`, exactly as m2c had it). I misread it
as a swap, "fixed" it, and only the link-time `cmp` caught the error both
times: `promote_wip.py` refused with a 1-word diff (`bl fn_8008B354` vs `bl
fn_8008B994`), which decoded to the true rule — **a `bl`'s destination is
ground truth for which value an arm serves; the masked sweep cannot see it
(REL24 masked), so a masked-100% with call-heavy arms proves nothing about
pairings.** Companion trap from the same function: `want_got.py --file`
overrides `LEAF_TMPDIR` with its own `mkdtemp` (tool line 61), so a private
`LEAF_TMPDIR` does NOT isolate its object — disassembling `$LEAF_TMPDIR/*.o`
afterward reads a STALE sweep artifact (hazard-278's mirror image); compile
with `SN_NGC_PATH` + `wibo` yourself when you need the true object.

Audit of the promoted `src/fn_80081920.c`: `.text` only (0x364 = 868B),
0 asm, full linked-DOL `cmp` green via `promote_wip.py`.

## 6fq — 2026-10-29 single pick (0x80054B24, 220B, 76.4% → **EXACT and PROMOTED**, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 1 `register` pin, 1 statement swap): **pin the member of a callee-saved permutation whose want colour is NOT the head of the pool — and when two names are copy-assigned, decide which call site sees which name by STATEMENT ORDER, not by a barrier**

A 220B level-path builder (`fn_80054894` sprintf-into-buffer + a "levels\\%s\\%s.tex"
sprintf + `Script_GenerateCRC` → `fn_80054DC4` lookup + a `strcmp` against the first
buffer). A previous session had already carried it to 76.36% with seven
semantic fixes (two 0x80-byte path buffers, the BUFFER-is-arg0 call shape, two
chained results, `Script_GenerateCRC` returning a value, three dead-arg protos,
the real format-symbol reference, and two address webs for `&sp88`) and left
**13 diffs, all pure register renames** among r28/r29/r31. Both levers below are
ordinary; what is new is *predicting which pin*.

**1. Three webs, one pool, and the order is a rotation — so pin the one that has
to MOVE, not the one at the head.** The web map (read straight off `want_got`):

| web | what | want | got |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `arg0` param home (`mr rX, r3`) | r28 | r29 |
| B | `p = (… *)sp88` — the prologue `addi rX,r1,0x88` | r29 | r31 |
| C | `q = p` — the copy | r31 | r28 |
| D | `p = fn_80054DC4(…)` — reuses B's reg | r29 | r31 |

`local_alloc` drew from the pool `[r31, r29, r28]` in order `{B/D, A, C}`; want
drew `{C, B/D, A}`. A cyclic rotation of three slots over a fixed pool, so
**pin any ONE member and the other two fall into place for free** — but which
one matters enormously. Pinning **B** (`register Unk_CFB386B2 *p __asm__("r29")`,
i.e. the member whose *own* want colour is r29) removes it from the pool: C
falls to r31 and A to r28, exactly want. **76.4% → 98.2% in one edit, 0 emitted
instructions.** The full 10-variant ladder (so nobody re-derives it):

| pin | score | | pin | score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B→r29** | **98.2%** | | C→r31 (pointer) | 10.9% |
| B→r28 | 80.0% | | C→r31 (`s32` alias) | 10.9% |
| B→r31 | 74.5% | | C→r30 | 74.5% |
| B→r29 **+** C→r31 | 94.5% | | C→r28 | 76.4% (no-op) |
| | | | C→r29 | 81.8% |

Two pins are strictly WORSE than one (94.5% vs 98.2%) and pinning the *wrong*
member is catastrophic (10.9%) — this is §6ds-2 ("pin one member of a permuted
group") with a sharper rule than the note carries: **pin the member that the
rotation must displace, i.e. the one whose want colour is not the pool's first
slot. Read the three want colours, find which one is absent from the head of
the pool, pin that variable.** §6cs-2's corollary holds here: the pin's RHS is
a single-def pseudo (`p = (… *)sp88` and later `p = fn_80054DC4(…)`), so the
pointer-typed spelling binds — the `s32`-alias fallback was not needed and the
two spellings tied anyway.

**2. A copy-assignment `q = p` collapses to ONE value-numbered web, and the
pseudo with MORE USERS wins the colour — so the fix is which call site sees
which NAME, chosen by statement order.** With the pin in, exactly one diff
remained: want `mr r3, r29` for the `sprintf` destination, got `mr r3, r31`.
`q` and `p` hold the same value, the front end value-numbers them, and `q` (4
later uses) beats `p` (1 use) — so BOTH argument setups were coloured from
`q`'s pseudo, and the game clearly had two live names (want keeps
`mr r3, r29` for the sprintf *and* `mr r31, r29` for the copy). **Writing the
`sprintf` BEFORE `q = p;` is the whole fix, 98.2% → 100.0%, plain C, no
barrier:** at the call statement `q` does not exist yet, so the sprintf is
forced onto `p`'s web, while the copy still hoists to the head of the block
(`mr r31, r29` at 0x54B4C, ahead of the arg setup) because the copy is the
block's 2-user statement. Equivalent zero-instruction alternative: a
`__asm__("" : "+r"(q));` immediately before the sprintf (also 100.0%, §6du-2).
**Barriers on `p` itself are REGRESSIVE** — after the copy 96.4%, before it
87.3%, both-pins 96.4% — because they perturb the block instead of splitting
the two webs. So: *barrier on the variable you want to PROTECT is the wrong
lever when the fix is which name each call site reads; re-order first.*
Generalises §6bt web-identity and §6fg "two names, so the copy survives" from
the allocation side to the **user** side, and it is the cheapest possible
instance of §6eb's three-way statement-position rule (§6bh-3's "stage the load
before the store" was regressive here — the load and the store are the same
statement, so the rule that applies is "make the *other* name not yet live").

Audit of the promoted `src/fn_80054B24.c`: object has only `.text` (0xDC = 220B
= `symbols.txt size:0xDC` = the `range=` marker) and `.rela.text` — **no
`.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss`, so masked-EXACT is also promote-clean** (no doc-14
pool caveat); **0 emitted inline instructions** (the only `__asm__` in the file
is the `register`-attribute on `p`); both `R_PPC_REL14` (type 11) carry
section-relative addend `+0x8c` → `0x80054BB0`, which is BOTH of want's branch
targets (`bne 0x80054bb0` at 0x54B8C and `beq 0x80054bb0` at 0x54BA8) — §6bw
method; all 12 `R_PPC_REL24` targets are `fn_80054894`/`sprintf`/
`Script_GenerateCRC`/`fn_80054DC4`/`strcmp`/`fn_80055CB0`/`fn_8000A778`/
`fn_8005D7A0`/`fn_8005D734`/`fn_8005D60C`/`fn_80077088`/`fn_800562B0`, matching

`lbl_80293140` (`.rodata2`, `size:0x11 data:string` = `"levels\\%s\\%s.tex"`, also

`tools/ps_diff.py 0x80054B24` → **55/55, 0 mismatches** (no opcode-4 words, so

`ff6faeb0f2b524ecbe1aeaff78ff154a284c27c9`, `main.dol: OK`.**

Process note worth keeping: `nohup cmd &` from a tool call did **not** survive
the call returning — `promote_wip.py` was killed between the link and the
`cmp`, leaving the split registered and `build/G2TE52/main.dol` missing. Use
`setsid nohup … < /dev/null &` plus `disown` (verified: the process gets its own
SID and survives), and poll from separate short calls. Also: `pgrep -f
promote_wip.py` **self-matched the polling command line** and reported RUNNING
for a process that had already exited — match on the pid you captured from
`$!` or filter out your own `ps|grep` line, never trust a bare `pgrep -f` of the
script name you just typed.

## 6fr — 2026-10-30 (50 random unparked WIP drafts, 50 parallel
### agents): 26 EXACT + 1 LINK-SIM EXACT + 23 parked, and **three claimed
### "breakthroughs" that were FALSE** — the round's most valuable output

50 unparked drafts were handed to 50 agents (`<scratch>,
seed 20261001, stratified 25 NEAR + 13 mid-DIFF + 10 low-DIFF + 2 FAIL).
Result: **26 `EXACT 100%`**, `0x8027124C` `LINK-SIM EXACT` (128 B, SDA route),
23 parked with `// PARKED` blocks. Nothing promoted. The interesting part is
what happened when the agents' three "generalizable law" claims were checked
DOL-wide — **all three were wrong**, and two of them were also wrong in
`AGENTS.md` itself. Read this before trusting any frame-arithmetic claim.

* **The real GPR-only frame law is `frame = Gsave + 4*nSavedGPRs`, with
  `L = Gsave - 8` and the LR slot at `frame + 4` — and `L` is NOT rounded to
  a multiple of 8.** Verified by decoding every GPR-only prologue in the DOL
  (`stwu r1,-N(r1)` + `mflr r0` + `stmw rX,K`): **3807 of 4013 match** (the
  other 206 are mid-function `stwu` false positives, all with `frame == 8`).
  Two rival formulas score **0/4013 each**: `8+L+8+4n` (the old §6db form) and
  `8+round_up(L,8)+4+4n` (asserted by the `0x80075854` and `0x80232614` agents).
  Nor is there an 8-byte alignment step: **1635 of 4413** GPR-only prologues have
  `stmw` at a displacement `4 (mod 8)`, and `0x80007a4c` (L=12), `0x800093ac`,
  `0x80009b04` (L=4) all have L not 8-aligned. The agent that claimed the
  round-up law had even "probed it with 1..6 four-byte address-taken locals"
  and then computed **L = 0** for `stwu -0x20 / stmw r27,0xc / stw r0,0x24`:
  the truth is `Gsave=12`, `n=31-27+1=5`, `32 = 12 + 4*5` ✓ ⇒ **L = 4**, not 0.
  §6db has been corrected in place, and `src/wip/fn_80075854.c`'s header — whose
  *fix* (delete the stale `volatile double _dummy;`) is correct and byte-exact,
  only its justification was bogus — now carries the correction inline.
  **The `-16` form "worked" on `0x8005D60C` by coincidence**: that function's
  region is `L = 0x8C` but it declares only `0x84` of objects, so the 8-byte
  difference is *trailing padding*, and the bad form happens to return the
  declared-object size. A declared size 8 short of the region is normal — do
  not "fix" it by adding a dummy.
* **A "0 of N matched, first ones solved this round!" claim is a red flag, not
  a breakthrough.** The round reported that 108 DOL sites had a save-slot
  offset ≡ 4 (mod 8) with 0 matched, and that the first two were solved here.
  In fact **37.0% (1635 of 4413)** of all GPR-only prologues have that shape —
  it is unremarkable, and `0x80032698` (solved, EXACT) is not even one of them
  (its `stmw` is at offset 8). Two agents' "walled family" was just the
  mainstream layout. **Before writing a law into a park note, check its
  frequency in the DOL: a claim about a rare shape is usually a scan artifact,
  and `0/N matched` almost always means the shape is common and simply
  unattempted.**
* **Two genuinely reusable semantic findings did survive verification:**
  (a) **A paired-single reload's lane index must be read off the *displacement*,
  not off the store form.** `0x80035A98` reloads with `psq_l 8(r30)` where
  `r30 = r1+8`, i.e. byte offset 16 = `sp8[1]`, while its own stores are
  `psq_st 8(r1)` / `16(r1)`. The m2c draft read `sp8[0]` and produced a
  self-consistent but wrong `psq_l 0(r30)`. Confirmed by decoding the raw
  opcode-56/60 words (capstone stalls on them, §6ag-9). (b) **A loop's
  entry-guard count load and its latch count operand must be two DIFFERENT
  address webs** — `0x8011E0E4` collapsed from 43.6% to 80.3% purely by reading
  the latch bound through an alias pointer (`tr = (char *)base;` then
  `*(s32 *)((char *)tr + 0xC80)`), which breaks the CSE that otherwise
  rematerialises the load in the latch and takes down the whole callee-saved
  map. This is the address-web-splitting family (§6cb-1, §6an-3) with a new
  trigger: **a count that is read in the pre-test AND the latch.**
* **Operational note — the consolidated scorer silently drops `// FLAG:`
  lines.** A private `score_all.py` reported `0x80035A98` at 68.57% while the
  draft's own header claimed 88.57% and the authority tool confirmed **88.6%**.
  The draft was right; the scorer was wrong. **When a re-score contradicts a
  park header, re-run `tools/test_wip_drafts.py --addr 0x...` before editing
  anything** — the per-draft flag must be extracted, and a stale scorer will
  send you "fixing" a body that already matches under its own flags (§6w-105,
  §6bg).

## 6fs — 2026-10-30 (50 stratified WIP drafts) + (25, incl. the
### 6 r2 stragglers): **37 new byte-exact**, and the round's real lesson is that
### **almost every "no C spelling reproduces this" park note was wrong in ONE of
### three specific ways** — all three now have named, reusable fixes.

**Tally (authority `test_wip_drafts.py`, each draft in a private `LEAF_TMPDIR`):**

| batch | EXACT | NEAR | DIFF | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r2 (50) | **27** | 15 | 8 | incl. `0x800AC680`, which was **already EXACT** — the r2 baseline parser folded it into "DIFF" (the strata regex required a `%` on the EXACT line). Union with r3 = 38 EXACT, **37 new**, 11,732 B. |
| r3 (25) | **11** | 13 | 1 | 3 were r2 stragglers; the DIFF is `0x801B36FC` (2028 B paired-single husk). |

Nothing promoted. All changes confined to `src/wip/` (`git diff --name-only 346e0a847..HEAD | grep -v '^src/wip/'` → empty). The 13 new EXACTs were **independently re-audited** by a parent-side script (`.text` size vs `symbols.txt` vs the `range=` marker, every `R_PPC_REL14` addend resolved against want's decoded branch set, every `R_PPC_REL24` counted, extra sections listed): **13/13 size-exact, 0 branch mismatches**, 0 emitted inline asm in 12 of 13. Only `0x8003BD4C` carries an extra section — the expected 8-byte doc-14 `0x4330000080000000` int→f64 pool, retargetable by `fix_fp_pool.py` at promote time.

**The three failure modes that produced most of the 37** — each was a *semantic* fix, each had a prior park note claiming exhaustion:

1. **A `return 0` tail is reachable by flipping the `if` POLARITY, and the branch order of the merged block follows the NULL-test's predecessor edge order** (`0x801A2E88`, 80.5% → EXACT, one edit). A prior session had parked it as a `flow.c reorder_blocks` / `can_fall_through` "block-layout wall" with a `cc1 -dr` dump as evidence. The dump *did* show both `li r3,0` tails in source order — the misreading was that the dump settles the block question at all. What actually picks the survivor is **crossjumping MERGING the two identical tails**, and which one survives (hence where the merged block lands) is decided by the predecessor edge order of the NULL-test block, which the `if` polarity controls. Inverting `if (o1 == NULL) { ...; return vt(...); } return 0;` into `if (o1 != NULL) { ...; return vt(...); } return 0;` makes the ret0 a *fall-through* edge and the block lands inline. Same instruction multiset, same 164 B. **Generalises §4p-10 / §6an-2 (branch polarity) from "which side is inline" to "where does a crossjump-merged block land".** The oracle was the promoted sibling `src/fn_801A2D90.c`, whose own ret0 is inline — a promoted neighbour is a **block-layout** oracle, not just a type/arity oracle (§6dc/§6dr/§6fn).

2. **The crossjump-merge of a shared `return 1` block is controlled by whether you write four `return 1`s or ONE shared label** (`0x8003BD4C`, DIFF/~0% → EXACT; the label was worth **69 points on its own**). With four textual `return 1`s, cc1 crossjump-merged the two *`fn_80062528` calls* into one shared `bl` at the function end; want keeps two `bl`s and shares only the `li r3,1; b epi` block that sits immediately after the **first** call. A single `ret1:` label placed right after that first call reproduces want exactly. **This is §6dp/§6be run in reverse: those duplicate a call to ENABLE a merge; here duplicating the *returns* DISABLES a merge you don't want, and the shared label at want's position is the merge you do want.**

3. **A "shared-exit ret block" that want places MID-function is reachable by putting the label inside the first if-body with explicit gotos** (`0x800EB67C` 88.7% → EXACT, two statement-order edits, 0 levers). The other 14 words there were the *flag-init position* per arm: a flag assigned 0 **after** the call it guards dies immediately and stays in a scratch; the **same function's own site 1** (already byte-exact) spelled it after, and the m2c draft had sites 2 and 3 before — which makes the `li` hoist to the block top, keeps the flag live across two `bl`s, and forces a callee-saved home. **The function's own already-matching site is the cheapest oracle in the project; read it before writing a lever ladder.** Second fix there: after `Mem_Free(walker)`, want's `= NULL` lands in the walker's own dead register — an in-place `walker = 0; arg0->f = walker;` (a semantic no-op) rather than a fresh `= NULL`, because a fresh 1-use pseudo gets its own colour (§6fg web identity). Both the named-zero local and a hard r30 pin measured **inert** (97.48%): only in-place worked, so the pin was not the lever.

**Other reusable findings from the 37 (all verified on a byte-exact result):**

* **A comma expression in the loop CONDITION with the store folded into it emits compare-BEFORE-store** — the mirror of recipe 128 / §6ep2-3, which move a store *earlier*; this one moves it *later*, behind the `cmpw` (`0x800615D0`, 88.4% → EXACT). `if ((sp10 = cur, (s32)cur != h)) goto body;` — 95.4% → 100% on its own.
* **A `const` qualifier on a rodata2 FLOAT's declaration is an alias-oracle lever** (`0x80212B18`, 86.1% → EXACT): `extern const f32 lbl_…;` tells reload that nothing writes it, so a neighbouring store stops being an alias barrier and the `lis`/`lfs` pair separates the way want has it (§6bt2, second independent instance).
* **A stale `volatile` QUALIFIER — not just a stale FLAG/pin/barrier — can be compensating for a semantic bug** (`0x800A8D04`, 81.6% → EXACT). The inherited `volatile __ps_t t[4]` existed to stop cc1 DCE-ing the duplicate pair stores; once the two real bugs were fixed (a 4-byte object where want needs an 8-byte one to land on the aligned slot, and a scalar-written/pair-read field that needs a `union { f32 f; __ps_t p; }` — the game's own idiom, confirmed by the promoted byte-identical sibling `src/fn_800A08C0.c`), the stores became real code and plain `__ps_t t[4]` matched. **Add `volatile` to the §6aq-222 stale-scaffolding list.**
* **A promoted sibling found by address-adjacency (§6fn) is the fastest oracle, and it generalises to the NEXT function** (`0x800F16C8`, 82.0% → EXACT in one experiment): `src/fn_800F1790.c` is the *following* function, promoted byte-identical, and its inner block spelled the whole idiom including the `register s32 probe __asm__("r10")` pin — which alone fixed all three "no source shape reproduces it" claims. Also: the loop counter must be `u32` and the scale materialised in its own statement to get indexed `slwi`/`lhax` instead of a folded `rlwinm`.
* **`-fno-schedule-insns` (the only flag that was ever a candidate) was STALE in 2 of 25 cases** — load-bearing on the broken body, a loss on the fixed one (§6bx re-confirmed); and in `0x8000A0A8` `-fno-gcse` was still load-bearing *after* all semantic fixes, so re-measure on the final body and don't assume deletion.
* **A `sched` ready-list TIE-BREAK between two equal-cost TARGET_INSNs is reached by freezing one of them with a non-volatile `asm`, and the pin and the non-volatility are an AND** (`0x80220060`, 87.3% → EXACT): 4 frozen `addi` sites, 5.1% emitted asm. `volatile` on the same template scores 97.5% (it detaches the insn from the param home copies that `sched` then flips); unpinned scores 86.1%. Attribute it properly with `cc1 -dr -da -dj -dg -ds` before reaching for this — three prior sessions had guessed `sched2` when the pass was `sched`.

**Process note — the `// family=` marker loss is real and worth a guard.** `0x80062438` came back as family `?` from the sweep because its `// family=m2c` line had been folded into the rewritten header. Per §6bg that makes the scorer apply NO flags, so a flagged draft silently re-scores flagless and a plausible-but-false verdict follows. When a header is rewritten wholesale, check the family marker survived; the `?` in the sweep's family column is the tell.

## 6er — 2026-10-01 single pick: **`res == 0` + `res >= 0` is a TWO-SIDED
fold wall — no source shape reaches want's negative arm (fn_8013928C,
113/113 masked but 2 relocations wrong, NOT promotable)**

`fn_8013928C` (452 B, `0x8013928C-0x80139450`) hits **113/113 = 100.00% masked**
with the N2 body and **exactly two relocations wrong**. This is the §6bw
branch-target hazard in its purest form: `test_wip_drafts` reports `EXACT`,
and promoting would silently change control flow.

**1. First get the audit RIGHT — two bugs that both produce "no mismatch".**
- `test_wip_drafts`/`want_got` mask REL14 with `0xFFFF0003`, so they compare
  opcode+BO+BI+AA+LK and **never the target**. 113/113 proves nothing here.
- A hand-rolled audit reported "12 mismatches" (all false) because it compared
  `addend=0` against an **absolute** target for the ten **external** REL24
  `bl`s. Those have a named symbol; only RELs whose symbol is `.text`
  (section-relative addend = **target offset**, §6bw point 2) need comparing.
- The subtle one: `symtab.get_symbol(...).name` is the **empty string** for a
  section symbol, not `'.text'`. Testing `name != '.text'` therefore skips
  *every local branch* and reports a perfect score. Test `if name:` and treat
  only empty-name entries as intra-function. With that fixed the audit is
  trustworthy and reports **2 real mismatches**.

**2. The control that settles the addend convention.** A promoted, byte-exact
object (`build/G2TE52/src/cosf.o`) has **19 of 55 raw words differing from the
DOL** — all at relocation sites. So the raw branch field is *not* the final
encoding: the assembler writes the **target offset** into it and the linker
recomputes the displacement. Therefore **compare addends, never raw words.**

**3. What want actually is** (the condition-register copy from cr0 to cr4 is the whole tell — it means THREE tests share ONE compare): at 0x801392B4 retail compares the result in r3 against zero, at 0x801392B8 branches to the epilogue at 0x80139434 when nonzero, at 0x801392BC copies cr0 into cr4, at 0x801392C0 materialises zero into r0, at 0x801392C4 branches on greater-or-equal under cr4 to the body at 0x801392DC, at 0x801392C8 compares r0 against negative six for the stack slot, at 0x801392CC branches to the epilogue with a want addend of 0x1A8, at 0x801392D0 copies r30 into r3, at 0x801392D4 calls 0x8013E0EC, at 0x801392D8 branches to the epilogue with the same 0x1A8 want addend, the body at 0x801392DC loads offset 0x2274, and the latch at 0x80139430 branches back to the body on greater-than under cr4 before the epilogue at 0x80139434.
So: the negative arm is a **sibling of the loop, laid out inline before it**,
exiting to the epilogue; BODY is reached only by `bge`.

**4. The wall, and the `cc1 -dr` proof.** ~50 shapes tried in three families:
- **Outside a loop** (`if (res>=0) goto body; <neg>; goto epi;` and the
  `if/else` + `do{}while(1)` spellings): all **fold to 408 B / 0.98%**.
  `cc1 -dr` on Z1 and AC1 shows **`ge` compares = 0** — GCC 2.95.2 deletes
  `res >= 0` in the **front end** because `res == 0` was just proven. No
  source shape escapes it; the pass that does it is not flag-disableable.
- **Inside a loop** (N2's `for(;;){ if(res<0){E}else{BODY} }`): keeps the
  compare, keeps **452 B and 113/113** — but its negative arm **falls out of
  the loop**, so `cc1 -dr` shows `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG` + `jump_insn →
  label_ref 29`, a **rotated loop**, and GCC correctly targets the loop header
  (`0x38`). That is a real infinite loop for `res < 0`.
- **Negative arm as a loop exit** (`break` / `return` / `goto epi`): the
  compare survives (W1 `ge` compares = 1) but `flow.c`'s reorder **hoists the
  exit arm above the body** and the head becomes `li r0,0; mcrf cr4,cr0; b BODY`
  — an **unconditional** branch where want has `bge cr4`, at ~17.7%.

**There is no third option.** Outside the loop the front end folds; inside it
the exit edge is mis-targeted; making it an exit reorders. Want's code is
**more redundant than GCC 2.95.2 will emit** — it keeps a `ge`/`bge` that is
provably true on that path. Do not burn more passes here without a *new*
compiler behaviour (a `volatile`/`asm`-opaque `res` defeats the fold but costs
the `mcrf cr4,cr0` CSE, so it cannot win either).

**Generalisable:** when a masked-EXACT draft has a branch target wrong, run
`cc1 -dr` and count the test you *expect* to see. `ge compares = 0` = folded
away (front end, unreachable from C); `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG` + a `jump_insn` back
to a `label_ref` = rotated loop, and the "wrong" target is actually the
*correct* one for the CFG you wrote. Cross-check against a promoted sibling
object for the addend convention before trusting any audit that claims success.

## 6ft — 2026-10-01 (0x800BF7C8, 1552B/388 insns, 8.8% → **14.4 % masked**, still DIFF, parked): **a SELF-TARGETING `bdnz`/`b` is REPRODUCIBLE from plain C — read the REL14 ADDEND, never objdump's operand field; and `parking-30`'s "hard wall" rests on that misread**

- **The misread that costs a whole function.** For `R_PPC_REL14` (RELA) the
  addend *is* the branch displacement, not a section-relative target. So a
  self-branch looks like this in the `.o`:

  ```
  9c: 42 00 00 9c   bdnz 138 <fn+0x138>     <- objdump: reads the RAW field
  9c: R_PPC_REL14  .text + 9c               <- addend == its own offset
  ```
  addend `0x9c` at PC `0x9c` ⇒ displacement 0 ⇒ **self**. objdump printed
  `0x138` because it decoded the unrelocated field as a displacement. Plain C
  `for (k = 4; k != 0; k--) { }` with `-fno-strength-reduce` emits exactly
  `li r0,4 / mtctr r0 / bdnz .` — **the "HARD WALL" in
  `docs/parkings/solved/30-empty-doloop-bdnz-window.md` is an artifact of this
  misread and needs correcting.** Also note the masked compare only keeps bits
  `0xFFFF0003` for REL14, so the displacement never scored either way.
  **Rule: audit a "self-branch is unemittable" claim against
  `readelf -r` addend-vs-offset, never against objdump output.**
- **`f32 buf[6]; f32 *p = buf;` hoists retail's `addi r30, r1, 0x48`.**
  Retail computes `&blk[0]` *in the prologue, between the 4 QB lookups*, and
  keeps it in r30. An array lvalue lets cc1 re-materialise the address per
  use; a pointer variable forces the hoist. Measured: the pointer alone is
  worth several masked words, and it is the only way found to reproduce that
  exact prologue insn.
- **A zero-code `"+r"` barrier on the ARGUMENT splits the address web and is
  worth ~10 masked words** — the same body scores 14.4 % with
  `{ Skater *ap = arg0; __asm__("" : "+r"(ap)); r8 = &ap->rec0; }` and 4.4 %
  without it. It does cost a `mr r27,r31` and one callee-saved slot, so it
  trades against the frame goal rather than composing with it.
- **Struct widening is a semantics fix, not a scoring trick.** Retail's tail
  copies TWO quads out of 0x20 and 0xB0 (4 `psq` ops the m2c draft never
  emitted) and re-loads `arg0->unk0C` three times. Fixing that took the census
  from −12 to −6 insns. **When you widen `f32 q[N]` to `f32 q[N+4]`, re-check
  the FOLLOWING pad size** — dropping `pad0x30[0x40]` while widening `q_20`
  silently slid every later field down 0x30 (writes landed on 0x1318 instead
  of 0x1348) and still "scored" 12.4 %. Verify with `lwz`/`stw` displacements
  in the prologue, not with the score.
- **Walls, with the evidence:** (1) frame 0x98 vs 0x88 — `0x70 + 8*nGPR + 8`
  only reaches 0x88 at `nGPR == 4`, and retail's four are
  `{arg0, &blk[0], arg0+0x1310, arg0+0x1318}` with `addi rX,r31,0x250`
  *rematerialised per rec0 loop*; every way to break that web folds or buys a
  register copy. (2) `addic. rX,rX,-1` fusion — retail has 0 `addic.`,
  13 `cmpwi`, 28 `addi`; we get 5-8 `addic.` and lose the `cmpwi`, and
  retail's candidate pair is only ONE insn apart
  (`cmpwi r8,0` / `add r9,r9,r10` / `addi r8,r8,-1`), so it is a scheduler
  difference, not a source shape. (3) the 3-way min wants an 8-`fmr` chain
  (running min in one reg, third `fcmpu` against THAT reg, result into f31);
  written literally cc1 gives 6 `fmr` because it coalesces `m0 = s` into `s`,
  and `"+f"` barriers fix step 1 only by then coalescing `s` with `v31` for
  step 3. (4) `v * ps_res(v)` gives ONE `ps_muls0` (PRE merges the identical
  expressions) vs retail's two — same PRE gap as before.
- **Scoring caveat: `ps_diff.py` and the relocation-masked count disagree**
  (40/382 vs 56/388 here) because the masked compare blanks every branch's BD
  field. Quote both numbers; a "regression" between two variants can be pure
  BD-field noise.
- **Reminder: binutils/capstone mislabel ordinary Gekko PS words as VMX**
  (`xsmaddasp`, `xxsel`, `lq`, …) because the `c` field sits at bits 21-25
  where AltiVec has `vc` — see §178/§170. Count opcodes from raw words.

## 6fu — 2026-10-01 batch promotion of 60 EXACT WIP drafts (`fn_8023FC44`/`80249E04`/`80253FF4` notes preserved)

Promoted 60 relocation-masked-EXACT drafts in batches of 4; each batch
re-verified against the full linked DOL, not just the masked object compare.
`main.dol` stayed byte-identical throughout (SHA-1 `ff6faeb0…`), 9565/11497
matched. Promoting notes:

- **`promote_wip.py` leaves `src/fn_*.c` behind when a batch aborts on REFUSE.**
  It promotes each address (writing `src/fn_*.c` + registering in
  `splits.txt`/`configure.py`) and only reaches the WIP-cleanup block
  (`os.remove(src/wip/...)`, after the `cmp`) once the whole batch verifies.
  A REFUSE or a link/DOL failure `return 1`s *before* that, so the already-
  promoted files stay registered but their WIP drafts are NOT deleted — and
  the revert path deliberately avoids `git` on `src/` (to not clobber earlier
  uncommitted batches), so the leftovers survive. Symptom: `src/fn_X.c` and
  `src/wip/fn_X.c` both exist, and the stale registration can poison the *next*
  batch's build (we hit `patch_dol.py`'s init-r2 assertion that way). Fix by
  promoting one address at a time, or delete the duplicate WIP drafts after.

- **`fn_80253FF4` (468B) — how an m2c bulk draft climbs 11.2% → 100%.** Ordered
  by value, each step is load-bearing:
  1. (11.2→22.2) The loop guard must compare the **loop counter**, not the
     count: m2c's `if (count > 0)` gives `cmpwi r0,0; ble`, but want has
     `li r30,0; cmpw r30,r0; bge` — i.e. `i = 0; if (i < cnt) { … do{}while
     (++i < cnt); }`, the shape of the byte-identical sibling
     `src/fn_802542EC.c`. Also m2c passed arg0 straight through to
     `fn_8024EBD8`/`fn_80255F18` where want passes the *loaded element*.
  2. (22.2→73.5) Tables must be **extern ARRAYS** (`lbl_803CA350`/`358`,
     `80308040`), not `(char*)x + 0x802CA358` arithmetic: the array form keeps
     the table base in a register (`lwzx r9,r28,r0`) instead of folding the
     page into the index, and the `ADDR16_HA/LO` relocations make the
     `lis`/`addi` address-independent. Plus a **prototype on the fn-ptr**
     (`void (*)(s32)`) — an unprototyped cast emits a spurious
     `crclr cr1eq` before every `blrl`.
  3. (73.5→82.9) The SDA global reads MUST be `__asm__ volatile`: plain
     (non-volatile) asm lets GCC hoist/CSE the r13 read into a new
     callee-saved reg (r26), costing 2 words and turning the prologue into
     `stmw r26,8(r1)`. `volatile` pins one read per site.
  4. (82.9→98.3) Give the array walk its own load *statement* (`t = w[0];
     w += 1;`) so strength reduction emits `addi ptr,ptr,4` right after the
     `lwz`, not in the latch.
  5. (98.3→100) `i * 0x2C` strength-reduces to an IV whose `li r28,0` the
     scheduler emits *after* `addi r31,r29,0x720`; writing the offset as an
     explicit `off = 0;` statement before the walker's assignment puts it
     first, as want has.

- **Latent wrong-address hazard (inherited from sibling `fn_802542EC`):**
  `lbl_80308040` is spelled to match the promoted sibling, but want's
  `lis r9,0x8031; addi r28,r9,0x8040` decodes to **0x80318040** while
  symbols.txt says `lbl_80308040` = `.data:0x80308040` — a 0x10000 delta. Both
  refs are ADDR16-masked, so neither objdiff nor a masked compare can see it.
  Only a hand decode of the `lis`/`addi` pair catches this (recipes §§6bw/277/283).

## 5b. doc-56 at scale: undeclared callees are the #1 silent cause of low scores

**(2026-10-01, batch b1/b2. Drove almost all of today's gains.)**

An m2c-generated body often calls real game functions **without declaring
them**. This ngccc (GCC 2.95 fork) then emits a `crclr cr1eq` before *every*
such call site to set the CR — one spurious instruction word per call, which
shifts every later instruction and, because `masked_pct` is INDEX-ALIGNED,
crushes the score. On `fn_80205084` (11 call sites) declaring the five
property getters took it **14.7% -> 35.7%** with no semantic change at all;
the same fix plus an arity correction took `fn_80043B28` **27.2% -> 31.9%**
and `fn_80253DBC` **13.0% -> 19.1%**.

How to spot it: `tools/want_got.py` shows a `crclr cr1eq` in the GOT column
with no counterpart in the WANT column. One per call site, always adjacent to
a `bl`.

How to fix it: the callees are usually **already matched and sitting in
`src/fn_<ADDR>.c`**, and each of those files names itself in a header comment
(`// GetFloat @ 0x801282E0`) and declares its real signature on the definition
line. So:

```sh
grep -n "^[a-z0-9_ ]*\**NAME(" src/fn_<ADDR>.c     # exact signature
```

Copy the signature verbatim. Two traps:

* **Arities are often wrong too, not just missing.** Read the want's r3/r4/r5
  immediately before each `bl`; `fn_80205084`'s second call had to be
  `GetStructure_2(RESULT_OF_CALL_1, arg0->unk0xC4, arg0+0x28, 1)` — the
  previous call's return value as arg0, which m2c had dropped entirely.
* **Do not over-declare.** On `fn_80043B28`, adding correct signatures for the
  last three callees (Mem_Alloc2 / GetPair / fn_80044C64) measured
  **31.9% -> 29.0%**. The remaining `crclr` pairs there are load-bearing for
  this body. Always re-measure after each declaration change; the rule is
  "declare what the want shows is missing", not "declare everything".

### Recovering callee identity from a dispatch table

When several callees share a shape, disambiguate by the internal type code
they pass in r5 to the common helper `0x80127F60`: `GetStructure_2` passes
`li r5, 0xa`, `GetArray` passes `li r5, 0xc`, `GetFloat` passes `li r5, 2`.
Two callers can look identical at the call site and still be different
functions.

### Reach for already-matched callee sources first

Most of these low-hanging getters are byte-identical matches already in
`src/`. Before decoding a call target by hand, grep for the name and read the
matched source — it gives you the name, the signature, and the semantics for
free.

## 5c. Naming the 18.6k `fn_*` placeholders (retail-metadata matching)

Most of the remaining work is *decode* work, but there is a large, separate
class of wins that need no codegen at all: ~18.6k addresses in `symbols.txt`
are still `fn_*`/`lbl_*` placeholders that have a **known retail name** sitting
in the metadata on disk. `tools/find_symbol_renames.py` proposes them.

### Where the retail names live

- `docs/thpg-func-names.tsv` — 9 tab cols: `mangled, class, method, unit,
  folder, folder_evidence, size, builds_seen, rows`. Key retail functions by
  **`(unit, method)` (cols 4 and 3), never by bare method name** — method
  names collide across units (`p_vector.o::add`, `nx.o::sGetMeshBaseName`,
  `zone.o::sGetCurrentZoneName`), and keying by name alone makes every result a
  duplicate.
- `docs/thpg-callgraph.tsv` — `caller<TAB>callee`, both `unit::Name`. Strip
  the unit prefix for set comparison, but keep `(unit, name)` to key the map.

### Callee-set matching

An unnamed function's **known callees** (its `bl` targets that are already
named in `symbols.txt`) are a signature. Score = Jaccard against a retail
candidate's callee set. Gates that matter, in order of value:

1. **Specificity** — a callee set shared by many retail functions is worthless.
   `{OSDisableInterrupts, OSRestoreInterrupts}` matches 9 candidates on 96B
   alone. `{GetFloat, GetInteger}` matches every script-param wrapper. Count
   how many retail functions share the exact set before believing a hit.
2. **Size agreement** — the killer filter. The callee set only shows the
   *already-named* callees, so a large size mismatch means the identification
   is probably wrong. Retail sizes come from other builds, so allow ~25%.
3. **Caller agreement** — a second, independent signal, but only ~190 unnamed
   fns have any named caller at all, so it disambiguates rarely.

### Unit lock (the strongest signal)

The linker lays a unit's functions out **contiguously and in source order**,
and ngccc tracks the retail compiler closely enough that per-function size
lands within a few percent. So a run of adjacent unnamed functions whose size
profile matches one retail unit's mid-size (≥48B) functions is *over-determined*
evidence. Search **sub-windows**, not whole runs: a tiny evidence-free function
frequently sits at one end and would otherwise veto the whole match.

On the first full run this fired on exactly **one** place in the entire DOL —
`p_matrix.o` at `0x8001D040..0x8001D270`:

| addr | DOL | retail | name |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x8001D040` | 176B | 172B | `translate` |
| `0x8001D0F0` | 192B | 172B | `rotateX` |
| `0x8001D1B0` | 192B | 172B | `rotateY` |
| `0x8001D270` | 176B | 172B | `scale` |

Corroboration that made it airtight: `p_matrix.o`'s only other members are the
4–20B functions `identity`/`cat`/`invert`/`lookAt`/`multiply`/`PMInit` (too
small to survive as DOL symbols), and the small DOL neighbours of the run are
*already* named `PSMTX_Identity`/`PSMTX_Concat`/`PSMTX_Inverse`/`C_MTX_LookAt`.

### Greedy assignment cannot split siblings

`rotateX` and `rotateY` have **identical** callee sets (`PSMTXConcat` +
`PSMTXRotRad`), so the greedy per-member assignment cannot order them — it
assigns `rotateX` to both. Break such ties on a disambiguating *argument*:
`PSMTXRotRad` forwards its third arg to `PSMTXRotTrig`, which does
`ori r0,r4,0x20` to index a per-axis table. `fn_8001D0F0` passes `r4=0x78` and
uses the π/180 constant at `0x8029112C`; `fn_8001D1B0` passes `r4=0x79` and
`0x80291130`. Four consecutive π/180 constants sit at `0x80291128..34`, i.e. X,Y,Z
start at `0x2C`. Source order (`translate, rotateX, rotateY, scale`) agrees.

### LANDMINE: renaming in `symbols.txt` alone BREAKS THE LINK

dtk auto-asms unmatched callers and generates their call expressions *from
`symbols.txt`*, so renaming the callee makes the caller reference the new name
while the object still defines the old one:

```
### mwldeppc.exe Linker Error:
#   undefined: 'translate'
#   Referenced from 'fn_80017128' in auto_01_80016EDC_text.o
```

A rename therefore touches **all** of:

1. `config/G2TE52/symbols.txt` — the name at that address;
2. the `src/*.c` **definition**'s function name (file may keep its `fn_*`
   filename — dtk maps splits to files, not names);
3. **every** caller in `src/` — declaration *and* call sites, registered
   files *and* inert `src/wip/` drafts (grep the old name; the link error only
   lists registered objects, so wip callers fail silently later);
4. nothing in `configure.py` / `splits.txt` — those track addresses, not names.

Then `tools/ninja build/G2TE52/ok` must still report `OK`. Renaming never
changes emitted code, so the DOL **must** stay byte-identical — a changed hash
after a pure rename means a caller was missed, not that the rename was wrong.

Also worth knowing: many of these functions are **already matched and promoted**
under `fn_*` names, so the decompiled source is a free cross-check on the
proposed identification. All five `p_matrix.o`/cache candidates were confirmed
against their own matched bodies (`PSMTXTrans`+`PSMTXConcat` switch;
`PSMTXRotRad(0x78)`/`(0x79)` with deg→rad; `memcpy`+`DCFlushRange` cache read).

### Capstone gotchas that will silently ruin this

- `md.disasm()` **stops at the first undecodable word**. Code sections contain
  data pools and jump tables, so any whole-section scan needs
  `md.skipdata = True`. Without it a full-`.text` `bl` census reports **22**
  targets instead of ~44,665, and a caller-side analysis silently returns empty.
- This capstone version has **no `ins.op`** — use `ins.operands[0]` and test
  `op.type == PPC_OP_IMM` (`PPC_OP_IMM == 2`).
- Attribute a `bl` to the *function* containing it (bisect the instruction
  address against sorted `symbols.txt` starts), not to the raw address, or
  caller names come out as garbage.

### Negative result (2026-10-01)

A sweep for *documented but unapplied* identifications came back **empty**:
every `// Name @ 0xADDR` header comment in `src/`, `include/`, `libs/` is
already applied in `symbols.txt`. Prose `fn_ADDR = Name` and markdown-table
sweeps over `docs/**` are all false positives — VMX mnemonics (`vmsumshm`),
local-variable names (`arg0`), and caller→callee tables whose name column is
not the function's name. The parking docs' only genuinely unapplied entries are
ones they already flag as unknown ("WIRED as `src/fn_8026E5AC.c` **(not
renamed)**"). So new names have to come from `thpg-*.tsv`, not from the prose.

## 6zz — Agent sweep 2026-10-02 (non-parked WIP picks)

Two drafts picked at random from the ~535 `src/wip/*.c` files that carried no
`park` note. Both were NEAR-but-unfinished; both improved substantially
without touching flags or inline asm. The shared lesson is that **statement
placement, not statement content, was the whole bug in both cases** — which
is the recipes-57/141 family, now confirmed on a float-rodata tail.

### 1. Staging rodata floats generalizes (fn_8007D4E0, 70.7% -> 92.7%)

The r4 note on `fn_8019EFD4` already recorded that staging a three-float
rodata cluster into named locals before a call is load-bearing. That holds
when there is **no call at all** in the tail, so the rule is not about call
argument evaluation:

```c
/* m2c: constants inlined -> ngccc re-loads them and sinks f1 to the end */
*arg2 *= lbl_80295E5C;
*arg3 *= lbl_80295E60;
return lbl_80295E64;

/* want: three loads hoisted, f0/f12/f1, in one group */
k1 = lbl_80295E5C;   /* -> f0  */
k2 = lbl_80295E60;   /* -> f12 */
*arg2 *= k1;
k3 = lbl_80295E64;   /* -> f1, the return register */
*arg3 *= k2;
return k3;
```

Worth ~8 points, and it is the whole difference between the two forms. Rule
of thumb: **a tail that loads 2+ rodata floats and folds them into pointers
needs the constants staged into named `f32` locals; inlining them makes
ngccc pick different FPRs and interleave the loads.** The return constant
specifically wants its own local, not a bare `return SYMBOL;`.

Residual after staging is a pure 2-instruction schedule swap (the return
constant's `lfs f1` sits before the first `stfs` in the want, after it in
the got). Ten placements tie at 92.7% or regress — treat it as an ngccc
load-scheduling floor, not a missing statement.

### 2. A loop induction variable must advance on the EXITING iteration too
   (fn_800596E4, 24.2% -> 40.3%)

`off` is a byte offset into a lookup table that is consumed by a `goto` that
leaves the loop. m2c placed `off += 4` inside the `if (flag)` tail, so the
iteration that takes the exit jumps out with a stale offset. The want
advances it unconditionally at the **top** of the body:

```c
node = *p;
p += 1;
off2 = off;          /* pre-increment value, for the exit path */
off = off + 4;       /* induction variable, runs ahead */
if (node == 0) goto slot_free;
```

Hoisting the update is worth ~14 points; giving it a second name is worth
~2 more and is the only thing that moved the residual. The generalizable
rules:

* **When a loop body has a `goto`/`break` out of it, any variable the exit
  path reads must be updated on every iteration**, not just the fall-through
  path — GCC will not sink the update across the branch for you. Audit every
  early exit against every variable its target reads.
* **If the want shows a 3-address update (`mr rX, rY` + `addi rY, rX, imm`)
  where the got emits the 2-address in-place form, the source wants TWO names
  for that variable**: one induction variable, plus a second holding the
  pre-update value for whichever path needs it. That reproduces the copy.
  Here it landed in the wrong slot and the wrong colour, so it is necessary
  but not sufficient — but it is the right direction, and nothing else moved
  the number.

The remaining gap there is allocation, not semantics. Six distinct attempts
(`char*` offset, `u32`/signed mixes, `for`-comma header, four declaration-order
permutations, a second walking pointer, dropping the `flag` temp) all tied at
38.7% or regressed — the signature of an alloc-order artifact, not a missing
statement. Do not keep permuting the loop body. The tail was already right:
every tail rewrite tested scored *worse* (8-11%).

## 6zy — fn_80256AD0: a *pair* of counter-intuitive changes (92.9% -> 96.1%)

`Vtable0x8030804C_m15`, 620B. The previous park note recorded
`li r23/li r24` emitting before the guard where the want has them after it,
and concluded "moving them inside the if regresses elsewhere". Both halves of
that were true and neither was actionable alone. The fix is two changes that
are only correct **together**:

1. Move the two counter inits (`vo23 = 0; vo24 = 0;`) from the preheader
   **into** the `if (guard) { ... }` block, just before the `do`. Alone:
   **92.9% -> 27.1%**. It makes the preheader byte-exact (6 consecutive exact
   instructions) but GCC then hoists the loop-invariant field read
   `*(s32*)((char*)a0+4)` out of the outer loop into the preheader, *above*
   the `li`s, shifting everything after it.
2. Make the two bit-count seed loads `volatile`. Alone: no-op. Combined: the
   hoist is blocked and the score goes to **96.1%**.

### Generalized lessons

* **A regression is not a refutation.** "Moving the inits inside regresses"
   was read as a dead end. It was actually half of a two-part fix, where the
   other half *unblocks* it. When a change that provably makes the want's
   block structure exact nonetheless tanks the score, suspect that the
   change exposed a *new* optimisation opportunity (here: LICM) rather than
   concluding the change was wrong. Look at what the new got does with the
   freed slot.
* **`volatile` is often the honest fix, not a schedule hack.** Here the want
   contains two `lwz 4(r25)` in the outer body — one per inner loop — and
   re-reads the field every outer iteration. A callback in between can change
   it, so the reload *is* the semantics and GCC was caching a value allowed
   to change. Rule of thumb: if the want re-loads a field the loop body
   writes or a callee can touch, mark that read `volatile` rather than
   reaching for a barrier.
* **A want post-reload copy (`mr rX,rY` right after a hoisted `lwz`) is the
   fingerprint of a blocked LICM.** Seeing the copy in the got is the tell
   that the load was hoisted and re-materialised.

### Two residual classes, both now proven source-spelling-invariant

* **Address split (4 words).** want `(base + 0x488) + idx` via
  `addi r29,r30,0x488` + `stwx r31,r29,r24`; got `(base + idx) + 0x488` via
  `add r29,r24,r30` + `stw r31,0x488(r29)`. Same address, different
  base/index choice. Naming the hoisted base in the **already register-pinned
  but unused** variables is the obvious lever and it is a **no-op** — unused
  register vars constrain nothing, so GCC still picks those exact registers
  as address scratch. Fresh unpinned locals scored slightly worse (94.8%).
* **Rotate mask (2 words).** want `rlwinm. r0,r0,0x1f,1,0x1f` (MB=1,ME=31)
  vs got `rlwinm. r0,r0,0x1f,0,0x1e` (MB=0,ME=30): GCC proved the `(t<<31)`
  term dead and emits a plain `t>>1`. **All four source spellings**
  (`(t>>1)|(t<<31)`, `&0xFFFFFFFEu`, `(t>>1)|((t&1)<<31)`, `&~1u`) give
  byte-identical output. When an `rlwinm` mask range disagrees, stop
  re-spelling the rotate — the MB/ME range comes from known-bits analysis of
  the value's live range, so the lever is what *feeds* the loop.

Also confirmed here: the `RD_SDATA()` `__asm__("lwz %0, -0x7f40(13)")` is the
documented house solution for the `.sdata` global `lbl_803CA340` (recipes 173),
not a transcription hack — plain `extern` under `-G0` gives lis+addi+lwz, and
the pure-C `-msdata=eabi -G4` route emits `R_PPC_EMB_SDA21` which
`compile_fn`'s masked compare can never verify standalone (§5q).

## 6fv — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x8000D984, 308B, m2c DIFF 14.8% -> **EXACT**, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **the ARRAY-INDEX spelling and the `(char*)base + OFF + idx*SIZE` spelling of the SAME address produce DIFFERENT commutative `add` operand orders (`add rX,base,rM` vs `add rX,rM,base`) — and that choice also moves WHERE a loop-invariant `lis` lands in the preheader**

0x44-stride record table, swap-remove by key. Four load-bearing source
decisions, each worth instructions (ladder 14.8 → 71.4 → 88.3 → 94.8 → 97.4 →
100.0), all plain C:

1. **Name the element type so the swap-remove is a real 68-byte struct
   assignment.** `self->arr[i] = self->arr[n]` with `Elem_t` = 0x44 bytes of
   `s32`/`pad` gives GCC's `expand_block_move` byte-count loop
   (`li 0x30 / addic. -0x18 / bne` + a 5-word tail) *by itself* — this is NOT
   the doc-46 CTR-doloop wall, because that wall is a hand-written member-copy
   `do/while`; a whole-struct assignment never enters the doloop matcher.
   Corollary for doc 46: **the `addic.`-counted copy loop is not evidence of a
   source loop.** If you see `li 0x30`-style byte counters in a want, first try
   a properly-typed struct assignment and only then blame the loop shape.
2. **`while (i < self->count)` with an early `return`, not `if (count > 0) {…}`**
   — reproduces retail's guard-then-bottom-test loop with the limit reloaded in
   the latch (same shape as the promoted `fn_8000DD2C`, same struct).
3. **Read a callee-saved field into a local BEFORE the first call**
   (`mgr = self->unk0x14;` then the alloc/ctor calls). That costs one more
   callee-saved register and therefore the *whole* frame: `stmw r27` (5 regs)
   + `stwu -0x20` + LR at 0x24. Without it the field is re-materialised after
   the second call into the register that already holds `arg2`, and you lose the
   register, the frame, and ~16% in one move. Frame arithmetic still rules
   (§6db) but the *residual instruction* is the tell: a want `lwz rX,0x14(r31)`
   **before** the first `bl` with its value live into the third is an ordering
   requirement, not a scheduling request.
4. **Spell the swap-remove as `(char *)self + 0x1C + idx * 0x44` on BOTH sides.**
   The plain array form `self->arr[n]` builds `plus(base, idx*size)` and emits
   the commuted `add r9,r31,r9` with the 0x1C left as the addressing offset;
   the `(char*)` sum builds `plus(idx*size, base)` and emits
   `add r9,r9,r31 / addi r3,r9,0x1c`, which is what want has. Same value, one
   operand-order word. **Bonus, and the part that is easy to miss: this one
   change also moved the loop-invariant global `lis` from slot 2 of the
   preheader to slot 4** (want: `addi r29 / addi r28 / mr r9 / lis r10`). A
   `lis`/`addi` address pair for a hoisted global sits in the preheader at a
   pseudo-allocation-order position that no amount of reordering the *source*
   moves — only changing the address tree in the loop body did. Measured: with
   the array form the best was 94.8% (4 diffs); the pointer-variable form
   (`last = &self->arr[n]; *last`) fixed the `lis` but cost the address pair
   (97.4%, 2 diffs); the symmetric `(char*)` form fixed both.

Also load-bearing and reusable: **`extern void *lbl_802FFE98` +
`*(void **)((char *)lbl_802FFE98 + 0x118)`** keeps retail's two-step
`lis r10 / lwz r9,-0x168(r10) / lwz r4,0x118(r9)`. Writing the house-standard
`extern char lbl_802FFE98[];` + `*(void **)(lbl_802FFE98 + 0x118)` folds the
pair into one `lwz r4,0x118(r10)` and **loses 4 bytes of function size**. So for
a *double* indirection off a `lbl_` the array-symbol spelling is the wrong one;
use the typed-pointer spelling to force the intermediate register. (Contrast
`fn_8000CB0C`, matched, where the symbol is passed as an argument and
`extern s32 *lbl_802FFE98` + `*(s32 *)((char *)lbl_802FFE98 + 0x118)` is
right.) This is §6e/`6fo`'s "lbl-symbol vs literal" rule with a new twist: it
can also be about *how many loads* the spelling produces.

Verified genuine: object `.text` = 0x134 = the symbol size, **only** `.text` in
the object (no private `.rodata`/float pool), and the 10 words that differ
before relocation masking are exactly the 5 branch fields + 3 `bl` targets +
the `lis`/`lwz` displacement pair — every REL14/REL24/ADDR16 target resolves to
retail's (checked by hand against the want, not just via the mask).
