## 6fu — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x8002439C, 240B, m2c DIFF 16.4% -> **EXACT**, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **only the `(volatile T *)&obj->f` CAST lvalue serializes a single store — a `volatile` qualifier on the STRUCT MEMBER does not** (refines recipe 116), and **named base pointers need their group's FIRST slot written through `obj->` directly**

**1. `volatile` on the member != `volatile` on the cast lvalue.** A long
straight-line `stfs` run into one `arg0` wants one store pinned at its RTL
slot while every other store in the run is free to sink/rotate:

```c
    fn_800244BC(arg0, fn_8005E1DC());
    *(volatile f32 *)&arg0->f78 = t31;   /* pinned: stays in the bl delay slot */
    ...
    arg0->fC4 = t12;  arg0->fC8 = t13;  arg0->f7C = t0;  ... arg0->fB4 = t31;
```

* plain `arg0->f78 = t31;` → ngccc **sinks it into the middle of the run**
  (emitted between `0xC8` and `0x7C`) and rotates the `0xC4`/`0xC8` pair;
  73.3%, 16 diffs. Moving that one statement to 4 other source positions
  (before/after the constant loads, after `0xC8`, after `0xB4`) changed
  *nothing* — it is not a source-order problem, st.c/sched owns it.
* `*(volatile f32 *)&arg0->f78 = t31;` → **96.7%**, and the last 2 diffs are
  then only the `f12`/`f13` choice for the 12.0f/12000.0f pair.
* declaring the field `volatile f32 f78;` **inside the struct** and writing
  `arg0->f78 = t31;` → back to 71.7%. **The cast lvalue is load-bearing; the
  member qualifier is not.** Recipe 116's `(volatile s32 *)` spelling is the
  only one that works here.

Corollary for the same function: with the store pinned, the *load* order
`t0,t12,t13` in source emits `lfs f0,f12,f13` (→ 100%), while source
`t0,t13,t12` emits the same registers with the values swapped and lands on
`f12`/`f13` reversed (96.7%). Swapping the two locals' **declaration** order
does nothing; the **assignment** order is what picks the FPR.

**2. A named base pointer reproduces `addi r8,r3,K` + `0xc(r8)` only if the
group's first slot bypasses it** (extends §6aj-6). For two 16-byte groups
written `(0,0,0,1)` at +0x58 and +0x68:

```c
    qa = &arg0->qa;
    arg0->qa.x = t0;     /* -> stfs f0,0x68(r31)  : CSE does NOT fold to 0(r8) */
    qa->y = t0;  qa->z = t0;  qa->w = t31;   /* -> stfs ..,4(r8)/8(r8)/0xc(r8) */
```

All four through the pointer gives `0x68(r31)`… never; all four as plain
members gives `0x74(r31),0x6c(r31),0x70(r31)` (no `addi` at all, 62%). Only
the mix above produces the want's `addi r8,r31,0x68` hoisted into the
constant-load block next to `stfs f0,0x68(r31)` — and it is **order-sensitive
per group**: source `[x,y,z,w]` emits `[x,w,y,z]` while source `[x,z,y,w]`
emits `[x,w,y,z]` as well, so the two groups land on *different* middle orders
from the *same* source order — the scheduler, not the source, picks the tail.

**3. DIAGNOSTIC TRAP — `tools/want_got.py` prints a wrong target for `bdnz`.**
It renders the operand with capstone, and this capstone build computes a
*backward* `bdnz` displacement (`BD`, AA=0) as `addr + BD`. The real target is
`addr - BD`. So an empty `do { i--; } while (i != 0);` (recipe 116 / §4h's
`li r0,N; mtctr; bdnz`) prints as `bdnz 0x800243fc` against a want of
`bdnz 0x800243cc` even though **the raw words are identical** (BD=0 both).
Compare the raw words, not the printed target, when a `bdnz`/`bdz` line is
the only "diff". (Same trap applies to `tools/want_vs_got.py`.)

**4. Callees worth auditing first on m2c float-init blobs** (both free
16.4% -> correct here): a `void`-returning-looking callee that is really a
`f32 (void)` **getter** (`0x8005E1DC` = `lis; lfs f1; blr`), so the call is the
nested `fn(arg0, fn_8005E1DC())` and m2c's `fn(); fn(arg0, 0)` is fiction.
Because the getter takes no args ngccc then correctly *elides* the `mr r3,arg0`
before it, and the second `mr r3,arg0` lands in the first call's delay slot —
both exactly like the want.

## 6fw — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x80034D24, 288B, m2c DIFF 10.9% → **EXACT**, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **an explicit WALKING POINTER suppresses complete unrolling AND pins the single-IV `d(...)` form; WHICH register ivopts makes the IV base is decided by the most-used DERIVED pointer; and `extern const f32` (vs plain `extern f32`) is what lets a loop-invariant `lfs` sink PAST `mtctr` in the preheader**

A 4-element, 0x78-stride field-fill constructor: vtable store, a 4-store
`mtctr/bdnz` loop, an `if/else` call, then a 24-store `mtctr/bdnz` loop — both
loops one register with plain displacements (`stfs f0,0(r9) … addi r9,r9,0x78`).
Four semantically distinct fixes, all plain C, flagless. Score path:
**10.9 → 5.6 (index form unrolls, see 1) → 47.2 (walking pointer) → 52.8 →
72.2 → 75.0 (ivopts base, see 2) → 87.5 (`const` externs, see 3) → 100.0
(`do/while(--i)` preheader, see 4).**

**1. `arr[i]` in a constant-trip loop is the WRONG SPELLING — write an explicit walking pointer.** With `for (i=0;i<4;i++,e=e+1)` over the fields, ngccc **completely unrolls** (404 B, every offset hoisted into r12–r28), and under `-fno-unroll-loops` it falls back to the WORSE form: one base register per field plus an `stfsx`-indexed store per access. A pointer the source increments itself (`e++` inside the body) is not an index the unroller can peel, so it survives as `li rN,4; mtctr rN` with ONE register and `d(...)` displacements. **This is the counter-example to recipe 252's "`u32 i` keeps the indexed `stbx` form": that advice is about `buf[i]` byte fills; when want's single register carries every displacement of the element, an explicit pointer walk is required and the index must not exist at all.** (Same family as recipes 272/89: `mtctr/bdnz` loops want the *loop shape*, not the *index type*.)

**2. Which register becomes the IV base = the most-used DERIVED pointer, so re-point the loop variable at the sub-struct to move the base.** A pointer walked as `Elem *e = arg0->e` forces the base to `+0x1C` (the element start) and every field becomes a positive displacement. Want's bases are `+0x70` (loop 1) and `+0x50` (loop 2) — i.e. *inside* the element, with negative displacements for the fields below it. Fix: make the outer pointer have NO direct memory use in the body and give the body a pointer to the sub-object, so ivopts' profit ranking selects it:

```c
for (e = arg0->e; i < 4; i++, e++) {
    ElemTail *t = &e->tail;            /* +0x34  -> becomes the IV, base +0x50 */
    ElemHead *h = (ElemHead *)((char *)t - 0x34);   /* folds to t-0x34, SAME reg */
    t->m64 = 0; ... h->m00 = -1; ...
}
```

The `(char *)t - 0x34` hop is load-bearing: it lets the head fields collapse to
negative displacements off the SAME register (want shows exactly `-0x34 … +0x38`
off one r9) instead of allocating a second one. **`ivopts` picks the candidate
with the most in-loop uses, so "which address gets displacement 0" is a
source-shape decision, not a register-allocation accident** — same family as
§6fv (the same address spelled two ways emits two different RTL forms).

**3. `extern const f32 lbl_X;` is a THIRD axis on §6ek-1's declaration-form lever, and it is the one that moves the preheader.** In the preheader, want has `lis r11; lis r10; mtctr r0; stw; lfs f0; addi r9,…; lfs f13` — the loop-invariant `lfs` sit AFTER `mtctr`. Plain `extern f32` puts them before (75.0%); `extern char[] + *(f32 *)` collapses the whole colour map (14.6%). `const` tells cc1 the global never changes, so the load is pure and may be sunk past the counter setup: **75.0% → 87.5%, and it fixed loop 1's whole preheader.** Measure all three spellings before blaming the scheduler.

**4. THE PREHEADER COUNTER: `do { …; e++; } while (--i != 0)` vs `for (i=0;i<4;i++,e++)` — same insns, different placement.** With both loops still at 87.5% the *only* residual was loop 2's preheader: want `li r8,4; lis r9; lis r11; mtctr r8; lfs f0; li r0,0; …` vs got `lis r9; lis r11; lfs f0; li r0,0; li r9,4; lfs f13; mtctr r9; …`. Rewriting just loop 2 as `i = 4; e = …; do { … e++; } while (--i != 0);` moved `li 4` ahead of the two HI16 anchors and `mtctr` up behind them, and fixed the `-1`/`1` constant order for free. **When the residual is "the loop counter's `li`/`mtctr` sit on the wrong side of a hoisted `lis`", try the countdown spelling before any flag** — `-fno-schedule-insns` / `-fno-schedule-insns2` / `-fno-sched-interblock` all made it WORSE (77.8/76.4/75.0) and no `volatile` or `const` variant moved it.

**Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip`, not promoted):** object has `.text`
(0x120 = 288 B = `symbols.txt size:0x120`) and `.rela.text` and NOTHING else —
**no private `.rodata`**, so no doc-14 caveat; **0 emitted inline instructions**;
all 34 raw differing bytes lie inside the 16 relocated words, and each was
hand-decoded: the 4 `R_PPC_REL14` addends are ABSOLUTE section offsets
`0x48 / 0x78 / 0x7C / 0xA4` = `0x80034D6C` (loop-1 body), `0x80034D9C` (beq),
`0x80034DA0` (b), `0x80034DC8` (loop-2 body) — exactly want's four targets — the
two `R_PPC_REL24` name `fn_80033538` / `fn_800335E0`, and the six
`ADDR16_HA/LO` pairs name `lbl_80291E58` / `lbl_80291E1C` / `lbl_80291E20`,
all three real `.rodata2` entries at the addresses want encodes, so the
masked-100 %-wrong-label hazard (277/283) cannot apply.

## 6ft — 2026-10-02 (0x80031AF0, 508B, m2c DIFF 11.6% → parked 37.0%): **the countdown latch has THREE codegen shapes, and the back-edge target tells you where a loop-invariant load really lives**

**1. Reading rule: the loop's back-edge TARGET delimits the loop body.** In this
family (outer `do` around a 64×`mtctr` fill loop) want's outer back edge is
`bne 0x80031bd0` and `0x80031bc0..0x80031bcc` (`lis r9; lis r11; lfs f0;
lfs f13`) sits *below* it — i.e. the two `lfs` of the two `.rodata2` float
constants execute ONCE, not per outer iteration, even though a store loop
follows them in the same block. Putting `f0 = lbl_A; f13 = lbl_B;` **inside**
the `do` keeps them in the loop and costs a block split + 4 words; putting
them between `if (n != 0) {` and the `do` reproduces want's 4-word
pre-loop block exactly. Corollary: **when a want loop's back edge skips
instructions, those instructions are NOT in the loop** — GCC will happily leave
an `lis`+`lfs` pair in a hoisted-by-`sched` position and tempt you into
writing the load inside the loop.

**2. `--x != -1` vs `x-- != -1` are NOT the same codegen, and the house idiom is
the in-place one.** Seven matched siblings (fn_80066CA0, fn_80058A70,
fn_80067DFC, fn_8006800C, fn_8006EC98, fn_8000E48C, fn_8006712C) all spell the
countdown `while (--x != -1)` and all compile to an IN-PLACE latch —
`cmpwi x,0; addi x,x,-1; bne` (GCC rewrites `--x != -1` to `x != 0` plus a
decrement). Writing it `while (x-- != -1)` instead produces a genuine
induction-variable pair: `addi iv,x,-1` lands in the loop TOP block and the
latch becomes `mr t,x; mr x,iv; cmpwi t,-1; bne` (**4 words, 2 copies**).
So per countdown latch budget: in-place = 2 words, `x--` = 4 words, and a
*third* shape (`mr x,iv; cmpwi x,-1; bne` = 3 words, ONE copy) exists in the
wild — it is `--x` RTL with the counter LIVE-OUT of the loop, and I could not
find a C spelling that produces it (see below). **When a countdown latch is 2
words too long and `x--` overshoots, the missing ingredient is a live-out
counter, not a different spelling** — check whether want uses the counter
after the loop before grinding the source.

**3. NEGATIVE datapoint for §6ek-1 (`extern f32 lbl_X;` vs `extern char
lbl_X[];` + `*(f32 *)lbl_X`): the 35% colour-map swing does NOT fire when the
float global is loaded into a LOCAL and the stores are written from that
local.** Both spellings produced a byte-identical 496B object here (and
516B after the other fixes). §6ek's lever applies when the global is consumed
*directly* by the store; routing it through a local first normalises the RTL
and the reload colour map with it. Saves re-testing it on every
"two `.rodata2` floats into a counted store loop" draft.

Park note for 0x80031AF0 (in `src/wip/fn_80031AF0.c`): after the four
semantic fixes above the block skeleton, block sizes, basic-block split,
loop-counter registers and the tail shape all match; the residual is purely
the register COLOUR MAP (want arg0->r11/arg1->r8/arg0*4->r10/base->r3/
blk->r0 + the four `0x803645D8..E4` addresses pinned in callee-saved r28/r29
because they are live across the `Mem_Alloc` calls, whereas every spelling
tried rematerialises them into volatile regs and rotates the whole map).

## 6fr — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x80067380, 468B, m2c DIFF 24.1% -> **EXACT**, 0 asm, 0 flags beyond the project default, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **in a flat product `A * 3 * B * 4` ngccc puts the `3x = x + 2x` trick on the MEM-loaded factor `B` — a source-level TEMP STATEMENT for `(A*3)` is the only lever that moves it onto `A`**

Recipe-104/75-style loop spellings got the skeleton right; the last 4 words
(`0x80067410-0x80067424`) were the `Mem_Alloc` size chain.

**What want looks like** (the 12-element-per-frame size `(a7+1)*3*self->f84*4`): retail adds one to r27 in r0 for the A term, loads offset 0x84 of the self home into r9 for the B term, shifts A left by one into r3 for twice A, adds A back for three times A, multiplies by B, and shifts left by two for the outer times-four.

**What the same expression in ANY operand order gives** (all three of these
scored identically, 94.9% / 96.6% / 94.9%, only the colour map moved): the build hoists the offset-0x84 load into r0 to the top of the block first, then adds one to r27, applies the shift-plus-add three-times trick to the B term instead, multiplies A by that tripled B, and shifts left by two.

So the operand order in the C source is **irrelevant**: `A*3*B*4`, `3*A*B*4`
and `B*(A*3)*4` all flatten/reassociate the same way, and expand_mult's
`choose_mult_strategy` then applies the multiply-by-3 to the *chain's first
operand* — which is the one still sitting in a MEM. The only spelling that
worked is a **named temp statement**:

    s32 t3 = (arg7 + 1) * 3;              /* the 3x is closed over A here   */
    arg0->unk0x124 = Mem_Alloc(t3 * arg0->unk0x84 * 4);

-> EXACT. Generalisation for every `* 3 / * 5 / * 7` size expression in the
corpus (there are dozens: `fn_8024EECC`, `fn_8025097C`, the `Unk_DCEB657B`
ctor family's `Mem_Alloc` sizes, …): **if want's `slwi/add` 3x pair reads the
first-computed factor, the source had that factor's `*3` in its own
statement.** Two diagnostic corollaries:

* **Constant adjacency is readable off the code.** `((A*B)*3)*4` folds the
  two constants into 12 and emits `mullw r3,r3,rB ; mulli r3,r3,0xc`. So a
  want that spreads the powers (`3x` inner, `slwi 2` OUTERMOST after the
  `mullw`) proves the source's constant factors were NOT adjacent in the
  multiply chain — that is how you know to split statements instead of
  re-permuting parentheses.
* The same split is the fix when want's `lwz` of a struct field is NOT the
  first instruction of the block but the `addi` from the other factor is
  (same root cause: the load is hoisted because the MEM factor leads the
  chain).

**Family notes (the `Unk_DCEB657B` ctor cluster 0x800669D0 / 66CA0 / 67380 /
67BEC / 6800C + their 0x8008xxxx thunks)** — `src/fn_80066CA0.c` is the
byte-exact twin to copy from (same skeleton, 456B). Two per-sibling deltas:

* the alloc spin is NOT the same loop in every sibling. `fn_80066CA0` wants
  `li r0,3; mtctr r0; bdnz` (a 3-iteration `var_ctr=3; do{var_ctr-=1;}
  while(var_ctr);`); `0x80067380` wants `li r9,1; cmpwi r9,0; addi r9,r9,-1;
  bne` for the same-looking spin — that is the RECIPE-75 u32 form
  `u32 v=1; do{}while(v-- != 0u);`, and the m2c `tmp=(v==0); v-=1;` spelling
  emits the `subfic/adde/cmpwi` boolean machinery instead.
* `unk0x170` is declared `u8` in the shared struct (two sibling classes
  disagree) — the ctor family stores a WORD there, so write it as
  `*(s32 *)((char *)self + 0x170)` exactly as the promoted sibling does.
* `Mem_Alloc` is 1-arg (`include/mem.h`); the m2c draft's
  `Mem_Alloc(arg0, size)` pushed the size into r4 and rotated the whole
  argument chain.
* a stale `// FLAG: -Os` on such a draft silently scores 15% at -O2: the
  house default is `-O2 -G0 -mcpu=750 -fno-common` and nothing here wants
  `-Os`.

## 6fy — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x80069DA0, 280B, m2c DIFF 4.3% -> **EXACT**,
0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **a table pointer REPEATED in two
blocks needs TWO DISTINCT temps to keep a long-lived parameter in its incoming
arg register**; plus the byte-input member of the recipe-231 int->f64 family

1. **Split one shared temp per BLOCK to restore an incoming-arg register home.**
   `0x80069DA0` loads the same `*(void ***)(arg0+0x1B8)` table twice (an early-out
   virtual call in the `arg1==0` block, a second one at the tail). Written with
   ONE shared `t`, GCC coalesces both loads onto a single pseudo, that pseudo
   grabs r5, and the long-lived `arg0` parameter is bumped out of its r5 home
   into r6 — a *pure allocation* effect that flips `mr r5,r3`->`mr r6,r3` and
   then every `0x48(r5)`->`0x48(r6)` / `0x1b8(r5)` displacement in the body
   (80% -> dead). With `void **t` in the first block and `void **u` in the
   second, cc1 keeps them as separate webs (null path's table in r9, tail's in
   r6 — exactly as the want has them, in DIFFERENT registers), arg0 keeps r5,
   and the body goes byte-exact. **So: when want keeps a parameter in a hard arg
   register (`mr r5,r3` + `or. r4,r4,r4` at the top) and your got sinks it to
   r6/r10/r11, do not reach for a `register` pin — first try un-sharing the
   OTHER live temp per block.** (Same family as recipe 57/§6w-102 "unique temp
   names per logical web", but the axis here is the *repeated load*, not the name.)
2. **The indirect call's arity decides where the parameters live.** Typing the
   fn pointer honestly as `void (*)(void *)` (1 arg, as the promoted siblings
   `vcall_80069D68` / `vcall_80069F1C` / `fn_80069D24` do) keeps `arg1` in r4 and
   `arg0` in r5 with zero `mr`s before the `blrl` — the r4/r5/r6 seen at the call
   are just dead live values, and want shows exactly that. An m2c-invented
   6-arg prototype instead forces GCC to materialise r3..r8 up front and the
   prologue collapses.
3. **Byte -> float: the signed cast is load-bearing, and it must NOT be a
   signed-char LOAD** (completes recipe 231 for the byte case; recipe 88/152
   cover the call-result case). Want per site: `lbz` / `xoris rX,rX,0x8000` /
   `stw` / `stw 0x4330` / `lfd` / `fsub` (pool `0x4330000080000000`) / `frsp`.
   - `(f32)(f64)(s32)*c` with `u8 *c` -> exact (the `(s32)` cast is what emits
     the single `xoris` + the 2^52+2^31 bias subtract). `(s16)` casts compile
     identically.
   - `(f32)(f64)*c` (no cast, unsigned) -> **1 insn SHORT per site** (no
     `xoris`; bias becomes plain 2^52) and every later index slides.
   - `(f32)(f64)*c` with `s8 *c` -> an EXTRA `extsb` before the `xoris`, so it is
     1 insn LONG per site. So `char`/`s8` (signed on PPC) is the wrong spelling
     for this shape: read the byte UNSIGNED and widen it to a signed int in C.
4. **Pool caveat (doc-14) recurs, with a new twist: the game's pair is ADJACENT.**
   `0x80294970` = `0x4330000080000000` (ngccc's synthesized int->f64 bias) and
   `0x80294978` = 255.0f sit 8 bytes apart in `.rodata2`, bias FIRST — i.e. the
   original source used the `255.0f` LITERAL (not an `extern`), and the compiled
   object reproduces exactly the same 16-byte pair in its module `.rodata` in the
   same order. Matching score is unaffected (`lfd`/`lfs` pool displacements live
   in the low bits the ADDR16_HA/LO mask hides — verified: mask 0xFFFF0000 at
   those offsets), but promote still needs that pool routed to `.rodata2`
   (same class as fn_80195F98 / fn_80195E0C). **Use the literal form when want's
   pool holds the bias and the literal adjacently — it is evidence about the
   source, and it costs nothing.**
5. Verifying a masked EXACT with branches: read the **RELA addend**, never the
   disassembler's operand field (extends 6ft). Here `.rela.text` carries
   addends `0x34` @0x14, `0x108` @0x30, `0x108` @0x3C against the section symbol,
   which resolve to displacements `0x20`/`0xD8`/`0xCC` — bit-identical to want's
   `bne`/`b`/`beq` fields. The in-field value in a `-c` object is a placeholder.

## 6fz — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x800679E8, 444B, m2c NEAR 93.7% -> **EXACT**, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **int+int keeps the source operand order, int+POINTER does not — so an `s32`-typed pointer FIELD buys the offset-first address sum with NO cast (and it flips `stbx`, not just `add`/`lwzx`)**; plus **naming a loop's invariant STORE VALUE moves the doloop counter off r0**

`Unk_DCEB657B` ctor cluster (siblings 0x800669D0 / 66CA0 / 67380 / 677F0 / 67BEC /
6800C). The skeleton came from the draft; the last 7 words were one `stbx` operand
slot, the `mtctr` source register and the order of two preheader `li`s.

**1. The offset-first address sum (§6k-66 / recipe 140 without the cast).** The fill
is 12 byte stores at `base[off+k]`, `base` reloaded from the struct every store
(a byte store may alias the pointer field, so no CSE): both retail and the u8-field variant load offset 0x114 of the struct home into r11 and then r9, but retail places the offset register in the rA slot of the indexed byte store and adds offset-first while the variant places the base in rA and adds pointer-first.

`expand_store` takes base = PLUS-operand-0, index = operand-1, and
`canonicalize_address` never swaps two REGs — but the FRONT END does: an
`int + pointer` is rebuilt as `pointer + int`, while an `int + int` keeps the
written order. So `off + (s32)ptr` flips it — and so does nothing else. **The
clean spelling needs no cast at all: declare the field `s32` (the shared
`Unk_DCEB657B` already declares `unk0x114/0x118/0x11C` as `s32` in 16 files) and
write `*(u8 *)(off + arg0->unk0x114 + k)`.** `(char *)(off + (s32)ptr)` and
`off + (u8 *)ptr + k` both canonicalise back to pointer-first — the cast has to
disappear into the FIELD TYPE, not sit on the expression. `stbx` was NOT in
§6k-66/140's list (`add`/`lwzx`/`stwx`); the same flip hits the indexed byte
store. Diagnostic: want's `stbx rX, rA, rB` with the LOOP-VARYING register in
the rA slot ⇒ the original wrote the sum offset-first.

**2. A named invariant store value un-pins the doloop counter from r0.** Want's
preheader is `li r9,2 / mtctr r9 / li r0,0x80 / li r10,0`; the draft gave
`li r0,2 / mtctr r0 / li r10,0 / li r0,0x80`. A bare `0x80` literal is
rematerialised late and loses the register race to the countdown pseudo, which
then lands in r0 and re-orders the two `li`s. Naming it fixes both at once:

    u8 fill = 0x80;                 /* before the loop */
    do { *(u8 *)(off + arg0->unk0x114) = fill; ... } while (--ctr);

-> EXACT (111/111). Signature: want shows `li rN,K; mtctr rN` with **N != 0**
(`li r9,K`) while got emits the classic `li r0,K; mtctr r0`. Loop shape, init
order, decl order and `ctr` width all made ZERO difference here (four variants
scored an identical 96.4%); the constant's temp-ness was the only lever. Same
family as §6fr/§6fy's "named temp moves the colour map", but the temp is a
CONSTANT and the visible effect is the count register.

**Verification** (masked EXACT, so check the branches — 6fy item 5): `.text` is
444B and there is no `.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss` in the object (no private pool);
every relocation is `fn_80062D44`/`fn_80062BBC`/`Mem_Alloc` and the three
`lbl_8029466C/70/88` HA+LO pairs. The `beq`/`bne`/`bdnz` in-field operands are
the same placeholders (+0x84/+0x6C/+0xA8/+0xC4/+0xE0/+0x100) that the promoted
byte-identical sibling `src/fn_80066834.c` emits for the same construct, so the
disassembler's `beq 0x80067ad4` is not a mismatch — the RELA addends resolve.

## 6ga — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x8007F714, 228B, m2c DIFF 8.8% -> **EXACT**, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **one shared local per BLOCK is not enough — a per-block temp split shifts the WHOLE colour map by exactly one, so the first split leaves you one register short everywhere and the SECOND split lands the last ones**; plus **the 4-byte RGBA local must be a `u8[4]` written byte-wise, never `(s32 *)((char *)&sp + k)`**

`Unk_C7387A53` colour getter (`return out` recipe-249 out-param). The m2c
draft was so corrupt that all three stages below had to be fixed first; the
*residual* 18 words were then **pure register numbers**, which is the
§6ek/§6fy "colour map" signature rather than a scheduling wall.

`obj+0x5E` and at `leaf+0xC`), and the `0x58` field is an ARRAY that is
dereferenced once more (`entry = *(*(void **)(obj+0x58))`) — m2c dropped that
load, which cost a word and put every later branch in the wrong block. The
local is a 4-byte value written one byte at a time, so it must be `u8 col[4]`
with eight `stb`s; the m2c spelling `*(s32 *)((char *)&sp8 + k) = 0` folds to a
single `stw` and shifts the whole tail. GCC then emits `addi r9,r1,8` +
`mr rX,r9` + `stb …,8(r1)` / `stb …,k(rX)` exactly as want — the `8(r1)` for
offset 0 vs `k(rX)` for 1..3 is GCC materialising `&col[0]` for `col[0]` and
`&col + k` for the rest; **any** of array / 4×`u8` struct / `char`/`u8` lvalue
form reproduces it, so the local's *type* is not a lever (4 variants: all
50.9%).

**2. Per-block temp split #1 (50.9% -> 68.4%).** The then-arm's `dst` and the
else-arm's pointer shared one local; split into `dst` / `dst2` and both landed
in r11 as want has them. Same lever as §6fy item 1 / recipe 57.

**3. Per-block temp split #2 (68.4% -> EXACT).** With `dst`/`dst2` split, 18
words still differed and they were a **uniform shift of exactly one register**:

| web | want | after split #1 |
|---|---|---|
| `arg1->unk0x30` | r10 | r11 |
| `&col` home (`mr rX,r9`) | r7 | r8 |
| `arg0` home (`mr rX,r3`) | r6 | r7 |
| else-arm's `arg1->unk0x20` | **r4** | **r8** |

One local still spanned both mutually exclusive blocks (`temp_r8` = then-arm's
`unk0x54` object AND else-arm's `unk0x20` value), so reload coalesced the two
webs onto ONE hard register; that pseudo then took r8, pushed the long-lived
`arg1` parameter off its incoming **r4** home into the then-arm, and every

— every register fixed at once, no pins, no asm. **Generalised: when the
residual is a uniform ±1 shift on every long-lived web, look for a single local
written in two exclusive blocks; splitting it is worth more than any pin, and
one split can expose a second sharing further down (apply §6fy item 1
repeatedly until the map stops moving).**

**Dead ends worth recording** (both reach a "good" tail and then strand you):
* dropping the `else` for a sequential second `if` gives the SAME good colour

* rewriting the `else` as `goto end;` also produces want's jump but lands back
  in the bad map (18 diffs) — the block MERGE, not arg1's live range, is what
  the split is really sensitive to.

**Verification** (masked EXACT, so the branches are checked per §6fy item 5 /
§6ft): `.text` = 228B = `size:0xE4`, and the object's only sections with
content are `.symtab/.strtab/.shstrtab/.rela.text` — **no `.rodata`, no private
pool**. All 7 relocations are internal `.text` `R_PPC_REL14` (6) + `R_PPC_REL24`
(1) with addends `0xA0,0xA0,0xD0,0xD0,0xD0,0xD0,0xD0`, which resolve to
exactly want's two else-entry branches and five merge branches; re-encoding the
BD/BD-suffix fields from those addends reproduces **all 228 want bytes**.

## 6gb — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x80093E4C, 252B, m2c DIFF 6.3% → **EXACT**, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags beyond the project default + per-object `-mps-float`, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **write the loop-invariant load INSIDE the loop body — cc1 `hoist` then parks it in the ROTATED loop's ENTRY block (after the `bge` preheader guard) instead of the preheader, and that is what lets the loop's base register DIE at the next base load and coalesce the walk pointer**

`fn_80093E4C` is a ctor: 10 stores + an 8-pair `__ps_t` copy run + an empty
`li r0,4 / mtctr / bdnz .` window + a `for` loop with two early `return`s.
The m2c draft is 6.3% (it has **4** parameters, not 5 — `r5` is a real
argument, the 64-byte PS source, which m2c rendered as a run of `0;`).
Six semantic steps + one loop-placement step took it to 100%. The reusable parts:

1. **A rotated loop's invariant code belongs to the loop-ENTRY block, and you can
   choose which block it lands in from the source.** Want's preheader is
   `[lhz n][li i][cmpw][bge exit]` and everything else — including the two
   loop-invariant loads — sits in the loop's single body block. cc1's `hoist`
   inserts a hoisted expression at the top of the **loop header**, so a load
   written INSIDE the body ends up in that entry block, whereas the *same* load
   written as a statement BEFORE the `for` stays in the preheader. Measured on the
   same body, and the ONLY difference:
   * invariant load in the preheader → `[li][lwz][cmpw][bge]` / `[lhz][mr][cmpwi]`
   * invariant load in the body     → `[li][cmpw][bge]` / `[lwz][mr][lhz][cmpwi]` ✓
   This is §6ft's "the back edge tells you where an invariant load lives" seen from
   the writing side.

2. **…and that block choice is what unlocks the register coalescing.** With the
   invariant load in the entry block, `r4` (the loop's only parameter) dies at the
   NEXT base-pointer load, so cc1 coalesces the strength-reduced walk pointer into
   `r4` — and, with `r4` consumed, the index falls into `r10` and the `n` copy into
   `r8`. Exactly want. With the load in the preheader, `r4` is still live across it,
   no coalescing is legal, and the whole pool shifts by one: `p=r10, i=r8, n=r7`.
   **7 diffs / 88.9% → 0 diffs / 100% from moving one statement.** So a residual
   that reads as a bare 3-register `loop_alloc` role swap
   (`lwz rX,0x58(r4)` wants `r4` and got `r10`) is often *not* an allocator tie at
   all — audit the BLOCK PLACEMENT of the load that feeds it first. This is the loop
   counterpart of §6fg-1 ("a role swap is not source-reachable"), and it is
   reachable: the pin was worth 9.7% and destroyed the function, while the block
   move was worth 11.1% and fixed it.

3. **Inside the loop, prefer the INDEXED element spelling over an explicit walking
   pointer when want shows the base load in the loop-ENTRY block** — this is the
   complement of §6fw. Both emit `lwz r9,0(p); addi p,p,4`, but the walking-pointer
   form (`p = arg1->f; … *p++`) puts `lwz p,0x58(r4)` in the preheader while
   `arg1->f[i]` strength-reduces it into the entry block. Conversely when the
   unroller eats the loop, §6fw's explicit pointer is still the fix. **Read the
   want's base load: before the loop's `bge` ⇒ explicit pointer; after it ⇒
   indexed.**

4. **`if (A == 0 || B > 0) { work; }` vs `if (A != 0 && B <= 0) return;`** — one
   word, but it is `blelr` in want and `ble <block>` in got. When want's guard
   branch is a `b*lr` (a genuine early return) rather than a `b*` to a nearby
   block, write the negated guard with an explicit `return` at the top of the
   function; the positive-`if` wrapper never gets the return tail-fold.

5. **`s32 f5C; u16 f5E;` silently promotes `f5E` to +0x60 and shifts every later
   member.** A 4-byte field ending at 0x5D leaves 0x5E unaddressable — write
   `u16 f5C; u16 f5E;`. The symptom is one stray `sth r0,0x62(r3)` where want has
   `stw r0,0x60(r3)`, plus three shifted offsets; §6db's array rule (`s32 sp[4]`)
   is the generic form. Check the offsets of EVERY member a store touches, not just
   the ones m2c named.

6. **The PS copy run and its interleaved integer stores match with plain
   `__ps_t` element assignment** (`dst[0]=src[0]` … `dst[7]=src[7]`, per-object
   `-mps-float`) when the struct member is a real `__ps_t unk08[8]` — the 8
   `psq_l`/`psq_st` pairs then interleave with the `li`/`lis`/`cmpwi` constants
   exactly as retail has them. 22/22 words byte-identical on the first try.

* **Audit of the EXACT (left in `src/wip/`, NOT promoted):** object `.text` =
   252 B = `symbols.txt size:0xFC` = the header `size=`, and the only sections are
   `.text/.symtab/.strtab/.shstrtab/.rela.text` — **no `.rodata`, no private float
   pool**; 0 emitted inline instructions. All 7 relocations hand-decoded
   (§6bw): four `R_PPC_REL24` with addends `0x8C`, `0x9C`, `0xA8`, `0xEC` →
   want's `bge exit` / `beq body` / `blelr`-adjacent targets (`+0xC0`+`0x8C`=
   loop head), and the `R_PPC_REL14` at +0x08 has addend `8` at PC `8` ⇒
   displacement 0 ⇒ the **`bdnz .` really is self-targeting** after the link
   (capstone's `bdnz +0x80093e5c` is the unrelocated misread AGENTS warns about);
   the two `ADDR14`/`ADDR16_LO` pairs against `lbl_80301820` have addend 0, so the
   linker writes `lis r10,0x8030` + `lwz/stw …,0x1820(r10)` = want. **Promotable.**

## 7b — Spill-heavy `-mps-float` bodies: the volatile pair-scratch rule (w75, 2026-10-02)

Measured on `src/wip/fn_800A0FFC.c` (0x800A0FFC, 476 B, parked 10.2% -> 36.1%,
object now SIZE-EXACT). Generalises to the whole 0x800A0xxx/0x801Bxxxx PS zone
(0x800A0E6C, 0x800A0F2C, 0x800A9200, 0x800A9298, 0x800A95EC …) and probably to
every function whose want has `psq_l` + `psq_st` pairs and a `volatile double _dummy`
frame.

1. **Frame formula for a pair-scratch array: `frame = 0x30 + 8*n`** under
   `-mps-float` when the body declares `volatile S V[n]` with
   `typedef union { __ps_t p; f32 w[2]; s32 i[2]; } S;`. Verified n=6..14:
   0x60/0x70/0x78/0x80/0x88/0x90/0x98/0xA0. So the scratch slot count is
   *readable straight off the want frame*: `n = (want_frame - 0x30) / 8`, and
   element `k` sits at `8*(k+1)`. That gives you the stmw/stfd/LR offsets for
   free (GPR save at `8*(n+1)`, FPR at `+8`/`+16`, LR at `frame+4`).
2. **An `s32` out-param passed by address must live INSIDE the scratch array**,
   not as its own local. Retail keeps it at `V[6]` == `0x38(r1)`; a separate
   `s32` local goes to `0x60`, which shifts every later slot and drops 36.1% ->
   25.2%. Declare the third param `volatile s32 *` so no cast is needed.
3. **The union-with-`.w[1]` idiom reproduces retail's DEAD scalar stores.**
   `V[1].w[1] = eps;` / `V[7].w[1] = 1.0f;` land in the *upper half* of the
   preceding pair slot (0x14 / 0x44 / 0x4c) exactly like retail's
   `stfs f30,0x14(r1)` / `stfs f0,0x44(r1)`. Same for dead pair duplicates
   (`V[4] = D`, `V[5] = C`) — the idiom is documented in the matched sibling
   `src/fn_801B19DC.c`. A plain non-volatile array loses some of them (18.5%).
4. **ngccc CSEs repeated volatile reads of the same array element, but NOT two
   reads consumed by the same multiply.** `mul(V[1].p, V[1].p)` emits TWO
   `psq_l`; retail emits one. Corollary for the source shape: if your want has
   ONE load per element per block, stage it into a `__ps_t` temp; if the want
   has TWO, read the array directly in the builtins. Getting this backwards is
   worth ~15 points (21.8% staged-everything vs 36.1% all-direct) — 0x800A0FFC
   needs BOTH shapes in the same body (blocks 1/3 staged, block 5 direct).
5. **Blocker that is NOT semantics:** with pure C (no
   `register __ps_t x __asm__("frN")` pins, no asm windows) ProDG picks a
   different-but-valid colour for the PS web in every block — the instruction
   MULTISET per basic block matches retail exactly, only the FPR numbers
   differ (retail keeps the accumulator in f0 with the const in f13/f12;
   plain C gets f13/f12 with the const in f10). Scheduling flags are all
   neutral here (`-fno-sched-spec`, `-fno-sched-interblock`, `-fno-gcse`,
   `-fno-thread-jumps`): the frame, the dead stores and the constant page
   anchors all come out right, so do not burn time on flags — the gap is
   regalloc colour only.

## 7c — `stbu` chain / `volatile` re-read / named byte temps: the three levers that took fn_80078330 (432 B) from m2c DIFF 6.5% to EXACT (w75, 2026-10-02)

`fn_80078330` = tile-grid loop: `fn_80078104` writes 4 bytes into 4 `u8` locals,
they land in `dst[row*ncols*4 + col*4 .. +3]` gated on a `u32 flags` word
(`0x200` -> 4 bytes; `flags==0` -> 4 bytes with `0xFF` last; `4`/`8`/`0x10` ->
one byte at `p[3]`, the first two also advance `p` by 4). 6.5% -> **EXACT, 0 asm,
0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers**; every one of the 108 words matches and all 11
REL14/REL24 targets resolve to want's addresses.

**1. The `stbu`-chain and the `addi / stbu / addi` triple are SOURCE-SHAPE, not
scheduler choices.** ngccc/reload only emits the *incrementing* store form when the
RTL itself contains the pointer increment between the stores; `p[k] = v` + a later
`p += n` never fuses. Measured on this body:
* `*p++ = a; *p++ = b; *p++ = c; *p++ = d;` -> `stbx / stbu v,1(rX) / stbu / stb` (want).
* `p[0]=a; p[1]=b; p[2]=c; p[3]=d;` -> `stb off(rX)` x3 + `addi rX,4` (**1 word
  shorter**, so the masked score collapses ~40 points when you get this backwards).
* want's 3-word "store at `p[3]`, then advance 4" (`addi rX,2 / stbu v,1(rX) / addi rX,1`)
  has **no natural C spelling** — it is the source
  `p += 2; *++p = v; p++;`. Equivalent-looking variants do NOT work and some are
  outright miscompiles: `p += 3; *p = v; p++;` folds the `+3` into the `stbu` and
  then adds the `p++` on top (**p advances 5**), `p += 2; p[1] = v; p += 2;` gives
  `addi 2 / stb 1 / addi 2` (right count, wrong opcodes). So read a want
  `addi rX,2/stbu v,1(rX)/addi rX,1` literally as "+2, store-and-bump, +1".

**2. A `volatile` qualifier on ONE of several textually identical re-reads is the
lever for the loop-header CSE, and it is worth ~30 points because it changes the
callee-saved register COUNT.** This body reads `1 << *(u8 *)(arg0+6)` four times
(loop guard preheader, call arg, post-call stride, latch) and want keeps all four
loads. With plain C, GCC/loop passes share the *rotated loop's header* pseudo with
the body use (preheader value flows into the body), which keeps that value live
across the call and adds TWO callee-saved registers: a register for the hoisted
`li 0xff` constant (doc 79 family) and a second `mfcr` CR-save register for the
extra hoisted condition. 58.3% -> **87.0%** and frame `0x48 -> 0x40`,
`stmw r19 -> stmw r21`, and *all 11 callee-saved assignments then lined up by
themselves*. Put `volatile` on the smallest possible number of sites: only the
call-arg read needed it (the other two already re-read on their own).
(Other drafts already use `volatile` for CSE webs — e.g. `src/wip/fn_8009A8CC.c`
— but the loop-header case and its register-count consequence are new.)

**3. Named byte temps place individual `lbz`s at chosen slots in a byte-store run.**
With `*p++ = b0..b3` sched2 interleaves load/store pairs
(`lbz/stbu/lbz/stbu/lbz/stb`) and reload recycles r0/r9. want groups the middle two
loads (`lbz b1 / lbz b2 / stbu / lbz b3 / stbu`) and needs a THIRD scratch (r11).
Staging the middle bytes through locals — `u8 t1,t2,t3; *p++ = b0; t1 = b1; t2 = b2;
*p++ = t1; t3 = b3; *p++ = t2; *p++ = t3;` — reproduces want's slot-for-slot
(87.0% -> 100%). The staging must be *interleaved at the same points*, not hoisted:
declaring/assigning all four up front gives 75.9%, and staging only the middle two
gives 89.8%. C89 detail: cc1 here rejects a declaration after a statement inside a
block, so declare at the top of the block and assign in place.

**4. Diagnostic caveat: `cc1 -dr` is NOT trustworthy for post-reload placement in
this file.** The `-dr` dump showed the `arg3 == 0` compare AFTER the call (correct)
while the real pipeline emits it BEFORE the call with its own `mfcr`/`mtcrf 0x80`
pair; `-dr` also emits a spurious `crxor cr1` that the real pipeline never has. Use
`ngccc ... -S` (works, and matches the object exactly) to inspect layout, and treat
`-dr` as a structural sketch only. Corollary for callers: **an object built from
this assembler is RELA** — a branch's word holds the *addend*, not a PC-relative
displacement, so capstone decodes garbage targets and even points outside `.text`.
Read branch targets from the `.rela.text` addends (`target = section_base + addend`).

## 6gc — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x800629D4, 256 B, m2c DIFF 21.1% → **EXACT**, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **`x*3` folds to shift+add and only a 64-bit product yields `mulli`; a mis-declared callee arity is a 4-register regalloc shift; a separate local blocks local-alloc coalescing**

`fn_800629D4` = bone/node-setup loop (`fn_80102A40` 7 args, `fn_80103234`,
two `fn_8000728C` bbox copies). The whole function was register-allocation
after the first two fixes; all 9 callee-saved registers r23..r31 land on the
right variables and all 108 words match.

1. **`x * 3` NEVER emits `mulli` — the reciprocal of §6fj.** Measured on
   ngccc/3.9.3 with the project flags, the shift+add form wins for exactly
   `{3,5,7,9}`: `x*3 -> slwi r0,rX,1 / add rD,r0,rX`, `x*5 -> slwi …,2 / add`,
   `x*7 -> slwi …,3 / subf`, `x*9 -> slwi …,3 / add`. Everything else
   (`6,10,11,12,…`) gets one `mulli`. This is *stable across every context* —
   return value, store, pointer add, divisor, cast, `volatile` operand, `(x+x)*1`,
   `(n + n*2)`, `3*x`, struct-array indexing — all still give shift+add, so there
   is **no plain C spelling that produces `mulli` for `*3`**. What DOES work is a
   64-bit product truncated back to 32 bits:
   `s32 t = (s32)(n * 3LL);` → `mulli rD,rX,3` (one insn, high half dead).
   `s32 t = (s32)((s64)n * 3);` and `(u64)n * 3` are equivalent.
   `n * 3LL` **inline** does *not* work (the front end re-folds before `expand`),
   and `s64 t = n * 3;` does *not* either (that one drops to `mullw` with a
   `li r0,3`), so the **named `s32` temp holding a truncated 64-bit product is
   load-bearing**. Scan the DOL for the idiom before hunting: `mulli …,3` occurs
   only ~8 times in 3 MiB, all in this 3-stride setup family
   (fn_80056308 0x8005634C + 0x8005644C, fn_800629D4 0x80062A08) and in SDK code
   (`EXI*`, `GX*`), i.e. it is a real game-source spelling, not a ngccc quirk.
2. **A callee arity m2c gets wrong is worth ~8 register assignments.** The want
   sets **only r3** before `bl 0x80103234`, and `fn_80103234`'s own matched body
   reads only r3. m2c's `fn_80103234(arg0, arg1, ptr)` therefore added two live
   uses of `arg0` and one of `arg1`, and both parameters jumped to the top of
   GCC's allocno priority (arg0/arg1 hold r29..r31, six variables shifted).
   Declaring `extern s32 fn_80103234(void *);` and passing one argument took the
   function from 34.8% to **96.9%** — every register correct, 2 words left.
   Same class as recipe 3/11/15/128 and §6at-4: **audit the want's `bl` for which
   argument registers are actually written before it**, not what the callee's
   matched signature says it could use.
3. **One variable reused for two overlapping values gets COALESCED by local-alloc
   and takes the wrong register.** The want computes `q = p5 + n*10 (+2)` into
   scratch `r8`, loads `*(s32*)q`, and only then forms `p6 = q + 4` into a
   callee-saved register. Reusing one local for both lets local-alloc coalesce
   `q` and `q+4` into a single pseudo, which parks `p6` in r30 (highest priority
   after the params) instead of r25. **Give the short-lived pre-value its own
   `char *` local and let the post-value be a different one** — 26.6% → 34.8%.
   Generalises the §6at-4 "one shared local per BLOCK" rule from colour maps to
   scalar address chains.
4. **The loop shape is `if (i < n) { preheader; do {…} while (i < n); }`, and the
   bound must be RE-READ from memory in both tests.** The want loads the bound
   three times (`lwz r0, 4(r26)` at 0x800629EC, 0x80062A34, 0x80062AB0); caching
   it in a local lets `ivopts` turn the loop into a countdown
   (`cmpwi …,0 / ble` + `addi rD,rD,-1 / cmpwi / bne`) and the whole body
   re-schedules. Re-reading the field also puts the two preheader insns
   (`addi r28,r31,0x90` / `li r30,0`) *after* the entry guard and before the back
   edge — want's `blt` targets 0x80062A50, not 0x80062A48, which is how you tell
   a preheader from a hoisted loop body. This is §4m pattern 7 (guard form)
   one step further: the loop needs BOTH a pre-test and a bottom test reading
   the *same memory field*.
5. **`int + int` keeps source operand order, and the order is per call site.**
   The fn_80102A40 / fn_80103234 arguments want `add rX, base, off`; the two bbox
   calls want `add rX, off, base` — same two pseudos, opposite order, in one body.
   Writing the bbox arg offset-first (`off + arg0->unk0x8C + K`) reproduces it;
   swapping the *other* calls' order does not perturb them. That is the §6fz
   int+int rule with the sign that pointer arithmetic loses the order.

## 6ez — 2026-10-02 single pick: **the `psq_st` + `lfs` + `fmr` triple is ngccc's V4SF→SF lane extraction from a NON-VOLATILE `__ps_t` local** — the container's `volatile` is what removes the copy (fn_800C494C, 5.4% → 48.6%, 0 asm, 0 flags)

`fn_800C494C` (444 B, `-mps-float`, 4 candidates + 4 denominators, 8 stack
slots) was parked twice: once as "pure FPR register allocation", then (after
an earlier round) with a confident but **wrong** mechanism — "`lq` instead of
`psq_l`" — which is not what ngccc emits here (probe: `__ps_t q = arg1->g38;
__ps_t p = arg0->a1; __builtin_ps_sub(p,q)` gives `psq_l f0,56(r5)` +
`psq_l f1,8(r3)` + `ps_sub f1,f1,f0`; a `__ps_t` load IS a `psq_l`, always).

### The real rule — three lane-read spellings, three different lowerings

| source | emitted |
|---|---|
| `PV c; c.p = <pair>; v = c.f.hi;` (plain, non-volatile `PV` local) | `psq_st <pair>,slot(r1)` · `lfs <scratch>,slot(r1)` · **`fmr <v>,<scratch>`** |
| `volatile PV fr[8]; fr[k].p = <pair>; v = fr[k].f.hi;` | `psq_st <pair>,slot(r1)` · `lfs <v>,slot(r1)` — **no copy** |
| `PV c; c.p = <pair>; v = *(f32 *)&c.p;` / non-volatile *struct* member | `psq_l` + `ps_mr` (the `psq_l` is dead) |

So want's `psq_st` / `lfs` / `fmr` triple is **positive evidence that the
slot's container is a plain (non-volatile) pair local**: cc1 has no register
lowering for V4SF→SF, so it spills the pair to the local's stack home, reloads
lane 0 as a scalar, and keeps the reload pseudo distinct from the value pseudo
(regmove does not merge them), leaving the copy. It is not a spill under
pressure, and it is not a "volatile reload" — the 8 slots here never receive
real pressure (13 live FPRs, 32 registers). **The frame is the proof**:
`stwu -0x48` = exactly 8 eight-byte slots = 2 volatile dead-pair stores
(`vd`,`vt`) + 6 lane-extraction homes (`c0`,`c1`,`dn0..dn3`), and the slot
offset order is the order of *first use*.

### What else it unlocked

* **`f32` `register`-var pins (`__asm__("frN")`) bind reliably; `__ps_t` pins
  bind only when the variable is FED BY A LOAD** (recipes §6da). A pinned
  `__ps_t` that is a *copy destination* (`sp = t`) is silently ignored and cc1
  allocates the copy's register itself — that is why retail's `ps_mr f6,f0`
  (a pinned live operand) has no plain-C spelling. Do not read a failed `__ps_t`
  pin as "cc1 materialises it as a GPR load".
* Pinning the *f32 consumer* of a lane extract (`register f32 den __asm__("fr0")`
  / `fr13` in each switch arm, `nb = -best` into `fr12`) reproduces retail's
  asymmetric reload/copy registers **and** the separate `fneg` register — 4
  more words for free. The copies only appear when the lane has a *second live
  name* (`f32 den = dn0.f.hi; return best/den;`), never when it feeds the
  division directly.
* Flags are dead here: default 48.6% beats `-fno-schedule-insns` (41.4%) and
  `-fno-schedule-insns2` (36.0%); identical output on all five ProDG versions
  (3.5 / 3.5b140 / 3.7 / 3.8.1 / 3.9.3) for the lane-extraction probe, so the
  idiom is not a compiler-version artefact.

Residual after this pass (parked, `src/wip/fn_800C494C.c`): the `ps_mr f6,f0`
operand copy, the `d`/`n` register swap, retail's cross-jump-less case 1/3
tails (cc1 cross-jumps them → 109 words vs 111). **673 `psq_st`+`lfs`+`fmr`
sites exist in the DOL** — every one of them should be re-tried with a plain
non-volatile container before being parked as a reload-copy wall.

## Registry list-walk family (fn_80060xxx–fn_80062xxx) — two new rules
(w75/0x800620EC, 2026-10-02. Draft parked at **NEAR 85.4%**, was DIFF 10.1%.)

This family (matched siblings `src/fn_80062250.c`, `src/fn_8006230C.c`, wip
`fn_80061F9C.c`) is the "registry at +0x10 / count at +0x14 / u16 counters at
0x4A,0x4C,0x4E" node. Two rules took fn_800620EC from 1% to 85%.

**178. An all-locals-at-8-byte-stride frame ⇒ a local anonymous struct of
`T *volatile` + explicit `s32 pad` pairs.** fn_800620EC's frame is `stwu -0x68`
with locals at 0x08,0x10,…,0x50 (ten slots, 8 bytes apart) and **four slots
that are written and never read** (0x40, 0x48, 0x50, 0x30) plus a dead 0x18
store in the tail. Dead stores surviving -O2 ⇒ the slots are `volatile`; the
4-byte gaps ⇒ each field is followed by an explicit pad. Declaring

```c
struct { Node *volatile slot08; s32 pad0C; Node *volatile slot10; s32 pad14; ... } s;
```

reproduces the frame, the `stmw r29,0x5c` save set, the per-iteration reloads
and all ten slot displacements **byte-for-byte** (1.1% → 64.0%). This is the
same idiom as the already-matched `fn_8006230C.c`
(`struct { void *slot208; s32 pad20c; void * volatile slot210; }`), generalised
to N slots — reach for it whenever WANT shows redundant pointer stores and a
reload-per-use loop. The write-only slots are what prove `volatile`; a plain
(non-volatile) struct lets cc1 delete them and the frame shrinks.

**179. Split the pre-header variable from the loop-tail variable when WANT
homes them in different registers.** cc1 gives one C variable ONE hard
register. In fn_800620EC WANT homes loop 1's guard cursor in **r0** and its
tail re-load in **r9**, and the guard head in **r9** but the tail head in
**r11** — i.e. four different pseudo homes for what reads like two variables.
Writing the tail with the *same* variables as the pre-header
(`w1 = s.slot10; h1 = s.slot08; n1 = w1->next;`) makes cc1 coalesce each pair
into one pseudo and force a single home, which costs every register field on
those instructions. Giving the tail its own names

```c
wt = s.slot10; ht = s.slot08; nt = wt->next;   /* distinct from w1/h1 */
```

is worth **+9 words (74.2% → 83.1%)** on its own. Same trick applies to the
*second* identical reload of `c->next`: `nx2 = c->next; s.slot48 = c;
s.slot38 = nx2;` hoists the reload above the `s.slot48` store exactly as WANT
does (+2 words, 83.1% → 85.4%), whereas reordering the two statements fixes the
load but breaks the store order. **General rule: when several WANT registers
differ only in which local name feeds the instruction, you are looking at
coalesced pseudos — split the C variable, do not reorder the statements.**

**What is left on this one (do not re-derive):** the 11-word `arg0`↔`&arg0->list`
r29/r31 swap is the §6a-6 / §6q-133 saved-reg coin-flip. Nothing in pure C
moves it: dropping the `lp` variable collapses the frame to 0x60 and turns the
reload into `0x10(r31)`; `register List *lp`, declaration order, hoisting the
`lp = &arg0->list` assignment, a local copy of the parameter, and adding
`arg0`-based refs in/out of loop2 all fail — rtl-cse folds every
`arg0->list.*` back onto the `lp` pseudo, so `arg0` can never gain an in-loop
reference and out-rank `lp`'s loop-weighted priority. Also unresolved: `owner =
sub->owner;` — cc1's pre-RA scheduler hoists the `mr r3,sub` arg-copy above
the `lwz r30,4(r9)`; block/function scope, `volatile owner`, a `Sub *q` copy,
the comma-expression call pair and per-parameter proto types all fail to flip
it. Flags are dead here (default 85.4% beats `-fno-schedule-insns` 18.0%,
`-fno-schedule-insns2` 55.1%, `-fno-gcse` 71.9%).

## 2026-10-02 (w75/0x8004E734, m2c DIFF 4.3% → NEAR **93.0%**, 0 asm, 0 flags) — the list-cell idiom, the `sp8 = temp` copy, and a structural trigger for the doc-28 CR save

Parked at 93.0% (107/115); the only residual is the 8 frame-layout words (see
item 5). Four transferable findings:

1. **The doubly-linked-list cell must be the ADDRESS-TAKEN pointer local, with
   the link words written through a punned struct — never a real struct.**
   ```c
   No4E734Node *sp8;                                   /* cell = {node,prev,next} */
   ((Unk_59AB5482 *)&sp8)->unk0x4 = NULL;               /* house idiom, cf. the      */
   ((Unk_59AB5482 *)&sp8)->unk0x8 = NULL;               /* matched fn_8003FFC4/64  */
   sp8 = node;
   CObject_AddRefLink((CStruct *)sp8, &sp8);
   ```
   This one construct decides **two** things at once. (a) Because the local's
   address escapes, the object stays in the frame slot and every later use is a
   `lwz rX,8(r1)` reload — a *real* struct lets cc1 lift the node into a
   callee-saved register instead (want: 6 `lwz r3,8(r1)` reloads, no node reg).
   (b) `&cell` lands in a saved register (`addi r9,r1,8 ; mr r27,r9 ;
   stw r29,4(r9)`), while a real struct makes cc1 rematerialise
   `addi r4,r1,8` at each of the three call sites. Both collapse together.
   Same family: the ~414 files that m2c emits as `((Unk_59AB5482 *)&sp8)`.

2. **Assign a call result through a SECOND local (`sp8 = temp`) instead of
   straight into the cell.** `temp = f(); ...zero two words...; sp8 = temp;` is
   what lets the following `if (sp8 != NULL)` test consume the raw return
   register (no reload) *and* schedules the `stw r3,8(r1)` AFTER the two zero
   stores. Assigning `sp8 = f()` first emits the store up front, re-`lwz`s it for
   the test, and costs 3 words. General: when you see "call → store result →
   test the stored value" in a want, split the assignment.

3. **A missing `mr r3,rN` before a `bl` is an argument audit, not a missed
   copy** (extends M4.93 / §6w-119). Want at 0x8004E840-0x8004E854 sets up only
   r4/r5 and calls `fn_8009E3D0`, so r3 — the value just reloaded from the cell —
   IS arg0: the source passes the *node*, not `self`. Passing `arg0` adds a
   `mr r3,r31`. (m2c had it as a 2-arg call with self first.)

4. **NEW structural trigger for the doc-28 / recipe-150 CR-save shape: put the
   countdown decrement BEFORE the loop's trailing conditional block.** Same
   source otherwise:
   ```c
   if (cond) { ...; break/goto done; }   /* path A */
   n--;                                   /* <-- here, not at the end */
   if (sp8) { RemoveRefLink(...); sp8 = 0; }
   } while (n != 0);
   done: if (n == 0) goto notfound;
   fn_8004EA60(arg0);
   ```
   Moving `n--` to the very end of the body yields `addic. rN,rN,-1 ; bne` plus a
   *fresh* `cmpwi` after the loop. With the decrement in front of the trailing
   `if`, cc1 materialises want's `addi r26,r26,-1 ; cmpwi cr4,r26,0 ; bne cr4`
   and lets the post-loop `if (n == 0)` **reuse the latch flags** (`beq cr4`,
   no second compare) — and that cross-`bl` CR liveness is what drags in
   `mfcr r12` / `stw r12,0x18(r1)` / `mtcrf 8,r12`. Pure C, no flags, no pins:
   on this body the move alone was 25.7% → 45.2% (index-aligned) and with items
   1-3 on top of it the function reaches 93.0%. Doc-28 members whose latch
   decrement sits last in the body are worth retrying in this shape first.

5. **Frame data point for doc-28: cc1 shares the CR-save slot with a WRITE-ONLY
   punned MEM.** The want's local area is 0x8..0x17 (cell 12 B + 4 B slack) with
   the CR save at 0x18 (frame 0x38, `stmw r25,0x1c`). With idiom (1) the three
   punned cell words get independent 4-byte slots 0x8/0xC/0x10 and cc1 **shares
   0x10 with the CR save** (that MEM is never read in the body, so its live
   range does not conflict) → frame 0x30, `stw r12,0x10(r1)`. Real 12-byte
   struct: frame 0x38 but CR at 0x1c (slot = align_up(size,8)+4); 16/20-byte
   structs: 0x1c/0x24; `volatile` on the cell or on the punned base does not
   stop the sharing; a dead 4th cell word is deleted before slot allocation.
   So "aggregate slot (4 B slack, CR at +0x10)" and "opaque punned base (r9
   + saved &cell)" are mutually exclusive in plain C here — 8 words is the wall.

## 79 — fn_8004BFE4 (COM list/slot family, w75): three reusable rules (93.3%)

1. **An explicitly-spelled `<< 2` index builds the store base-FIRST; a plain
   `a[i]` builds it index-first.** Both stores in this want are
   `stwx rS,rBase,rIndex` (`stwx r31,r22,r28`, `stwx r23,r25,r5`); every
   `tbl[arg2] = slot;` / `flags[arg2] = 1;` spelling emits
   `stwx rS,rIndex,rBase` instead (2 words off, ~6%). Spelling the index —
   `*(Slot **)((char *)tbl + (arg2 << 2)) = slot;`,
   `*(s32 *)((char *)flags + (arg2 << 2)) = 1;` — reverses it and both go
   exact. A pure cast swap (`(Slot **)((char *)tbl + arg2 * 4)`) does NOT:
   only the explicit shift does. Generalises to every want `stwx` whose
   base/index operands are transposed vs got.
2. **A strided record pool needs a record type of EXACTLY the stride.**
   `Unk_DB0E2BAB` (the house type for this COM family, used by the matched
   sibling src/fn_8004C2DC.c) is **0xBC bytes**, but the free-slot pool here
   is 48 records of **0x1C** at self+0x64 — `pool[j]` on `Unk_DB0E2BAB*`
   emits `addi r31,r31,0xb8`. A local 0x1C struct fixes the step. Also note
   the want keeps BOTH a `+0x1c` pointer walk and a separate `cmpwi r9,0x2f`
   counter: walking with a plain `T*` + counter gets strength-reduced into a
   pointer-END compare (`cmpw r31,r0`), which the want does not have — so
   write the counter off `pool[j]` and keep the walker as `slot++`. Same
   pool is at self+0x64 in fn_8004BEB0 / fn_8004C110 / fn_8004C458 /
   fn_8004D530 / fn_8004A4D8 (all still parked) — retry them with the 0x1C
   record first.
3. **§6a-6 pin-a-copy also cracks a PARAM-HOME swap (r25↔r26), and pinning
   ONE side is essential.** Plain C (every spelling: declaration/statement
   order, `for`/`while`, `*p++` vs `p++`, `tbl[i]` vs pointer walk, nested
   `if` vs `&&`, local vs inline address) homes arg0 in r26 and arg2 in r25
   where the want has r25/r26; ngccc's global.c gives the two params
   opposite priorities and no source shape moves them. Probing showed the
   decider is arg0's REFERENCE COUNT in the RTL (4 refs loses to arg2's 3;
   dropping one — deriving the pool base from `tbl`, or not passing arg0 to
   the callee — flips r25/r26 immediately). With
   `register s32 self __asm__("r25"); self = arg0;` (§6a-6) plus one
   character-level change per rule 1, 81.3% → 93.3%. Pinning r26 as well is
   WRONG: the second pin steals r22 for the arg2 copy (93.3% → 25.3%). Rule
   of thumb: pin only the register want homes FIRST, then let cc1 allocate
   the rest — pinning two registers of the same priority class reorders the
   whole prologue.

## 7q — 2026-10-02 single pick (0x800C4D88, 240B, 31.7% → **EXACT**): a retail
### `fmr`/`ps_mr` after a reload is produced by making the reloaded slot a
### **STANDALONE local whose address never escapes** — §6cx's "ps_mr has no
### plain-C spelling in this cc1" is wrong; and ngccc's local-slot assignment
### orders a 4-byte local BEFORE an 8-byte one regardless of declaration order

`fn_800C4D88` (PS math, `-mps-float`) went 31.7% → **100% (60/60)** in one
round, 0 emitted instructions, one GPR `register` pin, and one per-object flag.
Two of the four findings are new general rules; the other two are function-local.

* **BREAKTHROUGH (general). The reload copy needs a NON-ESCAPING local slot.**
  Want has `lfs f0,0x38(r1); fmr f13,f0; fcmpu cr7,f13,f11` (scalar lane
  reloaded, then copied to the compare's home) and `psq_l f13,64(r1); ps_mr
  f0,f13` (pair reloaded, then copied). Both are reachable in plain C — the
  slot must be a **standalone local whose address is never taken**, e.g.
  `SN_PS_type res; ... res.ps = <ps>; hi = res.flt.hi;`, and NOT a member of
  the block struct (`Blk { ... SN_PS_type s30; }`). With the member — volatile
  or not, and with or without a second `f32` name, or a `"+f"` barrier, or an
  FPR pin — cc1 coalesces the reload into the consumer and **both** copies
  vanish (object 232B, i.e. the old "two instructions short" state). With the
  standalone local the reload lands in a scratch FPR and is copied. The
  promoted byte-identical siblings `src/fn_800A11D8.c` / `src/fn_800A12D0.c`
  already use this spelling (`SN_PS_type dot;` + `x = dot.flt.hi;` as its own
  statement) — **when a PS residual is "one reload short of a `ps_mr`/`fmr`,
  first check whether the reloaded slot is a struct member, before concluding
  the copy is unemittable (§6cx / §6cw).**
  Corollary for the dead-store problem the split creates: the sibling pair
  stores must keep escaping (pass `&b.s10`), because with separate locals all
  six are DCE'd (the object loses 32 bytes). So: struct for the pairs whose
  address escapes, standalone union for the reloaded slot.
* **BREAKTHROUGH (general, silently order-changing). ngccc puts a 4-byte
  local BEFORE an 8-byte local of the same scope, regardless of declaration
  order.** Measured with 4 probe TUs: `{PSV r; f32 f;}`, `{f32 f; PSV r;}`,
  `{Blk; PSV; f32}`, `{PSV; Blk; f32}` all put the f32 at the LOWER offset.
  Here it silently swapped r1+0x38 (union) with r1+0x40 (f32) and cost both
  tail copies. Fix: declare the f32 as an 8-byte-padded struct
  (`struct { f32 v; char pad[4]; }`); the two then tie and the union lands
  first. **When a PS draft's frame is right but a standalone union keeps
  landing one slot too high, pad the neighbouring scalar to the union's size
  before you start hunting for a semantic cause.**
* **Function-local: the second block's `ps_muls0` order is REVERSED vs its
  emission.** Want emits `ps_muls0 f13,f9,f0` (P3*u, fresh f13) then
  `ps_muls0 f0,f10,f0` (P2*u, destructive on u). Writing `m3` first in the
  source gives the OPPOSITE order; writing `m2` first gives want's — with
  `-mps-float` alone. With `-fno-schedule-insns` the source order comes out
  straight, so `m3` first is right there. That inversion is the clearest
  evidence the flag below is a fitted crutch rather than the true cause.
* **Function-local: one GPR pin settles the two rodata page anchors.** Want
  has `lis r9`/`addi r9` for `lbl_80298F18` and a SEPARATE `lis r11` for
  `lbl_80299128`; without a pin ngccc gives the pair-address r11 and the
  float r9 (5 wrong words). `register char *kp __asm__("r9");` on the
  `char *` that holds the pair constant fixes it. Same shape as §6a-6's
  `register s32 self __asm__("r25")` and §6bd's GPR pins.
* **THE FLAG (disclosed, review before promoting). 100% needs the per-object
  `-fno-schedule-insns`; the same body with `-mps-float` alone is 83.3%, whose
  only residual is ngccc's scheduler giving P1 f8 / P0 f7 where want has
  P1 f7 / P0 f8 (and, with `-O2`, sinking `lfs f11` + `lwz r0` past
  `psq_st f0,8(r1)` and reordering the O0/K pair loads).** Retail was
  obviously built WITH scheduling, so the flag is NOT "retail had no
  scheduler" — the honest statement is that retail's *unscheduled* RTL order
  equals ours and ngccc's `sched` re-orders our graph differently than
  retail's. Pinning `p1`->fr7 / `p0`->fr8 does not fix the scheduled case
  (it drags the block with it: 86.7% flag / 80.0% swapped pins / 86.7% p0
  only). **So `-fno-schedule-insns` is a way to make retail's statement order
  come out literally, and any draft that lands 100% with it should say so
  loudly rather than pretend it is the semantic cause.**
  Diagnostic value even without the flag: `-fno-schedule-insns` renders the
  *statement order* of the object directly, which is how the first-block
  source order here was recovered (retail's order = `p1, o28, &K-anchor, p0,
  0.0f, p3, sub, p2, K, o20, s08, mul, flag, sub, merge, s00, madd`).
* **Verification discipline (worth repeating).** Before EXACT: object `.text`
  size == `symbols.txt` `size:` == header `size=`; sections == `.text` +
  `.rela.text` only (no private `.rodata`, so no doc-14 pool caveat — the
  masked 100% cannot be faked by a private float pool here because nothing is
  materialised); **hand-decode both REL14 targets** (the `0xFFFF0003` REL14
  mask cannot see the 14-bit LI — here both `beq` addends are 0xD8
  section-relative = 0x800C4E60, confirmed by hand) and the REL24 target.
