## 7r — 2026-10-02 (w75/0x800808EC, m2c DIFF 20.0% → 28.4%, 0 asm, 0 flags) — **a u16-typed TEMPORARY is what makes ngccc emit `lhzx` instead of `add`+`lbz <off+1>` (and the direct form reads the WRONG byte)**, plus the "guard sits *between* the two loop-init statements" shape

`fn_800808EC` (408 B) copies 4-byte records out of a node array into a
`void *` out-param, through two loops. Everything below is semantic; the
residue is register-number-only.

### 7r-1 — **THE NEW TRICK: `d[1] = *(u16 *)p` is NOT `lhzx`. Assign it to a `u16` temporary first.**

ProDG/3.9.3 turns a *narrowing store of a halfword load* into a byte load at
**offset +1** — i.e. the HIGH byte, which is not even what the C says:

| source | ngccc -O2 output |
|---|---|
| `d[1] = *(u16 *)((char *)q + j);` | `add 5,3,5` / `lbz 0,1(5)` / `stb 0,1(4)` — **wrong byte** |
| `u16 t = *(u16 *)((char *)q + j); d[1] = t;` | **`lhzx 0,3,5` / `stb 0,1(4)`** ← what retail emits |

Same for `(u8)`-casted values generally (`d = *(u8 *)(integer)` also triggers
`lbz 0,0(reg)` after the wide load). So: **whenever want has a load wider than
the store (`lhzx/lwzx` feeding `stb`), materialize the wide load in a variable
of the WIDE type and store that variable.** This is the mirror image of the
existing "byte-extraction needs `& 0xFF` from a wide local" note (§4c-2 /
recipe 8839 area) and it is likely to be sitting in parked m2c bodies all over
the corpus: m2c emits `(u8)` / `(s8)` casts on every narrow store. Zero asm, no
flags, and it is the *correct* C semantics, so it is safe to apply by default.

### 7r-2 — **one byte base + one byte offset gives you `lbzx`/`lhzx`/`lwzx`; a typed `T*` base re-scales the offset**

Retail reads the *same* 4-byte record four times at three widths
(`lbzx`,`lhzx`,`lwzx`+`srwi 8`,`add`+`lbz 3`). Source form:

```c
*(u8  *)((char *)base + j)            /* lbzx j,base   */
u16 t = *(u16 *)((char *)base + j);    /* lhzx j,base   */  (see 7r-1)
*(u32 *)((char *)base + j) >> 8       /* lwzx j,base   */
*((u8 *)((char *)base + j) + 3)       /* add base,j; lbz 3(...)  <- the +3 MUST
                                        be inside the byte pointer, else it
                                        folds into `lbzx` with index j+3 */
```
A `(s32 *)base + j` spelling re-scales j by 4 (`lwzx j4,base`) — this is the
same class of bug as the m2c scaled-pointer fix, but on the *base* cast, and it
also makes GCC strength-reduce `j` into a second induction variable (`addi
r,r,0x10`) that retail does not have. Keep the base a `char *`/`void *`.

### 7r-3 — **loop shape tell: if the guard is BETWEEN two init statements, the source is `i = 0; if (i < c) { a; j = 0; do {...} while (i < c); }`**

Retail places the guard first with a zero materialisation, a halfword load from offset 0x28, an unsigned compare, and a greater-or-equal exit branch, then the preheader copying the saved pointer into the fourth argument register and materialising a second zero, and finally the body with its own halfword reload, compare, and less-than back-edge.
A plain `while`/`for` over the same condition compiles to `b <guard placed
AFTER the body>` (verified in an isolated 4-statement loop too), i.e. a 1-shape
difference that shifts the whole function. Only the explicit `if` + `do/while`
double-test produces the retail form.

### 7r-4 — affine-strength-reduction fires across *sibling* stack arrays

Two stack out-params (`sp8` at r1+8, `sp2718` at r1+0x2718). Indexing the
second one with a byte offset makes GCC rewrite the address as
`add reg,&sp8,j ; lwz rX,0x2710(reg)` off the *sibling* array (it knows
`&sp2718 == &sp8 + 0x2710`), losing retail's `addi r27,r1,0x2718` + indexed
`lwzx`. Holding the second pointer in a **pseudo** (`s32 *pidx = sp2718;` passed
to the callee and reused in the loop) restores `lwzx r9,r29,r27`. Generalise:
*if retail materialises an array address once and indexes it in a loop, GCC will
happily re-derive it from a neighbouring frame slot — keep the address in a
variable.*

### 7r-5 — frame arithmetic confirmed again (§6db law), with the "absorb the
soft-save slots in the array size" trick: `stwu -0x4e40 / stmw r27,0x4e2c`
⇒ locals = `0x4e2c - 8` = 20004 B. `s32 sp8[2500]; s32 sp2718[2499];`
(19996 declared + 8 B of GCC soft-save slots) reproduces the prologue exactly.
Tuning the *second* array's length is legal (nothing indexes past
`script->unk0x24`) and is the cheapest way to land `Gsave`.

### 7r-6 — parked residue (register allocator, not semantics)

Want keeps three distinct registers for one pointer value: `r28` = `arg1`,
`r4` = loop-1 copy, `r31` = loop-2 copy. GCC 2.95's `equiv_allocation_numbers`
**always** coalesces the loop-2 `d = arg1` copy into `arg1` (it is dead after
it), which deletes the `mr r31,r28` shuffle and takes r31 away from `arg1`,
cascading into every other choice (V→r3 instead of r10, loop-1 i/j→r8/r10
instead of r7/r8). Tried and all coalesce: block-local copy, function-scope
shared pointer, two/three copies, struct pointer, `&x->field`, `+0` trick.
Blocking the coalesce needs `arg1` live *past* the copy, and the want has no
use after the loop — so this one may need a family-specific trick (e.g. making
the callee-clobbered `fn_8007E89C` read `arg1`).

## 7s — 2026-10-02 (w75/0x8019F830, 264B, m2c DIFF 6.7% → **EXACT**, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **a `bl` that the want calls ONCE and both tests and reuses must be bound to a named local — and re-writing the call twice in the source costs BOTH an extra `bl` and a callee-saved register (frame 0x10 → 0x18)**

Four independent semantic errors, all visible in the m2c bulk-fill body; fixing
them in one pass reached 100% in two compiles. Only the last one is new.

**7s-1 — bind the tested-and-reused callee result to a named local (NEW RULE).**
The want has ONE `bl 0x8009FDD8` whose result is null-tested (`cmpwi r3,0 /
beq`), called again two statements later as `arg0` to `fn_800CC038` and a third
time as the vtable base. m2c wrote `GetChecksum_3(arg0, 0x7149B753)` three
times, so ngccc emitted three calls. GCC 2.95 does **no** CSE across calls for
a non-`const` callee — *one syntactic occurrence = one `bl`, always*. So:

> **count the `bl`s in the want, count the call spellings in your body, and make
> them equal.** Each call the want makes exactly once needs a named local; each
> call the want makes twice needs two spellings.

The cost is not just the extra instruction. The duplicated call also inflated
the **callee-saved set and the frame**: the third `GetChecksum_3` result had to
survive the intervening `fn_8012772C` call, so GCC homed it in r28 *and* kept
the vtable pointer `t` in r29, giving `stwu r1,-0x18 / stmw r28,8(r1) /
stw r0,0x1c(r1)` against the want's `stwu r1,-0x10 / stmw r30,8(r1) /
stw r0,0x14(r1)`. With the call bound to a local, `t` is used only within one
expression (two `t[...]` reads) and stays in scratch r9 — the house vcall shape
— and only `temp_r30` needs a callee-saved home, so r30 is the *only* one and
the frame collapses to the want's 0x10. **So a frame-size/`stmw`-base mismatch
on a function with a vcall epilogue is often a "too many call spellings"
symptom, not a scheduling one** — fix the call count first, before touching
frames or `-f` flags.

**7s-2 — `lwz` where the want says `lha` = the vtable `this`-offset is `s16`.**
m2c read it as `*(s32 *)((char *)t + 0x60)`; the house shape is
`(signed short)((s16 *)t)[0x60/2]`, giving `lha` instead of `lwz`. Pairs with
recipes 1787-1800 and 3141. Also `lwz r9, 0x64(r9)` = member-fn slot `t[0x19]`.

**7s-3 — argument-order/result errors that m2c makes silently.** The
`fn_8012772C(0xF0D90109, <float>)` spelling had its two leading args swapped
(the callee at `0x8012772C` does `mr r30,r3 / mr r29,r4 / fmr f31,f1`, so
`r3`=object, `r4`=the `0xF0D90109` tag, `f1`=the float), and
`fn_800CC038(0, 0, 0, <float>)` threw away the preceding call's result that the
want passes in r3 (`lwz r9,0x38(r3)` is the callee's only argument use). Audit
arity/order from the callee prologue, not from m2c.

**7s-4 — the `f32`-vs-`s32` field width (re-confirmed, recipes 362/14497/
16272).** `*(s32 *)((char *)arg0 + 0x128) = farg0` → `fctiwz`+`stfd`+`lwz`+`stw`
quadruple, an 8-byte frame, and every later word shifted. Typing it `f32` was
the single biggest scoring jump (6.7% → 55.7% together with 7s-1/2/3).

Also: the two clamp constants are real `.rodata2` symbols
(`lbl_802AAFD0` = 1.0f, `lbl_802AAFD4` = 0.0f, declared in
`src/r2d_802AAFB4.c`) and must be spelled `extern float lbl_...;`, not
`*(f32 *)0x802AAFD0`, so the reference stays an `lis`+`lfs` relocation pair
against the shipped symbol instead of a private float-literal pool.

**143. NEVER stage a re-read struct pointer in a local — it deletes the
     reload + RMW that want has.** Recipes 141/142 control reload webs from the
     *other* side (splitting them); this is the collapse you must avoid. When
     want shows a pointer field reloaded from its owner right before a
     read-modify-write pair
     (`self->unk0x20->unk0x10 = 0; self->unk0x20->unk0x10 |= 8;` →
     `lwz r9,0x20(r31); stw r0,0x10(r9); ... lwz r9,0x20(r31); lwz r0,0x10(r9);
     ori r0,r0,8; stw r0,0x10(r9)`), writing it as
     `Obj *o = self->unk0x20; o->unk0x10 = 0; o->unk0x10 |= 8;` makes ngccc
     forward the constant store into the load, collapsing the whole RMW to
     `li 8` — object 20B short, 97.8% → 69.8% even though every other word was
     byte-identical (fn_800F4130). Fix = write the two statements off the
     *field* twice, never off a local: the intervening store through an
     un-proven-aliasing pointer forces the reload back. Same trap applies to
     `*(volatile ...)` fields (recipe 143b) and to any `p->f = C; p->f |= M;`.

**144. `char pad0xN[...]` — the NAME is a label, the array LENGTH is the
     offset.** `char pad0x0[0x50]; s16 unk0x68;` silently puts the field at
     **0x50**, not 0x68 (the second member's name is pure documentation), and
     the resulting `lha/lwz` pair shifts by 0x18 with no warning and no size
     change — fn_800F4130 scored 97.8% with every other word exact purely
     because of this. Same family as 7s-2. Rule: for `pad0xOFF[..]; T
     unk0xOFF2;` always make `OFF + sizeof(pad0xOFF) == OFF2`, and re-check it
     whenever a `struct` field name looks like it disagrees with its computed
     offset (`offsetof` in a scratch TU is the cheapest audit).

**145. `(s32)global_array` forces an `ori`; the typed-pointer spelling gets
     want's signed `lwz` displacement.** m2c writes
     `*(s32 *)((char *)lbl_802FFE98 + 0x118)` / `*(void **)(s32)lbl_802FFE98`.
     Casting a `char[]` global to an integer materialises its ADDRESS as a
     32-bit value → ngccc emits `lis -0x7fd1 / ori 0xfe98` (one word too many).
     Declaring `extern Unk_9994C3F5 *lbl_802FFE98;` and using the member
     (`lbl_802FFE98->unk0x11C`) gives want's `lis -0x7fd0 / lwz -0x168(r25)` —
     a *signed* displacement from the next page up — and hoists the base into
     a callee-saved reg so every call site reuses it (fn_800F4130, cf.
     `src/wip/fn_80076EEC.c` L1). Same rule as the `lbl_` rule in the brief.

## 7t — 2026-10-02 (w75/0x801A8580, 252B, m2c DIFF 15.9% → **EXACT**, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **the list-walk's SECOND exit is what keeps the first exit's redundant `li rX,0` alive — and ngccc's list scheduler breaks uid ties, so a countdown's `addi` lands before or after its own `beq` purely by STATEMENT ORDER**

Sentinel list walk (`node->0x4 == -1` ⇒ `node = NULL`) that counts one list
and then indexes a second one, i.e. the `fn_80153BB0` / `fn_8000A288` count
idiom applied twice. Four fixes, 15.9% → 100% in six compiles; **7t-1 and 7t-2
are new general rules** and either alone leaves you at 95%.

**7t-1 — split the loop's two exits with a `goto` LABEL placed AFTER a post-loop
`p = NULL;` (NEW RULE).** Retail ends the inner walk by comparing the node pointer in r9 against zero with a branch to the first exit label, then comparing the countdown in r11 against zero with a decrement and a branch to the second exit label, placing a dead zero materialisation into r9 at the first exit label even though the pointer is already zero, and joining at the second label on the word load from offset four plus the argument copy and call.

`L7`'s `li r9,0` looks like a store the compiler failed to DSE — it is not, it
is the *witness that the two exits were never merged*. Every spelling that
leaves the loop with ONE exit block makes GCC cross-jump the two arms together
and the store disappears (verified: `while (p) { if (!j) break; … }` and
`if (p) { do { if (!j) break; … } while (p); }` both emit `beq;beq` to a single
`lwz r3,4(r9)`, 248 B, and the `for(;;)` twin additionally produces **branches
to blocks ngccc never emits** — a 260 B object whose REL14 addends point past
`blr`, i.e. unlinkable code). The spelling that reproduces want, with the
post-loop store still dead and still emitted:

```c
for (;;) {
    if (p != NULL) {
        if (j == 0) goto found;     /* exit 2: SKIPS the store   */
        j--; p = p->next;
        if (p->f4 == -1) p = NULL;
        continue;                   /* back edge to the p-test  */
    }
    break;                          /* exit 1: falls to the store */
}
p = NULL;                            /* dead, but kept: want's li r9,0 */
found:
fn_801A8148(p->f4, arg1);
```

Both arms must be *spelled* (`break` for the null exit, `goto` for the counter
exit) — that is what keeps them textually distinct, so cross-jumping cannot
merge them, and the dead store gets a block of its own to live in. Corollary
for the other direction: if you ever see a want `li rX,0` sitting between a
loop's latch and the loop's first use of `rX`, look for a two-exit loop whose
arms are spelled differently, not for a missing DSE.

**7t-2 — a countdown's `addi` is placed by RTL uid (source statement order),
not by the test it belongs to (NEW RULE).** Want has `cmpwi r11,0; addi r11,-1;
beq L8`; the natural `if (j == 0) goto found; j--;` gives `cmpwi; beq; lwz;
addi` — one `addi` two slots late, 95.2%, and *every* spelling of the
decrement is identical: `j--`, `j = j - 1`, `j -= 1`, `j = -1 + j`,
walk-before-decrement, and the flag probe (`-fno-schedule-insns`,
`-fno-schedule-insns2`, `-fno-sched-spec`, `-fno-sched-interblock`,
`-fno-thread-jumps`, `-fno-peephole`) all keep `beq` second. ngccc's list
scheduler breaks priority ties on insn **uid**, so the decrement statement must
come *before* the statement that tests it while the test still reads the OLD
value — and GCC folds the fold-back for free:

```c
j--;                          /* uid n   */
if (j + 1 == 0) goto found;   /* uid n+1: folds to a compare of the PRE-decrement j */
p = p->next;
```

→ `cmpwi r11,0 ; addi r11,r11,-1 ; beq`. Semantics are identical to
`if (j == 0) goto found; j--;` (the extra decrement on the exit path is
unobservable: the counter is re-initialised each outer iteration). Do **not**
write `if (j-- == 0)`: that materialises `mr r0,r11` + `cmpwi r0,0` (an extra
copy, 256 B).

**7t-3 — a 0-arg callee's `s32` result can BE the next call's dead first arg
(extends §6t-3 / recipe 99).** Want's tail is `bl fn_801FC0E0` with no argument
setup, immediately followed by `lwz r4,0x18(r29); mr r5,r28; bl fn_801FBEDC` —
r4/r5 set, **r3 never written**. Neither callee reads r3 (`fn_801FC0E0`'s
prologue loads its own globals; `fn_801FBEDC` forwards r3/r4 to a 0-arg
helper). Declare them `s32 fn_801FC0E0(void);` and
`s32 fn_801FBEDC(s32, s32, s32);` and pass the first call's result as the dead
first argument — the result is already in r3 by ABI, so the arg-setup copy
folds away and r3 is left alone. Writing `fn_801FC0E0()` as `void` forces an
`mr r3,arg0` re-materialisation; passing `arg0` as the first arg of
`fn_801FBEDC` puts the `lwz` in r3 and the `mr` in r4.

**7t-4 — the count loop is the goto-into-do-while hybrid again (§6s-5), and the
list base must be a NAMED local.** `goto check; do { p = p->next; n += 1;
check:; if (p->f4 == -1) p = NULL; } while (p != NULL);` reproduces want's
entry-jump + bottom test byte-for-byte (a plain `while` puts the test on top
and costs ~8 B). And `l2 = (Node *)((char *)arg0 + 0x48); p = l2->unk0xC;` must
keep `l2` as a local: written inline as
`*(s32 *)((s32 *)((char *)arg0 + 0x48) + 0xC)` GCC folds the two addresses into
`lwz r9,0x78(r30)` and want has `addi r27,r29,0x48 / lwz r9,0xc(r27)`.

## 7u — 2026-10-02 (w75/0x8012DE30, 248B, m2c DIFF 19.4% → **EXACT**, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **ngccc's `balance_case_nodes` pivot is EXACTLY the node at index `floor((n+1)/2)-1` of the value-sorted case list — so when the formula proves want's root is unreachable, the tree can be ported to gotos, and the port lands want's `beq/bgt/b` cluster form verbatim**

A pool-node destructor: unlink, bail on a flag bit, then free a payload pointer
by a 7-value type enum. Two things had to be right, and the first one is a
compiler rule worth writing down.

**7u-1 — the pivot formula, and the corollary that a `switch` sometimes cannot
express want's tree at all.** The b-tree root is the case node at index
`floor((n+1)/2)-1` of the **value-sorted** list (0-based), where a
`case a: case b:` CLUSTER counts as ONE node and a `case a ... b:` RANGE counts
as one node too (recipes §6t-6/§70-124/§6ap-9 state the same rule; the ladder
below is the measured confirmation). Probe ladder on synthetic 4-node
`sink(s32)` switches: n=3 → idx 0, n=4 → 1, n=5 → 2, n=6 → 2, n=7 → 3, n=8 →
3, n=9 → 4, n=10 → 4, n=11 → 5, n=12 → 5; identical on all five in-tree ProDG
versions (3.5 / 3.5b140 / 3.7 / 3.8.1 / 3.9.3), so the compiler version is
never the lever for a tree shape. *Corollary that cost this function a day:*
count the nodes and check the pivot BEFORE permuting case order. Here the seven
values {3,4,5,6,7,10,12} give 6 nodes clustered / 7 split / 6 as a range, and
all three root at 6, while want roots at **5**. The arithmetic then says no
single `switch` can do it: the root's `bgt` into the 11-compare-word right
subtree is the *guarded* form, which §6fq-1's `emit_case_nodes` only emits when
the right child is non-trivial (≥2 nodes), so n≥4; but n=4 leaves only 2 nodes
on the right where want needs a 5-node subtree. Contradiction ⇒ switch family
dead, go to §6fq-1's goto port.

**7u-2 — the goto port that reproduces want's compare tree AND body order.**
Write the tests in want's physical order and route every arm to a `goto`d body
placed in want's body order; the *local holding the switch value must be `s32`*
(§7r's `s8` costs an `extsb`; reading a `u8` field straight into the tests
gives `cmplwi`+`bgt` instead of `cmpwi`+`bgt`, and `find_comparison` then folds
the `t==3`/`t>3` pair into a 3-word range check). With `s32 t` the flags are
reused and the two-test cluster comes out as want's 4-word
`cmpwi; beq A; bgt A; b default`. Two layout levers, both counter-intuitive:
(a) an **inline** `if (t == 5) { body; }` emits `bne` + the body inline, while
`if (t == 5) goto str5;` gives want's `beq` + the body out of line; (b) the
label ORDER in the source is the body order in the object (§70-125) — and a
label sitting immediately after its own test chain becomes the fallthrough,
which is what re-triggers the 3-word fold, so the arm labels must come after
the whole test chain. A real `switch` used for the high subtree
({6,7,10,12} + one empty `case 13:` to push the pivot to 10, §70-124) emits
want's 11 compare words exactly, but its case bodies land *inside* the block
group, so a pure-switch port mis-orders the bodies by 4 positions (79%) — full
goto port is 100%.

**7u-3 — aliasing struct field: a word and a byte inside it.** `lwz 0(r31);
andis. r9,r0,0x20` (bit 0x200000) testing the same byte the `lbz 2(r31)`
dispatch uses means the first four bytes are an alias, not a `s32` followed by
a `u8` (that spelling silently moves the byte to +4 and the payload to +0x10 —
19.4% with every offset wrong). Spell it
`union { s32 w; struct { char pad0[2]; u8 type; } t; } u;` (§6fq-2's union
rule). Cross-check the layout against the constructor at 0x801252BC:
`sth r11,2(r9)` + `rlwimi r0,r11,0x10,9,0xf` (clears word bits 9..15 = the
high byte of that halfword) + `rlwinm r0,r0,0,9,7` (keeps word bits 7..9) —
a `u16` at +2 inside a word at +0, §6bs's MSB-relative MB/ME arithmetic.

Audit of the EXACT body (left in `src/wip/`, not promoted): object is `.text`
(0xF8 = 248 B = the `range=` marker) + `.symtab`/`.strtab`/`.shstrtab`/
`.rela.text` only — **no `.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss`**, so no doc-14 float-pool
caveat; 0 emitted inline instructions; 12 `R_PPC_REL14` whose section-relative
addends are 0x44/0x64/0x70/0x7c/0x88/0x94/0xa0/0xb8/0xd4/0xe4 — every one a
real *instruction* address in want (0x8012DF04 = the default/tail,
0x8012DF14 = the epilogue the flag `bne` targets) — plus the 17 `R_PPC_REL24`
call sites, and no `ADDR16_HA/LO` relocations, so the hazard-277
masked-wrong-label case cannot apply. Promoteable.

## 6fx — 2026-10-02 (0x8020C79C, 220 B, m2c DIFF 17.2% → **EXACT**, 0 emitted asm, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **`extern const f32` on a rodata2 pool float is ALSO an ordering oracle for the constant-materialisation head, not just an alias oracle** — and a 4-store float run split across TWO base registers does NOT follow recipe 64's rotate-right

Three reusable results, all measured on this one function (LEAF_TMPDIR-scoped, no
build/promote):

**1. `extern const f32 lbl_X;` vs plain `extern f32 lbl_X;` — 96.4% → 100.0%.**
Same body, same flags, 2 words different. This is the *third* independent
instance of the `const` alias-oracle lever (§6fw/§6ek-1, 0x80212B18 and
0x80034D24), but with a **new symptom**: it does not sink a loop-invariant
`lfs` past `mtctr` — it changes which of `li r0,0` and `lfs f13` the scheduler
parks first in the constant-materialisation head. want has
`lis r11(QB) / li r0,0 / lfs f13 / ori r11`; plain `extern f32` emits
`lis r11 / lfs f13 / li r0,0 / ori r11`. **So when a function's only residual
is one adjacent-pair swap of a `li` against an `lfs` from a `.rodata2` pool,
re-declare the pool read `const` before touching anything else.** (`const`
tells cc1 nothing ever writes the object, so the pool read stops being an
alias barrier and reload/smp re-colour it.)

**2. A store run split across two base registers permutes [A,B,C,D] → [A,D,B,C],
so write it ASCENDING.** Recipe 64 (rotate right, [A,B,C,D]→[D,A,B,C]) does
*not* predict this run, and feeding rotate-right source scored 61.8%. The run
is one store through the struct pointer (`arg0->f90` → `stfs f0,0x90(r31)`)
plus three through a derived pointer (`t9->y/z/w` → `stfs f0,4/8(r9)`,
`stfs f13,0xc(r9)`), repeated for a second base. want's order is
`0x90, 0x9c, 0x94, 0x98`; **source `0x90, 0x94, 0x98, 0x9c` reproduces it
exactly**, while descending source re-orders the whole run *and* swaps the two
groups (56.4%). Rule of thumb: when a float/int store run mixes bases, try
ascending source order *first*, and only then reach for recipe 64's
rotate-right brute force. (Same idiom as the `1,4,2,3` note at §6j/9100.)

**3. The countdown latch is `i = 8; while (0 != i--)`, not `i = 7; while (…)`.**
`while (0 != n--)` (the operand-order flip from recipe 10556) yields want's
3-word `cmpwi r29,0 / addi r29,-1 / bne` latch; `for(;i!=0;i--)` and
`while(i!=0){…i--;}` both fuse to a 2-word `addic.` and the object comes out
2 words short. But the seed must be **8**: `while (0 != i--)` tests the
pre-decrement value, so 7 gives 7 iterations and cc1 emits `li r29, 6`;
8 gives 8 iterations and cc1 folds the seed to `li r29, 7` — which is also
the only reason want materialises a fresh `li r0,0` for the nine zero stores
instead of reusing the loop counter's final value. **If want's latch is
`cmpwi/addi/bne` (compare-then-decrement) its counter ends at −1, not 0: a
draft that reuses the counter as a zero constant has the wrong loop shape.**

Audit of the EXACT body (left in `src/wip/`, not promoted): object is `.text`
(0xDC = 220 B = the `range=` marker) + `.symtab`/`.strtab`/`.shstrtab`/
`.rela.text` only — **no `.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss`**, so the doc-14 float-pool
caveat cannot apply; 0 emitted inline instructions. Relocations: 4 `REL24`
(the three `fn_*` calls), 4 `ADDR16_HA`/`ADDR16_LO` pairs
(`lbl_802AF760`, `lbl_802AF4A0`, `lbl_802AF4A4`) and exactly **one `REL14`**,
the loop latch at 0x8020C7DC, whose only legal target is the loop head
0x8020C7C8 (`addi r3,r30,0x20`) — displacement −0x14, matching the want's
`4082ffec`, so the masked-EXACT branch-target caveat is discharged by
inspection. Also: the m2c draft's `// FLAG: -Os` is **wrong** here — `-Os`
measures 80.0%, the default `-O2` path 100.0% (frame/loop-latch shape both
move). Re-measure inherited flags after the body is right, not before.

## 7v — 2026-10-02 (w75/0x801AF82C, 492 B, m2c DIFF 23.6% → **EXACT**, 0 emitted asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **an `if/else` whose two arms assign the SAME web from a raw pointer SPLITS the sentinel walk into `mr rX,rY; cmpwi; bne; li rX,0` — the one-variable `if` and EVERY `?:` form get coalesced away** (extends §6ca's "a second variable does not split a web")

`0x801AF82C` (QB gap-menu script builder: sentinel-terminated node walk, `-1`
at `+4` ⇒ NULL, `psq_l/psq_st` float staging) went 23.6% → 97.6% on ONE
statement shape, then 100% on §4s's return polarity. Retail steps the loop by loading the next link from offset 0xC of the walk pointer into volatile r9 (dead before any call), loading the comparison value from offset four of that link, copying the raw link into loop-carried callee-saved r29, comparing the value against negative one, branching past on inequality, and otherwise materialising zero into r29 before the join.

and the ONLY source that produces the `mr r29,r9` copy is the **two-armed
if/else into a second variable**:

```c
raw = walk->unk0xC;
if (raw->unk0x4 == -1) { nxt = NULL; } else { nxt = raw; }
```

Measured on this body (all 492 B targets, relocation-masked):

| source for the sentinel step | result |
|---|---|
| `hd = walk->C; if (hd->f4 == -1) hd = NULL;` (one variable) | 488 B, **coalesced** — load folds into the callee-saved home, no copy |
| `hd = (raw->f4 == -1) ? NULL : raw;` (`?:`) | keeps the copy but **wrong arm order**: `li rX,0; cmpwi; beq L; mr rX,raw` |
| `hd = raw; if (raw->f4 == -1) hd = NULL;` (copy-then-zero) | **coalesced** — cc1 copy-propagation eats the copy, 488 B |
| `if (raw->f4 != -1) { hd = raw; } else { hd = NULL; }` | same wrong arm order as the `?:` |
| `raw = walk->C; if (raw->f4 == -1) raw = NULL; hd = raw;` | **coalesced**, 488 B |
| **`if (raw->f4 == -1) { hd = NULL; } else { hd = raw; }`** | **EXACT** — if-converted to `mr; cmpwi; bne; li` |

So §6ca's conclusion needs the qualifier: a second *variable* alone does not
split the web — but an if/else that assigns it in **both arms** does, with no
`__asm__` pin and no barrier (cc1 if-converts the diamond into
"copy the arm-common value, then conditionally zero", and the copy survives
because the pass runs AFTER RTL simplification). Corollary for the usual
three-web walk (scratch `raw`, carried `nxt`, loop var `walk`): **all three
must be separate C variables** — merging the carried pointer with the loop
variable, or the scratch with the pre-loop head, costs the `or. r31,r9,r9`
entry test (want) or flips r28/r29 between the hoisted `sp+8` frame base and
the carried pointer.

Two smaller confirmations:

* **§4s return polarity, second working form.** `return idx != 0;` (and every
  `==`-rewritten ternary) gives 1-first (`li r3,1; bne; li r3,0`); want wants
  0-first (`cmpwi; li r3,0; beq; li r3,1`). §4s prescribes the explicit
  `if (x == 0) return 0; else return 1;`; a **materialised local works
  identically and reads better** — `ret = 0; if (idx != 0) ret = 1; return ret;`
  (declaring `ret` with the other locals keeps the 0x38 frame / `checksum` at
  `0x18(r1)`; a block-scoped `s32 ret` also measures EXACT).
* **PS float staging (sibling of the matched `src/fn_8010E6DC.c`).** Three
  f32 args come from two 8-byte `__ps_t` struct members: `Pair fr[2]` at sp+8
  plus a `Pair *base` pointer (`base = fr;`) is what yields the pair of
  `psq_l f0,0x18(r31)` / `psq_st f0,8(r1)` with the hoisted `addi r28,r1,8`
  and `lfs f1,8(r1); lfs f2,0xc(r1); lfs f3,8(r28)` reload — a plain
  `f32`-typed struct member or three separate `lfs` sites do NOT. Needs
  `// extra_cflags: -mps-float` (the test harness auto-adds it for `__ps_t`).
  Node layout read off the psq offsets: vec3 at +0x18 (start_pos) and +0x28
  (start_dir), `+0x40` gap score, `+0x3C` times (matches matched
  `src/fn_801AED20.c` = `o->unk0x3C`).

Audit of the EXACT body (left in `src/wip/`, not promoted): object is `.text`
(0x1EC = 492 B = the `range=` marker) + `.symtab`/`.strtab`/`.shstrtab`/
`.rela.text` only — **no `.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss`**, so the doc-14 float-pool
caveat cannot apply; 0 emitted inline instructions. All 11 `REL24`s name real
DOL symbols at exactly the want's `bl` targets (`Script_RunScript` 0x80131008 —
use that name, not `fn_80131008`; the others are `GetChecksum_2`,
`CStruct_new/_ctor/_delete`, `AddChecksum/_Integer/_String`, `fn_801AED74`,
`fn_801AED20`, `fn_8012788C`); the five `REL14`s are section-local, and with a
byte-identical word stream their displacements resolve to the want's targets.
The callee-proto half of the fix is doc-56 again: `CStruct_new` returns its
arg (chained into `CStruct_ctor`) and `fn_801AED74` returns a value the caller
forwards to `AddString`; with implicit decls ngccc emits `crclr cr1eq` and the
whole tail shifts.

## 7w — 2026-10-03 (0x8000F68C 20.7% → **EXACT**; 0x8009DC9C 15.6% → **EXACT**): **ngccc's switch decision-tree compare SIGN is taken from the C type of the switch expression, and it changes the whole tree**

A big `switch` over QB hash constants compiled from an **`s32`** expression makes
ngccc emit a **signed** binary-search tree (`cmpw` + `bgt`, no `cmplw`). The
retail binary uses an **unsigned** tree (`cmpw` + `beq`, then `cmplw` + `bgt`)
at *every* node. That is not a one-instruction difference: the pivot choice
feeds `balance_case_nodes`, so a signed value produces a **completely different
tree shape** and a different arm layout.

**Oracle:** count `cmplw`/`bgtu` vs `cmpw`+`bgt` in the want. Any want with
`cmplw` next to `cmpw` on hash constants is unsigned; if your draft produces
`cmpw`+`bgt` you have the wrong signedness.

**Fix — retype the switch parameter (do NOT cast, do NOT stage a temp):**
change the *declared parameter type* `s32 argN` → `u32 argN`. Confirmed twice:

| fn | size | fix | before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x8000F68C` | 720 B | `s32 fn_8000F68C(..., s32 arg1)` → `u32 arg1` | 20.7% → **180/180 EXACT** |
| `0x8009DC9C` | 384 B | `s32 fn_8009DC9C(s32 arg0)` → `u32 arg0` | 15.6% → **96/96 EXACT** |

Both promoted; `main.dol` stayed byte-identical.

Corroborating evidence: the matched sibling `src/fn_8000F36C.c` — the *same*
23 case values and the *same* want tree — is declared
`char *fn_8000F36C(void *arg0, u32 arg1)`. When a hash switch is your only
problem, diff the neighbour's prototype before touching anything else.

**Hazard:** a typo in a case *value* silently adds a 24th node and re-roots the
entire tree (I turned `0xC7800B0` into `0xC78000B0` and dropped 80% → 16.3%).
Extract the want's `lis`/`ori` pairs programmatically and diff them against the
draft's case list before blaming codegen. Note `lis r0, 0xc78` is `0x0C7800B0`,
not `0xC7800B0`.

**Where else to look.** A scan of all of `src/wip/` for
(unsigned want-tree) × (signed switch param) × (no `u32 swv` staging already
tried) × (not already parked) left only **8** files:
`0x8002E3A8 0x80054048 0x8008573C 0x8009DC9C 0x800B48D4 0x801A2FE4 0x80207990
0x80242F80`. Of those only `0x8009DC9C` moved (the other seven are dominated by
bigger semantic errors — wrong prototypes, phantom args — and score flat under
the flip). So: **this recipe is nearly exhausted**; do not re-run it as a sweep.
Everything already carrying a `u32 swvN` staging temp (the "" family)
has had the equivalent experiment applied and moved on.

### 6g2 — 2026-10-03 (b27) a r30/r31 callee-saved coin-flip is CRACKABLE in pure
### C by SPLITTING one temp into two scope-locals — no register pin

`fn_800EE918` (`build CScript vehicle-sound block`, 456B) wanted `r31 = arg0`
and `r30 = <the struct pointer returned by fn_80129528 / GetStructure>`.  With
ONE local for that pointer (`temp_r30`, used by both the gear loop and the
later CAG block) the allocator produced the exact transpose —
`mr r30,r3` for arg0, struct pointer in r31 — and **everything else in the
456-byte body was already byte-identical**, so the whole function scored 77.2 %
on ~30 wrong words that were all the same `r3e`/`r3f` substitution.

Recipes §6z-3 and §6cs-4 say the answer is a pin, and a pin *does* fix the
registers:

```c
register CStruct *temp_r30 __asm__("r30");
```
→ 94.7 %.  **But the pin costs 6 more words in a different way:** the pinned
copy becomes a hard-reg copy that the scheduler can hoist, so
`lis r4,<hash>` (no inputs, PRIO 0) jumps **above** `mr r30,r3`, and the loop's
`addi r29,r29,0x10` jumps **above** the `bl`.  Two 2-word flips in two basic
blocks.  Block-scope pin (`register ... ` inside the `do {}`) is identical.
An `__asm__ volatile("" : : "r"(p))` barrier right after the assignment makes
it *worse* (464B — the volatile empty asm forces a spill; **never** put
`"memory"` there, `sp8`'s address escaped to GetArray so everything reloads).

**The pure-C fix: use TWO different locals for the two non-overlapping
live ranges.**  `arg0` is live over the whole function; the gear pointer is
live only inside the loop; the CAG pointer is live only inside the final `if`.
Splitting the shared temp gives three candidates for the same two callee-saved
homes, and ngccc then picks `r31 = arg0`, `r30 = loop_ptr`:

```c
do { loop_ptr = fn_80129528(sp8, i); ... } while (i < arg0->unk0x38);
...
if (arg0->unk0x20) { cag_ptr = GetStructure(QB_..., 1); ... }
```

→ **EXACT**, no pins, no flags.  (Block-scope pin on the loop pointer + an
unpinned `cag_ptr` = 96.5 %; it is dropping the pin entirely that gets the
last 4 words, because the pinned copy is what perturbs the scheduler.)

**Rule:** before pinning a callee-saved reg to fix a 2-register rotation,
check whether the two variables are actually *used in disjoint scopes*.  One
merged temp is the worst case for the allocator — give each live range its own
declaration and the allocator often lands on retail's map by itself.  Corollary:
an `arg`-scope pin on a copy of the param (`register CScript *a0 __asm__("r31"); a0 = arg0;`)
costs an extra `mr` (460B) when the param would otherwise have been coalesced —
pins on *locals* coalesce, pins on *copies of params* do not.

## 6g3 — 2026-10-03 (b31/0x8001E3CC, 284B, m2c 81.7% → **EXACT**, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **a "register-colouring tie-break" in a long `|`-chain is almost never a colouring problem — it is the CHAIN'S SPINE. Re-read the want for where the operand group is SPLIT across two slots, then stage the chain PREFIX into a named local and give the rest ONE further assignment.**

This function was parked as a dead register-allocation tie-break after "~60 compiles"
of flag and source-shape permutations (all 81.7%, 13 diffs, same 13 words). Two
structural facts in the want solved it outright.

**(1) The operand group is not one value — it is TWO slots of the chain.**
Previous draft had one local:
```c
g = ((arg5 << 18) & 0x40000) | 0x30000 | ((arg5 << 19) & 0x300000);
```
but want's arg5>1 arm computes the group in two non-adjacent slots: the first half rotates arg5 left by 0x12 and masks to 0x40000 then ORs in 0x30000 through one term register that is ORed into r3, the stack-slot value shifted left by 0x13 sits between the halves and is ORed into r3 next, and the second half rotates arg5 left by 0x13 and masks to 0x300000 through a later slot that is ORed into r3 last.
So the group splits into `g1` and `g2` occupying two different chain slots with
`arg_sp8<<19` in between. Emitting one `g` makes those instructions adjacent and
rotates every downstream scratch register by one — which is exactly the "rotated by
one" symptom the old park note described and never fixed. **Rule: when a big OR/ADD
chain misses only on register choice, count the chain's `or` slots in want and
check the operands land in the same slots. A group that want computes in two
non-adjacent places is two source locals, not one.**

**(2) The chain needs a fresh left spine.** With `g1`/`g2` split, the winning body
stages the *prefix* into a local and then does the remainder as ONE assignment:
```c
v  = arg_sp10 | (arg_sp14 << 2) | (arg4 << 4) | (arg3 << 7) | (arg2 << 10) | (arg1 << 13);
g1 = ((arg5 << 18) & 0x40000) | 0x30000;
g2 = (arg5 << 19) & 0x300000;
v  = v | g1 | (arg_sp8 << 19) | g2 | (arg_spC << 22) | ((arg0 << 25) + 0xC1000000);
lbl_80300280(v, arg1);
```
Scored ladder (`tools/want_got.py 0x8001E3CC --file`):
| body | diffs | % |
|---|---|---|
| one `g` local (old parked) | 13 | 81.7% |
| `g1`/`g2` split, whole chain inline | 20 | 71.8% |
| split + prefix local, tail as staged `v \|= ...` statements | 2 | 97.2% |
| split + prefix local, tail as ONE `v = v \| ...` | 0 | **100%** |

Note the 97.2% trap: writing the tail as separate `v |= x;` statements is ONE word
off. It must be a single `v = v | a | b | ...` assignment. And staging the prefix
while leaving the tail inline is 2.8% — the prefix local alone is not the fix, it
has to be prefix-local + single-expression tail.

**Generalised:** this is recipe 57 / §6z-128 (stage sub-expressions into named
temps to fix emission order) applied to the LEFT SPINE of a chain rather than to a
single operand. When a long `|`-chain is one or two words off with every opcode and
operand order already correct, try: (a) does want split an operand group into
non-adjacent slots? (b) does the chain need `v = <prefix>;` then `v = v | <rest>;`?
Both are free in plain C and neither needs a pin or a barrier.

## 6g4 — 2026-10-03 (b31/0x801B07D4, 160B, m2c 92.5% → **EXACT**, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins, 0 barriers): **a lone `li rX,0` misplaced by one slot against a loop guard is almost always TWO defects, not one: (a) you hand-strength-reduced an index that ngccc should strength-reduce itself, and (b) you cached the trip count in a local so the latch reload can't happen.**

The parked note called this "the classic IV-init hoist coin" and left it. It isn't a
coin — two independent source choices fix it, and both must be right.

**(a) Let ngccc do the strength reduction.** The draft carried a hand-written
byte-offset counter `var_r29 += 0x14`. Want's `r29` is ngccc's OWN derived IV from
`arg0->unk0x8 + i * 0x14`, and the giveaway is that its `li r29,0` init sits AFTER
the entry guard (`cmpw r31,r11; bge exit; li r29,0`) rather than in the entry block.
ngccc's strength reduction puts the derived-IV init in the loop preheader, which is
*after* the entry test; a source-level counter initialised before the loop lands in
the entry block instead. Measured (all `tools/want_got.py 0x801B07D4 --file`):
| body | diffs | % |
|---|---|---|
| hand `off` counter, `off = 0` before the loop (old parked) | 3 | 92.5% |
| hand `off` counter, `for (i = 0, off = 0; ...)` init clause | 19 | 51.3% |
| `i * 0x14`, trip count cached in `n` | 15 | 61.5% |
| `i * 0x14`, trip count RE-READ each test | 0 | **100%** |

**(b) Do not cache the trip count.** Write the test as `i < (s32)arg0->unk0x4`.
Want's latch is `lwz r0,4(r28); cmpw r31,r0; blt` — it RE-READS the field. Staging it
into a local `n` lets GCC hoist the load, which changes the bottom compare from
`lwz`-then-`cmpw` to a bare `cmpw` against a register held from the entry block and
cascades a further 15 words of misalignment on its own. This is the same
"re-read vs cache" family as doc 28's distant-CR avoidance, but on a plain integer
loop: **when want shows a `lwz` inside a loop latch, the source did NOT have that
value in a variable.**

Also dead ends, for the record: `while` and `do/while` forms of the same loop are
15-24 diffs, and writing `t_r30 = arg0->unk0x8; t_r30 += i * 0x14;` as two statements
is 21. Keep the indexing in ONE expression.

### 6g3 applicability boundary (verified negative on fn_8001EE4C, 2026-10-03)

6g3 was re-tried on **fn_8001EE4C** — the same `lbl_80300280` command-packing
family as the fn_8001E3CC win, with an identically-shaped OR chain — and **none of
its 20 variants beat the existing 91.9%**. Recorded so the recipe is not
re-applied blindly:

| variant | result |
|---|---|
| operand-order flip of the two trailing ORs | 91.9%, **byte-identical** |
| `(a1 * 0x100)` instead of `(a1 << 8)` | 91.9%, byte-identical |
| 6g3 proper: stage prefix, then one further assignment | 45.9% |
| stage prefix group only, shift on the left / right | 29.7% / 70.3% |
| stage both trailing groups into their own locals | 29.7% |
| stage only the trailing shift term into a local | 78.4% |
| `u32` staged local instead of `s32` | 78.4% |

**6g3 applies when**: the chain is ONE inline expression whose left spine is long
enough that ngccc's allocator picks the wrong accumulator register.

**6g3 does NOT apply when either**:
1. the chain is *already* decomposed into named locals (it is at maximum staging
   — fn_8001EE4C stages into `a` / `b` / `cmd`, so there is no spine left to
   re-anchor and splitting further only adds a pseudo and moves the birth point);
2. the residual is a single `or Rd, Ra, Rb` whose only difference from want is
   *which of the two accumulator registers is the destination*. That is an
   allocator choice, not a source-shape choice — and, per the table above,
   cc1 canonicalises commutative OR operands, so you cannot even steer it by
   swapping the operands in the source.

So the diagnostic is: **count how many `or` slots differ and by how much.** If
whole operands appear/disappear from the chain, it is 6g3. If one `or` has its
dest swapped with one of its srcs and nothing else moved, it is the allocator —
stop permuting the source.

**Scan note for future 6g3 sweeps**: a repo-wide scan for this shape (parked
draft with >=3 `|`/`^` in one statement and >=2 `<<`, size <= 900B) finds only
**6 candidates total**, and every one of them is either already solved
(fn_8001E3CC), DIFF (<50%, so semantics are wrong not register choice), or the
already-decomposed fn_8001EE4C. 6g3 is a narrow lever, not a family recipe.

## 6gd — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80139600, m2c 80.5% → **EXACT 41/41**, 0 asm, 0 flags, 0 pins): **a "missing explicit copy" (`mr Rd,Rs`) that ngccc coalesces away is usually a MISSING LOCAL, not a regalloc wall — give the field read its own name so something still references the loaded pointer**

`fn_80139600` (164B, `for (i=0;i<=0xFE;i++)` outer walk + inner `do/while` node
walk with a `blrl` vcall) sat at an 80.5% ceiling across three sessions and was
parked as a regalloc/coalescing artifact. It is neither: it is a missing
variable. One edit took it to **byte-exact**.

The want's inner-loop head keeps the fetched node pointer in **two** registers: it loads offset 0xC of the cursor into temporary r9, materialises three into r4, null-tests the cursor variable in r11 under condition field cr7 rather than the identity value, reads the negative-one field from offset four through r9 into r0, copies the temporary into r31 as the explicit cursor copy, compares r0 against negative one with a not-equal skip of eight bytes to a zero materialisation into r31, and guards the virtual call with an equal branch on cr7 that skips when the cursor is null.

The parked draft wrote the -1 test **inline** (`if (temp_r9->unk0x4 == -1)`).
That lets cc1 fold the load straight into the compare, so after the test
**nothing references `temp_r9` any more** except the copy `var_r31 = temp_r9` —
and coalescing merges those two pseudos. Result: `lwz r31,0xc(r11)` in place of
`lwz r9,...`, no `mr`, and a redundant `cmpw r31,r9` from the identity test the
draft used as the vcall guard. That is the entire 8-word residual.

The fix is to read the field through a local of its own so it stays live:

```c
temp_r9 = ((Unk_C8FEE62D *)var_r11)->unk0xC;
f4 = (s32) temp_r9->unk0x4;      /* <-- the whole fix */
var_r31 = temp_r9;
if (f4 == -1) { var_r31 = NULL; }
if (var_r11 != NULL) { ...vcall... }
```

80.5% → **100% (41/41)**, object 164 B == symbol 164 B, no flags, no pins, no
asm. Note the second-order effect: once `f4` holds `temp_r9` alive, the vcall
guard can be spelled as the honest `if (var_r11 != NULL)` — a NULL test on the
**cursor**, not the `var_r31 == temp_r9` identity test the draft had used — and
that is exactly what produces the wanted `cmpwi cr7,r11,0` / `beq cr7` pair with
**no** extra `cmpw`. The old draft had reached the right *test* by accident (the
identity form) and the wrong *spelling*; and the "null guard on var_r11"
variant that a previous session tried at 45% had the right spelling but no live
range separating `temp_r9` from the cursor, so it still coalesced.

**Rule (general, sibling of 6g3):** cc1's coalescing keys on *"does any live
range still reference this value"*, not on how the compare is spelled. So when a
want keeps a loaded pointer in a register across a branch that its own field
test would let you inline, **give the field read its own named local** — that is
what re-establishes the second reference and preserves both the `mr` and the
cr7 pair. The tell is a residual that is *one `mr Rd,Rs` plus one compare pair*:
a missing `mr` whose operands are both already live is nearly always a missing
local, not a colouring choice. Contrast 6g2/6g3, which are about *which*
register a value gets; 6gd is about a value having only *one* reference at all.

### 6gd applicability boundary — corpus-wide negative scan (2026-10-04, bf)

**Do not re-scan for 6gd.** I swept **every** parked draft in `src/wip/` (~1787)
with a purpose-built detector for this exact signature — want has
`<load into rX>` immediately followed by `<mr rD,rX>` where got has the *same*
load writing `rD` directly — plus a looser "any `mr rD,rS` in want with no such
copy anywhere in got" detector. Results:

* precise signature: **0 additional hits** beyond fn_80139600 itself;
* looser vanished-copy detector over the 159 drafts scoring ≥85 % with ≤6 wrong
  words: **0 hits**;
* the residual is real but rare because it needs a *specific* combination —
  a field read written inline in a compare **and** a cursor/copy of the same
  pointer **and** a branch that keeps both live. Drafts that merely *have* a
  missing `mr` are the ordinary §6a-6/§6q-133 param-home coin-flips, not 6gd.

So 6gd is a **single-function insight, not a family lever**. Use it when you
are already staring at one such residual (it is unmistakable once seen), not as
a sweep.

**Second negative result, same round — the "all-transposition" residual family
is NOT source-reachable.** A second detector found **36** parked drafts whose
*entire* residual is adjacent 2-instruction transpositions (right instructions,
right registers, wrong order) — the most attractive-looking shape there is. I
probed the three best and **every one produced a byte-identical object** under
every source shape tried:

| draft | residual | tried | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fn_801FBF90` 336B 97.6% | `mr r28,r3` / `mr r26,r4` swap (both params already hard-pinned) | swap decl order; plain assignments in both orders; drop the r26 pin; drop the r28 pin; drop both | 97.6% unchanged, or 86.9% when the r28 pin goes |
| `fn_8016F69C` 388B 97.9% | `addi r5,r1,0x18` / `stw r30,0x18(r1)` swap | bind `&sp18`/`&sp1C` into locals before the store (6gd-style: give the address its own live range) | 21.4% (both) / 97.9% unchanged (one) |
| `fn_8001593C` 120B 86.7% | 4-word rotation `addi/slwi/add./stw` | store before the pointer math; store after the if-block; stage the shift; stage `recs` | 86.7% byte-identical every time |

cc1 re-canonicalises these before `sched` ever sees them, so no statement order
reaches them — this is the doc-15 "not source-reachable" class the recipes
already describe. **Treat a pure adjacent transposition as a parking
candidate, not a permutation problem.**

**Third result — length mismatches ARE a separate, tractable-looking class.**
A length-mismatch scan found **1135** parked drafts whose compiled `.text`
differs from the symbol size (vs 36 all-transposition ones). Those are
*structural* residuals (a missing/extra instruction, a wrong frame), a
different lever from scheduling. Best current example `fn_8010C8BC`
(want 424B, got 428B, 90.7 %): the outer/inner loop bounds are read inline in
the `for` conditions. Giving the bound its own local via a comma expression
(`for (i = 0; (b = *(u32 *)&((CStruct *)sp10)->unk0x4, i < b); i++)`) **does
reach the correct 424 B length** — but only by restructuring the inner loop
too, which drops the score to 84.9 %. So the length is reachable; the current
shape is not. That class is the most promising unexplored direction and is
*not* covered by any existing recipe section.

Verification beyond the masked score (per AGENTS §5): all 6 conditional branches
match on opcode/BO/BI/AA/LK and each decodes to want's target offset
(0x34, 0x84, 0x60, 0x7c, 0x40, 0x18); every non-branch word is byte-identical.

## 6ge — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80115A28, m2c 85.7% → **EXACT 104/104**, 0 asm, 1 pre-existing flag): **a switch whose residual is "one constant pair in the wrong place" is usually a WRONG CASE LABEL, not a case-ordering problem — read the case→value map straight off the branch targets. Plus: several early `return X;` reassociate into arithmetic; want's single shared tail needs one positive test.**

Two independent fixes, both semantics-first (AGENTS §5). Neither is a flag,
pin, permutation or emitted instruction. This is the payoff from the
length-mismatch scan in §6gd — `fn_80115A28` was want 416B / got 420B.

### (1) 96.15% → 100%: the case labels were WRONG (a SET difference wearing an ORDER difference's clothes)

The residual after fix (2) was 4 words that *looked* like a materialisation
order problem: at offset 0x6C retail materialises 0x456D28D1 with one high/low half pair while the build materialises 0x365AA16A there, and at offset 0x94 retail materialises 0x365AA16A while the build materialises 0x3200752A.

The obvious read is "reorder the cases". It is not. **`0x3200752A`
(`QB_UNKNOWN_0x3200752A`) is not compared anywhere in want's switch tree** —
it is an m2c invention — and `0x456D28D1` is `QB_STRUCT`, which the draft
never mentions. The 4 words differ in **which constants are in the tree**, not
merely in what order; reordering cannot fix a set error.

**The method (cheap, exact):** want's switch is a binary search tree whose every
leaf `beq` targets one of a few `li r31,<value>; b <exit>` bodies. Dump the
tree, then read each body's value — the case→value map falls out with no
guessing:

```
0x80115B54 -> 1   {QB_INT, QB_INTEGER}
0x80115B5C -> 2   {QB_FLOAT}
0x80115B64 -> 0xD {QB_NAME, QB_CHECKSUM}
0x80115B6C -> 3   {QB_STRING}
0x80115B74 -> 6   {QB_VECTOR}
0x80115B7C -> 5   {QB_PAIR}
0x80115B84 -> 0xC {QB_ARRAY}
0x80115B8C -> 0xA {QB_STRUCTURE, QB_STRUCT}
```

The draft had `case QB_UNKNOWN_0x3200752A` as QB_NAME's partner and paired
QB_STRUCTURE with QB_CHECKSUM. Both wrong. Fixing the two labels → **EXACT**.

**Rules:**
1. **When a switch's residual is a constant pair in the wrong slot, audit the
   case SET before the case ORDER.** A pure ordering problem keeps the same
   constants; a set problem shows one constant in want that got never
   materialises. `grep` the header for want's constant — if it has a name and
   the draft does not use it, that is your missing case.
2. **m2c routinely invents `QB_UNKNOWN_0x…` labels and mis-pairs bodies.** A
   `QB_UNKNOWN_*` case label is a smell: check whether the value appears in
   want's tree at all before believing it.
3. **A hash can also be a case label.** Here `QB_NAME` (0xA1DC81F9) is *both*
   the first `GetChecksum_2` hash and a `case` label. It looks like a bug and
   is not — do not "clean it up".
4. Pairs that share a body in want share a `beq` target — that is how you tell
   which labels belong together without reading the source.

### (2) 420B → 416B (the +4): several early returns reassociate into arithmetic

Want's epilogue has ONE shared tail that several failure branches jump to: it record-tests r3 against itself and falls into a zero materialisation on equal, then loads the byte at offset two, materialises one, compares the byte against r31, skips on equal, and otherwise materialises zero.

The draft's two separate `if (...) return 0;` statements let cc1 fold the two
failure paths into one arithmetic compare and materialise the result with
`lbz / xor / subfic / adde` — four words instead of three, hence the +4B.
One positive test plus one trailing return reproduces want exactly:

```c
if (temp_r3 != NULL && temp_r3->unk0x2 == var_r31) { return 1; }
return 0;
```

**Rule: when want's epilogue has a single constant-materialising tail block that
several failure branches jump to, the C must be ONE positive test plus ONE
return.** Separate early returns let cc1 reassociate the condition into
arithmetic. Measured here: `&&`-form 96.15% and the correct length; an explicit
`res` variable with a shared tail 86.7%, nested ifs 84.8%, a single boolean
expression 84.8% — all keep 420B, i.e. none of them fixes the length, so the
length is the honest signal that you got the shape wrong.

Same family as 6g4 in spirit (give the result one shared home) but a different
trigger: 6gd is a *missing local*, this is a *shared tail*. Together they say
the reliable levers are the ones that change how many live ranges a value has.

Verification beyond the masked score: object `.text` = 0x1A0 = 416B ==
`symbols.txt`; **all 16 conditional branches hand-verified** for
opcode/BO/BI/AA/LK *and* target offset; all 30 raw differing words confirmed to
carry a relocation (so the masked compare is legitimate); no private
`.rodata`/`.data` (promote-clean).

## 6gg — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x8013A7D4, m2c 63.1% → parked **95.2%** (60/63), object 252 B == symbol, 0 asm, 0 flags): **a residual of "block-order swap + register-role colours" is usually THREE SOURCE-SEMANTIC defects in disguise: (a) the two 0x1388 tests are NOT symmetric in polarity, (b) `f - 1 + d` and `f + (d - 1)` produce different addi/add pairs, (c) two sites returning the same constant must share ONE tail. What is left after those really is the colouring.**

### Why this matters: the m2c note blamed the wrong layer

`fn_8013A7D4`'s park header said *"register-role colors (want keeps v in r9/p
in r11/d in r0; got rotates them) + block-order swap (want [big][small][tail]
[store_v], got [big][small][store_v][tail])"* and *"Every goto-restructure of
the CFG crashed to 1.6% (allocator re-color)"*. That diagnosis was wrong in a
useful way: the block order and the colour map were *downstream* of three
real semantic mistakes, and fixing them moved 63% → 80% → 92% → 95% with the
object length landing exactly on 252 B at 80%. The "allocator re-color crash"
was simply the correct C producing a different (correct-in-itself) layout.

### (a) 63% → 80%: the two 0x1388 comparisons have OPPOSITE polarity

want at 0x5c/0x60 (the *low-delta* site):

```
0058  subf r0, r9, r0        ; r0 = temp_r0 - v
005c  cmplwi r0, 0x1388
0060  bgt  STORE_V           ; if (r0 > 0x1388) -> store_v tail
0064  b    BIG               ; else -> the 17FC++/17F8--/|=2 block
```

want at 0x94/0x98 (the *high-delta* site) uses `ble`. So the SAME threshold
appears once as `bgt` and once as `ble`. The m2c draft had `ble` at both,
because it wrote the low-delta arm as the *taken* branch:

```c
if ((u32)(temp_r0 - temp_r9_2) <= 0x1388U) goto block_10;   /* WRONG side */
```

Inverting which arm carries the constant test —

```c
if ((u32)(temp_r0 - temp_r9_2) > 0x1388U) goto block_13;    /* store_v */
goto block_10;
```

— gives `bgt`. **This alone also flips the two tail blocks into want's order**,
because the store_v block becomes the fall-through-reachable one and cc1 emits
the shared `ret:` last. Do NOT stop at "the branch opcode is wrong" and keep
hunting the layout: getting the polarity right fixed 11 words at once.

Corollary for triage: when the same constant appears in two comparisons in
one function, **read both want branches' BO fields before assuming the source
tests are symmetric.** A draft that "has the right threshold twice" can still
be wrong once.

### (b) 80% → 92%: subtraction associativity is visible

want emits `addi r9,r9,-1` then `add r9,r9,r0` for the small-delta update —
i.e. `f += (d - 1)`. The m2c draft's `f = f - 1 + d` folds to the same
instructions *in that order* only by luck of cc1's reassociation; writing
`f + (d - 1)` makes it unconditional. The reversed spelling `(f - 1) + d` in
parentheses measured byte-identical to `f - 1 + d` (still 92%), so it is the
*unparenthesised* form that is load-bearing. Also `delta > 1U` must stay
`> 1U`: rewriting it as `<= 1U` (an equivalent-looking change) collapses the
whole function to 61% / 256 B.

### (c) 92% → 95%: two `return 1` sites need one shared tail

Two paths end in `return 1`. Written as two inline `return 1;` statements cc1
DUPLICATES the `li r3,1; blr` pair (+8 B, three extra blocks). Give both a
`goto ret;` into a single trailing `ret: return 1;`. This is the same shape
as §6ge's "one shared constant-materialising tail" rule from the other side —
there several sites collapsed into one tail; here two sites must not keep
two copies.

### The remaining 3 words really are the colouring

All three misses (0xcc/0xd0/0xdc) are one allocno: want homes the
small-delta block's `arg0->unk0xC` pointer in **r10**, ngccc picks **r11**.
Roughly a dozen source shapes were measured: one shared local for every
`unk0xC` load (87%, drops to 248 B), a separate `sm` local for the small
block (92%, and it *also* costs r11 in the store_v tail), hoisting `unk0xC`
into one `c` local (35%), two names c1/c2 (58%), an extra `temp_r10 = c1;`
round-trip (87%), rewriting the store_v tail as `temp_r11 = *(...);
temp_r11->unk0x4930 = v;` (92%), giving store_v a named `pv` for p (92%),
merging the two return-1 sites *through* the store_v block (87%), reloading p
in both tails (73%). This is the same wall as `fn_801297E4` / `fn_801115FC`:
an allocno preference no plain-C spelling reaches.

### Verification

Object `.text` = 0xFC = 252 B == `symbols.txt`. Sections: `.text`/`.symtab`/
`.strtab`/`.shstrtab`/`.rela.text` only (no private rodata/data).

Hand-verified all **10** relocated branches (7 `bc` + 3 `b`) for
opcode/BO/BI/AA/LK **and** decoded target offset against want. **9 of 10
match**; 0x48 is a genuine residual (`beq` want -> 0x00e4, got -> 0x00e0):
want's `temp_r0 == 0` path branches *past* the `lwz p,0x10(r3)` reload
because p is still live in r11 from 0x3c, while got reloads it into r9 one
instruction earlier. This is downstream of the same r10/r11 allocno split as
the three counted misses — the masked scorer hides it because the REL14 mask
keeps only opcode+BO+BI.

**Decoder gotcha worth keeping** (cost me a false "MISMATCH" on every branch):
PPC `bc` puts BD in **bits 2..15 as a signed WORD offset** (multiply by 4),
whereas `b`/`bl` put LI in the low 24 bits as a signed BYTE offset. Reading
BD as `(w>>16)&0x3FFC` picks up the BI/BO bits instead and yields garbage
targets. `<scratch> in this session's scratch dir
implements the correct form and exits non-zero on any mismatch.

## 6gf — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80113CC4, m2c 53.3% → parked **64.4%** (29/45), object 168 B vs 180 B, 0 asm, 1 pre-existing flag `-fno-cse-follow-jumps`): **ProDG has a broken DImode: it disagrees with retail about which half of an `r3:r4` pair is which, and it NEVER emits `rlwinm 31,31,31` + `cmpwi` for a low-word sign test. So a want containing `clrlwi rX,rY,0x1f ; cmpwi rX,0 ; b*` around a 64-bit value is a HARD wall, not a spelling problem**

Measured with standalone `-S` probes (`<scratch>, `asm3.py` — compile a
throwaway TU with `ngccc -O2 -G0 -mcpu=750 -fno-common -S` and print per-function asm).
For `u64 v = cal(a,i);`

| source | ngccc output | reads |
|---|---|---|
| `s32 lo = (s32)v; lo >= 0` | `cmpwi r4,0` | LOW |
| `(u32)v < 0x80000000u` | `nor 4,4,4 ; srwi 3,4,31` | LOW |
| `(u32)v >> 31 == 0` | `cmpwi r4,0` (+ `cror 31,30,29; mfcr 3; rlwinm 3,3,0,1` in the value-returning shape) | LOW |
| `u32 lo = (u32)v; (lo & 0x80000000u) == 0` | `cmpwi r4,0` | LOW |
| `(s64)v < 0`, `(s64)v >= 0` | `nor 3,3,3 ; srwi 3,3,31` | **HIGH (wrong)** |
| `(s32)v < 0`, `return v >= 0` | `nor 3,3,3 ; srwi 3,3,31` | **HIGH (wrong)** |
| `u64 v; (v>>63)==0` as s32 | `cmpwi r3,0` then `srwi r3,3,31` | HIGH |
| `u64 t = v >> 32` | `mr r4,r3` | **HIGH slot gets the LOW word** |
| `(v>>31) == 0` on the u64 | `slwi r11,r3,1 ; srwi r0,r4,31 ; or r10,r11,r0 ; srwi r9,r3,31 ; or` | scrambled |
| `((u32*)&v)[1]` / `((s32*)&v)[1]` | `stw r3,8(r1) ; stw r4,12(r1) ; lwz r3,12(r1)` | forces a **stack round-trip** |
| `struct {u32 lo,hi;}` pair return | same stack round-trip | worse |

Consequences for triage:
* **Every** spelling of "is the low word's sign bit clear" collapses to
  `cmpwi r4,0` + a signed branch. The branch form is reachable only via a trick
  that defeats the boolean fold (e.g. `u32 t = (u32)v >> 31; u32 w = t ^ 1u;
  if (w)` → `cmpwi r4,0 ; li r3,1 ; bge ; li r3,0`), and even then it is
  `cmpwi`+branch, never `clrlwi`+`cmpwi`. Fifteen spellings measured
  (`q1`–`q15`: named `u32 t`, named `s32 lo`, `!x`, `!= 0`, `t ^ 1u`,
  `u64 <= 0x7FFFFFFF`, `& 0x80000000` on u32/u64, `(v>>31)==0`,
  `s64 v = (s64)cal(...)`, `unsigned char` truncation) — **zero** produce `clrlwi`.
* **Different ProDG is not the escape.** All five installed compilers (3.5,
  3.5b140, 3.7, 3.8.1, 3.9.3) emit **byte-identical** code for
  `((u32)v >> 31) == 0` and for `s32 lo = (s32)v; lo >= 0`. It is one codebase
  with five front-end versions, so "this object was built with ProDG 3.7" never
  explains a DImode mismatch. Check this before blaming the compiler version.
* `-mps-float` and `-O1` change nothing here.
* The second tell-tale is `mr rA,r3 ; mr rB,r4` immediately after a call whose
  result is only used for the sign test: retail put the 64-bit result in a
  *non-hard* DImode allocno. No source spelling makes that survive regalloc —
  a distinct `u64`/`s64` local, an explicit `u64 copy = pair;`, and
  `s32 lo = (s32)pair;` all coalesce straight back into the return regs
  (thirteen variants, all 168 B / 29 words). Treat it as part of the same wall.
* Working spelling that genuinely reaches the **low** word when you need it as a
  *value*: `(u32)v < 0x80000000u`. Working spelling that reaches it as a
  *branch*: `s32 lo = (s32)v; if (lo >= 0)` (with a `t ^ 1u`-style side
  assignment to defeat the boolean fold).

Related: this is the second DImode-trust wall after `(u32)v >= 0x80000000u`
emitting `cmpwi + cror + mfcr` instead of a plain unsigned compare.

## 6gh — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80159C68 `ScriptGoalsEqualTo`, 61.3% → **EXACT 31/31**, object 124 B == symbol, 0 flags, 0 register pins, 1 `"+r"` barrier): **a float-equality tail that cc1 if-converts into `fcmpu cr7 ; mfcr ; rlwinm` is defeated by MERGING THE TWO `return 0` PATHS — a `goto` into one shared `return 0` (no barrier at all) or the already-promoted sibling's `"+r"(res)` barrier. The residue is always exactly +4 B.**

* **Symptom.** want ends
  `li r3,1 ; lfd ; lfd ; fsub ; frsp ; fcmpu cr0,f0,f12 ; beq END ; li r3,0 ; END:`
  but *every* spelling of `res = 1; if (a == b) {} else res = 0;` gives
  `frsp ; fcmpu cr7,f0,f12 ; mfcr r3 ; rlwinm r3,r3,31,31,31 ; b END ; li r3,0`
  — 5 insns, object 128 B vs want 124 B, and the masked scorer reports the
  whole tail (0x4c-0x7c) as a miss because the `li r3,1` is gone.
* **21 spellings measured, all if-convert** (128 B unless noted): `if/else`
  with both arms assigning, `? :`, `while (1) { …; break; }`, a named `s32`
  bool temp, an `f64` compare, `a < b` + `a > b` as two tests, comparing
  through a `f32 *`, reversed operand order, `if (a == b) { } else { … }`,
  `goto yes; return 0; yes: return 1;`, `"+f"` barriers on the converted
  value and on the stack float, a `"+r"` barrier on the *result* placed before
  the call (wrong place — it is load-bearing only AFTER `res = 1`),
  `volatile f32`, an extra statement after the tail. Flags are inert:
  `-fno-thread-jumps`, `-fno-gcse`, `-fexpensive-optimizations`,
  `-fbranch-count-reg`, `-fno-cse-follow-jumps` all give the same 128 B;
  `-Os`/`-O3` same, `-O1`/`-O0` worse, `-fno-schedule-insns` reorders
  everything and drops to 43.8%.
* **Hard-register pins DO defeat it but are not worth it.**
  `register s32 var_r3 __asm__("r3")` produces want's `fcmpu cr0 ; beq ; li r3,0`,
  but reserving r3 (a) pushes the int->float temp to r0 — `xoris r0,r3,0x8000`,
  124 B, wrong bytes; or (b) makes cc1 **drop the `li r3,1` outright**, 120 B.
  Pinning r5/r6/r7/r10/r11/r12 costs +8 B; r30/r31 spill and cost +20 B.
* **What actually works: merge the two `return 0` paths.** cc1 only if-converts
  when it can see a *pair* of foldable `li r3,0` stores. Collapse them:
  ```c
  if (GetFloat(arg0, 0, &sp8, 0) == 0) goto zero;
  fv = (f32)fn_801A6E64(...);
  if (fv == sp8) return 1;
  zero:
  return 0;
  ```
  This yields want's exact stream **including the `li r3,1` at 0x4c**, no
  barrier and no pin. The equivalent barrier form — used by the already
  promoted twin `src/fn_80159BEC.c` — is
  ```c
  res = 1;
  __asm__("" : "+r"(res));      /* AFTER res = 1, not before */
  if (fv == sp8) return res;
  return 0;
  ```
  Both are 124 B / 31-of-31. **Prefer the barrier form when a promoted
  sibling already uses it** so the two files stay diff-able.
* **The `(f32)` cast is not a `(f32)(f64)` cast.** ngccc lowers `(f32)(s32)x`
  through the magic-constant int->float expansion
  `xoris t,0x8000 ; stw t,lo ; lis r0,0x4330 ; stw r0,hi ; lfd f13,2^52+2^31 ;
  lfd f0,hi ; fsub ; frsp` — the exact dual of the matched float->int idiom
  `(s32)(f - lbl_2^31) ^ 0x80000000` (recipe 108, `src/fn_8005049C.c`,
  `src/fn_8016D52C.c`). `(f32)x` and `(f32)(f64)x` compile identically, so an
  m2c `(f32)(f64)` will *accidentally* match — write the plain cast anyway.
  The object DOES carry a private 8-byte `.rodata` with the magic double
  instead of referencing the game's `lbl_802A8170`/`lbl_802A8178`, which is the
  doc-14 shape: **not a blocker**, `tools/fix_fp_pool.py` retargets the HA/LO
  reloc pair and zeroes the pool at promote time (recipe 108's status line is
  stale on this point — see §4n's SOLVED note).
* **Verification done:** object `.text` 124 B == `symbols.txt` size; both
  internal `beq` reloc addends (104 -> 0x68, 108 -> 0x6c) decode to want's
  targets; both external `bl`s carry `R_PPC_CALL` relocs against
  `GetFloat` (0x801282E0) and `fn_801A6E64` (0x801A6E64). The twin
  `fn_80159BEC` (`bgt` / `fv > sp8`, pool slot `lbl_802A8170`) was already
  promoted and its body was the template — check `src/fn_<addr>.c` for the
  sibling BEFORE writing a new wip draft, `tools/sweepable_pool.py` counts
  those as `promoted` and the scorer skips them.

## 6gi — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x8011391C 5.1% → **86.5%**, and 0x80113224 35.1% → **EXACT 33/33**): **an m2c draft that scores under ~40% on a SMALL function is usually not a codegen problem at all — it is three trivially checkable defects: (a) garbage call arguments, (b) an UNDECLARED callee, (c) a pointer variable read through a pun. And: to make a value live in a callee-saved FPR, COPY IT OUT of the address-taken local into a plain one — `fv = sp8;` — never pass the address-taken local itself.**

### (a)+(b)+(c): re-read the want's `bl` sites before touching flags

* 0x80113224 `ScriptPlayMusicStream`: m2c wrote
  `GetFloat(...)` as `void GetFloat(s32,s32,s32,s32)` and left
  `PlayMusicStream` **completely undeclared**. Want's call sites are
  `bl GetChecksum_2` with `(arg0, 0, &sp8, 0)` and `bl GetFloat` with
  `(arg0, 0xFF6A9814, &spC, 0)`. Declaring all three callees with the return
  types they actually have (`s32 GetChecksum_2(CStruct*,s32,s32*,s32)`,
  `s32 GetFloat(CStruct*,s32,f32*,s32)`, `void PlayMusicStream(s32,f32)`),
  naming the default `extern f32 lbl_8029D10C`-style literal instead of
  `*(f32 *)0x8029D0E8`, and writing the positive arm as the `if` body took the
  object from 140 B/35% to **132 B == symbol, 33/33**. The undeclared callee
  alone was the whole +8 B (doc-56 `crclr cr1eq`).
  **Sweep for this class:** grep the wip draft for `(f32 *)0x` / `(s32 *)0x`
  address literals (should be an `extern lbl_…`), for calls to names that have
  no declaration in the file, and for a declared prototype whose parameter
  types disagree with `src/fn_<callee>.c`.
* 0x8011391C `ScriptSetGlobalPitchModulation`: m2c passed
  `GetFloat(0, &sp8, 0, 0x802A0000)` — pure garbage — never declared
  `fn_8011A888`, repeated `QB_ALL_SFX` where want materialises a *different*
  constant (`QB_ALL_STREAMS` = 0x6A3BD54B, built as `lis r4,0x6a3b ; ori
  r4,r4,0xd54b`), and punned `*(s32 *)&lbl_80302C34` where lbl_80302C34 is a
  plain `.data` s32. Fixing those four took 5.1% → **86.5%, object 148 B ==
  symbol**.
* Corollary: `(f32)intExpr` and `(f32)(f64)intExpr` compile identically (§6gh),
  so an m2c `(f32)(f64)` is not a bug — but a *missing* `(f32)` is.

### The `fv = sp8;` FPR-liveness trick

When a local's **address is taken** (`GetFloat(arg0, 0, &sp8, 0)`) and the
same variable is later passed by value to a final call, cc1 gives it a pure
stack home and **reloads it at the end** — no FPR is ever live across the
intervening calls, so the callee-saved `stfd f31`/`lfd f31` pair and the extra
frame simply do not appear. Copying it into a second, plain `f32` local
immediately after the call makes *that* local live across the calls:
```c
sp8 = lbl_8029D10C;
GetFloat(arg0, 0, &sp8, 0);
fv = sp8;                       /* <-- the whole 12-byte jump */
temp_r28 = lbl_80302C34;
temp_r29 = ContainsFlag(arg0, QB_ALL_SFX);
temp_r5  = ContainsFlag(arg0, QB_ALL_STREAMS);
fn_8011A888(temp_r28, temp_r29, temp_r5, fv);
```
gives want's exact `stfd f31,0x28(r1) / lfs f31,8(r1) / fmr f1,f31 / lfd
f31,0x28(r1)` and frame 0x30 instead of a 0x28 frame with a trailing
`lfs f1,0x10(r1)`. Rejected alternatives that do **not** work:
`register f32 sp8 __asm__("fr31")` (2.9% — the address-taken hard reg fights
the copy), `volatile f32 sp8` (2.9%), and dropping the dummy pad (73.0%,
still no f31). The one `volatile double _dummy` in the body is load-bearing
only for the frame *size* (0x30 vs 0x28) once `fv` exists.
Note the residual slot detail: the `volatile double` pad claims 0x8(r1)
whatever its declaration order, so `sp8` lands at 0x10 rather than want's 0x8
(three displacement-carrying words differ).

**Decoder gotcha #2 — `bl` in this DOL is NOT the textbook encoding, so a
bit-level branch checker silently "verifies" nothing.** At `0x8011324C` the word
is `0x48015485`: opcode 18, but **AA = 1 and LK = 0** — the encoding a standard
decoder reads as an absolute *branch*, not a branch-and-link (`0x80113280` ->
`0x48015061`, `0x80159C80` -> `0x4bfce661`, same pattern). Consequence: a
checker that decodes `bl` targets from bit fields prints garbage for every call
site and either reports false MISMATCHes or, worse, "agrees" with itself because
both sides run through the same wrong formula. **Verify call targets
structurally instead** (what `<scratch> does; exit 0 on both
EXACTs):
* want side <- `tools/disasm.py`'s own mnemonic + resolved target text. Note it
  prints addresses **UPPERCASE**: a `[0-9a-f]`-only regex silently drops every
  address containing A-F (it under-matched 2 of 3 call sites on first run).
* got side <- the object's `R_PPC_*` reloc at that same instruction offset:
  type 10 with addend 0 and a non-empty symbol is an **external call** (resolve
  the symbol through `symbols.txt`); type 10/11 with a non-zero addend is an
  **internal branch**.
* internal-branch addends are **function-relative**, so compare against the want
  target offset measured from the function entry, not from the branch
  (`branch at +0x20` targeting `+0x48` carries addend `0x68`).
* Filter reloc-vs-mnemonic pairs by offset, not by zipping two lists —
  otherwise an `R_PPC_REL24` on a plain `b` is miscounted as a call site.
Result for both EXACTs: all 5 external calls and all 4 internal branches match,
and both objects' `.text` equal `symbols.txt` exactly (124 B / 132 B).

### previous call's r3 result *is* this call's first argument**

symbol, 16.1%. Fixing the CFG first (delete the three `if (0)`s) alone got the
object to exactly 528 B; every remaining defect was then a size or register
question, not a structural one.

  `void` that the want actually uses as a value costs one `mr r3,X` per call
  site.** m2c wrote `fn_80191FD4(arg0);` (result discarded) because want's
  `bl fn_80191FD4` is followed by `cmpwi r31,0 / stw / bne` with no register
  setup at all — r3 already holds the object there. But r3 is caller-saved, so
  the next call (`GetChecksum_2(<obj>, QB_TRIGGER_OBJ_ID, &sp10, 1)`) needed a

  arg setup right after another `bl`" is positive evidence that the earlier
  callee returns a value — never 'fix' it by voiding the callee.**

  r3 (leaf, 0xF0 bytes), so it is 1-arg; want's r4/r5/r6 at that call site are
  leftovers (r5 even holds `&sp10` on the `arg3 == 0` path). Declaring 4 args

  reloads them (both are dead). A plain `s32 sp8 = 0;` is removed by cc1 (and
  the frame drops 0x38 → 0x30); `volatile s32 sp8 = 0;` emits the `stw` with no

  in r28 and `fn_800CBDE0()`'s result in r29; ngccc puts them the other way

  r4 that the freed QB_TRIGGER_OBJ_ID constant leaves behind. Robust against:

  nested `if`, early-return vs nested `if`, inverted compare, swapped branch

## 6g6 — 2026-10-03 (a15/0x801B4278, 396 B, m2c DIFF 15.4% → **NEAR 18.2%**, 0 asm, 1 flag): **under `-mps-float` it is not "a `__ps_t` live across a branch" that costs a frame slot (recipe 173) — it is a `__ps_t` live across a branch that is ALSO converted to `f32`.** Measured with 4 probe TUs (all `-mps-float`, `-O2 -G0 -mcpu=750 -fno-common`, `S V[9]` local pool so frame 0x50 is the no-extra-slot baseline): a PS value live across an `if` and used **only** by PS builtins afterwards → **frame unchanged**; the identical value with any `f32` use (`f32 x = m;` / `mag = m;`) → **+0x10** (an 8-byte home store + an `stfd`/`lfd` pair). The +0x10 is NOT avoidable by `register __ps_t`, by wrapping the variable in `union {__ps_t p; f32 w[2];}` or `SN_PS_type`, or by leaving the value unnamed and duplicating the expression so cc1 CSEs it — all four spellings measure identically. So a want whose frame leaves **zero** slack above its local pool, yet keeps a `ps_sum0` result in an FPR across a conditional call *and* copies it with `ps_mr` for the compare (`fcmpu cr0,f0,f12`), is not expressible in plain C: the project's matched siblings (src/fn_801B19DC.c, fn_801B27F8) buy it with `register __ps_t x __asm__("frN")` FPR pins. Corollary for triage: if a PS draft's frame is +0x10 and the residual is otherwise "every op in the right place", stop hunting the semantics — look for one `f32` copy of a PS value that is live across a branch. Second-order finding: `-fno-schedule-insns` alongside `-mps-float` was worth +2 points here (18.2% vs 16.2%) purely by making cc1 emit statement order literally (fn_801B4278 draft parked at that with the flag disclosed).

## 6g7 — 2026-10-03 (a06/0x80086B84, 524B, m2c 24.1% → NEAR **98.5%**, 0 asm, 0 flags): **a repeated 6-way float bbox test is ONE nested-if idiom (copy the matched sibling), and the "reload base" is the LAST field of the group — but a derived-IV init always lands at the END of the loop preheader.**

**The test itself is free.** `src/fn_8006C694.c` (matched) shows the exact
shape for

```c
r0 = 0;
if (o->x >= b->min_x) { if (o->y >= b->min_y) { if (o->z >= b->min_z) {
    if (o->x <= b->max_x) { if (o->y <= b->max_y) { if (o->z <= b->max_z) { r0 = 1; }}}}}}
```

— and it is byte-exact: `li r0,0` once per block, six
`fcmpu + cror crNun,crNeq,crNgt|crNlt + bns <merge>` (§ recipe 156 for the
negated form), `li r0,1` then `cmpwi` before the merge. Note which side gets
CSE'd: the **left** operand (the node-side struct) keeps its three values in
f11/f12/f13 for the three `<=` re-tests, while the **right** operand (the query
bbox passed in r31) is re-`lfs`ed at every single comparison. That asymmetry is
automatic — do not try to cache it. The `0/8/0x10` offsets mean the query
struct is `{f32 min[3]; f32 pad; f32 max[3];}`, not a packed 24-byte AABB.

**Three flags, not one.** Repeating that block N times needs N *distinct* 0/1
variables (`hit0/hit1/hit2`), each re-tested with its own `cmpwi`. With one
shared flag cc1's DSE deletes the 2nd and 3rd `li r0,0` (dead on the path that
reaches them) and every block after the first loses 4 words — that alone was
the difference between 93% and 98%.

**Reload base = largest field offset.** For three boxes walked with one
induction variable, `lfs -0x30/-0x2c/-0x28`, then `-0x18/-0x14/-0x10`, then
`0/4/8` from one base, ngccc picked base = *the last group member*
(`addi r30, node, 0x2A40`) and folded the other two to negative offsets. Writing
the pointer as `&entry[i].b[2]` (i.e. the third box) reproduces it; the natural
`e[i].b[0]/b[1]/b[2]` gives base `+0x2A10` with offsets `0/0x18/0x30` and 9
wrong words.

**The one thing I could not reproduce (parked blocker).** The residual is a
2-word swap inside the outer loop's preheader: want
`bl; mr r29,r28; mr r26,r3; addi r30,r28,0x2a40`, got
`bl; addi r30,r28,0x2a40; mr r26,r3; mr r29,r28` — i.e. want puts the
**derived** IV's init (`flags[i]`, strength-reduced) *before* the explicit
sibling init, my build always puts it last. And the two spellings are mutually
exclusive: making `p` an explicit walking pointer (`p = cur->flags; *p = 0;
p += 1;`) emits the init in the right slot but (a) CSEs `p + 0x2A40` so the
box pointer's base becomes r29 instead of cur, and (b) flips the callee-saved
colouring so `cur` takes r27 and the loop index r28 instead of the want's
r28/r27 (9 diffs, 93%). So: **derived IV ⇒ right colouring, wrong init slot;
explicit IV ⇒ wrong colouring.** Measured across 12 source spellings (derived
store `cur->flags[i]`, `*p` with explicit `p`, `(s32*)cur + i`,
`*(cur->flags + i)`, both-IVs-derived, explicit-box-pointer biased vs raw
`(u8*)cur + 0x2A40`, `b + 2`, `for` / `while` / `do-while`, comma-init in the
`for` header, and every ordering of the two inits): all of them land on exactly
one of those two states. Also noted: the loop counter is `u32`, since the want
uses `cmplwi r27,0x17f` (signed would be `cmpwi`) — one free word.

## 8a — Discarded-result RETURN types are a 2-word arg-move lever (fn_8011B9F4, 97.1% → 100.0%)

§4o lists "callee param types" as a scheduler lever for a lone 2-word
`mr`-order swap. The **return** type is an equally strong and much more
semantically decidable lever, and it shows up as one 2-word swap in a block
that otherwise matches. Mechanism: a declared non-void return makes
expand_call allocate a destination pseudo for the result; a declared `void`
does not. Removing/adding that pseudo changes the pressure in the call's basic
block, which is enough to flip an equal-priority ready-list tie between two
independent arg moves.

Two cases in one function, both found by reading the CALLEE, not the caller:

- callee that never writes r3 (`fn_8011A4E4` ends `lwz/stw` then `blr`, so it
  returns its own arg0) → caller must ignore the value, so declare it `void`.
  Fixed `mr r6,r29 ; mr r3,r28` → `mr r3,r28 ; mr r6,r29` at the arg setup.
