- callee that ends `mr r3,r31` after `mr r31,r3` (i.e. `return its argument`,
  `fn_801195DC`) → declaring it `void` was simply wrong. With the real
  `T *f(T *)` prototype the block's tie-break put the hoisted `addi r30,r1,0x20`
  before the ctor's `addi r3,r1,8`, exactly as the want had it.

Decision rule for a NEAR draft stuck on isolated `mr`/`addi` order swaps:
**audit every callee's RETURN path before touching statement order or flags.**
`grep`-grade check — if the callee ends without writing r3 it returns arg0, and
if the caller drops the value on the floor, `void` is the truth. Measurable
side-effect: `void*`/`B50Dst*`/`s32` param permutations were all no-ops here
(8 tried); only `s32` → `void` moved the needle.

## 6bw2 — 2026-10-03 single pick (0x8007297C, 620B, 16.77% → **EXACT**): **`rlwimi`-insert byte builds come from a 4×`u32:8` BITFIELD union (not a bswap), and ONE array makes dead stores live**

Two general levers, both found by reading the want's *own* instruction stream and
then reproducing it, no flags:

1. **`slwi r0,rX,24` + `rlwimi r0,rX,16,8,15` + `rlwimi r0,rX,8,16,23` +
   `rlwimi r0,rX,0,24,31` into ONE register is `rlwimi`-INSERT fusion, not a
   byte swap.** (Disassembler MB/ME are swapped vs. ngccc's asm: ngccc prints
   MSB-relative, so disassembler `MB,ME` ⇒ LSB bits `[31-ME .. 31-MB]`; confirm
   with `ngccc -S` on a one-function probe rather than reasoning from the
   disassembly.) Every plain-C spelling of the same value — `(x>>24)|((x>>8)&0xFF00)|
   ((x<<8)&0xFF0000)|(x<<24)`, the `((x<<24)&0xFF000000)|((x<<16)&0xFF0000)|…`
   "rotate-mask-or" form, `u32 r=v<<24; r|=…;`, `x*0x01010101`, `(x&0xFF)*0x01010101`,
   and even reading a union's byte fields and re-`<<`ing them — all lower to the
   7-insn `slwi`/`rlwinm`/`or`/`srwi` chain instead. The ONLY C that produces the
   insert chain is writing the SAME word through 8-bit BITFIELD members of a union:
   `union { struct { u32 a:8,b:8,c:8,d:8; } f; u32 w; } u;` — `u.f.a = x; u.f.b = x;
   u.f.c = x; u.f.d = x;` gives exactly `rlwimi 0,rX,24,0,7 / 16,8,15 / 8,16,23 /
   0,24,31`. Two corollaries worth remembering: (a) the FIRST member write must be
   a WHOLE-WORD write (`u.w = (x<<24)&0xFF000000;`) to get `rlwinm`/slwi instead of
   `rlwimi` for instruction #1 — a mixed word-view + bitfield-view sequence is
   exactly the §6bw-3 "two views = a union" shape; (b) an 8-bit field assignment
   takes the LOW 8 bits of the RHS, so `u.f.b = x` on the field at LSB bits 16..23
   compiles to `rlwimi 0,x,16,8,15` — i.e. the shift in the mnemonic is the *field's*
   position, not anything the source wrote. This extends recipe 110 / §6k from
   single inserts to a whole insert chain.

2. **Dead stores to a scalar local DIE; dead stores into an ADDRESS-TAKEN array
   survive.** Here want keeps four never-read stores (`stw r29,0x08` /
   `stw r30,0x0c/0x10/0x14`) that m2c faithfully reproduced as four scalars — and
   ngccc deleted all four, costing 4 insns *and* the frame (the `li r29,1` /
   `li r30,0` hoists into callee-saved regs disappeared with them, 676B vs 620B).
   Declaring ONE `s32 c[N]` array whose element at `+0x10` has its address taken
   (`&c[4]`) restored all four stores, interleaved them 1:1 with the following
   call's argument `li`s exactly as want does, and put the fctiwz/cvt temp at the
   want's offset. **So when a want has stores to slots nothing ever reads, do not
   reach for `volatile` first: ask whether the slot's neighbours are one object,
   and merge them into an array/struct with the address taken.** Bonus: the array
   size doubles as the frame-size knob (here `c[21]` = 84B at `+0x08` + 12B pad
   puts the cvt temp at `+0x68` and the frame at `0xc8`; `c[19..24]` all give
   0xd0/0xc8 shifts with every offset wrong).

3. **Signature-parameter ORDER is a register assignment, not cosmetics.** m2c emits
   a 7-param prototype in *use* order; if the real ABI order is 4 ints then 3 floats
   but m2c wrote `s32,s32,s32,f32,f32,f32,s32`, the last int lands in **r9**, not r5,
   and ngccc will silently `mr`+`cmpwi` the WRONG register with no diagnostic other
   than a drifting diff. Cross-check the caller's argument list (here
   `src/wip/fn_80072BE8.c`) before touching statement order.

4. Confirming note for recipe 108: a plain `(f32)(f64)s32` cast matches `.text`
   exactly AND hoists its synthesized constant into a callee-saved FPR exactly as
   want does, but it lands in module `.rodata`. The explicit union dance that names
   the real `.rodata2` double is *worse for the match*: it claims its own +8B slot
   (frame +8) and stops gcc from hoisting one copy of the global. The doc-14 pool
   wall is still a promote-time concern even for a masked-EXACT body.

## 6g8 — 2026-10-03 (a04/0x8004B798, 884 B, m2c DIFF 15.4% / object 908 B → **NEAR 29.9% with object 884 B == symbol**: **the 12-byte `{payload, next, prev}` CObject link temp must be a real `struct`, and cc1's register allocation here is so tight that adding ANY further local makes the draft strictly worse — "minimal-local spelling first", "explicit pointer for clarity" never**

Hand-rewriting the control flow from the DOL got this 884 B draft from a 908 B object to an
**exactly-sized** 884 B object: the m2c body modelled the link node as a bare `s32 *sp8`,
which pushes every other local down 4 bytes and yields frame `0x40`/`stmw r24`. Declaring
`typedef struct { Obj *payload; void *next, *prev; void *pad; } Unk_Link;` (the same 16-byte
idiom the matched `src/fn_8004BB2C.c`/`src/fn_8004B03C.c` use) pins `sp8` at `r1+0x8` and the
five `s32` out-params at `0x18/0x1c/0x20/0x24/0x28`, giving frame `0x50`, `stmw r25,0x34`,
`stw lr,0x54` — all three correct. The remaining 155 differing words here are **pure
regalloc/scheduling** (the two constants swap r27/r28; want keeps `&arg0->unk0x58` in a
callee-saved reg re-materialised on both join edges while cc1 rematerialises at each call site;
want keeps an address-taken `sp1C` in r29 across calls while cc1 leaves it in memory).

**The generalizable part is the sensitivity, not the fix.** Measured on this one draft, every
"make it clearer / hoist it / pin it" edit made it WORSE, because each extra pseudo shifts
cc1 2.95's `reg_alloc_order` for *every* value in the function:

| edit | score | size |
|---|---|---|
| minimal locals + literal `0`/`-1` stores (**kept**) | **29.9 %** | 884 B ✔ |
| `p58 = &arg0->unk0x58` once per block, use it everywhere | 14.5 % | 884 B |
| `p8 = &sp8` in the integer branch (the fn_8004BB2C idiom) | 20.8 % | 884 B |
| separate block-scoped result pointers instead of one shared `res` | 22.8 % | 876 B |
| shared `s32 t1` for the three `GetX` results (m2c's shape) | 11.8 % | 884 B |
| explicit `o = sp8.payload` preload before the release test | 12.2 % | 884 B |
| split `res = f(...)` from the two link stores | 15.8 % | 884 B |
| `s32 z1 = 0;` used instead of the literal `0` (recipe-64 idiom) | 7.8 % | 872 B |
| `if (sp1C) … else if (sp20) …` split into two `if`s | 23.6 % | 880 B |

So: for a draft that is already close, **count the locals first and treat any addition as a
regression risk**, and do not "borrow" a sibling's pointer-variable idiom unless want's
disasm actually shows a register holding that address. Conversely, *removing* a local the m2c
draft invented can be worth a lot on its own — here dropping the `s32 sp20 = -1` *initializer*
(the store belongs immediately before its `GetInteger` call, not at the top of the frame) was
alone worth **+17 points** (12.7 % → 29.9 %) and got the object to exact size. Triage rule:
when the object `.text` is a few bytes SHORT and the prologue looks right, suspect a local
that the want never initialises rather than a missing struct field.

## 8b — 2026-10-03 (a14/0x801A1C7C): **two address forms for one stack object = the source has BOTH a local array and a pointer alias into it; volatile read-counts are the fingerprint that reveals hidden f32 locals**

`0x801A1C7C` wanted `disp(sp)` for *most* references to its 160-byte local pool
but `disp(r27)` (r27 = `sp+8` = `&V[0]`) for nine of them. Two independent
lessons, both triage-grade. (1) **A want that mixes `off(sp)` and `off(rN)` for
the same object cannot come from one C variable.** A pointer alias makes every
access `base+disp`; a direct local array makes every access `off(sp)`. So the
source needs BOTH: the array spelled directly (for the `off(sp)` majority) and a
`volatile S *pv = V;` alias whose uses are exactly the `off(r27)` nine. Which
references land on which base is a reliable fingerprint for splitting the
original statements — here it identified `V[0].w[0]=z` (frame) vs
`pv[0].w[1]=z, pv[1].w[0]=z, pv[1].w[1]=o` (alias) and, in the sibling branch,
`V[0].p`/`pv[1].p` for the `psq_l` pair copies. Corollary: a second
`volatile S *pv4 = &V[4];` is what produces the want's lone
`addi r9,r1,0x28` + `0xc(r9)/4(r9)/8(r9)` store triple (+8 words on its own).
(2) **With a `volatile` array, every source mention of a slot emits its own
reload — so a *deficit* of reloads proves the missing mentions live in named
locals.** The want loaded `V[0].x`/`V[0].y`/`V[1].y` exactly once each (pinned
in callee-saved f11/f13/f10) while re-reading `V[1].x` five times; the naive
`V[6].w[0]=V[0].w[0]*V[0].w[0]` family needs eighteen reloads and never matches.
Counting want-reloads per slot therefore *derives* the source's local-variable
count instead of guessing it — `f32 a,b,c,d;` assigned from the volatile array
reproduced the product block instruction-for-instruction (28 for 28). Third
micro-lever from the same body: in `2.0f*(A+B)` ngccc emits the two `lfs` in
**source operand order**, so swapping `A+B` -> `B+A` flips their order and is a
legitimate single-variable fix (8 of the 12 `mm->f[]` sums needed it).

## 6fy2 — 2026-10-03 (0x800A0AA8, 740 B, m2c DIFF 25.3% → parked 35.0%): **`ps_muls0` (not `ps_mul`) is chosen by the SOURCE operand's type — a `union { f32 f; __ps_t p; }` local is the ONLY way to get an 8-byte-spaced slot with a 4-byte `stfs` fill, and `volatile` on the `__ps_t` struct members is what pins a PS store run to source order**

Four reusable results from one 740-byte QB `GetFloat`/`ContainsFlag` script
command (fn_800A0AA8; sibling fn_800A08C0 is already promoted and is the
proved reference for the same shapes). Measured with
`tools/ps_diff.py 0x800A0AA8` (LEAF_TMPDIR-scoped, no build/promote).

**1. `double * (float-in-ps)` → `ps_muls0`; `double * double` → `ps_mul`.** This
is the load-bearing fact and it is a *source-type* decision, not a flag: a
`__ps_t` operand whose pw1 is unknown must be multiplied with the FULL
`ps_mul`, while an operand that GCC knows came from an `f32` can use `ps_muls0`.
Retail's block is six `ps_muls0 fD,fA,fC` where `fC` is `psq_l` of a 4-byte
float slot. Written as `a = m->f88 * h;` with `__ps_t h` you get
`ps_mul f12,f12,f13` and every downstream register differs. The only spelling
that yields `ps_muls0` is a union with an `f32` member:

```c
typedef union { f32 f; __ps_t p; } U;   /* 8-byte slot, 8-byte aligned */
h.f = v1;                               /* -> stfs f0,0x138(r1)  (4-byte fill) */
a = __builtin_ps_muls0(m->f88, h.p);    /* -> psq_l f13,0x138 + ps_mr + ps_muls0 */
```
This generalises §6fb (f32-fill/`__ps_t`-copy-out) from *copies* to
*arithmetic*, and gives the missing half of it: the 8-byte-spaced local. A
plain `f32` local read through `((__ps_t *)&h)[0]` emits the same two
instructions but the frame slot is only 4 bytes wide, so a run of them lands
8 bytes off want's offsets. `__builtin_ps_add` / `__builtin_ps_sub` /
`__builtin_ps_muls0` are the only forms that emit `ps_add`/`ps_sub`/`ps_muls0`
for a PS accumulation; plain `+` on `__ps_t` gives `ps_add` but plain `-`
contraction produced `ps_madd`/`ps_madds0` in the branch arms (want has
`ps_muls0` + `ps_add` there), so the branch products must be written as
builtins too.

**2. `volatile` on the `__ps_t` struct members pins a `psq_st` run to SOURCE
order — and non-volatile members get freely sunk/recycled.** 33.7% → 35.0% and,
more importantly, it reproduced a 16-store `psq_st` run *offset-for-offset*.
Without `volatile`, cc1 moved `L.fF0/L.fF8` ahead of `L.fE0/L.fE8` and merged
the two `L.fC0` writes into the wrong slot group. Diagnostic in one look: a
want block whose `psq_st` run is monotonic in *struct offset* (0xE8, 0xF0,
0xF8, 0x100 …) — that can only be produced by ordering the stores, and
`volatile` is the only source-level way to order stores in C. Corollary: mark
the `Pt { volatile __ps_t x, y; }` sub-structs volatile too — making only the
0xC0..0x118 block volatile scored *worse* (33.2%), and making the union's `f32`
member volatile as well was much worse (25.0%, and 28 bytes short).

**3. Reading a global `f32` rodata2 constant three times has three distinct
codegen shapes; only one of them is retail's.** Retail emits, per constant,
`lis r9,hi` immediately followed by `lfs f31,lo(r9)` at the *point of first
use*, one `lfs` for all uses of that constant, with the address rematerialised
after every call. Measured, same body:

| source form | emitted shape | score |
|---|---|---|
| `extern const f32` + `s = lbl;` **after** the first call | one `lis`+`lfs lo(r)` per constant at first use; value held in a callee-saved FPR across calls (A/C→f31, S→f30) | **35.0%** |
| `extern const f32` + direct global reads | same address shape, but A/C→f30 and S→f31 | 26.6% |
| plain `extern f32` + `d1 = lbl;` locals | GCC keeps the *addresses* in GPRs (`lis r29,r30`) and reloads the value into f29/f30/f31 at every use | 1.0% |

So: when a want shows `lis rX,hi` + `lfs fY,lo(rX)` glued together at each
first use with the value then living across calls, you need `const` **and** a
named local assigned at that point — `const` alone leaves the constant in
memory and reloads it, no local at all loses the `const` CSE and puts the
address in a register. (`const` here is the §6fw/§6ek-1/§6fx alias oracle
again; the new part is that a named local is what turns the CSE'd load into a
callee-saved-FPR value instead of three reloads.)

**4. Residual for the parked function, stated so nobody re-derives it:** after
(1)+(2)+(3) the object is 732 B vs 740 B and 124/185 instructions have the
right *mnemonic* while only 64/185 are byte-equal. The 8-byte shortfall is two
words: want keeps each branch's two volatile reads of `L.p10.x/L.p10.y` inside
its own predecessor and tail-merges only `{muls0,muls0,psq_st,psq_st,add,add}`
(46 insns for the if/else chain); ngccc cross-jumps the whole SIDE arm onto the
DOWN-flag fall-through block instead, so the shared part carries the two
volatile loads once (44 insns). The other ~60 words are a pure register-allocation
difference (want: six products pinned in f9,f8,f7,f6,f11,f10 with the
accumulators in f13/f0 and the multiply operand in f12; got: products in
f13,f10,f12,f0,f8,f7 with accumulators in f6/f7 — ngccc *recycles* product
registers by hoisting the first two `ps_add`s above the remaining `ps_muls0`s).
Resistant to: 6 declaration orders of the `__ps_t` temporaries (byte-identical
objects), `ps_add(a,m58)` operand swap, `sh.f`/`d.f` store swap, a renamed union
typedef, moving the accumulator loads before the products, duplicating the
`L.p10` tail store into each arm, and both `-fno-schedule-insns` /
`-fno-schedule-insns2` (25.8% / 28.4% — i.e. the default scheduler is already
the best of the three, so the residual is a source-shape difference in the
RTL, not a flag). Class: same sched2 look-ahead wall as §6bu2.

## 6cp — 2026-10-03 (a02/0x80044614, 416 B, m2c DIFF 20.0% → parked 6.9% correct-body, 1 flag): **CComPtr/ref-cell walk rules — cell stride is 16 not 12, `&cell` must be homed through a pointer local, and the dead post-loop release block needs `-fno-thread-jumps`**

Applies to every function that walks `obj+0x64 -> obj+0x70` with
`CObject_AddRefLink(node, &cell)` / `CObject_RemoveRefLink(node, &cell)`
(0x80044614, 0x800447B4, 0x80044C64, …). Three transfer rules, all measured:

1. **The cell is 16 bytes on the stack although only 12 are live.** Wants put
   cell #1 at +8(r1) and cell #2 at +0x18(r1): stride 0x10, frame 0x48 with
   `stmw r25,0x2c` + `stw r0,0x4c`. Declaring the cell as the 12-byte
   `{void *f0; s32 f4; s32 f8;}` (what m2c emits, via `&cell` overlay math)
   makes cc1 put cell #2 at +0xC — overlapping cell #1's `f4` — and the frame
   collapses to 0x30. Fix: a real 16-byte `struct { void *f0; s32 f4; s32 f8;
   s32 pad; }`.
2. **Mixed MEM-base signature = `pa->f4/f8` through a pointer local, node store
   through the struct.** Wants emit `addi rX,r1,8` / `stw zero,4(rX)` /
   `stw zero,8(rX)` / `stw node,8(r1)` — two cell-field stores off a register
   base, the node store r1-relative. Source that reproduces it:
   `pa = &a; pa->f4 = 0; pa->f8 = 0; a.f0 = node;`. Both `((RefCell *)&a)->f4`
   and `*(s32*)((char*)&a + 4)` are canonicalised to MEM[0xC(r1)] (base reg
   gone). Second rule in the same breath: **`&cell` written inline never gets
   homed** — cc1 rematerialises `addi r4,r1,K` at every call site and drops to
   `stmw r26`; the address must be a `RefCell *pa = &cell` local. And
   **assigning `pb = &b` inside the loop body** puts the materialisation at the
   loop head (the want shape); the same assignment at function top hoists it
   into the prologue.
3. **`-fno-thread-jumps` (NEW flag for this project) preserves a provably-dead
   post-loop cleanup block.** Wants of this family end with
   `lwz rX,8(r1); cmpwi rX,0; bne loop; cmpwi r3,0; beq; mr r4,rCell; bl
   RemoveRefLink; li r0,0; stw r0,8(r1); li r3,1` — the release is dead on both
   edges. Default `-fthread-jumps` threads the edge and deletes 24 B; with
   `-fno-thread-jumps` the block survives (0x80044614: 380 B → 404 B) and the
   tail becomes instruction-for-instruction the want's. Even so cc1 coalesces
   the phi's incoming load with the phi result, so want's two `mr r3,r0`
   copies (load and phi kept as distinct pseudos) are NOT reachable in C — the
   house fix is the r3 pin used by the MATCHED src/fn_80044C64.c
   (`register s32 *copy __asm__("r3"); __asm__("" : "+r"(copy));`).
   Corollary: **a m2c husk can out-score a correct body** — the pre-a02 draft
   scored 20.0% purely because its broken +0xC cell offset the positional
   compare by two instructions, while the decoded body scored 6.9% with only 3
   of 104 slots wrong. Judge ref-cell walks on object size vs symbol size
   (404/416 here), never on the masked %.

## 6ar2 — 2026-10-03 (a11/0x80123BE0, 1328 B, m2c DIFF 16.27% → parked NEAR 78.61%, object 1328 B == symbol): **a memory-derived SECOND call's args must be hoisted into locals before the FIRST call, `(i & 0xF) * 0x20` (not `(i << 5) & 0x1E0`) defeats the loop-IV pass, and `memset`'s size arg must be `s32`**

Three reusable ngccc/GCC-2.95 facts, all measured on `src/wip/fn_80123BE0.c`
(the THUG2 stream/ARAM loader; both loops post `ARQPostRequest` twice).
1. **The want's arg-setup order is the fingerprint of locals.** The want
   computes the SECOND call's `src`/`len` (`addi r29,src,0x400`,
   `add r31,len,len`) BEFORE the first `bl`, in callee-saved registers. That
   is only possible if the source computed them into locals before the calls:
   every one of those args is derived from a GLOBAL load, and a call may
   clobber it, so cc1 must re-load after the call unless the value is already
   in a register. Copying them into `u32 src2, len2;` locals (+7% each loop)
   reproduces the want; leaving the expressions inline forces 3 extra `lbz`/
   `lwzx` reloads per iteration. Same trick for a base address: assigning
   `ctx = (char *)lbl_...;` INSIDE the loop body lets the loop optimizer hoist
   the 2-insn `lis`+`addi` into the preheader (where the want has it) —
   assigning it before the loop leaves it in the preamble and shifts the whole
   loop by 2 words.
2. **`(x & 0xF) * 0x20` vs `(x << 5) & 0x1E0` inside a loop.** Outside a loop
   both give `rlwinm rD,rS,5,23,26`, but in a counted `for` loop the second
   form is caught by the induction-variable pass (`li rX,0` in the preheader +
   `addi rX,rX,0x20` in the body + `rlwinm rD,rX,0,23,26`), while the first is
   not, so only it keeps the want's counter-derived `rlwinm rD,rI,5,23,26`.
   Worth trying on any loop that masks a shift (`(i<<k) & mask`).
3. **`crclr cr1eq` before a `memset` call tracks the SIGNEDNESS of the size
   parameter**, not the prototype's presence: `void *memset(void *,s32,u32);`
   emits `crclr cr1eq` before the call, `void *memset(void *,s32,s32);` (or a
   variable size) does not, even though both are prototyped. The house
   `void memset(void *,s32,u32)` spelling from 6bw2/§4r therefore injects one
   spurious word per memset call site; use `s32` for the size (the want's
   0x800 fits either way). Related: item 16's "prototype => no crclr" holds
   for every other callee tried here.
Also confirmed here: a `*(s32*)` spelling for an f32 global costs 5 insns per
store site (`fctiwz`+`stfd`+`lwz`+`stw`+`stw`) plus an extra FPR save, and the
unsigned-vs-signed int->f64 idiom (§231) is picked purely by the *cast* type —
`lbl_8039BE78` must be read as `u32` to get the `xoris`-free 2^52 form.

## 6zz — fn_8002C128 (float range test, 608B): BO polarity + the one-ret0-block-merge limit (agent a01, 2026-10-03)

Two transferable facts, both measured on ngccc/3.9.3 while rebuilding
0x8002C128 from 20% to 72.4% (object size exact, every basic block
byte-identical modulo reloc masks; only the tail blocks' `li r3,0` slot is
left). **(1) Read the want's float branches by BO, not by the mnemonic.** dtk
prints `ble` for BO=4/BI=1 (branch when CR0[GT] is CLEAR = `!(f1>f2)`) and
`bge` for BO=4/BI=0 (= `!(f1<f2)`), while BO=12 gives `bgt`/`blt`. So
`fcmpu cr0,f2,f0; ble ->L` means *continue when f2<=f0, else fall through* —
i.e. the branch is the "else" edge. Getting this backwards makes every
downstream block invert. The C forms (verified by micro-test, §6r-95/156
extended): `!(a<=b)` => `cror cr0un,cr0eq,cr0lt`+`bns`, `!(a>=b)` => `cror
cr0un,cr0eq,cr0gt`+`bns`, `!(a<b)` => bare `bns` on LT, `!(a>b)` => bare `bns`
on GT. **(2) ngccc's `jump()` block-merges only the ret0 block that is
CHAIN-ADJACENT to its block** — a `return 0;` written immediately after the
tests folds into the block (the `li r3,0` then gets hoisted to the block top by
the scheduler and the failure branches become bare `bns` to the epilogue), but
a `goto`-target label sitting after the `return 1` NEVER folds in: its branch is
redirected to the function's shared `li r3,0` sink instead. Worse, the fold
turns OFF above ~16-17 insns per block: a minimal repro (same source shape,
16-insn tail) folds both failure blocks; adding ONE `fsubs` to that tail (no
semantic change, 20 insns) makes ngccc stop folding and the first failure jump
to the shared sink. Practical recipe for a want that shows `li r3,0` early in a
block with two NaN-strict failure branches: write the FIRST test as
`if (!cond1) goto L;` and the SECOND as a plain `return 0;` with `L: return 0;`
after the `return 1;` — that is the only spelling that yields both the correct
`ble` polarity on the entry block AND the hoisted `li` in the tail (26%->72%).

## 6aa — 2026-10-03 (a17/0x8021C080, 308 B, m2c NEAR 94.81% → **EXACT**): **two page-anchored globals in the SAME page pick their address-base registers in SOURCE-MATERIALISATION order (r9, then r11), and a LO16-reloc'd `lwz` disp is MASKED by the scorer so it is never a real diff**

When a function needs two address constants whose pages coincide (e.g.
`lbl_802A83F8 = 0x802B0000-0x7c08` and `lbl_80303448 = 0x802B0000+0x3448`),
ngccc emits each as `lis` into a transient base + `addi`/`lwz` consumer and
allocates those bases in order **r9, r11, ...** — in the order the constants are
MATERIALISED, not the order they are consumed. m2c put `mgr = *(s32*)lbl_80303448;`
first, so the manager load took r9 (`lis r9; lwz r3,0(r9)`), the hook constant got
r11 (`addi r31,r11,...`), and `mr r29,r3` got dragged 3 words earlier — a 4-word
window that reads exactly like a "lis folding / `--lbl-types`" failure and is NOT
one. Fix: bind the OTHER constant to a local **before** the first load
(`hookv = (s32)lbl_802A83F8;` as the first statement, then the manager load, then
`itv[2] = hookv;`): the hook constant now materialises first and lands in r9 with
`addi r31,r9,-0x7c08`, the manager load takes r11 + `lwz r3,0x3448(r11)`, and
`mr r29,r3` lands in its original slot. 94.81% → 0 word diffs, one hoist.

Corollary that saves a round: in the masked scorer a `lwz rD, S@l(reg)` object
word and the want's literal `lwz rD, 0x1234(reg)` are **EQUAL** — the LO16 field
is masked, exactly like the HI16 of `lis`. So "the lwz is not folded into lis"
is never a real residual, and re-typing `extern char lbl_X[]` to a sized scalar
for that reason is always a wasted sweep. The *only* real signal in such a
window is which register each `lis`/`addi` names and the order of the window —
so diff the registers and the statement order, and check whether the second
constant could be materialised earlier in the SOURCE instead.

## 6a20 — 2026-10-03 (a20/0x800EB8F8, 304 B, m2c DIFF 12.82% → parked **NEAR 75.0%**, object 304 B == symbol): **reading ngccc branch targets from `.rela.text` addends, `(__ps_t)f32` is a silent no-op, psq_l does not CSE across an escaping-pointer store, and an address-escaping aggregate is how you keep otherwise-dead PS stores**

Five general facts from a 304-byte Gekko paired-single QB function
(fn_800EB8F8 = "advance two Vecs by dt", three calls to fn_800EBA28 whose first
argument is provably unused). Measured with
`tools/ps_diff.py 0x800EB8F8 --all` (which decodes both sides PS-aware and
applies the scorer masks; `want_got.py` and `tools/disasm.py` both stall on
Gekko PS words). All probes in a private LEAF_TMPDIR, no build, no promote.

**1. An object's real branch target is the `.rela.text` R_PPC_REL14/REL24
*addend* — a byte offset inside `.text`.** capstone (and therefore
`want_got.py` / `od`-style dumps) renders `target = addr + field`, i.e. it adds
the displacement *unshifted*. So for a **relocated** branch ngccc has put the
byte offset in the field and capstone is accidentally right; for a
**non-relocated** local branch capstone is off by a factor of 4. Read targets
off `ELFFile.get_section_by_name('.rela.text')` addends instead
(`r_addend` for REL14/REL24) — that is what proved fn_800EB8F8's five branches
(`+0x34,+0x64,+0x118,+0x11c,+0xf4`) were already byte-correct while the
disassembly looked wrong. Corollary: the scorer masks branch fields anyway, so
a "wrong-looking" branch target is never a real diff — only the branch's
opcode/BO/BI is.

**2. Assigning an `f32` to a `__ps_t` local is a silent NO-OP in ngccc.**
Probe TU, `-mps-float`: `f32 v; __ps_t a; a = v; return a;` compiles to
`blr` — the value is never materialised, and `(__ps_t)v` behaves the same.
`__builtin_ps_mr(f32)` ICEs (`optabs.c:4116`). The *only* way to feed a scalar
into a PS operand is therefore §6fy2's 8-byte union / 4-byte-slot form
(`h.f = v; ... __builtin_ps_muls0(x, h.p)`), which is why a want showing
`stfs f1,K(r1)` followed by `psq_l fD,K(r1)` can only be that shape — and the
`stfs` lands at the union's **offset 0**, so the +0 f32 member must be the one
you assign (getting this backwards shifts both by 4).

**3. `psq_l` loads are NOT CSE'd across a store through an escaping pointer.**
Writing `muls0(muls0(h->vB8,t),k)` four times in one statement run makes cc1
re-issue `psq_l fD,184(r28)` up to 3× per operand (measured: 344 B object vs
304 B want, 31.6%). Introducing plain, address-never-taken `__ps_t`
temporaries (`u0=muls0(h->vB8,t); w0=muls0(u0,k);`) restores the want's
single-load-per-operand shape and the exact 304 B size, because register
promotion means the intervening store through the escaping aggregate cannot
invalidate them. General rule: in a PS block, always bind each distinct
`psq_l`-able operand to a local once; do not rely on CSE.

**4. Dead 8-byte PS stores survive only if the aggregate's address escapes —
and the escape can be the call's own argument.** cc1 will not emit
`psq_st` to a local whose value is never read. Three ways to force them, in
increasing usefulness: (a) `volatile __ps_t` → store kept, **but every read is
also re-loaded**, so it costs you a `psq_l` per read (measured on the same fn:
32-byte frame, 56.6%); (b) `volatile __ps_t d[4]` with the reads kept on plain
non-volatile locals → stores kept, no reloads, but the store run comes out in
**forward** source order (agrees with 6fy2); (c) one `struct {__ps_t p0..p5;}`
whose address is passed to a call → all six stores kept, the run comes out in
**reverse** source order, and it also explains the want's `addi rD,sp+0x28` for
the same object. (c) is the one that matches wants which have both a dead store
run and a forward-arg `addi` into the middle of that run. Order of the members
in the struct is the order you must write the assignments in — reverse gives
p5,p4,p3,p2,p0,p1, which is the want's shape.

**5. Block ORDER (not branch polarity) is what `goto` buys you.** When a want
reads `cmpwi; bne BIG; <small copy>; b RET; BIG: ...`, writing
`if (f() != 0) { big } else { small }` gives `beq SMALL` with the copy
out-of-line — the opposite polarity, and every later word shifts. Writing
`if (f() != 0) goto big; small; goto done; big: ... done:` produces the want's
`bne BIG` + inline small block exactly, with the epilogue shared. Same trick for
the second if: `if (f() != 0) goto do_A; <B>; goto done; do_A: ... done:`.

Residual for the record (so nobody re-derives it): with frame, save area,
callee-saved assignment, all branch targets, every frame displacement and every
store address already matching, the last 19 words were pure **list-schedule
order / FPR choice** inside one PS window (the want interleaves two
independent `psq_l arg1` loads between the two `ps_muls0` and re-loads its two
scalar-fed ps locals *late*; we hoist all four multiplies first). Neither the
compute order of the four multiplies, `register __ps_t __asm__("frN")` FPR
pins, `-fno-schedule-insns2`, nor `-fno-expensive-optimizations` moved it
(`-fno-schedule-insns` alone is worse: 51%). It is a scheduler lock, not a
semantics error — triage it as such and do not burn a round re-deriving the
proto.

## 6bp — 2026-10-04 promotion round (0x8007297C, 0x800CC1D8, 0x80113BCC, 0x8011B9F4, 0x8019F938, 0x801CD68C, 0x8021C080, 0x80221C00, 0x80227D64, 0x80232B98 promoted; +10 fns, 9658 → 9668): **promote ONE ADDRESS PER RUN — a multi-address batch breaks the link even when every draft passes its gates and each promotes fine alone** and **`fix_fp_pool` mis-pairs HA/LO when one pool address has a `lfd` AND an `addi`**

1. **NEVER batch-promote. `promote_wip.py` accepting many addrs is a trap.**
   A 14-address batch failed the link (`.text` shrank 0x214, `_f_sdata2`
   moved 0x803CAF80 → 0x803CAD80, so `patch_dol`'s `BUILT_R2` assert fired
   and 541 520 bytes diverged). Bisecting showed the failure was NOT
   cumulative interference: `0x80120824`, `0x801227CC` and `0x80143B7C` each
   fail *alone*, while the other ten promote byte-identically one at a time.
   A 7-address batch that contained one bad address also poisoned the good
   ones, because the batch only reverts on the FIRST failure — the earlier
   successes stay half-registered against a broken link. **Always loop
   one address per `promote_wip.py` invocation and `cmp` between runs**, so
   a failure leaves the tree at the last known-good state.

2. **`fix_fp_pool` HA/LO pairing breaks when one pool address is referenced
   by BOTH an `lfd` and a separate `addi` (or by two `lfd`s at different
   offsets), because it grabs "the first ADDR16_LO within 0x40 bytes".**
   `fn_80120824` wants `lfd r0,0xD820(r9)` + `addi r9,r9,0xD820` — one
   address, two LO relocs. The tool paired the HA with the wrong LO and
   retargeted to `lbl_8029D820` (the `".ogg"` bytes) instead of
   `lbl_802AD820` (the `0.01`/`4096.0` doubles): a clean 0x10000 page error,
   2 bytes different in the DOL. `fn_801227CC` (4 sites → `lbl_8029E230`
   instead of `lbl_802AE230`) and `fn_80143B7C` (`lbl_8029F820` instead of
   `lbl_802AF820`) are the same shape. **Signature: a promotion that fails
   with exactly 2 differing bytes, one `fix_fp_pool` line naming an `lbl_`,
   and a `0x10000` page skew.** The masked scorer cannot see this — the
   reloc fields are masked — so the draft reads EXACT. Fix belongs in
   `fix_fp_pool.original_target_from_pair`: pair by *base register*
   (the `lis` destination must equal the load/addi's `rA`), not by
   proximity.

3. **`0x8025B340` fails with the big SDA shift, not the 2-byte pool skew**,
   so it is a separate root cause — likely a genuine payload/rodata claim
   (recipe 239's "verify a draft links BEFORE batch-promoting it"). Still
   parked in `src/wip/`.

## 9a — 2026-10-04 promotion round (0x80003AE8, 0x8004ADC8, 0x8004B270, 0x80040A20, 0x801B9110 promoted, 5 fns): **three levers that each took a 4-15% m2c husk straight to 100%, all with 0 emitted asm and no new flags**

**(1) A FUNCTION-POINTER FIELD'S ARITY IS A TYPE DECLARATION, NOT A CALL SITE (0x80040A20, 88.7% → EXACT).** m2c typed `Sub::unk0x4c` as `void (*)(u8*, s32, s32)` and passed `arg2`. Retail sets only r3 and r4 before `mtlr r0`/`blrl` — there is no r5 setup at all. Fixing the *field's* declaration to `(u8*, s32)` and dropping the third argument removes the stray `mr r5, r30` and the whole vcall setup lands. Triage rule: **for any `((T (*)(...))vt->f)(...)` vcall, count the argument registers the WANT sets between the preceding label and the `mtlr`** — do not trust m2c's arity, and fix it in the struct field so the declaration and the call move together. This is the "change the original variable type instead of casting" rule paying off where a cast cannot help.

**(2) A SHARED `Unk_*` STRUCT's FIELD TYPES ARE OFTEN ALL WRONG IN ONE DIRECTION; A FILE-LOCAL STRUCT IS THE FIX (0x801B9110, 3.9% → EXACT).** `Unk_52F5DCA2` declares `unk0xC` and `unk0xE4` as `s32`. Retail does `lwz r3,0xc(r31)` (a pointer) and `lfs f0,0xe4(r31)` (a float). With s32 fields every float use becomes `xoris`/`lfd`/`fsub`/`frsp`/`fctiwz`/`stfd` — 6 extra words and a `-0x20` frame instead of `-0x10`. Declaring a **local** struct with `void *unk0xC; f32 unk0xE4;` makes every access a single `lwz`/`lfs` and the frame collapses to native. **Do NOT edit the shared `include/structs.h`** — other drafts depend on the current shape; shadow it with a file-local typedef (same trick as 0x80003AE8's frame pad below). Corollary: `GetChecksum_3`/`GetFloat`-style accessors must be *declared*, or ngccc emits a `crclr cr1eq` that shifts the whole tail by one word.

**(3) AN EXPLICIT STACK MUST BE WRITTEN AS AN ARRAY TO GET `lwzu` (0x8004B270, 1% → EXACT).** m2c models the LIFO as a bare pointer walk (`var_r10 -= 4; *(s32 *)((char *)var_r10 - 4)`), which compiles to `addi r10,r10,-4` + `lwz`. Want's single `lwzu r11,-4(r10)` only comes from an array index (`node = *(T **)--p`). Also load-bearing there: the m2c **double-compare idiom** `var_r0 = (n > 0); if ((var_r0 != 0) && (n > 0))` is what expands to the 5-word `li r0,1 / cmpwi cr7 / bgt / li r0,0 / cmpwi r0,0 / beq / ble` run — collapsing it to `if (n > 0)` is 3 words short and scores 33%. And `count -= 1` must be the loop's FIRST statement, before the pop, or the `addi`/`lwzu` pair swaps order.

**(4) THE FRAME PAD IS EXACT, AND 24 BYTES IS A COMMON SIZE (0x80003AE8, 71.4% → EXACT).** The pure-expression body needs `stwu r1,-0x38`; retail has `-0x40`. `typedef struct { char x[24]; } Pad; Pad _pad;` closes it (ngccc rounds the frame to 8). `char x[16]` → 0x38 / 80.9%, `char x[20]` → 0x40 / 100% (rounds up like 24). No code is generated for `_pad`; it only sizes the frame. Two secondary wins in the same function: the rodata floats must be declared as **scalars** (`extern f32 lbl_...;`) not arrays indexed with `[0]`, and the out-struct stores must be in **ascending address order** (0x00, 0x04, 0x08, 0x0C) — the previous draft wrote 0x0C before 0x08 and ngccc emitted `stfs f1,8(r30)` ahead of `stfs f0,0xc(r30)`. **The pad is NOT a universal lever**: an automated sweep over 263 uncommented WIP drafts (`char x[N]` for N in 8..64) moved 40 of them but only by 1-5 points and produced ZERO new EXACTs. Use it when the want and got differ ONLY in `stwu`/`stfd`/`stw`/`lmw` offsets and every other word already matches; otherwise it is noise.

**(5) A `volatile` POINTER TO THE FIELD IS THE SOURCE-LEVEL WAY TO DEFEAT REL14 JUMP-THREADING — no flag, no asm (0x8004ADC8, masked-EXACT-but-REFUSED → EXACT).** `promote_wip.py` refused a 100%-masked draft because the `beq` at 0x8004AEA4 resolved to 0x8004AEE0 instead of 0x8004AEC4: retail re-loads and re-tests `sp8.f0` after the intervening indirect `vt2->f1` call, but ngccc forwards the earlier value and jump-threads the branch. Tried and rejected: `-fno-gcse`, `-fno-expensive-optimizations`, `-Os`, `-O1`, `-O3`, `-fno-schedule-insns`, and combinations (ngccc 2.95 accepts no `-fno-crossjumping` / `-fno-tree-pre`; `marking the whole local `volatile` costs 7 extra words and 11 branch diffs). What works:
```c
{ volatile CStruct **vpp = &sp8.f0;
  if (*vpp != NULL) { CObject_RemoveRefLink(*vpp, link); *vpp = NULL; } }
```
Generalises: **when `br_targets` reports a masked-EXACT draft with a single mismatched REL14 and the want visibly RELOADS the tested value, take the address of the field into a `volatile T **` and read through the pointer.** This is a new, cheap tool in the promotion-gate toolbox — reach for it before concluding "needs asm".

**(6) Parked with the correct body but still unreachable from C — the FPR/register-allocation wall (fn_80068B58 28.9%, fn_8005B68C 14.1%).** Both are semantically CORRECT and documented in-file: fn_80068B58's residual is that retail uses FOUR callee-saved regs (r28 mask, r29 arg0, r30 arg1, r31 node) where the draft needs three, and arg0 has no live use inside the loop in either version — so nothing in the source steers the allocator. fn_8005B68C trades `2*x`-hoisted-vs-per-arm against a clamp reload, and ngccc picks `mtctr`/`bdnz` vs `cmplw`/`blt` for the counted loop depending on whether the bound is a plain local. Same class as fn_800A95EC / docs/parkings/15: needs register pins, i.e. asm. **Park these with the full fix list in the header** (which is what made this round's two parks reusable) rather than the raw m2c husk.

## 6g9 — 2026-10-04 (0x801F36B0, 608 B, m2c DIFF 21.1% → parked **31.1%**, frame EXACT, 0 asm, 1 flag `-Os`): **a want's EXTRA CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER is often two loop-invariant ADDRESSES materialised in the INNER LOOP'S PREHEADER — and WHERE you declare them (loop body vs function scope) decides the whole colouring**

**The frame lever.** `Unk_5FCDF30E` (the m2c struct) makes this look like an ordinary
GPR draft: the want is `stwu r1,-0x40` / `stmw r21,0x14(r1)`, the m2c husk compiles to
`-0x38` / `stmw r22,0x10(r1)`. The instinct is "find the missing local". That is wrong.
The two extra words in the want are at 0x801F37E0/0x801F37E4 —
`addi r26,r30,0x303` and `addi r27,r30,0x301` — and they are **loop-invariant base
addresses**, sitting exactly where the innermost loop's preheader is (the inner
guard is 0x801F37D8 `cmplw r29,r0` / `bge`, the back edge 0x801F37B8 targets the
body at 0x801F37E8, i.e. it SKIPS the two `addi`). Reproduce them by declaring two
`u8 *` locals **at the top of the OUTER loop body**:

```c
for (i = 0; i < arg0->unk0x328; i++) {
    u8 *p303 = (u8 *)arg0 + 0x303;   /* = arg0->ent[i].taps  */
    u8 *p301 = (u8 *)arg0 + 0x301;   /* = arg0->ent[i].req   */
    ...
    if (p303[4 * i] != 0) AddInteger(obj, QB_NUM_TAPS);
    if (p301[4 * i] != 0) AddChecksum(obj, 0, QB_REQUIRE_PERFECT);
}
```
That alone takes the frame from 0x38 to **exactly 0x40 with `stmw r21`** and the
score 23.1% → 31.1%. **Placement is load-bearing and the two placements differ by
22 points:** the identical two locals at **function scope** also give 0x40 but score
**8.8%**, because cc1 then hoists them into the entry block (`addi r21,r30,0x303` /
`addi r22,r30,0x301` right after `stw r0,0x44(r1)`), which takes r21/r22 away and
pushes `arg1` out of r21 (`mr r23,r4`). So:

> **Triage rule for a `stmw rN` / frame-size mismatch: before hunting for a missing
> local, look in the want for loop-invariant `addi`/`lis` pairs sitting between a
> loop guard and its body. Materialise them as locals at the INNERMOST scope that
> still dominates their uses — not at function scope.**

This is the same family as §6dn ("the address got hoisted into a callee-saved reg")
and §6g8 ("any further local makes it strictly worse"), but the actionable part
here is the **scope of the declaration**, which neither of those covers.

**Loop shape: retail's nested loops here are GUARDED DO-WHILES.** All three loops
are `if (cond) do { ... } while (cond)`, never a plain `for`/`while`:
* outer loop 1 tests **`total`** at the guard (0x801F3710 `cmpw r28,r0`) but **`i`**
  at the latch (0x801F3758 `cmpw r29,r0`) — the double-compare is the signature, and
  m2c's `if (total < n) { do {...} while (i < n); }` reproduces it verbatim;
* it walks the `+0x300` entry array with a **pointer** (`addi r31,r30,0x300` /
  `addi r31,r31,4`), not an index;
* **do not cache `out` in a `set` local.** The want re-reads it from `0xc(r1)` on
  every iteration (0x801F37D0, 0x801F37F8, 0x801F38AC) because the intervening
  calls may clobber it. Introducing a `set` variable keeps it in a register and
  costs ~5 points. Same for the first loop's out-pointer at `8(r1)`.
* `j++` sits **before** the `fn_80129314` call and `k++` **after** it (0x801F38A0 vs
  0x801F38A8) — pure statement order, no semantic content.

**Negative results (so nobody re-tries them).** ngccc 2.95 **rotates** the innermost
loop (it drops the `cmplw r29,r0 / bge` guard and branches straight to the latch)
where retail keeps guard+latch; that rotation is 3 of the 4 words this draft is
still short, and the 4th is that got strength-reduces `4*i` to a running offset
(`li r26,0` / `addi r26,r26,4`) where want recomputes it from `i` (`slwi r0,r31,2` /
`mr r28,r0`). `-fno-crossjumping` and `-fno-tree-loop-optimize` are **rejected by
cc1** (not valid ngccc options); `-O2` (128 diffs) and `-fno-gcse` (107) both regress
against `-Os` (102), which the draft already carried. The residual is pure
callee-saved colouring with an identical instruction sequence — the §6f/§6g8
"needs register pins" wall.

**Semantics the m2c draft got wrong here** (all fixed in the parked body, listed
because each is a *declaration* bug, not a codegen bug): a tag!=0xD branch that
calls `fn_80129528` not `GetChecksum`; two flag fields of one 4-byte entry at
**+1 and +3** with the **+3 test first**; a chained callee (`fn_8003E7CC` feeding
`fn_80128F94`) whose void return must be a **pointer** or cc1 errors with "invalid
use of void expression"; and a magic constant that is `lis -0x2f23 / ori 0x47b`
= **0xD0DD047B**, not the `0xD0DC47B` the husk spells (one hex digit off in the
`lis` half — read `lis`+`ori` pairs as a unit, §4b).

## 6gj — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x800DFD2C m2c 34.6% → **EXACT 52/52**; 0x800DF924 39.7% → **NEAR 92.4%**; 0x80113F10 31.3% → **NEAR 51.4%** / size-exact): **`-Os` in a draft's FLAG line is almost always a stale m2c artefact; and ngccc's int<->float casts are TWO-WAY (u32 vs s32) with a magic-bias pool double, so the SIGNEDNESS OF EVERY CAST IS LOAD-BEARING**

Six reusable findings. All three drafts are left INERT in `src/wip` (nothing
promoted). Verified: `tools/test_wip_drafts.py --addr` for each, plus
`<scratch> (reloc-based call/branch target check) for the
EXACT one.

**(1) Drop `// FLAG: -Os`.** The game's game-code flag set is `-O2 -G0
-mcpu=750 -fno-common` (§4b). On 0x800DFD2C the *identical* body scored
**-Os 44/52 (84.6%) vs -O2 52/52 (100%)**; `-O1`/`-Os` were both 9/51 and
adding any `-fno-schedule-insns` was worse still (14/50). `-Os` disables the
scheduler that hoists the three FP-pool loads together — the exact thing want
shows. Before touching flags/pins on a draft, re-measure the body at bare
`-O2`; a `// FLAG:` line inherited from m2c is a red herring. (Same class as
`0x801F36B0`'s 1-flag `-Os` note in 6g9 — but there the flag was load-bearing,
so this is "measure", not "always drop".)

**(2) `(u32)` vs `(s32)` selects which pool double ngccc loads.** Complete
table for f32<->int in this compiler (extends recipe 231, which only had the
f64 side):

| C | emitted |
|---|---|
| `(f32)(f64)(u32)x` | `lis 0x4330; stw x; lfd; fsub <2^52>; frsp` |
| `(f32)(f64)(s32)x` | same + `xoris rX,rX,0x8000` first, `fsub <2^52+2^31>` |
| `(s32)f32val` | `fctiwz; stfd; lwz` — **no compare at all** |
| `(u32)f32val` | `fcmpu cr0,fX,f12(2^31); cror cr0un,cr0eq,cr0gt; bns/bso` then `fctiwz; stfd; lwz` on the `<2^31` side and `fsub <2^31>; fctiwz; stfd; lwz; xoris 0x8000` on the `>=2^31` side |

The `(u32)` form is a *branchy* unsigned conversion: the `xoris` re-inserts
2^31 as a raw bit, so `(v - 2^31) ^ 0x80000000 == (u32)v` for `v >= 2^31`.
Pool doubles are 2^52 = `0x4330000000000000` and 2^52+2^31 =
`0x4330000080000000`; ngccc synthesises them itself (doc 14 / `fix_fp_pool.py`
routes them, so this is NOT the old §4n pool blocker). Verified identical in
all five ProDG versions. Getting one cast's signedness wrong moves every
offset after it: on 0x800DFD2C the first cast being `s32` instead of `u32`
cost 34 points.

**(3) The compare that CONSUMES such a cast must have the same signedness.**
`fn(t) > (s32)k` emits `cmpw` (XO=0); `fn(t) > (u32)k` emits `cmplw`
(XO=32). One bit of XO, 1 point on 0x800DF924 (93.3% -> 94.4%). If want shows
`cmplw`, the C comparison operands are unsigned.

**(4) `(x > y) ? 1 : 0` and `res = 0/1` chains get if-converted to the
branchless `cmpw cr7 ; mfcr r3 ; rlwinm r3,r3,0x1e,0x1f,0x1f`**, which is
one instruction SHORT and shifts the whole epilogue. want's branchy form
`cmpw/cmpw cr0; li r3,1; bgt RET; li r3,0; b RET` comes from **nested `if`
blocks with an early `return 1` and a single trailing `return 0`**:

```c
if (a != NULL) { if (b != 0) { if (f() > (u32)k) { return 1; } } }
return 0;
```
This is the same cc1 if-conversion family as §6gh's `return 0` merge, seen
from the other side: there the fix was to *merge* two `return 0`s, here it is
to give the compiler a `return 1` it cannot fold away.

**(5) A 3-way SELECT must be ONE ternary expression, not an if/else-if chain,
when the arms are float expressions.** On 0x800DF924, writing the scale
selection as three `if` arms assigning to a local `v` lets ngccc tail-merge
all three into the float->int conversion and the FP registers collapse
(37%). Spelling it as one chained ternary

```c
k = (u32)((A || B) ? spC * SEC : ((C || D) ? spC * FRM : spC));
```
reproduces want exactly: first arm fully inlined, second arm jumping *into the
middle* of the first (just before the 2^31 load), third arm re-testing with
the opposite branch polarity (`bso` instead of `bns`+`b`). 82%. And note the
**operand order is observable** even though the multiply is commutative:
want is `spC * scale` (spC keeps f0, the constant goes to f13); writing
`scale * spC` keeps the *textually identical* `fmuls f0,f0,f13` but swaps
which value is in f0, costing ~9 points.

**(6) m2c's `lis`+`ori` constants: the `lis` half is the UNSIGNED image of the
signed immediate.** `-0x5aea` → `0xA516`, so `0xA5162BD2`; m2c's 0xA51542D2
was two digits off. Four constants wrong in 0x80113F10 (two of the four
happened to be self-consistent). Re-derive every `lis`+`ori` pair from the
signed `lis` immediate before assuming a codegen problem — see also the
`0xD0DD047B` note at the end of 6gi.

**Parked residuals (documented in the drafts, both named-cause, not
re-parked on "wall"):**
- 0x800DF924: want keeps TWO separate `li r3,0` tail blocks; every C spelling
  jump-threads the second into the first (360 B vs 368 B). `-fno-crossjumping`
  / `-fno-thread-jumps` are not in this ProDG fork.
- 0x80113F10: ngccc emits `fmr f0,f1` before `fctiwz`, which gives the float
  local a stack home and forces frame 0x28 + `stw r31` instead of want's
  frame 0x20 + `stmw r30`; separately, want's dispatch re-tests the first case
  pair with `cmplw` instead of reusing cr0 (16 vs 15 insns). Body is
  otherwise SIZE-EXACT at 280 B.

## 6gk — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80116018 `ScriptGetElement`, 30.1% → **NEAR 91.6%** / object 332 B == symbol, 0 asm, 0 flags): **when a `bl` has NO argument setup in front of it, the callee is being fed values the compiler happens to already hold in r3/r4 — read them off the PREVIOUS instructions and pass those, not what m2c guessed**

The m2c draft called `fn_801293FC()` with no arguments and `fn_8012954C()`-equivalent
with `arg1->unk0x18`. At 0x8011610C retail loads offset 0x18 of the arg1 home into r30 before the call, and at 0x80116110 it branches to 0x8012954C with no move into r3 and no immediate into r4,
and by then r3 = `sp8` (from `lbz r0, 2(r3)` in the switch dispatch) and r4 =
`spC` (from the `lwz r4, 0xc(r1)` bounds check). So the source is
`fn_8012954C(sp8, spC)` / `fn_801293FC(sp8, spC)`, and ngccc proves the point
by emitting no argument setup at all. Getting this wrong costs a redundant
`mr r3, rX` plus a stack reload in each of the two cases — **+35 points and
+8 bytes** here (56.5% → 91.6%, 340 B → 332 B == symbol).

Checklist when a `bl` sits in a bare block:
1. Walk BACK from the branch and list what is live in r3/r4/r5 at that point.
2. Compare with the callee's own body (`src/<callee>.c` or 4 instructions of
   disasm) to confirm the arity it actually reads.
3. If the callee reads r3 and r3 already holds the right value, the C
   argument is that same SSA value — passing any *other* variable is the bug.

Two more from the same draft:
- **`switch` must stay a `switch`.** An if/else-if chain over the same three
  type codes is 44.6% at the same object size; ngccc builds a different
  comparison tree than want's `{0xA, 0xC, 0x1}` binary search.
- **A `u8` discriminant read with `lbz` must be a `u8` field.** m2c read
  `*(s32 *)(sp8 + 2)`; the local struct is `{ u16 pad; u8 type; s32 count; }`
  and `type` must be `u8` for the `lbz`, `count` `s32` for the `lwz`.

## 6gl — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80116380 `ScriptGetRandomArrayElement`, 6.9% → **EXACT 102/102**, object 408 B == symbol, 0 asm, 0 flags): **`res = 0; if (c) {...; res = 1;} return res;` is almost never what want shows — read the `li r3,0 ; cmpwi ; beq <epilogue>` triple as an EARLY RETURN; and a value that must survive an intervening call has to be NAMED before that call**

Three defects in the old m2c draft, all found by reading want instead of
guessing. This is the companion to §6gk (same `ScriptGet*` family, same
`fn_80129xxx` value getters).

**(a) `res = 0; if (c) {...; res = 1;} return res;` -> early `return 0;`
(27.3% -> 79.2%).** At 0x801163E8 retail loads the count from offset four into r0, at 0x801163EC materialises the zero return value into r3 before the compare, at 0x801163F0 compares r0 against zero, and at 0x801163F4 branches on equal straight to the epilogue at 0x80116504 rather than to any later value materialisation.

The `li r3,0` *before* the compare and the branch straight to the epilogue is
a `return 0` in its own basic block. With a `res` variable ngccc instead keeps
`res` in r0 across the whole switch and ends with `li r0,1 ; mr r3,r0`
(two instructions) where want has one `li r3,1`. Generic form:

> `li rX,<ret> ; cmpwi/blr ; beq/bne <epilogue>` = `if (cond) { return <ret>; }`.
> Do not model it as an accumulator variable.

**(b) Name a value that must survive an intervening call (79.2% -> EXACT).** In case 2, at 0x801164C0 retail loads offset 0x18 of the arg1 home into r30 before the call, at 0x801164C4 copies r29 into r4, at 0x801164C8 calls 0x80129420 which clobbers r3, at 0x801164CC loads the high part for the constant argument into r4, at 0x801164D0 copies r30 into r3 after the call, and at 0x801164D8 calls 0x8012772C.

ngccc will otherwise sink `lwz r3,0x18(r31)` to just before `fn_8012772C`,
keep no surviving copy, and drop the `mr r3,r30` — 4 bytes short. Forcing the
read into a local **inside the case** reproduces it:

```c
case 2: { s32 sc = arg1->unk0x18;
          fn_80129420((s32)sp8, index);
          fn_8012772C(sc, QB_ELEMENT); break; }
```

Hoisting `sc = arg1->unk0x18` OUT of the switch (before it) is much worse
(41.8%) — the load has to stay per-case. Corollary for triage: a body that is
exactly one instruction short with everything else aligned is usually one
missing `mr rX,rY` that a named local would have forced.

**(c) Callee arity comes from the CALL SITE, not the promoted prototype.**
`src/fn_8012772C.c` declares `void fn_8012772C(CStruct *, s32, f32 farg0)`
(3 args) but this caller passes 2. `fn_80129420` returns `f32` and the result
is DISCARDED, so the C must call it as a statement (a bare statement keeps
`f1` unused and emits no code).

Also: `QB_ELEMENT` = 0xBEBFA1C6 and `QB_INDEX` = 0x7F8C98FE ARE named in
`include/qb_constants.h` — check the dictionary before leaving a raw
literal in a draft. (The same 0xBEBFA1C6 correction applies to
`src/wip/fn_80116018.c`, whose m2c draft had 0xBEBEA1C6.)

## 6gm — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80116164 `ScriptGetNextArrayElement` 8.9% → **EXACT 135/135**; bf/0x80115170 `ScriptGet2DArrayData` 23.1% → **EXACT 147/147**; both object size == symbol, 0 asm, 0 flags): **a run of `cmpwi r0,K ; beq <same target>` in want is TWO IDENTICAL `case` BODIES, NOT a fallthrough — "tidying" it into `case 3: case 4:` costs 55 points; and a struct field read in two arms of a diamond must be ONE named local, because GCC 2.95's CSE does not do it**

Companion to §6gk / §6gl (same `ScriptGet*` family, same `fn_80129xxx`
getters). Both of these are "the draft is right but 2 of 9 switch arms are
wrong" failures; the remaining arms already matched, which is what makes the
two defects look like codegen noise.

**(a) Duplicated identical `case` bodies are NOT a fallthrough (0x80115170,
42.3% → EXACT).** At 0x8011524C retail unsigned-compares r0 against three, at 0x80115250 branches on equal to 0x80115278, at 0x80115254 unsigned-compares against four, at 0x80115258 branches on equal to that same 0x80115278 block as case three, and at 0x8011525C branches unconditionally to the default at 0x8011537C.

and the target block is a single `AddString(sp8, spC, ...)` + `break`. m2c
had written the tidy

```c
case 3:
case 4:
    AddString(...);
    break;
```

which collapses to ONE `cmpwi` + ONE `beq`: object drops to 142 B (vs 588 B)
and the score to 42.3%. Writing the two `case` arms out with **duplicated
bodies** reproduces both compares and the exact 147/147 / 588 B. GCC 2.95 tail
-merges on `beq` but emits the tests from the arm labels, so it keeps the pair.

> Triage rule: `cmpwi r0,K ; beq <T> ; cmpwi r0,K2 ; beq <T>` with one shared
> target means *N separately-written case bodies*, not `case K: case K2:`.
> The opposite is also real — where the runs point at *different* blocks they
> genuinely are fallthroughs (§6gl's 0x80116380 / 0x80116164). Read the branch
> targets, don't assume.

**(b) The array COUNT is ONE named local, read before the index test
(0x80116164, 92% → EXACT).** At 0x801161D0 retail loads the stack slot at r1 plus eight into r9, at 0x801161D4 compares it against zero, at 0x801161D8 branches to the zero-return on equal, at 0x801161DC loads the stack slot at r1 plus 0xC into r11, at 0x801161E0 performs the single hoisted count load from offset four of that pointer back into r9, at 0x801161E4 compares r11 against zero, and at 0x801161E8 branches to the bump path on greater-or-equal.

`if (spC >= sp8->count) return 0;` spelled inline gives TWO `lwz …,4(r11)`
(one per diamond arm, 544 B). Merging to `if (spC < 0) {...} else { spC++; if (spC >= n) return 0; }`
with `n = sp8->count` *at the use site* gives one reload but an extra `b` and
loses the `>= 0` branch (536–540 B, 27–87%). Only the declaration-hoisted
`s32 n = sp8->count;` placed before the `spC < 0` test gives want's shape.
This is the general lesson of the file: **when a struct field is read in two
arms of a diamond, hoist it into a named local — GCC 2.95's CSE does not.**

**(c) Two-parameter prototype inferred from `mr r30,r4`.** 0x80116164 uses
arg0 exactly once, but the prologue's `mr r30,r4` means r4 is the SECOND
parameter, and r3 is still live (untouched) at the `GetArray(arg0,0,&sp8,0)`
call site, so arg0 needs no callee-saved home. A one-parameter prototype moves
arg1 into r3 and scores 8.0%. Rule: **a callee-saved spill of a register in
the prologue is a parameter, even when the parameter is used once.**

**(d) `fn_8012954C` / `fn_80129504` / `fn_801294E0` shapes.** In the 2D family
`fn_8012954C(spC, sp10)` is the *index descent* and `fn_8012954C(sub, sp14)`
the *value getter* — one function, two roles, exactly as in §6gl.
`fn_80129504` / `fn_801294E0` return a POINTER to a struct whose `f32` members
sit at +4/+8/+0xC: declare them returning `s32` and cast at the use site.
`GetArray` is called with `arg1->unk0x18`, not arg0; its `s32` return is
tested against 0 and on 0 the fallback is `spC = (s32)fn_801259C8(sp8, 1)`
(a `void *` return stored straight into the `s32` slot).

Verification: `tools/venv/bin/python <scratch> — 0x80116164
19/19 calls, 0x80115170 22/22 calls, and every internal-branch reloc addend
matches want's branch target. Both drafts remain **inert / unpromoted**.

## 6gn — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x801153BC `ScriptGet3DArrayData` 7.7% → **EXACT 156/156**, object 624 B == symbol, 0 asm, 0 flags; bf/0x8011562C `ScriptGetNDArrayData` 12.6% → parked **91.2%** with `-fno-cse-follow-jumps`, object 636 B == symbol): **when a function's SIBLING is already EXACT, rewrite the parked draft as a literal transliteration of the sibling's shape — the whole function often falls out in one step; and NESTING a call into another call's argument list is what makes cc1 hoist a frame reload above the inner call and cost a whole callee-saved register**

**(a) Sibling-transliteration beats incremental repair (0x801153BC,
7.7% → EXACT in one edit).** The `ScriptGet*` family is four near-identical
functions; once `ScriptGet2DArrayData` (0x80115170) was EXACT, the 3D version
needed nothing but its shape copied and two semantic fixes read off want:

* **A chained descent is TWO calls to the SAME function through a NAMED
  local**, and the *element* getter takes the LAST index, not the array:

  ```c
  sub = fn_8012954C(spC, sp10);   /* descend by index1 */
  sub = fn_8012954C(sub, sp14);   /* descend by index2 */
  switch (((Arr *)sub)->type) {
  case 1: AddInteger(arg1->unk0x18, QB_VAL, fn_801293FC(sub, sp18)); break;
  ```

  m2c had `fn_8012954C(spC, sp10); fn_8012954C(sp14);` (second call with a
  dangling single argument) and then `fn_801293FC(sp18)` in every case — i.e.
  it never passed the descended array pointer at all. want's
  `lwz r4,0x10(r1) ; lwz r3,0xc(r1) ; bl ; lwz r4,0x14(r1) ; bl` (r3 already
  holding the first result) plus `lbz r0,2(r3)` with no reload is the tell.

* **Case ORDER in the source need not follow want's binary-search tree.**
  0x801153BC's source order is 1, 2, 13, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12 while want tests
  5, 2, 1, 3, 4, 10, 6, 12, 13. Irrelevant — only the `cmpwi` values and the
  body of each arm matter.

> Generalise: the parked functions in a family are not independent problems.
> The cheapest first move is `diff`ing a parked draft against its EXACT
> sibling's structure, not against want.

**(b) NEVER nest one call inside another's argument list when the outer
argument is a frame slot (0x8011562C, 22.4% → 52.3%, and it fixes the
frame).** Retail loops by loading the stack slot at r1 plus 0x10 into r3, copying r30 into r4, incrementing r30, and calling fn_801293FC, then copying the call result into r4, loading the stack slot at r1 plus 0xC into r3, calling fn_8012954C, and storing the result back to r1 plus 0xC, with the bottom block reloading the 0x10 slot and its offset-four word, decrementing by one, and looping back on unsigned less-than against r30.

Written as `spC = fn_8012954C(spC, fn_801293FC(sp10, i));`, cc1 **hoists the
`spC` frame reload ABOVE `bl fn_801293FC`** so the value is live across a call,
needs a third callee-saved register, and emits `stwu r1,-0x28(r1)` /
`stmw r29,0x1c(r1)` / `mr r29,r4` instead of `stwu r1,-0x20(r1)` /
`stmw r30,0x18(r1)` / `mr r31,r4`. Written with a **named temp for the INNER
call**:

```c
s32 t = fn_801293FC(sp10, i);
spC = fn_8012954C(spC, t);
```

the reload lands after the call (as in want), only r30/r31 are saved, and the
score goes 22.4% → 52.3%. This is §6gl's "name a value that must survive a
call" seen from the other side: there the naming *keeps* a load alive; here
the naming *lets the compiler re-sink* it.

Also load-bearing here: the loop bound is `(u32)(count - 1)` — want's guard
is `cmplw`, not `cmpw` (§6gj). `while` instead of `do/while`, a `for` loop,
`u32 i`, a named `n` for the count, and `(s32)((u32)c - 1)` all measure worse.

**(c) `-fno-cse-follow-jumps` decides whether the array pointer lives in a
register across the dispatch (52.3% → 91.2%, 604 B → 636 B).** Without it
cc1 CSEs the descended-pointer reload and keeps it in **r3** across the whole
switch, which deletes the per-case `mr r3,r9` (7 instructions) and leaves the
object 32 B short. With it the object is size-exact. Same flag as the
0x80113CC4 draft; `-fno-schedule-insns` = 45.0%, `-fno-strength-reduce` and
`-fno-delayed-branch` = no change, `-fno-tree-pre` does not exist in this fork.

**(d) The remaining 8.8% is a register-residency wall.** Retail loads the stack slot at r1 plus 0xC into r9, copies r3 into r4, and loads the type byte from offset two of the pointer held in r9 so the pointer stays resident in r9 across the tree, with each case loading offset 0x18 of the arg1 home into r30, copying r9 into r3, and calling fn_801293FC.

The draft (same instruction count, same size, wrong register) copies r3 into r4 first, loads the stack slot into r3 instead, and reads the byte through r3, with each case reloading the stack slot into r3 rather than reusing a resident register before loading r30 and calling.

Rejected spellings, all ≤ 91.2%: `s32 sub = spC;` named copy (before *or*
after the `idx` call, in the switch and every case) — cc1 **coalesces the copy
back onto the frame slot**, and placing it before the call additionally wants a
third callee-saved reg (79.3%); `Arr *a = (Arr *)spC;`; `u8 ty = ...->type;`;
`s32 *pc = &spC;`; a `(char *)spC + 2` byte pun; `Arr *spC` instead of
`s32 spC`; `u32 idx` — every one of these produces **byte-identical output**,
so cc1 fully normalises them; a separate loop-carried `cur` also stored to
`spC` (14.4–77.4%, `cur` must survive the inner call so it takes a
callee-saved reg); `register s32 sub __asm__("r9")` **destroys the dispatch
tree** (33.5%), `__asm__("r28")` / `__asm__("r26")` = 88.7%. A value live
across JUMPS but never across a CALL in any path is exactly what plain C will
not make cc1 keep in a caller-saved register here — park it.

Verification: `calls3.py` on 0x801153BC gives 24/24 `bl` sites and every
internal-branch reloc addend matching want; 0x80115170 22/22. Both EXACT
drafts and the 0x8011562C NEAR draft remain **inert / unpromoted**.

## 6go — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80115E3C `ScriptForEachIn` 44.6% → **81.1%** in vrun / 73.9% under `test_wip_drafts.py`; bf/0x80114448 `ScriptGetTerrainTypeParam` 7.4% → 9.6%; bf/0x80116D2C `ScriptSetPrintText` 14.4% → **EXACT 76/76**): **a loop whose preheader JUMPS OVER the body to the condition (`b <COND>` with the body BELOW) is cc1's rotated `while` — `do/while` produces the opposite and costs 36 points; and `s32 pad[0xA0]` is 0x280 bytes**

**(a) `while`, not `do/while`, when want's preheader branches over the body
(0x80115E3C, 37.9% → 74.2% — the single biggest step in that function).**
Retail lays the loop out twice with the preheader loading the stack slot at r1 plus 0xC into r9, materialising zero into r29, and branching over the body to the condition; the body copies r30 into r3, calls fn_8012705C, increments r29, calls fn_80131008, and reloads the stack slot; and the condition loads offset four, unsigned-compares r29 against it, and loops back on less-than.

The preheader's `b` skips the body on the first pass, so the loop is
*bottom-tested* with the body laid out after the guard — cc1's rotated
`while`. Written as `do { ... } while (c);` cc1 emits the body falling
straight through from the preheader and **no `b` at all**, and every
instruction from there on shifts. `for (; i < n; i++)` measures identical to
`while`; only `do/while` is wrong.

Corollaries measured on the same body:
  * the index increment belongs at the **end** of the body, immediately
    before the last call (`addi r29,r29,1 ; bl fn_80131008`), not in a `for`
    header — worth ~1 point and 4 bytes;
  * the SECOND loop's bound must be a named **`u32`** local
    (`u32 n = (u32)count; while ((u32)i < n)`): +4.7 points / +4 bytes over
    inlining `(u32)((Arr *)spC)->count` at the test.

**(b) `s32 pad0x1C[0xA0]` is 0x280 bytes, not 0xA0.** The old draft's
`Sc` had `s32 pad0x1C[0xA0]` between `unk0x18` and `unk0xBC`, so `arg1->unk0xBC`
compiled to `lwz r5,0x29c(r31)`. Padding arrays in these structs must be
`char[]`. Same family as the `fix_scaled_ptr.py` sweep recorded in earlier
headers — **audit every `padN[...]` for its element type before believing an
offset.**

**(c) 0x80116D2C `ScriptSetPrintText`: m2c's `goto block_28` stitching and
temp-hoisted `else` arm are the whole 14.4% → EXACT gap.** want is a plain
`if (GetText(...)) { ...; sprintf(...); free } else { ...; sprintf(...) }`.
The two other defects were mechanical: `fn_80126EAC` is genuinely **0-argument
and chained** off `li r3,8 ; bl fn_80019D08` (declare `s32 fn_80126eac();` —
an explicit `(s32)` parameter is a *different* prototype to cc1), and the QB
constants QB_TEXTNAME 0xFF0DB407 / QB_PRINTFTEXT 0xBC4AC08B were raw hex in
the draft. All five string addresses decode as `lis r4,-0x7fd6 ; addi r4,r4,K`
pairs (0x802A0000 + K), not `lis`+`ori`.

**(d) 0x80114448 stays in the DIFF tier on a parameter-homing tie-break.**
The 7.4% -> 9.6% step below is a `vrun.py` figure: `test_wip_drafts.py`
classifies this body DIFF and prints no percentage for that tier. want
gives the heavily-used arg0 **r31** and the once-used arg1 **r29**
(`mr r31,r3 ; mr r29,r4`); the draft homes them the other way and the whole
body permutes. Hoisting `sp10 = 0` above the first call *does* produce want's
two separate zeros (`li r3,0` for sp10, `li r0,0` shared by sp8/spC) but
scores worse, so that `li r0,0` is a red herring. Also measured: `== 0`-first
arm order, a named `a0` copy, `void *` parameters, and an early-`return 0`
tail — all ≤ 9.6%.

Note on tooling: `vrun.py` and `test_wip_drafts.py` can disagree by several
points on the same body (0x80115E3C: 81.1% vs 73.9%) — `test_wip_drafts.py`
is the scorer that counts for the drafts, so re-measure there before parking.

## 6gp — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x8011261C `ScriptSetLightDiffuseColor` 87.5% → **EXACT 48/48**; bf/0x801126DC `ScriptGetLightCurrentColor` 5.0% → parked **97.5%** 78/80, object 320 B == symbol, 0 asm, 0 flags): **an 8-bit field that want materialises with a NEGATIVE `li` must be declared `s8` (write `-128`); and a packed word that must be re-read BYTE-WISE must be reached through an ADDRESS-TAKEN pointer — a plain local lets cc1 forward-props the word store and delete the initialising byte stores**

### (a) negative `li` ⇒ signed 8-bit field

want (0x801126DC +0x1c, and 0x8011261C) materialises negative 0x80 into r9 and stores that byte to offset three of the colour object.

ngccc folds a `u8` initialiser to `0x80` **no matter which cast you write** —
`(u8)-0x80`, `0x80`, `(unsigned char)0x80` all give `li r9,0x80`. Only a
**signed** declaration produces the negative constant, because the constant
goes through `convert`/`force_fit` on an `SImode` `-128` and is re-materialised
as a signed 8-bit value:

```c
typedef union {
    struct { u8 r; u8 g; u8 b; s8 a; } bytes;
    s32    value;
} Color;

p->bytes.a = -128;   /* s8  -> li r9,-0x80 ; stb r9,3(r29)   MATCH */
p->bytes.a = (u8)-128; /* u8 -> li r9, 0x80 ; stb r9,3(r29)   MISS */
```

Rule of thumb: **read the sign of the `li` and make the field match it.**
`li rK,-0x80` ⇒ `s8`; `li rK,0x80` ⇒ `u8`. (Same family: `li rK,-1` on a
stored byte ⇒ `s8` too.) Worth 10 points on 0x8011261C on its own.

### (b) byte-wise re-reads ⇒ address-taken pointer

0x801126DC initialises four bytes and then, after each call, re-reads them
individually. Written with a plain union local:

```c
Color col;
col.value = v0;                       /* callee result  */
AddInteger(arg1->unk0x18, QB_AMBIENT_RED, col.bytes.r);
```

cc1 sees the whole `col` object die at the last read, so it **forward-props the
word store into register extracts** (`srwi r5,r30,0x18` / `rlwinm` chains) and
then deletes all four initialising `stb`s as dead. Retail keeps all of them: it spills the word to r1 plus eight, then re-reads the red byte from that spill and the green and blue bytes from offsets one and two of the colour pointer into r5.

The fix is to make the object's **address escape** so cc1 cannot forward-prop:

```c
Color col;
Color *p = &col;              /* ADDRESS-TAKEN */
p->bytes.r = 0;  p->bytes.a = -128;  p->bytes.g = 0;  p->bytes.b = 0;
fn_80059284(&v0);
p->value = v0;                /* every field read now goes through p-> */
AddInteger(arg1->unk0x18, QB_AMBIENT_RED, p->bytes.r);
```

This was the entire 5.0% → 73.8% step (12 store/load instructions).
Corollary: it also reproduces want's **mixed base registers** — the first read
comes back off `r1` (`lbz r5,8(r1)`) while the later ones come off `r29`
(`lbz r5,1(r29)`), because after `addi r29,r1,8` cc1 has a live FP but the
`stw` was already issued. Do not "tidy" that; it is load-bearing.

### (c) `mr r30,r4` in the prologue ⇒ TWO parameters

`mr r30,r4` (rather than `mr r29,r3`) means **r4 is the second parameter** — even
when the first parameter is never read in the body. With a one-parameter
prototype the homing register lands on r3 and cc1 emits `mr r29,r3` instead,
which cascades into different base registers for the whole body. Worth **23
points** here (73.8% → 97.5%) purely through register homing. Cheap check on
any draft: `grep 'mr r29,r3' ` on the want prologue ⇒ you dropped a parameter.

### (d) residual — doc-15 arg-setup interleave (unresolved)

want hoists the first call's argument setup INTO the middle of the byte-store
block: retail materialises the call argument by adding 0xC to the frame pointer six instructions early, interleaved with byte stores to offsets three and two of the colour object, a copy of the fourth argument register into r30, further byte stores down to offset one, a condition-register clear, and then the call.

the draft sinks it one slot (`stb r9,3(r29) ; addi r3,r1,0xc`) — 2 words, the
doc-15 family (`docs/parkings/15-call-arg-setup-scheduling.md`, same wall as
fn_80112860). Measured and all worse — store orders `r,g,b,a` (97.5%, same 2
misses), `r,g,a,b` (97.5%), `a,r,g,b` (88.8%), `g,a,r,b` (88.8%), `b,a,r,g`
(90.0%), `r,b,g,a` (95.0%), `g,b,r,a` (90.0%), `a,g,b,r` (88.8%), `r,a,b,g`
(95.0%); packing the locals into a `struct { Color col; s32 v0,v1,v2; }` block
(22.4%, 340 B — cc1 loses the re-reads entirely); a second address-taken alias
`q` for the alpha store (4.7%); `s32 v[3]` + `&v[0]` (9.3%); `((s8*)p)[3] = -128`
(4.7%). Interleaving the CALL between the initialisers is far worse still
(`fn_80059284` right after the alpha store = 61.3%, before it = 67.5%): cc1
then relocates `addi r29` and the whole prologue. `volatile Color` (3.8%) and
dropping the initialisers outright (8.6%) are both far worse — it really is the
arg-setup placement, and store order is a red herring.

## 6gq — 2026-10-04 (bf): **the frame-slot order in this compiler is NOT declaration order and is NOT reachable from C** — recorded so it stops being re-attacked (0x801179F0 `ScriptStringToCharArray`, parked 83.3%, 9 residual words, all one cause)

`0x801179F0` wants a `char *` at `r1+8` and a `u16` at `r1+0xc`; every C body
puts them the other way round. Measured directly:

- `u16 h; char *s;` and `char *s; u16 h;` produce **byte-identical** objects —
  the two slots always come out in the same order. Declaration order is
  irrelevant.
- Renaming the accumulator (`zz`, `w`, `spA`, `aaa`, `szz`, `acc2`) changes
  nothing, so it is not name-sorted either.
- Packing both into one `struct { char *s; u16 h; }` / a matching `union` /
  `char blk[8]` + pointers is much worse: the object grows 216 B -> 224 B and
  every offset moves (7.1%, 7.1%, 5.4%).
- `volatile u16` = 43.6% / 220 B; an unused `s32 dummy` does not shift
  anything.

**Consequence: a residual that is purely "two frame slots are swapped" is a
wall. Spend one experiment on it, then park and write the measurement up.**
Contrast with the cases where the slot order IS reachable (0x8011313C
`ScriptPlayTrack`, 0x80112A94 `ScriptLoadSound`): there the locals are
genuinely ordered and the STORE order is what matters. Rule of thumb: if you
can name a source statement order that changes which `st*` instruction lands
at which address, keep tuning; if every permutation of the DECLARATIONS gives
the identical object, stop.

## 6gr — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80112A94 `ScriptLoadSound` 9.6% → **EXACT 94/94**; bf/0x80137E30 `fn_80137E30` 75.6% → **93.3%**; bf/0x80118DF8 `ScriptUnloadScene` → **EXACT**; bf/0x8011313C, 0x80117284, 0x80118DF8 all **EXACT**): **four rules that between them took five Script functions to byte-identical**

### (a) A global reached via a bare `lis` + displacement MUST be spelled `extern`, never a literal `*(T *)0xADDR`

This is the single biggest lever found this session (+82 points on
0x80112A94, and it is the difference between a 396-byte object and a
byte-exact 376-byte one). Retail loads the high-adjusted half 0x802A0000 into r9 and then loads float register f13 from the low-adjusted displacement negative 0x2F3C, reaching address 0x8029D0C4, with both words relocation-masked as high-adjusted and low-adjusted halves.

A literal cast instead materialises the whole address first through a different high half into r11, ORs in the low half 0xD0C4, and loads float register f0 from offset zero with one extra instruction.

Both words differ, and the desync cascades through the whole body.

**Rule (this is the useful generalisation of the AGENTS.md "`.sdata` globals
can't be scored" note):**
- want `lis rX,H ; lfs/lwz ..., D(rX)`  ⇒ **`extern`** with the real symbol
  name from `config/G2TE52/symbols.txt` (here `lbl_8029D0C4`, `.rodata2`;
  `lbl_80302C34`, `.data`). The scorer's `0xFFFF0000` mask on the LO word keeps
  `rX` and `D`, so `extern` scores clean.
- want `lis rX,H ; ori rX,X,K ; lfs ..., 0(rX)` ⇒ a **literal cast** is correct.

Corollary that matters for triage: the AGENTS.md warning about
`R_PPC_ADDR16_LO` masking is about the LO word's OPCODE being masked. If the
want form is `lis`+folded-displacement, the masked got still matches — so a
function touching rodata globals is **not** automatically unscoreable. Only
the `lis`+`ori`/`addi`-then-load shape is a hazard.

### (b) `register s32 v __asm__("rN");` — a hard register pin that works, and beats an asm barrier

want materialises a parameter into a specific register ONCE, early, and then
uses that register for both a guard and a call argument: it copies r7 into r6 once in the entry block at offset 0x24, tests r6 against zero at offset 0x3C in the guard, and still holds the fourth call argument in r6 at the call.

Plain C always coalesces `s32 a4 = arg4;` back onto `arg4`'s own register
(r7), so cc1 emits `cmpwi r7,0` and sinks the copy to the call site — worth
**13 points** on 0x80137E30. Both of these fix it:

```c
register s32 a4 __asm__("r6");          /* hard pin — PREFERRED, no statement */
a4 = arg4;
```

```c
s32 a4;
a4 = arg4;
__asm__ ("" : "+r" (a4));               /* zero-length barrier — also works */
```

Pin beats barrier (93.3% vs 91.1%) because it emits no statement at all. Two
placement rules: the pin must come with its `= arg4` **after** `arg0->unk0x4 = 0;`
(pin-then-copy-first = 15.2% / 184 B — cc1 emits two copies), and a barrier
placed *immediately* after `a4 = arg4;` is equally bad (23.9% / 184 B). The
barrier is otherwise insensitive to placement (91.1% anywhere else in the init
block); right before the guard it gives 86.7%. This was independently found
by another agent on the sibling 0x80137F30 (`a5` → `r6`) — pin both.

### (c) A parked `// FLAG: -fno-schedule-insns` is usually compensating for a MIS-TYPED CALLEE, not describing the target

0x80118DF8 `ScriptUnloadScene` sat at 55.3% with `// FLAG:
-fno-schedule-insns`, added by a 2026-09-13 flag sweep. With the signatures
fixed, the flag body is **55.6% / 144 B (8 bytes short)** and the bare `-O2`
body is **EXACT 38/38 / 152 B**. The flag was suppressing over-scheduling that
the *wrong body* caused. Re-measure every parked flag at bare `-O2` before
believing it — especially `-fno-schedule-insns`.

### (d) When a callee is passed a frame-slot VALUE that is immediately tested, it is passed BY VALUE

0x80118DF8: want does `lwz r3,8(r1) ; cmpwi r3,0 ; beq <end> ; bl 0x80054E1C`.
The old draft typed `fn_80054E1C(s32 *)`, which forces cc1 to keep the
*address* of the slot alive: it hoists `addi r31,r1,8` into the prologue and
rewrites every later access as `mr r3,r31` / `mr r5,r31`, shifting the whole
function by one word. Fixing value-vs-pointer was worth **~80 points**
(15-20% -> EXACT). This is the frame-slot analogue of §6gp(b): *any* wrong
pointer-vs-value typing makes cc1 pin the address and rewrites the prologue.

### (e) bonus — `subfic r0,r3,0 ; adde r3,r0,r3` is just `x != 0`

Several tiny Script wrappers (`ScriptClearMusicTrackList` and friends) emit
that pair for `fn(ContainsFlag(...) != 0)`. Write it as `!= 0`; do not try to
spell the two instructions.

## 6gs — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x8011391C `ScriptSetGlobalPitchModulation` 86.5% → **94.6%**; bf/0x801137A0 `ScriptSetSfxReverb` 9.6% → **95.7%**): **`-mps-float` is the honest replacement for the `volatile double _dummy` pad — prefer it on EVERY FPR-frame draft; and a float argument that must survive a call needs a NAMED `f32` local**

### (a) Drop the `_dummy` pad, add the flag

The long-standing workaround (AGENTS.md §5, and ~100 parked drafts) is to pad
the frame with `volatile double _dummy;` until `want_frame - native_frame`
diverges by the right multiple of 8, so the callee-saved-FPR save area lands
where want has it. **`-mps-float` does the same thing without lying about the
frame**, and it also gives the pad's slot back to a real local:

| function | pad | pad stripped + `-mps-float` |
|---|---|---|
| 0x8011391C | 86.5%, `sp8` pushed to `r1+0x10` by the pad | **94.6%**, `sp8` back at `r1+8`, object still 148 B |
| 0x801137A0 | n/a (no frame slot available) | **95.7%** (78.7% bare) — frame 0x28 → 0x30 |

0x8011391C is the clean demonstration: the pad was claiming `r1+0x8`, so the
real `f32` local `sp8` landed at `r1+0x10` and three displacements were wrong.
Removing the pad *and* adding the flag fixes the frame AND the slot at once.

**Sweep result (71 parked drafts with a pad, automated):** 5 improved
(0x802337CC 25.0→36.5, 0x800DCBD4 32.6→37.2, 0x801118C8 63.9→65.4,
0x80016EDC 66.4→67.8, 0x8011D870 23.3→24.0) and **the other 66 are
byte-identical either way** — so the flag is free but not universal. Two
warnings: (i) it is **PER-OBJECT** (AGENTS.md §4b — globally it breaks
FPR-frame matches); declare it with the `// extra_cflags:` marker.
