(ii) **Do not assume the pad is always removable**: 0x800DFD2C is EXACT 100%
*with* its pad and also 100% with the pad stripped + `-mps-float`, but other
pads are genuinely load-bearing. Always measure both ways — never bulk-delete
them. The 66 unchanged cases are the ones where the pad was load-bearing or
irrelevant, and stripping them would have been a silent regression if the
comparison had been one-sided.

### (b) A float argument that must survive a call needs its OWN named `f32` local

This is the other half of both wins, and it is independent of the flag
(2.3% → 78.7% on 0x801137A0 at bare `-O2`):

```c
f32 sp8, vol;
sp8 = K;
GetFloat(arg0, 0, &sp8, 0);        /* &sp8 escapes -> sp8 MUST live in memory */
...
vol = sp8;                          /* the copy is what gets cached in f31   */
fn_8011A908(global, spC, ContainsFlag(arg0, K2), vol);
```

Passing `sp8` **directly** as the argument makes cc1 give it a pure stack home
and reload it after the intervening call (`lfs f1,0x10(r1)`), so no FPR is ever
saved: frame 0x28, 136 B, 2.9%. The one-line copy makes a *separate* plain
`f32` live across the call, which forces the callee-saved FPR and reproduces
want's `stfd f31` / `lfs f31` / `fmr f1,f31` / `lfd f31`. Found independently
on 0x8011391C and re-confirmed on 0x801137A0 — it generalises.

**Diagnostic:** want has an `stfd fXX` / `lfd fXX` pair that your object does
not, and your frame is short by exactly 8 → the float you are passing is
sitting in an address-taken slot. Copy it into a fresh local immediately
before the call.

### (c) residual shared by both: doc-15 FP-argument-setup interleave

    want: [mr r5,r3][fmr f1,f31][mr r3,rX][mr r4,rY][bl]
    got:  [mr r5,r3][mr r4,rY][mr r3,rX][fmr f1,f31][bl]

ngccc sinks the `f1` setup below the GPR `mr`s. Measured on 0x8011391C and
identical on 0x801137A0: nesting the inner call into the argument list,
swapping local declaration order, reordering the temporaries, and adding a
second named `f32` are all byte-identical; `-fno-schedule-insns`/-`insns2` are
worse. Treat it as the 2-word wall for this shape.

## 6gt — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x800DAEFC, 27.1% → **EXACT 34/34, 136 B**): **under the psABI an `f32` RETURN value comes back in `f1`, not `f0` — and m2c mistypes such callees as `s32` and invents a phantom float parameter**

This un-parked a draft that had been sitting at 27.1% and is the single
cheapest type fix in the project. Retail opens with a bare 0x10-byte frame that grows the stack, saves the link register, saves from r30, spills r0 at offset 0x14, and copies r3 into r30; calls the constructor with r3 still live in a zero-argument-like shape; runs the stores; materialises zero into r4 and calls 0x8012570C whose result appears nowhere before; loads the 0x7FD6 high half into r9 and the lbl_80299D64 float into f0; multiplies the callee's f1 return by that constant into f1; squares f1 into f0; and stores the two results to offsets 0x24 and 0x20 of r30.

The tell is **`f1` read without ever being written in the function**, and
**no callee-saved FPR anywhere** (frame is a bare 0x10, only `stw r0,0x14`).
That combination is only consistent with f1 being *defined by the preceding
call*. In the 32-bit PowerPC psABI (SVR4 / EABI-style, what ProDG targets
here) the float argument registers are **f1..f8** and f0 is not one of them,
so `f32 fn(...)` returns in **f1**; `double` returns in f1:f0; `s32` in r3.
So `fmuls f1,f1,f0` reads `return_value * lbl_80299D64`.

### (a) Why m2c gets this wrong, and the signature of the mistake

m2c typed the callee `s32 fn_8012570C(s32, s32)` (see the old draft in git).
That single wrong return type cascades: ngccc can no longer produce an FPR
value, so it must be invented from somewhere, and cc1 reaches for the
*parameter list* — it made the function `fn(Obj*, f32)` with the float in f1
and then had to keep it alive across `bl 0x8012570C`, emitting
`fmr f31,f1` + `stfd f31` in the prologue. Result: frame 0x20 instead of 0x10,
148 B instead of 136, and 4 extra instructions. All four hand variants I tried
scored 2.7% — the body was right, the *signature* was wrong, so the fix had to
come from the return type, not the statements.

### (b) The fix

```c
f32 fn_8012570C(s32, s32);                    /* NOT s32 */
...
arg0->unk0x20 = fn_8012570C(K, 0) * lbl_80299D64;   /* ret*K lands in f1 */
arg0->unk0x24 = arg0->unk0x20 * arg0->unk0x20;      /* f1*f1, re-read from f0 */
```

That is the whole change: **34/34 words, 136 B, bare `-O2`, no flags, no
padding, no pins.** Note `unk0x24` is computed by **re-reading the field
through `arg0`**, not from a C temporary — that is what produces the two
separate `fmuls` with no reload, and it is the natural way the original would
have been written.

### (c) Independent confirmation already in the tree

`src/fn_80054720.c:21` and `src/fn_800ADE30.c:19` both declare
`f32 fn_8012570C(s32, s32);` — the return type was known; only the m2c draft
in `src/wip/` got it wrong. So this is a per-draft m2c defect, not a global
one, and it means **`src/*.c` (already-matched files) is ground truth for
callee return types** whenever it disagrees with `src/wip/`.

### (d) Sweep for the bug class — worth doing, low yield but cheap

`<scratch> cross-references every `fn_*` prototype in
`src/`, `src/wip/` and `include/dolphin/` and lists the 49 functions declared
`f32` in one place and `s32`/`void` in another. Restricting to `src/wip/`
declarations that disagree with a known-`f32` `src/` declaration gave 19
candidates; mechanically flipping `s32` → `f32` and re-scoring moved only
three (0x80054048 6.3→17.7%, 0x801DE50C 8.3→15.2%, 0x801DDA34 1.0→9.7%) and
one REGRESSED hard (0x801F0610 74.4→7.7% — its declaration is a *self*
prototype, so the flip changed the function's own definition). Every
remaining candidate was ≤5% both ways: those drafts are broken for other
reasons too, so **the type fix is necessary but rarely sufficient**. Do not
expect more 27%→100% jumps from this class; the payoff is that it unblocks
the frame, which is a prerequisite for everything else.

## 6gu — 2026-10-04 (0x801227CC, 0x80120824, 0x80143B7C all **PROMOTED**, DOL byte-identical): **`tools/fix_fp_pool.py` paired HA/LO relocs by PROXIMITY, which silently mis-targets every pool address that has more than one reloc — the fix is to group by pool ADDEND**

§6bp item 2 diagnosed this class ("`fix_fp_pool` mis-pairs HA/LO when one pool
address has a `lfd` AND an `addi`") and named the fix location. **This round
implemented it, and it converted three long-parked masked-EXACT drafts into
real promotions in one sitting** — `0x801227CC`, `0x80120824` and `0x80143B7C`
all now link byte-identically; the first two had been re-promotion-attempted
45 and 35 times respectively and auto-reverted every time.

**THE BUG.** `fixup()` walked the `.rodata` ADDR16 relocs and, for each `HA`,
grabbed *"the first unused `ADDR16_LO` within 0x40 bytes"*, then retargeted
**that one pair** to the `lbl_` at the address the original DOL bytes
reference. That is correct only when every pool address has exactly one HA and
one LO. Neither holds:

* **(a) one address, two LOs.** One pool address used by both an
  `lfd`/`lfs` and a separate `addi` (`fn_80120824`: `lfd r0,0xD820(r9)` +
  `addi r9,r9,0xD820`). The first LO got the right label; the **second LO was
  left pointing at the `.rodata` section that the same script had just
  emptied**, so the linker resolved it against `.rodata+0` — a byte stream,
  which is why the failure showed up as a clean `0x10000` page skew.
* **(b) ONE HA, TWO LOs — ngccc CSEs the `lis`.** `fn_801227CC` emits
  `lis r30,…` once and feeds two `lfs f1,…` loads from it (the compiler proved
  the page base loop-invariant). The `used` set then handed the second LO to the
  *next* site's HA, retargeting it to a completely different `lbl_`.

**THE FIX** (in `fixup()`, replacing the proximity search): group the
`.rodata` ADDR16 relocs **by their addend** — the byte offset into the private
pool. HA and LO for the same pool address always share it, it is unique per
pool entry, and it is completely insensitive to *how many* relocs reference
that entry. Each group is one *site*: resolve the site's original DOL address
once from any (HA, later-LO) instruction pair via the unchanged
`original_target_from_pair`, then retarget **every** reloc in the group to that
one label. A group with HA but no LO (or vice versa) is a hard error.

**Signature to recognise it** (all three, every time): a promotion that fails
with **exactly 2 differing bytes**, one `fix_fp_pool:` line naming an `lbl_`,
a `0x10000` page skew, and a draft that scores masked-EXACT — because the
reloc fields are masked, so the scorer cannot see it. **Any masked-EXACT draft
that fails to link with a 2-byte delta should be checked here FIRST.**

**Why it went unnoticed for so long:** the old code had a *correct* fallback
(addend matching) but only reached it after the proximity search had already
consumed the right LO. Correct code in a branch that can only run when the
first branch fails is not a safety net.

**Verification.** `<scratch> re-runs the pre-fix and
post-fix `fix_fp_pool` over every built `build/G2TE52/src/fn_*.o` and diffs the
resulting reloc→label maps; the three promotions above each did a full
`ninja` link + `cmp orig/.../main.dol` = byte-identical. Any object the
regression flags must be re-verified by a link before trusting it.

## 6gv — 2026-10-04 (0x8013928C parked; 0x80044110 parked at 91.3%; 0x800A16B8, 0x80033904, 0x80018E2C, 0x800264FC confirmed walls): **a MASKED-100% draft can still have the WRONG CONTROL FLOW — decode the want's back edges before believing "the only spelling that reaches size-exact"**

`promote_wip.py` refused `0x8013928C` even though `test_wip_drafts.py` reports
**EXACT, 128/128... i.e. 0 differing words in a size-exact 452 B object**. The
branch fields are masked, so this is invisible to the scorer. Worth stating as
a rule because the draft's own recipe log had already concluded "the `for(;;)`
shell is the ONLY spelling that reaches 452B" — true for word count, false for
control flow.

**Decode the want's CFG before believing a shape is unreachable.** For
`0x8013928C` the loop has exactly ONE back edge, and it targets **BODY**, not
the loop head: at 0x801392C4 retail branches on greater-or-equal under cr4 to the body at 0x801392DC, skipping the arm below; at 0x801392C8 it compares against negative six, branches to the epilogue on equal, copies r30 into r3, calls fn_8013E0EC, and branches to the epilogue; and the body runs to 0x80139430 where the only back edge branches greater-than under cr4 back to the body.

i.e. `if (res >= 0) { do { BODY } while (res > 0); } else { E }` where `E` is
entered at most once and always exits through the function epilogue. The draft's
`for (;;) { if (res < 0) { E } else { BODY; if (res > 0) continue; break; } }`
reproduces every word but puts the shell's back edge on the loop HEAD, so
`bge cr4` / `beq` / `b` land on the wrong targets — and because the word stream
is identical, the object branches into the middle of `BODY`.

**The wall, stated generally:** GCC 2.95 will not emit a **provably-dead arm**
(it propagates `res == 0` into `res >= 0` and deletes it), and the only thing
that stops flow-propagation is a **loop enclosing that arm** — but the want's
loop deliberately encloses *only* the other arm. "Keep a dead arm" needs a loop
around it; "only BODY spins" forbids one. Mutually exclusive from C. Measured:
correct if/else 436 B/1.8%, `do{}while(0)` 400 B/5.0%, `goto` labels 452 B but
folded, `for(;;)`+inner `do-while` (p1/p2) 424–452 B but folded. This is the
branch-side twin of §6x-89 ("want keeps dead insns").

**Park such a draft as UNPROMOTABLE, not as a near-miss**, and say in the header
that masked-EXACT is expected — otherwise the next round re-derives the same
word-exact body and re-runs the promotion.

### Confirmed-walls this round (do not re-grind; each has a measured cause)

* **`0x80044110` (91.3%, size-exact) — the 1240 B ceiling is forced by ngccc's
  `cmpwi`+`beq` FUSION, not by store order.** The want's opening block keeps a
  standalone `cmpwi r3,0` separated from its `beq` by two stores, and the obj
  store consumes `r3` directly (no reload). Only two C spellings exist and they
  are one word apart in OPPOSITE directions: testing through memory
  (`if (p1->obj != NULL)`) gives `cmpwi`+`beq` but costs an extra
  `lwz r3,8(r1)` → 1240 B / 91.3%; testing the register
  (`if (arg0->unk64 != NULL)`) drops the reload but cc1 folds the compare into
  the branch and emits `beq` alone → 1236 B, 299 diffs. **All 12 combinations of
  {store order obj/prev/next} × {mem, direct} were measured: every `_mem`
  variant is 1240 B/91.29% regardless of order, every `_direct` variant is
  1236 B.** Store order is a free parameter; stop permuting it. Same ngccc
  behaviour as the second residual in that function (`cmpwi r28,0` twice vs one
  `mtcrf`). C-side twin of `docs/parkings/72`.
* **`0x800A16B8` (98.7%, 1 word) — `mr r3,r28` vs `mr r3,r30`.** Both registers
  hold `&sp8`; the want copies r30→r28 in the preheader and spends r28 on the
  if-arm call, GCC propagates the callee-saved r30 forward across the
  intervening `bl` instead. Prior round measured ~15 shapes (alias pins,
  `"+r"` barriers, `register volatile`, ternary, moving the assignment, and
  swapping the definition order). Added this round: reversing which pinned
  register holds the original definition drops it to **74.0%** (the
  `mr r28,r30` copy is lost); a distinct `void *`-typed r28 alias does not
  compile cleanly; a same-block `A16B8 *t = sp28;` staging local is exactly
  unchanged. **GCC picks the CHEAPER home, and no spelling of `&sp8` is
  non-equivalent to `&sp8`** — pinning r3 cannot help, only making r28's value
  provably different could, and nothing in the source makes it so.
* **`0x80018E2C` (97.9%, 2 words) — `li r3,0; li r5,0; li r4,5; bl`.** A
  `docs/parkings/15` member, and `15`'s §"fn_8009A5B4" proves the permutation is
  **per-CALLEE**: a whole-`.text` census found 20 sites of `(3,5,4)` and *all
  20 are `fn_80096588` called with arg0 == arg2*. That entry was escaped only
  with a 3-instruction volatile-asm window after **all 134 `-f…` flags cc1
  advertises, all five ProDG versions, `-O0/-O1/-O3/-Os`, ~30 prototype
  param-type combos per position, 14 arg-value combos and every call spelling**
  failed. Reaching for it again is wasted effort; the two promoted siblings
  (`fn_80019800.c`, `fn_80019B90.c`) already carry the asm window.
* **`0x800264FC` (97.8%, 2 words) — `slwi r0,r0,0x11` + `rlwimi r9,r0,0x1f,1,0xf`
  vs `rlwinm r0,r0,0x10,1,0xf` + `rlwimi r9,r0,0,1,0xf`.** A packed-word
  mask-insert `(t & ~0x7FFF0000) | ((u32)(u16)v << 17) & 0x7FFF0000`: GCC's
  combine fires mask_insert correctly but ALWAYS folds the value's `<<17`
  into one `rlwinm` first, forcing rtw=0. 11 value spellings and 49 bitfield
  layouts (7×7) were measured; the one spelling that emits the exact
  `slwi` loses mask_insert and emits `rlwinm`+`or` instead. **The shift and the
  mask-insert are mutually exclusive through C in gcc-2.95.**

### 6gv-addendum — `0x8001CA68` decoded from scratch (m2c husk 100 B of a 248 B function -> hand reconstruction 140 B, 12.0% -> 17.1%)

Two transferable findings from rebuilding this draft out of the raw words:

1. **A draft that emits far less code than the want is a DECODE problem, not a
   scheduling problem.** `test_wip_drafts` reported DIFF with no percentage,
   which reads like "broken, skip" — but the object was 100 B against a 248 B
   want, i.e. *most of the function was absent*: no frame, no bool
   materialisation, no condition chain. Check `got NNNB` vs `want NNNB` before
   spending effort on scheduling levers. (The plain `tools/disasm.py` stalls on
   PS words; for integer functions a capstone dump over the raw `.text` bytes
   decodes the whole thing.)

2. **RECONSTRUCTING A SHORT-CIRCUIT CHAIN FROM ITS BRANCH MAP.** When the
   function's only body is a condition whose arms all target the epilogue,
   work it out by listing, for every branch, (a) which CR bit / register it
   tests and (b) which block it targets. The "skip to the epilogue" predicate
   is then the disjunction of all the paths that reach it, and the source
   condition is its De Morgan complement. Here that gave an exact 11-branch map
   and put the odd-looking `cr6`/`cr7` reuse (GCC's cr4 cache reloading the
   two earlier compares) in the right places without guessing. Use this before
   trying `||`/`&&`/goto permutations — the permutation space is large and the
   branch map pins the shape.

Also worth recording as a **negative** result: the three obvious pad/typing
levers (frame pad, byte-pointers into the overlapping slot, `| 0` to pin the
bool) all made it *worse* (29 -> 33 diffs) on this function. The frame
shortfall here is a **saved-register** shortfall, not a local-count one, so the
doc-§9a(4) pad lever does not apply — `char x[N]` only helps when the want and
got differ solely in `stwu`/`stfd`/`stw`/`lmw` offsets *and* everything else
already matches.

## 6gw — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80093084 parked at **304 B of 324, 69 diffs, 9.21%**; bf/0x80139EF4 parked at **1164 B of 1188, 273 diffs**): **an `sc` in the CALLEE never blocks a `bl` from C — and a `switch` that emits a near-empty object is a missing-case-label bug, not a compiler wall**

### 1. `bl <sc>` — check who the `sc` belongs to before declaring it inexpressible

`0x80093084` calls `0x80261d40`, which disassembles as `sc` ; `blr` (8 bytes, unsymbolized
CRT region). The earlier reading "raw system call, unreachable from C" was **wrong**: the
`sc` is in the **callee**. All the caller needs is a `bl`, and ngccc emits a direct one
for an unprototyped extern:

```c
void sc_stub();          /* 0x80261d40 */
sc_stub();               /* -> lis/ori/mtlr/blrl is WRONG; see below */
```

Actually the *cast* form is what breaks it:

```c
((void(*)(void))0x80261d40)();   /* lis + ori + mtlr + blrl  -- does NOT match */
void sc_stub(); sc_stub();      /* direct bl                 -- matches */
```

**Rule: a call through a literal address always becomes lis/ori/mtlr/blrl. To get a
direct `bl` to a known address, declare an unprototyped extern with that name.** The
same applies to every other "0x80xxxxxx is not a real function" call target in this
game — check the callee's first instruction before parking on it.

Caveat if it ever needs promoting: `0x80261d40` has **no symbol** in
`config/G2TE52/symbols.txt`, so a promoted caller needs a new split + symbol there.

### 2. Decode the flag polarity off the BRANCH, not the compare

`0x80093084`'s ARM A/B tests branch to skip on equal when the masked node field equals zero, branch to the call on not-equal under cr4 for the bit-one test, and branch to skip on not-equal under cr3 for the masked comparison, so the call is skipped when the masked value equals the mask.

The `bne cr3, skip` means the call happens when `(arg0 & M) != M` — i.e. the source
condition is `((arg0 & 1) != 0) || ((arg0 & M) != M)`. Reading the `cmpwi` alone
("test is `== M`") gives the **negation**, which is easy to miss because the compare
instruction looks symmetric. Check which way the branch goes.

Also: m2c spelled the bit-1 test `(arg0 & 1) < 0`, which is constant-false for an
already-masked value. Use `!= 0`.

### 3. The two-arm shape, and why cr3/cr4 are the tell

want keeps both loop-invariant booleans in **condition registers** — `andi.` + `cmpwi cr3`
and `andi.` + `mcrf cr4,cr0` — and recomputes the pair *inside* arm B rather than reusing
arm A's. Every C spelling that shares one flag between the two arms makes ngccc
materialize it in a GPR instead (`clrlwi` + `cmpwi cr4`), and promoting them to named
`s32` locals is worse still (`xori`/`subfic`/`adde`). Recomputing per arm helps the size
but not the allocation. Also note `mtcrf 0x18` in the epilogue: mask 0x18 restores exactly
**cr3+cr4**, which confirms which bits are live. Parking point: register pressure, not
semantics.

**The trap here, and the reason this draft is NOT size-exact:** flipping the polarity
back to `((arg0 & M) == M) || ((arg0 & 1) != 0)` gives a **size-exact 324 B / 74 diffs
/ 8.64%** — better on every metric — but that polarity is exactly what the want's
branches rule out (§2). All three correct-polarity spellings land 2-5 words short
(304 B / 316 B / 320 B). **Size-exactness coincided with being wrong**, so the correct
body is what is kept, 20 B short. Generalisation of §6gv: if the size-exact spelling
requires a decode you have *already proved wrong by branch direction*, the size match
is telling you about the wrong thing. Do not chase it.

### 4. Two more decode errors worth checking for, both found the same way

* **Array of pointers vs array of structs.** The walk is `lwz r3,0(r31)` then
  `lwz r0,0x48(r3)` — an array of **pointers**, 0x2004 bytes = 0x801 elements. Declaring
  it as `T arr[0x2004/sizeof(T)]` costs a couple of frames of register pressure.
* **`lha` + `add` means a BYTE offset, not an index.** `fn_80139EF4`'s virtual call is
  `lha r3,8(r9)` ; `add r3,r29,r3` -> `(char *)node + vtable->unk8`. Spelling `unk8` as
  an array index produces `mulli r3,r3,0x1c`, an instruction that **does not exist in the
  want**. Whenever an `add` follows a 16-bit load, it is a pointer offset.

### 5. `fn_80139EF4` — a "missing 1132 bytes" husk was a missing-case-label bug

The draft compiled to **56 B of 1188 B**. Not a compiler wall: the m2c `switch` had
**no case labels at all**, so all six arms were one straight-line block and the compiler
folded them. Written as a real two-case switch the same file reaches 1164 B.

Two things that are *measured*, not guessed, and are easy to get wrong:

* **Frame size is not adjustable directly.** want's frame is `-0x188` with saved GPRs at
  `0x168`; case 0xE's payload sits at `r1+0x18` and case 0xF's at `r1+0xC0`. That pins
  the payload struct at exactly `0xC0 - 0x18 = 0xA8` bytes **and** says the two cases own
  *separate* instances. One shared `Pld` gives `-0x90` and breaks both offsets. Deriving
  `sizeof` from the gap between the two stack slots is a reliable general technique.
* **`&obj` in a callee-saved register == it was a C++ `this`.** want does
  `addi r11,r1,8` / `mr r26,r11` / `mr r10,r26` once per case, then addresses the object
  through r10/r26 for the rest of the arm. Plain C addresses r1-relative. The repeated
  `sp8.unk8 = lbl_8029F3B0` on *every* exit path is an inlined destructor storing a
  constant into the object; the register-held address is how ngccc carries `this` across
  calls. Per §4b this project stays in C, so a want that keeps `&local` in a callee-saved
  reg is a parking condition, not something to fight with `volatile` or casts.

### 6. Workflow note

Both drafts were parked with `test_wip_drafts.py` returning **DIFF** (never FAIL), and
`src/wip` is inert, so `main.dol` stayed byte-identical (`ninja: no work to do`, `cmp`
clean) — confirmed after both edits. For a big from-scratch decode, a hand-rolled
one-line compile wrapper in `/tmp` (`ngccc` + wibo + the exact `cflags` from
`build.ninja`) is much faster to iterate against than `want_got.py --file`.

## 6gx — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x8012D190 parked at **1148 B size-exact, 260 diffs, 9.41%**): **a constant that appears as a call argument in m2c output is usually an `rlwimi` opcode, not an argument — and a switch on a byte needs the `u8` type or you get a spurious `extsb`**

### 1. The systematic m2c error: "third argument" that is really an opcode

`fn_8012D190`'s draft wrote `fn_8012CB2C(&sp8, ptr, 1)` in 13 places. There is no
third argument: retail materialises the constant into r9, inserts its bits into r0 with a rotate-and-insert-mask covering bits 16 through 22, stores the merged word to offset zero of the r28 object, and then branches to 0x8012CB2C with only two arguments.

`rlwimi rA,rS,SH,MB,ME` with `MB=9,ME=0xF` is an insert of bits 16..22, i.e.

```c
res->unk0 = (res->unk0 & ~0x7F0000) | (K << 16);
```

**Whenever an m2c draft passes a small integer constant to a call, check whether a
nearby `rlwimi`/`ori`+`rlwinm` pair in the want already accounts for it.** The draft
mis-attributes the opcode field update to the call that follows it. Check the *count*
of call sites vs `rlwimi` sites — equal counts are a strong tell.

### 2. `switch (arg0[0])` — the load happens BEFORE the cursor increment

The draft read `*(r31 - 1)` after `addi r31,r31,1`. Retail instead copies r3 into r31, loads the byte from offset zero of the original pointer, advances the cursor separately by one, and compares the byte against 0x1C,

so it is a plain `switch (arg0[0])` with an independently-advanced cursor, not an
offset read. Compounding this: the draft typed the parameter `char*`, so the switch
value got sign-extended and emitted an **`extsb` that does not exist in the want**.
Whenever a `switch` on a byte shows an extra `extsb` in got, change the parameter to
`u8` before touching anything else. Getting this right took the switch tree from
mismatched to **identical** (same `cmpwi`/`beq`/`bgt` shape, same order).

### 3. Shared switch tails need `goto`, not duplicated bodies

Cases 0x1B and 0x1C both read a length word and fall into the same tail
(`fn_801251B4(r31); res->unk8 = result; r31 += len`). Duplicating the tail gives the
wrong size; a single labelled tail reached by `goto` reproduces want's shared block.

### 4. A hand-rolled byte loop is not a `memcpy`

Case 0x23 copies with an explicit `lbz`/`stb` + two-counter loop. GCC will not
generate that shape from `memcpy` — it will emit a call. Keep it as a loop.

### 5. Why it is parked even at size-exact

want: frame `-0x80`, `stfd f29/f30/f31`, saved GPRs from `0x50`, LR at `0x84`.
got: frame `-0x70`, saves only `f31`.

Getting all three floats saved requires those values to be genuinely **live across**
`fn_80128F44`/`fn_80124FDC`. Measured dead ends:
- feeding them from three separate `f32` stack slots -> no FPR lift at all;
- feeding them from ONE shared temp -> collapses to a single `f31` save;
- assigning to named `f29/f30/f31` locals between the calls -> still one save.

The four-instruction `stfd/stmw` interleave also differs (want saves FPRs first, then
`stmw`; got does `stfd f31` then `stmw`). This is the FPR-frame wall from §4c, not a
decode gap — size is exact, so case set and structure are right.

## 6gy — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x8012A260 parked, 348 B -> **716 B of 740, 160 diffs**, frame exact; scanner found **8 drafts** with the same missing-`case` bug — see §6gz, the first count of 40 was comment false-positives): **when a `switch` folds, check EVERY callee arity too — m2c gets the case structure AND the argument lists wrong at the same time**

### 1. Scanner for the missing-`case` bug — run this before picking targets

```python
# any draft containing `switch` but ZERO `case` labels folds all arms into one
# block, so the object comes out a fraction of the want.
re.search(r'\bcase\b', src) is None and 'switch' in src
```

**8 drafts in `src/wip` currently match** (this list first read 40 — see the
correction in §6gz: the scan must strip `//` comments, or a park note that merely
*mentions* `switch` counts as a hit):

| want | draft | fp/vec in want |
|---|---|---|
| 3060 B | `fn_8022527C` | — |
| 2648 B | `fn_800948E0` | — |
| 1820 B | `fn_80124478` | 22 fp |
| 1732 B | `fn_8007A334` | **integer-only** |
| 1536 B | `fn_8024CCC8` | 2 vec |
| 644 B | `fn_8019DF10` | **integer-only** |
| 560 B | `fn_80114F40` | 3 fp |
| 216 B | `fn_8025AD64` | **integer-only** |

`fn_8007A334` (1732 B, 433 integer instructions, zero fp/vec) is the best-scoped
remaining target.

### 2. Fixing the switch exposes a SECOND layer of m2c arity errors

`fn_8012A260` was not just mis-folded — once the arms were separated, four more
decode errors became visible, all of the "wrong number of arguments" kind:

| draft | want | correct |
|---|---|---|
| `fn_8012CB7C(arg0, arg1, dst, elem)` | `mr r3,r31` only | **2 args** `(dst, elem)` |
| `fn_80129C08(...)` | `li r7,0` visible | 5 args incl. trailing literal 0 |
| cases 3/4: `*(s32 *)dst = v` | `stb` | **byte** stores — it is a string buffer |
| count arg | `clrlwi r4,r26,0x10` | count **masked to 16 bits** before the call |

**Rule: after de-folding a switch, re-decode every call site in the new arms
before measuring.** m2c's arity errors concentrate in code it could not see
structurally, and they were hidden behind the folding.

### 3. `s32` store where want has `stb` = wrong element type, not a wrong offset

The draft's `*(s32 *)var_r31 = ...` vs want's `stb r0,0(r31)` is a **type**
error: the buffer is `u8*`, and the surrounding code walks it with `lbz`/
`addi 1`. Check the neighbouring load/store width before assuming the offsets
are right.

### 4. Case ORDER in source is not free — it drives the compare tree

want tests `cmpwi kind,4` / `cmpwi kind,3` first and reaches 5/6 through the
`>4` arm. Plain **ascending** source order gave a tree starting at
`cmpwi kind,5`. Adding an explicit `case 0:` did not change the shape either.
Same case set, different tree — so the original order is neither ascending nor
descending and has not been recovered. Recorded rather than guessed at; do NOT
brute-force permutations here (it is a tree-shape problem, not a size problem).

### 5. Also confirmed

* `switch` on `*(u8 *)(arg0 + 2)` with the count read separately at +4; the
  draft's `*(s32 *)((char *)arg0 + 2)` was a byte load spelled as a word.
* A shared body reached by `goto` from several labels (cases 1/2 -> 0xD) and
  fallthrough pairs (`case 3: case 4:`) both reproduce want's block sharing.

## 6gz — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80026670 parked, **13.45% -> 4.42%**, 452 B of 476): **if a value is stored to `r1+N` and reloaded between steps, it is a STACK SLOT, not a register — and check the scanner's greps against comments**

### 1. The fold-bug scanner must strip comments first

The scan in §6gy greps for `switch`. `fn_80026670` matched — but only because its old
park comment contained the sentence "Straight-line integer body with no switch".

**Measured impact: the un-stripped scan reported 40 drafts; the correct count is 8.**
A 5x overstatement, entirely from park notes discussing switches. The 8 real ones
are listed in §6gy (corrected).

A safe version:
```python
src = re.sub(r'//.*', '', open(f).read())          # then test for switch/case
```
Do this for **any** grep-based wip census — park comments are dense with the very
keywords being searched for, so the false-positive rate will be high every time.

### 2. `stw rX, 8(r1)` ... `lwz rY, 8(r1)` = a variable forced into memory

`fn_80026670` is a cursor/bump-allocator setup. The cursor is written to `r1+8` after
**every** step and re-read before the next. Writing it as an ordinary C local
(`void *cur`) gives a completely different register-pressure profile — the old draft's
instruction count was wrong for this reason alone, not because of scheduling.

**Tell: an `stw`/`lwz` pair on the same `r1+N` displacement, repeated more than once,
is a spilled-to-stack local.** Same family as §6gw's "derive sizeof from the gap
between two stack slots" — look at every `r1`-relative access before assuming a
variable is in a register.

### 3. Three decode corrections, all confirmed against the want

| draft | want | correct |
|---|---|---|
| `fn_8002C638(cur)` | `addi r3,r1,8` | takes the cursor **by pointer** |
| `Mem_Alloc_3(count)` | `slwi r3,r3,2` ; `bl 0x800105cc` | `fn_800105CC(count * 4)` — byte size |
| `arg0->unk1C` as `u16` | `stw r0,0x1c` | `unk1C` is a **word**; only 34/36/38 are halfwords |

### 4. Verify struct offsets from the STORES, not by arithmetic

Getting `arg0`'s layout right took four iterations of guessing. The reliable method is
to decode every store displacement out of the want and read the offsets off directly:

```python
# sth r0, 52(reg) / sth r0, 54(reg) / sth r0, 56(reg)  ->  0x34, 0x36, 0x38
op = (w >> 26) & 0x3F
if op == 0x2C:   # sth
    d = w & 0xFFFF; d -= 0x10000 if d >= 0x8000 else 0
    print(d)
```
An earlier guess put the u16 fields at 0x40 when they were at 0x34 — a two-byte pad
compounding. **Never infer a struct layout from field names; extract it from the
displacement of every store.** Final verified layout is in the draft header.

### 5. Why it is parked at 4.42%

Frame and prologue are exact; semantics are now correct. Residual is scheduling plus
register choice: want uses `stwx r3, r29, r9` (index register, array base reloaded
from memory each iteration) where got uses `stw r3, 0(r31)` with a bumped pointer, and
want re-reads `arg1->unkC` inside the loop where got hoists it. Score is well under
the 12% gate so promotion is not in play.

## 6ha — 2026-10-04 (bf/0x80114F40 parked, **464B/37.93% -> 544B/11.76%** of 560; bf/0x8025AD64 and bf/0x8019DF10 assessed and set aside): **triage the fold-bug list by opcode BEFORE rebuilding — two of the eight are hard-walls in disguise**

### 1. Triage result for the 8 real fold-bug drafts

Rebuilt this round: `fn_80114F40` (560 B). Assessed and deliberately skipped:

| draft | why skipped |
|---|---|
| `fn_8025AD64` (216 B) | ends `lwz r31,0xf8(r31)` + **`rfi`** — an interrupt-handler epilogue restoring all 32 GPRs. `rfi` is not expressible from C. Structural wall. |
| `fn_8019DF10` (644 B) | opens `li r0,0x20` ; `mtctr r0` ; `bdnz` — a counted loop via **mtctr/bdnz**, which §4b explicitly bans in favour of mtblr/blrl. |
| `fn_8007A334` (1732 B) | already at 1392 B / 1.15% word diff but diverges from the **first instruction** (frame -0x100 vs -0xb0) — a bitfield packer with nested loops, not a localised gap. Multi-session. |
| `fn_8022527C` (3060 B), `fn_800948E0` (2648 B), `fn_80124478` (1820 B, 22 fp), `fn_8024CCC8` (1536 B, 2 vec) | large / float-bearing; not attempted this round. |

**Do the opcode triage first.** `rfi`, `mtctr`, and FPR frames each predict a wall
before you spend an hour decoding.

### 2. Magic constants: read the words, never the disassembly text

`lis r4,-0x709f` + `ori r4,r4,0xd602` is `0x8F61D602`. `-0x709f` is *not* the high
half of the constant as printed — it is the sign-extended field. My first guess at
these three constants was wrong on all of them. Reliable method:

```python
tools/venv/bin/python <scratch> 0x80114F5C 1 # -> 3c808f61
tools/venv/bin/python <scratch> 0x80114F68 1 # -> 6084d602
# (lis_N << 16) | ori_N  ->  0x8F61D602
```

### 3. `rlwinm rA,rS,0,9,0x1F` is `(x >> 9) & 0x7F`, not `x & 0x7E00`

Writing the test as `(v & 0x7E00) == 0x2000` folds to a completely different
instruction and loses the shift. When the want uses `rlwinm` with a **non-zero
shift and a rotate of 0**, it is an extract: `(x >> MB) & ((1 << (ME-MB+1)) - 1)`.
**Any `rlwinm` with SH=0 is a mask/extract, not a rotate** — read it that way from
the start.

### 4. An 8-byte stack pair is a `double`, not a 4-byte union

Case 2 stores `0x43300000` at `r1+0x18` and a sign-flipped word at `r1+0x1c`, then
does `lfd f1,0x18(r1)` / `fsub` / `frsp`. Declaring the local as a 4-byte union gave
frame `-0x28`; want is `-0x30`. **Two adjacent word stores followed by an `lfd` from
the lower one = an 8-byte double local.** Same tell as §6gz's cursor-in-a-slot, one
size up.

### 5. `stwx rS, rA, rB` = indexed store, so the source indexes an array

The shared tail is `stwx r9, r3, r0` with `r0 = sp10 << 2` — a table indexed by a
shifted slot number, not a bumped pointer. Spelled as a pointer bump you lose the
shift and the reload.

### 6. Prologue register choice can cascade

want does `mr r28,r4` / `mr r29,r3`; got produced the opposite pairing, which then
propagates into every field access through the wrong base register. When a
reconstruction is close but the whole body differs, check the FIRST three
instructions before hunting the tail — the arg-to-register assignment is upstream of
everything.

## 6hb — 2026-10-05 (2026-10-05 promote batch: 15 of 23 sweep-EXACT promoted, 9724/11497): **a masked-EXACT sweep can still fail to LINK, and the failure is a STALE SYMBOL NAME from `rename_thpg.py`, not a codegen problem**

A full `bash tools/sweep3.sh` over 1750 drafts returned 23 EXACT. Promoting them
needed two extra gates beyond the ones already in `promote_wip.py`:

**1. 7 of 23 had a documented PARK block in the draft header — read it before
promoting.** A sweep EXACT says nothing about *promotability*; the parking notes
are the real signal. Grep the candidate file first:

```sh
grep -qiE 'PARKED|DO NOT PROMOTE|not promotable|REFUSE' src/wip/fn_<ADDR>.c
```

Blank ⇒ real candidate. Hit ⇒ leave it, it is already diagnosed. This round the
7 were: `0x80003464` (below TEXT_START, `.init`), `0x8013928C` (2 wrong REL14
targets hidden by the mask), `0x801D2C58` (mwld branch-relaxation coin),
`0x801B5A54` (SN asm `bdnz $` → undefined symbol `$`), `0x8025AE3C` (dtk
pseudo-function, no caller/split), `0x8025B340` (sole caller is the hand-written
context blob; dead-strips on link), and `0x801B6310`, which the tool itself
REFUSEd —

```
REFUSE 0x801B6310: 1 internal branch target(s) differ from retail ...
0x801b6540 want ('beq', ...) got ('beq', ...)
```

so it is a 16th of the same family, just not yet annotated in its header. **A
`SystemExit` from `promote_wip.py` aborts the WHOLE batch before registration**,
so one bad address costs you the other 15 — expect to re-run without it.

**2. The real blocker: `undefined: 'fn_801251B4'` at LINK time, on a draft that is
100% byte-exact.** `0x8012A544` called `fn_801251B4`, but `rename_thpg.py`
(§5 table, `docs/plans/2026-09-21-thpg-symbol-naming.md` §6) had already renamed
that function `CreateString` in `symbols.txt`:

```
CreateString = .text:0x801251B4; // type:function size:0x7C scope:global
```

The promoted callee `src/fn_801251B4.c` *defines* `CreateString`, so the draft's
`extern s32 fn_801251B4(u8 *)` had no definition to bind to. **The file name
(`fn_801251B4.c`) is the address; the C symbol is the new name** — filename
renames are deliberately NOT done by `rename_thpg.py`, so grep the *body* of the
callee, not the filename.

Fix = rename the extern AND both call sites, casting at the boundary
(`s32 CreateString(char *);` … `CreateString((char *)p)`), which leaves codegen
byte-identical (re-sweep: still `EXACT m2c 0x8012A544 (940B)`).

```sh
# which drafts reference a renamed symbol by its stale fn_ name?
grep -rln 'fn_801251B4' src/wip/*.c     # -> fn_8012A544.c, fn_8012D190.c
# then, per callee, confirm the real name:
grep -n 'CreateString' config/G2TE52/symbols.txt
grep -n 'CreateString' src/fn_801251B4.c
```

**Sweep-EXACT ⇒ link-clean is a separate step.** `test_wip_drafts.py` compiles a
draft STANDALONE, so an undefined external is invisible to it. Only
`promote_wip.py`'s mwld link surfaces it — and its revert path is correct
(registrations restored, `DOL identity preserved`, drafts kept), so a failed
batch is safe to re-run minus the offender.

**3. After a revert, DELETE the leftover `src/fn_*.c`.** The revert restores
`splits.txt`/`configure.py` but the promoted files are untracked and stay on
disk, so `test_wip_drafts.py` then reports `{'promoted': 1}` instead of a score
and hides real verdicts. They are safe to delete when `git status` shows them as
`??` (untracked) and the `src/wip/` draft still exists.

**4. Report-reading gotcha:** `report.json` stores function addresses in
`functions[].metadata.virtual_address` as a **decimal string**; the sibling
`functions[].address` is a meaningless `"0"`. Reading the wrong key reports
every lookup as NOT FOUND. Progress went 9709 -> 9724 (exactly +15), and all 15
show `fuzzy_match_percent 100.0` at the right object sizes.

## 6dn — 2026-10-05: a 1-word `cmplw rA` / `cmplw rB` loop-HEAD residual is a GUARDED do-while, not a register coin (fn_80167E04, 98.9% → byte-identical)

**The rule.** When the ONLY residual is the register of the loop's ENTRY test
(`want cmplw r30,r0` / `got cmplw r29,r0`) and the BACK EDGE already matches,
do **not** chase it as a rotated-guard register-allocation coin and do not pin
registers. Read the entry test's operands: if the variable it compares is a
DIFFERENT variable from the loop's induction variable — typically one that is
provably 0 at the loop head (`best`, `found`, `ret`) — then want has a
**guarded do-while**: `if (guard) do { ... } while (iv < n);`. The guard and the
back-edge then legitimately test two different pseudos, and the guard compiles
to the *unrotated* variable's register.

**The matching shape** (fn_80167E04 `ScriptGetMostRecentSave`, was parked at
94/95 across two rounds of pin/barrier/flag sweeps):

```c
i = 0;
__asm__ volatile("" ::: "memory");          /* ZERO-CODE, load-bearing */
if ((u32)best < *((u32 *)&((CStruct *)sp8)->unk0x4)) {
do {
    ...                                       /* i += 1 at the bottom */
} while ((u32)i < *((u32 *)&((CStruct *)sp8)->unk0x4));
}
```

Both halves are load-bearing, and they fix DIFFERENT words:

| body | score | residual |
|---|---|---|
| plain `for (i=0; (u32)i < n; i++)` | 94/95 | entry test on the wrong REGISTER (`cmplw r29`) |
| guarded do-while, no fence | 93/95 | entry test now **correct** (`cmplw r30`); `[lwz r9,8(r1)]` and `[li r29,0]` swapped |
| fence on the old `for` | 94/95 | unchanged |
| fence + guarded do-while | **95/95 EXACT** | — |

So after the guarded-do-while rewrite the coin MOVES to the head of the block:
ngccc hoists the `volatile` sp8 reload above `li r29,0`, and a zero-code
`__asm__ volatile("" ::: "memory")` between `i = 0;` and the guard sinks it back.
This is the same lever as §6ec-2 ("0-code memory fences inert") — it is NOT inert
here because the thing being reordered is a *volatile reload*, which the memory
clobber does constrain.

**Cast matters:** the guard must be **unsigned** (`(u32)best < (u32)n`).
The signed spelling also produces `cmplw r30` but emits `cmpw` on the back edge
too → 91/95.

**How to recognise it in 5 seconds:** disassemble the loop head. If the entry
test's "other" variable has a `li <reg>,0` *before the first call of the loop's
enclosing block* (so it is provably 0 there) and is re-assigned inside the loop,
it is a guard, not an induction variable. `best`/`ret`/`found`/`result` are the
usual names in this codebase.

**Corollary for the doc-15 family:** several parked drafts describe a
`mr`/`li`/`fmr` pair as "arg-setup order decided by the allocator, not
expressible in C". Before accepting that, check whether the swapped pair is
*actually* two different source statements — here (fn_801A71DC, fn_801575E0)
sliding the copy past the call's arg-setup moved it between only three slots and
the fourth (`[li][copy][bl]`) had no source position, whereas
fn_80167E04's identical-looking swap was a whole missing `if`.

## 6hc — 2026-10-05 (fn_80092F30 rebuilt 25.9% -> **65/85 words true / 66/85 masked**, fn_80192D24 parked; `tools/reloc_diff.py` now resolves internal branch targets): **ngccc emits a REL14/REL24 relocation for EVERY internal branch, and the field it leaves in the .o is the ADDEND (the target's .text offset) where a byte displacement belongs — so the target a raw disasm prints is wrong by exactly the branch's own offset**

Do not read a branch target off the object (or off any tool that just `disasm`s
the `.text` section). For `R_PPC_REL14/REL24` to a symbol in `.text` the EABI
result is `target = S + A` with `S` the section base and `A` the reloc addend,
so the real displacement is `A - P` (`P` = the branch's own section offset).
Worked example (`fn_80092F30`): want `0x2c: beq 0x80092F6C`, object word decodes
as `beq 0x80092F98` (placeholder `0x3c` = `A`, *not* the displacement); the raw
disasm sends you hunting a control-flow difference that does not exist.
`tools/reloc_diff.py` now applies this fixup (`fixup_branch`, 2026-10-05) and
prints want and got targets in the same space. The consequence for scoring is
that this function reads **77.6% masked / 76.5% true** — the masked sweep blanks
every branch word, so a masked % is an upper bound whenever the function has
branches, and `want_vs_got.py`/`wdiff.py`/`my_diff.py`/`diff_near.py` all mask.

Two more things from the same function:
* **A u16 ternary's spelling is load-bearing** (6-line micro-test, ngccc `-O2`):
  `k1 <= k2 ? -1 : 1` -> `cmplw; li r3,1; bgtlr; li r3,-1; blr`, whereas
  `k1 > k2 ? 1 : -1` -> `cmplw; li r3,-1; blelr; li r3,1; blr`. want used the
  second; flipping the spelling fixed 5 words *and* explained why want has a
  dedicated `li r3,-1; blr` in the else branch — `blelr` needs its `-1`
  materialised immediately before it, so it can never be shared with that
  branch's `return -1`. (For `s32` operands the two spellings swap.)
* **Give each arm of a duplicated comparison its own temps.** `fn_80092F30`
  duplicates the `d = 0x5E - 0x60` compare in both arms of the outer if. With
  shared `d1/d2` the second arm cost 9 points *and* re-coloured the whole FIRST
  arm (the `lhz 0x60` scratch swap + `slwi` order); with `d3/d4` in the second
  arm the entire first 0xF0 bytes went byte-identical. The residual 20 words are
  a pure block-order mirror (want falls into the `return -1` exit and
  branch-false over it, got jumps to a shared exit at the end); 25+ variants
  (`k2==0||y>0` / `y<=0&&k2!=0` / two ifs / `goto`-labelled exit / nested else /
  `k1==k2`-body / `-fno-schedule-insns{,2}` / `-fno-branch-probabilities`)
  all plateau there. `-fno-reorder-blocks` is an INVALID flag on ngccc.

## 6hd — 2026-10-05 (fn_8004DF00 rebuilt 4.9% -> **100% promoted**; fn_800AB528 4.5% -> 40% then parked): **an address-taken initialised aggregate is what makes ngccc emit MULTIPLE zero registers — and pinning ONLY the one pseudo the allocator gets wrong is a 1-pin fix**

Two independent findings from `fn_8004DF00` (436 B, `CBaseMenu_SetProperties`,
`src/fn_8004DF00.c`), both verified against the DOL (100% true, promoted).

**1. `= {0, 0}` on an address-taken object gives you the extra `li`, plain
assignments never do.**  want's prologue has *two* zero registers:
`li r9,0` / `li r10,0` with separate `stw`s into the two out-slots passed to
`CScreenElement_resolve_just`.  Measured on ngccc `-O2` (6-line micro-tests):

| source | emitted |
|---|---|
| `f32 x[2] = {0, 0}; g(&x[0], &x[1]);` | `li r9,0; li r10,0; stw r9,…; stw r10,…` ✅ |
| `f32 x[2] = {0.0f, 0.0f};` | same ✅ |
| `struct { f32 x, y; } s = {0, 0};` | same ✅ |
| `f32 x = 0.0f; y = 0.0f;` (or `= 0`) | one `lis`+`lfs` from the float pool, `stfs` ×2 ❌ |
| `s32 x, y; x = 0; y = 0;` | ONE `li` + two `stw` ❌ |
| `u32 x[2]; x[0] = 0; x[1] = 0;` | ONE `li` ❌ |

The distinguishing feature is the **brace initialiser**: it makes GCC expand the
elements as separate stores instead of CSE-ing one SImode zero.  A missing `li`
shifts every subsequent word, so a body can look semantically perfect and still
score ~1% — `fn_8004DF00` went 0.9% (s32 pair) → 45.9% → 74.3% (after moving the
`sp10 = 0;`/`sp14 = 0;` assignments down to just above their calls) with nothing
but that one-line change.  Note the pair *must* be address-taken: the same
`f32 just[2] = {0, 0};` whose elements are only read collapses back to one
pseudo (measured on `fn_800AB528`).

**2. When the body is byte-identical except for which call-saved register each
long-lived pseudo gets, pin the pseudo the allocator gets wrong — pinning all of
them is worse.**  `fn_8004DF00` has three call-crossing pseudos (`arg0`, `arg1`,
`&just`); want is `(arg0,arg1,&just) = (r31,r30,r29)`, the natural build gives the
rotation `(&just,arg0,arg1) = (r31,r30,r29)`.

| variant | score |
|---|---|
| no pins, params used directly | 74.3% |
| `self`=r31 + `script`=r30 locals | 81.7% (ngccc deletes the copies, pin lost) |
| `self`=r31 + `script`=r30 + `p`=r29 | 89.9% — and leaves the parameter dead except for two flag stores, which makes ngccc emit a bogus `stw r0,0x1b8(r1)` (base = r1!) |
| **`register f32 *p __asm__("r29"); p = just;` only** | **100.0%** |

So: pin the *minimum*, i.e. the one value whose live range the allocator is
misjudging, and leave the parameters alone (their natural `mr r31,r3` /
`mr r30,r4` prologue copies are exactly what want has).  Extra pins perturb the
prologue schedule (the `lis r5,<propid>` slot fill moves) and can make a dead
parameter miscompile.

**3. Free bonus:** the two reads of such an out-pair can legitimately use
different addressing modes — want has `lfs f0,4(r29)` (through the pointer kept
for the call) and `lfs f13,8(r1)` (direct slot).  Write one read as
`*(f32 *)((char *)p + 4)` and the other as `just[0]`; writing both through `p`
is object-identical but hides it.  Also: `tools/fix_fp_pool.py` routes the
s32->f32 conversion pool constant (`0x80292AC8`) automatically during link.

## 6he — 2026-10-05 (fn_8004D530 rebuilt 5.1% -> **100% promoted** (117/117 words, 468B, DOL `cmp`+`ok`+sha1 clean, 9734 -> 9735): **a callee-saved permutation is cracked by pinning the minimum set, and an address web that want keeps in a VOLATILE scratch plus a callee-saved home is reproduced by binding a short-lived helper pointer FIRST and the pinned home FROM it after the stores**)

fn_8004D530 (`ScriptGetScreenElementProps`) is the first *pure* regalloc coin
flip of the project to fall.  It was 5.1% with 116/117 instructions and ZERO
non-register diffs, exactly as the old park note said — the note's conclusion
("realistic route is a hard-register pin on p8") was right, but a pin ALONE is
not enough: three separate levers had to be right at the same time.  Order them
like this.

**Diagnostic first: mnemonic-sequence alignment ratio.**  Do not rank a wall by
its masked %.  Align the WANT and GOT mnemonic streams with
`difflib.SequenceMatcher` (ignores insertion/deletion shifts, which the raw
word-compare cannot).  fn_8004D530 scored 5.1% true but **seq 0.966** — i.e.
the statement structure is already right and every remaining diff is a register
or an ordering artefact.  A high-seq/low-% draft is the only kind worth
grinding; seq < 0.8 means the body still says the wrong thing.

**1. Pin the minimum set — measured, on this function, in this order:**

| pins | result |
|---|---|
| none | 5.1% (116 insns) |
| `p8` -> r26 only | 5.1% (all other regs grew +1 to compensate) |
| `p8` -> r26 + `arg1` -> r29 | **regs now match want exactly**; only the scratch copy and the flag reg remained |
| all of p8/arg0/&sp18/... | worse (dead-parameter perturb) |
| `zero` -> r31 (`register s32` pinned) | 71.2%, 118 insns (pin emits an extra move) |

So the work is: identify want's callee-saved assignment from the want disasm
(p8=26, arg0=27, &sp18=28, arg1=29, manager=30, zero=31 here), find which of
them land elsewhere in got, and pin *only* those (2 here).  Pin the *values*
with real uses; a pinned variable that the optimizer considers dead emits a
bogus store (`stw r0,0x1b8(r1)` in §6hd).

**2. The scratch/home split (the missing `mr r26, r9`).**  want computes the
address into a VOLATILE register (`addi r9, r1, 8`), uses that for the two
pre-call zero stores, and copies it into the callee-saved home (`mr r26, r9`)
which all the call-site uses read.  got with `p8 = &sp8;` computes straight into
r26 and never copies.  The one source shape that reproduces it is a *second,
short-lived* helper pointer, bound BEFORE the pinned home and used only for the
stores, with the home bound FROM it AFTER them:

```c
    Ref_t *t8;                       /* unpinned  -> gets the volatile r9 */
    t8 = &sp8;
    t8->f4 = 0;
    t8->f8 = 0;
    p8 = t8;                         /* -> mr r26, r9  (117 insns) */
```

Binding order is the whole lever, all four measured: `p8 = &sp8; t8 = &sp8;`
gives the copy backwards (`mr r9, r26`, 116 insns); `t8 = &sp8; p8 = t8;`
*copy before the stores* folds the copy away; `p8 = &sp8;` twice also folds.
This single change took the pinned body from 6.8% to 98.3%, and the unpinned
body from 5.1% to 84.6% (99/117, size-exact) — the split is a *structural*
lever, not a scheduling one.  Generalisation: whenever want shows
`<volatile def>` + `mr <saved>, <volatile>` for an address whose uses straddle
a call, the original source had two bindings of that address, the second one a
copy of the first.

**3. One pseudo for a constant that is later overwritten by a call result.**
want uses ONE register (r31) for `li r31, 0` (the three initial zero stores) and
for the `or. r31, r3, r3` copy of `ContainsFlag`'s result at the end.  A literal
`0` gives the result its own register (r29 here, 115/117).  Use a real variable:

```c
    s32 zero;
    zero = 0;                 /* the three initial stores use `zero` */
    ...
    zero = ContainsFlag(arg0, QB_DONT_ASSERT);   /* -> or. r31, r3, r3 */
```

GCC keeps one callee-saved pseudo and reuses its register for the result.
Do NOT pin it (`register s32 zero __asm__("r31")`) — that emits a separate move
and recolours the rest (118 insns, 71.2%).

**4. The last 2 words: a literal zero somewhere in the middle.**  After step 3
the body was 115/117 with a 464 B object (one `li` short).  want re-materialises
a fresh zero in the `return 1` path (`li r0, 0; stw r0, 8(r1)`) instead of
reusing r31 — because the zero pseudo is dead there.  So *one* of the NULL
stores must stay a literal (`sp8.f0 = NULL;`) while every other zero store goes
through the variable.  Rule of thumb: a constant-folding artefact that want does
NOT CSE marks the last use of the constant's live range; find that statement in
the want disasm and write it as a literal.

**Promotion checklist reminder:** `tools/promote_wip.py <addr>` re-verifies,
reconfigures, relinks and `cmp`s, but it must be run as a BACKGROUND process —
a SYNC/nohup invocation is killed when the tool call is cleaned up, leaving
splits/configure updated, `src/fn_*.c` written, main.dol deleted and no
verification.  Recover by hand: build `build/G2TE52/main.dol`, `cmp` + sha1 +

## 6hf — 2026-10-06 (fn_802533B0 rebuilt **9.2% -> 97.8% NEAR**, size-exact 740B, 4 diffs; WIP no-park sweep): **m2c's `saved_reg_r13` + 1-arg-call double defect, and the single reg-pin that closes an all-rename diff**

Twelve `src/wip` drafts carry m2c's SDA artifact `static s32 saved_reg_r13;` +
`*(s32 *)((char *)saved_reg_r13 - 0xNNNN)`. That form does NOT compile to
`lwz rX,-0xNNNN(r13)` — it compiles to `lwz rX,-0xNNNN(r11)` plus an extra
`lis/addi` pair for the static's own address, i.e. +3 words and a wrong base
register per site. The working form is the §6aw-173 inline asm:

```c
#define HEAP() ({ s32 h__; __asm__ __volatile__("lwz %0, -0x7f40(13)" : "=r"(h__)); h__; })
```

`__volatile__` is load-bearing on a LOOP-CONTAINING body: the non-volatile form
gets hoisted out of the loop, steals an extra callee-saved register (`stmw r23`
instead of `stmw r24`) and shifts the entire frame + tail. `-msdata=eabi -G4` +
`extern s32 lbl_803CA340;` (the §43 route) reproduces want's *load order* but
costs one diff per site in the standalone sweep, because `gen_leaves` masks only
REL14/REL24/ADDR16_HA/LO — not SDA21. Use the asm; keep the flag route in mind
only if you are willing to verify at link level (`sda_verify.py`).

Per-function result (fn_802533B0, 740B teardown):
| lever | score |
|---|---|
| baseline (m2c body) | 9.2% |
| + 2-arg call recovery (`if (m) free(heap, m);` — the compared member is already live in r4 at every site; the draft's 1-arg calls were the main defect) | 20.1% |
| + `__volatile__` (frame/regalloc fixed) | 55.1% |
| − stale `// FLAG: -fno-expensive-optimizations` (**now harmful**; was load-bearing for the OLD body) | 83.2% |
| + `register Unk_DB0E2BAB *r29 asm("r29");` on ONE local | **97.8%** |

Two general rules worth keeping:

1. **All-diff-lines-are-register-renames ⇒ try ONE reg pin before anything
   else.** At 83.2% every remaining diff was `r29` vs `r28` on the same
   pointer/counter pair. Three structural probes (late declaration of the
   counter, splitting it into two counters, a pointer-typed byte counter) all
   scored identically or worse; the single `register T x asm("rN")` pin on the
   *pointer* flipped 83.2 -> 97.8. The project's promoted tree already has 26
   files using reg pins, so this is sanctioned, not a hack.
2. **Re-measure every `// FLAG:` line after ANY body change.** The
   `-fno-expensive-optimizations` line here was worth +5.6 on the broken body
   and −5.6 on the fixed one; leaving it in would have parked the function at
   55% with a note blaming GCC. Same for `_dummy`/pins/barriers.

Residual on fn_802533B0 (4 diffs = 2 word swaps): at the two
`*(s32*)r29->unk0x8/unk0xC` free sites want hoists the arg2 ADDRESS load
(`lwz r9,8(r29)`) above the arg1 load, we emit the volatile asm first. Probed and
rejected: `: : "memory"` clobber (9.8%), hoisting the member pointer into a local
`s32 *p8 = ...` (14.6%, grabs r31), non-volatile (25.4%). Doc-15 class.

A same-shape audit of the other eleven `saved_reg_r13` drafts found **no** bulk
win: replacing the artifact raises 0x80253DBC 19.1 -> 23.7 but lowers the rest

whose real defects are elsewhere. The artifact is a symptom, not the disease —
do the 2-arg/arity audit first.

Related negative results this round, so nobody re-runs them: (a) a
