## 6hg — 2026-10-06 (24 WIRED units flipped to 100.000%, 9736 -> **9760/11497** (84.892%), 51 asm sites replaced by real C, DOL `cmp`+sha1+`ok` clean): **a WIRED unit scored <100% is ALWAYS a scoring artifact, never a code defect — the DOL is hash-verified, so every unit with a `source_path` is byte-exact; and hand-written address/sda asm wedges are invisible to objdiff because they emit no relocations**

THE INVARIANT. `main.dol` is hash-verified byte-identical, and every
`Matching` unit's `.o` is linked into it. Therefore for EVERY unit that has
`metadata.source_path` in `build/G2TE52/report.json`, the object is byte-exact
by construction. So a wired unit sitting at 99.9% is never "nearly matched" —
the residual is objdiff geometry. Corollary: to find real work, filter on
`not source_path`. (This session started on the wrong foot by treating those
81 units as near-misses.)

WHY THE DOCK EXISTS. `objdiff-cli diff` compares our `.o` (base) against a
dtk-GENERATED target `.o` (`build/G2TE52/obj/<u>.o`), and dtk RECOVERS
relocations from the linked DOL: a word equal to `sym@ha`/`@l`/`@sda21`
becomes a reloc against that symbol. Any source that hardcodes the address
with inline asm produces the same BYTES but NO reloc, so objdiff cannot prove
the operand and docks it (`DIFF_ARG_MISMATCH`, or `DIFF_REPLACE` when the
whole operand text differs). Two wedge forms were in the tree, 24 units / 51
sites:

  A) SDA:  `__asm__ volatile("lfs %0,-0x7938(13)" : "=f"(x));`
     (displacement relative to `SDA_BASE = 0x803D2280`)
  B) non-SDA: `__asm__ volatile("lis %0,%1@ha" : "=r"(p) : "s"(lbl));`
     followed by `*(s32 *)((char *)p + 0x1NNN)`

FIX FOR (A) — mechanical, 21 files. Declare the `.sdata` target as a plain
SCALAR extern (`extern f32 lbl_803CA744;`, never `char[]`) and read it as
normal C, plus per-object `-msdata=eabi -G4` on its `Object()` in
configure.py. Scalar decls are 4 bytes, so -G4 suffices even for an object
dtk sizes at 0x60 (e.g. `lbl_803CA420`). mwld then emits the access r2-relative
and `tools/patch_dol.py` rewrites r2 -> r13 (+0xD00) as usual: bytes identical,
reloc present, objdiff 100%. Scalar-extern + `-msdata` is the ONLY way to get
`@sda21` from C; under `-G0` (the game default) plain C can never emit it,
which is exactly why the wedges existed (see `libs/runtime/src/__getreent.c`).

GOTCHA 1 (do not skip). The wedge was also a SCHEDULING BARRIER. Replacing it
with a plain C load lets the load float — cosf/sinf/rand moved the load behind
the first independent instruction and the DOL stopped matching. Fix: an empty
`__asm__ volatile("");` on the line after the load restores the retail order.
18 of the 21 files needed nothing; only these 3 did. Always `cmp` after each
batch and localise with the DOL-vs-DOL byte-range mapper (below).

GOTCHA 2 (class B is NOT a batch). For a non-SDA `.data` symbol, plain C gives
the right SHAPE (`lis rX,sym@ha; lwz rY,sym@l(rX)`) but not the right register:
fn_800AB604's `register s32 anc __asm__("r26")` base went r26 -> r27 and the
whole block re-ordered (99.96% -> 98.35%, DOL differs). A reload-generated base
pseudo cannot be pinned from C, so class B is per-function regalloc coaxing.
44 of the 57 remaining wired units are class B.

TOOLING (kept in /tmp, one-offs by policy; re-derive if needed).
 * object-vs-DOL word compare: flag a differing word as a REAL diff only when
   NO relocation overlaps it — and floor each reloc offset to a 4-byte
   instruction boundary, because ProDG puts `R_PPC_ADDR16_HA/LO` at
   instruction+2 (a naive `rel.get(off)` lookup reports false "NO-RELOC").
 * DOL-vs-DOL range mapper: file offset -> section -> vaddr -> owning symbol;
   this is how the cosf/sinf/rand scheduling regression was named in one shot.
 * `objdiff-cli diff -u <unit> -p . -o - --format json`: per-instruction
   `diff_kind`; the target side's operands ARE dtk's recovered relocs.

### 6hg follow-up: which of the 57 remaining wired units are NOT convertible (measured)

After the 24 SDA units above, 57 wired units stayed <100%. Two reformulations
were tried on the cleanest members of the other classes and BOTH were reverted
(the DOL is only safe because they were reverted):

 * fn_80198190 (1 diff, `addi r27,r9,sym@l` vs `subi r27,r9,0x57f8` — SAME bytes,
   since -0x57F8 == 0xA808). Replacing the `lis %0,%1@ha` wedge + `anchor -
   0x57F8` reconstruction with `lblbase = (s32)(char *)lbl_802AA808;` gives the
   right reloc pair but COLLAPSES the two-register form into ONE:
   `lis r27,@ha; addi r27,r27,@l` where retail is `lis r9,@ha; addi r27,r9,@l`.
   The hi-part pseudo cannot be bound to a register from C — the pinned
   `register s32 anchor __asm__("r9")` was the only thing holding r9, and an
   unpinned reload pseudo takes its own colour.
 * fn_8026EDA8 (1 diff, `lfd f0,lbl_802B22A0@l(r8)` vs `0x22a0(r8)`). A scalar
   `extern f64 lbl_802B22A0;` read emitted `@sda21` instead (the unit already
   carries `-msdata=eabi -G8`, and the symbol is 8B), costing an instruction
   (328 -> 324B); forcing it non-SDA with `extern f64 ...[2]` (16B > -G8)
   restored the `lis`/`lfd` pair but the base went r8 -> r11. Same wall.

So: the SDA-asm class (a plain `.sdata` scalar read, where the operand form does
not change) converts cleanly and is worth sweeping; the "pinned anchor + literal
displacement" class does NOT, because the pin is load-bearing and is exactly what
the reloc form removes. Also checked: converting the same wedge inside the inert
drafts is a regression (fn_802533B0 97.8 -> 90.8, reverted) — the statement-
expression macro `#define HEAP() ({...})` is load-bearing there too.

## 6hh — 2026-10-07 (fn_801B6310 **promoted**, 9760 -> **9761/11497** (84.900%), 712B, DOL `cmp`+sha1+`ok` clean, source has 0 `__asm__`): **a `promote_wip` "internal branch target differs" refusal on a masked-EXACT draft can be a REAL control-flow bug — read which block each test's false-case falls into; the `&&`-chain vs empty-then/else distinction is what decides it**

SYMPTOM. `0x801B6310` (712B) swept EXACT but promote_wip REFUSEd: at
`0x801B6540` want `beq 0x801B6558`, got `beq 0x801B65B8`. The masked compare
never sees branch targets (recipes §6bw), so 100% was blind to it — and so was
the draft's own park note, which called it a layout problem for "the
orchestrator" to fix.

READ THE REGION, NOT THE SCORE. The disassembly at 0x801B6530 compares r3 against zero, branches on equal to the body at 0x801B6558 which runs when the first call returns zero, loads the stack slot sp14 into r9, compares it against the 0x7D9D0008 constant, branches on equal to the tail epilogue at 0x801B65B8 when the slot holds the vertical-grab value, and otherwise falls into the body at 0x801B6558 with the second call plus the skate/walk dispatch.
Two DIFFERENT targets, both semantically meaningful:
`beq BODY` on the first test and `beq TAIL` on the second. That pair is the
exact signature of `if (X && Y) { } else { BODY }` — X false short-circuits to
the else arm, Y true skips it. The draft had
`(c1 != 0) && (sp14 != QB_VERT_GRAB) && (c2 != 0)`, which sends `c1 == 0` to
the function TAIL instead: **call2 was being skipped whenever call1 == 0**, a
real behaviour change (promote_wip was right to refuse, and the note's
"just a branch layout" framing was wrong).

FIX. Invert the middle term and move the work into the else arm, leaving an
empty then arm (that is what emits `beq BODY` / `beq TAIL` in that order):
```c
if ((GetChecksum_2(temp_r30_2, QB_SKATEACTION, &sp14, 0) != 0) && (sp14 == QB_VERT_GRAB)) {
    /* nothing */
} else {
    if (GetChecksum_2(temp_r3, QB_PEDTYPE, &sp18, 0) != 0) { ...unchanged... }
}
```
One reshape -> EXACT -> promoted. The inner SKATE/WALK dispatch needed no
change (its words already matched).

SCOPE / what this does NOT unlock (measured this round):
 * A full 8-slice re-sweep of all 1718 drafts still reports only the SAME 6
   blocked EXACTs (0x80003464 outside .text; 0x801B5A54 whole-body asm;
   0x8013928C fold wall; 0x801D2C58 linker relaxation; 0x8025AE3C dtk
   pseudo-function; 0x8025B340 dead-strip). The masked-EXACT seam is exhausted.
 * fn_8013928C: the failing two branches are DEAD (the arm is unreachable,
   `res == 0` is guaranteed by the preceding `bne`). Adding `break` to force
   the retail exit restructures the loop and drops the whole body to DIFF;
   a single `break` alone does the same. Leave parked.
 * fn_8011CF0C (98.1%) is a genuine sched2 reload-hoist wall, not this class —
   its note already rules out the post-call assignment and 0-code barriers.

## 6hi — 2026-10-07 (4 WIRED units flipped to 100.000%, 9761 -> **9765/11497** (84.935%): fn_8006A1DC, fn_80066834, fn_8001E248, fn_8012F8E8; DOL `cmp`+sha1+`ok` clean): **a `lis %0,sym@ha` wedge with a LITERAL displacement is fixable in real C — pin the base as a TYPED POINTER, assign the bare symbol address, and index it at offset 0; the pin survives only if the assignment and every use are in the SAME basic block**

### The defect
§6hg's follow-on. A wired unit whose objdiff reads

```
+0x40 DIFF_ARG_MISMATCH  target[lfs f0, lbl_80294A0C@l(r11)]  ours[lfs f0, 0x4a0c(r11)]
```

is byte-correct (`cmp` is clean — the DOL is hash-verified) but uncredited: the draft's wedge
`__asm__ volatile("lis %0,%1@ha" : "=r"(anc) : "s"(sym))` emits a reloc for the `lis`, while the
load's displacement is a hardcoded `sym & 0xFFFF`, which emits none. The register is *already*
right — only the displacement's reloc is missing. `0x4A0C == @l(lbl_80294A0C)` because the draft
reads `(char *)anc + disp` where `anc = @ha(sym)`, i.e. the effective address IS the symbol.

### The fix (works, deterministic)
Replace the pin's *value*, not the pin:

```c
/* before */                                        /* after */
register s32 pg __asm__("r11");                     register char *pg __asm__("r11");
__asm__ volatile("lis %0,%1@ha" : "=r"(pg)          extern f32 lbl_80294A0C[];
                                        : "s"(lbl_80294A0C));   /* delete */
...                                                 pg = (char *)&lbl_80294A0C;
c = *(f32 *)((char *)pg + 0x4A0C);                  c = *(f32 *)((char *)pg);
```

Because `pg` holds a *known symbol address* at offset 0, ngccc's address legitimation folds it into
the memory operand and emits `lis r11, sym@ha` **and** `lfs f0, sym@l(r11)` — both relocs — with the
register unchanged. All four units above landed at 100.000% this way, 2 of them 4 B functions.

### The rule that decides success (measure it, don't guess)
The elimination only happens under **local-alloc**, i.e. when the assignment and *every* use sit in
the **same basic block**. 13 shapes were auto-attempted and only same-BB ones took:

* **works**: assignment in the function body, use a few statements later, no branch between (the 4 above).
* **fails (extra `lis`+`addi @l`, size grows 4 B)**: the use is inside a `do {} while`/`if` body while the
  assignment is outside — global-alloc keeps a reload pseudo and materialises the full address. Auto-revert.
* **fails (register swap)**: two same-page pins get CSE'd onto one register (fn_80003830 r11↔r9).
* **fails (2 words, hoist position)**: dropping the pin and reading the global directly inside the loop
  gets the fold right but loop-opt appends the hoisted `lis` at the END of the preheader; retail has it
  one statement earlier. This is the residual wall for the remaining ~11 one-diff units (fn_8008E50,
  fn_80014FCC, fn_80059318, fn_800A234C, fn_800AB604, fn_800BD96C, fn_801399D8, fn_8016A048,
  fn_80186DF8, fn_801AA158, fn_8026EDA8) — all are Class A, all byte-exact, none convertible without
  breaking byte-identity. Do NOT re-run the sweeps below on them without new ideas.
* **`DIFF_OP_MISMATCH addi vs subi`** (fn_801399D8, fn_80198190, fn_801B06A0) is the *same* root cause:
  `subi rX, rY, 0x57f8` and `addi rX, rY, sym@l` are byte-identical; only the reloc differs.

Verification tool: `wedgecheck.py <obj> <vaddr> <size>` compares the object's `.text` against the DOL
slice with each word's **relocation immediate field masked**, so a register/opcode change is reported as
`NO-RELOC **REAL DIFF**` while a reloc-representation difference is not. Two batched experiments
(wedgeconv / wedgeconv2, in `<scratch>) applied a rewrite, rebuilt one object, and required
`wedgecheck` clean **and** `objdiff-cli diff` 0 diffs before keeping it — every reject auto-reverted, and
a mid-run crash that left two files written is why the final tree was re-verified with `git status` +
`wedgecheck` rather than trusted.

## 7f — 2026-10-07: fn_80139790 matched (Ctx/lexer zone, 0x801397xx) — 4 new levers

`fn_80139790` (584B, script-lexer walker over `fn_80138038`/`fn_801399D8`'s
address-taken `Ctx`) went 3.4% → **EXACT in one session** with four reusable
levers. The whole thing matched byte-for-byte **including branch addends and
`bl` relocations** (verified with an addend audit + REL24 symbol dump).

1. **`lhz` → `mr rX,rY` copy (a dead 4-byte miss).** WANT
   `lhz r0,0(p); mr r9,r0; sth r0,off16(r1); stw r9,off32(r1)` — the copy is
   NOT a mode conversion of a local. It appears when the source **stores the
   value into a `u16` FIELD of an address-taken aggregate and then re-reads
   that field into an `s32` field**:
   `ctx.u16f = *(u16 *)p; p += 2; ctx.s32f = ctx.u16f;` (CSE/store-forward
   gives GCC the stored value in HImode → `mr` for the widening store).
   Declaring a `u16 v` local + two stores does **not** do it (GCC promotes v
   to SImode, both stores reuse r0, object is 4B short). Only 2 such sites
   exist in the whole DOL (fn_80139790 @0x80139818 and fn_8013A398
   @0x8013A3CC) — both this Ctx family. Repro: `fn_8013A398`'s
   `hdr.f2 = *(u16 *)(p+1); hdr.f8 = hdr.f2;`.
2. **`nor r3,r3,r3` + `andi. r0,r3,1`.** `if (!(t & 1))` compiles to
   `andi.` + inverted branch (no `nor`); `y = !(t & 1); if (y)` compiles to
   **`xori r3,r3,1`** + `andi.`. The WANT form comes from
   **`y = ~t & 1; if (y) {…}`** — a bitwise NOT of the whole word then the
   mask. Rule: when WANT shows `nor` before an `andi.`-set condition, write
   the source as `~x & mask` (not `!(x & mask)`), and branch on `if (y)`
   (GCC emits `beq <skip>` for `if (y)`).
3. **The `mfcr`/`mtcrf 0x80` CR0 save across ONE conditional call** is
   doc-28's short-range class and fell out of plain C once the condition was
   forced into a value (lever 2). No second call is needed: writing the
   *same expression* twice makes GCC CSE the compare into cr0, and the
   intervening `bl` forces the `mfcr rX`/`mtcrf 0x80,rX` pair.
4. **`clrlwi r4,r0,0x18` on an `lbz` source.** Passing `p[5]` (byte load,
   range known 0..255) to a narrow param gives `mr r4,r0`. WANT's redundant
   mask appears when the source **reads a byte FIELD back after storing it**
   and passes that: `ctx.byte = p[5]; fn(base, ctx.byte, …)` — the read-back
   of the stored value (store-forwarded, SImode→QImode) emits
   `clrlwi r4,r0,0x18`. This also fixes the emission order: WANT's
   `clrlwi` *before* the `stb` (masking emitted first, store second).

Also confirmed: `ctx.dest = buf`-style init stores follow **source order**
(not reversed); the tail `for` loop over `ctx.arr[i]` needed the array as a
**4-byte-element member at the memset region's offset** (`u16 pad; Elem
arr[31];`) so the frame's 0xb0c bytes line up exactly.

## 7g — 2026-10-07: fn_8013A508 (8.0% → 67.2%) and fn_8013A398 (77.2% → **94.6%**, 368B == want) — the "**one local per distinct value**" rule + the masked-byte-index spelling

### 7g-1. ONE LOCAL PER DISTINCT VALUE (the big one; both functions, no flags/pins)

Reusing a single local for several *different* runtime values makes ngccc coalesce
their webs; the frame, the callee-saved register assignment and sometimes the
*values stored to fields* all change.  Measured twice:

* **0x8013A508** — one `val` was doing duty as (a) the s32 read out of the
  buffer, (b) the u16 `arg0->fA - 6` call argument, (c) the `fn_80137F30`
  result.  Splitting into `val` / `slen` / `cval` moved the frame from
  `stwu -0x38 / stmw r26,0x20` to the want's `stwu -0x40 / stmw r25,0x24` and
  made `obj->key` store the **s32 buffer value** (want `stw r28,8(r31)`) instead
  of the truncated u16.  8.0% → 67.2% (500B == want).
* **0x8013A398** — one `temp_r30` was the `fn_801399D8` result **and** the
  reloaded `sp8.unk0x0`.  Splitting into `s32 ret` + `void *buf` removed the
  extra `mr r3,r0` that made the function 4 bytes long:
  want `mr r30,r3; lwz r3,8(r1); cmpwi r3,0` vs got
  `lwz r0,8(r1); mr r30,r3; cmpwi r0,0; mr r3,r0`.
  77.2% → 94.6%, `.text` 372B → **368B == want**.
  The `void *buf` intermediate is load-bearing: `if (sp8.unk0x0 != NULL)` (no
  local) keeps the old bad schedule.

Rule of thumb: when a function reloads a field after a call and *also* holds
that call's result, give each its own local — even if the values look
interchangeable to a reader.

### 7g-2. The walk-pointer idiom: `p++; v = *(s32*)p; p += 4;` (separate statement)

0x8013A508's want does `lwzu r28,1(r31)` (post-increment load) **and then**
`addi r31,r31,4` *before* the branch, i.e. the walk pointer is advanced to p+5 up
front.  Writing `sp19 = p[4]; p6 = p + 5;` makes ngccc CSE that into
`addi r30,r28,5` (2 words short).  Split it:

```c
p++;                    /* lwzu: load+update                     */
val = *(s32 *)p;        /* the s32 at p+1                        */
p += 4;                 /* addi r31,r31,4                        */
...
sp19 = *p;              /* lbz 0(r31)                            */
p++;                    /* addi r31,r31,1                        */
p6 = p;                 /* p6 is just the moved pointer          */
```

### 7g-3. The byte-scaled table index `rlwinm rX,rX,2,0x16,0x1d`

That opcode is `(idx << 2) & 0x3FC` — an *identity* for a byte index, so it is
not a real mask.  It only appears when the index is a **signed** byte + an
unsigned cast:

```c
s8 idx;                       /* NOT u8/char-as-unsigned */
idx = p[0];
sp18 = idx;
lim = tab[(u8)idx];           /* -> rlwinm r0,r0,2,0x16,0x1d */
```

Every unsigned spelling folds to `slwi` (ngccc range-propagates the `lbz`):
`u8 idx; tab[idx]`, `tab[(u8)idx]`, `tab[idx & 0xff]`, u16/u32/int
intermediates, address-taken non-volatile slots, 8-bit bitfields, `s8*` pointer
loads, `(s8)` round trips — all tried.  The same opcode in `fn_8000A778` /
`fn_8000A7F8` is the CRC-table idiom `tab[(crc ^ byte) & 0xff]` (wider unsigned
operand, no sign extension) — useful as a *reference* for the mask form but it
cannot feed a plain `lbz`.

**Open blocker:** ngccc 3.9.3 always pairs that spelling with an extra
`extsb r0,r0` before the `stb` (the sign-extension of the signed byte), which
0x8013A508's want does **not** have.  ~120 spellings and 16 flag variants
(-O1/-O3/-Os, -fno-rerun-cse-after-loop, -fno-schedule-insns{,2},
-fno-strength-reduce, -fno-expensive-optimizations, -fno-regmove,
-fno-peephole, -fno-cse-follow-jumps, -fno-cse-skip-blocks, -fno-inline,
-fno-defer-pop) all keep the mask+extsb pair.  So the mask is reproducible but
not yet *cleanly*; the want's spelling (mask without extsb) is still unknown.

## 7h — 2026-10-07 (fn_8000B6F8 27.4% → **88.7% NEAR**, size-exact; fn_8000D478 11.8% → **68.4% NEAR**, 323/323 words; three PS drafts parked with a verified blocker; DOL `cmp`+sha1+`ok` clean): **frame-slot ORDERING is the real rule behind the "scalar-cast idiom" — declared/volatile locals are allocated LOW and address-taken scalar temps HIGH, so a pad can never move the temp back to r1+8; how to split a select so the `mr` appears; and the m2c-input gap for Paired-Single functions**

### 7h.1 — the select needs TWO variables, the second one assigned from a copy
`fn_8000B6F8`'s want has a *pre-loop* select that lives in r3 and is then
copied into the callee-saved loop variable: at offset 0x73C retail compares r9 against zero, at 0x740 materialises zero into r3, at 0x744 branches on equal to 0x74C, at 0x748 loads offset four into r3, and at 0x750 copies r3 into r31.

Measured (all with the family's `((It *)&scalar_local)` idiom):
* `v = (node != 0) ? node->f04 : 0;`            → `li r31,0 … lwz r31,4(r9)`, **no `mr`**, 4B short.
* `if (node) v = node->f04; else v = 0;`        → same, no `mr`.
* `t = 0; if (node) t = node->f04; v = t;`      → same, no `mr`.
* **`w = (node != 0) ? node->f04 : 0; v = w;`** → **`li r3,0 … lwz r3,4(r9) … mr r31,r3`** ✓
  (a *ternary* into a helper, then a plain copy).  The in-loop occurrence of the
  same ternary into `v` stays a direct `li r31,0 / lwz r31,4(r11)` — want really
  does use both shapes, so keep the loop select single-variable.
The mechanism is that the ternary result gets the caller-saved r3 because the
following mask block clobbers r3, and the copy into the loop variable is then
mandatory.  One merged variable lets the allocator go straight to r31 and the
`mr` (and 4 bytes) disappear.

### 7h.2 — branchless mask + flag forms (ngccc, from C)
* `m = (lbl[i] == -1) ? 0x80000000 : 0;` compiles to the branchless
  `lbz; extsb; subfic rX,rX,-1; addic rX,rX,-1; subfe rX,rX,rX; rlwinm rD,rX,0,0,0`
  (i.e. `-(x == -1) & 0x80000000`).  `if (lbl[i] == -1) m |= 0x80000000;` emits a
  real branch and loses all five instructions.
* the second mask constant must be **0x40000000**: `m |= 0x40000000` gives
  `oris rD,rD,0x4000`; writing `0x4000` gives `ori` — a wrong word that no
  relocation mask hides.
* `t = (fn() != 0) ? 1 : 0;` emits `li r0,1` then `bne`; the equivalent
  `if (fn() != 0) t = 1; else t = 0;` flips it to `li r0,0` + `beq`.

### 7h.3 — frame-slot ordering: declared locals LOW, scalar temps HIGH
The 12-byte iterator of the "stack iterator + `lbl_802901D8`" family must be
indexed through a **scalar cast** (`((It *)&scratch)->f[4/8]`) to materialise an
address pseudo (the two-register base `addi r11,r1,8` + `mr r30,r11`).  A
`struct`/`array`/`union`-member decl folds the base instead.  This leaves the
scalar's stack *slot* at r1+8 with a 4-byte object, so the frame is 0x18 while
the want is 0x20 — and it cannot be padded into place: ngccc allocates
**declared (and `volatile`) locals first, from r1+8 upward, and the address-taken
scalar's slot LAST**.  Measured: any pad at all pushes `&scratch` up by the pad
size (`volatile s32` ×1 → 0xc, ×2 → 0x10, ×3 → 0x14; `volatile f64/s64`,
`volatile s32[1]`, `s32 pad[1]`, `s32 *pad[1]`, and every declaration order all
behave the same).  The pad is still useful for the *frame size* (2 × 4-byte
`volatile s32` pads give exactly want's 0x20 frame and 0x18/0x24 save slots) —
you just also get the +8 on the base offset, i.e. 7 residual words instead of 62.
To finish it one needs a 12-byte *scalar-flavoured* temp (m2c/tooling note:
`assign_stack_temp` sizes the temp from the DECL, so an `s32` can never be
12 bytes) — e.g. a second address-taken scalar created *after* the first (temps
are allocated in first-use order), which requires a zero-code way to take that
second address; `(void)&x` does **not** mark a local addressable in 3.9.3.
Also measured for this family: the `-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop` FLAG was
load-bearing on the old 27% body and is now **harmful** (with it ngccc CSEs the
function-tail `lis/addi` pair into a spare callee-saved reg and drops to 244B);
always re-A/B a stale `// FLAG:` line on a rewritten body.

### 7h.4 — m2c's 4-byte stack-buffer placeholder vs the real buffer
`fn_8000D478` (1292B, 323 insns, pure integer) scored 11.8% because m2c modelled
the two stack buffers as `s32 sp8; s32 sp88;` (4 bytes each).  The want frame is
0x1b0 and the buffers are **sp8[0x80] at r1+8 and sp88[0x100] at r1+0x88** — with
those types the prologue (`stwu -0x1b0 / mfcr r12 / stmw r24,0x190 /
stw r0,0x1b4 / stw r12,0x18c`), the save area and every r1-relative access land
exactly, 11.8% → **68.4%**.  Two calibration rules learned:
* the local area is rounded up to 8 before the register-save area, so a buffer
  that is 8 bytes short/long of the truth still gives the right prologue
  (0xfc and 0x100 both → frame 0x1b0; 0x104 → 0x1b8).  Size the *last* buffer
  from the CR-save offset (want CR at 0x18c ⇒ locals end at 0x188).
* **index stack buffers through the ARRAY, not a pointer**: `sp88[n-4]` gives
  want's `addi r0,r3,-4` + `lbzx r9,r29,r0`; `p[n-4]` through a `char *` makes
  ngccc fold the offset into a displacement (`lbz r0,-4(r11)`) and the whole
  string check diverges (65.6% → 20.7%).
* a comparison result can legitimately live in **cr4** across calls (CR2..CR4
  are non-volatile in the EABI) — that is what produces a `mfcr r12 / stw r12 /
  … / mtcrf 8,r12` prologue/epilogue pair.  Just test `arg4 != 0` twice with
  calls in between; nothing special is needed in the C.

### 7h.5 — Paired-Single drafts: the blocker is the m2c INPUT, not emission
Word census of the three parked files (capstone + `tools/ps_disasm.py:ps_str`):
`fn_800086B0` 1952B/488 insns = **50.6% PS** (186 psq D-forms + 61 op-4 A-form
arithmetic), `fn_80047DFC` 9724B/2431 = **8.6% PS** (208 psq D-forms, *no* op-4
arithmetic), `fn_80052248` 4012B/1003 = **19.1% PS** (160 + 32).  capstone has no
Gekko PS tables, so it prints op-4 words as **bogus VMX mnemonics**
(`xxsel`/`xsmaddasp`/`vmsumshm`/`xxmrghd` — Gekko has no VMX units) and the psq
D-forms as `.byte`; `tools/fill_wip_drafts.py` feeds that text straight to m2c,
which turns each such word into an error → the stored bodies are `0;`
placeholders (they compile to 0.2–0.5% and are not salvageable by flag/pin
tuning).  Emission is NOT the wall (docs/parkings/06 M5.0t: ProDG 3.9.3 emits
every PS opcode from `__ps_t` + `-mps-float`, per-object via
`// extra_cflags: -mps-float`).  The unblock is a PS-aware m2c pre-pass:
`tools/ps_disasm.py` decodes the psq D-forms and `ps_str()` the X-form
`psq_lx`/`psq_stx`; `tools/ps_diff.py`'s `dec()` labels the rest.  m2c already
models `psq_l/psq_st` as f64 accesses (`arch_ppc.py:1026/1528`) but raises
`ErrorExpr("psq_l unimplemented")` at `:1558` and knows no `ps_*` arithmetic —
so a textual `psq_l/psq_st → lfd/stfd` rewrite covers all 208 words of
fn_80047DFC (the best first target: its PS content is ONLY loads/stores), with
`-mps-float` then making the f64 accesses emit psq_l/psq_st again.

## 7i — 2026-10-07 (fn_801EC7C4 14.1% → **84.6% NEAR sweep / 84.8% positional**, 369 words vs want 368, frame byte-exact; fn_801BA464 / fn_801BF5B8 / fn_801DBCAC re-measured and parked; DOL `cmp`+sha1+`ok` clean): **a base register from an explicit `s32 *p` (member access FOLDS, pointer arithmetic does NOT); one shared live zero pools `li r0,0`×N into `li r29,0`×1; splitting `a/f(x)` into two statements buys the `fmr` across the call; naming a constant `f32 d0` pins it in a callee-saved FPR so later compares reuse it; and routing two adjacent PS pair updates through `SN_PS_type *u` kills a base reload (+16%)**

### 7i.1 `x->a` folds the displacement; `p[1]`/`p[2]` off an explicit base pointer does NOT

THUG2 is full of the "state + timestamp" pair idiom. In want, only the three
sites in fn_801EC7C4: retail loads offset 0x15BC of the arg0 home into r9, derives the base by adding 0x24 into r30 without folding the displacement, loads index one through that base, compares it against zero, skips when zero, otherwise stores r29 to index one for the zeroing, calls Tmr_GetTime, adds the call result into r0, and stores the timestamp sum to index two.

Writing the obvious `if (x->unk0x28 != 0) { x->unk0x28 = 0; x->unk0x2C = ...; }`
makes ngccc emit `lwz r0, 0x28(r9)` / `stw r0, 0x28(r9)` / `stw r0, 0x2c(r9)` —
**same instruction count, different shape**, and every one of them misses. The
base+displacement form comes back only from an explicit pointer:

```c
    s32 *p = (s32 *) ((u8 *) arg0->unk0x15BC + 0x24);   /* base 0x24 */
    if (p[1] != 0) { p[1] = 0; p[2] = lbl + Tmr_GetTime(); }
```

Note the base is the **struct-aligned** offset (0x24 / 0x3C / 0x60), so the pair
is `p[1]`/`p[2]`, not `p[0]`/`p[1]`. Getting the base wrong by 4 also still
"looks` like the same source. Cross-check with `tools/want_dis.py`/`ps_disasm.py`
on that exact block. Same trick works for `&arg0->unk0x170` (`addi r29, r31, 0x170`
+ `mr r5, r29` + later `lbz r4, 0x5a(r29)`): assigning `T170 *p170 = &arg0->unk0x170;`
once at the top of the case is load-bearing — `&arg0->unk0x170` written inline
twice compiles to `addi r5, r31, 0x170` and loses both the `mr` and a word.

### 7i.2 One shared live zero pools the constants

Want emitted `li r29, 0` **once** and reused r29 for `p[1] = 0`, `p[1] = 0`
(second site) and `arg0->unk0x314 = 0`. The literal-`0` source emits `li r0,0`
three times (`li` census +2). Fix:

```c
    s32 z;              /* declared at top, no initialiser */
    ...
    z = 0;              /* placed where want's single `li` lands */
    sp18 = ((var_f31 - var_f1) * ...) + var_f1;
```

The *placement* of `z = 0;` matters: with the plain form ngccc hoisted the `li`
into the prologue (`li r27,0` before the first `bl`) and the +1-word shift broke
**every branch displacement** (REL14 keeps bits 2..15, so `beq`/`bge` addends are
compared, and the positional score collapsed 25.3% → 7.6%). Placing `z = 0;`
just before the lerp statement put it back.

### 7i.3 Split `a / f(x)` to get the `fmr` across the call

Want (3× per function) reloads the numerator from the paired-single spill at r1 plus 0x20 into f0, keeps it across the call in callee-saved f31, calls fn_801417B8, divides f31 by the call result into f1, loads the second argument byte from offset 0x5A of the r29 home after the call, copies r30 into r3, and calls fn_801C1FA4.

The one-expression form `fn(a, b, num / fn_801417B8(...))` lets the scheduler
**sink** the `lfs` past the `bl` and drop the `fmr` (-3 `fmr`, +3 `mr` once the
byte has to be kept in a register instead). Two named locals restore want:

```c
    f32 num = dot.flt.hi;
    f32 den = fn_801417B8(arg0->unk0xC, STAT);
    fn_801C1FA4(a, b, num / den);
```

Fun follow-on: with `num`/`den` the *global* callee-saved allocation flips —
`mr r31, r3` becomes `mr r30, r3` and `xori r30, r3, 1` becomes `xori r31, r3, 1`
(a pure r30/r31 role swap). Adding the shared `z` from 7i.2 at the same time
restores it. **Measure these two levers together, not one at a time.**

### 7i.4 Name a constant used across a call — that is what pins it in f31

Want kept `lbl_802AD8F0` in **f31** from the lerp expression all the way to a much
later `fcmpu cr0, f0, f31`. Using the symbol literal in every place let ngccc park
it in the volatile `f10`, the intervening `bl GetFloat` killed it, and the compare
reloaded it (`lis r9; lfs f11`) — +2 words plus a cascade of FP-register colour
drift through both integrator blocks. One named local closes all of it:

```c
    f32 d0;                       /* top of function */
    ...
    d0 = lbl_802AD8F0;            /* where want's `lfs f31` lands */
    sp18 = (... - d0) / (... - d0) ...;
    if ((x->unk0x40 != 0) && (arg0->unk0xC->unk0xB8.flt.lo < d0)) { ... sp18 = d0; ... }
```

68.5% → and it is the fix that then let 7i.5 work. Uses that want *does* re-load
(the else-branch compare, the tail `fn_8009F054` arg) must stay literals.

### 7i.5 Route adjacent PS pair updates through `SN_PS_type *u`

Two `psq_l`/`ps_add`/`psq_st` pairs on adjacent fields (`unk0xB8`/`unk0xC0`,
`unk0x58`/`unk0x60`) written as direct `a->b->c.ps = __builtin_ps_add(...)` made
ngccc reload `arg0->unk0xC` in the middle of the block (an extra `lwz`, off by
one, everything after shifted). Funnelling through a pointer:

```c
    SN_PS_type *u;
    ...
    u = &arg0->unk0xC->unk0xB8;
    u[0].ps = __builtin_ps_add(u[0].ps, v[0]);
    u[1].ps = __builtin_ps_add(u[1].ps, v[1]);
```

68.5% → **84.8%**, size 370 → 369 words. (The pointer must be declared *in the
block that uses it*; hoisting it to function scope changed allocation elsewhere.)

### 7i.6 Score mirage: a "win" that deletes instructions want has

Moving `s38.f = sp18;` to **after** the two `__builtin_ps_muls0(..., s38.p)` that
read it scored 77.7% on a 368-word body (vs 68.5% / 370 correct-order) and briefly
looked like the win. It is not: it reads the union before writing it, and the two
saved words reappeared as an extra `lwz`. Always run the **opcode census** for the
byte the win came from (`/tmp` harness: histogram `pdis.dis_words` over want and
got, diff the counts). If the delta is `lfs/stfs -1` while want has them, the
"improvement" is a shift artefact, not a match. Rejected and documented in the
file header instead.

### 7i.7 Negative result: blind `s32` → `f32` retype of an m2c husk makes it SMALLER

fn_801BA464's m2c body types every float operand as `s32`, so it is 77 words vs
want 763. Replacing the 196 `*(s32 *)((char *)&sp8 + k)` and 192
`*(s32 *)((char *)temp_r3 + 0xK)` reads with `*(f32 *)` **reduces** it to 68 words:
the `&spX + k` alias trick that gives m2c its frame layout stops working once the
scalars are float, and GCC merges/folds the blocks. The fix is structural —
declare `f32 A[16]; f32 *M; f32 O[16];` and rewrite the three 4x4 matmuls as
`O[0] = A[3]*M[12] + (A[2]*M[8] + (A[0]*M[0] + A[1]*M[4]));` — not a cast swap.
Recorded here so nobody repeats it.

### 7i.8 Census before you choose a target

`tools/ps_disasm.py <dol> <addr> <n>` + a `grep -c` census on the output is
cheaper than a disasm read and tells you which file to spend the session on:
fn_801BA464 turned out to be **branch-free** (0 conditional branches, 0 cmpwi,
0 mfcr, 6 calls, 390 lfs / 144 fmadds, only 62 PS words) — the only good target in
this batch after fn_801EC7C4. fn_801BF5B8 (435 PS words / 35%, `mfcr`+`mtcrf 8`,
42 calls) and fn_801DBCAC (447 PS words / 42%, `mfcr`+`mtcrf 0x18`, 53 calls) are
PS/CR-dominated and belong behind the PS-aware m2c pre-pass. The branch-free
straight-line profile is the one where ngccc's allocator is reproducible.

## 6hj — 2026-10-07 (**5 promoted**, 9765 → **9771/11497** (84.987%): fn_802206AC, fn_802209C4, fn_802413C0, fn_80024100, fn_80003984; DOL `cmp`+sha1+`ok` clean): **the SCAFFOLD-ABLATION SWEEP — every draft with a pin / zero-code barrier / `// FLAG:` scored against 5 ablations of its own scaffolding; the barrier's DELETION (not its placement) was the residual in all three "impossible" parks, and a `-Os` left over from an older body was worth 53 points on one function**

### The sweep
878 drafts carry a `register ... __asm__("rN")` pin, a zero-code
`__asm__("" : ...)` barrier or a `// FLAG:` line. For each, score the draft as-is
and `{nopin, nobar, nopin+nobar, noflag, nopin+nobar+noflag}` (masked, clamped to
the symbol size, FPR dual-test honoured). 146 strict improvements, **3 EXACT**,
and the two axes are cleanly separated:

| axis | biggest single win | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `nobar`  | 0x8015307C **+19.2** (73.3→92.4) | 8 more members +1…+9 |
| `noflag` | 0x80024100 **+53.4** (43.1→96.6) | also +18.1 (0x801C1364), +16.6 (0x8012F68C), +13.5 (0x80229E18), +12.3 (0x800DEEC4) |
| `nopin`  | 0x80166640 +4.8 (94.2→99.0) | only 3 improvements corpus-wide — the pins are mostly load-bearing (as the notes claimed) |
| `nopin+nobar(+noflag)` | 0x80003984 +9.0, 0x80229E18 +13.5 | the conjunction cases |

### The conjunction trap, again — and its new shape: DELETE, don't re-place
All three EXACTs came from **deleting** zero-code barriers:

* **0x802206AC / 0x802209C4** (384 B twins, `s0`/`m0` `"+r"` barriers). Their notes
  already recorded "pin removal helped 90.6→94.8", so the pin axis looked mined —
  but the two barriers are a *separate* piece: remove either alone and the score
  does not move; remove **both** (leaving the pins!) and both functions are
  byte-identical.
* **0x802413C0** (140 B) had tried mid-block `"+r"(r4v)` barriers in two other
  *positions* (w7/w8) and hoists (w4/w5) — the winning move was deleting the two
  `"+r"(p11)` barriers and changing nothing else.

> A park note that says "re-barriering/hoisting the value didn't pin it" has not
> tested the barrier's *deletion*. Score the deletion against the current body
> before trusting any "mid-block barrier doesn't help" verdict.

### The stale `// FLAG:` is worth re-measuring on EVERY body edit
`fn_80024100` was parked at 43.9% **because of its own `// FLAG: -Os`** (deleting
the line alone: 96.6%). The flag had been chosen against a body three rewrites
older. This is §6aq-222/§6bf again, now with a 53-point delta — the largest
single-line win found so far. After the flag was gone the function was a 2-word
zero-store rotation (source `[0x14, 0x20, 0x1C, 0x18]` → emission
`[0x14, 0x1C, 0x20, 0x18]`; writing the source as `[0x14, 0x1C, 0x20, 0x18]`
emits want's order) and `real_diffs` reported 0/58.

### fn_80003984 (`atan2f` fast path, 356 B) — four levers, one of them new
Parked at 85.4% with a note calling the residual "the rodata2 anchor interleave,
not reachable from C". In order:
1. the stale `// FLAG: -Os` deleted (**+9.0**);
2. the `register s32 xneg __asm__("r8")` pin **and** the `"+f"(c20)` barrier both
   deleted — again a conjunction (either one alone is score-neutral or worse);
3. **the c1c/c20 coefficient-load pair must be written `c1c` FIRST** (want emits
   `lfs f8` then `lfs f6`): **+2.2** → 96.6%;
4. the last 2 words were the *home register of the `lbl_8028FC24` constant*: want
   keeps it in **f0**, which is the register `t` is already pinned to — the two
   webs are sequential (constant's last use +0xb4, `t` written +0xb8), so a
   block-scoped `register f32 k24 __asm__("fr0");` legalises an
   **exclusive-range dual-pin** (§6ad-166) and closes it → EXACT.

The `fr0` pin is a **colour-selection** lever, not a scheduling one: `fr4` and
`fr3` pins on the same variable are exactly score-neutral (96.63%). So when a
2-word residual is "the same constant, one different FPR", the question is not
"how do I reschedule it" but "which webs already claim the wanted register, and
can I name the constant onto it?".

### The dual-pin lever's PRECONDITION: both variables must be the SAME mode
Retried on `fn_800BE410` (the longest-standing "constant wants f11" park, whose
own note called `register __ps_t z/t __asm__("fr11")` the likely blocker): four
spellings of a block-scoped `register f32 k11 __asm__("fr11")` for the
`lbl_80298E8C` constant **all reproduce the documented 31.4% / 336 B miscompile
exactly** (the `lis`/`lfs` pair vanishes; cc1 emits `fadds f11,f1,f11`).
Diagnosis: the register is already claimed by a **DFmode** `__ps_t` pin, and
cc1 2.95's hard-register machinery then folds the SFmode load away. So an
exclusive-range dual-pin requires the **same mode on both variables** (f32+f32
works, __ps_t+f32 does not). Same round, `fn_8002DB10` (96.4%, "loop invariant
`lo` wants f11") resisted the lever for a different reason: the want's
`fmr f11,f10` is a **copy whose DESTINATION only** is in question, so pinning the
*name* makes the value live from the arm's entry and collapses the body to 27.0%
— a pin is the wrong shape when the residual is a register-to-register copy.

### fn_801F50B0 (216 B): the asm-`li` birth → plain store + `"+r"` barrier
Parked 90.7% with a `__asm__ volatile("li %0, 0" : "=r"(var_r27));` birth for a
plain 0. Replacing it with **`var_r27 = 0;` followed by
`__asm__("" : "+r"(var_r27));`** moved the `li` out of the entry block and scored
96.3% (the bare `li` alone, `"+r"` before/after the next statement, a volatile
barrier, and all four `": "r"(call_result)` input ties are 92.6%). Residual is a
1-word call-shadow slot (`bl; li; mr` vs `li; bl; mr`) — parked with the note.

### Negative results (measured corpus-wide this round — do not repeat)
* **Per-pin and pin-PAIR removal on the 55 drafts ≥80% with ≥2 r-pins: zero
  wins.** Including 0x801A71DC (99.0%, 7 pins), 0x80175690 (98.9%), 0x80033904
  (98.4%), 0x8011CF0C (98.1%), 0x8016F69C (97.9%), 0x800B6404 (97.8%). The
  remaining pin-removal wins are single instances (0x8021CEC0 `-r10/spv` +1.7,
  0x80181DA0 `-r27/a1` +0.5, 0x8004BEB0 `-r11/psx` +1.3), not a class.
* **`volatile double _dummy` ablation (130 drafts that carry one): max +2.9**
  (0x800CD150 61.9→64.8), nothing near EXACT — the dummy is a *frame* device, and
  removing it does what the frame says, not what the score says.
* **`fr`-register-pin ablation (147 drafts): only low-score drafts moved**
  (0x80257704 4.8→17.1 with 19 fr-pins removed). Scalar `f32` `__asm__("frN")`
  pins are load-bearing far more often than not.

## 6hk — 2026-10-07 (**1 promoted** (fn_8019D438), 9771 → **9772/11497** (84.996%), plus **97 parked drafts re-measured to a strictly better body** (72 flag refreshes, 25 `volatile` strips); DOL `cmp`+sha1+`ok` clean): **the FLAG AXIS is a first-class residual lever, not a last resort — and `volatile` in a draft body is usually stale scaffolding**

Two corpus-wide sweeps, both cheap and mechanical, both re-runnable:

* **Flag-matrix refresh** (`tools/flagrefresh.py`, then the extra_cflags-only
  twin in `<scratch>): for every draft carrying
  `// FLAG:` / `// extra_cflags:`, re-score the body against 16 *replacement*
  flag sets (only the *drop* had ever been tested). 432 + 157 drafts →
  **77 strict improvements**, including two ≥+16 and one **+53 gained earlier
  this round by another agent on `-Os`**.
* **`volatile` ablation** (new axis; `<scratch>):
  662 drafts carry the keyword (622 not counting `_dummy`). Stripping every
  `volatile` from a draft's body and keeping only strict improvements gave

### The rule: a stale flag can masquerade as "unreachable register allocation"

`fn_8019D438` had been parked three times as a **doc-15 arg-setup /
regalloc coin-flip** — "the two same-page (0x8030) global anchors r9/r11 are
assigned to the opposite globals… Tried: separate store, temp+comma, volatile
store, early temp, `+r` barrier, `-fno-schedule-insns(2)/-fno-sched-spec/
-fno-gcse`". It was 97.6 % with **no** flag line. Adding `-fno-schedule-insns`
flipped the load order *and* the anchor colours, giving a true byte-exact
match: at 0x8019D584 retail anchors the two same-page 0x8030 globals in r9 and r11 respectively, at 0x8019D58C it loads offset 0x3148 through the r9 anchor into r10 and offset 0x5EAC through the r11 anchor into r3, and at 0x8019D598 it stores r30 to offset 0x10 of the first loaded global.
(`reloc_diff.py` confirms every reloc symbol and every REL14/REL24 target, so
this is a real match, not a masked one.)

Lesson: **the flag axis is ORTHOGONAL to the source, and the previous round's
"flag sweep" only ever tested *replacing* a flag the draft already had.** A
draft with no `// FLAG:` line has never been flag-swept at all. Run the matrix
over the *high-score* band first: 88 drafts ≥95 % + 92 in 90–95 % produced
exactly the one flip above, and the low-score band is not worth the compiles.

### Pin RETARGET — the axis that was never run (2026-10-07)

Every pin sweep so far REMOVED a pin or tested pin pairs.  Nothing had ever
retargeted one: a hint pin's *register number* is a guess as often as not, and
the space is small (30 legal GPRs).  `retarget.py` keeps every pin, changes
ONE pin's register, and keeps strict improvements:

* 72 drafts (≥70 %, 1–2 pins) × 30 registers → **one win**, and it is a
  legitimate one: `fn_801F2AE0` `t9: r9 -> r8`, **91.06 % → 93.50 %** (492 B ==
  symbol, 8 masked words left, all in the r8..r11 rotation family).  Before
  believing it, check the pin's live window for a call: here it is obj
  0x150–0x164 and the nearest calls are 0x14c/0x180, so the caller-saved hint
  is not live across a call (a hard-reg variable live across a call is a real
  miscompile, not a hint).

**FPR pins: the same axis is the most productive one found this round.**
`retarget_fr.py` does the identical thing for `__asm__("frN")` hints (59 drafts
with 1–2 FPR pins, ~2 400 compiles) and returned **11 wins**, the best being
`fn_800FE42C` `zerof: fr31 -> fr22`, **31.77 % → 58.12 %**, and `fn_80258EAC`
`fmagic: fr11 -> fr26`, **13.08 % → 28.46 %**.  The common shape is an FPR
pinned to **fr31** (a *callee-saved* FPR): moving it to an ordinary FPR removes
a prologue `stfd`/epilogue `lfd` pair that retail does not have, and the whole
body re-colours around it.  Do this axis first on any draft that still carries
an `fr` pin.  The 3–4-pin drafts add 7 more (`fn_80164ABC` `inX: fr1 -> fr11`,
53.59 % → **64.71 %**; `fn_800C4B08` `lim: fr9 -> fr28`, 7.50 % → 18.07 %).

**MANDATORY check before accepting any retarget: did the draft LOSE
size-exactness?**  Score the reverted pin and compare both object lengths with
the symbol size.  `fn_801D17E4`'s `k29: fr29 -> fr1` looked like +3.1 %, but the
object went 508 B (== symbol) → 504 B, i.e. the gain was an alignment artifact
and the draft silently stopped being size-exact.  It was reverted.  The general
shape of the guard:

```
lb = len(compile(reverted body)); ln = len(compile(new body)); sym = symbol size
reject if (lb == sym and ln != sym)          # lost exactness
```

Where BOTH are non-exact (the normal case for low-score drafts) a length change
is harmless: `masked_pct` scores positionally over the WANT range, so a shorter
object cannot score higher, and a longer one only has its extra tail ignored.

**TRAP — a NEGATIVE can be a tool bug: the tail-capture trap.**  The first cut
of `retarget.py`'s pin regex ended at the `)` of `__asm__("frN")` and did not
capture the optional declaration tail.  Substitution therefore DELETED the
initialiser: `register f32 L __asm__("fr29") = arg0->len1;` became
`register f32 L __asm__("fr29");`, leaving `L` uninitialised and read on the
very next line.  That scores *higher* (it deletes the load), so it is the same
class of mirage as the r1/r2 pins — and it was reported as the ONE win for
`fn_800BB738`.  Both sweep tools now capture and re-emit `(\s*=\s*[^;]+)?;`
(GPR tool group 4, FPR tool group 5; the GPR tool then must unpack 4-tuples).
With the tail preserved the SAME retarget is a genuine (if small) win and is
applied: `fn_800BB738` `L: fr9 -> fr29`, **21.9780 % → 23.0769 %**, object
364 B == symbol 364 B (the false-positive variant was 340 B, i.e. NOT
size-exact — the size check alone would have caught it).  **Rule: a sweep's
first "win" on a file it also just rewrote is a suspicion, not a result —
re-measure the edited file from disk, and prefer a size-exact body.**

**TRAP — `r1`/`r2` pins make the score go UP while emitting garbage.**  The
first cut of the sweep reported `fn_801F2AE0 t9: r9 -> r1` as a +2.44 win; the
object contains `slwi r1, r30, 5`, i.e. it clobbers the stack pointer, and it
scores *higher* than the honest r8 variant.  `r2` is the RTOC.  **Exclude r1
and r2 from every pin sweep, and always verify a retarget win by checking that
the emitted code does not write r1/r2 outside the prologue/epilogue.**

**`__builtin_expect` DOES NOT EXIST in ngccc 3.9.3 — and "it compiled" is not
evidence that a builtin exists.**  `__builtin_expect(c, 0)` produces exit
status 0 and an object, so it looks supported, but `readelf -s` shows
`__builtin_expect` as an **UNDEFINED GLOBAL SYMBOL**: ProDG cc1 has no such
builtin and silently emits an ordinary call to a function of that name.  The
object can never link, and any local score change from it is the cost of the
call, not a block-placement effect (on `fn_801D2C58` two `__builtin_expect`
sites turned a masked-EXACT 316 B draft into 460 B / 0 %).  Before using any
GCC-3-era builtin here, compile a probe and check its symbol table for an UND
reference; only `__builtin_ps_*` (and the classic integer builtins) are real.
Also: capture compiler exit statuses *without* a pipe (`cmd > log; echo $?`) —
an earlier check of this builtin appeared to pass only because `$?` came from
`head` in the pipeline.

## 7j — 2026-10-08 (fn_8011FDD0 macro draft 402 insns / 28.2% LCS → pointer-local rewrite **405 insns / 34.0% LCS** of 421, then parked with 8 measured loop variants; fn_800AEBCC prologue made **byte-exact (insns 0-21)** and the first-call block shape-exact, 0.8% → 1.8% masked; DOL `cmp`+sha1+`ok` clean): **the audio/TU house idiom is `char *pX = base + FIXED_OFFSET` + a separate `s32 temp` byte offset — and a pointer local that stays live ACROSS A CALL is a callee-saved global that inflates `stmw`/the frame**

### The idiom (read it off a MATCHED sibling, not off the binary)

`src/fn_801210C4.c` is a promoted, byte-identical function that contains the
same "stop voice" block as the parked `fn_8011FDD0`, and it shows the original
idiom verbatim:

```c
    char *base;  char *p1;  char *p2;  char *p3;  s32 temp;  s32 irq;
    base = lbl_8038F0C0;          /* table base, once */
    temp = arg0 * 0x21C;           /* the stride offset, once */
    p1 = base + 0x20C;             /* one pointer per FIELD BASE ... */
    p2 = base + 0x218;
    *(s32 *)(p2 + temp) = 0;       /* ... and the offset is added at each use */
    if (*(s32 *)(p1 + temp) != 0) { ... }
    p3 = base + 0x28;
    *(s32 *)(p3 + temp) = (*(s32 *)(p3 + temp) + 1) & 7;
```

The equivalent offset-macro spelling (`*(s32 *)(lbl_8038F0C0 + (o) + 0x20C)`)
parses to the same expression tree but **does not** produce the same code:
ngccc folds a *different* constant into the base (got kept `base+0x20C` and
derived the other fields with `addi rN, r30, -0x1e4`; want derives them from
`base`). Measured on `fn_8011FDD0`: macro form 402 insns / 28.2 %
register+const-normalised LCS-norm of want; pointer-local form 405 insns /
34.0 %. **Before writing offset macros for a new table-walking function, grep
`src/fn_*.c` for a matched sibling of the same subsystem and copy its shape.**

### The trap: keep every pointer local SINGLE-BLOCK

A pointer local that is assigned before a call and read after it is live across
the call, so it needs a callee-saved GPR. Each one you introduce *lowers* the
lowest saved register and *grows the frame by 4 bytes* (plus 8 more once the
save-area size crosses the next alignment). Measured on `fn_8011FDD0`:

| | want | this draft (pointer locals live across the AX/memset calls) |
|---|---|---|
| `stmw` | `r22, 0x50(r1)` | `r18, 0x50(r1)` |
| frame | `0x78` | `0x88` |

The four extra were exactly the hoisted `base` / `p5 = base+0x210` /
`p6 = base+0xC` webs (r19 / r23 / r20). In want those fields are
re-materialised into VOLATILE registers just before each use (p5 appears as
r7, r10 and r9 inside one block). Fix: spell a field as a single-use expression
when its live range would cross a call; keep the pointer-local form only for
webs that die before the next call. NB: *moving* the assignments into the two
branches did **not** drop the count (still `stmw r18`) and cost 3 points —
the web has to stop being a named, long-lived value at all.
Counterpart of docs/parkings/76 (the same lever in the other direction: hoist
an operand into a local to *force* a saved register).

### Frame parity is a two-axis problem — check BOTH before tuning anything else

`fn_800AEBCC` (2860 B, 18 saved FPRs + `stmw r20`) was 8 B short AND had the
wrong GPR count. Reading the four prologue numbers off the compile is enough to
separate the axes (same recipe as docs/parkings/76): retail grows the stack by 0x1E0, saves f14 at offset 0x150, saves from r20 at offset 0x120, and spills r0 at 0x1E4, while the build grows by 0x1D8, saves f14 at 0x148, saves from r14 at 0x108, and spills r0 at 0x1DC.

* `stmw` register *number* → the saved-GPR set (fix by scoping/one-typed-pointer,
  not by dummies);
* every offset uniformly ±8 → the locals area (fix with one
  `volatile double _dummy;`).

Both fixes together made `fn_800AEBCC`'s prologue **byte-exact**
(`0x800AEBCC-0x800AEC20`, insns 0-21) and its first-call block match want
instruction for instruction apart from one arg0 colour — from a draft that was
0.8 %. Also: m2c's `var_r3` + `void *temp` + a cast per access produced THREE
copies of arg0 (`mr r30,r3` + `mr r31,r3` + r3) where want has ONE
(`mr r27,r3`); collapsing them to a single typed local view is worth doing
before anything else in a body that is still wrong.

### Two tooling notes that cost time this round

* `tools/disasm.py` and `tools/want_got.py` **stall at the first opcode-4
  (paired-single) word** and print `?` for everything after it — on
  `fn_800AEBCC` that is instruction 85 of 715, so the percentage they report is
  computed against 85 instructions and is meaningless. Use
  `tools/ps_diff.py <addr> <size> "<flags>" --all` (PS-aware, keeps the draft's
  FLAG line) and score structurally.
* `tools/test_wip_drafts.py`'s index-aligned masked percentage collapses as soon
  as one block is off by a single instruction, so a draft whose streams agree
  block-for-block still reads as low-single-digit DIFF. Normalise registers and
  constants, then run a `difflib.SequenceMatcher` over the two mnemonics
  (`LCS-norm`) — that number tracks real progress (it moved 28.2 → 34.0 % on
  `fn_8011FDD0` while the masked percentage moved 3.1 → 3.3 %).

### Loop-shape wall (unresolved, for the next agent)

`fn_8011FDD0`'s first divergence is its lookup loop: want runs the outer
`j = 0..7` loop as a **CTR loop** (`li r0,8 / mtctr r0 ... bdnz`) with the
`i == 0` slot PEELED (strength-reduced pointers `cmpw r4,r6` / `lwz r0,0(r3)`)
and the `i >= 1` cases in a ROTATED inner loop (`li r10,0` at the top,
`addi r10,r10,1 / cmplwi r10,2 / bgt` at the bottom). Eight source variants
(nested `i=1..2` with the `i==0` test first, single `for (i=0; i<3; i++)` with
`break`, the same with `idx != -1`, `i <= 2`, a `while` outer, and
`for (j < 8 && idx < 0)` / `&& idx == -1` fused conditions) all produced
387-405 insns and 33.0-35.9 % LCS — none reproduced it. That is a GCC 2.95
`loop.c` decision (doloop + rotation preconditions), so attack it from the
loop-optimizer side, not with more statement permutations.

## 7k — 2026-10-08 (**1 promoted** (fn_800DBAE4 0.0% → 100%), 9778 → **9779/11497** (85.06%) / 42.68 % of bytes; CScreenElement_SetPos 7.4% → **95.65% NEAR** parked with a size-exact 184 B object; DOL `cmp`+sha1+`ok` clean): **the shared `Unk_*` field-bag structs LIE about member types — an `s32`-declared member that is really `f32` turns the whole body into int↔float round trips (0 %, object 2-3× the symbol); the cheap detector is a MNEMONIC-MULTISET delta between want and draft**

**The bug class.** Every `Unk_XXXXXXXX` in `include/structs.h` is
m2c's merge of the *field accesses of several different functions* that happen to
share a base register, so a member's type is whatever the MAJORITY of those
functions did. When the bag declares `s32` a member that is really `f32`, every
access becomes an int↔float conversion (`fctiwz`/`stfd`/`lwz`, or
`xoris`/`lfd`/`fcfid`/`fsub` for the reverse), the object blows up, and the
masked score sits at **0-15 % even when the control flow and the statement order
are already perfect**:

| fn | symbol | object with the bag | object with a local f32 view | score before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fn_800DBAE4` | 144 B | ~230 B | 144 B | 0.0 % → **100 %** (promoted) |
| `CScreenElement_SetPos` | 184 B | ~380 B | 184 B | 7.4 % → **95.65 %** (parked) |
| `fn_800DC680` | 388 B | 596 B | 432 B | (bag fix alone: 8.25 % → 5.15 %) |

**Fix = a FILE-LOCAL view with the true types**, not a cast and not an edit to
the shared header. `fn_800DBAE4`'s `ObjDBAE4` (f32 at 0x40/44/48 and 70/74/78,
s32 flag @0x8C, f32 cached @0x90) and `CScreenElement_SetPos`'s `F32Pair`
(`char pad0x0[0x18]; f32 f18, f1C;` addressed at `arg0+0xD0` and `arg0+0x88`)
both make the object byte-length-exact on their own.

**Do NOT "fix" the bag itself — measured.** Flipping `Unk_C101CE15`'s
0x40/0x44/0x48/0x4C/0x70/0x74/0x78/0x90 from `s32` to `f32` (correct for the
0x800DBxxx family) makes `fn_800D03DC` and `fn_800D12DC` stop COMPILING —
they do `arg0->unk0x40 & 0x40000` and `arg0->unk0x90 | 0x80000000` on the same
members — and `fn_800DC680` regresses 8.25 % → 5.15 %. The bag is a union of
distinct object types; the per-file view is the honest fix.

**DETECTOR — mnemonic-multiset delta (`<scratch>; whole
1654-draft pool in ~4 min on 8 cores).** Compile each draft, decode want and got
(capstone + the PS-quad decoder from `tools/ps_disasm.py`), and print
`Counter(want) - Counter(got)` alongside the score:

* `{ lfs:+1 } | { lwz:+1 }` — the type bug above. Fixable, high yield.
* **ZERO delta** — every opcode is present, only operands/order differ. 322 of
  1654 drafts are in this state; these are the doc-15 scheduling/allocator coins
  (do not re-grind them without a new mechanism).
* smallest NONZERO deltas that are BRANCHES (`{bgt:+1}|{ble:+1}`,
  `{beq:+1}|{bne:+1}`, `{b:+1}|{beq:+1}`) — inverted arm order / CFG shape.

**`fabs` is an ngccc BUILTIN.** A bare `fabs(x)` with NO prototype (or
`__builtin_fabs`) emits the single `fabs fX,fX` the game uses; declaring
`f64 fabs(f64)` or `f32 fabsf(f32)` changes the codegen. The
`warning: type mismatch in implicit declaration for built-in function 'fabs'`
is expected and harmless — the whole `0x800DBxxx` family is written this way.

**Two more measured details from this round.**
* `volatile double` dummies COUNT: `CScreenElement_SetPos` needed TWO for its 0x30 frame
  (native 0x20; recipe 63's `(want-native)/8`). One dummy → 0x28 frame and five
  shifted frame words (69.6 %).
* `tools/promote_wip.py` re-compiles the body extracted from the **draft file in
  `src/wip/`**, so a body verified from a `/tmp` copy still gets
  `REFUSE ... draft is NOT byte-exact`. Copy the verified body into the draft
  first, then promote.

**one wrong instruction type or one wrong address/register that shifts
everything after it**, not a scheduler coin. Neither needed a new compiler flag;
both were pure C-source fixes.

  (recipe §7k).** fn_800CB68C's vtable-node `+0x8` is added to a pointer

      ((__ps_t *)dst)[0] = ((__ps_t *)src)[0];

### 7m-3 Switch-codegen levers (new, both measured on fn_800E426C)

1. **Unsigned switch subject.** With a *signed* subject ngccc's balanced tree tested
   `0x96896315` first (descending); the retail tree tests `0x2299A9F2` first, i.e.
   **unsigned ascending**.  Declaring the switch's value (`u32 arg1`) — not just
   `switch ((u32)expr)` — is what flips the compare tree into want's order.
   14.63 % → 73.81 % on its own.
2. **ONE shared result variable across all arms.**  Write
   `var_r3 = fn(...)` in every arm and a single `return var_r3;` — never
   `return fn(...)`.  This is what produces want's preloaded `li r3,1` + `bne` plus the
   `lwz r0`/`mr r3,r0` epilogue.  80.95 → **100 %**.

### 7m-4 `-da` — read ngccc's own RTL dumps (technique, 1 compile)

```
SN_NGC_PATH=$PWD/build/compilers/ProDG/3.9.3 \
  build/tools/wibo build/compilers/ProDG/3.9.3/ngccc.exe \
  -O2 -G0 -mcpu=750 -fno-common -I $PWD/include -da -c t.c -o t.o
```
writes `t.c<XXXX>.TMP.{addressof,bp,cse,gcse,loop,cse2,jump,flow,combine,regmove,sched,lreg,greg,flow2,mach,jump2,sched2}`.
Hard registers appear as `(reg:SI 22 r22)`; pseudos keep their numbers across passes, so
*grep each dump for the pseudo and take the first file that contains it* — that names the
pass that created it.  Insn chain order is `(insn N prev next …)`, so comparing `.lreg`
with `.mach` shows exactly what sched2 reordered.
* Worked example (fn_80096884, 99.08 % — 2 words): the shared pseudo `244` appears first
  in **`.gcse`** as `(insn 626 (set (reg:SI 244) (reg:SI 105)) REG_EQUAL (plus (reg 31) 56))`
  — global CSE inserts a copy so one value is available on entry to the late block, and
  then *both* the last call's arg0 and the store read it (`mr r3, r22` / `stw r22`).
  Wanted shape needs the call's arg0 to be its own single-use pseudo, so reload has no
  live register to copy from and rematerialises `addi r3, r1, 0x38`.  10 further variants
  measured and all worse (pin r22 at the store 95.39 %; pin used for both stores 3.69 %;
  r26 pin 1.84 %; unpinned `pm` assigned early 88.02 % — the pseudo's creation order moves
  `&L.mtx` off r26; assigned late 99.08 % — copy-propagated away; `(Mtx *)((char *)&L.basis + 0x30)`
  99.08 % — cse folds it back; through the live `pb`/`psc` variables 39.63 %).  Parked at
  99.08 % with that note — the remaining lever is on gcse's copy insertion, not on the body.

### 7m-8 Compare-operand reload pins: the sweeper's blind spot (positive recipe)

The doc-75 declaration pin also closes *reload register picks at compare operands*
— a site class `tools/reload_pin_sweep.py` cannot reach (its regex covers
`NAME = EXPR;` and first-arg call sites only, so it prints `none` for these).
Recipe: name the loaded value and pin **the value** (never the memory variable):

```c
    register s32 vw __asm__("r3");            /* function scope */
    ...
    if (GetChecksum_2(sp1C, QB_EXIT_STATE_ACTION, &sp20, 0) != 0) {
        vw = sp20;                            /* the reload, now homed r3 */
        if (vw == QB_WAIT_ANIM_FINISHED) {
```

and the same shape is the residual class on `fn_80062438` (93.10 %, latch reload
`lwz r10,8(r1)` vs want `r9`) and `fn_800A16B8` (98.70 %, `mr r3,r28` vs `r30`) —

the draft: a row whose differing words are all register renames is the *entry
point*, not the diagnosis — `fn_80123690`'s 3-word "rename" turned out to be a
swapped `subf` operand pair (`cap - h` vs `h - cap`, a real semantic bug).

On `fn_80062438` pinning the latch reload to r9 collapses the entry block

`base22 -> r9` pin drops 96.2 % -> 50.6 %. Apply pins ONE at a time and
re-measure: the sweep's per-pin numbers are NOT additive.

|---|---|---|

## 7n — 2026-10-09 (const-sweep: **4 promoted** — fn_800D512C (95.6→100), fn_8005E55C (89.5→100), fn_801A1B2C (90.0→100), fn_801C09A4 (24.3→100); DOL `cmp` clean after every one): **`extern const f32` on rodata float constants is a scheduler lever — it frees loads to sink past `f32 *` stores**

Mechanism: a plain `extern f32 lbl_X;` may alias any store through an `f32 *`
(and GCC 2.95.2 assumes it does), so constant loads are pinned above the
stores. `extern const f32` tells the compiler the store cannot alias the
constant, and sched2 is then free to sink the `lfs` to its use — which is what
retail did. The classic residual is a hoisted divisor/multiplier load:
want `lis ; fmuls ; lfs ; fmuls ; fdivs`, got `lis ; lfs ; fmuls ; fmuls ; fdivs`
(fn_800D5078's twin fn_800D512C, fn_801A1B2C's `li r0,0` vs `lfs` tie,
fn_8005E55C's 4-insn `mr/lfs/lfs/addi` window, fn_801C09A4's whole PS schedule).

decl, compile the draft as-is vs with `extern <t>` → `extern const <t>` (same
`draft_flags`, same dummy treatment) and diff the masked pct. Provisional
script: `<scratch> (promote to `tools/` + doc
if it earns a second run). 2026-10-09 full sweep: 665 drafts, 4 new EXACTs

## 7o — 2026-10-09 (fn_80056308 96.8→97.6): **a NAMED local defeats the `unsigned field > 0` tree-level range fold** (signed-compare polarity)

Symptom: want `lhz r9, 8(r4)` + `cmpwi r9, 0` + `ble` (i.e. `if (field > 0)` where the
field is a `u16`), got `... + beq`, and `if (field < 0)` compiles the block AWAY (GCC
knows the `lhz` result is non-negative). ngccc folds `(s32)u16field > 0` → `!= 0`
in `fold()` because the comparand is a *conversion from an unsigned type*; `volatile`
on the field does NOT stop it, and declaring the field/loading it as `s16` fixes the
branch but swaps `lhz` → `lha` (a wash).

Fix: route the halfword through a NAMED local of the *promoted* signed type first:

```c
    s32 u8v;                       /* declared with the other locals */
    ...
    u8v = ((Cell *) temp_r4)->unk8;   /* lhz + zero-extend, in its own stmt */
    if (u8v > 0) { ... }              /* stays a SIGNED `> 0` -> cmpwi/ble */
```

With a VAR_DECL on the left of `>`, the folder can no longer see the unsigned
conversion, so the signed `> 0` survives; the load stays `lhz` and reload coalesces
the local straight into the same register (byte-identical everywhere else).
Generalisable to any draft whose only diff is a branch polarity/kind on a
sub-word or unsigned field: try `<named s32 local> = <field>;` + the original
relational spelling before touching flags. (Same family as §7m's warning: check the
mnemonic before assuming a schedule wall — `beq` vs `ble` is a C fix, not sched2.)

Residual after the fix (parked at 97.6%): 3 words of `fn_80102A40` arg setup where
the want sinks `add r3, r3, r31` to last-before-`bl` and we sink it 4th. Eight
arg1 spellings (own local sum, base-pointer local, `(s32)` cast, `[]` indexing,
`(s32)off`, no cast, `*(s32*)arg4`) are all byte-identical to each other → the
order is below the AST (pre-sched emission order / sched2 priority); needs an
`ngccc -da` .rtl/.mach diff, not more permutation.

**NOT A NEW LEVER.** This is the rule of `docs/parkings/solved/09-init-struct-store-order.md`
(ADDENDUM 2026-09-17: "a run of independent stores to the *same base* is emitted
rotated right by one (last store first), so write it rotated left by one" — proved on
`fn_800F3598`), already carried in this file as §4p-24 / §6k-64 / §6an-198, and refined
there by "store-run rotation is per STORE CLASS, not per run" (fn_80121CD0: four
zero-stores rotated inside a six-store run whose two data stores stayed put). Read those
FIRST; `grep -i rotat AGENTS-recipes.md` before any park that says "the source cannot
express this".

Symptom: a 12-statement reset block (6 stores through `base`/r30 + 5 through
`temp_r9 = base+1` + the 0xC word store) sat at 44/46 words for a week, with a
parked note claiming "both stores are independent same-base byte writes, so this
is an allocator/scheduler tie the source cannot express". That note is exactly
the verdict doc 09's 2026-09-17 addendum already falsifies.

What THIS case adds beyond doc 09 / §24/§64/§198 (all measured here):
- TWO runs plus a data-register split. The `temp_r9` run (offsets 2-6) must be
  written ASCENDING so it rotates into want's `6,2,3,4,5`; the r11 0xFF pair is
  its own STORE CLASS, so its two members rotate against each other (source
  `8,7` → emitted `7,8`) — matching §198's "per class, not per run". The 0xC
  word store has to be moved to the HEAD of its r30 group as well.
- Hill-climbing is UNRELIABLE for this class.* From the draft order every single
  swap/move/3-cycle is non-improving (95.65% is a steep local optimum), so
  permuting the existing block never escapes. What worked: probes in isolation
  (`p[7]=0xFF; p[8]=0xFF;` → `stb 8; stb 7`, i.e. one class; `p[7]=0xFF;
  p[8]=0;` → 7,8, source order — two classes) then an EXHAUSTIVE sweep of the
  r30 group (7! = 5040) with the r9 run held ascending. 24 of the 5040 hit 100%,
  all with the ascending tail — that is the load-bearing half.
- *Gotcha that invalidated the first "100%": `gen_leaves.compile_fn` derives its
  scratch filename from the ADDRESS alone, so 8 parallel `Pool` workers on one
  `LEAF_TMPDIR` race on one `.c`/`.o` pair and a worker reads another's
  half-written object — that produced a bogus 100% plus `ELFParseError` /
  wibo `TimeoutExpired` noise. Use per-candidate unique filenames (name hash) or
  at minimum a per-worker `LEAF_TMPDIR`; and re-verify any surprise EXACT.

Verification habit worth repeating: a masked-EXACT hides the branch fields, so
before trusting one, read the reloc addends — here all 8 masked words were
REL14/REL24 placeholders whose addends (`0x3c,0x34,0x20,0x9c,0x94,0x80`) resolve
to exactly the DOL's displacements (`0x20,0x0C,0xFFE8,0x20,0x0C,0xFFE8`).

Stale-ref note: this match makes WIP.md's "Parked with best-match bodies" entry
for fn_80244924 false, and PROGRESS.md's `auto_01_80244924_text` unit stale
(needs the documented report regen).
[5,1,2,3,4]. And the 0xC word store has to be moved to the HEAD of the r30 group
(not where m2c put it) so it emits first.

```c
    arg0->unk0xC = 0;                 /* word store FIRST of the group */
    temp_r9 = (char *)arg0 + 1;
    *(u8 *)((char *)arg0 + (s32)0x8) = 0xFF;   /* note: 8 before 7 — see below */
    *(u8 *)((char *)arg0 + (s32)0x7) = 0xFF;
    *(u8 *)((char *)arg0 + (s32)0xA) = 0;
    *(u8 *)((char *)arg0 + (s32)0x9) = 0;
    *(u8 *)((char *)arg0 + (s32)0x1) = 0;
    *(u8 *)((char *)temp_r9 + (s32)0x1) = 0;   /* ascending run */
    *(u8 *)((char *)temp_r9 + (s32)0x2) = 0;
    *(u8 *)((char *)temp_r9 + (s32)0x3) = 0;
    *(u8 *)((char *)temp_r9 + (s32)0x4) = 0;
    *(u8 *)((char *)temp_r9 + (s32)0x5) = 0;
```

Verification habit worth repeating (above): a masked-EXACT hides the branch
fields, so read the reloc addends before trusting one — all 8 masked words here
were REL14/REL24 placeholders whose addends resolve to exactly the DOL's
displacements.
