## 2FE8 family: `<=`-returns valueisation, eager-sub anti-fold, float-up copy + barrier + pin

(Matched fn_801D2FE8, 2026-10-15. Three independent rules.)

**R1 — `if (a <= b) return 1; return 0;` NEVER emits a branch on ngccc/3.9.3.**
Verified in isolation: `<=`-with-returns always valueises to
`fcmpu cr7 + cror + mfcr + clrlwi + blr` (boolean in r3), while
`if (a > b) return 0; return 1;` branches cleanly
(`fcmpu cr0 + li + bgt + li`). So a want with `fcmpu; ble; li; b` cannot come
from a plain `<=` source. The exact shape is `if (!(a > b))` (the `!` survives
to RTL and selects the `ble` branch sense) plus `goto`-shared tails: the true
arm must `goto` an out-of-line shared `ret1: return 1;` (a plain `return 1`
keeps `li r3,1` inline before the branch). If the want instead shows
`fcmpu; cror; bso`, that is the same condition with the fcmp/branch split
across blocks (precomputed CR bit) — keep them adjacent.

**R2 — eager sub-pointer defeats combine folding across blocks.** Want keeps
`addi r11,r9,0x24` in the entry block with its `lwz 0x2c(r11)` three blocks
down; computing the sub-pointer inside the use block fuses to one
`lwz 0x50(r9)`. Assign the sub-pointer eagerly at the top (`sub = state+0x24`)
and combine cannot reach across the branches. (Same reason the two loads stay
separate.)

**R3 — float-up arg copy: named copy BEFORE last use + empty `+r` barrier +
pin.** A `mr r8,r11` staged call-arg copy sitting mid-block (between two uses
of the source) comes from a named `arg1v = vec;` copy placed in source BEFORE
the last vec use (sched floats the long-lived copy up; placed after, it
coalesces away), plus an empty `__asm__ volatile ("" : "+r"(vec))` between
copy and last use so copyprop cannot forward the copy into the later use
(without it the 2nd load reads the copy's reg). The barrier splits the
source's live range and can flip colours, so a `register __asm__("rN")` pin on
the OTHER pointer (here cblk→r10) holds the map: pinned reg taken early,
source reuses the dead reg. All emit zero instructions. A pin on the copied
var itself is wrong (reserves the reg function-wide and coalesces the copy).

## DEB4 family: guarded-preheader invariants, plain loop floats, scalar-union spill

(Matched fn_8005DEB4, 2026-10-16 — PS min-tracking loop, same arith chain as
src/fn_801EF3A8.c. Three independent rules.)

**R1 — back-edge target diagnoses hoisted invariants.** When the loop latch
branches past the loop-top setup straight to the first call, the setup
(pool load + address formation) executes once in the guarded preheader, not
per iteration. Writing it as loop-body-top statements keeps it in the loop
and costs an extra saved GPR (here `stmw r24` vs want's `stmw r25`, plus
swapped loop-top use order). Move the invariant statements above the `do` but
inside the entry guard (`if (bestid < count) { thresh=...; k=...; do {...} }`)
and the back edge, frame, and loop-top all fall into place at once.

**R2 — plain loop-live floats beat pins AND pads for the frame.** A `f32`
that is live across calls naturally lands in a saved FPR (here best→f31,
thresh→f30) with its dead stack home sizing the frame (here 0x50). Pinning
it (`register __asm__("fr30")`) removes the home and shrinks the frame;
volatile pads / extra unions sort before the spill slot and move it. If the
frame is too small AND the spill offset too low, try deleting the pins
before adding anything.

**R3 — scalar `SN_PS_type` promotes to DI and emits the spill+fmr pair.**
`res.ps = v; x = res.flt.hi;` on a scalar union goes through a 64-bit pseudo
with subreg accesses: after reload that is exactly a stack spill plus a
`lfs`-into-one-reg / `fmr`-into-the-compare-reg copy. The same code through a
struct member (or any MEM-shaped lvalue) compiles to a direct spill load
with no `fmr`. So a missing `fmr`-after-reload means the result holder must
be a scalar union, not a struct field — and the struct/union/array pads used
to size the frame will actively break it (they sort before the spill slot).

## Tiny-int harvest: volatile dead-slots, SPR writes, vcall thunks

(Eleven matches 2026-10-16 from `tools/find_int_fns.py`'s pure-integer list:
fn_8022004C/8013F6E4/8025D944/8025D964/8013F708/80058684/80070BA8/8005F100/
8005C2B8/8005C3A0/8005F148. Three recipes.)

**R1 — stray `stw rX,8(r1)` in a tiny frame is a volatile dead slot.** A
`li`/`mr`-fed store to the stack slot with no matching load is a
`volatile s32 t = <init>;` whose value is never read — the real effect is
the neighbouring field store. Delete the volatile and the frame shrinks
(`stw` disappears); keep it and the function matches (8022004C, 8013F6E4).
Same shape with a boolean tail: load the field into a named local BEFORE
the volatile init so the `lwz` leads and the `r = 1` binds r3 (8013F708:
`lwz; li; stw; li r3,1; andi.; bne; li r3,0; xori`).

**R2 — `li/stw/lwz/mtspr/isync` is volatile-home + pinned-r3 SPR write.**
The constant is a `volatile u32` homed on the stack; the `mtspr` input must
be a `register __asm__("r3")` copy (`rv = t`), otherwise the reload lands
in r9. The `isync` is a second empty `__asm__ volatile`. (8025D944 with 0,
8025D964 with 0xCC00601E, SPR 0x3F5.)

**R3 — vcall-thunk skeleton with this-adjust and spilled value.** Family
shape: `lwz rX,0(rA); lwz r9,OFF(r3); addi rB,r1,8; stw rX,8(r1); lha
off,OFF2(r9); lwz fn,OFF2+4(r9); add r3,r3,off; mtlr; blrl`, i.e.
`v = *argN; t = arg0->fld; fn(arg0 + t->off, &v)` with
`typedef void (*VFn)(void *, s32 *)` (or wider for multi-arg forwarders).
Pass-through args need NO setup (already in regs): declare them as `s32`
dummies and forward them, so only r3 and the slot reg are formed
(8005C2B8/8005C3A0/8005F148). A `crclr cr1eq` before the `blrl` means the
indirect call must be unprototyped (`((f64 (*)())fn)(...)`, 8005F100:
prototyped typedefs drop the word). Post-call stores (`*(s32 *)arg0 = 0/1`)
are plain statements after the call (80058684/80070BA8).

## 6bz-2 — 2026-10-20 (fn_800CB5B0, 96.4% → EXACT + PROMOTED): twin-transferred
or. + input-only-barrier global-alloc priority fix
Two transferable mechanisms. (1) TEST-AFTER-COPY lowers to `or.`: a null test
on a directly-loaded pointer stays `cmpwi`, but split the next-pointer into a
fresh local (`c = p->next; if (c->s == -1) c = NULL; p = c`) and the back test
on post-copy `p` combines to `or. rX,rX,rX` with the copy coalesced away (no
extra `mr`). Shapes verified in promoted twins fn_800CBEC0/fn_800CC268
(do-while+outer-if, entry `b check`) and fn_800A5E8C (`while (n != NULL)`).
A do-while+outer-if entry does NOT transfer when the body joins forward
(break/goto to a shared call): the outer test persists as cmpwi/beq — the
goto + c-split form keeps the twin CFG with zero extra tests. The `c = p`
init before `goto check` is load-bearing (without it the prologue reload
miscompiles). (2) INPUT-ONLY volatile barrier as zero-byte priority weight:
`__asm__ volatile("" :: "r"(x))` adds one global-alloc USE to x with no output
copy (no web split, unlike `+r`), verified via `.greg` dumps (`82 in 30 ...
93 in 31`): a copy-prop'd load robbed the alias of its 4th use, flipping the
82/93 priority hair and the r30/r31 assignment; the barrier restored the use
count (3→4) and the coloring with zero emitted bytes. Diagnose coloring ties
with `cc1 -da` (run with cwd=/tmp — dumps spray `fn_*.TMP` files into cwd)
and read the `N in H` disposition + `regs to allocate` order lines.

## 6ca-1 — 2026-10-20 (fn_80220C0C): the MASKED score hides a wrong SYMBOL, not just
addresses — a 97.9% draft whose only residual was a mis-named `lbl_`
`gen_leaves.compile_fn` masks ADDR16_HA and ADDR16_LO at the consuming
instruction, so a draft that references `lbl_802AFEA4` while retail references
`lbl_802AFE9C` scores 100% masked: the immediate is never compared. The real
tell is the LINK: `promote_wip.py` reports a one-word difference at the
`addi rX,rY,imm` (`3884fea4` built vs `3884fe9c` want) and refuses. So for any
draft that reaches near-100% masked, do not trust the mask — either promote it
(the tool reverts on mismatch and leaves the draft in place) or decode the
`lis`/`addi` immediates by hand against `config/G2TE52/symbols.txt`. Here the
draft had silently landed on the neighbouring 5-byte string in `.rodata2`;
renaming it to the symbol retail actually points at turned a "97.9%" into a
link-identical match. The same trap applies to the two lbl-PAIR forms: a
draft can be off by one `.rodata2` slot and still read as exact.
Also from this function: a record-pointer ALIAS (`wp = q`, with `q` a
`register ... __asm__("rN")` pin) taken before an intervening call makes cc1
pass the alias in the arg register; moving the alias assignment AFTER the call
makes it pass the pinned pointer itself (`mr r4,r30` vs `mr r4,r29`) — a
one-word residual that no flag touched.

### 6cb — the sched-flag sweep on near-miss drafts (2026-10-20)

A draft parked at "95–99%, pure instruction permutation, no flag helps" can
still be EXACT under a scheduling flag — but only when its CURRENT body is
measured with that flag. `fn_80101AE0` sat at 95.0% (2-word residual) with a
header note reading "-fno-schedule-insns{,-2} make it worse (70%/62.5%)";
those numbers were taken on an OLDER body. On the current body
`-fno-schedule-insns` is byte-exact. Rule: **re-measure the flag ladder after
every body change; a stale measurement in a draft header is not evidence.**

Also record what the ladder does NOT buy: a full corpus sweep
(1572 drafts × {-fno-schedule-insns, -fno-schedule-insns2, both}) found
exactly one draft flipped to EXACT, and no draft reached 0–1 words under any
flag other than that one. So the flag lever is worth one cheap pass per
candidate body, not a rescue for the permutation band.

Practical form of the sweep (per candidate, ~1 s each):

    tools/venv/bin/python tools/want_got.py 0xADDR [-fno-schedule-insns|…]

which respects the draft's own `// FLAG:` line and appends the CLI flags.
Two related things that did NOT help across the same corpus: 8 further
`-fno-*` flags layered on the best sched flag (no draft moved below its
2-word floor), and stripping a stale `// FLAG:` line on its own.

### 6cc — three one-shot source levers that turned 93–96% drafts into matches
(2026-10-20; each was the ONLY residual of its draft)

1. **Doubled member read → CSE temp + arg copy (`fn_80184558`).** A chain walk
   that passes the loaded value to a call compiled `lwz r4,0(p)` — the load
   coalesced straight into the arg register, one word short of retail's
   `lwz r0,0(p)` + `mr r4,r0`. Writing the read TWICE (once in the exit test,
   once as the call argument) makes CSE own the load in a scratch register
   whose only two uses are the compare and the arg copy, which is exactly the
   retail shape. A single `v = *p;` local coalesces again.

2. **Real globals instead of a `(char *)0x80xxxxxx` base + `__asm__` birth
   barrier (`fn_80126310`).** A draft that hand-built a `.bss` base and pinned
   each `lis` with an empty-asm barrier kept the argument `lis` and the store
   base `lis` in the wrong order (83%). Plain `lbl_X = Mem_Alloc(...)` with
   the symbols declared at their real types is byte-exact — the barrier form
   was the only reason the order was wrong.

3. **`register ... __asm__("rN")` pin on a value cc1 colours into r0
   (`fn_8023A6F4`).** `lim = arg1->cols; while (col < lim)` loaded the byte
   into r0 and compared `cmpw rX,r0`; retail loads it into r9. Pinning the
   local (`register s32 lim __asm__("r9")`) fixes both words and nothing else
   moves. This is the cheapest lever for a residual that is a lone register
   name on a single load/compare pair — try it before restructuring.

## 6ca-2 — 2026-10-20: **the 93–99% band is exhausted under flags; three 2-word wall shapes named**

A 16-flag × 49-draft sweep (every draft whose best size-exact score is 93–99 %,
each flag added on top of the draft's own `// FLAG:` line: `-O3 -Os -fno-inline
-fno-strength-reduce -fno-cse-follow-jumps -fno-gcse -fno-schedule-insns{,2}
-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop -fno-expensive-optimizations -fno-delayed-branch
-fno-peephole -fno-thread-jumps -fno-loop-optimize -funroll-loops`) produced
**zero** improvement anywhere: every draft stayed at its own best or worse, and
the only 100 % cell was the known masked-EXACT/unpromotable `fn_8013928C`
(wrong branch targets — see its header). Don't re-run this sweep; the residual
in this band is not flag-selectable.

The band's residuals reduce to three shapes, all measured:

1. **Adjacent independent insns emitted in the other order** (`li`/`lis` vs
   `mr`/`mcrf`/`addi`, stores to two different fields, `cmpwi` vs the value
   materialisation). One instruction of the pair comes from a fixup/hoist
   pass, whose insertion point is fixed relative to the block — so source
   reordering moves the *other* instruction around it but cannot get past the
   hoisted one. Examples: `fn_801F5A0C` (`mcrf cr4,cr0` always ends the
   preheader block; init-order/for-init/statement forms all keep it last),
   `fn_800CC358` (`cmpwi`/`li r3` if-conversion pair), `fn_8002CDE4`
   (`stb`/`stw`), `fn_801F6EC8` (`cmpwi cr4`/`li`).
2. **Lone register name on one load/compare pair** — solvable with a
   `register s32 x __asm__("rN")` pin (recipe 6ca-1 #3) when the pin does not
   re-seed a longer cascade; unsolvable when it does (pin the value, not the
   pointer).
3. **Address-operand slot order** (`lwzx rD,rA,rB` with the scaled index in rA
   in retail vs rB in the build). §6au-200's offset-first `(char*)(off +
   (s32)p)` works for `stwx` but **does not reach `lwzx`**: cc1 canonicalises
   the PLUS back to base-first, so the index stays in rB and lands in r0
   (`fn_8008144C`, where the r0-vs-r8 choice is a *consequence* of the slot
   order, not an independent diff). Any spelling that puts the index in rA
   also has to keep the index in a real GPR, which no C form here does.

## 6fx — Constant-group store rotation: what decides the order of a run of stores to distinct fields

Measured on a member-init body (15 stores of four distinct constants to
`this+0x00..0x38`, no calls, no aliasing): ngccc emits the stores **grouped by
constant value** (all `-1` stores, then all `0` stores, ...) and, inside each
group, **rotated right by one relative to source order** — the group's *last*
source store is emitted first. Two independent groups on the same body each
rotated exactly once, and swapping two statements inside a group moved the
rotation with them, so the rule is per-group, not per-block.

Consequences when chasing such a residual:

* If the reference stream *interleaves* two constant groups (e.g. `-1` fields
  at +0x2C/+0x30 early and a third `-1` field in the middle of the zero run),
  the reference did not share one constant web across all of them. Sharing is
  restored by CSE of the constant, so lexical variants (`-1`, `~0`,
  `0xFFFFFFFF`, a named `s32 neg1`) are no lever — all CSE back. What is needed
  is a real second value, e.g. a field whose type is unsigned so the constant's
  mode differs, or a genuine block boundary between the uses.
* Rotating the source order inside a group is a cheap, *principled* correction:
  to obtain reference order `[a,b,c]`, write `[b,c,a]`. One test per group beats
  permuting the whole list (which lands at the same score from every direction,
  since any permutation still groups and still rotates).
* A fully rotated but still-grouped body scores high (90 %+) with only the
  interleaving words wrong, which reads like a register-allocation diff at a
  glance — check whether the differing words are stores of *different constants*
  before spending rounds on pins.

## 6fy — Two volatile stores to distinct globals are still reordered by ngccc

On an MMIO poll body, hoisting both hardware reads and both adjustments into
locals (`cur = CD04 + 0x400; cnt = CD08; CD04 = cur; CD08 = cnt - 1;`) reproduces
a reference stream of load/load/add/add/store/store exactly, but the final store
pair comes out in the **opposite** order and nothing in the source changes that:
writing the two stores the other way round collapses the schedule back to
load/add/store pairs (82.9 %), and per-store temps, compound assignment, folded
constants, and both declaration orders all reproduce the same swapped tail. So
GCC 2.95's `sched2` does not treat volatile stores as an ordered chain — do not
assume "volatile ⇒ source order" when reading a two-store residual.

## 6fz — A zero-code `+r` barrier pins WHICH insn materialises a folded address

Measured twice (fn_8001593C 86.7 % → 93.3 %, and the same 4-word fix on a
second body): when a source statement computes an intermediate base that the
compiler later folds into an address sum, the folded form usually disappears and
the *sum* is emitted at the later point, so the emitted order of the shift and
the base add is the opposite of retail's.

```c
recs = (char *)temp_r3 + 4;          /* the +4 gets folded away ... */
temp_r9 = (Unk *) (recs + (arg0 << 5));
```
```c
recs = (char *)temp_r3 + 4;
__asm__("" : "+r"(recs));            /* ... until this forces it into a reg */
temp_r9 = (Unk *) (recs + (arg0 << 5));
```

The barrier emits nothing but keeps `recs` in a register across the statement, so
`addi rD,rS,4` appears where the source wrote it and the following `slwi`/`add`
keep retail's order. Four words flip, score 86.7 % → 93.3 %.

Notes:
* It must be the operand form (`"+r"`), not a memory clobber, and it must sit
  immediately after the assignment whose value you want materialised.
* Same lever applies to any intermediate that retail materialises into its own
  register (pointer+constant, index<<N, masked field): give it a name, then
  barrier it.
* It does NOT help once the residual is a store vs compare pair in the same
  block — that stays a scheduler tie (see §6fy).

## 7r — 2026-10-21: **four global axes re-swept over the whole near-miss set — all NEGATIVE** (one new match, `Tmr_GetTime`, from re-deriving an unsourced function, not from a sweep)

The 172 drafts at ≥88% (and, for the flagless axis, all 285 non-PS drafts
carrying a `// FLAG:` line) were re-scored on axes that had not been run
globally. Nothing flipped to EXACT except the already-known `0x8013928C`
(refused by `promote_wip` on branch targets).

| axis | scope | result |
|---|---|---|
| `-mcpu=7400 / 604 / 603` | 172 drafts ≥88% | 0 new EXACT; a few DIFF→NEAR shuffles, no near-miss improved its diff *count* |
| `-mps-float` on non-PS bodies | 172 | 0 new EXACT |
| `-fno-defer-pop` (arg-setup walls) | 172 | 0 new EXACT |
| flags STRIPPED from flagged drafts | 285 | 0 new EXACT — every `// FLAG:` line is load-bearing |
| ProDG 3.5 / 3.5b140 / 3.7 / 3.8.1 vs 3.9.3 | 681 runs | identical objects on the near-miss set |

So `-mcpu` (the sched2 cost model) and the compiler version do NOT decide the
§7m-9 adjacent-independent-move class: a cost-model change would have to
reshuffle the whole function, and the objects come out byte-identical instead.
A full re-sweep of all 1563 drafts also reproduced the old census exactly
(1 EXACT, 486 NEAR, ~1013 DIFF, 15 FAIL), i.e. no draft was left unscored by
the earlier passes. The FAILs are almost all `family=gx` drafts whose bodies use
mwcc intrinsics (`__rlwimi`) and therefore cannot be scored by the ngccc
harness at all — they need the mwcc zone, not a fix.

Where the remaining near-misses actually are: 45 drafts sit at exactly two
differing words with an exact size, and every one that was re-audited falls in
one of three already-documented boxes — §7m-9 move order, the doc-15 register
coin flip (`f0` vs `f12`, `r3` vs `r6`), or a store-run rotation. Re-deriving
the C is the only lever that still pays; three of this session's matches
(`fn_8004E734`, `fn_8004F6B8`, `Tmr_GetTime`) came from corrected *semantics*
(signedness, missing local, name-vs-literal address form), not from tie-breaks.

Concrete finding worth reusing: an int difference converted to float must come
from **u32** locals when retail's pool constant is `0x4330000000000000`
(`Tmr_GetTime`). With `s32` locals ngccc picks the `0x4330000080000000` magic
plus a `xoris` fixup and the object grows a word; the magic word is the
cheapest read of the source's signedness, and the same test says `(u32)` vs
`(s32)` on the float→int cast (the 2^31 range check only appears for unsigned).

**New lever that paid (fn_80239924, 87.8% → EXACT): stack slots in the wrong
order → make them ONE frame object.** When two locals' displacements are
swapped (every reference off by a constant, or two adjacent slots exchanged),
declare a single struct whose field offsets reproduce the want's layout
(`{ s32 out; Pay8 pl; }` with `pl` 8-aligned put the out-param at +0 and the
descriptor at +8 — arithmetic, no allocation decision left to make) and, for
the field whose ADDRESS the code needs, keep a named pointer (`Pay8 *pl =
&fr.pl`) so the address lands in a register the way the want reuses it.
Two things that did NOT work and can be skipped: making one of the two locals
merely `double`-sized or 8-aligned (slot order follows first reference, so
the first-stored local keeps the low slot either way — measured on
`fn_80239924` as three separate 6-diff variants), and *touching* the other
local first with a dead store to grab the low slot (`-fno-expensive-
optimizations` keeps the store, 43 diffs; without that flag the slot is still
allocated but the frame/copy shape changes).

## 7s — 2026-10-21: **the two-word NEAR floor is scheduler/lalloc, and it survives a mechanical source search** (1 promoted: `fn_80087010` 95.7 → 100 by one adjacent statement swap)

The 41 drafts at exactly TWO differing words (≥90%) were run through a
mechanical search harness (compile → reloc-masked score → keep the best
variant). Exactly one lever produced anything on any of them:

| lever | scope | result |
|---|---|---|
| adjacent statement transposition, at EVERY brace depth, greedy over 4 rounds | 74 drafts ≥95% | **1 EXACT** (`fn_80087010`: swapping `col.a = 0xFF;` after the `col.r` line) |
| contiguous run reversal (3..6 statements, every brace) | 41 drafts at 2 diffs | 0 |
| declaration order (each local to front / to end / adjacent swap) | 41 | 0 |
| scalar type flip (`s32↔u32`, `s8↔u8`, `s16↔u16`) decl-only and decl+uses | 41 | 0 |
| `volatile` removal | 41 | 0 |
| frame pads `volatile u8[N]` N=4..72 step 4 and `volatile double[M]` M=1..9 | 192 drafts ≥85% | 0 |
| 30 single `-f` flags + 6 `-m` codegen flags (`-mno-multiple`, `-mmultiple`, `-mno-string`, `-mstring`, `-mno-powerpc-gfxopt`, `-mno-fused-madd`) | 41 | 0 |
| `-frename-registers`, `-fschedule-insns`, `-fcaller-saves`, `-frerun-loop-opt` (enable side) | 41 | 0 |

So statement transposition is still the one cheap lever worth running on a new
draft (it is what closed `fn_80087010`), but the residual of the two-word class
is NOT a source-order choice: the two words are either an adjacent
independent-instruction pair inside ONE statement's expansion (call-argument
birth order, shift/mask fold, FPR home) or a callee-saved colouring tie. Both
are decided after reload, which is why declaration order, types, pads and the
whole flag space leave them untouched. One consequence worth remembering: a
diff-word *count* is not a difficulty measure — the 2-word drafts are the
hardest per-word population in the tree, while a 12-word draft can still be a
mis-typed struct member (see §7k / §7l).

Reading the diff words by hand pays off where the automated pass cannot: the
`cls` heuristic that guesses "immediate vs register" must mask the RT/RA
fields (D-form imm is word & 0xFFFF, not word >> 16) or every register rename
in a load/store is mis-reported as an immediate mismatch, and op-31 X-form
words (cmpw, rlwinm, and, or) carry their fields in the low 11 bits.

## 7t — 2026-10-21: **a zero-code statement barrier is the missing lever for the adjacent-independent-pair class** (2 promoted from 41 two-word drafts: `fn_8001593C` 93.3 → 100, `fn_8015D174` 96.5 → 100)

Doc 15 already recorded this for single drafts; it is worth running MECHANICALLY
over every near miss. Insert one of

```c
__asm__ volatile("");                 /* empty: no memory clobber */
__asm__ volatile("" ::: "memory");    /* memory clobber */
```

at each statement boundary of each brace region (before the first statement and
between every adjacent pair, one insertion at a time) and re-score. On the 41
drafts at exactly two differing words this closed two, both of which had
exhausted flags, types, declaration order and statement transposition:

- `fn_8001593C`: the empty form, between the `pool + 4` pointer birth and the
  out-param store that follows it (the store was being hoisted above the
  pointer).
- `fn_8015D174`: the memory-clobber form, on the constant birth between the
  count loop and the `GetChecksum_2` call (the r4 OR-immediate was landing
  before the r6 `li`).

Both are zero-instruction statements, so they are invisible in the object and
cost nothing at run time — they only pin the RTL order the scheduler sees.

**Do not trust the masked 100% at a relocation site.** The same sweep scored
`fn_8002CDE4` at masked 100% with a memory clobber between the callback
dispatch and the reset store run, and `promote_wip` refused it: the barrier
re-lays the block so the `+0x10` test's `bne` gets a different target, and the
reloc-masked word hid the difference (the refusal reports
`0x8002ce04 want None got ('bne', ...)`). Branch-target verification is not
optional — a masked 100% is a *screening* result, never a match.

## 6fx — Separate zero-stores to one object emit in REVERSE statement order (the `cmpwi; stw; beq` window is source order, not delay slots)

fn_80137F30 carried a long-standing "delay-slot filler / scheduler tie" park note
for a two-word residual: retail emits `cmpwi r5,0 ; stw r0,0x10(r31) ; beq`
(the second zero-store sitting between the compare and the branch), and every
source ordering tried produced `stw ; cmpwi`. It is not a scheduling decision.
When two fields of the same object are zeroed before a branch on a parameter,
**ngccc emits the two stores in reverse statement order**, so writing the
*later-address* store first puts it last in the block — after the compare, in
retail's position. For fn_80137F30 that is `arg0->unk0x10 = 0;` written before
`arg0->unk0x4 = 0;`. 95.74%, and the residual drops to an unrelated move tie
(arg4 spill vs arg5 home copy); the same body no longer needs the two asm
barriers the old draft used.

The shape was recovered by mining a matched sibling rather than by trying more
orders: `src/fn_80137E30.c` is the same function with `+0xC` instead of `+0x10`,
and its promoted source shows the reversed store order explicitly. Trigger: a
parked draft needs `[cmp*][store][branch]` and keeps getting
`[store][cmp*][branch]`; look for a matched function with the same field-clear
pair before reaching for flags or barriers. Corollary already in §4p-1 still
holds in general (statement order matters), this just pins the *direction* for
the same-object zero-store pair.

## 6ga — `cond ? 1 : 0` in a RETURN picks the other flag shape: an explicit if/else assignment + `return local` reproduces the `li 0 ; beq ; li 1 ; b` window

fn_800F2EDC (172 B) sat at 93.0% on exactly three words:

    want  cmpwi rD,0 ; li r3,0 ; beq L ; li r3,1 ; b L
    got   cmpwi rD,0 ; li r3,1 ; bne L ; li r3,0      (falls into L)

Both are `x != 0`, but `emit_store_flag` picks the *cheaper* direction for an
expression: materialise 1, branch on NE, and let the 0 arm fall through into the
common return label. Retail materialises the **false** value first and branches
*over* the true value, paying an explicit merge jump — the signature of an
if/else whose two arms each assign a local:

```c
    if (call_that_returns_int(...) != 0) {
        res = 1;
    } else {
        res = 0;
    }
    return res;
```

Measured inert on this body (all still 3 diffs): `return x != 0;`,
`return (s32)(x != 0);`, `return x != 0 ? 1 : 0;`, `return x == 0 ? 0 : 1;`,
`return !(x == 0);`, `return x != 0u ? 1 : 0;`, `return x > 0 ? 1 : 0;`, and
binding the call to a temp first. Worse (16-18 diffs): `s32 res = 0;` at the
declaration or as a statement before the `if` — the initialiser gets sunk below
the call and perturbs the argument homes. **The `else` arm must be the only
definition of `res`; do not pre-initialise it.** EXACT at 172 B.

Trigger: a small function whose only residual is a `li`/`bne`/`li` versus
`li`/`beq`/`li ; b` trapezoid at a return, with the C written as a ternary or a
bare comparison. `bl`-produced flags mean the ternary form is what ngccc
prefers; if retail has the extra merge jump, it was an if/else.

## 6gb — `extern const` is a general load-hoist oracle (not just for rodata float pools), and one object can want a different `-mcpu`

Two mechanisms found by sweeping the near-diff population in bulk rather than
one draft at a time.

**1. `const` on an `extern` scalar.** If a function reads a global after a store
through a caller-supplied pointer, a plain `extern f32 lbl;` lets the compiler
assume the store may alias that global, so the load cannot move above it. Adding
`const` removes the write, the load hoists, and the block lands on retail's. This
had never been tried corpus-wide: sweeping every draft with `extern <scalar>` at
diff<=20 found 3 solves (0x8007D4E0 4->0, 0x800D61C4 4->0, 0x800DB9D4 11->0)
and several partial improvements. Apply it to the *declaration*, keep the type,
and prefer the minimal set of names that wins (one name is often enough; the
per-name sweep reports which).

**2. `-mcpu=<other>` as a per-object flag.** 0x80005A90 (112B, `-mps-float`)
sits at 6 diffs on the default scheduler model and is byte-exact with
`-mcpu=603`; the 603 issue model orders the paired-single block the way retail
did. When a `-mps-float` draft is stuck on pure PS-ordering ties, sweep
`-mcpu=601/602/603/604/740/745/7400/7450/860/powerpc` before concluding the tie
is a wall — the cost is one compile each and the DOL check is still the arbiter.
(The same sweep over the whole diff<=12 population produced this one hit, so
expect it to be rare: it is a scheduler-model coincidence, not evidence that the
TU used 603.)

Both levers were found with `/tmp` sweeps that compile every draft once per
variant and rank by the masked diff count; the harness is throwaway, the two
declaration/flag edits are what belongs in the source.

**3. `-mcpu` also fixes plain-FP value selection, not just PS ordering.**
0x80096BE8 (336B, eight-corner box builder) selects each output lane with
`andi.`/`beq`/two `stfsx` conditional stores in retail, while every 750-model
compile widens the same ternary to `fmr f0,...`/single store pair at an
identical instruction count. `-mcpu=630` (so does `-mcpu=745`/`rs64a`; 601-604
do not) reproduces retail's two-store form byte for byte, along with the rest of
the body at 15 diffs -> 0. So when an FP-heap draft is stuck on a
"conditional store versus `fmr` select" residual with an exact instruction
count, the `-mcpu` sweep is again the cheapest lever.

A full 1546-draft sweep over `-mcpu={401,403,505,601,602,603,604,620,630,740,
745,801,821,860,powerpc,rs64a}` yielded exactly this one exact match, so treat
the lever as rare but worth one pass whenever a draft is otherwise size-exact.

## 7x — the near-miss sweep census: every global axis run to exhaustion, and the one that still pays

The near-miss population (drafts inside 3-6 words of retail, size-exact) has been
swept by script along every axis below. Each sweep compiles the draft body once
per variant and ranks by the reloc-masked diff count. Nothing is left in these
directions, so re-running them only costs an afternoon — reach for a new
mechanism instead.

| axis | space tried | exact hits |
|---|---|---|
| `-mcpu` | 401/403/505/601/602/603/604/620/630/740/745/801/821/860/powerpc/rs64a over all 1546 drafts | 1 (0x80096BE8 — the FP value-selection case in the later `6gb` note) |
| `-mtune` | the same 16 models over all drafts | 0 |
| `extern const` / `*const` / pointee-`const` | every scalar and pointer extern, one name at a time, plus all-names | 3 (the load-hoist cases in the later `6gb` note) then 0 more |
| alias / ABI / codegen flags | `-fstrict-aliasing`, `-fno-strict-aliasing`, `-fargument-{alias,noalias,noalias-global}`, `-fno-builtin`, `-meabi`, `-mno-eabi`, `-fno-peephole`, `-fno-keep-static-consts`, `-fkeep-inline-functions`, `-fno-inline-functions`, `-O3`, `-funroll-loops`, `-fno-strength-reduce`, `-fno-schedule-insns{,2}`, `-mno-multiple`, `-mno-string`, `-mno-powerpc-gpopt/-gfxopt`, `-mno-fused-madd`, `-mupdate`, `-mminimal-toc`, `-mno-fp-in-toc`, `-mnew-mnemonics`, `-mno-sdata` | 0 (several half-score improvements, none exact) |
| dropping a draft's own `// FLAG:` | all-flags-dropped and each single flag dropped, over all 415 drafts that carry a FLAG line | 0 |
| statement placement | adjacent swap / two-slot skip / full reverse of every depth-1 statement, over the 95 size-exact drafts at diff<=5, plus every permutation of a suspect store run (all 6 orders of 0x80240DC0's three `stfs`, also with the neighbouring `li`/`stw` interleaved) | 0 (the worst case stays two words: retail emits the run in descending offset order, which no spelling of these three stores reaches) |
| declaration placement | the same moves plus **every** permutation of up to 8 declarations (colouring oracle) on the closest 44 | 0 |
| ternary rewrites | `c ? a : b` -> `if/else` in both polarities, for assignments and returns, every occurrence in every draft | 0 |
| type width/sign | each `s32/u32/s16/u16/s8/u8` token replaced by every other width, one at a time, over the diff<=5 population | 0 exact, 3 drafts improved by one or two words |
| callee prototypes | every draft prototype rewritten to the signature of that callee's matched definition (a table built from all 9242 `src/*.c` definitions), one at a time and all at once | 1 (0x800A13F0) and 17 partial improvements |
| empty-asm barriers | `__asm__ volatile("" ::: "memory")` inserted at each depth-1 statement boundary of every size-exact draft at diff<=5 | 0 promotable: the single masked-100 (0x8002CDE4) fails the internal branch-target audit, and four more only halve |

The prototype row is the one worth repeating: the engine's script accessors
return `s32` (`GetFloat(CStruct *, s32, f32 *, s32)` and the rest of that
family), and a draft that declares one as returning `f32` is size-exact yet
three words off in the call window. Before sweeping anything, check that every
callee's declared signature matches the matched definition of that callee —
`src/*.c` is the authority, and it already covers the whole game.

Corollary for triage: when a draft is size-exact at 1-3 words and all of the
above leave it unchanged, the residual is either a reload/coalescing artefact
(fix by changing which *values* exist, not by reordering) or a scheduler tie
between two compiler-generated instructions (a `lis`/home-copy pair, or the two
`li`s of one call's constant args), which no source spelling can reorder. Park
with the measured note rather than re-sweeping.

## 7y — 2026-10-22: three fixes that are one insight (role/width/truncation), and how far it reaches

Three parks fell in one round to the same observation: the body's *variable
structure* was wrong, not the register allocator's tie-break. Each has a
distinct tell, so they are worth recognising separately.

1. **Byte-lane accumulator chains: spell every truncation retail performs.**
   A chain of byte-sized accumulators stored to consecutive `u8` members and
   conditionally xored with 0x40/0x80 carries an explicit `clrlwi` at *every*
   boundary in retail. Declaring the local `u8` is not enough (GCC folds a mask
   it can prove dead): write `acc = wide & 0xff;` for the chain entry and
   `next = (u8)(s8)acc;` where retail has the second truncation. `s8 acc` alone
   trades the first `clrlwi` for an `extsb`; the pair fixes both ends.
   (fn_8000BF80, 98.1 -> 100.)

2. **Field WIDTHS decide the shape of a zero/copy run.** When the loaded/stored
   widths say two 4-byte fields are really one 8-byte pair (plus a trailing
   int), "three hand-written zero stores" become two 8-byte stores + the index
   store, and a word-by-word copy loop becomes an ordinary struct assignment;
   the store order then falls out of the compiler instead of being searched.
   Re-derive widths from the memory ops *before* permuting a store run.
   (fn_80014150, 95.2 -> 100.)

3. **An FPR destination that resists pins and flags is usually a wrong local
   COUNT.** If the residual copy has the right source register and only the
   destination differs, count retail's roles: result / loop-carried value /
   clamp source as three locals, with the result assigned only inside the
   dispatch branch. One temp playing two roles is what lets the allocator pick
   the wrong register; split it and the copy lands where retail puts it.
   Doc 32's "allocation tie-break" label is wrong whenever the draft has fewer
   roles than retail. (fn_8002DB10, 96.4 -> 100.)

**Boundary, measured over the whole `src/wip` corpus (2026-10-22).**

- Draft sweep over all 1538 files in `src/wip`: 4 EXACT, 461 NEAR, 1010 DIFF,
  15 FAIL, 46 without a function boundary (2 stub/tp drafts are not compiled).
  Three of the EXACT are the three above; the fourth, 0x8013928C, is the known
  masked-EXACT refused on branch targets.
- Residual census of the 461 NEAR: 207 order-only, 39 register-only, 165 shape,
  50 shape+size. The near band is dominated by scheduler and `local_alloc` ties
  (the 7x census), not by width/role errors. **Decode each word independently
  when classifying**: capstone's streaming `disasm()` stops at the first
  undecodable word and every later instruction then compares as `?` == `?`,
  which inflated the register-only count from 39 to 78 before this was fixed.
- Truncation count (`clrlwi`/`extsb`/`extsh`) differs from retail in only 7 of
  the NEAR drafts — all at <=81% and all size-short. No near-match is blocked on
  a *missing* truncation. The 90%+ shape is the INVERSE: retail truncates a
  `u16` whose range GCC proves (fn_80137CF8), and no spelling restores it —
  `x & 0xffff`, `(u16)` on the assignment and a `u16` intermediate are all
  byte-identical. An `s8`-typed load on fn_8000D478's tail comparisons measures
  70.3% -> 67.8% (compares + case-6 store) / 25.2% (compares only).
- 8-byte op census (`lfd`/`stfd`): only 3 drafts have retail using more than the
  draft, all <=59%. The near-match store-run cases (fn_8004E0B4, fn_800AE8C4,
  fn_8009E004, fn_8012B2A0) are scheduling/hoist artefacts already traced with
  `cc1 -dr`/`-ds`, not width errors.
- The role-count lever only applies where the draft's web count really is wrong.
  Inlining the clamp expression instead of naming the temp (fn_800340C4) measures 92.31%
  against 97.2%; that function and fn_8008144C / fn_800BE410 / fn_80166640 /
  fn_801F2AE0 are the documented allocator/registry class, where the webs are
  already the right count and no split changes the colour.
- Checklist pass over all 39 register-only drafts: **no fn_8002DB10-class role
  error remains**. The two genuinely multi-role drafts are fn_80166640's
  `temp_r30` (an s32 default value plus three CStruct-ctor roles, all six split
  configurations byte-neutral at 99.04%) and fn_8012CD84's `n`/`o` (reused by
  three switch cases; per-case splits byte-identical at 92.96%). The rest split
  into compiler-generated page-anchor/`extendsfdf2` pseudos, reload scratch
  hardregs, and pairwise `mr` transpositions — none reachable by a role split.

## 7z — 2026-10-22: **adjacent-statement sweep over all 207 order-only NEAR drafts** (21 improved, 17 kept, best 75.0 → 96.1 and 91.2 → 98.9; 0 promoted by the sweep — see §7za for the three EXACT drafts promoted the same day)

Population: the size-exact NEAR drafts whose residual is pure order (same
instruction multiset, different sequence) — 207 of the 461 NEAR after the §7y
decoder fix. Method: a greedy adjacent-statement hill climb (swap each
statement with its successor at every brace depth, keep the best, iterate)
scored with `test_wip_drafts.test_one`, so every accepted move is a real
compile of the draft with its own `// FLAG:` / `-mps-float` lines.

| outcome | count |
|---|---|
| score improved | 21 |
| unchanged | 186 |
| EXACT | 0 |

### The residual of this class is not uniform — only one third of it moves

- **Field-store runs in a local mirror block are the big win.** `fn_80175690`
  91.2 → **98.9** (724B) came from writing `fr.sp24 = qb;` first in a five-store
  block, plus moving `fn_8022A9B8` above `fn_802332B8`. `fn_800EB8F8`
  75.0 → **96.1** (304B, PS) came from placing `k.f.a = lbl_8029ACE0;` *between*
  the two `ps_muls0` calls, which lands the literal `lfs` between the u0/u1
  multiplies. Both are pure scheduling-visible source order, and both functions
  were previously parked as "scheduler owns this". Re-test any parked
  multi-store/constant-load window with this lever first.
- **Independent loads hoisted above a zero-code barrier** pay a point or two
  (`fn_800FE27C` 90.0 → 91.7 when both `b` loads go above the `+r` barriers).
- **Call/arg-setup interleavings** are worth 2-8 points on their own
  (`fn_8023869C` 72.4 → 77.6, `fn_8013B8FC` 92.9 → 94.2, `fn_8026FD2C`
  86.5 → 88.0) but never close a draft.
- **Two-word transpositions inside one statement's expansion do not move.**
  Every draft at ≤4 diffs stayed where §7s says it lives; the best accepted
  permutation leaves `fn_80175690` at exactly its documented 2-word residue.

### A score-greedy climb happily proposes semantically wrong code — check the diff

4 of the 21 winners were dependent reorders and were reverted: `fn_800EA4D8`
stored `W[0].p = r` *above* `r = ps_rsqrte(t)` (previous value), `fn_80110B84`
did `var_f13 = pp` before `pp` was recomputed, `fn_80143258` stored `pair[1]`
before the `xoris` conversion of `lo`, and `fn_80250E24` did `rlo &= rm` before
`rm >>= rn`. Each scored higher than the correct-order source. Rule: a moved
statement may not read a value that another moved statement defines; accept
only moves across independent statements (independent locals, distinct fields
of a local mirror, pure computes across a barrier).

Declaration-order moves are legitimate **only** for local scratch mirrors:
`fn_800620EC` (84.3 → 87.6) and `fn_800252C0` (77.8 → 85.2) both reorder
struct members so the emitted offsets change, which is safe because the struct
is a stack-scratch layout whose address never escapes and whose members are
only accessed by name. Reordering members of a struct that mirrors real memory
(or is passed out) is a semantic bug.

Score deltas for the kept set (old → new): 800200D8 72.8→75.9, 8002062C
89.2→90.8, 800252C0 77.8→85.2, 8005FA84 68.0→70.0, 800620EC 84.3→87.6,
800A3778 61.3→66.9, 800FD81C 55.6→56.6, 800FE27C 90.0→91.7, 8010CC40
73.7→74.4, 8013B8FC 92.9→94.2, 80175690 91.2→98.9, 80180390 75.5→78.4,
801B23FC 93.4→94.0, 802340AC 60.0→60.9, 8023869C 72.4→77.6, 8026FD2C
86.5→88.0, 800EB8F8 75.0→96.1. All drafts stay inert, so the DOL is unchanged
by this sweep.

Follow-ups that did NOT move anything, so they are not re-run:

- **Statement barriers** (§7t) at every boundary of `fn_80175690`'s pre-loop
  region: both forms, all six positions, best 97.79 vs the 98.90 from the
  store-order fix. The residual is one `li r5,1`/`stb` slot that the header
  already records as pin-resistant.
- **The `fn_800EB8F8` tail**: barriers between `pa[0]`/`pa[1]`/`y +=`, the
  `y +=` line first or in the middle, both barrier forms — best 92.11 against
  96.05. Its 3-word rotation is not a statement-order choice.
- **Move-to-anywhere relocation** (not just adjacent swaps) over eight drafts
  at 93.9-94.8 (`801DA420`, `801F5A0C`, `801F4F88`, `8013B8FC`, `801B23FC`,
  `800CC358`, `800AE8C4`, `80005F80`): zero improvement anywhere, 240 candidates
  per draft. Once adjacent transposition has been climbed to a fixed point, the
  remaining words in this band are post-reload slot decisions — the reach of a
  reordering search is exhausted.

## 7za — 2026-10-22: **three EXACT drafts promoted; one was a masked-EXACT store-order trap** (fn_8000BF80 1044B, fn_8002DB10 444B, fn_80014150 248B)

The three drafts sitting at `EXACT` in `src/wip/` were run through
`promote_wip.py` (which rebuilds and `cmp`s the whole DOL, not just the object).
Two promoted straight away. The third was refused with a **2-byte DOL diff**:

```
differing bytes: 2; first at DOL vaddr 0x80014317
orig  addi r11, r11, -0xc8      (lbl_802FFF38)
built addi r11, r11, -0xA8      (lbl_802FFF58)
```

The masked word cannot see which symbol an `addi` targets, so the two
`lbl_802FFFxx = 0` stores being in the wrong order still scored EXACT. This is
the §6fx rule in a relocation coat: separate zero-stores to two objects emit in
**reverse statement order**, so writing the later-address store first fixed it
and the DOL went byte-identical. Anyone promoting a masked EXACT that touches
two neighbouring globals of the same size should expect exactly this and pre-empt
it by writing the later address first.

Takeaway for the near band: `promote_wip.py`'s DOL gate is the only real
verification — a `test_wip_drafts` EXACT can hide a relocation target, so always
promote from EXACT drafts rather than trusting the percentage.

## 7zb — 2026-10-22: **a scalar pair-copy in the body inflates callee-saved GPR use and shifts the whole frame — the prologue cascade's most common root cause** (fn_800D4E34 85.7 → 87.2, prologue + PS tail now byte-exact)

`fn_800D4E34` (532 B) carried 19 diffs that looked like "the frame is 8 bytes
too big and every home/offset is shifted by one" — classic board-level
regalloc. It was not: two 8-byte copies in the 0x100 flag arm were written as
member assignments (`r9->unk0x58 = arg0->unk0x230;`) on members whose type the
draft struct declares as 8 bytes. ngccc copies those with **two scalar
`lwz`/`stw` pairs**, and because the copied values cross a preceding `bl`, the
scalar form keeps them in **callee-saved GPRs** — `stmw r28` (r28/r29/r30),
frame 0x18, arg0 homed in r30. Retail copies the same bytes with
**`psq_l`/`psq_st`** into f0, needs no GPR, and runs frame 0x10 with only r31
saved.

Fix, one line per copy:

```c
*(__ps_t *)((char *)r9 + 0x58) = *(__ps_t *)((char *)arg0 + 0x230);
```

plus `// FLAG: -mps-float` (per-object only, as always). That single change
removed the entire 18-word prologue/home/offset cascade and left the residual
in one contiguous float block.

Rules that follow:

- **A prologue that saves more GPRs than retail is a symptom, not a cause.**
  Diff the *number of `stmw` slots* and the frame size first; if got saves one
  or more extra callee-saved registers, look for a value that got had to keep
  across a call — a scalarised copy, a cached field, or a hoisted load — rather
  than trying to steer the allocator.
- **8-byte struct members want `__ps_t`, not two words.** Any member the want
  copies with `psq_l`/`psq_st` (displacements multiple of 8) must be copied
  through an `__ps_t` cast in the draft; the member-assignment spelling is
  semantically identical but scalarises and taxes the GPR file.
- Same function also had two one-word *type/order* halves, both worth checking
  on any unsigned-compare or `!=`-of-two-compares shape: retail `cmplwi`
  means the tested member is **unsigned** (add `(u32)` at the use, not in the
  shared struct), and `a != b` on two comparisons emits the creqv
  condition-register pair in **operand order**, so the source operand order is
  load-bearing (`(dir > c) != (oldb0 > c)` vs the reverse: one word).
- Remaining ceiling on this body is FPR colouring of `{cur, 0.0f, dir}` across
  f9/f10/f12/f13; the float locals' declaration order is inert (7 permutations,
  byte-identical), so do not re-grind order there.

Census behind that rule (all 1535 drafts rescored, then filtered):

- **Frame-size mismatch = 26 drafts.** These are the prologue-cascade
  candidates; the harness reports want/got `stwu` frames, so a mismatch is a
  one-glance filter. Sorted by score: `8004B314` 85.8 (-80/-88), `8024E2C8` 84.2
  (-40/-32), `80129EA0` 80.8, `8023DE60` 80.2 (-56/-64), `8014DDFC` 77.3
  (-24/-32), `8021FAB4` 76.6, `8017B7EC` 72.9, `80192D24` 70.8, `8013BB68`
  69.9, `8013A508` 68.0, `801805DC` 64.8, `800CD150` 64.8, `800F2E00` 62.8,
  `800FE42C` 59.9, `80124110` 56.9, `8011E9A0` 55.9, `801826E8` 54.6,
  `80139BDC` 53.0, `800179D0` 52.8, `801A3ABC` 50.2, `80112C0C` 50.0,
  `801622D4` 49.5,  `801A3E4C` 49.4, `800AA1F4` 48.8, `8019AA88` 46.0, `8020F938` 45.9.
- **Paired-single words: want > got in only 7 drafts** (`8005B11C` 91.1 4v3,
  `80211E5C` 69.7 17v16, `801B9FD0` 58.6 44v43, `800FDE38` 51.5 29v28,
  `8006BF04` 49.3 31v30, `800EDB3C` 46.6 4v0, `8020F938` 45.9 21v14). So a
  scalarised pair copy is a narrow, already-mostly-covered class — the count
  is a fast negative filter, not a general lever.

## 7zc — 2026-10-22: **diff-kind census of all 462 NEAR drafts: only 40 are pure colour, and most "semantic" words are one-slot displacements pretending to be semantic**

The near band is routinely described as "scheduler ties", but nothing had
measured what the words actually are. Rescoring all 1535 drafts and classifying
every differing word by its *instruction pair* (same mnemonic + register-only
difference = colour; anything else = shape) gives:

- **40 drafts are pure colour** (`colour == ndiff`): nothing but register-name
  rotation. These cannot be improved from C; they are allocator coin flips.
  **Superseded — see §7zi**: `fn_80191050` was one of these and promoted EXACT
  once *both* swapped webs were pinned and the schedule flag was dropped, so a
  pure-colour draft is a pin target first and a coin flip only after that fails.
- **The rest look semantic but usually are not.** A single instruction placed
  one slot early/late makes 3–4 *consecutive* words differ with different
  mnemonics (`li` vs `stb`, `or.` vs `lwz`, `lfs` vs `lis`), so a 4-word
  "semantic" residual is frequently one moved instruction. Check for a
  contiguous shifted window before believing the census's "other" count.
- **The genuine semantic leftovers in the 85–99% band are one-liners**: an
  unsigned test emitted signed (`cmpwi` where want has `cmplwi` — add `(u32)`
  at the use site, not in the shared struct), an 8-byte copy scalarised where
  want has `psq_l`/`psq_st` (§7zb), or the operand order of an `!=` between two
  comparisons.

Also closed in the same pass (all measured on the six best near-band drafts
`8018CAF4` 95.9, `80086B84` 98.5, `801A71DC` 99.0, `801903B8` 98.6,
`80234588` 97.3, `80040734` 98.9):

- **PPC-specific flags are not a lever.** `-msched-prolog`, `-mno-sched-prolog`
  and `-mno-sched-epilog` do not exist in ProDG cc1 (all compile-fail, 0.00%).
  `-mno-update` collapses everything to <2%, `-mno-multiple` to <11% (retail
  relies on `stmw`/`lmw` and on update-form addressing).
- **`fn_80009F64`'s two listed untried levers are now measured**: a 2-instruction
  volatile window over the counter RMW gives 75.0%, and the split-RMW readiness
  change is byte-neutral at 95.45% (its historical readiness argument does not
  reproduce). Its 2-word residual stands.

### 7zc-addendum — field-width/kind scans do not find type bugs in this band

Two further population scans, both negative:

- **Width-family mismatches** (a differing word whose mnemonics are two members of
  one load/store width family — `lbz`/`lhz`/`lha`/`lwz`, `stb`/`sth`/`stw`,
  `cmpwi`/`cmplwi`, `lfs`/`lfd`): 36 drafts hit. Spot-checked five
  (`800C4414` 89.2, `801C0FF4` 83.2, `80043EE8` 68.0, `801628FC` 84.2,
  `8007E030` 73.3) and **every one is a one-instruction displacement** — the
  "wrong width" word is the *same* instruction one slot later, so the two
  mnemonics being compared belong to different instructions. Tightening the
  comparison to "same base register and same operand shape" (dropping the
  displacement value) does not help; the hits survive it.
- **`cmpwi` vs `cmplwi` population hits** are the same story except where the
  same-site comparison is exact; the only real instance found this session was
  `fn_800D4E34`'s `unk0x18` guard (§7zb).

So: when a draft's residual reads as "wrong width / wrong compare" at one site,
first check the *neighbours* — if the neighbouring words are the same
instruction set shifted, the class is displacement and no type edit will move
it. Real type bugs appear as a width mismatch with **identical** surrounding
instructions on both sides.

- **Declared-flag staleness: 415 drafts with a `FLAG:`/`extra_cflags:` line
  re-scored with the flag list emptied, and with each flag removed
  individually: 0 drafts improved.** The parked flags are all still
  load-bearing, so do not re-run the "maybe the flag is stale now" sweep.
- **`-mps-float` blind spot: none.** The 7 drafts where want has more

- **Exact-position signed/unsigned compare scan** (`cmplwi>cmpwi`,
  `cmplw>cmpw`, `cmpldi>cmpdi` on the *same* operands): 6 hits, all
  `nd >= 40` except `8025A894` (96.67%, 2 words). That one is an mwcc/asm

Near-band drafts re-probed this round and left parked (each at its own wall,
one entry each so they are not re-attempted): `8021546C` 96.34 — the same
`mr r30,r3` / `lis r4` swap at **three identical sites**, so one mechanism
would finish it: barriers cost 1.8 points (`"+r"` 25%), dropping the
`__asm__("r30")` pin costs 14 points, flags inert; `80066EB0` 95.71 — the same
`addi r9,r30,2` / `cmpwi r30,-3` swap three times, pinned delay-loop idiom;
`80178520` 94.78 — `addi r23,r1,0x18` hoisted over the `bl` (address home
across the call, want rematerialises it in the loop preheader).
`800EF4CC` (72 B, 18 insns) was rebuilt end-to-end as a control: the ceiling
stays 61.1% because want keeps **three separate `li`-zero registers** plus a
