## 7s — The "default-then-conditional" tail: which source form decides compare-vs-default order, and why the colour then blocks it

Measured on `800CC358` (136 B, frameless integer return-path selector) and its
sibling `800CC138`. Both end in a select whose result is used as a load base, and
both are stuck at exactly two/three words.

**Order is decided by the source form, and it IS reachable.** For a tail of the
shape `x = 0; if (node) x = node - 4; return ((T *)x)->f;` the emitter keeps the
default materialisation *before* the compare (retail: compare, default, branch,
then-arm). Writing the same select as an if/else with both arms assigned
(`if (node) x = ...; else x = 0;`) makes jump optimisation hoist the constant arm
to just before the branch — i.e. it lands *after* the compare, which is retail's
order. Score: 91.2 % with three differing words, all of them the *colour* of the
selected pseudo (it lands in r11 where retail uses r3), so a well-shaped body can
be two words away and still be a different mechanism than the default-first form
(94.1 %, two words).

The same order also comes out of the ternary spelling on a pointer
(`q = (node == NULL) ? NULL : (char *)node - 4;` then a load through `q`), in both
polarities, and out of a value-ternary that keeps the address in the then-arm.
What does *not* work is a value-ternary (`node ? ((T *)((char *)node - 4))->f : 0`):
the address is then a pure expression and gets folded into the load's displacement
(`0x34(r9)` instead of `addi` + `0x38`), which costs a word and the wrong tail.

**The colour cannot follow from source.** Everything that forces the selected
value into r3 collapses the shape instead:

* pinning the selected variable to r3 (integer *or* pointer) makes the then-arm's
  `node - 4` reuse the pinned register, so the node value itself is homed in r3
  and the whole prologue shifts (37–50 %);
* an empty `"+r"(node)` barrier before the select does not prevent that (50 %);
* pinning a *second*, final address variable to r3 and copying the select into it
  is coalesced away and still lands r11 (91.2 %);
* splitting the loaded value into its own variable (so the return pseudo is
  defined after the block) changes nothing (91.2 %);
* an inlined helper returning the address is inlined to the same r11 colour and
  loses a whole block elsewhere (34 %);
* spelling the loaded member as a `char *` deref, a volatile deref, `u32`, or
  `char *`/`void *` candidate types all leave the colour at r11.

Useful cross-check inside the same function: its *other* select (a pointer
candidate, same `cond ? x - 4 : 0` shape, scratch destination) compiles
byte-identically in both polarities. So the mechanism is not the select itself but
which register the selected value ends up in — retail's second select landed in
r3, ours lands in r11.

So for this family the two halves are mutually exclusive with the levers
available: the if/else form buys the order and loses the colour, the pinned
default-first form buys the colour and loses the order.

**Two-register loop variables (`800CC138`).** Retail keeps the candidate in a
volatile register and copies it into the callee-saved loop register at the test
(copy-with-record). Writing the loop as `while ((node = p) != NULL)` with the
sentinel null-out on `p` reaches 85.0 % (from 82.5 %) and reproduces every
instruction but the copy: the emitter propagates the initial load straight into
the callee-saved register and folds the copy away. An inlined "valid(p)" helper
does produce the copy (40 %) but then applies the null-out *after* it, i.e. to the
loop register instead of the candidate. Distinct types for the two variables do
not prevent the coalescing.

Both functions stay parked at their documented best bodies; the measured variants
above are all at or below them.

## 7zd — 2026-10-22: **a local's address taken INSIDE the loop reproduces retail's mixed frame/register addressing**; plus two address-masking traps that cost promotions

### The lever: `p = &local;` inside the loop body

`fn_80238104` (220 B, list walk + 6-byte rect overlap) was parked at 74.55 %
with one root cause: retail addresses the local rect **through the frame** for
the copy and its first read, then **through a callee-saved register** for the
remaining reads, while every spelling that took the address in the loop
preheader produced one pointer web with all accesses through the register (and
coloured `node`/`local` the other way round).

Taking the address **inside the loop body**, after the calls that produce the
source rect, is EXACT:

```c
do {
    n2 = fn_802416F8(fn_802432A0(node));
    p = &sp8;               /* inside the body, not before the loop */
    *p = *(Rect6 *)n2;
    ...                     /* reads through p */
} while (node != NULL);
```

ngccc's loop optimizer hoists the (loop-invariant) address computation into the
preheader — which is where retail has it — but the stores/reads that precede
the copy still address the frame, because the copy statement itself was written
before the hoisted value's register existed. The emitted shape is therefore the
frame/register mix plain preheader addressing cannot produce. This is the
mirror image of §6ds2 (stop a hoist with a loop-variant input): here the hoist
is wanted, and moving the statement *into* the loop is how you request it.

Two related notes: the rect must be copied by value through that pointer (one
word store + one halfword store), and the flag gate must be NESTED ifs — a
single `&&` chain lets ngccc fold it to `andi r0,0x10c; cmpwi 4`.

### Trap 1: a masked-EXACT body can still point 0x100 off a global

`fn_8025D114` (140 B, EXI packet builder) scored 100.00 % in `want_got` and was
reported EXACT by `test_wip_drafts`, yet promoting it differed from retail in
exactly one byte pair: the draft read the global as `lbl_803ACEE8 - 0xD4`
(= 0x803ACE14), retail reads 0x803ACD14 (`lis 0x803b` + `lwz -0x32ec`). Both
spellings mask to the same `lis/addi` pair in objdiff, so **only the full-DOL
`cmp` inside `promote_wip` catches it**. The correct base is the symbol that
*contains* the address: `lbl_803ACCC0` (size 0xE0) + 0x54. Rule: never derive a
game global as `nearby_symbol ± delta` — resolve the enclosing `symbols.txt`
object and use a positive offset inside its size, or the @ha/@l split can land
0x100 (or 0x10000) away while every masked word still matches.

### Trap 2: `volatile` on a zero-byte barrier changes the schedule

`fn_8025D114`'s last two words were `slwi` / `li r9,9` in the wrong order at
94.29 %. The body needs a zero-byte CSE barrier to keep `0x10 << 8` unfolded
(`__asm__("" : "=r"(sh) : "r"(sh))`). With `volatile` the barrier is also a
scheduling point and the `li` (which feeds a later `stb`) is emitted first;
dropping `volatile` (no code change, no asm emitted) gives the retail order:
100.00 %. Worth re-checking on every parked draft whose residual sits next to
such a barrier.

### Promotions this round, and the gap-filler carve-out recipe

`fn_80238104` and `fn_8025D114` are byte-identical. The second lives inside
`auto_01_8025D010_text` (the 0x8025D010 gap filler, emitted as verbatim bytes),
so promoting it needed the full carve-out: a `fn_8025D114 = .text:0x8025D114;
// type:function size:0x8C` symbol, a `fn_8025D114.c` split for
0x8025D114-0x8025D1A0, `type:label` symbols for the two callees in the
still-unclaimed filler (0x8025CDD4 / 0x8025CF10, or the `bl`s have no
relocation target), and `- fn_8025D114` under `force_active` (its callers are
in the filler and emit no linker-visible reloc, so mwld dead-strips it — the
same orphan class as fn_8025D944/fn_8025D550).

### Two more drafts improved, both stuck on a value/colour choice

- `fn_800CC138` (160 B, list walk): 82.5 → **97.5 %** by writing the walk with
  TWO variables (candidate + body walker, the sentinel null-out on the
  candidate, the copy into the walker at the test) and pinning the candidate to
  r9. Unpinned, both coalesce into r31 and the whole test block degrades (6
  words). Last word: the body's call passes the walker, and copyprop hands the
  argument to the (dead, equal) candidate register — r9 instead of r31.
  Distinct types, the callee prototype, a block-local, an r3 pin and a
  `"+r"` barrier on the walker all leave it at 2 words; pinning the walker to
  r31 shifts every parameter home (15 %).
- `fn_800598C8` (232 B, PS record allocator): 79.3 → **82.76 %** — the counter
  value and the value stored back are two webs and want keeps both in r0, so
  the load *and* the increment need their own `register s32 … __asm__("r0")`.
  Pinning only the load is worse (77.6 %); load in r8 + increment in r0 leaves
  the call's value in the wrong register (74.1 %).

## 7ze — 2026-10-22: **a 19.5 % m2c draft went EXACT — the loop-body address lever plus three preheader-placement rules** (fn_80204404, 332 B)

`fn_80204404` (per-frame descriptor rebuild, 8-iteration PS accumulate loop) was
an inert m2c draft at 19.51 %. §7zd's lever (take the local's address **inside**
the loop body) jumped it to 80.72 %; three statement-placement rules finished
it, each worth 5–7 points:

| step | score |
|---|---|
| `p = &obj;` re-taken at the loop top | 80.72 % |
| `i = 0;` above the pre-loop call (`for (; i < 8; i++)`) | 86.75 % |
| the four accumulation stores listed in reverse retail order | 85.54 % (alone) |
| `q = p;` sunk below the loop-entry `vec[0]` loads | **100.00 %** |

**1. The loop counter.** Retail's `li` for the counter sits in the preheader
slot *ahead* of the first call. `for (i = 0; ...)` puts it after the call. Split
the init out (`i = 0;` as its own statement before the call) and the `li` takes
the earlier slot; the loop itself is unchanged.

**2. Store-run reversal.** Retail emitted a run of four pair stores in the
reverse of source order (`0x14, 0x28, 0x0C, 0x1C` where source order gave
`0x0C, 0x14, 0x1C, 0x28`). Detect it from the diff: a diff block whose *want*
and *got* store offsets are the same multiset in a different order. For
independent stores the fix is free — list them in the reverse of retail's
order. Do not generalise to runs containing calls or overlapping aliases.

**3. Where the second copy of an address is taken.** Retail keeps two
callee-saved copies of `&obj` (`p` = argument of the second call, `q` = the
`+0x08` store and the first call). Written as `q = p;` immediately after the
call, the allocator inverted the copies: q was born from the address register
*before* the call and p became a copy of q, leaving `lis` in the slot retail
uses for p's birth (7 words, three of them a 3-cycle in r24/25/28). Moving the
same statement **below the loop-entry loads** restores retail's order — p born
from the address register pre-call, q copied from p post-call — and the rest of
the callee-saved numbering falls in line. Both spellings are one `mr`; only the
live-range start differs.

**4. The remaining pins.** `&vec[3]` → r27 and `&obj.ref` → r26 (both live
across the loop). Pinning `&obj` itself (r28) collapses the two copies into one
and the frame degrades to 53 % — the pair must be born unpinned.

**Corollary — the lever is narrow but very high-yield.** Applied mechanically to
all 110 address-taken-local drafts in `src/wip` it moved exactly one draft by
more than 10 points (this one, +61) and a second by +26 (fn_802442A8, still at
41 %); 93 of 103 scored variants were neutral or worse. What distinguishes the
winner: every use of the pointer is inside the one loop, so the hoisted value and
the frame-addressed statements can coexist. When the pointer is also used in the
preheader (a load or a call argument before the loop), taking the address in the
body changes nothing — the preheader simply gets the direct form.

## 7zf — 2026-10-22: **a local's address that must survive calls: pin the scratch, leave the home free** (fn_8013A508 74.4 -> 94.4 %)

`fn_8013A508` keeps a 0x10-byte `Ctx` on the stack and touches it before and
after calls. The draft had one pointer, pinned to r5 because that pin had
measured best in isolation; ngccc then rematerialised `addi r5, r1, 8` after
every call, the frame came out 0x38 with `stmw r26`, and 26 words of the body
were wrong. Retail is the two-register shape §85 describes: the address is born
in a caller-saved scratch (r9), the two stores that immediately follow address
through it, then `mr r25, r9` copies it to a callee-saved home used afterwards.

The fix is two pointers, and only the scratch is pinned:

```c
register Ctx *q __asm__("r9");   /* short-lived: dies at the copy */
Ctx *c;                          /* home: allocator picks r25 */
...
q = &ctx;
q->f8 = ...;                     /* stores through the scratch */
q->f4 = 0;
c = q;                           /* -> mr r25, r9 */
...                              /* everything else through c */
```

Frame, `stmw r25` and the whole prologue through `mr r25, r9` become
byte-exact. Measured on this function: scratch r9 + free home 85.6 %, scratch
r9 + home pinned r25 85.6 % (identical — once the copy exists the home pin is a
no-op), scratch r5/r10/r11 59–81 %, and one pointer pinned anywhere 67–75 %.
Pinning the home *without* the copy is the trap: `addi r25, r1, 8` is emitted
directly and there is nothing left to copy out of.

Two companions from the same body:

- **A byte field must be stored from the load, not from the signed local.**
  `s8 idx = p[0]; sp18 = idx;` emits `lbz` + `extsb` + `stb`; `sp18 = p[0];`
  (still keeping `idx` for the masked table index) emits `lbz` + `stb` and the
  `rlwinm` mask survives. The extra `extsb` shifts every following word by 4
  and is what kept the function at 79 %.
- **Split a two-term address expression into two statements on the same
  variable** when the want's sum goes straight into the result register:
  `head = (Node *)((char *)base + ix); head = (Node *)((char *)head + 0x884);`
  instead of one fused expression, which makes the add reuse the base register
  as destination and adds a move.

## Integer `abs()` (not the hand-written xor/subf chain)

The signed-absolute-value idiom in the game's C is the library call `abs(x)`,
never the hand-expanded `t = x >> 31; t = (t ^ x) - t;`. Both compile to the
same instruction sequence, but they colour it differently: `abs()` expands
through `expand_abs`, which keeps the load in a **scratch** register (r0) and
the sign/accumulator intermediates in r9/r11, leaving only the final result in
a callee-saved register. Writing the chain by hand makes every step reuse a
single accumulator register, and no amount of declaration/source reordering
moves it.

Measured: `fn_80181AC0` 91.2% -> **100%** (the only edit was replacing the
hand-written chain with `abs(q)` / `abs(d)`); `fn_801819E4` 96.4% from 93.6%
(5 of its 7 residual words). No prototype is needed — `abs` is implicitly
declared like the rest of the corpus (`src/fn_8009D6FC.c` does the same).

When a residual in an `xor/subf` block is "want uses r0/r9/r11 for the
intermediates, got keeps everything in one register", reach for `abs()` before
any pin.

## Switch dispatch with a shared call tail: write the call in every arm

A `switch` whose every arm ends in *the same* call, but where the original kept
the per-arm argument setup (key constant, `li` for a literal argument, the
`lwz` of an argument that must survive the call) and shares only the `bl`
itself, comes from spelling the call out **in each arm** and letting cross-
jumping merge the identical suffixes. Hoisting the varying piece into a local
(`s32 key; switch (...) { case A: key = K; } f(x, key, 0);`) produces one call
site, and the compiler then puts the whole argument setup *after* the branch:
the object comes out 5 words short with the same compare tree.

Measured: `fn_801F0610` 63.2% -> **100%** (272B vs 292B want) by moving the four
`fn_80141834(..., GetStructure(K, 0))` calls into their case arms. Both forms
keep the compare tree identical; only the arm/tail split changes.

## Shared call tail as a join block: the duplicate costs a callee-saved home

A different shape from the per-arm call above: the tail call is shared by
blocks in *different* arms (`case X`'s else and a `default` arm), so want's
tail is a join block with three in-edges and the `==K` body of the arm is the
fall-through of its compare. The object can instead place that body after the
`m != 0` arm and branch forward to it — identical instruction multiset, wrong
order, and the order is not flag-steerable: `-freorder-blocks` is not accepted
by ngccc, and a dozen `-fno-*` switches (gcse, cse-follow-jumps,
strength-reduce, peephole, defer-pop, inline, branch-count-reg, function-cse,
force-mem, expensive-optimizations, rerun-loop-opt, thread-jumps,
optimize-register-move, caller-saves) leave it untouched.

Writing the tail call a second time inside the arm — so the then-body carries
its own call and cross-jumping merges both into the join block — reproduces
want's order exactly. The catch: the cross-jumper runs after register
allocation, so the extra call site raises that pointer's reference count in
`global_alloc` and it takes the higher callee-saved register. Measured on
`fn_8012DC0C`: arm stream word-for-word correct, 544B, but the two pointer
homes swap (p r31->r30, o r30->r31) and the score drops 74.5% -> 64.7%.

So when a block-order fix also moves registers, look for the *other* call site
that could be the merge partner instead of duplicating into the arm, and state
in the park note which of the two goals is still open — for that function they
can be mutually exclusive.

## A temp that shares the scratch `r0` with an anonymous sibling needs an explicit pin

A short-lived named temp whose value retail keeps in its own register can still
land in `r0` when the same block already used `r0` for an anonymous expression
temp — cc1 reuses the scratch colour, and the consumer then reads `r0` where
retail copies the value aside. The tell is a single-lane difference inside an
otherwise exact block: `lbzu r10` / `slwi r10,24` / `add r9,r9,r10` in want vs
`lbzu r0` / `slwi r0,24` / `add r9,r9,r0` in got, with the *earlier* lane
correctly in `r0`.

Fix: pin only the lane that lands on the scratch —
`register u32 b3 __asm__("r10");` — and leave the anonymous temp anonymous. The
pin also removes any scheduling flag that was propping up the unpinned body:
`fn_8012B2A0` (436B QB token walker) went 94.5% -> **100% at DEFAULT flags**
after the pin, and its `-fno-schedule-insns2` became unnecessary. A copy of the
pinned variable (`c = s;`) is NOT a substitute: local-alloc ties the two and
drops the copy, so the object stays a word short.

Related: doc 82 §6 (solved/82-switch-case-tree-no-default.md) for the whole
varint-tail recipe (anonymous first byte, `u32` + `<<=` for the shifted lanes,
`v *= 6; p += v;` tail).

Scan result (2026-10-23): the signature does **not** recur in the parked pool.
`tools/regdiff_scan.py` over all 1,529 `src/wip` drafts (every draft whose whole
residual is a register rename) returns 12 pure-rename members and **none** has a
want-named-vs-got-`r0` pair — the r0 lane needs an anonymous temp next to the
named one in the same block, which is rare. Reach for the pin only when the
want/got diff actually shows `r0` on one side; for the named-vs-named swaps the
ordinary `register ... __asm__("rN")` pin ladder applies instead.

## 7zg — 2026-10-23: **triage the residual before touching it: three kinds, and only one is source-fixable; plus "re-measure the pins"** (fn_801AACA4 94.4 -> 98.4 %)

Before writing variants for a NEAR draft, decode want and got and split every
differing word into three buckets:

| bucket | test | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| **opcode/imm** | mnemonic differs, or the same mnemonic with a different constant | a source/semantics suspect — this is the only bucket C can usually fix |
| **register-only** | `mnemonic` and every immediate equal, wrong `rN`/`fN` | allocator tie: the value is right, the home is not |
| **reorder** | the differing window of want is a permutation of the same window in got | scheduler tie: identical instruction multiset, different order |

Census of the pooled drafts (459 non-stub drafts that compiled, all ≥ 50 %):

- 456 scored NEAR; of the 142 at ≥ 90 %, **31 have an *empty* opcode/imm bucket
  (pure reorder)** and only 2 have a wrong immediate that is not part of a
  permutation. 61 are within two non-permuted words.
- The pure-reorder members are the trap: the whole body is already
  byte-identical modulo instruction order, so they present as "99 % — one
  tweak" but every lever that changes statement order leaves the pair where it
  was.

So: if the opcode/imm bucket is empty, stop writing source variants. Sweep
flags once, record the result, and park — the remaining control is the
allocator's, not the source's.

**Re-measure the register pins before iterating.** Pins accumulate across
rounds and outlive the body they were measured on. Strip every
`register ... __asm__("rN")` (and every empty `__asm__("" ...)` barrier), keep
everything else, and re-score: on `fn_801AACA4` the *pinned* body scores 94.4 %
and the pin-free body **98.4 %** — the pin anchored a callee-saved home copy in
the slot retail does not use, and once it was gone the other five residual words
(fn_80060490's 7th-arg slot, the trailing `mr r3,r30`) matched too. Four other
drafts in the pool also score higher pin-free (60.8 -> 67.7, 62.3 -> 62.8,
69.2 -> 70.1). A pin is only a valid next step *after* the pin-free score is
known — otherwise you may be pinning against your own earlier pin.

**Flags measured neutral on this class** (byte-identical or worse on every
member probed; do not re-run them): `-fforce-addr`, `-fno-force-mem`,
`-fno-optimize-register-move`, `-fno-regmove`, `-fno-branch-count-reg`,
`-fno-delayed-branch`, `-fno-peephole`, `-fsched-spec-load`,
`-fno-sched-spec-load`, `-fno-sched-spec-load-dangerous`, `-fno-inline`,
`-finline-functions`, `-fomit-frame-pointer`, `-fno-strength-reduce`,
`-fno-function-cse`, `-fno-optimize-sibling-calls`, `-fno-rename-registers`,
`-fno-defer-pop`, `-fno-caller-saves`, `-fno-expensive-optimizations`,
`-fno-thread-jumps`, `-fno-cse-follow-jumps`. `-fno-gcse` and
`-fno-schedule-insns` change the body wholesale (3–14 %), so their neutrality
on a 99 % draft is not evidence either way — they are never usable here.

## 7zh — 2026-10-23: **one wrong word at a call argument can be follow-jumps CSE forwarding; `-fno-cse-follow-jumps` per object** (fn_800CC138 97.5 -> 100 %)

Symptom: the whole body is byte-exact except one call's argument register — want
loads the argument from the long-lived home (`mr r3, r31`), the build copies the
*sibling* pseudo instead (`mr r3, r9`), and the sibling is provably dead and
equal at that point. Source-level attempts all fail because the value is right
and the register is chosen by CSE, not by source order: retyping the candidate
(`void*`/`u32`/`u8*`), changing the callee prototype (`s32`/`CStruct*`/`void*`),
routing the argument through a block-local or an `r3`-pinned variable, a
zero-byte `+r` barrier on the walker, and pinning the walker home instead (that
last one shifts every parameter home by a register).

The lever is a per-object flag: **`-fno-cse-follow-jumps`**. CSE across jumps is
what substitutes the equivalent pseudo into the argument; suppressing it leaves
the argument on the home and the object becomes byte-exact (160 B, all 40
words). Wire it with the draft's `// FLAG:` line — `promote_wip.py` carries it
into `configure.py` as `extra_cflags`. This is established practice, not a new
device: `fn_801A8354.c` already builds with the same flag.

Triage rule: when the residual is a *single* `mr` into `r3`..`r10` at a call and
every other word matches, try the per-draft CSE flags (`-fno-cse-follow-jumps`,
`-fno-rerun-cse-after-loop`, `-fno-gcse`) before writing another source shape.

**Pool-wide flag census (459 non-stub drafts, 35 flag sets each: 18 optimization
toggles, `-O1`/`-Os`, and the `-mno-string/multiple/update/powerpc-gfxopt`,
`-mminimal-toc`, `-mno-fp-in-toc` target switches): one exact hit — this
function.** 28 drafts scored higher under some flag; the largest jumps were
`-fno-regmove` (+11.1 points on a 73.6 % body), `-Os` (+5.4), and
`-fno-schedule-insns2` (+13.6 on a 68.2 % body), none of which came close to a
match. Pairing a draft's best flag with a second flag added nothing beyond two
+1.8 points. Conclusion: flags are a real but thin lever on this pool — check the
CSE trio on every single-word call-argument residual, and do not run another
pool-wide flag sweep.

## 7zi — 2026-10-23: **pure-colour drafts ARE reachable from C — pin the two swapped webs and drop the flag that was masking the swap** (fn_80191050, 528 B → EXACT)

§7zc concluded that the "pure colour" drafts (`colour == ndiff`: every differing
word is the same instruction with a different register) "cannot be improved from
C". That is too strong. `fn_80191050` was one of them — 4 register words, size
exact — and it promoted EXACT with **two zero-code pins and no flags at all**.

The lever that did it:

- The draft carried `-fno-schedule-insns`. That flag fixed the *roles* (arg1 in
  r28, `fn_800CBDE0`'s result in r29) but left 2 words wrong at the `sp10` init
  (`stw` before `cmpwi`; retail compares first).
- Dropping the flag restores retail's `cmpwi`/`stw` order but returns the role
  swap (10 words). Neither state is promotable, so the flag is a crutch that
  hides two independent defects.
- Fix: pin **both** swapped webs and use default flags —
  `register s32 temp_r29 asm("r29")` on the call result, and a
  `register s32 sel asm("r4")` staging copy for the selector whose reload had
  been landing in r9 (r4 is the home the dead `QB_TRIGGER_OBJ_ID` constant
  leaves free). 0 emitted instructions, 0 flags, 0 diffs.

Why this differs from the single-pin attempts this pool is full of: one pin
only moves *its own* pseudo; the allocator then re-colours the counterpart into
the vacated home, so the residual rotates rather than disappears. Pin the pair
(the value and its counterpart), or pin the web and the register the *reload*
keeps stealing, and drop the flag **before** concluding the body is blocked.

every one below already carries a measured pin result in its draft header, and

## 7zj — 2026-10-23: the 95-99 % band's residual is a **direct-call argument-setup transposition**, and §6dl's permutation lever cannot reach it (measured plateau on all three flagged members)

`fn_80040734` (748 B), `fn_801903B8` (564 B) and `fn_801575E0` (1444 B) each stop
on the same two-to-four words: **two independent argument-setup instructions of
one call, emitted in the opposite order**. Everything around them — including the
rest of the same call's setup and every other word of the function — is
byte-identical.

| fn | the pair, in want's order |
|---|---|
| `80040734` | copy of arg0 into r3, then the float duplicate that fills f2 for arg5 |
| `801903B8` | the QB constant's materialisation, then the `arg0->unk0x20` load |
| `801575E0` | `mr r3,r30` then `li r5,0` at the first SetProp; **the reverse** at the loop-tail copy |

**Why §6dl does not apply.** §6dl works because an *indirect* call's C argument
list is free: the cast's parameter types decide which register each value lands
in, so the list order encodes want's emission order. A **direct** call has a
fixed prototype — position decides the register — and here both arguments of
every pair are integer-class, so permuting the list permutes the registers
instead of the order. There is no equivalent free parameter, which is why this
class behaves differently from the arg-order sites §6dl solved.

**Why it is not source-reachable.** In `fn_801575E0` the same construct (two
SetProp call sites whose surrounding `lis`/`ori`/`bl` words are identical)
wants `mr`-first at one site and `li`-first at the other, and this build emits
the mirror image at each. Any source-level lever that tipped one site would tip
both, so reproducing want needs a per-site difference that the source does not
have. Same reading for `fn_801903B8`: its three later `ContainsFlag` sites want
the load *first* and already match, so the load-vs-constant order is not a
property of the expression, only of the scheduler state at that point in the
block.

**Measured on all three, no movement** (2 / 2 / 4 words respectively, i.e. the
current score): `-fno-caller-saves`, `-fno-keep-static-consts`,
`-fno-thread-jumps`, `-fno-branch-count-reg`, `-fno-function-cse`,
`-fno-optimize-register-move`, `-fno-regmove`, `-fno-force-mem`, `-fno-inline`,
`-fno-strict-aliasing`, `-fno-defer-pop`, `-fno-optimize-sibling-calls`,
`-fno-delayed-branch`, `-fno-sched-interblock`, `-ffixed-r6|r7|r8|r10|r12`,
`-fno-strength-reduce`, `-O3`. Worse: `-fno-cse-follow-jumps` (43 on `80040734`,
inert on the other two), `-ffixed-r9` (14 / 6 / 18), `-O1` (114 on `80040734`,
338 on `801575E0`), `-Os` (325 on `801575E0`), `-fno-expensive-optimizations`
on `801575E0` (347 — for `80040734` it is the opposite: that flag is
load-bearing, the default pipeline gives 4). Body forms measured inert: the constant or the object pointer in a named
local (any scope), a `(CStruct *)` cast on the member, two separately loaded
float locals, and an empty `"+f"` or memory-clobber barrier on the copied float.
A `"+r"` barrier moves the materialisation one block too early: on
`801903B8`'s constant it costs 4 words (input-only `"r"` 5), and on `80040734`'s
arg0 itself 12. A `"+r"` barrier on a local copy of arg0 does not compile with
this cc1.

**Triage rule so this is not re-swept.** Treat a 2-4 word residual as this class
only when (a) every differing word is argument setup for one call, (b) the
neighbouring words are byte-identical, and (c) want shows *both* orders at
different sites of the same function. Then check the one reachable route first:
whether want carries `crclr cr1eq` before the `bl` — if so the callee must be
left unprototyped (recipe 87 / M8.16), which also re-schedules the arg setup.
None of these three has a `crclr`, so that route is closed here. After that,
record and move on: `tools/test_wip_drafts.py` plus the flag matrix above is the
whole search space, and the remaining members of the band listed at the end of
§7zi are the same class.
